dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-remraam.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach International GCSE mathematics under both boards and at both tiers. The first conversation is about which of the four problems below is actually present, because the plans that follow from them have almost nothing in common.

intro.heading: The same message, four different problems
paragraphs: Messages about maths arrive in one shape. My child is struggling in maths, the last assessment was disappointing, can you help. Underneath that single sentence sit four distinct situations, and the help that works for one does nothing for another. Treating them as one problem called needs maths tutoring is the most expensive mistake in this market, because the family pays for a plan aimed at somebody else's child.

The first is the student performing two grades below their own classwork. They follow lessons, they can do the questions when sitting with a teacher, and the paper comes back worse than anyone expected. This is almost always execution: method not shown, early rounding, question order never planned, command terms skipped. It responds quickly and visibly.

The second is the student already at their tier ceiling. They are working hard and well, and the grade they are receiving is close to the maximum their entry allows. No amount of tutoring changes that, and a provider who takes the booking without saying so is selling something they know will not work. What that family needs is a tier conversation with the school, not an hourly rate.

The third freezes. They can do the mathematics at the kitchen table and cannot do it in the hall, and their scripts show questions attempted, abandoned and sometimes attempted again. More teaching makes this worse by raising the stakes. What helps is a large volume of successful, timed, marked work until the evidence of competence outweighs the fear.

The fourth simply does not practise. Nothing happens between lessons, the understanding is real but never consolidated, and each assessment arrives on knowledge that has decayed. This student does not need more input; they need a structure and somebody who checks it. Remraam helps here, because South View School sits close by and the afternoon is short enough to leave usable evening time.

A fifth situation exists and is rarer than families fear: genuine content absence, where whole questions are untouched rather than partly attempted. That is the only one of the five needing months rather than weeks, and it is also the one most often assumed when something faster is actually going on. Distinguishing it costs nothing more than looking at a marked script properly, which is why this page asks for one before proposing anything at all.

None of this requires a tutor to diagnose, incidentally. A parent holding a marked paper and the descriptions above can usually place their own child within a few minutes, and for two of the five profiles the next step is a conversation with the school rather than a purchase. That is an awkward thing for a tutoring page to say and it is the most useful sentence on it.

sections.heading: Four kinds of struggling maths student
paragraphs: The four profiles are distinguishable from a marked paper and a short conversation, and getting the distinction right is worth more than any choice of tutor. Each has a different signature, a different plan and a different honest timescale, and two of them need less paid help than families expect.

The underperformer's script shows scattered small losses across almost every question: a right method with no working, a rounded intermediate value, an abandoned final page. Nothing is absent and marks are leaking everywhere. The ceiling student's script shows near-maximum performance on the questions the paper contains, which is the one pattern tutoring cannot improve.

The freezer's script is distinctive and often misread as content absence. Questions are started, crossed out, restarted, and the handwriting deteriorates down the page. Sometimes a later question is answered well while an earlier, easier one is blank, which is the clearest single sign that the problem is not knowledge. More teaching raises the stakes and makes it worse.

The non-practiser's script shows competence on recent topics and nothing on older ones, because what was understood was never consolidated. Their classwork is fine, their homework is often late, and their assessments decline through the year as the content behind them grows. The intervention is structural, and the cheapest version of it is a parent who checks a short daily block.

A mixed picture is common and does not invalidate the exercise. A student can be both a non-practiser and an underperformer, in which case the structure comes first because execution drills need something to drill. What matters is deciding an order rather than attempting all of it, since a plan aimed at four problems at once is a plan aimed at none.

sections.heading: Which topics are actually worth the time
paragraphs: Revision time is finite and topics are not equally valuable. The question that should drive a plan is how many marks a topic reliably carries in the paper the student is sitting, multiplied by how much of that the student is currently losing. Most self-directed revision ignores both halves and works through a textbook in order.

Number and algebra dominate. They appear in their own questions and inside almost every other topic, so a student weak in rearrangement or in handling fractions and indices loses marks in geometry, trigonometry and statistics as well. That makes algebra the highest-value repair in the subject by a clear margin, and also the slowest, which is an uncomfortable combination.

Geometry and trigonometry are next and are more self-contained, which makes them good targets close to a series: a focused fortnight on circle theorems or on the sine and cosine rules can produce visible gains without needing anything else to be in place. Statistics and probability vary more by board and tier but reward exactly the same mechanical discipline.

At the far end are topics that carry few marks and consume time out of proportion. Near a series, deliberately leaving one alone is a legitimate strategy, and a good plan says which topics are being written off rather than pretending everything will be covered. That honesty is also what makes the rest of the plan credible.

The multiplication that drives this is worth stating explicitly: value equals marks the topic carries times the proportion the student is currently losing. A topic worth many marks that the student already handles is not a priority, and a topic worth few marks they always get wrong is not either. Both halves have to be read off the same marked script.

sections.heading: The papers compared, and why practising them together fails
paragraphs: Both boards examine mathematics across more than one paper, and the papers do not test the same thing. Practising them interchangeably trains neither, which is one of the quieter reasons a diligent student plateaus despite doing plenty of past questions.

Where a paper allows a calculator, the skill being tested shifts towards interpretation, multi-step problem setup and efficient use of the machine. Where one does not, the test is fluency: exact values, fraction arithmetic, mental estimation and the ability to carry a manipulation without a safety net. A student who always has a calculator to hand in homework loses the second silently, because nothing in a normal week exposes it.

There is also a structural difference across a paper that students rarely exploit. Early questions are short and reward speed; later ones are multi-step and reward planning and shown method. A student who spends the same amount of time per mark throughout runs out of road, and a student who attempts questions strictly in order often abandons marks they could have collected later in the paper.

The practical fix is simple to state and takes a fortnight to install. Practise each paper type separately. Before each practice paper, decide a question order and a time allocation by marks. Mark against the scheme afterwards, not just the answers, so that the method marks become visible.

One more habit belongs here, and it is about the first five minutes. A student who reads the whole paper before starting knows where the long questions are and can allocate accordingly; one who starts at question one blind cannot. Five minutes spent reading feels like five minutes lost and buys back considerably more at the end.

sections.heading: The ceiling conversation, had honestly
paragraphs: The second profile deserves its own section because it is the one the market handles worst. A student working hard and sitting near the top of what their tier allows cannot be improved by tutoring in any meaningful sense, and the honest response is to say so and explain what can be done instead.

What can be done is a conversation with the school. Ask which tier the student is entered for, what evidence the department would want in order to review it, and the last date an amendment can be made. Those three answers turn a vague frustration into either a plan or a closed door, and both are better than paying for hours that cannot change the outcome.

If the amendment window has closed, the useful reframing is about what comes next rather than about this grade. A capped maths grade may not meet a sixth form's threshold for an A Level or a Higher Level Diploma route, and that is worth checking directly with the receiving school, which sets its own thresholds. Some will consider other evidence; some will not.

There is also a legitimate narrower use of tutoring for this student: making sure that every mark their tier does contain is actually collected. That is a short execution block rather than a term of teaching, and it is a smaller purchase than the one most families are expecting to make.

This conversation is also worth having a year earlier, in Year 10, when the decision is still live rather than being appealed. A student aiming at a science A Level or a Higher Level Diploma subject needs the higher tier, and the work that secures that placement is harder topics met early rather than revision done late. That is the one piece of timing advice that would prevent most of these conversations entirely.

sections.heading: The student who freezes
paragraphs: Exam anxiety in mathematics has a recognisable signature and a counter-intuitive remedy. The signature is in the script: questions begun and crossed out, work restarted, handwriting degrading down the page, and sometimes a harder later question answered while an easier earlier one sits blank. Parents and teachers frequently read this as not knowing enough, and respond with more teaching.

More teaching usually makes it worse, because it confirms the student's belief that they are behind and raises the stakes of the next assessment. What helps is the opposite: a large volume of questions at a difficulty the student can actually complete, timed from the beginning in short sections, marked promptly so that success is visible and recorded.

The sequencing matters. The hardest topics are deliberately deferred, not because they do not matter but because the immediate job is to accumulate evidence of competence under time pressure. Once a student has a run of completed, timed, marked work behind them, the harder material becomes approachable, and the same content that defeated them in October is often unremarkable in February.

This is slow work by the standards of the other profiles, usually six to ten weeks, and it is the profile where a group class is least useful, because a room of peers is part of what produces the freezing. It is also the profile where a tutor's manner matters more than their subject depth, which is a real thing to ask about in a trial lesson.
bullets: The signature is started-and-abandoned work, not untouched questions
More teaching raises the stakes and tends to worsen it

sections.heading: Remraam practicalities for the student who will not practise
paragraphs: The fourth profile is the most common and the least glamorous, and Remraam is a better place to address it than most of this belt. The community is low-rise apartments in Dubailand, built as Al Thamam and Al Ramth with its own park and retail, reached from Al Qudra Road and Emirates Road. South View School sits close by and takes students through Year 11.

The short run matters because the intervention is structural. A student home soon after four has a genuinely usable early evening, and a twenty-minute block at half past four with somebody in the house is a different proposition from the same block at half past eight after a long journey. Families moving here from communities with longer commutes often do not realise how much that changes what is possible.

The structure itself should be small and daily rather than large and weekly. Twenty minutes four times a week, with the work set in advance and marked at the start of the next session, consolidates what lessons deliver. One two-hour catch-up at the weekend does not, because mathematics decays between contacts and consolidation needs frequency rather than duration.

The accountability is the part a tutor actually sells here. Setting work is easy and free; checking it, marking it and discussing what it exposed is the service, and it is why a session for this profile looks like a review meeting rather than a lesson. Parents who want the cheapest version of this can do the checking themselves, and that works when it is sustainable.
bullets: A short school run makes an early-evening block realistic in this community

sections.heading: What each plan costs, with sources
paragraphs: Because the four profiles need different plans, they cost different amounts, and the two cheapest are the ones families least expect. The ceiling student needs a school conversation and perhaps a short execution block. The non-practiser needs a weekly review hour, which can sit at the lower end of the market. The underperformer needs four to six weeks of twice-weekly work. The freezer needs the longest commitment.

The published bands are worth reading before any of that is priced. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour in Dubai, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, and marking a student's weekly blocks is work that tier can do well. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150.

Subject specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table giving AED 200 to 450 or more, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and home tutors at AED 200 to 500.

Monthly, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with market packages including AED 799 for eight online sessions. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. These are market figures with their sources named, not IB Gram prices.

sections.heading: Permits, premises and what a tutor may not do
paragraphs: An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students.

MoHRE's own service listing is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, shows no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted as the penalty is unverified.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute instead, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram has no UAE premises, holds no such permit and does not describe its tutors using a regulator's name. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules also bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school.

On materials and coursework, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to their publishers and are linked rather than circulated. Where a centre runs assessed work it must be the student's own, so a tutor explains criteria, critiques an approach and marks a draft the student wrote, and never writes, drafts, completes or edits the work to completion.

faqs.question: How do we tell which kind of maths problem our child has?
faqs.answer: From a marked paper rather than from how it feels, because all four situations present identically at home. Scattered small losses across nearly every question means execution. Near-maximum performance on the questions present means the tier is the limit. Questions started, crossed out and restarted, with a later question answered better than an earlier one, means anxiety. Recent topics fine and older topics empty means consolidation. Whole questions untouched means genuine content absence, which is the only one needing months.

faqs.question: Can tutoring help a student already at the top of the Core tier?
faqs.answer: Not in the way the family is hoping. Core and Foundation cap the available grade because the paper does not contain the questions that earn more, so a student performing near that maximum cannot be lifted by more teaching. The useful action is three questions to the school: which tier is my child entered for, what evidence would you want to review it, and what is the last date an amendment is possible. A short block to collect every mark the tier does contain is still worthwhile, and that is four sessions rather than a term.

faqs.question: Our son can do maths at home and falls apart in the exam. What works?
faqs.answer: Volume of successful work under time, not more teaching. The script usually shows questions begun and abandoned, restarted, with handwriting degrading, and sometimes a harder later question answered while an easier earlier one is blank. More teaching confirms his belief that he is behind and raises the stakes. What helps is a large quantity of questions at a difficulty he completes, timed from the start in short sections, marked promptly, with the hardest topics deliberately deferred until a record of success exists.

faqs.question: What should a student do between sessions if they currently do nothing?
faqs.answer: Twenty minutes, four times a week, set in advance and marked at the start of the next session. Small and frequent beats large and occasional in mathematics, because fluency decays between contacts and consolidation depends on frequency rather than duration. Remraam helps here: with South View School close by, a student home soon after four has a genuinely usable early evening, which is a different proposition from the same block at half past eight after a long run from elsewhere in this belt.

faqs.question: Which topic should we fix first if time is short?
faqs.answer: Algebra and number, almost always, because they carry marks directly and also sit inside geometry, trigonometry and statistics. A student weak at rearrangement or at indices and fractions loses marks in topics that look unrelated. The uncomfortable part is that algebra is both the highest-value repair and one of the slowest. Close to a series, self-contained topics like circle theorems or the sine and cosine rules give faster visible gains, and a good plan says which low-density topics are being left alone deliberately.

faqs.question: Why does practising past papers not seem to help our daughter?
faqs.answer: Three common reasons. She may be practising the wrong board's papers, since Cambridge and Pearson phrase questions differently and expect different written method. She may be practising calculator and non-calculator papers interchangeably, which trains neither. Or she may be marking answers rather than marking against the scheme, which hides where the method marks sat. Checking the code on the paper against her entry, separating the paper types, and marking line by line against the published scheme usually fixes it.

faqs.question: Is a group class useful for a student with exam anxiety?
faqs.answer: Usually the least useful format for that profile. A room of peers is often part of what produces the freezing in the first place, and a group's pace does not allow the careful sequencing that builds a record of success. Group classes work well for broad revision where everyone in the room sits the same code at the same tier. For anxiety, one-to-one with a tutor whose manner suits the student matters more than subject depth, which is a real thing to assess in a trial lesson.

faqs.question: How quickly should an execution problem show improvement?
faqs.answer: Three to six weeks, and if it does not, the diagnosis was wrong. Shown method, rounding discipline, question order and command-term reading are habits, and habits respond to drilling on that timescale. The way to see it is to retest the same question types rather than to wait for the next school assessment, which measures too many variables at once. A provider who proposes a term for an execution problem has either not read the script or is selling length rather than help.

faqs.question: What does it mean when a later question is answered better than an earlier one?
faqs.answer: It is the clearest single sign that knowledge is not the problem. A student who answers a harder question on page six while leaving an easier one on page two blank has the mathematics and lost it to something situational: panic, time allocation, or a decision early in the paper that derailed the rest. That pattern points at the anxiety or execution profiles rather than at content absence, and it changes the plan completely, which is why the script matters more than the grade.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week is too many?
faqs.answer: More than two during term, in almost every case. The limiting factor is the student's own practice time between sessions, and a third hour of input leaves no room to consolidate the first two. For the consolidation profile, one session is right and the value is in the checking rather than the teaching. The exception is a school holiday, where three or four sessions in a week is realistic because nothing else is competing, and that is the natural window for closing a content gap.

faqs.question: Should a Remraam family try school support before paying?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this community is unusually well placed for it. South View School sits close by, so staying for a clinic or support session and getting home at a reasonable hour is practical in a way it is not from Mudon, Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square. The subject teacher sets the mock, knows the mark scheme and has context on your child. What school support cannot provide is sustained one-to-one attention on one student's error pattern week after week.

faqs.question: Does a cheap tutor make sense for marking weekly work?
faqs.answer: For that specific job, often yes. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour in Dubai, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, and marking a student's short weekly sets against answers and schemes is work that tier can do well. What it rarely provides is the diagnosis: deciding from a marked paper which of the four profiles applies and which topics carry the most recoverable marks.

faqs.question: What if the marked paper shows whole questions untouched?
faqs.answer: Then it is content absence rather than any of the other three, and the honest timescale is months. The plan becomes sequenced teaching of the topics carrying the most marks in the real paper, with low-density topics excluded on purpose, and a stated ceiling rather than an implied one. A provider who promises to rebuild two years of foundations in an eight-week block is selling something that does not exist, and the script is what distinguishes this case from an execution problem.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Al Thamam or Al Ramth?
faqs.answer: Not one arranged through IB Gram. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only. Visiting tutors exist in Dubai and are advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel folded into the price, per Bestimate's Dubai cost table and the rates home tutors publish. The online route also avoids a fixed arrival window, which matters for the consolidation profile where an early-evening slot is doing most of the work.

intro.heading: What does moving a maths grade actually cost?
paragraphs: Serena sits off Al Qudra Road at the far edge of the Dubailand belt, among clusters including Bella Casa and Casa Viva. The families there who contact us about IGCSE maths almost always frame it as a grade: the report says 5 and the target is 7, or the mock came back at 4 and nobody knows why. That is a better starting point than a subject name, because grade moves can be priced.

The price depends on which move it is. Getting a 4 to a 5 is usually about securing the marks that are already nearly there: method shown, units kept, the easier topics made reliable. That is four to eight sessions. Getting a 6 to a 7 is a different job, because the remaining marks sit in the harder questions and in timing, and it takes longer. And a move that requires a tier change is not a tutoring job at all until the school has agreed it.

Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor teaching online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table at AED 200 to 450+. Budget online tuition starts at AED 33 to 65, per Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, and Serena sits at the top of that range because the round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — and there is no UAE office or centre. Serena students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which removes the travel premium rather than discounting it. For maths that costs almost nothing in teaching quality, because the subject's working surface is a page of algebra that transfers to a shared screen with the advantage that the annotated file is kept.

What follows is the arithmetic. Each grade move with the sessions and AED it typically needs. Where a term's budget works hardest by year group. The economics of a tier change, including when it stops being possible. Topic-level pricing, because some topics cost four sessions and return more than others return in twenty. The honest group-versus-pair-versus-one-to-one comparison. The resources you should never pay for. And the second series as a budget line.

Every figure names its publisher so you can check it. Where a decision depends on your child's specific entry, the answer sits in the school's entry statement rather than on any page, including this one.

programmes.name: Year 9
programmes.description: The cheapest place to buy a grade, and almost nobody buys here. Six to ten sessions on algebraic fluency, fractions, indices and negative numbers, costing roughly AED 900 to 3,000 at the mid band, routinely removes the need for a weekly arrangement in Year 11. The money works because nothing has become a habit yet.
programmes.countryNote: Year 9 is also when option choices are set in Dubai schools, including whether Additional Maths is realistic. For Serena families the commute matters here: a subject expecting frequent after-school catch-up is harder to sustain from a school fifty minutes away, and that is worth factoring into the choice.

programmes.name: Year 10
programmes.description: The year to buy topic-by-topic work as each topic is taught, so gaps appear now rather than in Year 11 revision. A weekly slot across the year is roughly thirty sessions and AED 4,500 to 9,000 at the qualified-tutor band. What makes it worth that is past-paper questions on each topic at the time it is covered, rather than homework review.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai schools enter students for maths in the June series at the end of Year 10. If yours does, the entry deadline sits months earlier, the tier decision arrives sooner, and the budget shifts forward a year. Confirm the entry list in writing with the exam office.

programmes.name: Year 11
programmes.description: Where most of the money in this market is spent and where it buys the least, because purchases happen under time pressure. A mock-driven block of six to twelve sessions is AED 900 to 3,600 and moves more than a general weekly year. A February start with no diagnosis costs more and delivers less, which is the pattern to avoid.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The second series is a resit route, so a realistic Year 11 budget allows for one subject being sat twice — a second entry fee, quoted by the centre, plus a short further block.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-serena.subjectsIntro: These are the maths topics Serena families ask about, each with its own cost logic: how many sessions it takes and how many marks it returns.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Three to five sessions, and the highest return in the subject because geometry, trigonometry and graph work all depend on it. A student fluent in rearranging and factorising gains marks in topics that are never taught again.

subjects.name: Method marks and working
subjects.description: One or two sessions of strict marking. Not a topic at all, and the cheapest marks available: showing working, keeping units, not rounding mid-calculation, answering the command word. Usually worth more than any single topic taught.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions and indices
subjects.description: Two to four sessions. A reliable upper-tier stumbling block where students either know the rules or guess, and the guessing is visible within one question. Directly worth marks on the harder paper.

subjects.name: Transformations of graphs
subjects.description: Two sessions, properly taught as operations on a function's input and output rather than memorised shift rules. Prevents a recurring loss that reappears every time two transformations are combined.

subjects.name: Trigonometry, including non-right-angled
subjects.description: Three to five sessions. Sine and cosine rules, area, bearings and 3D problems, where losses come from setup rather than formulae. Diagram discipline — a drawn north line, a labelled triangle — recovers most of them.

subjects.name: Probability and tree diagrams
subjects.description: One to two sessions and highly predictable question structures, which makes it one of the best-value targets in the final weeks before a series. Conditional and without-replacement problems produce errors that close immediately.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.description: Two to four sessions. Cumulative frequency, box plots and histograms with unequal class widths. Frequency density is the classic single-topic gap: it costs a specific set of marks on one question and nothing else, which makes it efficient to target.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.description: Three to five sessions and the right first target at the lower tier, where these topics carry a large share of the paper. For a confident Extended student they are already secure and spending here is waste.

subjects.name: Vectors and geometric proof
subjects.description: Five to eight sessions for a modest mark allocation, which makes it the lowest priority when time or money is short unless a top grade is the target and everything else is secure.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fluency or calculator discipline
subjects.description: Two to three sessions, and which one you need depends on the board. Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator written paper; Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout. Buying the wrong one of these two trains a habit the examination does not test.

sections.heading: What each grade move costs
paragraphs: Here is the table families actually want and nobody publishes. It prices the common grade moves in IGCSE maths by the sessions they typically need, at the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 an hour that most of this work sits in. The figures assume the move is realistic within the tier, which is a separate question addressed below.

The pattern is that moves at the lower and middle of the range are cheaper per grade than moves at the top. Getting a 4 to a 5 is largely about securing marks already nearly earned — method shown, units kept, the predictable topics made reliable — and that is habit work with a fast return. Getting a 6 to a 7 means the remaining marks are in the harder questions and in timing, which takes sustained work rather than a short block.

The second pattern is that delay costs differently depending on the move. Habit work stays cheap almost until the exam, so a family short of money in April should spend it there. Content work becomes progressively less effective and, in the final weeks, turns into damage limitation. A Year 10 with a content gap should spend now; a Year 11 in March should spend on technique.

Our own first session exists to place a student in one of these rows honestly, including the row that says four sessions and then stop. We would rather be known for that than for selling a weekly year, and in maths specifically the four-session row is the most common correct answer.

sections.heading: Where a term's budget works hardest
paragraphs: Suppose a family has a fixed amount to spend in one term. Where it goes depends on the year group, and the right answer changes more than most providers admit. This is the allocation we would recommend, including the cases where the honest advice is to spend nothing yet.

In Year 9, spend on algebra. It is the cheapest grade a family will ever buy, it compounds for two years, and six to ten sessions is usually the whole intervention. In Year 10, spend on the topics as they are taught, with past-paper questions on each one at the time: the point is to find gaps while there is still time to close them cheaply.

In the first term of Year 11, spend on diagnosis and habits: strict marking of past work until method and reading losses stop appearing. In the second term, spend on timed papers and whichever one or two topics the marked work keeps showing. In the final weeks, spend on technique and reliability rather than new content, because new content at that point rarely survives contact with an exam.

And the case for spending nothing: a student whose marked papers show marks lost almost entirely to carelessness within topics they clearly know, and whose school provides subject clinics and extra marking, may need structure rather than tuition. Two or three sessions to set up a marking routine the student runs alone is a legitimate and cheap outcome. We will say so when the papers say so.

sections.heading: The economics of a tier change
paragraphs: Some grade targets are impossible within the tier a student is entered for, and spending money on them without knowing that is the worst outcome in this whole market. Tier sets the ceiling, and the ceiling is not negotiable with a tutor.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended, with Core graded C to G and Extended A* to E; the 0980 variant reports on the 9 to 1 scale with the Core tier capped. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher, reporting 5 to 1 and 9 to 4 respectively. Structures and grading can be revised between specification versions, so confirm against the board's current documents and your child's entry statement.

The cost consequence is twofold. If a student is in the right tier, money should go to the topics and habits that carry their own paper — and for a Core or Foundation student that means number, ratio, percentages and accuracy, not the top-tier topics that do not appear. If a student should move tier, the first step is a conversation with the school, not a tutoring purchase, and it is time-limited: entry deadlines sit months before the exam window and a late change is an administrative problem on top of an academic one.

What a tutor can contribute is evidence. Two marked papers usually show whether the issue is tier or preparation: a student losing marks on method, reading and timing is in the right tier with the wrong habits; a student for whom whole question types are blank may be in the wrong one. Get that read before the entry deadline rather than after it, because afterwards the only available purchase is making the most of the ceiling that exists.
bullets: 0580 Core is graded C-G and Extended A*-E; 4MA1 Foundation reports 5-1 and Higher 9-4

sections.heading: Topic-level pricing: what each fix costs and returns
paragraphs: Within a tier, topics differ sharply in how many sessions they take and how many marks they return. A family paying by the hour deserves that information, and it is rarely volunteered because it tends to recommend buying less.

The best-value targets are method marks, algebraic manipulation, and the predictable question structures: probability trees, histogram frequency density, bearings with a drawn north line. Each is a small number of sessions with a reliable return, and the question forms repeat year to year so the practice transfers completely. For a Core or Foundation student, number, ratio and percentages belong in the same category because they carry a large share of that paper.

The poorest value when time is short is vectors and geometric proof at the top tier, which absorbs five to eight sessions for a modest allocation, and any topic the student has already secured. The most common waste we see from this belt is a weekly session spent reviewing homework the student got right, which feels productive to everyone present and changes nothing on a paper.

The practical test for a parent paying by the hour is to ask, each week, which specific lost marks the session was aimed at. A tutor working from a marked paper will answer with a question type. A tutor working from a textbook will answer with a chapter. The first is worth AED 250 an hour; the second is worth AED 50 and is being sold at AED 250.

sections.heading: Group, pair or one-to-one: the maths economics
paragraphs: Group maths classes are the cheapest formal option in this belt and are sold hard by centres in Motor City and Sports City, with monthly packages advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions. Whether they are good value depends on the diagnosis rather than on the format, and the honest answer differs by case.

A group class delivers a fixed syllabus at a fixed pace to a fixed timetable. For a student who is broadly on track and simply needs more exposure and more practice, the per-student economics are unbeatable and the structure helps. For a student with a specific diagnosed gap, a group cannot address it, and the money buys hours in a room rather than marks on a paper. Add the drive from Serena — thirty to forty minutes each way plus waiting — and the real cost per session is around two hours of household time as well as the fee.

A pair sits between the two and is underused in this belt. Two students on the same board, tier and subject, taught together online, splits the rate while keeping the attention individual enough to diagnose. Between Serena, Villanova and Mudon it is easy to arrange because nobody travels. It stops working the moment the two are on different boards, which is why the entry statement comes first.

One-to-one is the most expensive per hour and the cheapest per outcome when the problem is specific. The decision rule we would give any family: if you can state the problem in one sentence, buy one-to-one and buy few hours. If you cannot, buy two or three sessions to find out, because buying thirty hours to discover the problem costs more than three hours spent diagnosing it.

sections.heading: What you should never pay for
paragraphs: Several things are sold in this market that are free, and a family on a budget should recognise them before a quote is accepted.

Board material is first. Cambridge and Pearson publish their specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary information, and a tutor should cite and link them rather than reselling them as a resource pack. A provider charging for them is selling access to something free and redistributing material it does not own. The same applies to formula sheets and syllabus summaries that are reproductions of board documents.

Diagnostic tests are second, in the sense that your child's school has already produced a better one. A marked mock paper is more informative than any placement test, because it was taken under realistic conditions on the right specification. A provider charging for an initial assessment is charging you to replace a document you already have at home.

Third, promises about the final grade. Nobody controls an examination outcome, and a refund claim means nothing unless the exact terms are printed on the same screen as the promise. Fourth, premium rates justified by unevidenced examiner status: we do not describe tutors as examiners where current status cannot be shown, and examiner status gives no access to marking, boundaries or paper content in any case. Fifth, a star rating nobody can trace — competitor pages in this market show conflicting rating figures within a single page, which tells you what those numbers are worth.
bullets: Board specifications, past papers and mark schemes are free and should be linked
The school's marked mock beats any paid diagnostic test
No promises about final grades; refund claims need published terms

sections.heading: The second series as a budget line
paragraphs: Families in this belt routinely spend the entire tutoring budget before results, which leaves no capacity to respond to one. Because there are two series a year, responding is genuinely possible, and it should be planned for rather than improvised.

Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate sitting here, so any advice built on a February window belongs to another country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and its exams officers' guide states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exam officer which zone applies.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. As checkable reference points: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables for later series that may be revised, so work from the live official timetable.

The budget consequence is specific. A resit means a second entry fee, quoted by the examination centre rather than by any tutor, plus typically eight to fifteen further sessions — fewer than the original work, because the diagnosis already exists. A Year 11 plan that holds back a reserve for that possibility is a realistic plan. One that assumes everything lands first time is a hopeful one, and hope is the most expensive thing in this market.

sections.heading: The checks that cost nothing
paragraphs: Three verifications are free and worth making whatever you decide to spend, and together they prevent the most expensive mistakes available in this market.

The first is the entry statement from the school: board, syllabus code and tier for every subject. It settles which past papers are worth an hour and whether a target grade is even available. Departments inside one Dubai school sometimes differ, so check subject by subject rather than school-wide.

The second is the permit, if you are hiring an individual directly. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service with a two-working-day completion time and no listed fee. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it is free, no tutor should be adding a licensing cost to a quote, and no fine schedule is published, so any penalty figure quoted at you is unverified.

The third is what the school already provides: subject clinics, pre-mock revision, lunchtime catch-up, and a head of department who will say candidly how a cohort is doing and whether extra marking is available. Families in this belt routinely pay for what is already included. Where school support is good, the efficient outside purchase is narrow — one diagnosed topic, or technique work — rather than a weekly arrangement running all year.

process.title: Tell us the grade you have and the grade you want
process.description: Plus the board, the tier and a photograph of the most recent marked paper. Framing it as a move rather than a subject lets us place it in the pricing table honestly, including the cases where the target is not available within the current tier and the conversation needs to happen with the school first.

process.title: Sessions estimated, then priced
process.description: We say how many sessions the move looks like before quoting a rate, because the range runs from two to thirty and the rate is the less informative number. A single headline figure quoted before anyone has read a paper is set for the seller's convenience rather than the student's need.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: A real lesson with the person who would continue, no card required, spent on the marked paper rather than on a placement test. It ends with a session count and an order of work. Sometimes the count is smaller than you came expecting; occasionally the answer is a marking routine rather than tuition.

process.title: A plan with a stop date and a reserve
process.description: The plan names the target, the order, the number of sessions and the date it ends. It also recommends keeping a reserve for a second entry fee, because the November series exists and a plan that has spent everything by May cannot respond to a result.

whyPoints.title: Priced by the move, not the hour
whyPoints.description: A 4 to a 5 is four to eight sessions of habit work; a 6 to a 7 is ten to sixteen of harder content and timing. Pricing the move rather than quoting a rate is the only way a family can judge what they are actually committing to across a term.

whyPoints.title: Tier checked before money is spent
whyPoints.description: Core and Foundation tiers cap the available grade, so a target above the ceiling cannot be bought at any rate. We read the entry statement and two marked papers before recommending a plan, and say when the first conversation belongs with the school rather than with us.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium on a long drive
whyPoints.description: Serena is among the furthest-out addresses in this belt, so an in-home arrangement carries the top of the AED 50 to 150 hourly travel premium. Online delivery removes it, and in maths the format costs almost nothing in teaching quality.

whyPoints.title: Free things identified as free
whyPoints.description: Board specifications, past papers and mark schemes are published and should be linked rather than resold. The school's marked mock beats any paid diagnostic. And school subject clinics often cover what a family was about to buy.

whyPoints.title: Figures with their publishers
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names the competitor page or rate table it came from and is presented as the market rather than our price. No promises about final grades, no unevidenced examiner claims, no self-awarded ratings, and no regulator approval implied.

faqs.question: What does it cost to move my child from a 5 to a 7 in IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Typically ten to sixteen sessions, which at the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 an hour is roughly AED 1,500 to 4,800. The reason it costs more than a 4 to a 5 is where the remaining marks sit: in the harder questions and in pace under time pressure, rather than in method marks that are nearly earned already. A 4 to a 5 is usually four to eight sessions and AED 600 to 2,400, because it is mostly habit work with a fast return.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start maths tutoring in Year 9 or Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 9, by a wide margin, and almost nobody does. Six to ten sessions on algebraic fluency, fractions, indices and negative numbers costs roughly AED 900 to 3,000 and compounds for two years, because nothing has become a habit yet and the course has not started. The same family in February of Year 11 buys hours under time pressure with no runway for the cheap fixes, which is how AED 8,000 gets spent for a smaller movement than AED 2,000 would have produced earlier.

faqs.question: Why does the tier matter before I spend anything on maths?
faqs.answer: Because it caps the grade, and no rate changes that. Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended, with Core graded C to G and Extended A* to E; Pearson 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher, reporting 5 to 1 and 9 to 4. Spending specialist money on top-tier topics for a Core student is waste, because those topics are not on their paper. Confirm the tier from the entry statement, check it against the board's current documents, and raise any tier change with the school before the entry deadline.

faqs.question: Which maths topics give the best return per dirham?
faqs.answer: Method marks and working discipline first — one or two sessions of strict marking, returning marks spread across the whole paper. Then algebraic manipulation, three to five sessions, because geometry, trigonometry and graph work all depend on it. Then the predictable question structures: probability trees, histogram frequency density, bearings with a drawn north line, each one or two sessions with a reliable return. For Core and Foundation students, number, ratio and percentages belong at the top because they carry a large share of that paper.

faqs.question: Which maths topics are the worst use of a limited budget?
faqs.answer: Vectors and geometric proof at the top tier, which absorb five to eight sessions for a modest mark allocation and should wait until everything cheaper is secure. And any topic the student has already got right, which is the most common waste we see: a weekly session spent reviewing correct homework feels productive to everybody in the room and changes nothing on a paper. Ask each week which specific lost marks the session was aimed at — a good tutor answers with a question type, not a chapter.

faqs.question: How should I spend one term's budget if that is all I have?
faqs.answer: It depends on the year. Year 9: algebraic fluency, six to ten sessions. Year 10: the topics as they are taught, with past-paper questions on each. First term of Year 11: diagnosis and habit work from marked papers. Second term: timed papers plus the one or two topics the marked work keeps showing. Final weeks: reliability and technique, not new content, because new content rarely survives contact with the exam room. If the papers show a strong student losing marks to carelessness, two sessions setting up a marking routine may be the whole answer.

faqs.question: Are group maths classes in Motor City worth the saving?
faqs.answer: If your child is broadly on track and needs more practice, yes — packages in this market are advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions and the structure helps. If there is a specific diagnosed gap, no: a group delivers one pace to everyone and cannot reach it. The hidden cost from Serena is the drive, thirty to forty minutes each way plus waiting, so roughly two hours of household time per session. Counted properly, a short one-to-one block is often cheaper to the finish line.

faqs.question: Can two Serena households share a maths tutor to split the cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the two students are on the same board and tier in the same subject with a similar starting point. A pair session lowers the cost per student materially and, because nothing travels, a Serena student and a Villanova or Mudon student can share without either family driving. It works well for content and exam technique. It does not work where the boards differ — Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 need different practice — which is why the entry statement comes before the arrangement.

faqs.question: Which maths tutoring charges should a Serena parent simply decline?
faqs.answer: Board material, first: Cambridge and Pearson publish specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary information, and a tutor should link them rather than reselling them as a resource pack. A paid diagnostic test, second, because your child's marked mock is a better diagnostic and you already have it. Promises about final grades, third, since nobody controls an examination outcome and a refund claim needs published terms. And a premium justified by examiner status that cannot be evidenced.

faqs.question: What is the budget for a November maths resit from Serena?
faqs.answer: A second entry fee, quoted by the examination centre rather than by any tutor, plus typically eight to fifteen further sessions — fewer than the original work because the diagnosis already exists. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates and Pearson runs May/June and November, so there is a route each year. Ask the school's exam office for the actual entry figure rather than estimating it, and keep a reserve in the budget, because a plan that has spent everything by May cannot act on a result.

faqs.question: Will a maths tutor visit our home in Serena, and what does that add?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours: IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video and home visits are a service we run only in India, so nobody will arrive at a Dubailand address. Independent in-home tutors work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Serena at the top of that range because the round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes. The premium buys presence. For maths it buys little else, since the lesson is a page of algebra that transfers well to a shared screen.

faqs.question: Does the quoted rate include VAT, and what else should I confirm?
faqs.answer: Ask, and require the answer in writing before the first paid session — we will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an opinion. Also confirm whether the quote is per hour or per lesson and whether an hour means sixty minutes, how much cancellation notice avoids a charge, and whether any materials fee applies. On that last point, nothing published by Cambridge or Pearson should appear on an invoice.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor with more sessions better value than a dearer one with fewer?
faqs.answer: Compare total cost to the finish line rather than the rate. A budget tutor at AED 50 an hour who needs thirty sessions to achieve what a specialist does in eight is more expensive, and the thirty sessions also consume thirty weeks. The questions that reveal which you are dealing with: which syllabus code and tier would you work from, what do you want to see before the first session, and how many sessions do you think this takes. A tutor who names a number is thinking about your child.

faqs.question: Do private maths tutors in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and, according to u.ae, is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applying through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service with a two-working-day completion time. Because the permit is free, no tutor should pass on a licensing cost. No fine schedule is published, so treat any penalty figure quoted at you as unverified.

The first lesson is free and taught by the tutor who would continue. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online, so there is no travel premium on an Al Qudra Road address.

intro.heading: What a maths tutor has to know that is not simply maths
paragraphs: A good mathematician is not automatically a good IGCSE maths tutor, and the gap between the two is where a Sobha Hartland family's money gets wasted. An engineer can solve every question on a Higher tier paper and still not know that a student who writes only the correct answer forfeits the method marks, or that one specification tests arithmetic without a calculator and the other does not, or that a Core entry caps the grade regardless of performance. Those are facts about the examination rather than about mathematics.

So the honest answer to the question behind this search is that plenty of people near you can do the maths, and far fewer know the paper. The second group is small in every Dubai community, not because Hartland is unusual but because the people who know a specification best are usually teaching it full time at a school and have a few evening hours a week at most. Those hours are taken early in the academic year, which is why asking in September gives a wider choice than asking in March.

Rather than offer reassurance, this page gives you the content. It sets out what the two main specifications actually demand topic by topic, including where they diverge, because a tutor who has taught only one usually assumes the other is the same. It explains how a maths mark scheme awards credit, so you can look at your own child's marked paper and see where the marks went. It states what each tier can reach, which is the single most consequential fact in Year 10 and the one schools decide without much discussion.

The practical use of all this is a short list of questions. If a prospective tutor can name the awarding body before you tell them, use the right tier vocabulary, say whether a calculator is permitted in each paper, and describe what an M mark is, they have taught this examination. If they talk about enjoying maths and building confidence, they may be perfectly pleasant and they have not answered the question. Both outcomes are worth knowing in the first conversation rather than in the final term.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE maths tuition to Sobha Hartland as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor matched to the specification rather than to the postcode. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below give the topic comparison, the mark-scheme mechanics, the tier ceilings, the resit calendar and what we will not do with assessed work. Nothing here promises a grade, and anyone promising one in maths at this level is describing a sales position rather than a teaching one.

sections.heading: Topic by topic: what the two main specifications actually demand
paragraphs: This is the section a tutor should be able to discuss without notes, and it is the most practical test of whether they have taught the paper. The two main IGCSE maths specifications in Dubai share most of their content and diverge at the top of each tier, which is exactly where the grades being fought over are decided. A tutor who has taught one and assumes the other matches will be right about number and wrong about the parts that separate a 7 from an 8.

Both cover number, algebra and graphs, coordinate geometry, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, probability and statistics, with sets and Venn diagram work appearing in the higher tiers. The upper tiers of both now reach introductory calculus: Cambridge's Extended content extends to functions and differentiation, and Pearson's Higher tier includes differentiation along with transformation of functions, three-dimensional trigonometry and vectors. The emphasis differs, the question styles differ, and the formulae provided in the examination differ, which is why practice has to come from the right paper.

The table sets out the comparison as it stands, with one caveat stated plainly: specifications are revised, and a page is a reason to check rather than a substitute for checking. Confirm the current content list with the school or on the awarding body's own site before building a revision programme around it, and never rely on an older sibling's experience, because a sibling two years ahead may have sat a different syllabus version of the same qualification.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper, and what it actually exposes
paragraphs: Where a specification includes a paper taken without a calculator, it changes the nature of the whole course, and this is the single most common place a tutor prepared for the other board goes wrong. A non-calculator paper does not test different mathematics. It tests the same mathematics at a speed and accuracy that only comes from automatic arithmetic, and it punishes a student whose every multiplication is a small project.

What it exposes, in practice, is fractions, percentages, index work, surd manipulation where the tier includes it, and the ability to carry a calculation through several steps without writing down a decimal approximation too early. Students who have done all their practice with a calculator in hand have usually never discovered that they cannot do these quickly, because the calculator has been quietly covering for them for three years. The discovery, when it comes, tends to be in a mock.

The remedy is unglamorous and reliable. Short, frequent practice, every session, on arithmetic and algebraic manipulation without a calculator, measured by timing the same question types across weeks so the improvement is visible to the student rather than asserted by the tutor. It is the work students resist most and the work that moves a grade most dependably at this level. If your child's specification includes such a paper and their tutor has never set non-calculator practice, that is a specification mismatch rather than a style preference, and it is worth raising directly rather than hoping it corrects itself nearer the examination.

sections.heading: Mark-scheme mechanics: why right answers score badly
paragraphs: A maths mark scheme does not simply check the answer, and understanding how it does work is the cheapest insight available to a parent. Marks come in three kinds. Method marks, written M in the scheme, are awarded for a correct approach even when the arithmetic goes wrong afterwards. Accuracy marks, written A, are awarded for a correct value and usually depend on the method mark being earned first. Independent marks, written B, are awarded for a correct statement or value on its own.

This structure explains the single most common complaint we hear from Hartland parents, which is that a child got the right answers and a disappointing mark. A student who works mentally and writes only a final value has no method shown, so on a four-mark question they can score one mark for a correct answer and forfeit three, or in some schemes score nothing if the answer is wrong despite the approach having been sound. Conversely a student who shows a correct method and slips in the arithmetic keeps most of the marks.

The practical consequence is a teachable habit rather than a knowledge gain, which makes it fast and cheap to fix. Write the method. Write the substitution. Write the required final statement in geometry and trigonometry questions. Keep units. Do not round until the end. Any tutor who has taught the paper will talk in these terms within the first lesson, and a parent can check their own child's marked script against the table below without understanding the mathematics at all.

sections.heading: Tier ceilings: the decision that sets the grade range
paragraphs: A tier entry determines the grades available to a student, which makes it a more consequential decision than any amount of tutoring. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics runs Core and Extended as separate entries; Pearson Edexcel Specification A runs Foundation and Higher on the same principle. The lower tier cannot reach the top grades however well a student performs, and the higher tier can produce a low grade if a student cannot access the harder half of the paper.

Schools make the decision from class performance, usually in Year 10, and are right in most cases. The exceptions are predictable. A student capped by a weak Year 9 who has since improved may be sitting a paper with a ceiling below their ability. A student promoted on effort rather than on algebraic security may spend two years unable to answer a third of each paper. Both situations are visible in a single marked script to anyone who knows what to look for, and neither is a tutoring problem.

This is why a tier review is the best possible use of a first session for a Year 10 student in Sobha Hartland. It either confirms the school's judgement, which is worth knowing, or gives you specific evidence for a conversation with the maths department while a change is still administratively possible. Entry decisions and their deadlines belong to the school, so raise it early: the same conversation in Year 11 is usually a conversation about a resit instead.

paragraphs: Maths is the best-covered subject in the Dubai tutoring market, which means a Hartland family genuinely has a choice here rather than taking what is available. That makes the comparison worth doing properly, on the variables that matter for a single-subject problem rather than on general preference.

On specification matching, online wins because the pool is the whole market and the code can be honoured rather than approximated. On accountability, online tends to win because marked practice and written feedback exist as documents a parent can inspect, while verbal comments at a kitchen table do not. On cost, online wins by the travel premium: in-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour because travel is inside the figure, against about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. On non-calculator drill, which this page argues is central, the formats are equal in principle and online is easier in practice, because short timed exercises are simple to set, submit and mark remotely. The one variable where a nearby tutor has a real claim is supervision: a fourteen-year-old who will not practise unless someone is physically present is a genuine category, and for that family a local arrangement is the right answer. sections.heading: June, November and the resit question
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series that appears in some online revision material is offered to India only, so it has no place in a Dubai student's plan, and material quoting it should make you doubt the rest of the document. November functions as the resit route inside the same academic year for both main awarding bodies, which is useful to know before results day rather than after it.

Read the published record backwards and the resit question turns into a number of weeks rather than a vague option. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. The November 2026 final timetable then ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from that series arrive in January, as November 2025 results did when they reached students on 22 January 2026. A Sobha Hartland family tracing that sequence has barely ten weeks between a disappointing August grade and the first November maths paper, and most of those weeks fall inside the opening term of Year 12 alongside new work. Those are past dates, cited so you can see the shape of the cycle rather than so you can act on them.

For anything ahead, open the awarding body's live timetable rather than a restatement, including this page's. Pearson publishes provisional timetables and revises them. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school which zone your centre sits in, and use the timetable they issue rather than one found online.

sections.heading: KHDA, the Hartland schools and the post-16 threshold
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Annual inspection runs on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, published school by school, and the secondary mathematics commentary inside a report is a free second opinion on whether a weak grade reflects the student or the department.

Scale explains why tutoring quality varies so widely. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. A market that large, using several awarding bodies, produces a tutoring supply in which nothing visibly distinguishes a specification-literate teacher from a confident generalist unless a parent asks. Separately, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year.

The grade's later use deserves one clear statement. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five, alongside one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is incorrect. Equivalency is a process the ministry performs, so verify your own case through its attestation channel rather than through any tutoring service. On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or accredited by Cambridge, Pearson or Oxford AQA, and does not claim to be.

sections.heading: What we will not supply, and getting started from Sobha Hartland
paragraphs: Two things are not available from us at any price. The first is assessed work. IGCSE maths has no coursework component in the main specifications, which removes most of the temptation, but at least one operator ranking for UAE curriculum queries sells completed assessed work in other subjects at a published price, and the students buying it are the same students. Submitting work that is not your own is malpractice and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

The second is examination material. We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or Oxford AQA syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, and we do not host them for download. We reference them and link to the awarding body's own page. That is the lawful position and the more useful one, because the official version is the current version, while a stale document circulating in a parents' group is a reliable way to revise content that has been withdrawn.

To start, send the awarding body and specification code from the examinations officer, the tier, the latest grade labelled as mock or classwork, and a photograph of one marked paper. The script is worth more than any description, because it shows whether the losses are method marks, arithmetic speed or inaccessible content. We then propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson. Ask them to name the specification before you tell them, ask what an M mark is, and ask afterwards for a written account of where the marks are going. If any of those answers is vague, do not book, with us or anyone else.
