faqs.question: How do I tell whether a maths tutor knows my child's specification or just maths?
faqs.answer: Three questions settle it in a first conversation. Ask them to name the awarding body and code before you tell them. Ask whether a calculator is permitted in each paper on that specification, because the answer differs between the two main boards and changes the whole drill. And ask what an M mark is and how a student loses one. A tutor who answers all three has taught this examination. A tutor who talks about enjoying maths and building confidence may be pleasant and has not answered the question.

faqs.question: Why did my child get the right answers and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Because mark schemes award method separately from accuracy. Method marks, written M, are earned by a correct approach that is written down, and on a four-mark question a student who works mentally and records only a final value can forfeit three of them even when the value is right. Accuracy marks usually depend on the method mark being earned first. The fix is a habit rather than knowledge: write the method, write the substitution, write the required final statement, keep units, and round only at the end.

faqs.question: Does the content actually differ between Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Most of it is shared and the divergence sits at the top of each tier, which is exactly where contested grades are decided. Both cover number, algebra and graphs, coordinate geometry, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, probability and statistics. Cambridge's Extended content extends to functions and introductory differentiation; Pearson's Higher tier includes differentiation, transformation of functions, three-dimensional trigonometry and vectors. Question styles and the formulae provided also differ, which is why practice has to come from the student's own specification rather than from whatever is to hand.

faqs.question: My child has never practised maths without a calculator. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is, if their specification includes a paper taken without one. A non-calculator paper tests the same mathematics at a speed only automatic arithmetic allows, and a student whose every multiplication is a small project runs out of time while understanding everything. The exposure is usually fractions, percentages, index work and carrying exact values through several steps. The remedy is short, frequent timed practice every session, benchmarked across weeks. It is the work students resist most and the work that moves a grade most reliably.

faqs.question: Can my child's tier be changed if it looks wrong?
faqs.answer: Entry decisions and their deadlines belong to the school, so it depends on when you raise it. A tier caps the grade range available regardless of performance, and misplacement is visible in one marked script: a capped student who is answering everything correctly, or a promoted student who cannot attempt a third of the paper. Raise it in Year 10 with the script as evidence and a change may be possible. The same conversation in Year 11 is usually a conversation about a November resit instead.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth taking alongside IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: For a secure Extended or Higher tier student heading to A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level, it is useful preparation because it introduces calculus, trigonometric identities and function work at a level the main specification does not reach. For a student who is still shaky on Extended algebra it is a mistake, because the difficulty they will meet in Additional Mathematics is almost always an unresolved Extended gap wearing a harder name. Secure the main specification first and the decision answers itself.

faqs.question: What should we use as the exam timetable?
faqs.answer: Only the one the school issues. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and its guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A timetable found online may belong to another zone entirely. Ask the examinations officer which zone your centre is in, and for future series open the awarding body's live timetable rather than any restatement of it.

faqs.question: Can my child resit IGCSE maths in November?
faqs.answer: Yes, for both main awarding bodies November functions as a resit route inside the same academic year, which is worth knowing before results day rather than after. The pattern is visible in the published record: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entry goes through the school's examinations officer shortly after summer results, and the preparation window is roughly eight to ten weeks, which is enough if the script is used to target it.

faqs.question: How many sessions does an algebra problem take to fix?
faqs.answer: Six to ten weekly sessions, in most cases, because fluency is built by frequency rather than by intensity. The work is deliberately repetitive: expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving, until it becomes automatic rather than careful. Progress should be benchmarked by timing the same question types across weeks so the student can see it rather than being told about it. A method-marks problem is faster, often a half-term. Content the student genuinely cannot access is slower and may be a tier question instead.

faqs.question: Does it matter that the tutor is not in Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: For maths it matters very little, and maths is the best-covered subject in this market so you have a genuine choice. What matters is whether the tutor has taught your child's specification, whether they set non-calculator practice where the board tests it, and whether you can inspect marked scripts afterwards. Online delivery lets the match be made on those grounds rather than on who will drive here through 4pm traffic. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes at all; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class good enough for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For a named topic shared by the group, often yes, and it is the cheapest format available near Hartland. For a method-marks habit, no, because an individual habit will not be noticed in a room of six and that is precisely the kind of loss that costs most. Note also that a centre usually teaches one awarding body, so check that it matches your child's entry before assuming the practice is relevant. The test is whether you can name the gap: if you can, a group class may be efficient.

faqs.question: What grade does my child need in IGCSE maths for A Level or IB Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Schools set their own thresholds, commonly a 7 or equivalent, so ask your child's school directly rather than relying on a general figure. More useful than the threshold is the distinction between meeting it and being ready: both A Level Mathematics and IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assume algebraic fluency that a borderline grade does not demonstrate. A Year 11 block aimed at algebra specifically, rather than at general revision, is better preparation than scraping the threshold and hoping.

faqs.question: Will you give us past papers and mark schemes to work through?
faqs.answer: We do not reproduce, distribute or host awarding-body syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We reference them and link to the board's own page, which is both the lawful position and the more useful one, because the official version is the current one while a stale PDF circulating in a parents' group is a common route to revising withdrawn content. Tutors set practice from material they can legitimately access and mark it against the published criteria, which is the part that produces the improvement anyway.

faqs.question: How quickly can you find an IGCSE maths tutor for us?
faqs.answer: Usually days, and sometimes the same day if you send the specification code with a photograph of a marked script. Maths is the best-covered subject in the market, so the constraint is normally the slot rather than the subject: the early-evening Gulf Standard Time hours Hartland families want after the school run fill first, and the better tutors are largely committed by October. Oxford AQA specifications and Specification B take longer, because fewer tutors have taught them, and we will say so rather than improvising.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan, mocks or travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online delivery makes it routine rather than a favour. During Ramadan sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar slot, with no journey to renegotiate at either end. In mock weeks a session can pause or redirect to whatever the mock has just exposed, which is often the most productive single session of the year. When a family travels the lesson follows the student. Agree which time zone the session is pinned to if you are leaving the Gulf, and give notice so the slot is held.

faqs.question: What is the one thing to send that helps most?
faqs.answer: A photograph of one marked script, with the awarding body, code and tier written alongside it. It tells us what no description can. Correct answers with no working point to method marks. Slow, hesitant early arithmetic points to non-calculator fluency. Blank questions in the second half of the paper point to content the student cannot access, which may be a tier matter rather than a teaching one. With that one image we can usually propose a tutor the same day.

intro.heading: Why maths is the homework that gets dropped in Barsha Heights
paragraphs: There is a specific pattern in this community and it is worth naming before any syllabus talk. Barsha Heights has no large school campus inside it, so secondary students board a bus in the morning and travel outward, to Al Barsha, Al Barsha South, Al Sufouh or further. The return is a multi-stop route rather than a bell, so a child is home somewhere between a quarter past five and six. After that there is an evening, and the evening has room for two subjects honestly done rather than four.

Mathematics is reliably the one that loses out, and not through laziness. English reading can be done on a sofa. Science revision can be done from a summary sheet. Mathematics requires a desk, a clear head and a full attempt at a question that cannot be half-done, and it takes the longest of anything on the list. A tired fifteen-year-old with four tasks and ninety minutes will rationally do the three that can be finished. Over a term the arithmetic of that choice is visible in a mock paper.

That is the problem a tutor in this community is actually solving, and it changes what the hour should be. If the week genuinely contains no independent practice time, a session spent reviewing work the student did not do is wasted. The session has to be the place where the practice happens: full questions attempted under supervision, corrected immediately, with the method written down. That is a different design from a review tutorial and it is the right one for most Barsha Heights families.

Before any of that, two facts about your child's course have to be established, and families frequently know neither. Which board, Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, because the papers are structured differently. And which tier, because both boards tier mathematics and the tier caps the grade. Cambridge runs Core and Extended; Pearson runs Foundation and Higher. The tier is fixed at the final entry deadline, months before the paper is sat, and no amount of good teaching afterwards changes which questions appear in front of your child.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the question, the working and the mark scheme shared on a surface both people can write on. For a student who has already spent an hour in a vehicle, the absence of another journey is not a compromise, and for mathematics specifically a shared digital whiteboard is genuinely better than two people leaning over one exercise book.

A short word on what this page does not contain. There is no claim here that IB Gram is approved or accredited by any board or regulator, because it is not, and no guarantee about a grade, because nobody can honestly offer one. What follows instead is the content split between the two tiers, the structural differences between the two boards, an honest estimate of how long each common repair takes, and the published Dubai market rates with their sources attached so you can check any quote you are given, from us or from anybody else.

The question-style distribution differs enough from Cambridge that a student switching boards mid-course misjudges pacing in their first full paper. programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for A Level mathematics or Higher Level Diploma mathematics. Calculus and kinematics arrive here before anywhere else on a student's timetable, and the content is dense. Late intervention works poorly, which makes this the clearest case on the option block for starting early rather than booking a rescue in the second term.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools that offer it typically restrict entry to students already secure at Extended level, so a student struggling with 0580 Extended and also entered for 0606 usually has a single underlying algebra problem showing up in two places rather than two separate problems.

programmes.name: What the Maths Grade Opens or Closes
programmes.description: The IGCSE mathematics grade is the most commonly specified sixth-form entry requirement in Dubai, for both A Level and the IB Diploma, and the higher mathematics routes at 16 generally assume Extended or Higher tier content as the floor. It also feeds Ministry of Education equivalency for students later applying to UAE universities.
programmes.countryNote: The published British-track equivalency rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Verify the current rules with the Ministry rather than any tutoring site.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-tecom.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics is a set of topic areas that behave very differently under tutoring. These are the ones Barsha Heights students most often need, with where the marks disappear.

subjects.name: Number and the four operations
subjects.description: Standard form, bounds, percentages and reverse percentages, ratio in three parts. Reverse percentage is the single most reliably mishandled topic at either tier: students subtract a percentage rather than dividing by a multiplier, and the error is invisible to them because the answer looks plausible.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: The topic everything else depends on. Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. A student who manipulates hesitantly spends their trigonometry lesson doing algebra badly, which is why a diagnosis almost always lands here whatever the stated complaint was.

subjects.name: Quadratics and the formula
subjects.description: Factorising, completing the square, the quadratic formula and solving by graph. Marks are lost on sign errors inside the formula and on giving one root where the question asks for both. Completing the square is routinely learned as a ritual rather than a method, which breaks as soon as the coefficient of the squared term is not one.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, transformations of graphs. One of the clearest Core-to-Extended boundary topics, so a student moved up a tier mid-course usually meets this with no foundation at all and needs it taught from the start rather than revised.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry at both tiers; the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and three-dimensional work at Extended and Higher. Students lose marks by using right-angled methods on a non-right-angled triangle, and by leaving the calculator in the wrong angle mode for an entire question.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, vector geometry and the four transformations with full descriptions. The marks here sit in the description as much as the construction: a correctly drawn rotation with no centre or direction stated earns a fraction of what it should.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, cumulative frequency and histograms with unequal class widths. Histograms with unequal widths are the standing Extended trap, because frequency density has to be computed and students plot frequency instead, losing the whole question rather than part of it.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar shapes
subjects.description: Areas, volumes, arcs and sectors, and at Extended the area and volume scale factors for similar shapes. Scale factors are where able students lose marks: lengths scale by k, areas by k squared, volumes by k cubed, and the question is usually designed to punish applying the wrong one.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fluency
subjects.description: Exact values, fraction arithmetic, surds where examined, and multiplication without a device. A distinct skill that does not develop by accident and will not show up in a classroom test taken with a calculator on the desk. Where a board examines a non-calculator component, this needs deliberate sessions with the device put away.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Using memory rather than rounding mid-calculation, checking angle mode, reading a value to the precision the question asks for. Premature rounding is a quiet and expensive habit: the method is right, the final answer is outside tolerance, and the student has no idea why the mark was withheld.

subjects.name: Showing working
subjects.description: Not a topic but the largest single recoverable loss on any mathematics paper. Method marks exist and are awarded for intervening steps. Students praised for being quick at mental arithmetic are the most prone to forfeiting them, and the fix is a habit rather than a concept, which makes it the fastest gain available at any point in the course.

subjects.name: Exam pacing
subjects.description: Over-answering early questions and running out of time on the last page is a recurring pattern at both tiers and on both boards. It is diagnosable from a timed script and fixable in a handful of sessions, and it is invisible in untimed homework, which is why it survives until a mock reveals it.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE maths tutor in TECOM is actually hired to do
paragraphs: An IGCSE maths tutor in TECOM, as this works in practice, is one supervised hour a week doing the mathematics the evening did not have room for. Published Dubai market rates for a qualified online subject tutor sit at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and the first session is free and is a timed section from a real paper, marked.

The reason to describe the hour that way rather than as tutoring in general is that it changes the session design, and the wrong design wastes the only hour the week allows. A review tutorial assumes the student has attempted work independently and needs it explained. For a Barsha Heights student who got home at twenty to six and had four subjects to cover, that assumption often fails. The session that works is one where attempts happen inside the hour, under supervision, with immediate correction and the method written out.

There is a diagnostic benefit to that design as well. A tutor watching a student attempt a question sees where the method breaks, which is almost never where the student says it does. Families report that their child cannot do trigonometry; the tutor watches and sees that the trigonometry is fine and the rearranging is not. That distinction is invisible in a marked homework book and obvious within ten minutes of supervised work.

Before the first session, two facts are worth establishing from the school documents. The board, Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, because the papers are structured differently and the pacing differs. And the tier, Core or Extended on Cambridge, Foundation or Higher on Pearson, because the tier determines the grade ceiling and which questions appear. A tutor who does not ask for both in the first message has not started from the right place.

sections.heading: The tier boundary: what Extended contains that Core does not
paragraphs: This is the most consequential table a Year 10 parent can read, and almost nobody publishes it. Both main boards tier mathematics, and the tier caps the grade: a Cambridge Core candidate cannot reach the top grades and neither can a Pearson Foundation candidate, regardless of how well they perform, because the questions that access those grades do not appear on their paper. The tier is fixed at the final entry deadline, months before the exam.

The content difference is specific rather than a matter of difficulty. Extended and Higher contain whole topics that Core and Foundation do not touch at all: function notation with composite and inverse functions, graph transformations, vectors beyond the basics, the sine and cosine rules, histograms with unequal class widths, and the area and volume scale factors for similar shapes. A student moved up a tier in Year 11 has not met any of that, and treating it as revision rather than as new teaching is the standard mistake.

The practical sequence for a family who wants a higher-tier entry runs backwards from the deadline. The school decides on internal evidence, usually at the end of Year 10 or early in Year 11. That evidence is produced in classwork and assessments during that period. So the work that supports a tier change has to happen before the term in which the decision is made, which in practice means Year 10. A request raised in the term the entry is submitted is asking the school to act on evidence that does not exist.

It is worth being blunt about the other direction too. For some students Core or Foundation is the right entry, and a family pushing for a higher tier against the school's judgement can produce a worse grade rather than a better one, because a weaker candidate on a harder paper scores poorly across the whole of it. The useful contribution a tutor makes here is a diagnostic rather than an opinion: a timed section of a higher-tier paper tells you plainly whether the student is close.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1, side by side
paragraphs: Two boards, the same subject name, and enough structural difference that a tutor used only to one will prepare a candidate on the other for the wrong things. If your child has switched schools inside Dubai, which happens constantly in this corridor, they may well have switched boards too, and that is worth two dedicated sessions rather than an assumption.

The clearest difference is the calculator position. Pearson 4MA1 is two written papers of equal weight, two hours each, with a calculator permitted throughout. Cambridge has revised the 0580 structure, including the introduction of a non-calculator component, so a Cambridge candidate may face a paper where the device is unavailable. Non-calculator fluency, which means exact values, fraction arithmetic and multiplication by hand, is a separate teachable skill that does not develop incidentally and will never show up in a classroom test taken with a calculator on the desk.

The second difference is the shape of a paper. The question-style distribution and the ramp from accessible to demanding differ between the boards, which is why a student who switches misjudges pacing on their first full paper and runs out of time on the last page. That is diagnosable from a single timed script and fixable in a handful of sessions, and it has nothing to do with mathematical ability.

Both boards tier, and both tiers have a grade ceiling, so the tier question applies whichever row you are in. And both publish their current specifications online, which is the authority rather than any summary, including this one. Cambridge publishes zone-specific timetables and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so a family planning around a date should always open the live official document rather than trust a restated one.

sections.heading: The topics that cost the most marks, and how long each takes to fix
paragraphs: Mathematics is unusual among IGCSE subjects in that the recurring errors are few, specific and highly diagnosable, which makes a published list genuinely useful rather than generic. The table below gives the topic, the error students actually make, and an honest estimate of how long it takes to fix, because that last column is what a family needs when there are six weeks left and a decision to make.

The fastest fixes are habits rather than concepts. Showing working costs nothing to teach and recovers method marks immediately. Checking the calculator's angle mode takes one session to become automatic. Not rounding mid-calculation is a single instruction repeated until it sticks. These three together frequently account for more lost marks on a script than any content topic, and they are available to any student at any point in the course, including the week before a paper.

The slowest fixes are the foundational ones. Algebraic fluency is weeks of work, not sessions, because it is a reflex rather than a technique. Any student who hesitates over rearranging will keep paying for it in every topic that uses it, which is most of them. That is why a diagnosis so often lands on algebra when the family came in asking about trigonometry: the trigonometry is a symptom and the algebra is the cause.

Between the two sit the higher-tier topics that are simply unfamiliar: functions, transformations, histograms with unequal class widths, scale factors for area and volume. Each is a few sessions of genuine teaching and then secure, which makes them good value late in a course if the student is otherwise sound. A six-week window spent on three unfamiliar higher-tier topics plus the three habits above is a realistic plan. The same window spent trying to rebuild algebra from nothing is not.

sections.heading: Group classes against one-to-one, measured per mark rather than per hour
paragraphs: Dubai has plenty of group tuition and it is cheaper per hour, which makes it look like obvious value. The useful comparison is not cost per hour though; it is cost per mark recovered, and for mathematics specifically the two diverge sharply because mathematics errors are individual. Two students in the same class losing marks for different reasons both receive the explanation aimed at the average of them.

Here are the published numbers, all read in October 2026 and published by other providers. Budget online and university-student tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and beyond, TutorChase quoting AED 270. Centre group classes are typically lower per student and vary by centre. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors. None of those is IB Gram's price list.

The per-mark argument works like this. A group class at a third of a one-to-one rate that addresses your child's actual error for ten minutes of a ninety-minute session has delivered ten minutes of relevant teaching. A one-to-one hour at three times the rate that spends fifty of its sixty minutes on exactly your child's error has delivered five times the relevant teaching for three times the cost. That calculation only works where the error is individual, which in mathematics it almost always is, and it does not work for subjects where a class can usefully cover the same ground together.

Group classes do have genuine advantages we will not argue away. They provide routine, peer company and a fixed commitment, and for a student whose problem is motivation rather than method they can be the better buy. The honest test is whether the child's difficulty is shared with the rest of the class. If the whole set is weak on histograms, a class is efficient. If your child alone cannot rearrange, a class is a waiting room.

sections.heading: Non-calculator work, and why it has to be deliberate
paragraphs: Where a board examines a non-calculator component, the skill it demands is genuinely separate from mathematical understanding, and treating the two as the same thing is how able students lose marks across a whole paper. Cambridge has revised the 0580 structure to include a non-calculator component, so a current Cambridge candidate should establish from the live syllabus whether they face one. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout, which removes the issue for those candidates entirely.

What non-calculator fluency actually consists of is short enough to list: fraction arithmetic without converting to decimals, exact values rather than rounded ones, multiplication and division by hand, recognising common squares and cubes, and manipulating surds where examined. None of that is conceptually difficult. All of it is a reflex that only develops through practice, and a student who has reached Year 10 reaching for a device on every line has not built the reflex.

The diagnostic problem is that this weakness is invisible in ordinary school assessment. A classroom test with calculators permitted tells you nothing about it. A homework task done at a desk with a phone nearby tells you less. The first time most students discover the gap is in a mock, which is late but not fatal, and the fix is sessions with the device genuinely put away rather than sessions where the student is asked not to use it.

The reverse skill matters too, and gets even less attention. Calculator technique is examined: using memory instead of rounding mid-calculation, checking the angle mode before a trigonometry question, and reading an answer to the precision the question asks for rather than the precision the screen offers. Premature rounding is the most expensive of these, because the method is correct, the answer falls outside tolerance, and the student has no idea why the mark was not awarded.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects, the week, and what that means for homework
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. One KHDA requirement bears directly on whether a Year 11 student has time to practise mathematics, and it is almost never connected to tutoring in anything a family reads.

Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA setting the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes are required by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for Arabs and non-Arabs strictly prohibited because of differing curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

Add those to nine or ten IGCSE subjects and the independent study time a mathematics syllabus assumes is largely notional. For a Barsha Heights student with an hour a day in a vehicle on top, the week genuinely does not contain it. When a parent says their child has no time to do past papers, this is usually the literal truth rather than a reframed excuse, and recognising that is what makes the supervised-practice session design the right one.

IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none of those relationships. The reason to set out the framework is that it explains the shape of the problem. A provider who promises to fit three extra hours of mathematics into this week has not looked at the week.

sections.heading: Booking, and the honest limits
paragraphs: Send three things: the board, the tier, and a marked piece of work if you have one. A marked script is worth more than any description, because it shows whether marks went to method, to content, to a calculator habit or to time. The first session is free and is a timed section from a real paper rather than an introduction, and you receive a short written note afterwards splitting the lost marks and estimating what the remaining window allows.

Then tell us when your child is actually home. In Barsha Heights that is usually between a quarter past five and six, depending on the bus route, and the workable slots are 17:30 and 18:00. Those happen to be the most demanded tutoring hours in the Dubai year, with demand peaking in the second term when mocks arrive, so securing one in term one is worth real money even though it costs nothing extra.

Three limits worth stating up front. Availability concentrates, so a second-term request for an 18:00 weekday slot is the hardest thing to staff in the calendar. Some combinations are thin, particularly 0606 Additional Mathematics for a specific weekend time. And if no UAE-based tutor is free for your combination, we will say whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time, and you may decline. No competitor researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

Finally, the format, once more: IB Gram runs no home visits in Dubai and no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the question, the working and the mark scheme on a shared surface. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there, and the same tutor keeps the same student through the change rather than a reshuffle.

faqs.question: Why does my child never finish their maths homework?
faqs.answer: Often because the evening does not contain it. Barsha Heights children travel outward to school and return on multi-stop bus routes between a quarter past five and six, leaving an evening with room for two subjects honestly done rather than four. Mathematics loses out rationally rather than lazily: it needs a desk and a clear head, it cannot be half-done, and it takes the longest of anything on the list. That is why the useful session design here is supervised practice inside the hour rather than a review of work that did not happen.

faqs.question: What does Extended contain that Core does not in IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Whole topics rather than harder versions of the same ones. Function notation with composite and inverse functions, graph transformations, the sine and cosine rules for non-right-angled triangles, vectors beyond basic column form, histograms with unequal class widths, area and volume scale factors for similar shapes, and completing the square. A student moved up a tier in Year 11 has met none of it, so it has to be taught from first principles rather than revised. Confirm the exact content split against the live syllabus document, since boards revise them.

faqs.question: Is a tier move still possible once Year 11 has started in Barsha Heights?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but the sequence runs backwards from the entry deadline and most families raise it too late. Schools decide on internal evidence, usually at the end of Year 10 or early in Year 11, and that evidence is produced in classwork during that period. A request made in the term the entry is submitted asks the school to act on evidence that does not exist. The useful contribution a tutor makes is a diagnostic rather than an argument: a timed section of a higher-tier paper shows plainly whether the student is close.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Enough to change what a tutor should prepare. Pearson 4MA1 is two written papers of equal weight, two hours each, with a calculator permitted throughout, tiered Foundation or Higher. Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core or Extended and has been revised to include a non-calculator component, so a Cambridge candidate may face a paper without a device. The question ramp also differs, which is why students switching boards mid-course misjudge pacing on their first full paper. Check the live specification on each board's own site.

faqs.question: How do I build non-calculator fluency?
faqs.answer: Deliberately, with the device genuinely put away rather than merely discouraged. The skill is short to describe: fraction arithmetic without converting to decimals, exact values rather than rounded ones, multiplication and division by hand, recognising common squares and cubes, and surds where examined. None of it is conceptually hard and all of it is a reflex that only develops through practice. The reason it survives undetected to Year 11 is that a classroom test taken with a calculator on the desk reveals nothing about it.

faqs.question: Which maths errors are quickest to fix before an exam?
faqs.answer: Habits rather than concepts, and they are worth doing first. Showing working recovers method marks immediately and takes one session plus repetition. Checking the calculator's angle mode becomes automatic in a session. Not rounding mid-calculation is one instruction repeated until it sticks. Reverse percentages take one or two sessions. Together these frequently account for more lost marks on a script than any single content topic, and they are available to any student at any point, including the week before a paper.

faqs.question: Which maths topic takes the longest to repair?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fluency, by a wide margin, because it is a reflex rather than a technique and reflexes take weeks rather than sessions. A student who hesitates over rearranging keeps paying for it in every topic that uses it, which is most of them. That is why a diagnosis so often lands on algebra when a family arrived asking about trigonometry: the trigonometry was a symptom. If this is the problem and the exam is six weeks away, the honest plan targets habits and unfamiliar higher-tier topics instead.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether your child's difficulty is shared with the room. If the whole set is weak on histograms, a class covers it efficiently and costs less per hour. If your child alone cannot rearrange an equation, a class is a waiting room in which the explanation is aimed at the average of several different problems. Mathematics errors are unusually individual, which is why the per-hour comparison misleads and the relevant comparison is minutes of teaching aimed at your child's actual error.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 put budget online and university-student tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors. None of those is IB Gram's price.

faqs.question: Is carrying 0606 alongside 0580 Extended a sensible load?
faqs.answer: Only if they are already secure at Extended level, which is usually how schools gate it. Calculus and kinematics arrive in 0606 before anywhere else on a student's timetable and the content is dense, so late intervention works badly. The useful observation is that 0580 Extended and 0606 share an algebraic foundation, so a student struggling in both almost always has one underlying problem showing up twice rather than two separate problems. Treating it that way saves a surprising number of hours.

faqs.question: My child runs out of time on maths papers. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and reasonably quickly, but only from a timed script. The usual cause is over-answering the early accessible questions and then rushing or abandoning the last page, which is invisible in untimed homework and therefore survives until a mock reveals it. Three or four sessions of timed sections to real duration, with the time per question actually recorded, fixes the pattern in most students. It has nothing to do with mathematical ability and a great deal to do with never having practised under a clock.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child sit in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series as the main sitting, with November as the resit route; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson International GCSE runs a May or June window and a November window. One Cambridge detail costs candidates exams: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with different timetables, Cambridge states that using the correct version is essential, and it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your exams officer for the zone.

faqs.question: What time are maths sessions for Barsha Heights families?
faqs.answer: Usually 17:30 or 18:00, set by the bus route rather than by a school bell. Children travelling north to Al Sufouh and the coast have the shortest run and can sometimes manage 17:00; those travelling inland to Al Barsha South are realistically 18:00. Those evening hours are the most demanded tutoring slots in the Dubai year and demand peaks in the second term, so arranging one in term one secures it at no extra cost. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our tower in Barsha Heights?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and we say so plainly rather than letting a family discover it after a call. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the question, the working and the mark scheme on a surface both people can write on, which for mathematics is genuinely better than two people leaning over one exercise book. For a child already in a vehicle for an hour a day, avoiding a fourth journey is most of the argument.

faqs.question: What if you cannot staff the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a date, rather than taking the booking and hoping. Availability concentrates in the second term and in the weeks before a series, and the 18:00 weekday slots that Barsha Heights bus routes produce are the hardest hours in the calendar to staff. Some combinations are thinner still, particularly Additional Mathematics 0606 for a specific weekend time. If no UAE-based tutor is free, we will say whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time and you may decline.

intro.heading: Start with the cheapest thing that works
paragraphs: There is a reasonable chance your child does not need a paid maths tutor yet. Before anything is booked, three cheaper things exist in this community and all of them are routinely skipped. The school's own after-school maths clinic is already inside the fees you pay. Past papers and the school's mark schemes are free. And a single diagnostic hour, bought once, tells you whether the problem is practice, technique or tier, which decides whether you need six hours or sixty.

That order matters because the Dubai market is enormously wide. Published rates in 2026 run from roughly AED 45 an hour for budget and university-student online tutoring up to AED 450 and beyond for subject specialists, with premium named tutors quoted at AED 500 to 650. The same subject, the same syllabus, a tenfold spread. Nothing about a grade-5 Year 10 who has stopped practising requires the top of that range, and plenty of families in The Greens pay it anyway because it was the first number they were quoted.

Where the money genuinely has to be spent is narrower than the marketing suggests. A tier change from Core to Extended is a term of unfamiliar content and needs someone who knows precisely which topics sit beyond the shared core. A target of a grade 8 or 9 needs someone fluent in the mark scheme, because the last two bands are won on method marks and wording rather than on answers. A re-sit against a November deadline needs a plan, not enthusiasm. Those three jobs justify specialist rates. General catch-up usually does not.

The second decision that moves the bill is which syllabus your child is actually on, and most parents in this community cannot name it. Cambridge 0580 and its nine-to-one sibling 0980 sit one paper without a calculator and one with. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics assumes a graphic display calculator and adds an investigation paper, which makes it a different course to teach. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers. A tutor priced for one of these and teaching another wastes the first month.

Everything below is built in that order: the options from free upwards, the tier decision, the syllabus codes, where marks are genuinely lost, what a term buys, and what a re-sit costs in time. Every AED figure is a published Dubai market rate rather than ours, and all IB Gram lessons in the UAE are delivered one-to-one over live video, since home visits are an India-only service.

One more thing worth settling before you spend anything. Ask the school which tier your child is entered for and when that entry closes, because the tier caps the grade and the deadline sits months ahead of the paper. A UAE candidate sits the June series or the November series, and a Cambridge June entry closes in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper; Pearson's November 2026 papers ran to 19 November 2026 on an entry filed earlier in the year. That is the gap most families underestimate. A tutor hired after the entry has closed cannot change a ceiling that was fixed before revision started, and knowing that in Year 10 is worth more than any negotiation over an hourly rate.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics is one subject and a dozen separable skills. These are the topics that actually cost marks in the schools around The Greens, with the reason each one costs them.

subjects.name: Arithmetic without a calculator
subjects.description: Fractions, decimals, standard form and percentage change done by hand under time pressure. Students who met the whole course with a calculator on the desk are fluent in method and slow in execution, and on the Cambridge non-calculator paper slow is the same as wrong.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and simplifying algebraic fractions. It is the skill every other topic depends on, so a weakness here shows up as scattered losses across the whole paper rather than as one identifiable gap.

subjects.name: Sequences and the nth term
subjects.description: Linear, quadratic and, at Extended, cubic and exponential sequences. Students usually recognise the pattern and lose the marks writing the general rule, which is an algebra problem wearing a sequences costume.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry and graphs
subjects.description: Gradients, parallel and perpendicular lines, and sketching quadratics and reciprocals. Marks concentrate in the questions that give a graph and ask for the equation, where a sketch is not enough and the algebra has to be written out.

subjects.name: Functions and transformations
subjects.description: Composite and inverse functions and the transformations of a curve. This is content a Core candidate never meets, which makes it the main cost of moving a student up a tier partway through Year 10 or Year 11.

subjects.name: Mensuration and three-dimensional work
subjects.description: Surface area, volume, arcs, sectors and problems that combine solids. The losses are almost always units and rounding rather than concepts, and both are fixed by habit rather than by teaching.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry at Core; the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and three-dimensional bearings at Extended. The bearings questions are the reliable marks most students drop, because the diagram is never drawn.

subjects.name: Vectors and matrices
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and geometric proof using vector paths. Marks come from writing a route through a diagram in vector form, which is a notation skill rather than a reasoning one and improves quickly with practice.

subjects.name: Probability, including conditional
subjects.description: Tree and Venn diagrams at both tiers, with conditional probability at Extended. Students lose marks by multiplying when the question has removed an item without replacement, which is a reading error that drilling the same question type does not fix.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals and box plots. Histogram frequency density is the single most predictable lost mark in the subject, and it takes about twenty minutes to teach properly.

subjects.name: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
subjects.description: Direct and inverse proportion, compound interest, exponential growth and speed problems. These appear in the four and five-mark problems at the end of a paper, where the mathematics is simple and the extraction of information from the wording is not.

subjects.name: Multi-step problem solving
subjects.description: The long questions carrying four or five marks each, which combine two or three topics and award method marks along the way. Students who abandon these questions lose far more than they realise, since partial working is credited and a blank space is not.

sections.heading: The cheapest honest way to get IGCSE maths help in The Greens
paragraphs: The table below lists every realistic option in ascending order of cost, including the two that cost nothing. It is deliberately unflattering to the expensive end, because the expensive end is what every other page for this query leads with. Read it from the top and stop at the first row that matches your child's actual problem rather than your level of worry.

Two rows deserve emphasis. The school's own after-school clinic is already inside fees you have paid, and in the schools around The Greens it is typically run by the teacher who will mark the mocks. Past papers with the published mark schemes are free from the school and are the single highest-yield activity in Year 11, provided somebody looks at the pattern of errors rather than only the total.

The paid rows separate on a simple question: are you buying repetition or diagnosis? Repetition is a commodity, and the budget end of the Dubai market, advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, supplies it adequately for a Core or Foundation candidate who understands the method. Diagnosis is not a commodity. Identifying that a student is losing eleven marks a paper to histogram frequency density and unit conversion, rather than to a general weakness in statistics, is what the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and upwards is actually for.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that caps the grade
paragraphs: This is the most consequential and least discussed decision in IGCSE mathematics. Cambridge 0580 is tiered: a Core entry makes grades C to G available and an Extended entry makes A* to E available. Pearson 4MA1 does the same thing under different names, with Foundation reaching partway up the scale and Higher reaching the top. The tier is fixed by the school's examination entry, months before the paper, and no amount of revision afterwards raises the ceiling it sets.

The practical consequence is that a parent discovering a Core entry in April is discovering something that cannot be changed for that series. A parent discovering it in September of Year 11 still has time, and the conversation with the school is specific rather than general: here is the mark my child produced on a recent Extended paper, here are the topics beyond the shared core they have not yet met, is there a route to moving the entry.

Moving up costs roughly a term of unfamiliar content. Functions and transformations, vectors, conditional probability and the harder algebraic work sit outside the Core syllabus entirely, so the student is not revising, they are learning. That is real work and it is the one scenario in IGCSE mathematics where a specialist rate is straightforwardly justified, because the tutor needs to know exactly which topics the Core course omitted.

The reverse case is just as real and nobody sells it. A student entered for Extended who is reliably producing marks in the lower bands may be better served by consolidating what the entry already allows than by chasing content they will not reach. That conversation belongs with the school, and a tutor's job in it is to supply evidence from timed papers rather than an opinion.

sections.heading: Which maths syllabus you are actually paying for
paragraphs: Four mathematics codes are sat at sixteen in the schools around The Greens, and they ask for different things. A tutor who teaches one well and the others vaguely will spend the first month coaching the wrong paper structure, which is a cost whatever the hourly rate. The code is printed on the examination entry, and asking for it is a two-minute job that removes the most avoidable mismatch in this market.

Cambridge 0580 and 0980 are the same course reported on different grade scales, nine to one on 0980 and A* to G on 0580. Both sit one paper without a calculator and one with, on the syllabus examined from 2025. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics is a genuinely different animal: it assumes a graphic display calculator and adds an investigation paper, so a share of the grade comes from exploring an unfamiliar problem. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both of its two-hour papers.

The investigation paper on 0607 is where mispricing bites hardest. A tutor whose experience is entirely 0580 has never taught that component, and it cannot be improvised from general mathematical ability because it is assessed on process. Families in the Emirates Living cluster whose children are heading for the Diploma are disproportionately on 0607, so this is a local rather than a theoretical risk.

Verify every code on the board's own site rather than on a tutoring page, this one included. Cambridge publishes syllabuses at cambridgeinternational.org and Pearson at qualifications.pearson.com, and both revise specifications on a published cycle. Cambridge also allocates each examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, and what that costs to fix
paragraphs: Marks in IGCSE mathematics are lost in predictable places, and the price of fixing each one varies by an order of magnitude. Histogram frequency density takes about twenty minutes to teach and recurs in almost every series. Unit conversion and rounding errors in mensuration are habits rather than gaps and are fixed by checking working aloud for three sessions. Neither needs a specialist and both are worth more marks than most families expect.

A second group costs more. Algebraic fluency is the substrate of the whole paper, so a weakness there appears as scattered losses rather than a single identifiable gap, and rebuilding it takes weeks of short daily practice rather than hours of explanation. On the Cambridge non-calculator paper this is the dominant cost, because students who met the course with a calculator permanently available have method without execution.

A third group is reading rather than mathematics. The four and five-mark problems at the end of a paper combine two or three topics and award method marks along the way, and the commonest error is abandoning them. A student who writes the first two steps of a five-mark question earns marks a blank space does not, and teaching that habit is cheap, fast and worth more than another topic.

The diagnostic hour exists to tell you which of those three groups you are dealing with. A general impression that a child is weak at statistics is not a diagnosis and cannot be priced. Eleven marks lost across frequency density, cumulative frequency reading and grouped-data means can be fixed in two sessions. That is the difference between a six-hour plan and a sixty-hour one, and it is why the cheapest purchase on this page is the first one.

sections.heading: What a term of tutoring buys, and what it does not
paragraphs: A term is roughly twelve weeks, so a weekly hour is twelve sessions. At the Dubai market's middle band of AED 150 to 300 an hour that is about AED 1,800 to 3,600 for the term, and at specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 it is AED 2,400 to 5,400. Those are the real numbers a family should hold in mind, because an hourly figure makes a decision feel smaller than it is.

Twelve sessions, used well, reliably does three things. It clears two or three named topics completely. It builds the habit of timed paper practice, which most students will not do unsupervised. And it produces evidence about the tier, which is the one decision with a hard deadline attached. That is a good return and it is achievable at the middle of the market rather than the top.

What twelve sessions will not do is rebuild two years of missing algebra, and no honest provider should imply otherwise. A Year 11 producing grade-2 marks on Extended papers is not a tutoring problem of one term's size; that situation needs a conversation with the school about the tier first and a longer plan second. Buying a term of specialist hours against it is the most expensive way to arrive at the same conclusion.

Nobody can promise a particular grade from a particular number of sessions, and a provider who does should be questioned rather than hired. What twelve sessions can promise is that the student will have sat complete papers under timed conditions, had them marked against the published criteria, and been told plainly which topics still cost marks.

sections.heading: Group, centre or one-to-one: the value question here
paragraphs: Group classes are genuinely cheaper per student, and in the Al Sufouh and Al Barsha belt within reach of The Greens they are genuinely available. The question is not price but fit. A group works when three or four students are weak on the same topics and at roughly the same level, because the teaching is identical for all of them and the discussion between students adds something a one-to-one session does not.

A group fails in a specific and predictable way. One student is a tier behind the others, or has a different gap, and the pace is set by the median. That student attends for a term, feels busy, and produces the same marks in the mocks. Parents rarely find out until the mock results arrive, because attendance and effort both look fine from outside.

Tuition centres with premises are a different legal animal from an individual tutor in the UAE, which is worth knowing when you compare them. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An individual providing private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit instead.

One-to-one online sits between the two on price and above both on precision, because the hour is spent on your child's error pattern rather than on the group's. For a family in The Greens it also avoids the travel premium entirely. IB Gram does not run a centre in Dubai and does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics 0606 and the step into post-16 maths
paragraphs: Additional Mathematics is the most under-supported qualification in this market. It is taken alongside 0580 or 0607 by top sets in Year 11, it introduces calculus, logarithms and binomial expansion, and it is frequently taught in whatever curriculum time is left over. Students are not behind on it, because nobody has seen it before, which makes a short block of support unusually efficient.

Its value is forward-looking. A student who has met differentiation and integration at sixteen begins A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches with the first term already familiar, and the first term is where most post-16 mathematics attrition happens. Pearson's Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 plays the same role on the Edexcel route.

The cost case is straightforward. A block of six to eight sessions in Year 11 on 0606 content costs less than a term of remedial work in Year 12, and it is bought at a quieter point in the calendar. For Greens families whose children are heading for engineering, mathematics or physics, this is the cheapest hedge available against a difficult first Diploma or A Level year.

The caution is that 0606 should not be bought as a status purchase. A student who is not secure on Extended 0580 content gains nothing from calculus a year early and loses time they needed for the main qualification. The diagnostic question is whether the 0580 Extended marks are already in the top two bands; if they are not, the money belongs on 0580.

sections.heading: Re-sits, the November option and private candidates
paragraphs: A missed grade is not a lost year, and the published calendars show why. Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May and June and again in November each year. Either board therefore offers a second attempt within months rather than a year.

The table below lays out what the published dates mean in practice for the two series a UAE candidate can actually sit. Pearson's completed November 2025 series is the cleanest illustration, because every date in it is settled: the papers ran in late October and November and the grades reached students on 22 January 2026, a wait of just over two months. Its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026 on the same pattern. On the Cambridge side, June entries close in the spring and results follow in August, while the November series exists as the second attempt, with grades arriving the following January.

Entering as a private candidate rather than through the school is possible and adds administration rather than difficulty. The centre handles the entry, the fee is set by the centre and the board rather than by a tutor, and the deadlines are earlier than families expect. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the right habit is to work from the live official timetable rather than from a restated date on any tutoring page, including this one.

The planning point for a Greens family is the gap between the last paper and the result. Three to five months is normal. A student re-sitting in November to strengthen a post-16 application needs that arithmetic in front of them in September, not in January, because the application deadline rarely moves to accommodate it.

sections.heading: What to stop paying for
paragraphs: Supervised homework. A tutor who spends the hour watching your child complete the work the school set is being paid teaching rates for invigilation. It feels productive because the homework gets done, and it produces no change in a mock mark. If three consecutive sessions have no agenda beyond the current homework, the arrangement has drifted and should either be redirected or stopped.

A standing weekly hour that outlived its purpose. The block that fixed two topics in October frequently continues until May because cancelling feels like giving up. Each term is worth a direct question: which two topics will the next twelve sessions clear, and what evidence says they are still weak. If the answer is vague, the money is buying reassurance rather than marks.

The travel premium. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and monthly packages of four two-hour visits have been advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. At the same qualification level, online rates sit lower. For a household in The Greens whose usable weekday window runs from about four o'clock to half past seven, that premium costs evening minutes as well as dirhams.

And anything that looks like a guaranteed outcome. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any page that promises one is either describing a refund policy it has not published or making a claim it cannot stand behind. What can be promised is the process: a diagnostic first, named topics, timed papers, and an honest answer when tutoring is not the right purchase.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to get IGCSE maths help in The Greens?
faqs.answer: In order: the school's own after-school maths clinic, which is already inside your fees and usually run by the teacher who marks the mocks; past papers with the published mark schemes, which cost nothing; and then a single diagnostic hour to find out whether anything more is needed. Only after those three does paid weekly tutoring make sense. The budget end of the Dubai market is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour and is adequate for repetition at Core or Foundation tier.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A weekly hour is four or five sessions a month. On published 2026 Dubai rates that is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, and AED 1,000 to beyond AED 2,000 for exam-year specialist support according to Bestimate's Dubai cost table. In-home packages of four two-hour visits have been advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month. None of these is an IB Gram price; they are market observations for comparison.

faqs.question: Does a tuition-centre group class in Al Barsha actually save money on IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, and in the Al Sufouh and Al Barsha belt near The Greens groups are genuinely available. The saving is real when three or four students are weak on the same topics at the same tier, since the teaching is identical for all of them. It disappears when one student is a tier behind or has a different gap, because the pace follows the median and that student produces the same mock marks after a full term of attendance.

faqs.question: Is my child entered for Core or Extended IGCSE maths, and does it change the fee?
faqs.answer: The tier is on the school's examination entry and it changes both the grade available and the work required. Cambridge Core makes grades C to G available and Extended makes A* to E available; Pearson Foundation and Higher do the same under different names. Rates do not differ by tier, but hours do: moving a student up a tier means teaching functions, vectors and conditional probability from scratch, which is a term of new content rather than revision.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths syllabus is my child on: 0580, 0607 or 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Check the examination entry rather than the prospectus. Cambridge 0580, and its nine-to-one sibling 0980, sit one paper without a calculator and one with. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics assumes a graphic display calculator and adds an investigation paper, which makes it a different course to teach and is common among students heading into the Diploma. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both two-hour papers. Verify any code at cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com.

faqs.question: Can a tutor move my child from a grade 5 to a grade 7 in IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: No tutor can promise a grade, and treat any provider who does as a reason to ask harder questions. What is realistic depends on the diagnosis. A grade 5 produced by scattered careless losses and abandoned long questions often moves with a term of timed practice and a habit change. A grade 5 produced by missing algebraic foundations is a longer job, and if the entry is Core then the ceiling is fixed regardless. The diagnostic session is what tells you which you have.

faqs.question: How many hours of IGCSE maths tutoring does a Year 11 usually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families buy. Twelve sessions across a term reliably clears two or three named topics, establishes timed paper practice and produces evidence about the tier, which is a good return at the middle of the market. Students carrying several gaps need a weekly hour across the year. Students who simply stopped practising often need a six-session block and nothing more. The difference is identified in one diagnostic hour, which is why that purchase comes first.

faqs.question: Is Additional Maths 0606 worth paying for alongside IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: It is, if the main qualification is already secure in the top two bands. Nobody is behind on 0606 because nobody has seen calculus, logarithms or binomial expansion before, so a block of six to eight sessions is unusually efficient and it makes the first term of A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches familiar rather than new. If Extended 0580 marks are not yet strong, the same money belongs on 0580 instead.

faqs.question: Do we pay more for a tutor who knows both Cambridge and Edexcel maths?
faqs.answer: Not usually, and breadth is less valuable here than it sounds. Your child sits one syllabus, so what matters is depth on that one: how the mark scheme words method marks, what the non-calculator paper assumes, whether an investigation paper is part of the course. A tutor who names your code and says when they last taught it is worth more than one who lists every board. Breadth becomes useful only if siblings are on different routes.

faqs.question: Is it better value to start IGCSE maths tutoring in Year 10 rather than Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is better value for two reasons that have nothing to do with rates. The tier decision is still open, so evidence from timed papers can influence a decision that later becomes fixed at the entry deadline. And foundational algebraic fluency can still be rebuilt through short regular practice, which stops being possible once the calendar is dominated by mocks and revision. Year 11 support is narrower work bought at a busier point in the tutoring year.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE maths re-sit cost a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Entry fees are set by the examination centre and the board rather than by a tutor, so ask the centre directly. The cost that surprises families is time rather than money. In the UAE a re-sit means the November series, or the following June, and both close their entries months before the papers. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and its November 2026 papers finished on 19 November 2026 on the same timetable pattern. A Cambridge June re-sit returns a grade in August. Two to five months from last paper to usable result is normal, so decide the re-sit route before results day rather than after it.

faqs.question: Does a calculator-paper weakness need different tutoring from a non-calculator one?
faqs.answer: Yes, and conflating them is a common waste. On the Cambridge syllabus examined from 2025 one paper is sat without a calculator, and weakness there is about execution: exact values, surds, fractions and arithmetic under time pressure, rebuilt by short daily practice rather than explanation. Calculator-paper weakness is usually about reading the question and interpreting output. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout, so this split does not apply on that route at all.

faqs.question: What should we stop paying for in IGCSE maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Supervised homework, first of all: a tutor watching your child finish school-set work is being paid teaching rates for invigilation. Second, a weekly hour that outlived the two topics it was bought to fix. Third, the in-home travel premium, quoted in Dubai from about AED 180 to 500 an hour, which buys transport rather than teaching. A useful rule is to ask each term which two topics the next twelve sessions will clear, and to stop if the answer is vague.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE maths rates in The Greens different from the rest of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Hourly rates barely vary by community, because the market is emirate-wide and most delivery is online. What varies is what is already available free. The Greens and The Views share school clinic timetables, the Al Sufouh belt has real group classes within reach, and families in The Springs often have siblings a year apart on the same syllabus. Checking those first is where the saving actually sits, rather than in negotiating a lower hourly figure.

faqs.question: Does the price of IGCSE maths tutoring include past-paper marking?
faqs.answer: Ask, because it varies and it matters more than the rate. Marking a complete paper properly against the published scheme takes real time outside the session, and a provider who does it is giving you the diagnosis that justifies their rate. One who only discusses answers in the hour is selling something cheaper than it looks. Boards own their papers and mark schemes, so those are referenced and linked from cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than redistributed.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-lakes.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE mathematics by specification rather than by subject name. In a trial lesson, ask one to name a topic that appears on Extended papers and not on Core. A tutor who answers immediately has taught the specification; one who talks about confidence has not.

intro.heading: Four specifications, one subject name, and the question you are really asking
paragraphs: Answer the question honestly: there probably is somebody within a short drive of The Lakes who teaches mathematics, and there is a decent chance they do not teach the specification your child is entered for. 'IGCSE maths' names at least four courses in Dubai schools. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core papers graded C to G and Extended papers graded A* to E. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 splits into a Foundation tier capped at grade 5 and a Higher tier running 9 down to 4 with an allowed 3. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is a fifth thing again.

Those are not difficulty settings on one course. They are different content lists with different papers and different ceilings. Surds, algebraic fractions, function notation, the sine and cosine rules, vectors, histograms with unequal class widths and the gradient-function work all sit on Extended and Higher and not on Core or Foundation. A tutor teaching the wrong one of those pairs is either covering material that will never be examined, or leaving out a quarter of what will be.

That is why the supply question in Emirates Living is sharper for mathematics than for most subjects. Within fifteen minutes of Deema or Hattan there are tutors who can teach mathematics; the set who have taught Pearson 4MA1 Higher papers recently, know which topics the non-calculator paper favours, and can mark to the board's method-mark conventions, is considerably smaller. Hiring by distance means hiring from the first set and hoping.

So the delivery position, stated plainly because the search phrase points the other way. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service offered only in India, and nobody arrives at a Lakes address under any arrangement sold here. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper open on a shared screen and the student's working annotated as it happens. The in-home market exists in Dubai and is published at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against AED 150 to AED 300 online for comparable credentials.

What follows is the detail a maths page should contain and almost none of them do. Which papers each specification sits and what the calculator rules are. Which topics are tier-restricted, so you can tell whether your child is being taught the right list. Where marks are actually lost, which is rarely where families assume. What a grade 9 or an A* asks for beyond correct answers. What the market charges and whether the top of the band is worth it for one subject. And a twenty-minute method for checking a tutor before you pay them anything.

One framing note before any of that. Mathematics is the subject where a tutoring mistake is cheapest to make and most expensive to discover. A history tutor working slightly off-syllabus still teaches a student to argue from evidence. A maths tutor teaching the wrong tier is teaching content that cannot be examined, and the student's confidence rises while their mark does not, because practice on the wrong question types feels like progress. The way to avoid that is not to find a better tutor; it is to start from the entry sheet, agree a named topic strand, and check the mark on it after six sessions rather than after a mock.
