dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-lakes.programmesIntro: Mathematics is the subject that gates the most routes at 16, so the sequence around it matters. Here are the four stages a Lakes family plans across and what mathematics does at each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Tiered into Core and Extended, with Core papers graded C to G and Extended papers graded A* to E. The current syllabus examines each tier with two papers, one non-calculator and one calculator, so paper structure differs from cohorts entered under earlier versions. Extended carries additional content including surds, functions, the sine and cosine rules, vectors and the gradient-function work.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone version of the timetable must be used, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Ask your school's examinations officer for the zone and the syllabus year your child is entered against, because both change what the revision plan should look like.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Two written papers of equal weight, tiered into Foundation and Higher, graded 9 to 1. Foundation caps at grade 5; Higher runs from 9 down to 4 with an allowed 3 below that. Calculators are permitted in both papers, which changes the balance of skills compared with a specification that includes a non-calculator paper. Higher tier adds surds, functions, vectors and gradient-function work.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs May/June and November series and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. Several schools in the Al Barsha corridor enter Pearson for mathematics while using Cambridge for the sciences.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics and Pearson Further Pure
programmes.description: Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics and Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics are taken alongside the main qualification by students heading for A Level or Higher Level mathematics. Both cover material that overlaps the beginning of a post-16 course, including calculus and more advanced trigonometry, and both are graded separately from the main maths grade.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai these are offered by some schools and not others, and they are the clearest signal that a student is being prepared for Higher Level or A Level mathematics rather than simply finishing IGCSE. A student who has sat one arrives in Year 12 with a genuine advantage; a student who has not is not disadvantaged, provided the transition is planned.

programmes.name: A Level, IB Higher Level and the step up
programmes.description: A Level Mathematics and IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches both assume algebraic fluency that IGCSE only partly tests. The commonest failure in Year 12 is not new content but unpractised manipulation - rearranging, factorising, handling surds and indices without a calculator - which is exactly the material on the Extended and Higher tiers.
programmes.countryNote: A Lakes student intending Higher Level Analysis and Approaches or A Level Mathematics should be on Extended or Higher tier, and should expect a bridging block over the summer. Market rates for that bridging work sit at the specialist band of AED 200 to AED 450 and above, which is a reason to get the tier right in Year 10 rather than repair it at 17.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-lakes.subjectsIntro: The specifications first, then the subjects where mathematics is the limiting factor rather than the subject itself. Both matter when deciding where a single tutoring hour should go.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Extended
subjects.description: The tier that keeps post-16 mathematics open. Carries surds, algebraic fractions, function notation, the sine and cosine rules, three-dimensional trigonometry, vectors, histograms with unequal class widths and gradient-function work. Most losses sit in the multi-step questions at the end of the calculator paper and in unshown working on the non-calculator one.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Core
subjects.description: A complete course with a hard ceiling at grade C, and a sound entry for a student who needs a secure pass rather than a top grade. The tutoring aim here is reliability: arithmetic without slips, standard procedures executed under time, and the question types that recur on every paper. Tier-change conversations belong in Year 10.

subjects.name: Pearson 4MA1 Higher
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers with calculators permitted in both, which shifts the emphasis toward problem interpretation rather than hand computation. Higher tier adds surds, functions, vectors and gradient-function work. Students lose marks by writing calculator output without the method that produced it.

subjects.name: Pearson 4MA1 Foundation
subjects.description: Capped at grade 5, which is below many sixth-form conditions, so the tier decision has consequences beyond the grade itself. The efficient work is accuracy and question-type recognition rather than coverage, and the honest conversation is whether a move to Higher is viable before the entry deadline.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: An extra qualification covering material that overlaps the start of A Level and IB Higher Level mathematics, including calculus and extended trigonometry. Students sitting it need tutoring that treats it as a post-16 course rather than as harder IGCSE, which is a different teaching register entirely.

subjects.name: Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Pearson's equivalent extension, again graded separately. Offered by some Dubai schools and not others. A student taking it is being prepared for a mathematical route at 18, and the tutoring should be aimed at the harder manipulation that a post-16 course will assume on day one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject where weak mathematics shows up first. Rearranging equations, handling standard form, reading gradients from graphs and managing units are maths skills marked in a physics paper. A student losing physics marks on calculation is often best helped by two sessions of algebra rather than more physics content.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations, concentration and percentage yield are arithmetic under pressure, and the losses are proportion and unit errors rather than chemistry. Students who recite equations and misplace a factor of ten are telling you that the mathematics, not the chemistry, needs the hour.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Ratio analysis, break-even, index numbers and percentage change carry marks in both subjects and are routinely dropped by students who can discuss the concepts fluently. Diagram accuracy in economics is also a mathematical skill: axes labelled, shifts drawn properly, intersections read.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Binary, hexadecimal, logic and trace tables are mathematical in character, and the board's pseudocode conventions are a notation to learn rather than a programming skill. A student who codes well in a real language can still lose marks on paper for precisely this reason.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-lakes.regionsIntro: The specification a child is entered for depends on the school, and the school depends on which direction they travel in the morning. These notes describe the mathematics picture around Emirates Living.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Six clusters whose teenagers mostly sit IGCSE outside the community. One street can contain a Cambridge Extended candidate and a Pearson Higher candidate, which is why a shared tutor rarely works for two neighbours.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Emirates International School Meadows runs the IB continuum, so Meadows students more often meet criterion-marked MYP mathematics in Standard or Extended streams than an IGCSE tiered paper.

sections.heading: Does anyone near The Lakes know your child's maths specification?
paragraphs: This is the question the search phrase is really asking, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. Within a short drive of Emirates Living there are tutors who teach mathematics. The subset who have recently taught the specification and tier your child is entered for - who know which topics sit on Extended and not on Core, how the current Cambridge paper structure splits between non-calculator and calculator work, and how Pearson's method marks are awarded - is much smaller than the subset who teach maths.

You can test the claim yourself in one question. Ask a prospective tutor to name three topics that appear on Extended papers and not on Core, or on Higher and not on Foundation. The answer should arrive immediately and should include something like surds, function notation and the sine or cosine rule. A tutor who begins talking about building confidence has told you they have not taught the specification, which is not a character judgement but is decisive information.

The reason this matters more in mathematics than elsewhere is the tier ceiling. Cambridge Core papers are graded C to G and Extended run A* to E. Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5 while Higher runs 9 down to 4 with an allowed 3. A tutor teaching Extended content to a Core candidate is wasting the hour; a tutor teaching Core content to an Extended candidate is leaving a quarter of the examinable material untouched. Either error is invisible until a mock paper, by which point two terms have gone.

What online delivery changes is only which set you hire from. The tutor is chosen because they teach 4MA1 Higher, not because they live near Ghadeer, and the lesson begins when the student sits down rather than when a car finds the gate. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The in-home market in Dubai is published at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, and this page prints those figures rather than avoiding them.

sections.heading: The four papers your child might actually be sitting
paragraphs: Mathematics is the IGCSE subject where paper structure differs most between boards and between syllabus years, and getting it wrong wastes revision time in a way that is hard to recover. Cambridge 0580's current syllabus examines each tier with two papers, one non-calculator and one calculator, which is a change from the arrangement earlier cohorts sat. Pearson 4MA1 examines two equally weighted papers with calculators permitted in both. That single difference reshapes what a revision plan should prioritise.

Think about what it means practically. A Cambridge candidate under the current syllabus has to be fluent without a calculator - exact surd values, index manipulation, fraction arithmetic, standard trigonometric values - because an entire paper depends on it. A Pearson candidate can use a calculator throughout, so the marks shift toward interpreting the question correctly and recording method, and the common failure is writing down a calculator output with no visible steps behind it.

Cambridge's administration adds one more variable. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's examinations officer for the zone and build the revision calendar from that timetable, not from a version found online.

The table below sets out the four common routes with the facts that are stable across syllabus years - tier, grade range, calculator position and what each implies for tutoring. Confirm paper durations and mark totals against the current syllabus document for your child's cohort on the board's own site; we reference those documents and link to them rather than reproducing them, because they are the boards' copyright and because they are revised.

sections.heading: Which topics are tier-restricted, and how to check you are being taught the right list
paragraphs: Here is the practical test of whether a tutor is teaching the right course. Both boards restrict a substantial block of content to the upper tier, and the restricted block is consistent enough to be usable as a checklist. If your child is an Extended or Higher candidate and has never met function notation, surds or the sine rule, somebody is teaching the lower list. If they are a Core or Foundation candidate and spending evenings on vectors, somebody is teaching the upper one.

The upper-tier block covers, broadly: surds and exact values; algebraic fractions and harder rearrangement; function notation, including composite and inverse functions; trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, meaning the sine and cosine rules and work in three dimensions; vectors as column quantities with magnitude; histograms with unequal class widths and cumulative frequency; and the gradient-function work that leads into calculus. None of that appears on a Core or Foundation paper.

The lower-tier content is not a reduced version of the same questions either, which is the second common error. A Core paper asks different question types, with more structure given and fewer multi-step chains, so a Core candidate drilled on Extended questions performs worse rather than better - the practice does not resemble what they will sit. Matching the practice to the paper is most of what good mathematics tutoring is.

Use the table as a conversation with your child rather than with a tutor. Go through the rows and ask whether each has appeared in class this year. The gaps you find are either tier-appropriate, in which case nothing is wrong, or they are a genuine coverage problem that needs raising with the school before it needs tutoring. Either outcome is worth the fifteen minutes, and both are cheaper than six weeks of the wrong lessons.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Not where families think. The dominant loss is not wrong answers; it is right answers with no visible route to them. Both boards award method marks, and a correct final answer with no working earns fewer marks than a wrong final answer with a sound method shown. Students who have learned to compute mentally lose marks steadily and invisibly for two years, and the fix is a habit rather than knowledge.

The second loss is the end of each paper. Marks are not distributed evenly: the last few questions carry multi-step chains where a student must choose an approach, carry a result forward and finish. Students who have only practised single-step questions reliably stall at the second step, and the three or four marks per question add up to a grade. Practising the last page of past papers specifically, rather than working forward from the first, is the single most efficient revision change available.

The third is unit and form errors: an answer given to the wrong degree of accuracy, a length given where an area was asked for, a probability written as a percentage greater than one hundred, a decimal where an exact value was required. Each is one mark and they recur across a paper. A student losing six marks this way across two papers is losing most of a grade boundary on something that takes two sessions to correct.

The fourth is time. Both boards' papers reward a student who abandons a stuck question and returns to it, and punish one who spends eleven minutes on a four-mark question out of stubbornness. Timed practice teaches this and nothing else does; discussion of time management in the abstract changes no behaviour. It is also why a ninety-minute session with a fresh student on a Friday afternoon is worth more than an hour at 18:30 after a bus from Al Barsha.

sections.heading: Calculators, formula provision and the things nobody teaches
paragraphs: Two mechanical matters decide more marks than their profile suggests. The first is the calculator: which model the school requires, whether the student can use its statistical and fraction functions fluently, and whether they can produce exact forms where the paper demands them. A student who owns the right calculator and uses a tenth of it is giving away marks on every paper where speed matters. Two sessions of calculator fluency is among the cheapest interventions available.

Where a specification includes a non-calculator paper, as Cambridge 0580's current syllabus does, the inverse problem appears. Students who have relied on a calculator for two years cannot handle surds, index laws, fraction arithmetic or exact trigonometric values at speed, and an entire paper is built on those skills. Short, frequent drill - thirty minutes twice a week rather than an hour once - is the format that produces fluency, because fluency is about retrieval speed rather than understanding.

The second mechanical matter is formula provision. Each specification states which formulae are given in the examination and which must be recalled, and students routinely memorise the given ones and fail to memorise the rest. Check the current syllabus document for your child's cohort rather than relying on what an older sibling remembers, because provision is revised. Then build the recall list explicitly - it is usually a single sheet, and a single sheet is a weekend's work rather than a term's.

One boundary to state while we are on documents. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them, cite the official address and link out; we do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads. A provider offering you a pack of mark schemes is distributing someone else's copyright material, and for unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure for the student. Official past material comes through your school's examinations officer.

sections.heading: What a grade 9 or an A* actually asks for
paragraphs: The top band is not the same subject played faster. Reaching the highest grades on either board requires three things that are rarely taught explicitly. First, complete accuracy on the routine material, because at that level a dropped sign is the difference between bands rather than an irritation. Second, the ability to begin an unstructured multi-step question without a prompt - choosing an approach rather than executing a given one. Third, fluency without a calculator, which carries into every post-16 course.

A student sitting at a solid 6 or a B who wants the top grade is therefore buying something different from a student moving from a 4 to a 6. The latter is usually a technique purchase: command of question types, visible method, accuracy, time. The former is a selection-and-start purchase, and it needs harder questions, more open ones, and a tutor willing to leave the student stuck for two minutes rather than rescuing them. That is a specific teaching skill and worth asking about.

It is also the most expensive grade to buy, which is worth knowing before committing. Moving two grades in the middle of the range is achievable in a term of well-aimed weekly work. Moving from a 6 to a 9 generally takes longer, costs more and succeeds less often, because the marks at the top of the paper are the ones designed to separate. If the household budget is limited and another subject sits two grades below target, the other subject is the better purchase.

There are no published grade boundaries on this page, and there will not be. Boundaries are set per series by the board and published by them, and they move; reproducing them here would be both a copyright matter and misleading. Your school's examinations officer can discuss historical boundaries in context, which is the right place for that conversation because the context - the paper, the cohort, the series - is what makes a boundary meaningful.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor costs in this market, and whether the top band is worth it
paragraphs: Start at the specialist end, because that is where the question actually sits for a single subject. A 2026 Dubai rate study places examination-year specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above; one agency publishes AED 270 an hour for specialist work and one premium provider publishes AED 650. Below that, the qualified-subject-tutor band runs AED 150 to AED 300, with one agency listing AED 150 specifically for IGCSE support against AED 200 for IB. Platform rates for university-student tutors start around AED 33 to AED 65.

So is the specialist band worth it for one IGCSE mathematics grade? Sometimes, and the test is specific. Pay the specialist rate when the work requires somebody who has taught the tier recently and marks to the board's conventions - a 6 to a 9 attempt, a tier-change decision, or a Pearson Higher candidate whose method marks are being lost systematically. Pay the qualified-tutor rate for everything else, which is most cases, including the common and valuable move from a 4 to a 6.

Do not pay the premium rate for drill. Non-calculator fluency, times-table-level retrieval and recurring question types are taught perfectly well at the lower end of the qualified band, and they are exactly the work that benefits from frequency rather than seniority. A household spending AED 450 an hour on surds practice is buying a seniority it is not using. Splitting the work - specialist hours for diagnosis and hard questions, cheaper hours for drill - is the efficient structure and almost nobody suggests it.

Two notes on the figures. Each is another provider's published rate or a published rate study, read in October 2026, and attributed in the table so you can open the source and check. And none of them is an IB Gram price: we quote after the free trial lesson, against the specification, the tier and the diagnosis, with no package to buy. We state no VAT position, because the UAE treatment of tuition fees is a Federal Tax Authority matter - ask any provider directly and keep the answer.

sections.heading: Checking a maths tutor in twenty minutes
paragraphs: You do not need to be a mathematician to assess one, and twenty minutes is enough. Open a past paper from your child's own specification and tier at the last page. Ask the tutor to talk through the final question as if teaching it. You are listening for three things: whether they identify what the question is really testing, whether they say out loud where a student would typically lose a mark, and whether they show the working rather than announce the answer.

Then ask the specification question. Name three topics on Extended and not on Core, or on Higher and not on Foundation. Then ask which formulae are given in the examination for this specification and which must be recalled. A tutor who has taught the course answers both quickly. A tutor who has not will generalise, and the generalisation is the answer you needed.

Third, ask what they would set between lessons and how it would be marked. The correct answer involves written work, returned with method marks identified rather than ticks and crosses. A tutor who sets nothing is selling contact time, and contact time without a feedback cycle does not move a mathematics grade - which is why two shorter sessions with work in between frequently outperform one longer session without.

Finally, ask the two administrative questions. What is their permit position - the UAE private tuition work permit is issued by MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free of charge for two years, with a stated two-working-day processing time, so there is no reason not to hold one. And where are they based, because a tutor teaching into Gulf Standard Time from elsewhere is perfectly workable but you should know before you book rather than afterwards.

sections.heading: Starting from The Lakes, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Send four things: the school, the year, the specification code with its tier, and a photograph of one marked piece of mathematics - ideally a mock paper rather than a homework sheet. The marked paper tells us whether the losses are method marks, accuracy, multi-step chains or genuine coverage gaps, and those four diagnoses need four different first lessons. We come back with a tutor who teaches that code at that tier and a proposed focus for the first three sessions.

The trial lesson is free, covers one subject, takes no card details, and is spent on a real past question rather than on an assessment questionnaire. You are judging whether the tutor's diagnosis matches the marked paper in front of you. If it does not, say so and we will propose someone else; if it does, the focus and the review point get written down before the second lesson.

The availability limit is narrower in mathematics than families expect, because the specification and tier combination narrows the pool. Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher match quickly. A Core or Foundation candidate who needs a tutor comfortable teaching to a capped tier, or a student sitting 0606 or 4PM1 alongside the main qualification, can take longer, and the tutor may be based outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time. We say which, and from where, first.

What we will not claim: no grade promise, no improvement figure, no statistic about past students without the number, the date and the method. No approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, because IB Gram holds none of them. No UAE office, because there isn't one. No tutor described as an examiner without current evidence. And no board material supplied as a download, because it is not ours to distribute.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a maths tutor actually knows my child's specification?
faqs.answer: Ask two questions and listen for speed. First, name three topics that appear on Extended papers and not on Core, or on Higher and not on Foundation - the answer should include something like surds, function notation and the sine or cosine rule, and it should arrive immediately. Second, which formulae are given in the examination for this specification and which must be recalled. A tutor who has taught the course answers both quickly. One who talks about building confidence instead has told you what you needed to know.

faqs.question: Is there a maths tutor in The Lakes who teaches Cambridge 0580 Extended?
faqs.answer: There are maths tutors within a short drive of Emirates Living; whether one of them has recently taught 0580 Extended, knows the current non-calculator and calculator paper split and marks to Cambridge's method-mark conventions is a much narrower question. That is why we match on the code and tier rather than on distance, and why lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

faqs.question: Our neighbour's child sits 4MA1 and ours sits 0580. How differently should they revise?
faqs.answer: Two things that change a revision plan. Cambridge 0580's current syllabus examines each tier with a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper, so an entire paper rests on surds, index laws, fraction arithmetic and exact trigonometric values. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both of its equally weighted papers, which shifts the marks toward interpreting the question and recording method. Grade scales also differ: Cambridge Core runs C to G and Extended A* to E, while Pearson Foundation caps at 5 and Higher runs 9 to 4 with an allowed 3.

faqs.question: Which maths topics are Extended or Higher tier only?
faqs.answer: Broadly: surds and exact values; algebraic fractions and harder rearrangement; function notation including composite and inverse functions; trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, meaning the sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional work; vectors as column quantities with magnitude; histograms with unequal class widths and cumulative frequency; and gradient functions with turning points. None of these appear on a Core or Foundation paper. Use the list as a checklist with your child, then confirm it against the current syllabus document for their cohort on the board's own site.

faqs.question: Is there a non-calculator maths paper in IGCSE now?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge 0580 under the current syllabus, yes - each tier is examined with one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper, which is a change from the arrangement earlier cohorts sat. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers. Because this has changed, confirm the syllabus year your child is entered against as well as the code, since a revision plan built on the wrong structure wastes effort. Where a non-calculator paper applies, short frequent drill on surds, indices and fraction arithmetic is the format that produces fluency.

faqs.question: Which calculator does my child need, and does the school supply one?
faqs.answer: The school sets the permitted model and does not usually supply it, so ask the mathematics department directly rather than buying from a general recommendation. The more useful question is whether your child can actually use the one they own: fraction entry, statistical functions, exact-form output and memory recall all save time that converts into marks on a calculator paper. Two sessions of calculator fluency is among the cheapest interventions available, and it is almost never taught in class because it is assumed.

faqs.question: What formulae are given in the exam and what has to be memorised?
faqs.answer: Each specification states this explicitly, and provision is revised, so check the current syllabus document for your child's cohort rather than relying on what an older sibling remembers. The predictable failure is memorising the formulae that are given and never learning the ones that are not. Build the recall list as a single sheet and rehearse it: it is usually a weekend's work rather than a term's, and it removes a category of lost marks entirely. We link the official syllabus documents rather than reproducing them.

faqs.question: Does my child need Additional Mathematics for A Level or IB Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: Not as a requirement, but it helps. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics and Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure cover material overlapping the start of a post-16 course, including calculus and extended trigonometry, and a student who has sat one arrives in Year 12 with a real advantage. A student who has not is not disadvantaged provided the transition is planned, usually with a bridging block over the summer. Whether either is offered depends on the school, so ask the mathematics department in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

faqs.question: My child gets the right answer and still loses marks. Why does that happen?
faqs.answer: Because both boards award method marks, and a correct final answer with no visible working earns fewer marks than a wrong answer with a sound method shown. Students who compute mentally lose marks steadily and invisibly for two years. The fix is a habit rather than knowledge: write the step, then the substitution, then the answer, every time, including on questions that feel too easy to bother with. It takes about three weeks of marked written work to become automatic, and it is often worth most of a grade.

faqs.question: What does a grade 9 or an A* actually require beyond correct answers?
faqs.answer: Three things that are rarely taught explicitly. Complete accuracy on routine material, because at that level a dropped sign separates bands. The ability to start an unstructured multi-step question without a prompt, choosing the approach rather than executing a given one. And fluency without a calculator, which carries into every post-16 course. That is a different purchase from a 4-to-6 move, it takes longer and it costs more, so if another subject sits two grades below target, that subject is usually the better hour to buy.

faqs.question: Should my child move from Foundation to Higher tier?
faqs.answer: It depends on the destination and the deadline. Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5 and Cambridge Core at grade C, which cannot satisfy a sixth-form condition asking for a 6 or a B however well the student performs. So if a post-16 route needs more than the cap, the move has to be considered. The constraint is timing: tier decisions effectively lock at the board's final entry deadline, which sits months before the papers. That makes this a Year 10 conversation with the mathematics department, not a spring-term one.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE maths tutors charge in Dubai, and is the top band worth it?
faqs.answer: Published rates run roughly AED 33 to AED 65 for platform student tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online - one agency lists AED 150 specifically for IGCSE - AED 200 to AED 450 and above for examination-year specialists, with one agency at AED 270 and one premium provider at AED 650. The specialist band is worth it for tier decisions, method-mark diagnosis and a 6-to-9 attempt. It is not worth it for non-calculator drill, which works better cheaply and frequently.

faqs.question: The tutor offered to us normally teaches A Level. Is that a problem for a Year 11?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but the failure mode is specific enough to ask about. A post-16 teacher may be entirely fluent in the mathematics and unfamiliar with the paper: which topics are tier-restricted, how method marks are allocated, what a Core paper's question types look like, and how much structure a Foundation candidate is given. The risk is a Core candidate taught like a young A Level student, which makes performance worse rather than better because the practice stops resembling the paper. Ask which specification and tier they taught most recently, and what happened.

faqs.question: Eight weeks from the series and algebra is the weakness. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With the last page of past papers, not the first. Marks are not evenly distributed and the multi-step chains at the end of each paper are where grades are decided, and they are almost always algebra-dependent. Run timed papers, mark them to the method-mark conventions, and work only on the strands the marking exposes. In parallel, thirty minutes twice a week on manipulation - rearranging, factorising, algebraic fractions - because fluency is about retrieval speed and that needs frequency rather than long sessions.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free who teaches our exact specification and tier?
faqs.answer: We tell you before you book, which no competitor page researched in this market does. Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher match quickly. A Core or Foundation candidate needing a tutor comfortable teaching to a capped tier, or a student sitting 0606 or 4PM1 alongside the main qualification, can take longer, and the proposed tutor may be based outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time. We state the expected wait and the tutor's location first, so the choice is yours rather than a surprise in week three.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-meadows.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below names the maths syllabuses they have taught and the tier they usually prepare candidates for. Put the nine questions further down this page to them in the trial lesson; the specificity of the answers will tell you more than any profile can.

intro.heading: A maths tutor who knows the subject is not the same as one who knows the paper
paragraphs: Nearly every adult who studied mathematics to eighteen can teach quadratics. Far fewer can tell you, without looking it up, whether your child's Cambridge paper permits a calculator, what the grade ceiling is on the tier they have been entered for, or how many marks a bearings question typically carries and where candidates throw them away. The first group is large and locally available. The second group is what you are actually trying to hire, and the gap between them is invisible in a profile, a recommendation or a rate.

That gap is the real problem behind a search for a tutor near The Meadows. Emirates Living is residential and gated, with no tuition centres inside it, so the local supply is individuals who live nearby and teach whatever is asked for. Many of them are good. Almost none of them is selected for having taught Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher to an exam cohort within the last two years, because nobody who hires them asks. Distance is a filter that cannot distinguish the two groups, which is why this page provides one that can.

Below are nine questions, with the answers set out so you can mark the responses yourself. They are not trick questions and they do not require you to know any mathematics. They are the facts a person who has prepared candidates for these papers holds without effort: the paper structure, the tier ceilings, the calculator rules, what is printed on the formula list and what is not, where method marks live, and which topics reliably cost candidates marks. A tutor who cannot answer them may still be a pleasant and useful presence. They are not an exam specialist, and in Year 11 that difference is the whole thing you are buying.

The rest of the page is the reference material behind those questions: the paper structure for both boards and both tiers, the tier decision set out with the evidence that should drive it and the deadline that closes it, a topic-level map of where marks are lost, the Additional Mathematics question, the formula list and calculator reality, the published Dubai rates with sources attached, and the gap between IGCSE maths and whatever comes next. All of it is checkable against the boards' own documents, and the page says where.

IB Gram's delivery is one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to addresses in The Meadows or anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service our India operation runs, and the in-home rates quoted further down belong to other providers in this market rather than to us. Removing the drive is what allows a student in Meadows 8 to work with somebody who has taught their exact paper instead of the closest person who teaches maths.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-meadows.programmesIntro: Maths runs continuously from Year 7 to Year 13 and the tutoring question changes at each junction. These are the four stages behind almost every maths enquiry that reaches us from Emirates Living.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 and Cambridge Lower Secondary maths
programmes.description: Three years of internally assessed work in which the algebraic foundation is either built or quietly skipped. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October give the first externally marked signal. A student who cannot rearrange a formula, handle negative indices or work confidently with fractions at the end of Year 9 will meet all three again in an IGCSE paper, under time pressure, with marks attached.
programmes.countryNote: Families around Emirates Living rarely buy maths support at this stage, which is why the Year 11 bills are so large. A fortnightly hour in Year 8 spent on arithmetic fluency and algebraic manipulation is the single cheapest intervention available in the whole secondary run, and it leaves nothing visible behind to prove it worked, which is precisely why nobody buys it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Two written papers per tier and no coursework, which makes this the most measurable subject in the Year 11 timetable. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended with different papers and different grade ceilings; Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher. The tier is locked at entry, months before the exam, and it caps the grade available regardless of how well the candidate performs.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools carried 37 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, making this the single largest tutoring demand in the schools that buses from The Meadows serve. It also means local profiles advertise IGCSE maths heavily, and that the words on a profile say nothing about whether the tutor has seen the current papers.

programmes.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge 0606 and Pearson 4PM1, taken alongside the main maths course by students heading for A Level Maths, Further Maths or Diploma Higher Level. Calculus, trigonometric identities, series and matrices arrive a year early, with two papers and no coursework. It is a genuine extra qualification and a genuine extra workload, and it is frequently taken for the wrong reason.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Emirates Living offer it as an option or a set-based add-on, and parents often read it as a signal of ability rather than a workload decision. The useful test is whether the student is comfortable with unscaffolded algebra now, not whether they are getting a grade 8 in the main course on scaffolded questions.

programmes.name: A Level Mathematics and Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: The two destinations out of IGCSE maths in this neighbourhood, and the reason the quality of the IGCSE foundation matters beyond the grade. A Level Mathematics assumes algebraic fluency and expects unprompted reasoning; Diploma Analysis and Approaches sits one paper without a calculator and adds an internally assessed exploration. Neither scaffolds questions the way an IGCSE paper does.
programmes.countryNote: Because the sixth form is usually on the same campus, the step is treated as administrative by families here. The tutoring enquiries that arrive each November from Year 12 students who held a grade 8 at IGCSE suggest otherwise. A short diagnostic block in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is the cheapest way to find out whether the foundation is actually there.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-meadows.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is listed first, broken into the specific courses a student in this neighbourhood might be entered for. The subjects after it are the ones most often paired with maths tutoring, where the overlap with a maths tutor's skill set is real or illusory.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Extended
subjects.levels: Extended tier, grades A* to E
subjects.description: The tier the majority of students in Dubai's British-curriculum schools sit. Two written papers of equal weight, no coursework. The marks that separate a grade 6 from a grade 8 are overwhelmingly in algebraic manipulation, non-right-angled trigonometry, and the final parts of long structured questions where method is available and never written down.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Core
subjects.levels: Core tier, targeted at grades C to G
subjects.description: A narrower content list with a hard grade ceiling at C. For a student consistently scoring in the lowest bands on Extended papers, Core converts far more of the available marks into a grade. For a student near the Core ceiling it is the tier, not the ability, that is limiting the result, and that is a decision to make before the entry deadline.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.levels: Foundation grades 5 to 1 · Higher grades 9 to 4
subjects.description: Two written papers of equal weight, with a calculator permitted. Foundation caps at grade 5 and Higher reaches 9 with an allowed grade 3 below the normal range. The tier question here is sharper than at Cambridge because the Foundation ceiling sits lower, and a student capable of a 6 entered at Foundation cannot reach it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Two papers covering calculus, trigonometric identities, series, vectors and matrices, taken alongside 0580. It rewards algebraic confidence and punishes students who rely on scaffolded questions. Taken for the right reason it is excellent preparation for A Level or Diploma Higher Level maths; taken as a status signal it damages the main grade.

subjects.name: Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
subjects.description: The Pearson equivalent of Additional Mathematics, with two written papers and a heavier pure emphasis. Useful where the school offers it and the student is already fluent. The common error is adding it in the autumn of Year 11, when the main course still needs the hours it will consume.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 · 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: The most genuine pairing with maths, because unit handling, rearrangement and graph interpretation transfer directly and a large share of physics marks are mathematical. A tutor strong in both can save a family real money. The limit is the practical component, which Cambridge examines separately and Pearson examines inside the written papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 · 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Moles, concentration and electrolysis calculations are maths problems in chemical clothing and respond well to a mathematician. The rest of the grade, organic pathways and practical method language, does not, so pairing maths with chemistry works for a specific slice of the course and no further.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 · 4CP0)
subjects.description: Binary and hexadecimal representation, logic and algorithmic trace work overlap substantially with discrete maths topics. The theory paper's content on networks and systems does not, and the programming component needs somebody who has written code. A maths tutor covers perhaps half the course well.

subjects.name: Economics (0455 · 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and quantitative work give a maths tutor something concrete to add, particularly on elasticity calculations and index numbers. The grade, though, is decided by evaluation questions that need a conditional judgement, and no amount of numerical accuracy substitutes for that.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450 · 4BS1)
subjects.description: Break-even analysis, cash-flow forecasting and ratio work are the maths-adjacent parts and are commonly the parts students drop marks on. The case-study application that carries most of the paper requires a subject specialist, so this is a partial pairing at best.

subjects.name: Statistics (0452 · 4ST1)
subjects.description: Where offered, a natural second subject for a maths tutor, covering data presentation, probability and hypothesis-style reasoning. Students often find it easier than the main maths course and then lose marks on interpretation, which is the examined skill rather than the calculation.

subjects.name: ICT (0417 · 0983)
subjects.description: The spreadsheet modelling and database tasks are the components students lose most marks on and the ones a numerate tutor can genuinely help with, because precision in formulae and in data handling carries marks on its own. The theory paper is unrelated to maths entirely.

sections.heading: Nine questions only somebody who has taught the syllabus can answer
paragraphs: Use these in a trial lesson. You do not need to know the mathematics; you need to notice whether the answer is immediate and specific or general and warm. One: which board and syllabus code is my child entered for, and which tier? A specialist asks for the statement of entry before answering anything else. Two: how many papers will my child sit in maths, how long is each, and what is each worth? Three: what is the highest grade available on the tier my child has been entered for?

Four: which of the papers permits a calculator, and what does that change about how you teach? Five: which formulae are printed on the paper and which does my child have to memorise? Six: what is a method mark, and how does a student earn one on a question they get wrong? Seven: name three topics where candidates on this paper reliably lose marks, and say why. Eight: how will you mark my child's timed work, against the published mark scheme or by impression? Nine: what would make you tell me this is not working?

The answers are set out in this page so you can mark the responses. Questions one to five are factual and a specialist answers them in seconds. Question six separates the exam teachers from the subject teachers: method marks are awarded for correct working even where the final answer is wrong, which is why writing nothing down is the most expensive habit in the subject. Question seven should produce specifics, not reassurance. Questions eight and nine are about accountability, and a tutor who has thought about failure is considerably more likely to notice it.

sections.heading: Papers, tiers and ceilings: what each entry actually allows
paragraphs: Both boards assess maths entirely by terminal written papers, with no coursework, and both split the subject by tier. Cambridge 0580 runs Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher. The important consequence is that the tier caps the grade. A Cambridge Core candidate cannot be awarded above a C, and a Pearson Foundation candidate cannot be awarded above a grade 5, no matter how completely they answer the paper. That ceiling is fixed at entry, months before the exam, by a decision that is often taken on classwork impressions.

Paper structure has also changed, which catches out tutors who last taught the subject some years ago. The current Cambridge 0580 syllabus, first examined in 2025, splits the assessment into a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper of equal weight at each tier. Pearson 4MA1 sits two papers with a calculator permitted in both. If a tutor describes a single long calculator paper carrying most of the Cambridge grade, they are describing the previous structure, and that is a useful diagnostic about how recently they have taught it.

Verify the structure for your child's specific series rather than relying on any page, including this one. The syllabus PDF on cambridgeinternational.org and the specification on qualifications.pearson.com are the authoritative documents, and your school's exams officer holds the statement of entry that says which code and tier apply. The table below gives the shape of each entry and the grade range it permits, which is the part that governs every planning decision that follows.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and the evidence that should drive it
paragraphs: This is the highest-stakes decision in IGCSE maths and it is routinely made on the wrong information. The question is not whether your child is capable of Extended or Higher content. It is which tier converts more of the marks they can actually produce under timed conditions into a grade. A student scoring consistently in the lowest bands on Extended papers may well convert far more on Core, and a student sitting near the Core ceiling is being limited by the tier rather than by their mathematics.

The evidence that answers it is specific: timed sections from both tiers, sat under conditions, marked against both published schemes. Classwork does not answer it, because classwork is scaffolded and untimed. A single end-of-term percentage does not answer it, because it conflates tiers and topics. A subject teacher's view is valuable and should be sought, but it is a judgement formed alongside twenty-five other students and benefits from being tested against marked evidence that you hold.

The deadline is the part that turns a decision into a problem. Entries close months before the papers are sat, and in the UAE the papers mean June or November: a Cambridge June entry closes in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper, and Pearson's November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026 on an entry filed earlier in the year. So the autumn term is the one window in which a June tier is still genuinely open, while November candidates are already sitting. A family who concludes after the entry has closed that the tier was wrong is past the point at which it could be changed. Have the conversation in the autumn term, on evidence that exists by October, and treat the mock results as confirmation rather than as the trigger.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks are lost, topic by topic
paragraphs: Marks in this subject leak from a short and stable list of places, and a tutor who knows the syllabus can name them without being prompted. Algebraic manipulation is first and largest: a student who cannot reliably rearrange, factorise or handle indices loses marks across every topic that uses algebra, which is most of the paper. The loss is not visible as an algebra problem; it appears as a mistake in a trigonometry question or a failure to finish a problem about volume.

Then come the specific recurring offenders. Bearings and non-right-angled trigonometry, where the sine and cosine rules are known and the diagram is drawn wrongly. Compound and reverse percentages, where the method is reversed. Probability with and without replacement, where the second branch is not adjusted. Standard form arithmetic. Volume and surface area of compound solids, where one component is forgotten. Transformations described incompletely, losing a mark for a missing centre or scale factor. Vectors, where notation collapses under pressure.

The unifying failure is procedural rather than conceptual: unwritten method. Both boards award method marks for correct working, so a four-mark question answered with a single wrong number scores zero where two lines of visible rearrangement would have scored two. Students do this because they have been rewarded for speed and correct answers throughout their schooling. The fix is to mark their own work against the published scheme until they can see the marks they are giving away, and it costs nothing beyond the discipline of doing it.

sections.heading: The formula list, the calculator and what examiners do not give you
paragraphs: Both boards print a formula list, and in both cases students assume it contains more than it does. The result is predictable: a candidate reaches a question needing a formula they expected to be printed, finds it is not, and loses the question. Which formulae appear varies by board, by tier and by syllabus version, so the only sensible approach is to print the formula page from the current syllabus document, put it on the desk, and build a memorised list of what is missing. That exercise takes twenty minutes and is rarely done.

Calculator rules now differ in a way that matters. The current Cambridge 0580 structure, first examined in 2025, sets one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper of equal weight at each tier, while Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers. A student preparing for a Cambridge entry needs genuine arithmetic and algebraic fluency by hand, because half the marks are available without technology. Confirm which situation applies to your child's series on the board's own syllabus document rather than assuming from an older cohort's experience.

On the calculator itself, the practical guidance is unglamorous and useful. Use the model the school specifies, and use the same one all year: students lose marks in the exam because the menu structure of a borrowed calculator differs from the one they practised on. Learn the memory and fraction functions properly, because repeated re-entry of intermediate values introduces rounding errors that cost accuracy marks. And check the mode settings before starting a paper, since a calculator left in the wrong angle mode converts a correct method into a wrong answer across a whole question.

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs here, and what you can verify yourself
paragraphs: Begin with what is independently checkable, because that is the part of any price conversation you can act on. Every rate in this section was published by the provider named beside it and read from its own material in October 2026, which means you can open those sites and confirm them without taking our word for anything. That is a low bar and almost nobody in this market clears it: of the competitor pages researched for this cluster, three publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars rather than dirhams.

The checkable picture looks like this. Budget online tutoring is published from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which sets the qualified-subject-tutor band at roughly AED 150 to 300. TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist support. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200 to 500, and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages in circulation include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

None of those figures is an IB Gram price, and we do not publish a rate card, because the tier, the subject and the number of weeks change the answer and a single number across thousands of neighbourhood pages would be fiction in most of them. What we publish instead is a free trial lesson and a consultation. What the table is for is calibration: if a quote you have been given in The Meadows sits well outside these bands, ask what the difference is buying. The usual honest answers are travel time, group size or examiner experience, and only one of those is teaching.

sections.heading: Method marks, accuracy marks and the habit that wins both
paragraphs: Mark schemes in both boards distinguish between marks for method and marks for accuracy, and understanding that distinction is worth more to a Year 11 student than almost any content revision. A method mark rewards a correct approach even when the arithmetic goes wrong. An accuracy mark rewards the right value, correctly rounded, in the right units. A student who writes only answers forfeits every method mark available, which on a long structured question can be most of the marks on offer.

The habit that collects both is mechanical: write the method as a visible line, substitute values explicitly, keep unrounded intermediate values in the calculator rather than re-entering rounded ones, and state the final answer with units and to the accuracy the question asks for. None of that is mathematics. It is exam behaviour, it is learnable in a fortnight, and it is the single largest free gain available to most candidates sitting these papers.

The way to install it is to make the student the marker. Give them a past paper, their own completed script and the published mark scheme, and have them award their own marks line by line. The first time they do this they usually discover two or three marks per page that they had earned the thinking for and failed to claim. That discovery does more than any instruction, it costs nothing, and the role of a paid tutor in it is to set the work, verify the marking and keep the error log. A tutor who hands you this routine rather than selling you the hour is worth keeping.

sections.heading: From IGCSE maths to A Level or the Diploma: the gap nobody prices
paragraphs: A good IGCSE maths grade is not evidence that a student is ready for what follows, and in this neighbourhood the assumption that it is costs money in the November of Year 12. The reason is structural. IGCSE questions are scaffolded: they tell the candidate which method to use, break multi-step problems into labelled parts, and signal the topic by their position on the paper. A Level and Diploma questions do considerably less of this, and the skill they examine is deciding what to do, which an IGCSE paper barely tests.

The two destinations have different versions of the gap. A Level Mathematics assumes immediate algebraic fluency and spends very little time rebuilding it, so a student who was relying on a calculator and on scaffolding struggles within weeks. Diploma Analysis and Approaches adds two further obstacles: a calculator-free paper at both levels, and an internally assessed exploration worth twenty per cent of the grade which has to be produced over months alongside five other subjects.

The cheap intervention is a diagnostic block in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, four to six sessions on unscaffolded problems and calculator-free manipulation. It is cheap because it is short, it is effective because it identifies the gap before the new course has buried it, and almost nobody buys it because the Year 11 results have just arrived and everyone is relieved. The expensive version of the same intervention arrives in November, with a term of poor marks already recorded and a course decision that may now need revisiting.

sections.heading: Starting from The Meadows, with the honest limits
paragraphs: What to send: the board, the syllabus code, the tier, the year group, and the most recent marked work you have. The statement of entry from your school's exams officer carries the first three. Then tell us what time your child actually walks through the door, because the nine Meadows sub-communities sit at different points on the bus loop and a slot set against the school bell rather than the arrival time is the most common reason a weekly arrangement stops by half term.

What happens next: a free 45-minute trial, one-to-one over live video, with the tutor who would teach the term rather than a consultant, and no card details required to book it. Put the nine questions from this page to them. If the answers are specific, you have found an exam specialist. If they are warm and general, you have found a maths graduate, which may still be useful for homework support at a lower rate but is not what a Year 11 entry needs.

The limits, stated before you book. Availability is deep for Extended and Higher tier maths at common times and thinner for Additional Mathematics, for Core tier late in the year and for weekend morning slots in January, when demand across Dubai peaks at once. Where no UAE-based tutor covers the combination you need, the match may be an experienced IGCSE maths specialist teaching from outside the UAE on the same live video format and the same Gulf Standard Time slot, and we say so in advance. No tutor will promise a grade. No tutor will come to a villa in Emirates Living, because in-home visiting is not a service we sell in the UAE. And nothing here claims approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership with Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, because IB Gram holds none of those and operates no UAE office.

process.title: Get the statement of entry
process.description: One email to your school's exams officer produces the board, the four-character syllabus code and the tier for every subject. Those three facts determine the papers, the calculator rules and the grade ceiling, and no sensible tutoring decision can be made before you hold them. A tutor who does not ask for them has not read the assessment.

process.title: Ask the nine questions
process.description: Put the list from this page to any tutor you are considering, ours included, in the trial lesson. You are marking specificity rather than mathematics: paper count, tier ceiling, calculator rules, formula list, method marks and three named topics where candidates lose marks. Vague answers are a complete answer in themselves.

process.title: Settle the tier on timed evidence
process.description: If the tier is still open, buy the two-session diagnostic: timed sections from both tiers, sat under conditions, marked against both published schemes. Take the written comparison to the subject teacher. Do this in the autumn term, because entries close months before the papers and a January realisation is two months too late.

process.title: Choose frequency over session length
process.description: Two forty-five minute sessions a week beat one ninety-minute session for maths, because fluency is built by frequent retrieval. If scheduling allows only one, insist that timed work is set between sessions and formally marked rather than discussed, or the hour becomes a conversation about maths.

process.title: Make the student the marker
process.description: Have your child mark their own script against the published scheme, line by line, and count the marks they earned the thinking for but failed to claim. That number changes behaviour faster than instruction does. The tutor's job is to set the work, verify the marking and keep the error log by topic.

process.title: Plan to the entry deadline, not the exam
process.description: Mark the entry deadline, the mock window and the exam window from the dates your school's exams officer holds, read against the live timetable PDF on the board's own site. Autumn work decides the tier and the forecast grade; spring work decides the marks. They are different jobs.

faqs.question: How many papers does my child sit for Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580?
faqs.answer: Two written papers at each tier, of equal weight, with no coursework. The current syllabus, first examined in 2025, sets one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper at both Core and Extended. That is a change from the older structure, in which calculators were permitted throughout and one long paper carried most of the grade, so a tutor who describes the old arrangement has not taught the course recently. Confirm the structure for your child's specific series on the syllabus PDF at cambridgeinternational.org, and get the code and tier from the statement of entry your school's exams officer issues.

faqs.question: Is there really a non-calculator maths paper now?
faqs.answer: For the current Cambridge 0580 syllabus, yes: the assessment at each tier includes a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper of equal weight. Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, permits a calculator in both of its papers. This single difference changes what tutoring should do: a Cambridge candidate needs genuine arithmetic and algebraic fluency by hand, because half the marks are available without technology, while a Pearson candidate needs calculator discipline and accuracy. Check which applies to your child on the board's own syllabus document rather than assuming from an older cohort.

faqs.question: What is the highest grade available on Core or Foundation tier?
faqs.answer: Cambridge 0580 Core is targeted at grades C to G and cannot be awarded above a C. Pearson 4MA1 Foundation covers grades 5 to 1 and cannot be awarded above a 5. Extended runs A* to E at Cambridge and Higher runs 9 to 4 at Pearson, with an allowed grade 3. The ceiling is fixed by the entry, not by performance, which means a student capable of a 6 who is entered at Foundation cannot reach it. This is why the tier decision has to be made on timed evidence before the entry deadline closes.

faqs.question: How do we decide between Core and Extended before the deadline?
faqs.answer: On marked timed evidence rather than classwork, because classwork is scaffolded and untimed. Have your child sit timed sections from both tiers under conditions, marked against both published schemes, and compare how many marks each tier converts. Large unattempted sections and lowest-band scores on the higher tier point one way; near-full marks on the lower tier point the other, because then the ceiling rather than the mathematics is the limit. Take the written comparison to the subject teacher, and do it in the autumn term, because a Cambridge June entry closes in the spring and after that the tier is fixed for the papers.

faqs.question: Should my child take Additional Mathematics 0606 as well?
faqs.answer: Only if they are already fluent with unscaffolded algebra, not as a signal of ability. It is a separate qualification with two further papers covering calculus, trigonometric identities, series, vectors and matrices, and it consumes hours the main course may still need. Taken for the right reason by a student heading for A Level Maths, Further Maths or Diploma Higher Level, it is genuinely useful preparation. Added in the autumn of Year 11 to an already stretched timetable, it tends to cost marks in the main entry, which is the grade universities will actually look at.

faqs.question: Which formulae are printed on the paper and which must be memorised?
faqs.answer: Both boards print a formula list and both leave out formulae that students assume will be there, with the contents varying by board, tier and syllabus version. The reliable approach takes twenty minutes: download the current syllabus document, print the formula page, and build a memorised list of everything your child needs that is not on it. Students lose whole questions by reaching for a formula they expected to be supplied. No tutor's recollection substitutes for the current document, and a tutor who offers one from memory should be checked against it.

faqs.question: My child understands the maths but keeps losing marks. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always method and accuracy rather than content. Mark schemes award method marks for a correct approach even when the arithmetic fails, so a student who writes only final answers forfeits them on every question. Accuracy marks need the right value, correct units and the rounding the question asked for. The fix is to make the student mark their own script against the published scheme, line by line, and count the marks they earned the thinking for and failed to claim. That count usually runs to two or three per page and it changes behaviour faster than any instruction.

faqs.question: Which board sets the tougher maths paper for a Year 11 student here?
faqs.answer: They are different rather than ranked, and claims either way usually come from somebody who has taught only one. The current Cambridge structure includes a non-calculator paper at both tiers, which makes manual fluency a graded requirement. Pearson permits a calculator throughout, which shifts the difficulty towards accuracy, interpretation and question volume. Cambridge's Core tier ceiling sits at C and Pearson's Foundation ceiling at grade 5. Your child sits whichever the school has entered them for, so the useful question is not which is harder but what their specific paper demands.

faqs.question: How long before the exam should maths tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than demand suggests. Year 10, at one hour a week while content is still being taught, is the cheapest and most effective window, and it produces the marked timed evidence the tier decision needs. The autumn of Year 11 is the point at which technique work changes the forecast grade. By January, specialists in this subject are booked, rates sit at the top of their published bands, every family on the same bus route is looking at once, and the content gap is a year old. The honest rule is that each term of delay roughly doubles what the same improvement costs.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches A Level maths also teach IGCSE maths well?
faqs.answer: Often, but it is not automatic and the failure mode is specific. A tutor used to A Level will teach the mathematics correctly and may miss the exam-technique layer that decides an IGCSE grade: the method-mark discipline, the command-word conventions, the specific recurring question types, and which formulae this particular paper prints. Ask them which tier your child is entered for and what the ceiling is. If the answer is immediate, the A Level background is an asset. If they have to think about it, they are teaching the subject rather than the paper.

faqs.question: Does my child need a particular calculator model?
faqs.answer: Use the model the school specifies and use the same one all year. Students lose marks in examinations because a borrowed or newly bought calculator has a different menu structure from the one they practised on, and under time pressure that costs whole questions. Learn the memory and fraction functions properly, because re-entering rounded intermediate values introduces rounding errors that cost accuracy marks. Check the angle mode before starting any paper. None of this is mathematics, and all of it is marks.

faqs.question: What is the gap between IGCSE maths and A Level or Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: Scaffolding. IGCSE questions indicate the method, split multi-step problems into labelled parts and signal the topic by position on the paper. A Level and Diploma questions do far less of that, and the skill they examine is deciding what to do. A Level Mathematics also assumes immediate algebraic fluency, while Diploma Analysis and Approaches adds a calculator-free paper at both levels and an internally assessed exploration worth a fifth of the grade. A four-to-six session diagnostic block in the summer after Year 11 identifies the gap before the new course buries it.

faqs.question: My child's mock result is two grades below target. What should we do first?
faqs.answer: Diagnose before buying hours. Sit a full paper under timed conditions, mark it against the published scheme, and allocate the lost marks into four categories: content not known, method not shown, accuracy and rounding, and questions not attempted. Those four point at completely different interventions with different costs. Unattempted questions are a pace problem fixed by sitting full papers. Unshown method is a fortnight of habit change. Only genuine content gaps justify a long teaching block, and they are usually the smallest category of the four.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class at a centre worth considering?
faqs.answer: For shared content delivery, yes, and the hourly saving is real: centre group classes in Dubai are advertised at roughly AED 60 to 150 per student against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified one-to-one online tutor. For a specific diagnosed gap, no, because the pace is set by the median student in the room and an hour divided among six is ten minutes each. Add the travel: a round trip from The Meadows to an Al Barsha centre at half past four commonly runs to ninety minutes door to door, four times the lesson's useful content.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor knows the syllabus rather than just the subject?
faqs.answer: Ask factual questions with checkable answers and watch how quickly they come. Which board and tier is my child entered for? How many papers, how long, what weighting? What is the grade ceiling on that tier? Which paper permits a calculator? Which formulae are printed? What is a method mark and how is one earned on a question answered incorrectly? Name three topics where candidates reliably lose marks. A specialist answers all of these without hesitation. Everyone else answers in terms of confidence, effort and rapport, which are real but are not what you are short of.

faqs.question: Does a private maths tutor in Dubai need a permit from MoHRE?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listed with no fee and two working days through MoHRE's app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so quoted amounts are rumour.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-springs.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE and International GCSE Mathematics to students in The Springs and across Emirates Living. Each one works from the exact syllabus code and tier on your child's entry, and every lesson is one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Five qualifications, one name, and a very wide price range
paragraphs: A Springs parent comparing two maths quotes is usually comparing two numbers attached to completely different jobs. The phrase IGCSE maths covers at least five qualifications in this community: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 and Mathematics B 4MB1, with Further Pure 4PM1 as a sixth in a handful of schools. They differ in paper count, in whether a calculator is allowed, in tiering and in the grade range available. A tutor fluent in one can be genuinely weak in another.

That matters financially because the wrong match is invisible for about eight lessons. A tutor who knows 0580 inside out will teach an Edexcel 4MA1 student competently and still leave them unprepared for a paper structure they have never practised. At published Dubai rates of AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor, eight lessons is AED 1,200 to 2,400 spent before anybody notices. One email to the school's examinations officer prevents all of it.

The second financial variable is the tier, because it caps the outcome. Cambridge 0580 Core entry offers grades C to G; Extended offers A* to E. Pearson 4MA1 Foundation offers grades 5 to 1; Higher offers 9 to 4, with a 3 allowed. A family paying specialist rates to lift a child from grade C to grade A while the school has entered them at Core tier is paying for something the entry form has already ruled out, and no tutor can fix that in the spring of Year 11.

The third is the paper. Marks are lost in specific, diagnosable places: algebraic manipulation under time pressure, bearings and vectors, multi-step probability, transformations described imprecisely, and the non-calculator paper where a student who has leaned on technology for two years finally has to think. Each of those has a different cost to fix, and the cheapest ones are often the ones nobody addresses because they look too small to buy lessons for.

This page sets out the dirham figures with their sources, counts the hours honestly rather than promising outcomes, and names the four places a maths budget leaks in a Springs household. Delivery is stated plainly up front: lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai, because home tutoring is a service offered only in India, and a maths lesson on a shared whiteboard loses nothing by arriving on a screen.

One framing point before the numbers. The cheapest version of this decision is the one taken before any money has moved, because four questions asked at the start cost nothing and change everything that follows. Which code and tier is the entry. Which paper is losing the marks. Whether the cause is content, accuracy or timing. And how many lessons the answer to those three justifies. A family that settles those before comparing rates almost always buys fewer hours than one that starts with a price list.
