dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: These are the topic areas where Emirates Living families most often ask for maths help, with what the question usually looks like and what the fix costs in lessons rather than in dirhams.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. Almost every diagnostic starts here because weakness shows up elsewhere as a topic problem. Four to six lessons of marked practice usually moves it, and it pays back across every other topic on the paper.

subjects.name: Fractions, indices and surds
subjects.description: The non-calculator paper lives here. A student who has used technology for two years often cannot simplify confidently under time pressure. Cheap to fix, routinely untaught as a separate skill, and worth marks on every paper in the series.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Quadratic and reciprocal graphs, transformations, gradients and areas under curves. Marks are lost sketching without axes labels and reading intercepts off a calculator display rather than reasoning. The graph question is usually worth more than students treat it as.

subjects.name: Trigonometry, bearings and vectors
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, three-dimensional problems, bearings written imprecisely and column vectors. A recurring Dubai weak point where the mathematics is understood and the diagram discipline is not, which makes it one of the highest-return topics to tutor.

subjects.name: Probability and tree diagrams
subjects.description: Multi-step conditional probability with and without replacement. Students who can draw a tree still lose marks by multiplying along the wrong branch or leaving the final answer unsimplified. Three lessons is often the whole fix.

subjects.name: Transformations and loci
subjects.description: Describing a transformation fully, with centre, scale factor, direction and mirror line, is a mark-scheme habit rather than a concept. Students lose two or three marks a paper here, which is a grade boundary in a close year.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measures
subjects.description: Surface area, volume, similar shapes, density, speed and unit conversion. The arithmetic is simple and the unit discipline is not, which is why these questions reward careful setting-out more than ability.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.description: Cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal class widths, and interpretation sentences. The interpretation marks are frequently left blank because students treat the question as finished once the diagram is drawn.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606 and Further Pure 4PM1
subjects.description: The fourth-option courses that bridge into A Level or Higher Level IB maths. Calculus, series and more demanding algebra. Fewer tutors in this market teach them, which is why they are worth asking about specifically rather than assuming coverage.

subjects.name: Examination technique and timing
subjects.description: Minute allocation against marks, choosing a method quickly, and knowing when to abandon a question. Not a topic, and not taught in most classrooms, but the commonest cause of a student who is fine in class and loses marks in papers.

sections.heading: The five qualifications sold as IGCSE maths, and why the code decides the price
paragraphs: Before comparing any two quotes, find out exactly what your child is sitting. In schools serving The Springs the realistic list is Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 and Mathematics B 4MB1, with Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 appearing in a few schools as a fourth option. These are not variations on a theme. They differ in paper count, calculator policy, tiering and the grade range available.

The practical difference shows up in the first marked past paper. A 0607 student sits an investigation component and is expected to use a graphic display calculator throughout; a 4MA1 student sits two conventional two-hour papers; a 4MB1 student sits a Higher-tier-only course with no Foundation route at all. A tutor who has taught only one of these will prepare a student competently for the wrong paper, and the family will not find out until a mock.

Pricing follows scarcity. Tutors for 0580 and 4MA1 are plentiful in this market because those are the volume qualifications. Tutors for 0606, 0607 and 4PM1 are not, which is why those requests should be made explicitly rather than assumed to be covered by anyone advertising IGCSE maths in Dubai. Asking the question at the start costs nothing; discovering it at lesson eight costs whatever eight lessons cost.

Paper numbers, durations and calculator policies are revised by both boards from time to time, so the table below should be confirmed against the syllabus document for your child's actual examination series rather than taken as permanent.

sections.heading: The tier is the ceiling, and the ceiling is the first thing to price
paragraphs: Tier entry is the most consequential maths decision in a British-curriculum Springs household and the one most often discovered rather than decided. Cambridge 0580 Core entry makes grades C to G available and nothing above. Pearson 4MA1 Foundation makes grades 5 to 1 available. Higher and Extended entry open the full range but also set harder papers, where a student pitched too high can end up with a lower grade than they would have earned at the tier below.

A family paying AED 250 an hour to move a child from a predicted C towards an A, while the school has entered that child at Core tier, is buying something the entry form has already excluded. This is not a rare scenario. It happens most often when the tier was set quietly in Year 10 on the basis of one assessment and nobody told the parents explicitly.

The sequence that avoids it takes two emails. Ask the department which tier your child is entered or provisionally entered at, and what evidence that decision rests on. Then ask when the final entry deadline falls. In most Dubai schools the decision remains movable through the autumn of Year 11 with the department's agreement, and a tutor's diagnostic in Year 10 is the strongest evidence a parent can bring to that conversation.

Where a child is genuinely borderline, the honest tutoring question is not how to get the higher tier but which tier produces the better outcome. A secure grade 5 at Foundation is worth more to a post-16 application than a grade 4 scraped at Higher after two terms of anxiety, and a tutor who will say that out loud is worth more than one who will not.

sections.heading: What IGCSE maths help costs around Emirates Living, and what the premium buys
paragraphs: Take the in-home premium first, because it is the clearest illustration of what a rate actually includes. In-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table showing 180 to 350 and independent home tutors 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages in this market run AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Named specialists teaching online are quoted at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. At AED 300 an hour, the money is buying either a journey or a syllabus specialism, and the teaching hour itself is the same length in both.

Below that premium, qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The budget band, advertised by EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, generally buys a university student working from a textbook. Monthly online packages at around AED 799 for eight sessions sit between the two. At the top, premium and examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement give the household view: AED 240 to 600 in the budget band, AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Those are the numbers a Springs budget actually feels, and they are the ones to compare against a school fee that KHDA confirmed will not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's AED 1.5 billion incentives package.

All of the above are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, reproduced so you can judge any quote you are given. They are not IB Gram's price list. Our conversation starts with a free trial lesson and an honest estimate of how many hours the diagnosis justifies, which is a different question from what an hour costs.

sections.heading: Counting hours honestly instead of promising grades
paragraphs: No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone in this market who offers one should be treated with real scepticism. What can be described honestly is what families typically buy for a given starting point, and how much of the work has to come from the student rather than the tutor. The table below is a planning aid built from the shape of the qualification, not a forecast about any child.

Two things drive the hour count more than ability. The first is how much of the syllabus has been taught: a student in the autumn of Year 10 who is behind on three topics needs fewer hours than a student in the spring of Year 11 who is behind on twelve, because in the first case the school is still teaching the content and the tutor is reinforcing it. The second is whether the problem is content, accuracy or timing. Content needs teaching. Accuracy needs marked written practice. Timing needs whole papers under the clock, which almost no student does voluntarily at home.

The least efficient purchase in the whole market is open-ended weekly tutoring with no named target. It renews by default, it feels productive, and after two terms nobody can say what changed. A block with a stated endpoint - this component, these lessons, this total - forces the conversation that makes the spend accountable.

Ask any tutor to put a number on the lessons they think the diagnosis justifies, and to say what should be different at the end of them. A specialist will answer. A provider who will not name a number is quietly selling an open-ended subscription.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper is a separate skill with a separate price
paragraphs: A student who has had a calculator available for every piece of mathematics since Year 7 has not practised arithmetic reasoning, and that shows up as a sudden cliff on the non-calculator component. Parents read it as a content problem and buy content lessons. It is not a content problem. It is a fluency problem, and fluency responds to short daily practice far better than to a weekly hour.

What the paper actually asks for is manageable: fraction arithmetic without decimals, index laws applied cleanly, surds simplified, standard form manipulated, estimation to sensible significant figures, and the recognition that an exact answer is often expected rather than a decimal approximation. None of that is hard mathematics. All of it is unpractised.

The efficient purchase here is a short block - six to eight lessons - combined with a daily ten-minute routine that costs nothing. The tutor's job is to diagnose which of the six skills is missing, model the method, set the right practice and mark it properly. The student's job is the ten minutes. A family that buys the lessons and skips the ten minutes has bought half a product.

This is also the cheapest grade movement available in the whole qualification, which is why it belongs in a page about cost. Two or three marks a paper recovered on arithmetic fluency, across two papers, is a grade boundary in a close year, and it costs a fraction of what re-teaching trigonometry costs.

sections.heading: Retake arithmetic: November, the next June, or a private candidate entry
paragraphs: If results come back below what a post-16 place requires, the decision is financial as well as academic, and the windows are fixed by the boards rather than by anybody's preference. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. Pearson International GCSE sits in May/June and November, with the November 2026 International GCSE timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Put the two series a UAE candidate can sit next to each other and the retake choice makes itself. November is the fast route: Pearson's November 2026 papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and the grade follows in January, as the November 2025 series showed when results reached students on 22 January 2026. The next June is the thorough route: entries close in the spring, the papers run in June and the grade arrives in August, in time for a post-16 place. Both close their entries well before the first paper, so the real deadline is the entry, not the exam, and a family deciding once revision has started has already chosen for itself.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the wrong version of the timetable is the centre's responsibility, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination as a result. Revise towards your school's own copy of the correct zone timetable, never a forum post or a generic calendar.

The cost comparison is straightforward once the dates are known. A November re-sit means a short intense block over roughly ten weeks, during which a student is also starting post-16 courses. Waiting for the following June means a longer, cheaper, calmer run but a year's delay in the grade being available. A private candidate entry through an approved examination centre adds an entry fee and administrative work that the school would otherwise have handled.

sections.heading: Four ways a maths budget leaks in a Springs household
paragraphs: The first leak is the wrong code. Paying for a 0580 specialist to prepare a 4MA1 candidate, or assuming anyone advertising IGCSE maths in Dubai can handle 0607 or 4PM1, costs eight lessons before it surfaces. One email fixes it permanently.

The second is the mixed group class. Group tuition is genuinely cheaper per hour and genuinely works where a cohort shares one gap. The Dubai reality is often a group advertised for IGCSE maths that contains Core and Extended students, two boards and two school sequences, producing an hour that fits nobody exactly. For a specific topic weakness, that is the most expensive cheap option in the market.

The third is content lessons bought to solve a timing problem. A student who is fine in class and loses marks in papers does not need more topics. They need whole papers under the clock, marked properly, with feedback on method choice and minute allocation. A tutor who responds to a poor mock by re-teaching the syllabus has misread the diagnosis and will bill for two terms.

The fourth is the open-ended weekly arrangement with no named target. It renews by default, feels productive, and resists review. A block with a stated component, a stated number of lessons and a stated total is the version a family can actually audit, and asking for that is reasonable regardless of who the provider is. A fifth, smaller leak is worth naming: paying a subject specialist to supervise homework. If what the household needs is somebody making sure the work happens at five o'clock, that is a different and much cheaper product, and merging the two inflates the bill without improving the mark.
bullets: Confirm the syllabus code before the first lesson, not after the first mock
Ask what board and tier the other students in a group class are on
Fix timing with timed papers, not with more content
Buy blocks with a named endpoint rather than an open subscription

sections.heading: Starting from The Springs, and the limits stated before payment
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Email the examinations officer for the board, code and tier. Find a recent marked paper or the school's question-level analysis of a mock. Pick the slot the week can actually hold, which in most of this community is 17:00 on a weekday or a Saturday morning, because the bus reaches the later Springs numbers closer to 16:45 than to 16:00. Then take the free trial lesson.

The trial is sixty minutes of real teaching on your child's own paper, and it ends with the tutor writing down what they found: whether the gap is content, accuracy or timing, which topics are involved, and how many lessons that justifies. That note is the basis of any quote. A provider who quotes before diagnosing is quoting for a product rather than for your child.

Three limits, said before money changes hands. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, because home tutoring is an India-only service. Narrow combinations - 0606 or 4PM1 at a fixed hour, for example - cannot always be filled from the UAE-based pool, and when they cannot we say so and offer a specialist elsewhere at the same rate rather than substituting someone unsuitable. And no grade can be guaranteed by anyone.

On coursework and practice materials, the boundary matters. A tutor teaches method, explains what a mark scheme rewards, and gives feedback on the student's own written work. Boards' past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents are the boards' copyright: a tutor should reference and link them, not hand over a folder of reproduced material, and a provider offering a library of board documents is telling you something about how they operate.

faqs.question: How do I know which maths qualification my child is actually sitting?
faqs.answer: Email the examinations officer and ask for the board, the code and the tier. The answer will be a short line: Cambridge 0580 Extended, Cambridge 0607 Core, Pearson 4MA1 Higher, Pearson 4MB1, and so on. It matters because these are six different qualifications with different paper counts, calculator policies and grade ranges, not variations on one syllabus. A tutor who has only ever taught one of them will prepare your child competently for the wrong paper structure, and the first time anyone notices is usually a mock.

faqs.question: Does Core or Foundation entry limit what tutoring can achieve?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the most important thing on the page. Cambridge 0580 Core entry makes grades C to G available and nothing higher. Pearson 4MA1 Foundation makes grades 5 to 1 available. If you are paying specialist rates in the hope of an A or a grade 7 while the school has entered your child at the lower tier, the entry form has already excluded that outcome. Ask the department which tier your child is entered at, what evidence it rests on, and when the final entry deadline falls.

faqs.question: What should a Springs family expect to pay per hour for IGCSE maths support?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures, read in October 2026, run as follows. Budget online tutoring is advertised from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Named specialists are AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one, travel included, is AED 180 to 500. These are other providers' rates, quoted so you can judge any number you are given, including ours.

faqs.question: Why would I pay the same for an online specialist as for a tutor who drives to Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: Because at the same price those two things are not the same product. The in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour includes the journey; the online specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above includes the syllabus specialism instead. The teaching hour is sixty minutes either way. For maths specifically, a shared digital whiteboard that keeps every worked solution is more useful in March than a notebook filled in October. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so the choice we can offer is the specialism.

faqs.question: How many lessons does fixing the non-calculator paper usually take?
faqs.answer: Six to eight, plus about ten minutes of daily practice that costs nothing. The non-calculator component is not harder mathematics; it is unpractised arithmetic reasoning, and it breaks down into six skills: fraction work without decimals, index laws, surds, standard form, sensible estimation and giving exact rather than decimal answers. A tutor diagnoses which of the six is missing and marks the practice properly. A family that buys the lessons and skips the daily ten minutes has bought half the product.

faqs.question: Is a group IGCSE maths class in Dubai cheaper in practice?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes. In practice it depends entirely on who else is in the room. A group drawn from one school, one board and one tier, all stuck on the same topic, is good value. A group advertised simply as IGCSE maths often mixes Core with Extended, Cambridge with Pearson, and two different school sequences, which produces an hour aimed at nobody precisely. For a specific diagnosed topic weakness that is the most expensive cheap option available. Ask what board and tier the other students are on before booking anything.

faqs.question: My child is strong in lessons and weak in maths papers. What should we actually buy?
faqs.answer: Not more content. That pattern is almost always timing, method selection and notation, and it is diagnosed by marking a complete paper rather than by covering more topics. The right purchase is four to six lessons built around full papers sat under timed conditions, with feedback on how the minutes were allocated against the marks available and where method choice cost time. A tutor who responds to a poor mock by re-teaching the syllabus has misread the problem and will bill for two terms.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time in the course to start maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 9, before the options evening, and almost nobody does it. Six to ten lessons on algebraic fluency, fractions, indices and rearranging formulae at that point prevents the gap that otherwise reappears in Year 11 looking like a problem with the new syllabus. The next best entry point is the autumn of Year 10, when content is still being taught for the first time and the tier decision is still movable. The most expensive is the spring of Year 11, when the whole Dubai cohort is competing for the same tutors.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking as a fourth option?
faqs.answer: For a student heading to A Level mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, usually yes, because it covers calculus and series that otherwise land cold in the first post-16 term. The practical caution is availability: far fewer tutors in Dubai teach 0606 or Pearson Further Pure 4PM1 than teach 0580 or 4MA1, so support should be confirmed as available before the option is taken rather than assumed. Ask the question explicitly; coverage of IGCSE maths does not imply coverage of these.

faqs.question: Should my child re-sit in November or wait for the next June series?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether a grade is needed before January. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November re-sit means roughly ten weeks of intense work while also starting post-16 courses. Waiting for the following summer gives a longer, calmer, cheaper run with one weekly slot, at the cost of a year's delay. A two-lesson diagnostic before deciding is money well spent either way.

faqs.question: Why do board entry deadlines matter to my tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: Because they close options months before the papers. A UAE candidate sits the June series or the November series, and in both cases the entry is filed long in advance: Cambridge June entries close in the spring, and Pearson's November 2026 papers, which ran to 19 November 2026, were entered earlier in the year. By the time revision feels urgent, the tier and the subject list are already fixed, so a family deciding late is choosing between marks inside a ceiling rather than choosing the ceiling. Cambridge also allocates centres to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used.

faqs.question: Should a maths tutor be supplying us with board past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: A responsible one will not, and the reason is worth knowing. Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents are the boards' copyright. A tutor should reference them, link to the official source and work through questions with your child, rather than distributing reproduced material. A provider advertising a library of board documents as a selling point is telling you how they operate. Your child's school can supply legitimate access to past material through its own board account, which is the proper route.

faqs.question: Does the maths tutor we hire in Dubai need to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app and e-services. The u.ae guidance states that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so nobody should quote you an amount.

faqs.question: Do maths lessons continue during Ramadan and the long summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the hour moved rather than the plan changed. School days shorten during Ramadan and the productive window shifts later, so a 17:00 slot usually becomes 20:30 or later for the month; families who arrange that in advance keep continuity rather than losing four weeks. The long summer break, from late June or early July into early September, is the only interruption-free block in a two-year course and the best time for fluency work. Lessons also continue while a family travels, since everything runs over video.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is free for our code and tier at the hour we need?
faqs.answer: We say so. A narrow request - Cambridge 0607 Extended at a fixed half-hour on a Wednesday, or Further Pure 4PM1 at all - cannot always be filled from the UAE-based pool. The honest options are then a specialist elsewhere teaching in your Gulf Standard Time slot at the same rate, a different hour with the right person, or a wait with a realistic estimate. Filling a booked slot with an available but unsuitable tutor is how families end up paying specialist money for general help.

faqs.question: How will I know the money is doing anything?
faqs.answer: Because the plan names what should be different and when. A block starts from a marked paper, states which component it targets, how many lessons it runs for and what the endpoint looks like, and ends with a written handover. At four lessons there is a review against that plan. If nothing has moved, the right answer is a different tutor or a different diagnosis, not more of the same. Open-ended weekly arrangements with no stated target are the ones that resist this question for two terms.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-springs.closingHeading: Confirm the code, find the marked paper, then compare prices

intro.heading: Two specifications, and the one your child sits decides everything
paragraphs: The first question any mathematics tutor should ask is which specification your child is entered for. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and splits into Core and Extended. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1 and splits into Foundation and Higher tiers, with two written papers at each tier. Both report on the 9 to 1 scale, both are respected equally by universities, and they are not the same qualification. Past papers do not transfer between them and a tutor fluent in one is not automatically fluent in the other.

Most parents do not know which their child sits, which is entirely reasonable and easily fixed: the school's examinations officer can confirm the code in an email. It is worth getting before the first session rather than after it, because the difference shows up immediately in question style. Cambridge questions tend to be shorter and more numerous, moving quickly between topics; Pearson questions more often build in several parts on a single context. Students who are good at one style are not automatically good at the other.

The second question is topic-level. Mathematics is the most diagnosable subject on a school timetable, because almost every lost mark has one identifiable cause. In this community the recurring causes are consistent: algebraic manipulation that is slow rather than wrong, method marks forfeited by writing only an answer, trigonometry applied without checking which rule the triangle allows, and probability questions answered by instinct rather than by a tree or a table. None of these require a general mathematics course to repair.

The Sustainable City makes one part of this easier. The community sits off Al Qudra Road with a school inside its own gates, so children attending it are home in the middle of the afternoon rather than at the end of it. Mathematics is a subject where session timing has a measurable effect, because manipulation under fatigue produces errors a student would never make at four in the afternoon. Households commuting out to Motor City or Arabian Ranches should plan on a 5.30pm start or a weekend block.

Delivery is online and said plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in this community. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard on which the working appears as it is written. For mathematics that is close to a complete substitute for sitting at the same table, because the diagnostic information a tutor needs is precisely the line where the student hesitates. What the format removes is the two car journeys at either end of a visit, which is why an online session can start while a teenager is still able to concentrate, and why the tutor can be the person who teaches your child's specification rather than the person who lives closest to it.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-sustainab.programmesIntro: Mathematics at this stage is three jobs: finishing the preparation that should have happened earlier, covering the specification, and converting knowledge into marks. These are the stages and what each one requires.

programmes.name: Year 9 preparation
programmes.description: The specification assumes fluency in operations that are not themselves examined: negatives, fractions, indices, rearranging, and reading a question precisely. A student who has to think about those cannot simultaneously think about the problem containing them. Everything on this list can be fixed in a term at this stage and becomes expensive to fix later.
programmes.countryNote: Mid-phase arrivals are common across this belt as families move between communities and systems. A child joining a British-curriculum school in Year 9 from an American or CBSE sequence usually has two or three specific missing topics rather than a general weakness, and naming them before the IGCSE course begins is the cheapest intervention available.

programmes.name: Year 10, covering the specification
programmes.description: Content is met for the first time and the tier question is forming. The habits that decide the final grade are built here: writing method out, checking a result against the context, and distinguishing a question type from a question. Students who get through Year 10 on recall rather than understanding usually stall in the second year.
programmes.countryNote: Internal Year 10 examinations in most Dubai schools feed directly into the tier decision for Year 11, and that decision has an entry deadline. A family hoping to keep Extended or Higher tier open should treat the end of Year 10 as the deadline for making it realistic, because after that the option closes administratively.

programmes.name: Year 11, converting knowledge into marks
programmes.description: In the examination year, almost all measurable improvement in mathematics comes from technique: showing method, pacing against marks, reading command words, and checking answers against the situation described. A student who can do the mathematics and loses eight marks a paper to habit is the commonest profile we see, and it is the fastest to improve.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June series, with November available as the resit route. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only and is not open to a Dubai candidate. Entry and tier decisions close months before the papers, so the useful question in the fourth term is what is already fixed rather than what could be.

programmes.name: Into A Level Mathematics or IB
programmes.description: IGCSE mathematics is the gateway to A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches, and schools set their own grade thresholds for entry, usually in the top bands and sometimes with a specific requirement on the Extended or Higher tier paper. A student aiming at either route needs one named grade rather than a strong overall profile.
programmes.countryNote: Additional Mathematics, where a Dubai school offers it, is the usual bridge into A Level or Higher Level work, and it is where the step up in algebraic demand first becomes visible. Students who find it uncomfortable have useful early information about which post-16 mathematics route will suit them.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-sustainab.subjectsIntro: What follows is the content map. These are the topic areas both specifications assess, with the specific thing that costs marks in each. A tutoring enquiry that names two of these is worth three that describe a general difficulty.

subjects.name: Number and accuracy
subjects.description: Standard form, upper and lower bounds, percentage change in both directions, and rounding to significant figures. Bounds questions are the reliable mark-loser: students calculate correctly and then select the wrong bound for a division. Reverse percentage questions are the second, because the instinct is to work forwards.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. This is the fluency layer the whole specification rests on, and slowness here produces errors in topics that have nothing to do with algebra. Quadratic factorising with a coefficient on the squared term is the single most common sticking point.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous equations
subjects.description: Simultaneous equations with one linear and one quadratic appear in the higher tiers and reward a methodical substitution. Inequality questions lose marks on the notation and on reversing the sign when multiplying by a negative, which is a habit rather than a gap.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, gradients, and reading information off a curve. Students frequently calculate a gradient correctly and then omit the units or the context, which is where the final mark sits. Transformation questions reward describing the change precisely rather than approximately.

subjects.name: Geometry, trigonometry and Pythagoras
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems in the higher tiers, and the choice between the sine rule, the cosine rule and basic trigonometry. The recurring error is applying a right-angle method to a triangle that has no right angle. Reasons must be stated in angle questions, and an unjustified correct answer scores less.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar shapes
subjects.description: Volume and surface area of composite solids, arcs and sectors, and length, area and volume scale factors. Scale-factor questions are consistently under-answered because students apply the length factor to an area or a volume, which is one of the most predictable lost marks in the whole specification.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability in the higher tiers, averages from grouped data, and cumulative frequency. Marks go missing when students answer a probability question by intuition instead of drawing the structure, and when grouped-data estimates are given as exact values.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and combined transformations. Vector proof questions reward writing the route around the shape explicitly; students who try to see the answer rather than construct it lose the method marks even when the conclusion is right.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: Current specifications include assessment without a calculator, and fluency with fractions, surds and index laws is assumed there. Students who have relied on a calculator throughout Year 10 discover this late. Confirm with your school which papers your child sits without one.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside or after IGCSE mathematics as preparation for A Level or Higher Level work. Calculus and trigonometric identities are the pressure points, and students who cope by pattern-matching rather than understanding fail precisely the unfamiliar questions that distinguish the top grades.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1, as a parent needs it
paragraphs: These are two different qualifications that cover broadly similar mathematics in different shapes, and the practical differences matter more than the content differences. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended, with Core capping the achievable grade and Extended reaching the top bands. Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher tiers, with two written papers at each tier, each two hours and each worth 100 marks, and a calculator permitted throughout.

Question style is where students feel the difference. Cambridge papers tend to carry a larger number of shorter questions, moving briskly between topics, which rewards breadth and penalises a student who is slow to switch context. Pearson papers more often build several parts on one scenario, which rewards a student who can follow a thread and penalises one who loses the context between parts. A student who performs well on one style will not necessarily perform well on the other, which is one reason past papers from the wrong board mislead.

The current Cambridge specification includes assessment without a calculator, which catches out students who have relied on one through Year 10. Because syllabus structures are revised, the paper numbers, durations and calculator rules should be confirmed with your school rather than taken from any website, including this one. What does not change is the practical advice: get the syllabus code from the examinations officer, then revise only from that board's past papers. Mixing the two sets is one of the most common causes of a student feeling unprepared despite having done a great deal of work.

sections.heading: The five topics that cost the most marks, and why
paragraphs: Across both specifications the same handful of topics generate most of the avoidable losses, and they are not the topics students fear. Students worry about circle theorems and vectors, which are hard but relatively well taught. The marks actually disappear in bounds, scale factors, reverse percentages, probability structure and inequality notation — topics that feel routine, get less revision time, and carry predictable traps that recur paper after paper.

Take scale factors, the clearest example. A question gives a length scale factor and asks for an area or a volume. The correct response squares or cubes the factor; the common response applies the length factor directly. Students who make this error almost always know the rule when asked directly, which means it is not a knowledge gap but a recognition failure: they did not notice which quantity the question asked about. That distinction changes the fix entirely, from teaching to question-reading practice.

Bounds behave the same way. A student calculates the upper and lower bound of each quantity correctly and then, dividing one by the other, selects the wrong combination for the maximum. It takes one session to explain and several weeks of repetition to make reliable. The table below lists the recurring traps with the fix, because a parent who knows these can check whether a tutor is actually working on them or just covering topics in order. If four sessions pass without any of these appearing, that is a reasonable question to ask.

sections.heading: Method marks: the cheapest grade improvement in the subject
paragraphs: Both specifications award method marks on multi-step questions. A student who writes only a final answer gets everything if it is right and nothing if it is wrong. A student who writes the method gets most of the marks even when the arithmetic slips at the last step. Over a two-hour paper that difference is routinely worth several marks, and several marks is frequently a grade boundary. Nothing else in mathematics tutoring is this cheap to fix.

The reason students resist is that writing method feels slow under time pressure, and at this age the instinct to save time is strong. The correction is not an explanation, because most students already understand the point when told. It is enforcement: every multi-step question in every session, with the tutor declining to look at an answer that arrives without working. Two to four weeks of that produces a habit that survives into the examination hall.

Reading a mark scheme with a student is the other half. Official schemes distinguish method marks from accuracy marks, and seeing their own answer against that breakdown is what converts an abstract instruction into a reason. A student who sees that three of five marks were available before any final answer tends to stop arguing about it. We work from the schemes the school legitimately holds and reference the boards' published material rather than distributing it. Once a student has seen two or three of their own answers broken down that way, the argument about writing method generally ends.

sections.heading: How a past paper should actually be worked
paragraphs: Most students use past papers as a familiarity exercise: attempt, check, feel reassured. That builds recognition rather than performance, and recognition fails under timing. The method that works is less comfortable. Attempt the question cold with no notes and a clock running. Mark it against the official scheme without charity. Write each lost mark as a reason rather than a number. Then rework only the reasons that repeat.

The classification matters more than the score. Content not known, command word misread, method not shown, arithmetic slip, and ran out of time are five different problems with five different fixes, and a student who records seventy-two percent has learned nothing actionable. A student who records that four of their eight lost marks were method marks has a plan for the week. This is the single habit that most distinguishes students whose mathematics improves from students who merely do more papers.

A practical note on volume. Four questions worked this way are worth more than a complete paper skimmed, and the first two weeks of any block we run are deliberately low on content for exactly this reason. Parents sometimes read that as slow progress. It is the diagnosis that makes the rest of the block efficient, and skipping it is how eight weeks of tutoring becomes eight weeks of general revision. sections.heading: One-to-one, a group class or a centre: what each can diagnose
paragraphs: The honest comparison here is not about price per hour but about what each format can detect. A one-to-one session can identify that a student knows the scale-factor rule but fails to notice which quantity the question asks for. A group class of eight cannot, because the teaching has to address the average and the quiet student's specific recognition failure never surfaces. That is the real difference, and it explains why a cheaper format sometimes produces no change at all.

Published Dubai rates frame the trade-off. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visiting rates run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, and one premium provider advertises AED 650.

For IGCSE mathematics specifically, the qualified online tier is usually the right purchase, because the work is diagnosis and enforcement rather than rare expertise. Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. All of these figures belong to the companies and rate guides that published them and were read in October 2026. IB Gram publishes no hourly list on these pages and quotes after a free trial.

sections.heading: The grade that decides the next course
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics is a gateway qualification, and the gate is specific. Schools in Dubai set their own entry requirements for A Level Mathematics and for IB Analysis and Approaches, usually in the top grade bands and sometimes with a condition on the Extended or Higher tier paper rather than on the overall grade. A student aiming at either route needs one named grade in one named subject, which is a much narrower target than a good profile across nine subjects.

That narrowness is useful, because it tells a family where to spend. A student targeting A Level Mathematics with a predicted 6 and a requirement of 7 has a precise, affordable problem. The same student spreading tutoring across four subjects to lift everything by half a grade has an expensive and diffuse one. Ask the school's head of sixth form or the Diploma coordinator for the exact threshold, in writing, before deciding where the money goes.

For UAE university plans there is a separate rule worth knowing. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. That is a minimum threshold rather than a competitive one, and it should not be confused with what a selective university actually asks for.

sections.heading: Timing a mathematics session in a Dubai week
paragraphs: Mathematics is less forgiving of fatigue than most subjects, because manipulation errors multiply when concentration drops and a session spent making avoidable slips teaches the wrong lesson. That makes session timing a practical variable rather than an administrative one. A student at school inside The Sustainable City can start at 3.30pm; a student travelling back from Motor City or Al Barsha is not realistically available until 5.30pm, and by seven the value of the hour has dropped noticeably.

The UAE week shapes the options. Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday leaves Saturday and Sunday as the only full days, which is why weekend sessions suit commuting households and why a two-hour weekend block is often the right format for whole-paper practice in the final term. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and the useful study window moves after Iftar, where a mathematics session frequently works better than any afternoon slot in that month.

On our side, slots are held in Gulf Standard Time, move after Iftar through Ramadan with the same tutor, and can pause during a school's own examination fortnight when additional sessions produce fatigue rather than marks. We do not rotate students between tutors to fill a diary. In mathematics the tutor's accumulated knowledge of which operation a student gets wrong under pressure is most of the value, and it takes weeks to rebuild with somebody new. That is also why we would rather hold one protected slot all year than fill a diary with sessions that keep moving.

faqs.question: How do we find out whether our child sits 0580 or 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Email the school's examinations officer rather than the subject teacher and ask for the syllabus code and the tier. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended tiers; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers. The codes matter because the papers differ in length, calculator rules and question style, and past papers do not transfer between them. It takes a day to establish and saves the first two sessions from being spent on the wrong board's question style.

faqs.question: Which five IGCSE maths topics cost students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Not the ones students fear. Across both specifications the avoidable losses cluster in length, area and volume scale factors, upper and lower bounds, reverse percentages, probability questions answered without drawing a tree or table, and inequalities where the sign is not reversed when multiplying by a negative. All five feel routine, which is why they get less revision time, and all five carry traps that recur paper after paper. Students usually know the rules when asked directly, which means the fix is question-reading practice rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks when he can do the maths?
faqs.answer: Most often because he writes only the final answer. Both specifications award method marks across multi-step questions, so an answer arriving alone scores everything when right and nothing when wrong, while written method scores most of the marks even when the last line slips. Over a two-hour paper that is routinely worth several marks and several marks is frequently a grade boundary. It takes two to four weeks of enforcement rather than explanation, because it is a habit rather than a misunderstanding.

faqs.question: Does the calculator rule differ between the two boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it catches families out. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout its two papers. The current Cambridge specification includes assessment without one, which is a problem for students who have relied on a calculator through Year 10 and have let fraction, surd and index fluency lapse. Because syllabus structures are revised periodically, confirm the paper arrangements with your school rather than relying on any website, then make sure revision practice matches the conditions your child will actually sit under.

faqs.question: What is the right way to use an IGCSE maths past paper?
faqs.answer: Attempt the question cold with no notes and a clock running, then mark it against the official scheme without charity, writing each lost mark as a reason rather than a number: content not known, command word misread, method not shown, arithmetic slip, or ran out of time. Then rework only the reasons that repeat. Four questions processed this way are worth more than a whole paper skimmed, because a percentage score is not actionable and a classified list of causes is a plan for the week.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a centre a reasonable alternative to one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends on the problem rather than the budget. A group class can address gaps common to the group, and that is genuinely useful for broad revision. What it cannot detect is an individual recognition failure — a student who knows the scale-factor rule but never notices which quantity the question asks for will stay silent in a class of eight and the error will persist. If a specific question type keeps failing, one-to-one is what finds the cause; if the issue is general coverage, a class may be enough.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Year 10. Will tutoring now actually help in Year 11?
faqs.answer: More than it will in Year 11 itself, in most cases. Year 10 is when content is met for the first time, when the habits that decide the final grade form, and when internal results feed the tier decision for Year 11. Fixing algebraic fluency or method-writing while the content is new takes a handful of sessions; the same gap in the fifth term has to be fixed while five other subjects compete for the hours and a predicted grade is already recorded. The gap does not change, only the cost of closing it.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for IGCSE maths tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates put qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included. For IGCSE mathematics the qualified online tier is usually the right purchase, because the work is diagnosis and enforcement. Those figures were read in October 2026 and are the market's, not ours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work effectively on mathematics over video?
faqs.answer: Mathematics is the subject where online works best, because the whole discipline is the working on the page and a shared whiteboard shows that working as it appears. The tutor sees the line where the student hesitates, which is exactly the diagnostic information needed. Questions shared on screen and annotated step by step reproduce what happens on paper closely. The honest exception is younger children, roughly Year 5 and below, who often need an adult physically present for reasons unconnected to the subject.

faqs.question: What grade does my child need for A Level Maths or IB Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: That is set by the school rather than by the board, usually in the top grade bands and sometimes with a condition on the Extended or Higher tier paper specifically rather than the overall grade. Ask the head of sixth form or the Diploma coordinator for the threshold in writing before deciding where tutoring money goes, because a student needing one named grade in one subject has a precise and affordable problem, while a family lifting four subjects by half a grade has an expensive and diffuse one.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth taking if the school offers it?
faqs.answer: For a student heading towards A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, usually yes, because it is where the step up in algebraic demand becomes visible while there is still time to respond to it. Calculus and trigonometric identities are the pressure points. A student who finds it genuinely uncomfortable has learned something valuable early about which post-16 mathematics route will suit them, which is worth more than the grade itself. For a student not continuing with mathematics, the time is usually better spent elsewhere.

faqs.question: Can we start with one session a week and increase later?
faqs.answer: That is what we would recommend. One weekly session with real between-session work beats two sessions that displace the work, and in mathematics the between-session repetition is where fluency actually improves. We increase to two in the weeks before a mock block or the series, and we increase sooner if the diagnosis shows a content gap rather than a habit problem. Starting at two and discovering the student cannot absorb it wastes a month and sours the arrangement.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa if we are willing to pay the premium?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, at any price, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Sustainable City or any neighbouring community. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard. Home tutoring is a service we operate in India only. For mathematics the format difference is minimal, because the working is visible either way, and the gain is that the tutor is chosen for the specification they teach rather than for the distance they can drive at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: Do you hand out past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright. We reference them, point to the official sources, and work from material your child's school legitimately holds, with questions shown on screen during sessions. A service advertising an unlimited paper bank raises a fair question about provenance. The school's own holdings are also the papers your child will be marked against, so they are the better source in practice as well as the correct one.

faqs.question: How soon should we see marks move?
faqs.answer: For a habit problem such as unwritten method, about three to four weeks, because it shows up directly in the next marked paper. Fluency problems take four to eight weeks since they improve through repetition rather than instruction. Genuine content gaps take one to three weeks per topic. Each session note records which error classes appeared, so the trend is visible in the record rather than in anecdote. We publish no improvement statistics, because a figure with no sample size, date or method is marketing rather than evidence.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-sustainab.closingBody: Send the syllabus code and tier, and a photograph of a recently marked paper. Those two things are usually enough to name the three topics costing the marks and the error classes behind them, which is where the first month of sessions should go. Next is a free trial lesson on the weakest topic with the tutor who would continue, then a short written plan listing the specific topics and the date it counts back from. Lessons run one-to-one over live video into The Sustainable City in Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. If the target grade is not reachable in the time left, we will say so first.

Each is matched to a code and tier, and each plan is built from where your child sits in the six-term course rather than from a generic revision schedule.

intro.heading: Six terms, and each one assumes the last one worked
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where a calendar matters most, because the content is cumulative in a way that history and biology are not. A student who never secured negative-number arithmetic will meet it again in algebra, then in coordinate geometry, then in trigonometry, and the same weakness will cost marks in all three. That is why the useful question is not whether your child needs a maths tutor but which term they are in and which prerequisite the next term assumes.

This page therefore maps the two-year course by term: the topics that typically arrive in each, the fluency each one takes for granted, and the specific signal that tells a parent the plan has slipped. It then counts backwards from the June series — tier and entry deadlines, the mock block, the final ten weeks — and sets out how the November resit decision actually works, because it is made within weeks of results rather than at leisure.

The Valley adds one structural complication worth naming early. This is a newer community on the road to Al Ain with no school inside its own boundary at the time of writing, so children here travel outward in two directions and attend several different schools. Schools teach the same specification in different topic orders, which means a mid-year move — common in this community — leaves a student with two or three genuinely unmet topics while two or three others have been covered twice over.

Two facts set the outer edges of any plan. Cambridge International examines IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and its February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route for a candidate sitting in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Entry decisions, including Core against Extended or Foundation against Higher, close months before the papers and are made by the school on the board's schedule.

Delivery is stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard where the working appears as it is written and questions shared on screen. Home visits exist in our India operation only. For mathematics the format costs almost nothing, because the diagnostic information a tutor needs is the line where the student stops being sure. It also removes the two car journeys either side of a visit, which in a household where the school run has already taken an hour from the day is the difference between a session a student can use and one they merely sit through.

programmes.name: Year 9, the prerequisite year
programmes.description: Nothing is externally assessed, which is exactly why this is the cheapest year to intervene. The specification assumes fluency with negatives, fractions, index laws and rearranging, and a student who has to think about those cannot think about the problem containing them. All of it is fixable in a term here and expensive to fix in Year 11.

A child joining a British-curriculum school in Year 9 usually has two or three specific unmet topics rather than a general weakness, and naming them before the IGCSE course begins is the cheapest intervention available in this community.

programmes.name: Year 10, terms one to three
programmes.description: Content arrives for the first time and the habits that decide the grade form here: writing method out, checking a result against the context, distinguishing a question type from a question. Internal examinations at the end of the year inform the tier decision for Year 11, which has an entry deadline attached rather than being an opinion.
programmes.countryNote: Because Valley children attend several different schools, the timing of internal examinations and tier decisions differs between neighbours. A family hoping to keep Extended or Higher tier open should ask its own school when entries are finalised, since a reassurance from the house opposite carries no information about a different school's timetable.

programmes.name: Year 11, terms four to six
programmes.description: One mock block, entries closing months ahead of the papers, predicted grades drawn from the mocks, then study leave and the series. Almost all measurable improvement in this year is technique: showing method, pacing against marks, reading command words, and checking an answer against the situation described rather than against a feeling.
programmes.countryNote: For Valley students the commute is the binding constraint on this year. One protected weekday evening for content and a weekend block for whole papers is the structure that survives all three terms; two weekday hours in a household with a long school run usually ends with the second cancelled and the between-session work undone.

programmes.description: The November series is the planned resit route for a Dubai candidate who misses a grade in June, and the entry closes months before the papers, so the decision is made within weeks of results. Separately, schools set their own thresholds for A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches, usually in the top bands.

Ask the school about entry deadlines in the week results arrive rather than a month later, when the window may have closed.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-valley.subjectsIntro: The content map, organised by the fluency each area assumes. An enquiry naming two of these areas is worth three describing a general difficulty with mathematics.

subjects.name: Number and accuracy
subjects.description: Standard form, upper and lower bounds, percentage change in both directions and significant figures. Bounds questions are the reliable loser: students calculate both bounds correctly then select the wrong combination for a division. Reverse percentage questions lose marks because the instinct is to work forwards.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. This is the fluency layer the whole specification rests on, and slowness here produces errors in topics that have nothing to do with algebra. Factorising a quadratic with a coefficient on the squared term is the single commonest sticking point.

subjects.name: Equations and simultaneous equations
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic pairs appear in the higher tiers and reward methodical substitution. Inequality questions lose marks on notation and on failing to reverse the sign when multiplying by a negative, which is a habit rather than a gap in understanding.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, gradients and reading information from a curve. Students frequently compute a gradient correctly then omit the units or the contextual meaning, which is where the final mark sits. Transformation questions reward precise description rather than approximate description.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems in the higher tiers, and choosing between the sine rule, the cosine rule and basic trigonometry. The recurring error is applying a right-angle method to a triangle that has no right angle, and an unjustified correct answer in an angle question scores below a justified one.

subjects.name: Mensuration and scale factors
subjects.description: Composite solids, arcs and sectors, and length, area and volume scale factors. Scale-factor questions are consistently under-answered because students apply the length factor to an area or volume, which is one of the most predictable lost marks in the whole specification.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability at the higher tiers, averages from grouped data and cumulative frequency. Marks disappear when a probability question is answered by instinct rather than by drawing the structure, and when grouped-data estimates are presented as exact values.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and combined transformations. Vector proofs reward writing the route around the shape explicitly; students who try to see the answer rather than construct it lose the method marks even when the conclusion is correct.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fluency
subjects.description: Current specifications include assessment without a calculator, where fluency with fractions, surds and index laws is assumed. Students who relied on a calculator through Year 10 discover this late. Confirm with your school which papers your child sits without one.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside or after IGCSE mathematics as preparation for A Level or Higher Level study. Calculus and trigonometric identities are the pressure points, and students who cope by pattern-matching fail the unfamiliar questions that separate the top grades.

sections.heading: The two-year course, term by term, with the prerequisite each term assumes
paragraphs: This is the table that explains why mathematics goes wrong gradually. Each term introduces topics that assume fluency built earlier, so a gap does not stay where it started: it reappears in a new disguise every few months. A student who never secured rearranging will meet it in equations, then in formulae, then in trigonometry and then in every physics calculation, and each appearance looks like a new problem to a parent reading a report.

Schools vary in topic order, which matters in this community specifically because children here attend several different schools and families move in mid-year. Two students in the same street can be two topics apart in the same specification. That is why we ask for the school's scheme of work or at least the current topic rather than assuming a sequence, and why a mid-year arrival needs a diagnostic rather than a general catch-up programme.

The behind-schedule signals in the final column are deliberately specific, because general worry is not actionable. Finding this term's work hard is normal. Being unable to do last term's work unprompted is a retention problem that will compound, and that is the point at which a term of weekly sessions costs far less than the alternative eighteen months later. Parents who use that column as a termly check rarely end up buying the expensive version of the same repair, because they catch the gap in the term it appears rather than two years later.

sections.heading: The countdown to the June series
paragraphs: Read this sequence from the bottom up and the planning logic becomes clear. The series dates are fixed by the board. Study leave is fixed by the school. The mock block sits a term before study leave because predicted grades depend on it. Entries, including the tier, close before all of that. And the internal Year 10 examinations that inform the tier decision sit a year earlier still, which is why the cheap interventions are all early.

The deadline families most often meet by accident is the tier entry. Core against Extended in a Cambridge subject, or Foundation against Higher in Pearson, is decided by the school against the board's schedule and is not adjustable in the examination hall. By the time a parent is worried about a grade in the final term, the achievable ceiling may already be fixed. In The Valley this needs asking about directly, because schools in the two travel directions work to different internal timetables.

One thing to avoid is building a revision plan from dates copied off a website. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, and Cambridge allocates centres to administrative zones with separate timetable versions, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong version was used. The school's published timetable is the authority; the board's live timetable page is the backup. What does not change from year to year is the order of events in the table below, which is the part a family can plan against.

sections.heading: The final ten weeks, week by week
paragraphs: The last stretch before study leave is the part families most want help with and the part most often spent badly, usually on re-teaching content that cannot be absorbed in time. The highest-yield work in this window is technique, because technique transfers across every question on the paper while a newly met topic might appear once. A student who fixes method discipline and pacing in ten weeks will gain more marks than one who covers three new topics.

The shape below is what we run. It begins with two diagnostic weeks that look slower than parents expect: timed questions rather than teaching, with lost marks classified by reason rather than counted. That classification is what makes the following eight weeks efficient. Skipping it to feel productive is the commonest and most expensive mistake in short-block mathematics tutoring, because the work then addresses assumed gaps instead of real ones.

The between-session work carries at least as much weight as the sessions, and in a commuting household it has to be realistic. One tutored hour is roughly one per cent of a student's week. Each session here sets a named output — three questions on one topic, attempted under timing and self-marked against the official scheme, corrections brought back next time — rather than an instruction to revise. A family treating the hour as the whole intervention gets a fraction of the result that a family treating it as a weekly planning meeting gets.

sections.heading: Mid-year arrivals and the topic-order problem
paragraphs: This is a Valley-specific section because the community is new and still filling, which means a high proportion of its students have changed school within the last year or two. Schools teach the same specification in different orders. One covers trigonometry in the second term of Year 10 and circle theorems in Year 11; another does the reverse. A student moving between them does not arrive behind or ahead; they arrive with a jagged profile, strong in most places and missing two or three specific things.

That distinction matters because the remedy is different. A student who is behind needs a sustained catch-up programme. A student with a jagged profile needs two or three specific topics taught and the rest left alone, which is a fraction of the work and a fraction of the cost. Families frequently buy the former when they need the latter, usually because nobody has looked at the two schemes of work side by side.

The diagnostic is straightforward and worth doing in the first term after a move. Ask both schools for the topic sequence if possible, or simply work through a mixed-topic paper and record which topics the student cannot start. The pattern is usually obvious: three topics unmet, two topics covered twice, everything else intact. Done early that is a half-term of targeted work; discovered in Year 11 it competes with five other subjects and a mock block, and the same three topics then cost three times as much to close.

sections.heading: The November series as a planned route
paragraphs: Most families first hear about the November series in the week June results arrive, which is late but not fatal. For a Dubai candidate it is the resit route: Cambridge examines in June and November, and the February and March series is India-only, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The entry closes months before the papers, so the decision has to be made quickly rather than considered over a term.

Whether it is worth entering depends on one question: does the intended next step actually require that grade. A student who needs a specific mathematics grade for A Level Mathematics, for IB Analysis and Approaches, or for a named post-16 route has a clear reason. A student who has moved on to a programme that does not need it rarely gains enough to justify a term of work. Ask the school's head of sixth form before deciding, in the week results arrive.

If a resit is the plan, the work is almost entirely technique rather than content, because the content has already been taught twice. Pearson's published history is a useful guide to the rhythm of the thing: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That means a student entering in November is working to a result that arrives in the following January, which has implications for post-16 applications worth checking with the school at the same time as the entry itself.

sections.heading: What each stage costs, and where the money works hardest
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. Specialists in IGCSE and A Level are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included.

For IGCSE mathematics the qualified online tier is usually the right purchase, because the work is diagnosis and enforcement rather than rare expertise. The more useful question is when rather than how much. A term of prerequisite work in Year 9 or early Year 10 costs the same per hour as a crash course in term six and achieves considerably more, because it prevents the gaps the crash course then cannot close.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, with monthly packages advertised at AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. sections.heading: Materials, honesty and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright. We reference them, cite the official sources, and work from material your child's school legitimately holds, with questions shown on screen during sessions. A service advertising an unlimited paper bank invites a fair question about provenance, and the school's own holdings are in any case the papers your child will be marked against.

Where a subject carries assessed work completed outside the examination hall, the boundary is explicit: submitted work must be the student's own and is authenticated by the school. A tutor may teach the content, explain the criteria, question a method and comment on the student's own writing. A tutor may not write any part of a submission, redraft to completion, or supply a model to be edited. One operation in this market sells completed internal assessments for another qualification at AED 3,750, which establishes what the trade costs and why it should be refused.

On regulators: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with ADEK in Abu Dhabi, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them or from Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE office. An individual tutoring privately in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.
