sections.heading: Fitting mathematics into a Valley week
paragraphs: Mathematics is less forgiving of fatigue than most subjects, because tired students make manipulation errors they would not otherwise make and then those errors get reviewed as though they were real. With no school inside this community, a secondary student is realistically home around a quarter past five, and the value of an hour drops noticeably after seven. That makes session timing a planning variable rather than an administrative detail.

The structure that works splits the work by its needs. Fluency drilling benefits from frequency rather than length, so two short weekday slots beat one long one where a household can manage it, and short daily between-session sets matter more than the length of any single session. Whole papers and mark-scheme review need uninterrupted time, which in this community genuinely exists only at the weekend. One weekday slot plus one weekend block is the pattern that lasts.

The UAE calendar shapes the rest. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, leaving Saturday and Sunday as the only full days. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the productive window moves after Iftar, where a mathematics session is frequently better than any afternoon slot in that month. We hold slots in Gulf Standard Time, move them after Iftar with the same tutor retained, and pause blocks during a school's own examination fortnight rather than adding sessions that produce fatigue. We also keep the same tutor across a term rather than rotating students to fill a diary, because knowing which operation a particular student rushes under pressure is most of what makes a later session efficient.

process.description: Schools teach the specification in different orders, so knowing what is being taught this week matters. A photograph of recently marked work is the rest of the diagnosis, because mathematics losses are visible on the page rather than inferred from a description.

process.description: Run by the tutor who would continue, on a topic the student currently fails rather than one they can perform. It ends with the tutor naming the first two topics they would address and roughly how long each should take. If the match is wrong, we propose someone else.

process.description: Each note records which error classes appeared — content, command word, method, arithmetic or timing — rather than which topics were covered. Over a month those classes either thin out or they do not, and if they do not we change the approach or the tutor.

whyPoints.title: Planned by term, not by panic
whyPoints.description: Mathematics is cumulative, so the work in Year 10 term two and Year 11 term five is genuinely different. We plan from where your child sits in the six-term course, which is what prevents a family buying revision when a prerequisite needed closing.

whyPoints.title: Topic order checked, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Schools teach the same specification in different sequences, and in a community where families move in mid-year that produces jagged profiles rather than general weakness. We diagnose which, because the two need completely different amounts of work.

whyPoints.title: Tier deadlines flagged early

faqs.question: Which term should we start IGCSE maths tutoring in?
faqs.answer: Year 9 or the first term of Year 10 if the aim is to prevent problems, because mathematics is cumulative and every later topic inherits the fluency layer beneath it. A student who never secured rearranging will meet that gap in equations, then formulae, then trigonometry, and each appearance looks like a new problem on a report. Fixing it before the IGCSE course begins takes a handful of sessions; fixing it in term five means competing with five other subjects and a mock block already behind you.

faqs.question: Why does my son seem to struggle with a different maths topic every term?
faqs.answer: Usually because it is the same gap wearing different clothes. The specification is cumulative, so weak fluency in negatives, fractions, index laws or rearranging reappears in algebra, then in graphs, then in trigonometry, and each time it looks like a new topic failing. The diagnosis is straightforward from a mixed-topic paper: record which questions he cannot start as against which he starts correctly and then slips in. The second pattern is a fluency problem and it is fixable in four to eight weeks.

faqs.question: When does the tier decision close, and can we influence it?
faqs.answer: The school decides the entry against the board's schedule, usually informed by internal Year 10 examinations, and it is not adjustable in the examination hall. Core caps the achievable grade in Cambridge subjects while Extended reaches the top bands; Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers in some subjects. You can influence it only while there is still time to change the evidence, which means Year 10. Ask your own school when entries are finalised, because schools in the two travel directions from The Valley work to different internal timetables.

faqs.question: We moved school mid-year and the topics do not line up. How much work is that?
faqs.answer: Usually much less than it looks. Schools teach the same specification in different orders, so a mid-year arrival typically has two or three genuinely unmet topics and two or three covered twice, rather than being behind overall. That is a jagged profile rather than a deficit, and the fix is those specific topics taught and the rest left alone — about half a term of targeted work. Families often buy a sustained catch-up programme when they need a short diagnostic and three topics.

faqs.question: What should the last ten weeks before the June series contain?
faqs.answer: Technique rather than content, because technique transfers across every question on the paper while a newly met topic might appear once. The shape that works is two diagnostic weeks of timed questions with losses classified by reason, then four weeks on the highest-mark recurring topics and method discipline, then non-calculator fluency where the specification requires it, then whole papers under timing for the final fortnight. Re-teaching a whole course in that window is the standard way the time gets wasted.

faqs.question: Is the November series worth entering if June goes badly?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the intended next step requires that specific grade. A student needing a named mathematics grade for A Level Mathematics, IB Analysis and Approaches or another post-16 route has a clear reason; a student who has moved on to something that does not need it usually does not. The entry closes months before the papers, so the decision is made within weeks of results rather than at leisure. Ask the head of sixth form in the week results arrive, not a month later.

faqs.question: How do we know which calculator rules apply to our child's papers?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer, because the boards differ. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout its two papers, while the current Cambridge specification includes assessment without one, which catches out students who relied on a calculator through Year 10 and let fraction, surd and index fluency lapse. Specifications are revised periodically, so confirm with the school rather than relying on any website. Then make sure revision practice matches the conditions your child will actually sit under, which is where the marks are lost.

faqs.question: Does it matter that no tutor lives in The Valley itself?
faqs.answer: Not for mathematics. There is no school inside this community at the time of writing, so there is no local cohort and no school-gate network recommending subject specialists, which means a proximity search returns almost nothing here. What matters is whether the tutor teaches your child's specification and tier and can diagnose where marks are going. IB Gram delivers online one-to-one and sends no tutors to UAE addresses, which is what makes a specification-matched tutor available at all in this neighbourhood.

faqs.question: Should a maths session be on a weekday or at the weekend?
faqs.answer: Both, if the household can manage it, and for different work. Fluency drilling benefits from frequency rather than length, so a short weekday slot plus daily between-session sets is the right shape for manipulation. Whole papers and mark-scheme review need uninterrupted time, which in a community with a long outbound school run genuinely exists only at the weekend. One weekday slot and one weekend block is the pattern that survives all three terms of Year 11 here.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for a term of maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: At the published market rate for a qualified online subject tutor of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, one weekly session across a twelve to fourteen week term comes to roughly AED 1,800 to AED 4,200 in a single subject, and Bestimate's monthly estimate for one weekly hour is AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. The more useful question is when: the same money spent in Year 10 prevents gaps that the same money spent in term six cannot close. Those figures were read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Our son writes almost nothing down. How much is that costing him?
faqs.answer: Because both specifications award method marks across multi-step questions, so a student who writes only the final answer forfeits all of them whenever the answer is wrong and gains nothing when it is right. Over a two-hour paper that is routinely worth several marks, and several marks is frequently a grade boundary. It takes two to four weeks of enforcement rather than one explanation, since it is a habit. It is the cheapest grade improvement available in IGCSE mathematics.

faqs.question: Our school offers Additional Mathematics. Should our daughter take it?
faqs.answer: For a student heading towards A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches, usually yes, because it is where the step up in algebraic demand becomes visible while there is still time to respond to it. Calculus and trigonometric identities are the pressure points. A student who finds it genuinely uncomfortable has learned something useful early about which post-16 mathematics route suits them. For a student not continuing with mathematics, the same hours are generally better spent elsewhere.

faqs.question: Can you work from our school's scheme of work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we ask for it or at least for the current topic, because schools teach the same specification in different orders and a tutor running a parallel sequence makes a student hold two courses at once. Sessions are sequenced against what the school is teaching that week, so the tutoring reinforces rather than duplicates. In this community that matters more than usual, since children here attend several different schools and no two are necessarily at the same point.

faqs.question: What happens in the first two sessions?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis rather than teaching, which parents sometimes read as slow progress. The student attempts timed questions across mixed topics, the work is marked without charity, and each lost mark is recorded as a reason rather than a number: content not known, command word misread, method not shown, arithmetic slip, or ran out of time. That classification is what makes the following weeks efficient, because the work then addresses the real gaps instead of the assumed ones.

faqs.question: Do you publish success rates for IGCSE maths students?
faqs.answer: No, because a figure without a sample size, a date and a method is a marketing claim rather than evidence. Several providers in this market publish self-asserted ratings that differ from their own page text. What we publish instead is checkable: the syllabus codes, the series open to UAE candidates, the AED bands with their publishers and the month read, and a plain statement of the approvals we do not hold. Progress in an individual case is visible in the session notes rather than in a percentage.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-views.tutorsIntro: Mathematics is the first subject Views families fund and the one they most often fund blind. Tutors here are matched on the awarding body, the syllabus code and the tier, because the paper your child will actually open in May is the only thing worth preparing for.

intro.heading: Five qualifications, one word, and the question nobody asks the school
paragraphs: The honest version of your search is this: you want somebody within reach who knows the paper your child is sitting. The reach part is easy to solve and the knowing part is where this market quietly fails. Within a short drive of Emirates Golf Club there are capable mathematics teachers and a number of tuition centres. What is much harder to find locally, free on the evening you have available, is somebody who can tell you without hesitating whether your child is entered for Cambridge 0580 or 0980, whether the tier caps the grade at C or at 5, and which of the two papers is sat without a calculator.

That is not pedantry. A Views student could be sitting Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, graded A* to G. They could be sitting 0980, which is the same mathematics graded 9 to 1. They could be sitting Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, which assumes a graphic display calculator throughout and is favoured by schools pointing children at the IB. They could be taking Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 alongside the main course. Or they could be on Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A, 4MA1, with Foundation and Higher tiers and a different paper structure again. Dubai schools choose subject by subject, and splitting boards across a timetable is ordinary here.

Get the code wrong and a tutor still teaches useful mathematics. They simply teach it in the wrong proportions, with the wrong calculator policy, towards the wrong paper. A student preparing for a two-hour Pearson Higher paper and a student preparing for a Cambridge Extended non-calculator paper need different work in the last ten weeks, and the difference is worth grades rather than marks.

So IB Gram drops proximity as a criterion and keeps the two that decide whether an hour helps: the code and the tier. The lesson arrives over live video, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor weekly and a written note afterwards. Nobody drives to a Views tower; in-home visiting is a service we run in India only. For mathematics that is a straightforward gain, because the work is shared-screen work: a past-paper question opened beside its mark scheme, a solution written out line by line so the method marks are visible, a graph replotted until the scale is right.

The rest of this page is a reference you can use against any tutor, ours included. It sets out the five qualifications and who sits them, the paper structures by board, the dozen topics that cost Views students the most marks, why method marks decide more grades than knowledge does, and what the jump to Diploma mathematics actually requires. It gives you questions that separate somebody who teaches the paper from somebody who is good at mathematics, and it shows you how to verify any AED rate you are quoted against figures already published in this market.

What it does not do is reproduce board material. Cambridge and Pearson past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables are their copyright; we reference them, cite the official pages and work from what your child legitimately has. We publish no grade guarantee and claim no approval from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA or the Ministry of Education, because IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and holds none.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-views.programmesIntro: Before a tutor is useful, somebody has to establish which qualification is on the entry. These are the five that turn up on Dubai school entries, with what each one is for.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The default British-curriculum mathematics qualification, offered in two graded forms: 0580 reported A* to G and 0980 reported 9 to 1, with the same subject content. Each is tiered. A Core entry sits two papers and is capped at grade C, or grade 5 in the 9 to 1 version. An Extended entry sits two harder papers and reaches A* or grade 9. From the 2025 series Cambridge included a non-calculator paper in this syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: This is what most Views students sitting Cambridge mathematics are entered for, and the grading version differs between schools in the same neighbourhood. Ask which one appears on the statement of entry, because a parent comparing a child's grade 6 with a cousin's grade B is comparing two different scales of the same qualification.

programmes.name: Cambridge International Mathematics
programmes.description: A separate Cambridge syllabus built around technology use, with a graphic display calculator assumed throughout rather than permitted on one paper. Also tiered into Core and Extended. The emphasis falls on modelling, interpretation and using a device deliberately, which makes it a markedly different preparation from 0580 even where the topic list looks similar.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running the IB continuum, or planning to, often enter students for 0607 because it feeds Diploma mathematics more naturally than 0580 does. A Views family whose child is on 0607 and is being tutored from 0580 past papers is being prepared for the wrong examination, and the mismatch is easy to miss.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Taken alongside the main IGCSE by strong mathematicians, covering material that overlaps the start of A Level and Diploma Higher Level: calculus, trigonometric identities, series and functions handled formally. Calculators are permitted. It is not a replacement for the main qualification but an extension of it.
programmes.countryNote: The best single preparation available for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and the reason some Views students arrive in DP1 comfortable while classmates with the same main grade struggle. Where a school offers it, it is worth asking whether your child should be in the set.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Two papers of two hours each, both with a calculator permitted, tiered into Foundation and Higher. Foundation is capped at grade 5 and Higher reaches grade 9 with an allowed grade 3 below the normal floor. Pearson offers series in May or June and in November each year, with results dates published for each series.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools serving Emirates Living enter mathematics with Pearson while using Cambridge for sciences, so a Views household can legitimately have two boards on one timetable. The two-hour paper length is itself a preparation issue: stamina across two long papers is a different skill from four shorter ones.

programmes.name: Pearson Further Pure Mathematics
programmes.description: Pearson's extension qualification, the counterpart to Cambridge 0606. Two papers covering calculus, series, coordinate geometry and trigonometry at a level that overlaps the first term of A Level or Diploma Higher Level mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Less commonly offered in Dubai than 0606 but present in some schools. Students who sit it tend to find the transition into Higher Level mathematics the easiest of any route, which is worth knowing when a school asks whether your child should take an extra mathematics option in Year 11.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-the-views.subjectsIntro: Mathematics rarely arrives on its own. These are the IGCSE subjects most often tutored alongside it for Views students, with the specific thing each one needs rather than a general description.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The subject funded first in most households. Marks are lost to method rather than knowledge: answers reached by an unfollowable route, algebra skipped three lines at a time, and a non-calculator paper met by a student who has not worked without a device since Year 9.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Extension courses taken alongside the main paper. The content overlaps the start of A Level and Diploma Higher Level, so the marks lost here are usually in formal notation and in sustaining a multi-step argument rather than in the individual techniques.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject whose problems most often turn out to be mathematical. A student who cannot rearrange a formula confidently will fail physics questions they understand, and the repair belongs in the mathematics session rather than the physics one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic is the first obstacle and it is proportional reasoning in disguise. Students who struggle with ratio in mathematics struggle with moles in chemistry, and tutoring one usually improves the other without being asked to.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline and answer length, plus the statistics and experimental-design strands that get far less practice time than they carry in marks. Magnification and scale calculations are a recurring quiet loss.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading summary carry most of the marks and respond faster to coaching than any other IGCSE component. A student who learns to plan for four minutes before writing typically gains more per hour here than anywhere else.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram precision and data response. The quantitative questions on elasticity and index numbers are where a mathematically shaky student concedes marks without noticing, which is why it pairs so often with mathematics tutoring.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Break-even, cash flow and ratio analysis are mathematics questions inside a business paper. Students who can define the terms and not compute the figures lose the higher-band marks, and the fix is arithmetic confidence rather than more business theory.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and data representation. Binary and hexadecimal conversion is pure number work, and students weak in place value in mathematics are weak in it here, in the same way and for the same reason.

subjects.name: ICT
subjects.description: Spreadsheet formulas and data handling in the practical papers. The theory paper rewards precise vocabulary that students approximate, and the practical papers reward exactly the deliberate, step-checking habit mathematics tutoring tends to build.

sections.heading: Five qualifications, one name: what your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a Views parent can do before buying any mathematics tutoring is find the statement of entry or an exam entry letter and read the code on it. It takes two minutes and it determines whether an hour of tutoring is aimed at the right paper.

Cambridge offers the mainstream syllabus in two graded versions. 0580 is reported on the A* to G scale and 0980 reports the identical content on the 9 to 1 scale. Schools in the same part of Dubai choose differently, which is why two Views children in the same year can hold grades that are not directly comparable. Both are tiered: a Core entry sits two papers and cannot be awarded above grade C, or grade 5 on the numbered scale, while an Extended entry reaches A* or grade 9. From the 2025 series Cambridge included a non-calculator paper in this syllabus, a change that caught a cohort of students who had worked with a device for every assessment since Year 7.

Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is a different syllabus rather than a variant. A graphic display calculator is assumed throughout, and the emphasis sits on modelling and interpretation. Schools running or planning the IB continuum frequently prefer it because it leads into Diploma mathematics more naturally. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A, 4MA1, takes a third approach: two papers of two hours, calculators permitted on both, Foundation capped at grade 5 and Higher reaching grade 9 with an allowed grade 3. And alongside any of these sit the extension qualifications, Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4MB1, taken by students heading for Higher Level or A Level.

One caution applies to everything in this section. Awarding bodies revise syllabuses, change paper structures and move assessment models, and a tutoring page is not the authority on any of it. Check the current specification on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com, and confirm the entry with your child's school. We reference those documents rather than reproducing them, because they are the boards' copyright.

sections.heading: What the papers look like, and why stamina is a separate skill
paragraphs: Two students can cover the same topics and still be unprepared for each other's examination, because the shape of the paper is itself a thing to train for. The number of papers, their length and whether a device is permitted change how a student should revise in the final six weeks.

A Pearson 4MA1 candidate sits two papers of two hours with a calculator on both. The challenge there is endurance and consistency: a hundred marks in a single sitting, with the back end of the paper carrying the harder multi-step questions at exactly the point concentration is fading. Practice has to include whole papers to time, not question sets, because a student who scores well on twenty-minute sections and fades after ninety minutes has a problem no amount of topic revision will reveal.

A Cambridge Extended candidate sits two papers as well, one of them without a calculator since the 2025 series. The challenge is different: the non-calculator paper exposes arithmetic and algebraic fluency directly, and a student who has typed every calculation since Year 7 will lose marks on work they understand perfectly. The fix is mechanical and slightly tedious, which is why schools rarely have time for it and why it is one of the better uses of a paid hour.

A 0607 candidate faces a third situation again: the device is assumed rather than permitted, so questions are written on the premise that computation is free and interpretation is the assessed skill. Preparing a 0607 student from 0580 papers under-trains exactly the thing they will be marked on. The table sets out the shapes side by side so you can see which preparation your child's entry actually calls for.

sections.heading: The dozen topics that cost Views students the most marks
paragraphs: Across the IGCSE mathematics students we see from Emirates Living, lost marks concentrate in a short list of topics, and the list is stable enough to plan against. Knowing it lets a family use a limited number of paid hours on the places where the marks actually are instead of revising from page one.

At the top sits algebraic manipulation in all its forms: expanding and factorising, rearranging a formula to change the subject, and algebraic fractions. These are not topics so much as a skill every other topic hides inside it, which is why a student can appear to have a problem with trigonometry and in fact have a problem with rearranging. Simultaneous equations and quadratics follow, especially where a question requires choosing a method rather than applying the one just taught.

The second cluster is proportional reasoning: ratio, direct and inverse proportion, percentage change and reverse percentages, and compound interest. Reverse percentage questions are reliably the worst-answered on any paper, because students subtract when they should divide and the error is invisible to them. The third cluster is geometry with reasons attached, where circle theorems and angle work in parallel lines require a stated justification rather than a correct number, and the mark is for the reason.

Then the ones that look advanced and are mostly technique: trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, where the sine and cosine rules are applied to the wrong configuration; vectors, where notation defeats students who understand the geometry; transformations of graphs, where a sign is mishandled; probability from tree diagrams and set notation, where the error is reading the question; and histograms with unequal class widths, which almost nobody is taught carefully. Standard form and surds round out the list, and both are pure non-calculator exposure.

sections.heading: Method marks decide more grades than knowledge does
paragraphs: If a Views parent takes one thing from this page, it should be this. On both boards, a large share of the available marks are awarded for the method rather than the final answer, and a student who reaches the right number by a route the examiner cannot follow loses those marks entirely. This is the commonest reason a child who understands the mathematics comes home with a grade that makes no sense to anybody.

The habit forms early and innocently. A capable student in Year 9 does three lines of algebra in their head because it is faster, writes the answer, and is marked correct by a teacher with thirty books to get through. By Year 11 the questions have five steps and the same student writes two lines, loses three method marks on each of six questions, and finishes with a grade 6 on a paper they could have scored a grade 8 on. Nothing about their understanding is at fault.

Fixing it requires a mark scheme and somebody willing to be irritating about it. A tutor opens a past-paper question, has the student write the full solution, then compares it line by line against where the marks were actually allocated. Two or three sessions of that is usually enough for the penny to drop, and the gain is immediate because it applies to every question on both papers rather than to one topic. It is also the single clearest demonstration of why a tutor needs the right code: the mark allocation and the expected working differ between Cambridge and Pearson papers.

There is a second, related habit worth naming. Students abandon questions rather than banking partial credit. A multi-step question where the first part is accessible and the last part is not still carries marks for the accessible parts, and a student who skips the whole question because they cannot see the end of it is giving away marks they already own. Training a child to write what they can and move on is worth more in the final month than any new content.

sections.heading: From IGCSE mathematics to the Diploma: the gap that opens in October
paragraphs: A great many Views students go from IGCSE mathematics into the IB Diploma, and the handover is where the most expensive surprise in this whole cycle lives. An Extended grade 7, or a grade 7 on the numbered scale, reads as a strong result and is one. It is not, by itself, preparation for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.

The reason is the difference between competence and fluency. IGCSE rewards a student who can carry out a technique when asked for it. Diploma Higher Level assumes the technique is automatic and spends its time on what is built on top: formal proof, calculus developed properly, and problems where three or four techniques have to be combined without being named. A student who has to think about rearranging has no capacity left for the actual question, and that shortfall does not appear in September when the course is revising. It appears in late October when the first proof and calculus unit arrives.

The students who make the transition comfortably are almost always the ones who took Additional Mathematics 0606 or Further Pure 4MB1, or who did deliberate bridging work in the summer. That is a cheap intervention: four to eight sessions in July and August on algebraic fluency, notation conventions and the habits of formal argument. Repairing the same gap in February of DP1, with a syllabus running alongside it, costs several times as much and recovers less.

sections.heading: Ten minutes of questions that tell you whether a tutor knows the paper
paragraphs: You do not need to be a mathematician to test one. You need a handful of questions whose answers are specific enough that general competence cannot cover for them, and the willingness to notice a vague reply. Ask these of us in the free first lesson, and ask them of anybody else you are considering.

Start with the code. A tutor who teaches these papers routinely will ask you for it before you offer it, and will react to the answer: a different reaction to 0607 than to 0580, a question about the tier, a question about which grading scale the school uses. A tutor who says that it is all the same mathematics is telling you something true and useless, because you are not buying mathematics, you are buying preparation for one examination.

Then ask about the calculator position and the tier ceiling, because those two facts shape the entire final term and a person who has prepared candidates knows them without pausing. Ask what they would want to see before the second session; the answer you want involves your child's marked work rather than the tutor's own diagnostic. And ask how they handle method marks, which is the question that most reliably separates a teacher from somebody who is simply good at the subject.

A tutor who says they will check the current specification and come back to you is being honest and that is a better sign than a confident wrong answer. Syllabuses genuinely change, and the 0580 non-calculator paper is recent enough that a tutor returning from a few years away could reasonably need to confirm it. What should worry you is fluency without specificity: lots of reassurance, no codes, no tiers, no mention of mark schemes.

sections.heading: What this costs, and how to check any figure you are quoted
paragraphs: A parent in The Views can verify almost any tutoring quote in about fifteen minutes, which is unusual in this market and worth doing. The method is simple: find out what band a quote sits in, then check whether the service matches the band. The bands below are other providers' own published figures, read in October 2026, and they are all publicly visible on the providers' sites.

At the bottom, online tutoring from university students is advertised at roughly AED 33 to AED 52 an hour by Tutopiya and from AED 45 to AED 65 by EdFlik. Qualified online subject tutoring begins around AED 150, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 or more at the specialist end. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, with Bestimate's usual band AED 180 to AED 350. Premium and former-examiner tutors are quoted up to AED 650 by BartyED.

So the check runs like this. If you are quoted AED 250 an hour, you are in the named-specialist band, and the questions in the previous section are what that band should be able to answer without hesitating. If you are quoted AED 60, you are buying supervision, which is a legitimate purchase for a drifting Year 10 student and will not diagnose a mock script. If you are quoted AED 400 for an online hour, ask what the premium is for, because the published market does not support that figure for a standard IGCSE hour without a specific reason such as examiner experience, which should be evidenced rather than asserted.

Two further checks are worth running on any quote. Ask whether the figure is per hour or per session, because a fifty-minute session priced hourly is a ten per cent difference nobody mentions. And ask what is included: marked work between sessions, written notes, access to the tutor's own resources. None of these figures is ours. IB Gram publishes no fixed price list on these pages, because the code, the tier and the slot all change what the right tutor costs, and the honest version is a quote after a free first lesson.

sections.heading: Starting from The Views, and the limits we state before you book
paragraphs: Three pieces of information get this moving: the school, the code and tier from a statement of entry or a school letter, and the evenings that are genuinely free. If you cannot find the code, tell us the school and the year and we will tell you what to ask for. A marked mock script or a recent assessment is worth more than any of it, because it shows whether the marks went to method, to a specific topic, or to running out of time on a two-hour paper.

Then the free first lesson. One per family, around thirty minutes, no charge and no card details taken. A good one ends with the tutor naming the pattern rather than the topic, and saying what the first four sessions would do about it. If what you hear instead is a general plan to cover the syllabus, that is useful information and it cost you nothing.

The arrangement afterwards is intentionally unremarkable. Same tutor, same evening, a short written note after each session recording what was covered and what to practise. Those notes are how you judge in week six whether the same weakness is still being described, which is a much better signal than a feeling about progress. If the match is wrong, say so after the second lesson and we will change the tutor.

The limits, stated before anything is booked. Nobody travels to a UAE address; in-home visiting is an India-only service. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables, because they belong to the boards; we cite the official pages and work from what your child legitimately holds. We guarantee no grade. We hold and claim no approval from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA or the Ministry of Education. And where no tutor for your child's code and tier is free in your slot, you get a realistic date instead of a substitute.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0580 the same qualification as 0980?
faqs.answer: The subject content is the same; the reporting scale is not. 0580 is graded A* to G and 0980 reports the identical mathematics on the 9 to 1 scale. Schools in the same part of Dubai choose differently, so two Views children in the same year group can hold grades that are not directly comparable. Both syllabuses are tiered, with the Core route capped at grade C on 0580 and grade 5 on 0980. Check which version appears on your child's statement of entry rather than assuming the neighbours' answer applies.

faqs.question: My child has a maths paper without a calculator. Since when?
faqs.answer: Cambridge included a non-calculator paper in its mainstream IGCSE mathematics syllabus from the 2025 series. For a cohort that had used a device for every assessment since Year 7, that is a genuine shift rather than a technicality, because the non-calculator paper exposes arithmetic and algebraic fluency directly. Pearson's 4MA1 papers both permit a calculator, so a child moving between schools can go from one position to the other. The remedy is mechanical: timed by-hand algebra and arithmetic, marked against a real mark scheme.

faqs.question: What is Cambridge 0607 and why is my child doing it instead of 0580?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is a separate syllabus that assumes a graphic display calculator throughout rather than permitting one on a single paper, with more emphasis on modelling and interpreting results. Schools running the IB continuum, or planning it, often prefer it because it feeds Diploma mathematics more naturally. The practical consequence is that a 0607 student tutored from 0580 past papers is being prepared for the wrong examination, which is easy to miss because the topic lists look similar on paper.

faqs.question: Should my child take Additional Mathematics as well?
faqs.answer: If they are heading for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level or A Level mathematics and the school offers it, it is the best preparation available. Cambridge 0606 and Pearson 4MB1 cover material that overlaps the start of those courses: calculus, trigonometric identities, series and formal functions. Students who take one of them tend to find the sixth-form transition easiest of any route. The cost is timetable space and workload in Year 11, so it suits a student who is comfortable rather than one already stretched across nine subjects.

faqs.question: Why does my child get the right answer and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Because a large share of the available marks are awarded for method rather than the final answer, and a solution the examiner cannot follow forfeits them. The habit starts in Year 9, when a capable student does three lines of algebra mentally and is marked correct. By Year 11 the questions have five steps, and the same student concedes three method marks on each of six questions. The remedy is a mark scheme and somebody prepared to be irritating about full written solutions, usually across two or three sessions.

faqs.question: Which maths topics should we spend the paid hours on?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation first, because it is hidden inside every other topic and a student who struggles to rearrange a formula will appear to struggle with trigonometry instead. Then proportional reasoning: reverse percentages and inverse proportion are reliably the worst-answered questions on any paper. Then geometry with reasons attached, where the mark is for the stated justification rather than the number. Vectors, set notation and histograms with unequal class widths round out the list, and all three are notation problems rather than conceptual ones.

faqs.question: Will an Extended grade 7 be enough for Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: Usually not on its own, and this catches Views families every year. An Extended grade 7 shows competence across an IGCSE syllabus. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes the techniques are automatic and spends its time on proof, formal calculus and multi-step problems that combine several methods without naming them. The gap appears in late October of DP1, not September. Four to eight bridging sessions over the summer cost far less than repairing it in February while a new syllabus runs alongside.

faqs.question: Does the tier my child is entered for cap the grade?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is settled months before revision begins. A Cambridge Core entry cannot be awarded above grade C on 0580 or grade 5 on 0980. A Pearson Foundation entry is capped at grade 5, while Higher reaches grade 9 with an allowed grade 3 below the usual floor. If your child is capable of more than the ceiling of their entry, that is a conversation to have with the school in the autumn while the entry can still be changed, not in March when the decision has been submitted.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class at a centre in Barsha Heights worth it?
faqs.answer: It can be, under one condition: the students in the group share the same awarding body, the same syllabus code and the same tier. Where they do, the saving is real and the teaching is efficient. Where they do not, the class teaches to an average that fits nobody, and a parent spends two hours of driving and waiting to deliver a one-hour lesson. Ask the centre directly which code and tier the group is prepared for before paying for a term of it.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a quoted AED rate is reasonable?
faqs.answer: Place it against bands that are already published. Online student-tutor supervision is advertised in Dubai at roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, qualified online subject tutoring from about AED 150, named specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, and premium examiner-led tutors up to AED 650. Those are other providers' own October 2026 figures. Then check the service matches the band: an AED 250 hour should answer code, tier and mark-scheme questions without hesitating.

faqs.question: Is the price per hour or per session, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more than parents expect, and it is worth asking before the first booking. A fifty-minute session quoted at an hourly rate is a difference of roughly a sixth of what you pay, and across a two-year arrangement that is substantial. Ask three things: how long a session actually runs, whether marking work between sessions is included, and whether written notes are provided. None of the figures published on this page are ours; your own quote follows the free first lesson, because the code, the tier and the slot all change it.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 and coping. Is it too early for tutoring?
faqs.answer: For mathematics specifically, Year 10 is the cheapest and most effective time, because the content is cumulative. A gap in indices or in solving equations now becomes a failure in algebraic fractions and trigonometry next year, and repairing it then costs several times as much as preventing it. A single weekly hour from the autumn of Year 10 generally outperforms a crisis block in the spring of Year 11, both in cost and in grade. If the problem is organisation rather than understanding, supervision is the cheaper answer.

faqs.question: Can my child sit maths with one board and sciences with another?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Dubai it happens constantly. Schools choose specifications subject by subject, so a Views student may sit Pearson Edexcel mathematics alongside Cambridge sciences in the same series. The grades are unaffected. What is affected is preparation, because the boards structure papers differently, set different calculator policies and reward working differently. Tell any prospective tutor the code rather than the subject name, and ask which board's papers they normally teach from before committing to a term.

faqs.question: What if the tutor we need is not free on our evening?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date. The 17:00 to 18:00 window is the one every Emirates Living family wants, and for a specific code and tier it is sometimes genuinely full. The alternative to saying so is placing a tutor who prepares a different paper, which costs a term before anyone notices the mismatch. Usually the fix is an adjacent evening or a weekend morning. Occasionally it is a wait of a few days, and whether to hold the slot is your decision rather than ours.

intro.heading: Maths is a chain, and the chain runs on a calendar
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where timing matters most and where families wait longest. The reason is structural rather than psychological. Most school subjects are a set of topics that can be learned in almost any order; a pupil who missed a history unit can learn it later without the gap affecting anything else. Mathematics is a chain. Algebraic manipulation carries equations. Equations carry functions and graphs. Trigonometry assumes both. Mensuration and compound measures assume unit handling. Statistics assumes proportion. A weakness early in the chain does not stay where it was.

That is why a Year 10 autumn gap looks, by the following February, like four separate problems. The pupil has not developed four weaknesses; they have carried one into four topics that needed it. And it is why the diagnostic question in mathematics is never simply which topics are weak, but where in the chain the first break is. A tutor who teaches the four surface topics will produce four small improvements and leave the cause intact.

So this page is organised around the chain and the calendar together: what each term of the two years has to deliver before the next one begins, which topic depends on which, and what the remaining weeks can honestly reach from wherever you are reading. It also sets out the series dates that are actually verifiable, because UAE-facing pages repeatedly get them wrong.

Tilal Al Ghaf has one genuine advantage in a calendar-driven subject. The community has a British-curriculum school inside its boundary, and DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City next door have their own provision, so the school run is short and pupils are frequently home before four. For mathematics that means an early weekday session is realistic, and a pupil at four-thirty makes arithmetic errors at a far lower rate than the same pupil at seven. In a subject where precision is the whole game, that is not a minor scheduling detail.

Before anything else, establish the specification. Ask the exams officer for the awarding body, the syllabus code and the tier, in writing. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580, tiered Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher. Edexcel permits a calculator in both papers, while Cambridge's current structure pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator one — so confirm which papers your child sits, because that structure was revised relatively recently.

IB Gram delivers mathematics tuition to Tilal Al Ghaf as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For mathematics the format costs very little, because a session is worked problems on a shared screen with every line of the pupil's working visible, and it widens the shortlist to everyone who teaches that exact code and tier.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE mathematics topics Tilal Al Ghaf families ask about, ordered roughly by where they sit in the chain rather than by syllabus order, with what each one depends on.

subjects.name: Number, fractions and proportion
subjects.description: The first link. Fractions, percentages, reverse percentages, ratio, direct and inverse proportion, standard form and bounds. Reverse percentages are the most commonly failed lower-tier topic, and upper and lower bounds the most commonly failed higher-tier one.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: The load-bearing link. Expanding, factorising, simplifying and rearranging. Everything after this depends on it, which is why a pupil who hesitates here loses marks in physics and chemistry as well, and why maths tutoring often appears to improve three subjects at once.

subjects.name: Equations and inequalities
subjects.levels: Both boards, extended at the higher tier
subjects.description: Depends directly on manipulation. Linear, simultaneous and quadratic equations, then inequalities and regions. Completing the square and the quadratic formula are higher-tier staples where the error pattern is sign management rather than method.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.levels: Both boards, extended at the higher tier
subjects.description: Depends on equations. Sketching, transformations, intersections and, at the higher tier, inverse and composite functions. Marks are lost by plotting rather than sketching, which wastes time, and by omitting intercepts and asymptotes the question asked for.

subjects.name: Sequences
subjects.levels: Both boards, extended at the higher tier
subjects.description: Depends on algebraic manipulation. Linear and quadratic nth terms, and geometric sequences at the higher tier. The quadratic nth term is a procedure teachable in one session and then permanent, and a frequent source of free marks for pupils never shown the method.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and bearings
subjects.levels: Both boards, extended at the higher tier
subjects.description: Depends on manipulation and on proportion. Right-angled trigonometry, then the sine and cosine rules. Bearings questions are lost through diagram errors rather than trigonometry, and the fix is drawing north lines at every point before any calculation.

subjects.name: Geometry and circle theorems
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, similarity, congruence and circle theorems. Learnable in two sessions and then productive every series, but only if the pupil names the theorem used, since unnamed reasoning loses the communication marks even with a correct answer.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measures
subjects.description: Depends on unit handling and on proportion. Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors, plus speed, density and pressure. Unit conversion, especially between volume units, is the dominant loss and it costs a mark at a time across the whole paper.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Depends on fractions and proportion. Tree and Venn diagrams, conditional probability and set language. Conditional probability is the standard trap: pupils multiply along the wrong branch or forget that the denominator has changed.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Depends on proportion and on graph reading. Averages from tables, cumulative frequency, histograms and box plots. Histograms with unequal class widths are the reliable higher-tier loss, because frequency density is a step pupils skip.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Depends on algebraic manipulation. Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and the four transformations. Proof questions reward writing the route algebraically first, and pupils who reason from the diagram alone generally lose the method marks.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: A skill set in its own right where a non-calculator paper is sat. Fractions, surds, indices, standard form and exact values by hand, all of which decay quietly across two years of calculator use. The only way to check is to remove the device in a session.

sections.heading: The chain: which topics depend on which
paragraphs: This is the table that should drive an IGCSE mathematics diagnosis and that nobody publishes. Mathematics topics are not independent, and the practical consequence is that a pupil's four weak topics usually trace back to one earlier weakness they all share. Teaching the four produces four small improvements and leaves the cause untouched, which is why some pupils receive a year of tutoring and move half a grade.

Read the dependency column rather than the topic column. Trigonometry questions are lost by pupils who can do trigonometry and cannot rearrange, because the question requires rearranging before the trigonometry begins. Mensuration questions are lost by pupils who understand volume and cannot convert units. Statistics questions are lost by pupils who know what a histogram is and cannot handle proportion. In each case the topic named on the report is the symptom and the link beneath it is the cause.

The diagnostic procedure follows directly. Take a marked paper and, for each lost mark, ask not which topic the question was about but which step actually failed. A pupil who set up the equation correctly and then made a sign error while rearranging has an algebra problem, whatever the question's heading said. Do that across a paper and the pattern is usually unambiguous: most of the losses failed at the same step, two or three links earlier than the topic list suggests.

This is also why the two-year calendar matters so much in mathematics specifically. The chain is built in order, and the early links are built in Year 9 and the first half of Year 10. A pupil whose manipulation is secure by Christmas of Year 10 will absorb everything that follows; a pupil whose manipulation is shaky will appear to develop a new weakness every half term. The cheapest moment to intervene is therefore the one at which nothing appears to be wrong yet.

sections.heading: The two years counted forwards, with what closes at each point
paragraphs: Having set out the chain, here is the calendar it is built on. The purpose of this table is to let a family see from wherever they are reading what is still possible and what has already been decided. The two IGCSE years are not an undifferentiated stretch of study; they have phases with different possibilities and different costs.

Year 9 and the first term of Year 10 are when the early links are laid. This is the phase in which an hour of tutoring buys the most, and in which almost nobody books any, because no report has yet said anything alarming. By the end of Year 10 roughly half the specification has been taught and the provisional tier decision has usually been made inside the school on the basis of assessments the family may not have seen.

Year 11's first term produces the mock series, which is the best evidence available and the trigger for most bookings. From that point the entry has usually gone in and the tier is fixed. The second term is the technique term, where command terms, enforced working, unit discipline and pacing respond within weeks even without much content teaching. The final weeks are papers and pacing only, and attempting to teach new content then displaces the practice that would have consolidated what the pupil already knows.

Use the table by writing your own child's dates into it: the mock window, the entry deadline the exams officer gives you, and the first paper. Then count the weeks to the nearest. That count decides whether you are buying content teaching, technique repair or pacing practice, and knowing which you are buying is what separates a plan from a hope.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of maths can honestly do
paragraphs: Most families in this community arrive six to ten weeks before a mock or a series, so it is worth being precise about that window. Eight weeks at two sessions a week is roughly sixteen taught hours plus set work, and in mathematics specifically it does three things reliably.

First, it finds the first break in the chain, which is a single session of work and frequently the most valuable hour a family buys. Second, it repairs technique: enforced working so method marks survive, unit discipline, answering the command term, and finishing the paper. Those are habits rather than knowledge and they respond within a fortnight each. Third, it repairs two or three named topics chosen from the marked mock rather than from the pupil's impression of what is hard — typically the higher-tier-only topics such as bounds, histograms with unequal class widths, vector proof or the quadratic nth term, each of which is a session or two and then permanent.

What eight weeks does not do is rebuild a chain whose early links were never secure. If manipulation is unreliable, every topic downstream is unreliable, and no amount of topic teaching compensates because the pupil fails at the same step each time. That needs volume, which means four or five sessions a week in a school break, and in the eight weeks before a series that break does not exist. Saying so is more useful than promising otherwise, and it changes what the eight weeks should target: the marks still reachable rather than all of them.

There is one further thing a short block reliably changes which is hard to measure. A pupil who has been quietly avoiding mathematics revision because they do not know where to start will do the work once someone has broken it into a sequence of small timed sets. That shift usually happens by the third session, and for some pupils it accounts for most of the eventual gain.

sections.heading: The series, and the dates that are verifiable
paragraphs: Whatever the plan, it ends on a fixed date, and that date is worth getting right because UAE-facing pages repeatedly get it wrong. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists and is offered to India only; a candidate in Dubai does not sit it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

Cambridge adds one operational detail that costs nothing to check and can cost a paper if ignored. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. A parent who downloads a timetable and builds a revision plan on it should confirm the zone with the exams officer first.

The Pearson dates worth quoting are backward-looking, which is what makes them checkable rather than speculative. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For any series still ahead, use the month and check the live official timetable, because Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised.

The practical consequence for a mathematics plan is the lag between decision points and papers. Entries close months before the series. The tier is fixed with the entry. A resit is an entry for the next series rather than something taken on demand, which for a June result means November. So the window in which tutoring can change the shape of the outcome, rather than just the margin, is earlier than it feels — and in a chain-built subject, earlier still.

sections.heading: Holidays and Ramadan: when fluency can actually be rebuilt
paragraphs: In a chain-built subject the school breaks are not a pause in the plan; they are the only part of the plan where the early links can be repaired. Fluency in arithmetic and algebraic manipulation comes from volume rather than from explanation, and volume requires four or five sessions a week, which term time cannot accommodate alongside school work.

The Year 10 summer is the highest-value block in the two years and the one families most often leave empty. Nothing is being assessed, no deadlines are running, and two or three weeks at four or five sessions a week can take a pupil from hesitant manipulation to fluent manipulation. A pupil who does that arrives in Year 11 able to absorb the remaining specification; a pupil who does not spends Year 11 appearing to develop a new weakness every half term.

The winter break in Year 11 is the second most valuable, because it sits immediately after the mock series. The mock has just produced the diagnosis, and the break provides the only concentrated time left in which to act on it. A family who gets the mock marked and categorised in the last week of term and then runs a block over the break has used the calendar as well as it can be used.

Ramadan reshapes the week rather than removing it. School hours shorten and the usable evening moves, so sessions shift to the earlier afternoon or a post-Iftar slot. In a sequential subject the adjustment that works is a shorter session at the same frequency rather than skipped weeks, because a fortnight's gap costs more than two shortened sessions do. Where Ramadan falls close to the series, plan the block before it begins. An online slot is far easier to move than a drive across Dubai, and in a fixed countdown that flexibility is worth more than it sounds.

sections.heading: What waiting costs, in dirhams
paragraphs: The market bands first, read in October 2026 from competitors' own published figures. EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE, TutorChase at AED 270, BartyED at AED 650. Bestimate's Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with monthly estimates of AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Now the comparison that matters in a chain-built subject. A pupil supported weekly from the start of Year 10 needs roughly sixty to seventy hours across two years and arrives at the series with the chain intact. At the qualified subject tutor band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour that is roughly AED 9,000 to AED 21,000 spread over twenty-four months, which is a modest recurring monthly line. A pupil supported only from a Year 11 mock needs roughly forty hours compressed into twenty weeks, roughly AED 6,000 to AED 12,000, and reaches a lower ceiling because the early links cannot be rebuilt in term time.

So the later route is cheaper in total and buys less, which is the opposite of how families usually read it. The reason is not that late tutoring is poor value per hour; it is that the thing most needed late — fluency in the early links — is the one thing a term-time block cannot deliver. A family who understands that will either start earlier or deliberately target the late block at technique and named topics rather than expecting it to fix the foundation.

For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion. The fee line is flat and predictable; tutoring is the variable one. IB Gram publishes no hourly rate here because the right figure depends on board, tier and weeks remaining, but the band above lets you judge any quote including ours, and the first lesson is free.

sections.heading: The tier, and when the conversation has to happen
paragraphs: The tier entry is the most consequential administrative decision of the two years and it is made on a calendar most families never see. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade that can be awarded regardless of how well the paper is answered. The Extended and Higher tiers reach the full range and are effectively prerequisites for A Level Mathematics and for IB Analysis and Approaches at either level.

Schools decide tiers for sound reasons. A pupil placed on a tier they cannot cope with performs badly, and a secure grade on the lower tier beats a poor one on the higher. The failure mode is not bad judgement but timing: the decision is made early, on limited evidence, and families frequently discover it after the entry has gone in. Entries close months before papers are sat.

So the conversation belongs in Year 10 rather than Year 11. Ask the school which tier your child is provisionally entered for, when the entry closes, and what evidence would support a change. In almost every case the answer is performance on a higher-tier paper, which is exactly what a tutor can produce: a full past paper at the higher tier worked under timing and marked against the published scheme, with the breakdown attached.

That document is honest in both directions, which is why it is worth producing. A respectable mark gives you a concrete case rather than a parental opinion. A weak one tells you in Year 10 that the lower tier is the right call, which redirects the tutoring towards securing a strong grade on the tier your child will actually sit instead of chasing one they will not. Either outcome is better than finding out in April.

sections.heading: Permits, papers and the claims to distrust
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated and most Dubai parents have not been told. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine amount appears on this page: Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and the figure circulating online could not be verified. A provider printing a penalty figure to create urgency is using a number nobody has published.

On materials, the limit is firm. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works through questions from legitimately obtained material and teaches the pupil to read a mark scheme themselves. In a chain-built subject that matters doubly, because a pupil who can read a mark scheme can see which step failed and therefore diagnose themselves between sessions.

Two further claims to treat sceptically wherever they appear. Examiner status, which we do not use as a selling point for anyone whose current status cannot be evidenced and which gives no access to marking, boundaries or unseen papers. And any promise about the outcome, which we will not make because nobody controls it. What we will give you after a marked paper is a statement of where in the chain the first break sits and an honest view of what the remaining weeks can reach.

faqs.question: Why does my child seem to get worse at maths every half term?
faqs.answer: Because mathematics is a chain and they are carrying one early weakness into each new topic. Algebraic manipulation carries equations, which carry functions and graphs, which trigonometry assumes. A pupil whose rearranging is shaky will fail at the same step in four different topics, and the report will record four weaknesses rather than one. The fix is to trace lost marks to the step that actually failed rather than the topic heading, which usually points two or three links earlier than expected.

faqs.question: When in the two IGCSE years should maths tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Year 9 or the first term of Year 10, which is when almost nobody books it because no report has yet said anything alarming. The early links — arithmetic, fractions, proportion and algebraic manipulation — are laid then, and a pupil who has them secure by Christmas of Year 10 absorbs everything that follows. A pupil who does not spends Year 11 appearing to develop new weaknesses. The cheapest moment to intervene is the one at which nothing looks wrong.

faqs.question: What can eight weeks of IGCSE maths tutoring achieve?
faqs.answer: Three things reliably. It locates the first break in the chain, which is usually one session of work and often the most valuable hour a family buys. It repairs technique: enforced working so method marks survive, unit discipline, answering the command term and finishing the paper. And it repairs two or three named topics chosen from the marked mock. What it cannot do is rebuild fluency in the early links, because that needs volume and volume needs a school break.

faqs.question: Can we book an in-home IGCSE maths tutor through IB Gram?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run only in India. For mathematics the format costs very little, because a session is worked problems on a shared screen with every line of the pupil's working visible and a paper marked in front of them. What it gains is a shortlist of tutors who teach your child's exact syllabus code and tier rather than those who will drive out past Hessa Street.

faqs.question: How should we use the summer between Year 10 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: As the fluency window, because it is the only one. Four or five sessions a week for two or three weeks can take a pupil from hesitant algebraic manipulation to fluent manipulation, which is the single change that makes the whole of Year 11 easier. Nothing is being assessed and no deadlines are running, so the time is genuinely available. Most families leave it empty and then spend Year 11 paying specialist rates to patch topics the fluency would have carried.

faqs.question: Which series will a Tilal Al Ghaf maths candidate sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Those are what UAE candidates use. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any UAE-facing page quoting a February window is describing a different country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise.

faqs.question: When is it too late to challenge my child's maths tier?
faqs.answer: Once the entry has gone in, which happens months before the papers. So the conversation belongs in Year 10. Ask the school which tier your child is provisionally entered for, when the entry closes, and what evidence would support a change — which in almost every case means performance on a higher-tier paper. A full higher-tier past paper worked under timing and marked against the published scheme is the most persuasive document you can bring, and it is honest in both directions.

faqs.question: What does starting late actually cost compared with starting early?
faqs.answer: Less money and a lower ceiling. Weekly support from the start of Year 10 is roughly sixty to seventy hours across two years, about AED 9,000 to AED 21,000 at the mid market band read in October 2026, spread as a modest monthly line. A Year 11 block from the mock is about forty hours, roughly AED 6,000 to AED 12,000, compressed into twenty weeks. The late route is cheaper precisely because it cannot deliver what is most needed late, which is fluency in the early links.

faqs.question: Does my child's paper allow a calculator?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, permits a calculator in both papers. Cambridge 0580's current structure pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator one at each tier, and that structure was revised relatively recently, so confirm with the school which papers your child sits. The difference matters: a pupil who has used a calculator for two years and then meets a non-calculator paper loses marks across the whole paper rather than in one topic.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan fit into an exam-year maths plan?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and the usable evening moves, so sessions shift to the earlier afternoon or to a post-Iftar slot. In a sequential subject the adjustment that works is a shorter session at the same frequency rather than skipped weeks, because a fortnight's gap costs more than two shortened sessions. Where Ramadan falls close to the series, plan that block before it begins rather than improvising. An online slot is considerably easier to move than a tutor's drive across Dubai.

faqs.question: Which higher-tier topics are worth most late in Year 11?
faqs.answer: The ones that are self-contained, because each is a session or two and then permanent. Upper and lower bounds, histograms with unequal class widths, the quadratic nth term, circle theorems where the theorem must be named, and vector proof written algebraically rather than reasoned from the diagram. Alongside them, the leakage habits: unshown method, unit conversion in volume questions, and unnamed reasoning. Content teaching stops being realistic late, but those two groups together often move a grade.

faqs.question: Is an early weekday session better for maths?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this community allows one. Tilal Al Ghaf has a school inside the boundary and neighbouring communities have their own provision, so pupils are often home before four and a four-thirty start is realistic. In mathematics that matters more than in most subjects: a tired pupil makes arithmetic errors rather than conceptual ones, so a session spent on precision work gets a materially better return from an alert pupil than from one who has already worked for three hours.

faqs.question: What should my child do in the summer after the series?
faqs.answer: Six to eight bridging sessions, which is the most underused window in a school career because the exams are over and nothing feels urgent. A Level Mathematics and IB Analysis and Approaches both assume algebraic fluency beyond a comfortable Extended or Higher pass and both begin at pace in the first week of Year 12. A short block covering manipulation, logarithms and early calculus notation prevents a difficult first term and costs less than the catch-up tutoring that otherwise starts in October.

faqs.question: Will a tutor supply mark schemes for us to use at home?
faqs.answer: No. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works through questions from legitimately obtained material and teaches your child to read a mark scheme themselves. In a chain-built subject that is doubly valuable, because a pupil who can read a scheme can see which step failed and diagnose themselves between sessions rather than waiting to be told.

faqs.question: Is a private tuition permit something we should ask to see?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of pages quoting amounts. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.closingHeading: Find the break, then find the block
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.closingBody: Two questions settle an IGCSE mathematics plan. Where in the chain is the first break — which means tracing lost marks on a real paper to the step that failed rather than the topic the question was about — and how many weeks are left before the series. If the break is in the early links and a school break is available, the holiday block is the answer and term-time sessions will patch rather than repair. If the links are sound and the losses are technique, eight weeks of enforced working, unit discipline and timed papers will move the grade. Tilal Al Ghaf's short school run lets you put that work in an early slot while your child is still alert. Sessions run live and one-to-one over video at Gulf Standard Time. We make no home visits in the UAE and promise no grades.
