sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Edexcel 4MA1, and why the board changes the plan
paragraphs: Schools serving Umm Suqeim run both boards, sometimes in the same building for different cohorts, and the two examine mathematics differently enough that practice written for one is only partly useful for the other. A family paying for hours should know which code is on the entry form before the first lesson, not after the first mock.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper in each tier since the 2025 syllabus revision. That non-calculator paper is a specific discipline: fractions, surds, standard form and algebraic manipulation done cleanly by hand, under time. Students who have spent four years typing expressions into a handset meet it late and lose marks to arithmetic rather than to method.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus 4MA1, runs two written papers per tier, each two hours and worth 100 marks, with a calculator permitted throughout. The arithmetic is therefore less exposed and the question length more demanding, and preparation shifts towards sustaining accuracy across a long paper and towards using the calculator efficiently rather than towards manual manipulation.

Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 is a third syllabus, common in schools that also run the Middle Years Programme or feed the IB Diploma, with a graphics calculator assumed and its own paper structure. Because syllabuses are revised, the only safe method is to read the current syllabus document on the board's own site for the series your child will sit, and to link it rather than to rely on a summary. Any tutor who cannot tell you which code they are teaching to is guessing with your hours.

sections.heading: Five ways IGCSE maths money gets wasted in this catchment
paragraphs: Waste here is rarely dramatic. It looks like a reasonable arrangement that quietly returns nothing, and it is usually one of five patterns. Naming them is more useful than any amount of reassurance, because each one is avoidable by a decision rather than by spending more.

The first is buying the wrong band. A student whose problem is that nobody checks their homework does not need an examination specialist at the top of the table, and a Year 11 candidate three months from a series does not need a patient supervisor. The second is starting too late. The same twenty hours bought across Year 10 and Year 11 produce more than twenty hours bought in April, because content can still be taught properly rather than patched.

The third is paying for reteaching that the school is already doing. A tutor who covers the same lesson the class covered, a week behind, is adding repetition rather than teaching, and repetition is the cheapest thing in a student's life to arrange for free. The fourth is group classes bought on price. A group of six at a third of the one-to-one rate looks like value until the content is pitched for the middle of the room, at which point a stronger student is paying to be bored and a weaker one is paying to be lost.

The fifth is the travel premium paid without thinking. The published in-home band runs to AED 500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor online, and for many Umm Suqeim households the premium buys a commute rather than a better mathematician. It is a reasonable thing to buy if presence in the room is what the student needs; it is pure cost if it is simply the arrangement that was assumed.

sections.heading: A two-year IGCSE maths budget for an Umm Suqeim household, written out
paragraphs: Families plan tutoring in hourly rates and pay for it monthly, which is how a reasonable decision becomes an unexamined standing order. The table below converts the published bands into the shapes families actually buy, so the total is visible before the first lesson rather than after the twentieth.

The figures are derived arithmetic on published market bands, not an IB Gram price list and not a quote. They assume roughly thirty-six teaching weeks in a Dubai school year, which is why a weekly hour comes out near nine hours a term. Term structures differ between schools in this corridor, so treat the row shapes as the useful part and recalculate the totals against whatever rate you are actually offered.

Context helps as well. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A household whose school fees are flat for a year has a clearer view of what a tutoring line can absorb, and that is a better moment to plan two years of support than the week before a mock.

The last row is the one most families never price. Entering as a private candidate, resitting a paper in a later series, or bridging into a post-16 course that a capped tier closed are all real costs with real administrative steps, and they are the costs that a single early diagnostic hour is competing against. Seen that way, the cheapest line in the table is the first one.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks leak, and which leaks are cheap to fix
paragraphs: A marked script is the only honest basis for spending money on this subject, because marks do not leak evenly. They leak in a small number of recognisable places, and some of those places are far cheaper to repair than others. Knowing which is which is how a family buys ten useful hours instead of thirty vague ones.

The cheapest repair is method writing. Examiners award method marks for a correct approach even when the final answer is wrong, and a student who writes only answers forfeits every one of them. This is a habit, not a knowledge gap, and it responds to a handful of marking sessions. The second cheapest is question recognition: knowing that a particular phrasing wants a ratio method, or that a worded problem is a simultaneous equation in disguise. That too is pattern exposure rather than new content.

The mid-price repairs are the standard algebra leaks. Rearranging formulae with the subject appearing twice. Fractions in algebraic form. Indices and standard form under time. Solving quadratics by the method the question implies rather than the one the student prefers. Each of these takes a few weeks of short regular practice and each reappears across several papers, which is why they are good value.

The expensive repairs are the structural ones. A student who does not have secure number sense, or who cannot handle fractions without a calculator, is carrying a gap from Year 7 into a Year 11 paper, and that is months of work rather than weeks. The honest thing to say to a family in April is that this gap cannot be closed before a June series, and that the useful plan is to secure the marks that are reachable rather than to pretend otherwise.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards from an Umm Suqeim diary
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so any plan built around it is built on the wrong calendar for a Dubai family. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are likewise available in May and June and again in November.

The important structural fact is that entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and they are administered by the school rather than by the family. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results reach students in January, with the November 2025 results having landed on 22 January 2026. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Those are the published dates for those series, and they are the right shape to plan against.

Cambridge adds a trap worth knowing. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. That is the school's responsibility to administer, but it is the reason a parent should take dates from the school's own entry letter rather than from a general timetable found online.

Because provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and can be revised, the only safe method is to work from the live official timetable on the board's own site and from the school's entry confirmation. A tutoring plan that counts backwards from a confirmed paper date is worth considerably more than one that counts forward from today, and the counting backwards is where a mock script, a targeted block and a final technique phase fall into their natural order.

sections.heading: Is the person you are paying permitted to tutor in Dubai?
paragraphs: This is a cost question as well as a legal one, because an arrangement that cannot continue is money spent on a relationship with no term. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE's own service page lists it as private tutor licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because the permit carries no fee, any tutor who cites permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is describing something else. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you either.

A separate regime applies to anything with premises and staff. A tutoring operation running a centre in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. That is a specific permit issued to institutions, and no individual tutor and no online platform should describe themselves as approved by KHDA on the strength of it. IB Gram does not hold it and does not claim it.

There is also a conflict-of-interest rule worth knowing before a family hires a teacher from their own child's school. The permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their school. Treat your child's own classroom teacher as off limits and ask the school if in doubt.

sections.heading: Starting, pausing and stopping without wasting money
paragraphs: The first hour is free and it exists to produce a decision rather than a relationship. A useful trial lesson ends with a short written note naming what is secure, what is not, which tier the evidence supports, and which three or four topics are costing the most marks. If what comes back is encouragement without specifics, you have learned something useful at no cost and you should stop there.

Tell us the syllabus code if you know it and the school and year group if you do not. Cambridge 0580 Extended, Edexcel 4MA1 Higher and Cambridge 0607 are three different requests, and a request that says only IGCSE maths takes longer to match because the matching has to be redone once the code is known. Tell us the hour your child is genuinely home and settled, measured rather than hoped for, because a slot that starts late every week is a slot you are part-funding for nothing.

Pausing is normal and should cost nothing. Travel weeks, mock fortnights, Ramadan and the examination period itself all change what a household can absorb, and a sensible arrangement pauses rather than limps. Stopping should be equally easy: there is no minimum term, and a term review that concludes the hour is no longer earning its place is a successful review, not a failed one.

On availability, we state the limit rather than imply none. There are hours in a Dubai evening when every specialist in a narrow subject is already teaching, and the alternatives are then put to you plainly: a different hour with the tutor you want, the hour you want with a tutor who is strong but less specialised, or a place in the queue. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, so you will never be quoted the travel premium this page has spent so long describing.

process.title: Send the syllabus code and the real arrival time
process.description: Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1 or Cambridge 0607, the tier if it is set, and the hour your child is actually home and settled. If you do not know the code, send the school and year group and we will establish it before matching anybody to the slot.

process.title: A free diagnostic lesson with a marked paper
process.description: One hour with the tutor who would teach the weekly slot, built around a timed paper at the relevant tier. It ends with a written note on tier, on the topics costing the most marks, and on whether paid hours are the right purchase at all.

process.title: Agree the shape and the total before the first invoice
process.description: Weekly across two years, a targeted block before a series, or nothing further. The number of hours, the rate per clock hour and the expected total are stated in writing first, so the monthly figure is a decision rather than a standing order nobody revisits.

process.title: Teach ahead, then test under conditions
process.description: Lessons run slightly ahead of the school's scheme so the class consolidates rather than confuses, and once a term the student sits a past paper under timed conditions, marked against the published scheme. The plan then follows what the script shows rather than what anyone assumed.

process.title: Review the cost every term
process.description: A short conversation about what has moved, what has not, and whether the hour still earns its place in the budget. Reducing to fortnightly, pausing for a travel block, or stopping altogether are all normal outcomes and none of them requires notice.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can check before you talk to us
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the organisation that published it, with the month the page was read. You can sanity-check any quote in this market, including ours, against sources you can open yourself rather than against an assurance.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code, not to the year group
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Edexcel 4MA1 Higher are examined differently, and practice written for one is only partly useful for the other. A tutor is proposed because they teach the code on your child's entry form.

whyPoints.title: Tier evidence a school can read
whyPoints.description: A marked timed script with a topic-by-topic mark breakdown, produced early enough to inform the entry decision. That is a document a mathematics department can act on, and it is worth more than an opinion delivered in April.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium, because nobody travels
whyPoints.description: The published in-home band runs to AED 500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor online, and most of that gap is a commute. Teaching over live video removes the premium and widens the pool of tutors who teach your exact syllabus.

whyPoints.title: No minimum term and no package pressure
whyPoints.description: Hours are bought in the shape the evidence supports. Pausing for travel or examinations costs nothing, stopping needs no notice, and a term review that ends the arrangement is treated as a result rather than a problem.

whyPoints.title: Limits disclosed before you commit
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free at the hour you want, we say so and set out the alternatives honestly. Nobody is matched on the grounds of being available, because that failure only surfaces when a mock script comes back in the spring.

faqs.question: How much should an Umm Suqeim family budget per month for IGCSE maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's published Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement run roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, as read in October 2026. Market packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures rather than ours. The useful exercise is to multiply whatever rate you are offered by the number of teaching weeks in your school's year before agreeing to it.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor at AED 45 an hour a false economy for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. If the problem is that nobody sits with your child while they work, the budget band does that job and does it for a fifth of specialist money. It becomes a false economy when the problem is paper technique, tier judgement or a topic-level diagnosis from a marked script, because those need somebody who knows the syllabus and the mark scheme. The error families make is not buying cheap; it is buying the wrong band for the problem they actually have, in either direction.

faqs.question: Does the Core tier cap my child's IGCSE maths grade?
faqs.answer: Yes. Core with Cambridge and Foundation with Pearson Edexcel both cap the achievable grade, generally around a 5. For a student who would not reach that ceiling anyway the lower tier is protective, because the paper is accessible and marks are earned rather than stared at. For a student capable of a 6 or 7 it closes A Level mathematics at most schools and Higher Level Diploma mathematics, and tutoring afterwards does not reopen them. Settle it with a timed higher-tier paper, marked properly, in Year 10.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths syllabus is my child entered for, and does it change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: It changes it substantially, and the entry form is the only reliable source. Cambridge 0580 pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper in each tier since the 2025 revision, so manual manipulation matters. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 runs two two-hour papers of 100 marks each with a calculator throughout, so sustained accuracy and calculator efficiency matter more. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics assumes a graphics calculator and has its own structure. Ask the school for the code and read the current syllabus on the board's own site.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put two of my children in one tutoring session?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per child and usually less effective, which is the honest answer. Two students at different stages share an hour pitched between them, so one is revisiting and the other is behind for most of the lesson. Where it does work is two children at genuinely the same point in the same syllabus, revising together before a series. For ordinary teaching, two staggered half-length slots generally return more per dirham than one shared hour, and the arithmetic is worth doing before booking.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home maths tutor in Dubai more expensive than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because you are buying a commute as well as an hour of teaching. Published Dubai bands put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 including travel, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The difference is largely the cost of someone crossing the city in evening traffic, not a difference in subject knowledge. It buys presence in the room, which some students genuinely need. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the premium is not something we can quote.

faqs.question: When should we start paying for IGCSE maths support, Year 10 or Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if the aim is value rather than reassurance. The same number of hours bought across two years produces more than the same hours compressed into the spring of Year 11, because content can still be taught properly rather than patched, and because the tier decision is still open. Twenty hours in Year 10 and Year 11 together typically moves more than thirty hours bought in April. The one good reason to start late is a targeted technique block chosen by a marked mock script.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE maths tutoring rates in Dubai go up before the exams?
faqs.answer: Demand does, which has the same effect on availability as a price rise. The weeks before a June or November series are when every specialist's evening slots fill, so the hours left are the inconvenient ones and the choice of tutor narrows to whoever is free. Families who fix a slot in the autumn keep both the hour and the person. Rather than watching for a price change, assume the scarce resource is the evening slot and book it early, because that is the thing that actually runs out.

faqs.question: What hidden extras show up on a Dubai tutoring invoice?
faqs.answer: Four recur. A lesson priced as an hour but taught for fifty minutes, which raises the real cost by a sixth. A cancellation rule that charges the family for a tutor's change of plan. A materials line, which should only ever cover a tutor's own written work, because board past papers and mark schemes cannot legitimately be supplied as downloads. And a package that bills for hours the student will not use. Ask about each before the first invoice rather than after it, and ask whether a quoted figure includes VAT.

faqs.question: Are group IGCSE maths classes in Al Barsha better value than one-to-one online?
faqs.answer: On the headline rate, yes; on cost per mark gained, usually not. A group of six is taught at the pace of the middle of the room, so a stronger student pays to revisit material and a weaker one pays to fall behind quietly. Groups work where the content is genuinely common, for instance a timed-paper clinic in the last month before a series. For teaching new algebra to a specific student with a specific gap, the one-to-one hour is the thing that does the work.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Dubai sit for Cambridge IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: June or November. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a plan built around it is built on the wrong calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations run in May and June and again in November. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers and are administered by the school, so take your dates from the school's entry confirmation and the board's live official timetable.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit, and does it add to the fee?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it adds nothing to the fee, because it is free. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule. Any tutor citing permit costs in a quote is describing something else.

faqs.question: Can we pause IGCSE maths lessons during travel or mock weeks without paying?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the arrangement should be built to allow it. Dubai households travel in the long breaks, mock fortnights absorb every free evening, and Ramadan reorganises the whole week. An arrangement that limps through those periods at reduced attention wastes money more quietly than one that pauses cleanly and restarts. There is no minimum term here, pausing costs nothing, and the sensible pattern is to agree the likely pause weeks at the start of the term rather than negotiating each one as it arrives.

faqs.question: Will tutoring help my child meet UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Tutoring is not required for equivalency and nobody should tell you otherwise. For the British track the Ministry's published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Mathematics is commonly one of the five, so a secure pass matters. Verify current requirements on the Ministry's own channel rather than through any tutor.

faqs.question: What should a first diagnostic hour produce for the money?
faqs.answer: A document, not a feeling. Expect a timed paper at the relevant tier marked against the published scheme, a mark breakdown showing which topics the marks actually went to, a clear statement on whether the current tier entry is supported by that evidence, and a recommendation on how many hours are worth buying and in what shape. If what comes back is a general sense that your child is capable and needs confidence, the hour has told you about the tutor rather than the student.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.closingHeading: Price the two years before you buy the first hour

The first lesson is free and built around a timed paper, and it ends with a written note on tier, on the topics costing the most marks, and on how many hours are actually worth buying. If the answer is none, we will say so, and you will still have a marked script and a mark breakdown to show the school. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no minimum term and no travel premium, because nobody travels.

intro.heading: The bill is set by the hours, not by the rate
paragraphs: Families in Villanova — the townhouse clusters off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand — usually start the search for an IGCSE maths tutor by comparing hourly rates. That is the wrong variable to optimise. Published Dubai rates for maths run from AED 33 at the budget online end to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, but the difference between a AED 4,000 year and a AED 12,000 year is almost never the rate. It is the number of sessions.

The number of sessions is decided by three things, and a parent can influence all of them. First, how early you start: a problem addressed in Year 9 or early Year 10 takes a fraction of the hours it takes in February of Year 11. Second, whether anybody has read a marked paper, because hours aimed at a diagnosed gap do several times the work of hours spent re-teaching content the student already has. Third, the tier, which sets the grade ceiling and therefore what the hours are even for.

Maths is the most tutored subject in this market, which means the widest spread of both prices and competence. It also means it is the subject where the default purchase — a standing weekly session through the school year, bought in September without a diagnosis — is most common and least efficient. At the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, that default costs roughly AED 4,500 to 9,000 for the year in one subject.

On the 'home tutor' question, which arrives in most enquiries from this community: IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses. Home visits are a service we offer only in India, and teaching for Villanova is live, one-to-one and online. That removes the in-home travel premium, which in this belt sits at the top of the AED 50 to 150 per hour range because the drive out to Al Qudra Road is long. Independent in-home maths tutors do work here at AED 180 to 500 if presence in the room is what your child needs.

Everything priced below is attributed to whoever published it, whether that is a competitor's own page or Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. None of it is IB Gram's price list; we quote per student after the free trial lesson, once somebody has looked at the work and can say how many sessions this realistically takes.

One piece of context for the budget. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Fees are the fixed line this year. Tutoring is the line a family actually controls, which is a reason to plan it rather than react to a report card.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-villanova.programmesIntro: The cost of IGCSE maths support is almost entirely a function of when you start. These are the three windows and what each typically consumes.

programmes.name: Year 9 — the cheap window
programmes.description: Six to ten sessions in Year 9, costing roughly AED 1,000 to 3,000 at mid bands, commonly removes the need for a year of Year 11 tuition. The work is unglamorous: rearranging equations, fractions and indices, negative numbers handled without hesitation. A student fluent in those finds the IGCSE course ordinary; a student who is not will fight it for two years.
programmes.countryNote: Year 9 in Dubai is also when option choices are set, including whether Additional Maths is realistic and whether triple science is on. Those decisions change the maths workload and the post-16 routes available, so two sessions spent on the decision can be worth more than a term spent on content.

programmes.name: Year 10 — steady spend
programmes.description: Most families who spend here buy a weekly slot across the year: roughly thirty sessions, AED 4,500 to 9,000 at the qualified-tutor band. What makes that worth paying is topic-by-topic past-paper work as each topic is taught, so gaps appear in Year 10 rather than in Year 11 revision. What makes it a waste is a session spent reviewing the week's homework without a mark scheme in sight.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai schools enter students for maths in the June series at the end of Year 10. If yours does, the entry deadline sits months earlier and the whole budget shifts forward a year. Get the entry list from the exam office in writing rather than assuming the standard two-year pattern.

programmes.name: Year 11 — the expensive window
programmes.description: Where most of the money in this market is spent and where it buys the least, because purchases happen under time pressure. A mock-driven block of six to twelve sessions costs roughly AED 1,000 to 4,000 and moves more marks than a year of general weekly tuition. A February start with no diagnosis costs more and delivers less, which is the pattern worth avoiding.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The second series is a resit route, which means a realistic Year 11 budget allows for one subject being sat twice — a second entry fee and possibly a further short block of hours.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-villanova.subjectsIntro: This page is about maths, so these are the topics within it, with the cost logic attached: which ones repay tutoring quickly and which absorb hours without moving a grade.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The highest-return topic in the subject because everything else depends on it. Rearranging, expanding, factorising and simplifying fractions. A student fluent here gains marks in geometry, trigonometry and graph questions without those topics being taught again. Usually three to five sessions of real work.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions and indices
subjects.description: A reliable Extended-tier stumbling block and a frequent source of lost method marks. Students either know the rules or guess, and the guessing is visible within one question. Cheap to fix and immediately worth marks on the harder papers.

subjects.name: Transformations of graphs
subjects.description: The most commonly mis-taught topic in this market. Students memorise shift rules instead of understanding operations on a function's input and output, then fail as soon as two transformations combine. Teaching it properly takes two sessions and prevents a recurring loss.

subjects.name: Trigonometry, including non-right-angled
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and 3D problems. Marks go missing on setup rather than on the formula, which means diagram discipline recovers most of them. Bearings questions in particular reward a drawn north line every time.

subjects.name: Probability and tree diagrams
subjects.description: Conditional probability and without-replacement problems produce predictable errors that are fixable in one or two sessions. A good-value topic to target because the questions are structurally similar year to year and the technique transfers completely.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.description: Cumulative frequency, box plots, histograms with unequal class widths, and averages from grouped data. Histogram frequency density is the classic single-topic gap that costs a specific set of marks on one question and nothing else, which makes it an efficient target.

subjects.name: Vectors and geometry proof
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector paths and the geometric reasoning questions on the harder papers. Absorbs hours for a modest number of marks, so for a student short of time this is lower priority than algebra or trigonometry unless a target grade needs the top band.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.description: Compound interest, reverse percentages, ratio sharing and standard form. For a Core or Foundation student these topics carry a large share of the paper, which makes them the right first target. For a confident Extended student they are already secure and tutoring here wastes money.

subjects.name: Calculator technique and non-calculator fluency
subjects.description: Board structures differ on this and it matters: Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator written paper alongside a calculator paper, while Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout. Confirm the current structure for your child's entry, then practise the matching habit — hand fluency or calculator discipline.

subjects.name: Exam technique and method marks
subjects.description: Not a topic but the cheapest marks available. Showing working, answering the command word, keeping units and not rounding mid-calculation. Marking three papers strictly to the mark scheme routinely recovers more marks than three topics taught, at a fraction of the hours.

sections.heading: What actually decides the size of the bill
paragraphs: Two Villanova families can hire the same tutor at the same rate and spend AED 3,000 and AED 11,000 respectively. The difference is hours, and hours are decided before the tutor is chosen. The table below sets out the honest estimates by starting point, which is the information no tutoring page publishes because it tends to recommend buying less.

The pattern in it is consistent. Early and diagnosed is cheap. Late and undiagnosed is expensive. A student with a marked mock showing method errors needs six to twelve sessions. The same student six months later, with the same errors now habitual and a shorter runway, needs more hours to achieve less. The cost of delay in maths is measured in sessions rather than in rates.

The second pattern is about what the hours are spent on. Re-teaching content a student already knows feels productive to everyone in the room and changes nothing on a paper. Marking a paper strictly, categorising the losses and drilling the specific habit that produced them feels slower and moves grades. A parent can tell which is happening by asking what the session's homework was: a page of similar questions is the first; three questions and a rule about showing working is the second.

Our own practice follows from this. The free trial lesson exists to produce an hours estimate from the work rather than a rate quoted from a price list. Sometimes that estimate is smaller than the family expected. Occasionally it is that no tutoring is needed and the student should be marking their own papers against the mark scheme, which costs nothing.

sections.heading: Tier sets the ceiling, and therefore the budget
paragraphs: Before any money is spent, confirm the tier in writing. It decides the highest grade available to your child, which decides what tutoring can and cannot achieve, which decides how much of it is worth buying. Families regularly discover the tier after months of sessions aimed at a grade the entry did not permit.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended, with Core graded from C to G and Extended from A* to E; the 0980 variant reports on the 9 to 1 scale with the Core tier capped. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher, with Foundation reporting 5 to 1 and Higher 9 to 4. Structures and grading can be revised between specification versions, so confirm against the board's current documents and your child's entry.

The budget consequence is direct. A Core or Foundation student aiming for the top of their tier needs accuracy and exam technique, which is a small number of well-marked hours. A student who should move tier needs a content programme and a conversation with the school about the entry, which is a larger commitment and has a deadline attached. Spending specialist money on a Core student's top-band topics is a waste, because those topics are not on their paper.

The question a tutor can genuinely help with is whether the current performance is a tier problem or a preparation problem. A student losing marks on method and reading rather than on content is usually in the right tier with the wrong habits, and the cheap fix applies. One losing marks because whole topics are missing is a different case, and the school holds the assessment record that should decide it.

sections.heading: Board structures differ, and buying the wrong practice is pure waste
paragraphs: The cheapest avoidable error in IGCSE maths tutoring is practising the wrong board's papers. The content overlaps enough that nobody notices for weeks, and the format difference shows up as a timing problem in the real exam, which then gets misdiagnosed as weak knowledge and treated with more hours.

The structures to confirm are the paper count, the calculator rules and the formula provision. Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator written paper alongside a calculator paper, so hand fluency is directly examined. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, which shifts the examined habit towards efficient and well-documented calculator use. Formula provision also differs, and a student who has learned to expect a formula on the page loses marks when it is not there.

That difference changes what the sessions are for. A Cambridge student needs regular non-calculator work: arithmetic with fractions, surds where relevant, and mental estimation. A Pearson student needs calculator discipline: showing the input, sketching what the display showed, and not trusting a window that hides a root. Buying the wrong one of those two is buying hours that do not touch the examined skill.

Confirm all of it against the board's current specification for your child's entry year, because paper structures are revised between versions. Those documents are free to read on the board's own site and are the thing any competent tutor works from. Nobody should be selling them to you as a resource pack.

sections.heading: Which maths topics repay tutoring, and which absorb it
paragraphs: Not all topics cost the same to fix or return the same number of marks, and a family paying by the hour should know the difference. This is the ranking we would use when time or money is limited.

Highest return, in order: exam technique and method marks; algebraic manipulation; the specific tier-relevant topics that carry the most paper marks. Exam technique comes first because it is not a topic at all — it is showing working, answering the command word, keeping units and not rounding mid-calculation. Three papers marked strictly to the mark scheme routinely recover more marks than three topics taught, and they take a third of the time.

Algebra comes next because everything depends on it. A student fluent in rearranging and factorising gains marks in geometry, trigonometry and graph work without those being taught again. For Core and Foundation students, number, ratio and percentages carry a large share of the paper and deserve the same priority that algebra gets at the higher tier.

Lowest return when time is short: vectors and geometric proof at the top tier, which absorb hours for a modest mark allocation, and any topic the student has already secured. The commonest waste we see in this belt is a weekly session spent reviewing homework the student got right, which is comfortable for everybody and changes nothing. If you are paying by the hour, ask each week which specific lost marks the session was aimed at.
bullets: Best value: exam technique and method marks, then algebraic manipulation
For Core and Foundation: number, ratio and percentages carry the paper
Lowest value when short of time: vectors and proof at the top tier
Ask weekly which lost marks the session was aimed at

sections.heading: Per-hour bands for maths, and what each one really delivers
paragraphs: Maths has the widest price spread of any subject in this market because it has the most sellers. Knowing what each band buys prevents the two classic errors: paying specialist rates for supervision, and paying supervision rates for a diagnosis that will never arrive.

At AED 33 to 65 — Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 — you are buying routine: someone to sit with a student and keep them working through exercises. For a Year 8 who will not start unprompted, that is appropriate and good value. It will not identify why a Year 11 is losing method marks on the harder paper.

At AED 150 to 300 you are buying a trained subject teacher who works from the specification; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. This is the right band for most IGCSE maths work and where the hours in the first table are priced. Above it, AED 200 to 450 or more buys board-specific depth and mark-scheme-accurate marking, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 table showing AED 200 to 450+. The top band, AED 500 to 650 and above with BartyED at AED 650, buys scarcity.

In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, per Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. For maths specifically the premium buys less than in other subjects, because the work happens on a visible page and a shared screen reproduces that almost perfectly — with the useful addition that both people keep the annotated file.

sections.heading: What a marked mock tells you before you spend anything
paragraphs: The single most valuable document in this process is free, and your child's school already produced it. A marked mock paper, read properly, tells you how many hours to buy and what they should be spent on. Most families read the total and file it.

Read it instead by category. Go through every lost mark and label it: knowledge, meaning the student did not know the content; method, meaning they knew it and lost process marks through unshown working, rounding or notation; or reading, meaning they answered a different question from the one asked. Add up the three categories. The proportions are usually a surprise.

In most marked papers we see from this belt, method and reading together account for a substantial share of the loss. That matters financially because those two categories close fastest — a handful of sessions with strict marking and a rule about showing working — while knowledge gaps need teaching time. A family that knows its split can buy six sessions with confidence instead of thirty with hope.

If there is no mock yet, the first two sessions of any arrangement should generate the equivalent evidence from timed past-paper work rather than from a conversation about what the student finds hard. Students are poor witnesses to their own errors, not because they are careless but because the errors are invisible from the inside. The paper is not. Keep the categorised list somewhere you can find it, because it is also the document that tells you when to stop paying: when the method and reading columns have emptied and only a short knowledge list remains, the expensive part of the job is done.
bullets: Label every lost mark: knowledge, method, or reading the question
Method and reading errors close fastest and are usually the larger share
Knowing the split converts a vague year into a defined block
No mock yet? Spend two sessions generating the evidence, not discussing it

sections.heading: Additional Maths, and whether it is worth paying for
paragraphs: A recurring Villanova question, usually from a parent of a strong Year 10: should we add Additional Maths, and should we buy tutoring for it? The honest answer is that it depends on the post-16 plan, and that it is one of the few places where extra tuition is often genuinely the wrong purchase.

Additional Maths exists as a bridge for students who will take maths further — a preparation for A Level Mathematics or for the algebraic demand of IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. For a student heading in that direction it is useful and the content is not wasted. For a student who will take Applications and Interpretation, or who will not take maths beyond sixteen, it is an extra examined subject competing for the same evenings as the five that matter more.

The budget logic follows. If your child is heading to AA HL or A Level Mathematics and is comfortable with the main IGCSE course, the money is better spent on Additional Maths or on a bridging block than on more support for a course they already handle. If your child is working hard to secure a grade in the main course, adding another maths qualification and tutoring for it is spending in two directions at once.

There is also the Ministry of Education equivalency angle worth noting. For the British track, five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. An additional maths qualification can help that arithmetic, but a weaker grade in a core subject hurts it, so the sequencing question is worth asking before the subject is added.
bullets: Useful if the student is heading to A Level Maths or IB AA at Higher Level
Questionable if maths stops at sixteen or the main course is still a struggle
Spending on a bridging block often beats more support for a secure course
Remember the MoE five-subject count excludes Arabic and Islamic Education

sections.heading: Entry deadlines, resits and the costs that arrive late
paragraphs: Tutoring is the planned cost. Exam administration is the one that surprises families, and the calendar drives it. For a Villanova household, getting the series right is a budget decision as much as an academic one.

Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a UAE candidate, so advice built around a February window belongs to another country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exam officer which zone applies.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Checkable reference points: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables for later series which may be revised, so always open the live official timetable rather than relying on a restated date.

The financial consequence is that a resit is a second entry fee plus, usually, a further block of hours and a term of divided attention while the next course starts. A Year 11 budget allowing for one subject re-sat in the second series is realistic. One that assumes everything lands first time is optimistic, and the families who get caught out are the ones who had spent their whole tutoring budget by May.

process.title: Send the board, tier and a marked paper
process.description: Three things make the first exchange useful: the syllabus code, the tier, and a photograph of the most recent marked paper. With those we can estimate the hours before anyone discusses a rate, which is the right order. Without them the first two sessions go on finding out what the paper already shows.

process.title: Hours estimated, then priced
process.description: We quote after the free trial lesson because the rate depends on the level of work and the number of sessions depends on the evidence. A single headline figure quoted before anyone has seen a marked paper is a figure set for the seller's convenience rather than the student's need.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: A real lesson with the person who would continue, no card required. It produces a diagnosis and an hours estimate: which losses are knowledge, which are method, which are reading the question. Sometimes the estimate is smaller than you came expecting, and occasionally it is that no tutoring is needed.

process.title: A plan with a session count and a finish date
process.description: You get the topics, the order, the number of sessions and the date it ends, set against the school's own deadlines and the board entry date. A plan without a finish date is a subscription. Eight sessions that close a gap beat thirty that keep a slot warm.

whyPoints.title: Hours before rates
whyPoints.description: The size of an IGCSE maths bill is set by the number of sessions, not the hourly figure, so the free trial lesson produces an hours estimate from marked work. That occasionally means recommending fewer sessions than a family arrived expecting to buy, which is the point of estimating honestly.

whyPoints.title: No travel, so no travel premium
whyPoints.description: Nobody drives to Al Qudra Road and no parent drives to Motor City. That removes the AED 50 to 150 hourly premium a visiting tutor charges in this belt and the two hours of household time a centre visit consumes. In maths the online format gives up almost nothing.

whyPoints.title: Board and tier confirmed first
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ on tiering and calculator rules, so practice on the wrong board's papers is wasted money that nobody notices for weeks. We confirm the specification and tier before the first session rather than after a term of it.

whyPoints.title: Marked to the mark scheme
whyPoints.description: Work is marked the way the examiner marks it, with method marks, notation and rounding treated seriously rather than ticked as broadly right. That is where the cheapest recoverable marks are, and it is why three strictly marked papers often beat three topics taught.

whyPoints.title: Every figure sourced
whyPoints.description: Each AED band on this page names who published it and is presented as the market rather than our price. We publish no statistic without a source, no self-awarded rating, and nothing sold that should not be — no promises about final grades and no resold board material.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tutoring cost for a Villanova family over a year?
faqs.answer: At the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, a weekly slot across the school year is roughly thirty sessions and AED 4,500 to 9,000. A mock-driven block of six to twelve sessions is AED 900 to 3,600 and for many Year 11 students does more. In-home visits to this community run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. Those are published market figures; our own rate is quoted after the free trial, once the hours estimate exists.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions does my child actually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the starting point far more than on the tutor. A Year 9 with shaky algebra typically needs six to ten sessions. A Year 10 with one diagnosed topic gap needs four to eight. A Year 11 working from a marked mock needs six to twelve. A student genuinely behind on content needs twenty to thirty across a year. The expensive case is a February start with no diagnosis, where hours get bought under pressure and there is no time left for the cheap fixes.

faqs.question: Why does the tier matter before I spend money on maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Because it sets the highest grade available, which decides what the hours can achieve. Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended, with Core graded C to G and Extended A* to E; Pearson 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher, reporting 5 to 1 and 9 to 4. Spending specialist money on top-band topics for a Core student is waste, because those topics are not on their paper. Confirm the tier in writing from the entry statement and check it against the board's current documents.

faqs.question: My Villanova neighbour's child does a different maths paper - why?
faqs.answer: For tutoring, yes. Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator written paper alongside a calculator paper, so hand fluency is directly examined. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, which shifts the examined habit towards documented, efficient calculator use. Formula provision also differs. Practising the wrong board's past papers is the cheapest avoidable waste in this market: the content looks similar enough that nobody notices for weeks, and the mismatch shows up as a timing problem in the real exam.

faqs.question: Which maths topics give the best return for the money?
faqs.answer: Exam technique first, which is not a topic: showing working, answering the command word, keeping units, not rounding mid-calculation. Three papers marked strictly to the mark scheme routinely recover more marks than three topics taught. Then algebraic manipulation, because geometry, trigonometry and graph work all depend on it. For Core and Foundation students, number, ratio and percentages carry a large share of the paper. Lowest return when time is short: vectors and geometric proof at the top tier.

faqs.question: Can I use my child's mock paper to decide how much tutoring to buy?
faqs.answer: That is exactly what it is for, and it is free. Go through every lost mark and label it knowledge, method, or reading the question, then total the three categories. In most papers we see from this belt, method and reading together are a large share, and those close fastest — a handful of sessions with strict marking and a rule about showing working. Knowledge gaps need teaching time. Knowing your split turns a vague year of sessions into a defined block.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class at a Motor City centre cheaper overall?
faqs.answer: Per hour, clearly; monthly packages in this market are advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions. Overall, count the drive: twenty-five to forty minutes each way from Villanova plus waiting is around two hours of household time per session. A group also delivers one pace to everyone, which suits a student who is broadly on track and needs more practice, and cannot address an individual diagnosed gap. If you can name the problem in one sentence, a short one-to-one block is usually cheaper to the finish line.

faqs.question: Will a maths tutor come to our house in Villanova?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video; home visits are a service we offer only in India, so no tutor will arrive at a Dubailand address. Independent in-home maths tutors work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, and Villanova sits at the top of that range because the drive is long. For maths the online format gives up unusually little, since the whole lesson is a shared working surface that both people can write on and keep.

faqs.question: Should we add Additional Maths, and pay for tutoring in it?
faqs.answer: Only if your child is heading towards A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and is already comfortable with the main IGCSE course. In that case the content is not wasted and the money is better spent there than on more support for a course they already handle. If maths stops at sixteen, or the main course is still a struggle, adding a second maths qualification plus tutoring for it is spending in two directions at once.

faqs.question: What if we run out of budget before the June series?
faqs.answer: Then spend what is left on marking rather than teaching. The cheapest effective arrangement for a student with some content knowledge is two or three sessions in which a timed past paper is marked strictly to the mark scheme and the losses categorised, with the student doing the papers alone between sessions. That is where most recoverable marks are. It also helps to keep a small reserve: a resit in the November series means a second entry fee, which no tutoring quote includes.

faqs.question: How much does a maths resit cost after a disappointing June result?
faqs.answer: A second entry fee, quoted by the exam centre rather than by any tutor, plus whatever further hours you decide on — typically eight to fifteen sessions for a focused resit, since the diagnosis already exists. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates and Pearson runs May/June and November, so there is a route each year. Ask the school's exam office for the actual entry figure rather than estimating it, because centre charges vary.

faqs.question: Are maths tutors working with Dubai students required to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. A MoHRE private tuition work permit is required for individuals providing private tutoring in the UAE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years according to u.ae. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because the permit is free, no tutor should be passing on a licensing cost. No fine schedule is published, so treat any amount quoted at you as unverified.

faqs.question: Does the quoted hourly price include VAT and materials?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get it in writing. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an opinion — so the practical rule is to require clarity from whoever is invoicing you. On materials: nobody should be charging you for Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes or specifications, which are published by the boards and should be linked rather than resold as a resource pack.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education affect the maths plan in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, through the timetable. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with instructional time based on a 40-minute lesson unit and separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Those periods are real workload competing with maths revision. Note also that for Ministry of Education British-track equivalency, Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the five subjects that count, which is worth knowing when option choices are being made.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-villanova.closingHeading: Price the hours, not the hour
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-villanova.closingBody: Before you hire an IGCSE maths tutor in Villanova, do two things that cost nothing. Get the entry statement so you know the board and the tier, and go through the last marked paper labelling each lost mark as knowledge, method or reading. Those two documents turn a vague year of weekly sessions into a defined number of hours with a defined target. Send them to us and you will get an honest hours estimate and a rate quoted after the free trial lesson, taught by the tutor who would continue. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online, and nobody drives to Dubailand.

dubai/igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the IGCSE subjects Dubai families most often choose to fund: mathematics, the three sciences, English and the humanities with the heaviest written loads. Each profile names the board and syllabus code, because that decides which paper your child is actually sitting and therefore what the hours buy.

intro.heading: Nine subjects, one budget
paragraphs: The honest starting point for this search is arithmetic rather than pedagogy. A Dubai Year 11 student is usually entered for eight or nine IGCSE subjects. Published one-to-one rates in this city run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist. Multiply any of those by nine subjects across two terms and the number is beyond almost every family. So the real question is never whether to buy tutoring; it is which subjects to buy it for.

Almost nobody in this market helps with that decision, because the decision reduces revenue. A provider selling a package across a whole timetable earns more than one that says four of those nine subjects do not need paid help. This page takes the other position: price the choice openly, state which subjects repay the spend and why, and let a family allocate a fixed budget deliberately instead of spreading it until nothing changes.

Timing is the second lever, and it is the one families do not know they are pulling. Rates do not rise by published increase as the window approaches, but availability collapses, and what is left in the final weeks is whoever is free rather than whoever knows the specification. A term booked in the first half of the year costs the same per hour and buys a materially better tutor. Booking late is the most expensive decision available here and it never appears on a price list.

The third lever is what the hour contains. A rate that covers only live minutes is not comparable with one that includes setting and marking work between sessions, and for examination preparation the marked script is the product. Two quotes at AED 250 an hour can differ by a third in real value on that single line, and the only way to see it is to ask in writing before booking.

The window itself is worth stating plainly, because competitors never do. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in a May/June window and a November window. The February and March series that appears in search results is offered to India only, so it is not a route for a candidate sitting in Dubai. Entry deadlines fall months before the papers and are handled by the exam centre.

Sessions are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, since that is an India-only service, and for a family rationing a budget that matters directly: every published Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one above the online band, and the gap is travel rather than teaching. Removing it is the one saving that costs nothing in quality.

dubai/igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: What a term costs depends heavily on which year your child is in, because the useful work is different and so is the volume. These are the three stages Dubai families buy for.

programmes.name: Pre-IGCSE year
programmes.description: The cheapest place in the whole sequence to spend money, and the one families skip. Algebra fluency, scientific vocabulary and the habit of writing method out in full are built here for a fraction of what the same gaps cost to repair in Year 11, when every hour is competing with eight other subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools finalise IGCSE option choices during Year 9, so a term of support here also informs a decision rather than only a grade. A student choosing triple science without the algebra to carry physics is a predictable and expensive problem eighteen months later.

programmes.name: IGCSE first year
programmes.description: Half the syllabus is untaught, so whole papers are poor value and topic questions marked to the scheme are good value. A term here in one or two subjects costs the same per hour as a term in Year 11 and does more, because it removes the gaps before they compound into a revision crisis.
programmes.countryNote: Tier decisions for Cambridge Core and Extended, or Pearson Foundation and Higher, are usually confirmed during or at the end of Year 10 in Dubai schools. A marked paper of the correct tier is the cheapest evidence available for that conversation.

programmes.name: IGCSE examination year
programmes.description: The expensive year, because the window is fixed and the timetable is full. The work that pays is whole papers under timing, marked and reworked, plus the practical or alternative-to-practical component that almost nobody prepares. Allocation matters more than hours: two subjects done properly beats nine done thinly.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mock examinations typically fall in the second term, and Ramadan currently sits across the February-and-March part of the academic year, shortening school hours for several weeks. Both compress the useful preparation window, which is another argument for booking the term early.

dubai/igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: The grid below is ordered by the question families actually ask: does paying for this subject change the grade. Each entry names what the money buys and where it is better spent elsewhere.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Usually the best single purchase on a Dubai timetable. Method marks are recoverable without new content, the paper structure rewards drilled technique, and the subject underpins physics and chemistry grades, so one tutor can affect three results.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Worth funding where the loss is units, significant figures and the alternative-to-practical component, which is cheap to fix and almost never taught at home. Less worth funding where the algebra is the real problem, in which case the money belongs in mathematics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations and ionic equations with state symbols carry marks that a correct answer alone does not earn. A short block aimed at calculation types and equation conventions often moves more marks per dirham than a full term of general support.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The subject where self-study with a mark scheme works best, because the losses are vocabulary and precision rather than reasoning. A monthly audited session plus the student's own marked practice is often enough, which frees budget for elsewhere.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Funding helps where the loss is audience, form and purpose on directed writing, which is structural and teachable. It helps less where a student simply reads too little, since that is a habit no hourly rate fixes inside a term.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification from First Language English with its own task structure. Confirm which one is on the entry form before buying anything, because preparation for the wrong one costs a grade and the error is common in Dubai households.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Short blocks are excellent value here. The recurring losses are generic answers that ignore the named context and missing evaluation at the end of longer questions, both of which are patterns a student can learn in four marked questions.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Structure-heavy and therefore responsive to paid help, particularly on source handling and case study detail. The content itself is largely a memory task the student can do unaided, so target the structure and nothing else.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0654 and 0653; Pearson Science Double Award
subjects.description: Worth funding carefully, because the paper pattern differs from the separate sciences and students are frequently given the wrong past papers. One session establishing the correct material can be worth more than a term of misdirected practice.

dubai/igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: Location affects price in this city mainly through travel, which online delivery removes entirely. These notes cover the scheduling reality instead, since a cancelled session is the most expensive hour a family buys.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Large British-curriculum Year 11 cohorts with mocks clustered in the same fortnight, so local in-home tutors are fully committed in the second term. The online pool is unaffected, which is where the saving and the availability both sit.

regions.note: Villa communities where in-home quotes run towards the upper end of the published AED 180 to 500 band because of distance between gates. The teaching is not better at that price; the drive is simply longer.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Long eastern commutes mean weekday sessions start late and finish tired, and cancelled sessions are the single biggest waste of budget here. A weekend block plus a short midweek check-in holds far better.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Short school runs make a 16:30 start realistic, which is the cheapest slot in the city in practical terms because it is the one least likely to be cancelled. Worth claiming early in the term.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Sports City
regions.note: Apartment communities with many mid-year arrivals, which raises the risk of practising the wrong board's papers. One code-check session here routinely saves weeks of misdirected revision and the money that went with it.

regions.name: Deira, Al Nahda and Al Qusais
regions.note: Dense, established school provision and households often running several children through examinations at once. Prioritising across siblings rather than within one timetable is the budgeting question that actually matters in this part of the city.

schoolClusters.note: Large Year 11 cohorts entering both Cambridge and Pearson, which means tutoring demand in this part of the city peaks in the same weeks every year. Families who book a term before the mock window pay the same rate for a materially better match.

dubai/igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.modesIntro: Three ways to spend a fixed budget, described by what each one costs and what it leaves behind. All three are delivered online, one to one.

modes.title: One subject, one term, weekly
modes.description: The standard purchase and the easiest to price. Twelve sessions across a term in a single subject, each setting and marking work. At published Dubai bands of AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor, that is roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600 for the term, and it should produce twelve marked artefacts you can look at.
bullets: Twelve sessions, one subject, a fixed term end date
Work set and marked between sessions, not only discussed
Raw marks logged so the first and last compare directly
A topic list that shortens rather than being rewritten

modes.title: Component blocks across three subjects
modes.description: The option most families should consider and few are offered. Four sessions each on three narrow components: alternative to practical, mole calculations, business evaluation paragraphs. Same total hours as one subject for a term, spread across three results, and aimed only at losses that are known to be recoverable.
bullets: Three components, four sessions each, all with end dates
Chosen from a marked paper rather than from a feeling
Each block closes with a written note of what remains
No rolling commitment once a block finishes

modes.title: Final-weeks paper sprint
modes.description: Six to eight weeks of whole papers under timing in the two highest-priority subjects, marked and reworked on the lost marks only. The most expensive format per week and sometimes the right one, but it should be entered knowingly: it changes habits and pacing rather than filling content gaps.
bullets: Whole papers of the correct board, code and tier
Losses classified as content, command term, method or time
A stated number of weeks, not an open arrangement
An honest statement of what the weeks can and cannot reach

sections.heading: What the May and June window actually is
paragraphs: Two boards, two slightly different answers, and a search phrase that blurs them. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in a May/June window and a November window. A Dubai candidate is therefore either a Cambridge June candidate or a Pearson May/June candidate, and most households containing both have never noticed the difference.

The February and March series that appears constantly in search results is offered to India only. It is not a route for a candidate sitting in the UAE, and a Dubai family planning around those dates is planning around the wrong country's calendar. This matters because the dates are months apart and an entry deadline missed is a year lost.

Entry deadlines are set by the boards and administered by the exam centre, which for most students is their own school. They fall months before the papers, and once passed the next opportunity is the following series. A private candidate entering a subject their school does not offer has to find a centre that accepts private entries and meet that centre's internal deadline, which is earlier again.

Cambridge adds one further detail that nobody in this market mentions. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and the board states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. Open the live official timetable for your centre's zone rather than a copy published on a tutoring site.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the window, with the money in view
paragraphs: A revision calendar is also a spending calendar, and setting them out together changes decisions. The expensive weeks are the ones closest to the papers, not because rates rise but because availability falls and because the work that remains is lower-yield. The cheap weeks are the early ones, when a term of one subject costs the same per hour and removes gaps rather than managing them.

Work backwards in blocks rather than dates, because blocks stay true from year to year. Entries close months before the papers. Mock examinations fall in the second term in most Dubai schools. The practical or alternative-to-practical component should be drilled six to eight weeks out, since it is narrow and fast. Whole-paper rehearsal belongs in the final four to six weeks. Results arrive in August, with Pearson's June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day.

The resit route sits at the far end of this calendar and should be understood before it is needed. A Cambridge candidate who does not get the grade in June sits November, and Pearson has a November window too. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which shows the real lag: a November candidate does not have a confirmed grade until the middle of the following January.
The table sets the blocks out with what should be done and what it typically costs at published rates. The column that matters is the last one: the same money buys more the earlier it is spent.

sections.heading: The nine-subject budget problem, priced honestly
paragraphs: Set out the arithmetic and the decision makes itself. At the mid published band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, a weekly session in one subject for a term costs roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600. Across nine subjects that is AED 16,200 to 32,400 a term, which no normal family funds and which would in any case be the wrong plan, because several of those subjects do not need paid help at all.

The alternative is deliberate allocation. Rank the nine by recoverable marks rather than by current grade, which needs one marked paper per subject and no more. A subject losing marks to method, command terms and presentation has high recoverability and responds inside a few weeks. A subject where whole topics are missing has low short-term recoverability and may be the wrong place for the final term's money, however alarming the current grade looks.

Then fund the top two with a term each and the next three with component blocks, and let the remaining four run on self-marked practice with a monthly audit. That shape costs a fraction of the full-timetable figure and produces more marked work, because the hours are concentrated where they convert. It is also the plan a provider loses money recommending, which is why it is rarely recommended.

The table prices three realistic shapes for the same timetable. Read the last column, which is the one that matters: the number of marked artefacts a family ends the term holding. Spreading a budget thin reliably produces the fewest.
