sections.heading: What moves the number in this emirate specifically
paragraphs: Travel is the first and largest driver. Every published Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one above online one-to-one, with Bestimate recording AED 180 to 350 for a home visit and independent tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The difference is the drive, not the teaching, and in Arabian Ranches or Mirdif the drive is longest and the premium widest.

Timing is the second. Nobody publishes a seasonal increase, and yet the final six weeks before the window are materially more expensive in real terms, because the tutors who know the specification are committed and what remains is whoever is available. A family booking in the first term gets the same hourly figure and a better match, which is the only free upgrade on offer in this market.

Inclusion of marking is the third, and it is where two apparently identical quotes diverge most. Setting work, marking it to the published scheme and writing usable comments takes real time outside the session. A rate that excludes it is cheaper per hour and considerably worse value for examination preparation, where the marked script is the entire product.

Two smaller drivers are worth naming. Level and tier, since Extended and Higher tier work and the separate sciences attract a higher specialist rate than Core or combined science. And subject scarcity, where a thinly covered subject such as a less common language or a specialist humanities option draws the upper end of the specialist band simply because few people teach it. None of these is a Dubai cost-of-living effect; they are all specification and supply effects.
bullets: Travel: removable at no cost to teaching quality
Timing: same rate, better tutor, if booked early
Marking: the line that makes two quotes comparable
Tier and scarcity: real specialist premiums, worth paying knowingly

sections.heading: Group classes, one-to-one and self-study, compared on price
paragraphs: Dubai has a large tuition-centre sector offering group classes, and for some families that is the right purchase. The honest difficulty is that none of the centres examined for this page published a per-student hourly figure, so no group rate can be quoted here with a source attached. What a parent can do is ask for it directly, in the form that makes comparison possible: the price per student per hour, the maximum group size, and whether work is marked individually.

Group classes work best where the content is being delivered rather than diagnosed. A class of six can be taught mole calculations efficiently. A class of six cannot read six different marked scripts and tell each student which of their habits is costing marks, which is the part of examination preparation that actually moves a grade late in the year. The mismatch between what a group does well and what a Year 11 needs in the final term is the thing to weigh.

Self-study with periodic audits is the most underrated option and the cheapest by a wide margin. A student who can self-mark against a published scheme and maintain an error log is doing the highest-value activity in the whole plan, and they need a tutor perhaps monthly to check the marking is honest and the log is narrowing. Teaching a student to do that is a two-session job, after which the running cost collapses.

sections.heading: Entry fees, resits and the costs that are not tuition
paragraphs: Tuition is not the only line in an examination year, and the others catch families out. Examination entry fees are set and collected by the exam centre, which for most Dubai students is their own school, and they vary by board, by subject and by whether the candidate is internal or private. No figure is quoted here because none could be sourced reliably for this page, and an invented number would be worse than none. The school's exams officer can give you the current schedule in writing.

Private candidate entries cost more in administration as well as in fees. A student taking a subject their school does not offer must find a centre that accepts private entries, meet that centre's earlier internal deadline, and in some science specifications arrange access to a practical component the centre may or may not run. All of that is worth confirming before paying for a term of tutoring in the subject.

A resit is the largest contingent cost in the year, and it is the one families never budget for. A November entry means another entry fee, another preparation block and a confirmed grade that arrives much later: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For a student holding a sixth-form or university place conditional on June grades, that lag is the consequence rather than the fee.

The useful move is to do the resit arithmetic on results day rather than in a panic three weeks later. Which component carried the loss, whether the losses were habit-shaped or content-shaped, and whether the target grade is reachable in the months available. A short decision block for that costs a fraction of a resit term spent on an unreachable target.

sections.heading: Where the marks go in the subjects Dubai families fund most
paragraphs: Mathematics is the most commonly funded subject in this city and the most reliably rewarding, for a reason worth understanding. The mark scheme pays for a visible route to the answer, so a capable student who works mentally and writes one line is discarding marks already earned. That habit changes within three marked papers, and because mathematics underpins physics and chemistry, one tutor's work can show up in three grades.

The science practical component is the largest untouched opportunity on any Dubai timetable. On Cambridge codes the alternative-to-practical paper carries a real share of the grade and needs no laboratory, because it is a written paper about practical work: results tables with units in the headings, instruments read to the correct precision, scales that fill the grid, lines of best fit, and specific errors rather than generic human error. Four sessions there is among the best value available in the whole year.

In the written humanities and in business and economics, the recurring losses are structural: generic answers that ignore the named context in the stem, and no evaluation at the end of extended responses. Both are patterns, both are learnable in four marked questions, and both are why short component blocks in these subjects outperform full terms of general support.

English divides. Where the loss is audience, form and purpose on directed writing, paid help is effective because the fault is structural and visible between two of the student's own drafts. Where the student simply reads very little, no hourly rate repairs that inside a term, and the honest advice is to spend the money elsewhere and the time on reading. Saying so costs a sale and is the correct answer.

sections.heading: Buying this well: what to ask, and what to refuse
paragraphs: Four questions make any quote in this market comparable. How long is the session. Is setting and marking work between sessions included. How many complete marked papers will exist at the end of the block. And what is the end date. A provider who answers all four in writing is quoting a service; one who answers in subjects and months is quoting a subscription.

Two things are worth refusing outright. The first is a package across a whole timetable, because it cannot produce marked work in nine subjects and is priced as though it could. The second is any offer to supply papers and mark schemes as downloads, because those belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and privately circulated copies are frequently from superseded specifications or retyped with errors.

One thing is worth insisting on: that the first session establishes the board, the syllabus code and the tier from the entry form rather than from the subject name. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are both called IGCSE Mathematics and set different papers. A term spent on the wrong one is the most expensive mistake available in this market, and it is entirely preventable with one photograph.

Every AED figure on this page belongs to the provider or source that published it, including EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED. None is an IB Gram price; our rate is quoted after the free trial lesson, with the session length and the marking inclusion stated. No success rate, average grade or satisfaction figure appears anywhere here, because none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method, and no tutor can promise a grade.

process.title: Photograph the statement of entry
process.description: It carries the board, syllabus code and tier for every subject, and the exams officer can add the centre's zone and the entry fee schedule. Thirty seconds of checking prevents the most expensive error in IGCSE preparation, which is a term spent on the other board's papers.

process.title: Rank the nine subjects by recoverable marks
process.description: One marked paper per subject, with losses classified as content, command term, method or time. Subjects losing marks to habits are high-recoverability and cheap to fix. Subjects missing whole topics are expensive and slow. Rank by that rather than by the grade that worries you most.

process.title: A free trial lesson, then a written quote
process.description: A real session with the tutor who would continue, no card details beforehand, spent on a marked script. The quote that follows should state session length, whether marking is included, the number of sessions, the end date and how many marked papers will exist at the end.

process.title: Fund two deep, three in blocks, four self-marked
process.description: Weekly sessions in the two highest-recoverability subjects, four-session component blocks in three more, and self-marked practice with monthly audits in the rest. That shape costs far less than a full-timetable package and produces considerably more marked work.

process.title: Do the resit arithmetic in August, not September
process.description: On results day, work from component marks rather than the grade: which component carried the loss, whether the losses were habits or content, and whether the target is reachable in the months available. A short decision block beats a resit term aimed at an impossible number.

whyPoints.title: We price the choice, not a package
whyPoints.description: A quote states the subject, the number of sessions, the end date and how many marked papers will exist afterwards. Recommending that four of nine subjects need no paid help costs us revenue and is usually the correct advice for a Dubai Year 11.

whyPoints.title: Early booking is the free upgrade
whyPoints.description: Rates do not rise near the window but availability collapses, so the same hourly figure buys a materially better specialist in the first term than in the last six weeks. Nobody advertises this because it moves revenue earlier rather than increasing it.

whyPoints.title: The practical component is not skipped
whyPoints.description: The Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper needs no laboratory, carries a real share of the grade and is the most neglected component in this city. Four sessions on table conventions, instrument precision and specific errors is the best value on most timetables.

whyPoints.title: Marking stated in writing
whyPoints.description: Setting and marking work outside the session is the line that makes two AED 250 quotes differ by a third in value. It is stated explicitly when we quote, because for examination preparation the marked script is the product rather than the conversation.

whyPoints.description: Every rate here is credited to the provider that published it, and no entry fee or group-class figure is quoted because none could be sourced. No success rate or average grade appears either, since neither could be produced with a sample size and a method.

faqs.question: What exactly is the May and June window for Cambridge and Pearson candidates?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in a May/June window and a November window. So a Dubai candidate is either a Cambridge June candidate or a Pearson May/June candidate, and households with children at different schools often contain both. The February and March series visible in search results is offered to India only and is not a route for a candidate sitting in the UAE.

faqs.question: How much would it cost to tutor all nine IGCSE subjects in Dubai?
faqs.answer: At the published mid band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, a weekly session in one subject for a term is roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600. Across nine subjects that is AED 16,200 to 32,400 a term. Almost no family funds that, and it would be the wrong plan anyway, because several subjects on a typical timetable need no paid help. The better approach is to fund two subjects weekly, three as short component blocks, and leave the rest on self-marked practice with monthly audits.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects actually repay the money spent on them?
faqs.answer: Mathematics usually repays most, because method marks are recoverable without new content and the subject underpins physics and chemistry grades. The Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper repays extraordinarily well for the hours involved, since it needs no laboratory and is almost never practised. Business, economics, geography and history repay short structural blocks aimed at context application and evaluation. Biology often does not need paid hours at all, because its losses are vocabulary and precision, which a student can fix with a mark scheme and monthly audits.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE examination entry cost, and who decides it?
faqs.answer: Entry fees are set and collected by the exam centre, which for most Dubai students is their own school, and they vary by board, subject and whether the candidate is internal or private. No figure is published here because none could be sourced reliably for this page, and an invented number would be worse than none at all. Ask the school's exams officer for the current schedule in writing, and ask separately about private candidate entries, which carry additional administration and sometimes a practical access question in the sciences.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a Dubai tuition centre better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For delivering content to a cohort, often yes. For the work that moves a grade in the final term, usually not, because a class cannot read six different marked scripts and tell each student which habit is costing them marks. None of the centres reviewed for this page published a per-student hourly figure, so ask for it in the form that allows comparison: price per student per hour, maximum group size, and whether work is marked individually. Those three answers settle it quickly.

faqs.question: When does the entry deadline for the written window fall?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, set by the board and administered by the exam centre, which is normally your child's school. Once it passes, the next opportunity is the following series, which for a Cambridge candidate means waiting from June to November. A private candidate entering a subject their school does not offer faces an earlier internal deadline at whichever centre accepts them. Ask the exams officer for the centre's own deadline rather than the board's, because the centre's is the one that binds your family.

faqs.question: When do June results arrive and what can we do with them?
faqs.answer: In August. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, which is the published pattern to plan against. The useful thing to do on results day is not to react to the grade but to get the component marks, because they show whether one paper carried the loss or whether it was spread. That distinction decides whether a November resit is a narrow fix with a good case or a long rebuild with a weak one, and it is worth an hour of somebody's time.

faqs.question: Does the price go up as the examination window gets closer?
faqs.answer: Not as a published increase, and that is what makes it deceptive. What happens instead is that the tutors who know the specification become fully committed, so the same hourly rate buys a weaker match in the final six weeks than it does in the first term. In real terms the late booking is considerably more expensive. Booking a term early is the only free upgrade available in this market, and no provider advertises it because it moves revenue earlier rather than increasing it.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to our house in Mirdif or Arabian Ranches for revision?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that is an India-only service, and all sessions are delivered online over live video. For a family rationing a budget this matters directly. Every published Dubai rate table places in-home one-to-one above the online band, with home visits at AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in against AED 150 to 300 online, and the difference is the drive rather than the teaching. Removing it costs nothing in quality.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start in September or in January?
faqs.answer: September, for two reasons that have nothing to do with the rate. Content gaps are still fixable in the first term, so hours convert into marks rather than into damage control. And full tutor choice exists, meaning the same hourly figure buys a specialist in your child's exact specification rather than whoever is free. A January start is viable and narrower: realistically two subjects deep, one or two component blocks, and an honest statement of what will not be covered.

faqs.question: What should a term of one subject actually cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Twelve weekly sessions at the published qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 an hour is roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600 for the term. At the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above it is AED 2,400 to 5,400 and up. Those are market figures from Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table rather than IB Gram prices. Whatever you are quoted, the figure to compare is cost per marked artefact, because twelve sessions that produce no marked work are not twelve sessions of preparation.

faqs.question: Does the quoted rate include marking my child's papers?
faqs.answer: Ask in writing, because it differs across this market and it is the single line that makes two similar quotes incomparable. Setting work, marking it against the published scheme and writing usable comments takes real time outside the lesson. A rate excluding it is cheaper per hour and much worse value for examination preparation, where the marked script is the product. IB Gram states the inclusion when quoting, along with session length, because without both the hourly number means very little.

faqs.question: Can we save money by having one tutor cover three subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A tutor with a physical-sciences background can often cover mathematics and physics well, and a humanities tutor may cover geography and history credibly. The saving is in scheduling and continuity rather than in the hourly rate. Where the tutor knows one subject deeply and the others loosely, the economy is false, because the hours go into general support rather than into the specific component losses that actually move a grade.

faqs.question: What should we do if August results are not what we needed?
faqs.answer: Get the component marks before deciding anything. A loss concentrated in one paper is a strong case for a November entry with a narrow plan; marks lost evenly across every component is a weak one. Then check the practical consequence: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November candidate has no confirmed grade until the middle of the following January, which matters if a sixth-form or university place depends on it. Do that arithmetic in August rather than in September.

faqs.question: Are there affordable options if the budget is genuinely tight?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the cheapest is also one of the most effective. Teach the student to self-mark against the published mark scheme and keep a four-column error log, which is a two-session job, then buy a monthly audited session to check the marking is honest and the log is narrowing. At published rates that is roughly AED 450 to 1,350 a term across several subjects. Add one component block in the highest-return place, usually the science practical paper, and a tight budget still produces real marked work.

dubai/igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Decide where the money goes before you spend any
dubai/igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.closingBody: Do three cheap things first. Photograph the statement of entry so the board, code and tier are known for every subject. Have your child sit one paper per subject and classify the losses as content, command term, method or time. Then rank the nine by recoverable marks rather than by the grade that worries you most. With that in hand, book the free trial lesson and ask for a written quote stating session length, whether marking is included, the number of sessions, the end date and how many marked papers will exist afterwards. Every AED figure on this page is attributed, so you can check the whole comparison yourself.

intro.heading: The question a Dubai IGCSE mock is really asking
paragraphs: An IGCSE mock is a tier decision disguised as a grade. By the time a Dubai school runs Year 11 mocks, usually somewhere between November and January, it has already made provisional entry choices: which board, which tier, and in tiered subjects whether the student sits Core or Extended. The mock tests whether those choices were right. A student scoring 62 per cent on an Extended paper and a student scoring 91 per cent on a Core paper can both be described as doing well, and only one of them is entered for a paper that can reach a grade 9.

That is the piece families most often do not have. Parents in Dubai frequently know the subject and the predicted grade but not the syllabus code, and the code changes everything about what revision should contain. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 cover overlapping content through different paper structures, different formula provision and different question styles. Working through the wrong board's past papers for six weeks is a common and entirely avoidable waste, and we see it every mock season.

The second thing a mock reveals is the shape of the loss rather than its size. IGCSE papers are shorter and more numerous than Diploma papers, which means pacing errors show up differently: a student who runs out of time on a 90-minute paper usually has a method problem, not a speed problem, because they spent twelve minutes on a four-mark question. Marked scripts make this visible in a way no report comment does. So does the blank-space pattern, which tells you whether questions were skipped by choice or reached too late.

Dubai's own context tightens the timetable. UK-curriculum schools account for the largest share of Dubai private enrolment, which means the mock period lands on tens of thousands of households in the same six weeks, and specialist availability in the sciences narrows accordingly. KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Year 11 student that is fixed timetable, and revision hours have to come from the remaining week rather than from the one a template assumes.

All of our UAE sessions run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The reason to prefer the online format here is practical rather than philosophical: a family in Mirdif needing a Pearson 4CH1 specialist is choosing from everyone who teaches that syllabus rather than from everyone who will drive to Mirdif at 5pm.

dubai/igcse-mock-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits inside a longer school sequence, and mock preparation looks different at each point in it. Here is what the stage means for a Dubai student and for the work.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 into IGCSE
programmes.description: The years before IGCSE begins. Schools make option choices at the end of Year 9, and end-of-year assessments here are the evidence used for setting and tiering. A weak Year 9 Mathematics result can route a student into a Core entry two years early without anyone framing it as a decision.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary widely in when they start the IGCSE course: some begin in Year 9, most in Year 10. Families moving mid-year between Dubai schools frequently discover their child has started a different board, or a different tier, from the one they left. Checking the syllabus code at enrolment saves a painful discovery in the Year 11 mock.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10
programmes.description: Course content is taught across Years 10 and 11, with many Dubai schools running a formal Year 10 mock in the summer term. That paper is the earliest reliable signal on tier, and it arrives while a tier change is still administratively easy rather than contested.
programmes.countryNote: The most useful mock work in Dubai happens in Year 10, and the least of it is bought then. A Year 10 summer mock showing a ceiling on Core content gives a full academic year to build towards Extended. The same information arriving in the Year 11 January mock gives weeks, and usually the entry stays as it is.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11
programmes.description: The examination year. Mocks fall between November and January at most Dubai schools, final entries are made months before the exam window, and the June series is the main sitting for UAE candidates with November available as a resit route. Coursework or practical components in some subjects run alongside.
programmes.countryNote: Year 11 in Dubai carries a double load: IGCSE papers and the KHDA mandatory subjects, which do not pause for exam season. Students taking nine or ten subjects often find the mock fortnight is the first time they have attempted all of them under time in one week, and the result is as much about stamina as content.

programmes.name: What the grades feed into
programmes.description: IGCSE grades decide sixth-form entry at most Dubai schools, with specific grade requirements for A Level subjects or IB Diploma Higher Levels. They also carry forward into Ministry of Education equivalency, where five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or 3 are required on the British track.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools publish their own sixth-form entry grades, and they differ. A grade 6 in Mathematics may open Mathematics AA SL at one school and nothing at another. Mock results are the point at which a family can still realistically plan around those thresholds rather than react to them in August.

dubai/igcse-mock-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects Dubai families most often bring to us after a mock, with the component that actually bleeds marks in each and the board codes to check on the entry.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Mock losses are dominated by method presentation and by one or two unlearned topics, usually vectors, transformations or histograms. Extended candidates lose most on the last four questions of Paper 4. Sessions rebuild working-out so method marks survive arithmetic slips.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits cause the most mock damage, followed by the practical paper where candidates describe an experiment without naming a control variable. Unit and prefix errors quietly remove marks from otherwise correct answers throughout.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and electrolysis dominate the lost marks, with organic chemistry a late-course gap because it is often taught in the weeks around the mock. Extended candidates also lose marks on qualitative analysis detail the mark scheme states precisely.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mock scripts show content known loosely and command terms answered wrongly: 'describe' answered as 'explain', and comparisons made without a comparative word. Transport in plants and homeostasis are the recurring topic gaps in Dubai cohorts.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: The directed-writing and reading-response questions carry most of the risk, because they reward precise reference to the passage rather than general comment. Students who write fluently but do not quote lose marks they do not notice losing.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A large entry in Dubai. Mock losses cluster in the summary task, where word limits and own-words requirements are strictly applied, and in the listening paper where students answer from context rather than from what was said.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram labelling and the evaluation question decide the grade. Mock answers routinely list advantages and disadvantages without reaching a judgement, which caps the mark whatever the content knowledge behind it.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace-table questions are where marks go. Students who can program in Python often lose marks writing algorithms in the format the mark scheme requires, which is a presentation problem rather than a coding one.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Dubai cohorts alongside Mathematics. Mock losses concentrate in calculus applications and in trigonometric identities, and the paper is unforgiving of partial method because the questions are longer.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: KHDA requires these in all Dubai private schools, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. They sit outside the IGCSE entry but inside the student's week, which is why revision timetables must account for them.

dubai/igcse-mock-exam-preparation.regionsTitle: Where Dubai's Year 11 mock pressure lands
dubai/igcse-mock-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: UK-curriculum provision is spread right across Dubai, and mock timing, school-run length and household rhythm differ by community. Below is what the mock weeks look like in several of them.

regions.name: Al Barsha and The Greens
regions.note: Dense British-school cluster. Mock timetables at adjacent schools can differ by a fortnight, so students in the same friendship group are often revising different papers in different weeks.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Village Circle
regions.note: Fast-growing UK-curriculum catchment with large Year 11 cohorts. Requests here skew towards Pearson Edexcel codes, which changes which past papers are worth buying.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer schools with growing Year 11 groups. Mock weeks often fall right before the winter break, so families either front-load December or lose momentum across the holiday.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Mixed Indian and British provision with longer school runs. Evening session slots work better than late-afternoon ones, and January demand peaks later here than in newer districts.

regions.name: The Springs and The Lakes
regions.note: Established villa communities feeding long-standing British schools. Students here commonly sit nine or ten subjects, so the mock fortnight is a stamina test as much as a knowledge one.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah
regions.note: Older British schools with Cambridge-heavy entries. Science practical paper preparation is the most frequent request from this cluster after the November mock.

regions.name: Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Shorter commutes make earlier weekday sessions feasible. Many families here moved mid-sequence between schools, so verifying the board code on the entry matters more than average.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Apartment households with compressed evenings. Mock support is usually requested at short notice, four or five weeks out, rather than planned a term ahead.

schoolClusters.city: Established British-curriculum schools across Dubai
schoolClusters.note: These schools have run IGCSE for years, mark mocks against published mark schemes, and generally return scripts with subject comments attached. Their mock windows and board choices differ, so the entry document rather than the school name is what tells you which paper your child sits.

schoolClusters.city: Newer Dubai schools with growing Year 11 entries
schoolClusters.note: A cluster of schools opened in the last decade now runs full IGCSE cohorts. Entries here are split between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel more often than in the older schools, and tier decisions are frequently still open at the time of the Year 11 mock.

dubai/igcse-mock-exam-preparation.modesIntro: IGCSE mock support is bought in three shapes. All three run one-to-one over live video, and all three start from the board code and tier rather than from a generic syllabus.

modes.title: Board and tier audit
modes.description: A single session, usually the first thing a family needs. The tutor confirms the syllabus code and tier from the entry or the mock paper itself, states what the tier's grade ceiling is, and names which past-paper series are actually relevant. Families frequently leave this session with a different revision plan than the one they arrived with.

modes.title: Weekly subject block to the June series
modes.description: Regular sessions in one to three subjects running from the mock result through to the June window, with timed questions set and marked between sessions. The plan is written against the school's own dates, including coursework and practical components, and is reviewed at the halfway point against new marked work.

modes.title: Pre-mock or pre-exam intensive
modes.description: A short dense block in the final two to three weeks before a mock or a real paper, narrowed to the published scope. Full-length timed papers with marked feedback, aimed at pacing and technique rather than new content, which is the right target when the calendar is this tight.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: find the code before you revise
paragraphs: Dubai schools use both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, sometimes in the same building for different subjects. The two qualifications are comparable in standing and different in execution. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ in paper count, in what the formula sheet gives you, and in how questions are worded. A past paper from the wrong board teaches the wrong habits.

The code is printed on the entry statement, on the front of the mock paper if the school used a past paper, and is usually on the subject page of the school's curriculum handbook. If none of those are to hand, the subject teacher will confirm it in a sentence. This is a two-minute check that saves weeks, and it is the first thing we ask for, because the answer determines everything downstream.

Pearson also offers a modular route in some subjects, where units can be sat across sessions rather than all at the end. Cambridge is terminal by default. For a Dubai family that affects what a mock result means: a modular candidate may already hold a banked unit result, which changes both the risk profile and where the remaining revision hours should go. Nobody can plan that without knowing which structure applies.

Where a student sits different subjects with different boards, which happens in Dubai more than parents expect, the revision plan has to be board-specific subject by subject. The table below sets out the codes we are asked about most. Verify each against the school's entry rather than against this page, because entries change and schools occasionally switch boards between cohorts.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: the grade ceiling nobody mentions
paragraphs: In tiered subjects a student is entered for either the Core or the Extended paper, or Foundation and Higher in the Pearson wording. The tier sets the range of grades available. A Core entry cannot reach the top grades however well the paper is answered, and that is the fact most likely to be missing from a Dubai family's understanding of a strong mock result.

The mock is the moment that decision becomes visible. A student scoring in the nineties on a Core paper is telling you the tier is wrong, not that the subject is finished. A student scoring in the fifties on an Extended paper may still be better served by Extended, because a secure pass from a higher ceiling can be worth more than a comfortable one from a lower, depending on what the sixth form requires. That judgement belongs to the school, but a family cannot even enter the conversation without knowing the ceiling exists.

Dubai adds a consequence beyond the grade. Sixth-form entry at Dubai schools is usually specified in grades, and IB Diploma Higher Level entry in particular often requires a grade that a Core paper cannot award. So does Ministry of Education equivalency at the margin: the British track requires five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or 3, which Core can satisfy, but a university programme asking for higher grades in specific subjects may not be reachable from a Core entry.

The practical move after a mock is to ask the subject teacher three things: which tier is the current entry, what is the grade ceiling, and when does the entry close for a change. The third question is the urgent one, because entries are made months ahead of the exam window and the window for a change is administrative rather than academic.

sections.heading: The UAE exam calendar, counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. UAE candidates sit June and November. The February/March series exists, but Cambridge offers it to India only, and any Dubai revision plan built around it is built around the wrong country's calendar.

There is a Cambridge administrative detail worth knowing, because it has consequences. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is the school's responsibility rather than yours, but if you are reading a timetable off the internet rather than off the school's letter, that is the sentence to remember.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. Pearson's published record shows how long these timelines are: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than from a restated date.

Counted backwards, that gives a Dubai Year 11 family a clear sequence. The mock is the diagnostic, final entries close months before the papers, coursework and practical components land earlier than most plans assume, and the November series is the resit route rather than the main event. The table lays out the order; the dates belong to the boards and should be read from their own timetable pages.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE mock marks actually leak
paragraphs: Across Dubai mock scripts the same four leaks recur, and none of them is 'does not know the subject'. The first is command-term mismatch. IGCSE mark schemes are specific about what 'describe', 'explain', 'compare' and 'suggest' require, and a student who answers all four the same way scores full marks on one of them. Fixing this is fast, because the content is already there.

The second is method invisibility. In Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, method marks are awarded for working that is written down. A student who solves a problem mentally and writes one line gets the answer mark or nothing. Dubai mock scripts are full of correct thinking that earned nothing, and the repair is a habit change rather than a knowledge gain.

The third is topic-local coverage. Most IGCSE subjects have two or three topics that sit late in the teaching order and are therefore thin at mock time: organic chemistry, transport in plants, vectors and transformations, histograms. If the mock scope included them and the student has not been taught them properly yet, the mock mark understates the position considerably, and the right response is to note it and move on rather than panic.

The fourth is paper-specific technique, which is where the practical papers sit. A Cambridge practical or alternative-to-practical paper asks for named variables, specific apparatus and a repeatable procedure. Students who have done the experiments in a Dubai school laboratory still lose marks writing them up, because the write-up is a format rather than a memory. Each of these four needs different hours, and separating them is what the first session with the script is for.
bullets: Command terms: the content was known, the answer shape was wrong
Method marks: correct reasoning that was never written down
Late-taught topics: a real gap, but one the calendar explains
Practical write-up: a format to learn, not an experiment to redo

sections.heading: What IGCSE mock tutoring costs in Dubai
paragraphs: Comparing providers in this market is harder than it should be, because each quotes a different unit: an hour, a session, a month, a block. The figures below are other providers' published rates as read in October 2026, presented as the market rather than as our price list. Publishing them at all is unusual in this SERP; three of the six strongest-ranking pages for Dubai tutoring queries show no price whatsoever, and two of the rest quote in US dollars.

IGCSE rates sit below IB Diploma rates across every band, which is worth knowing because some providers quote a single figure for both. Unitors, for example, publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour against AED 200 for IB. At the budget end EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, and at the specialist end TutorChase publishes AED 270 while Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaches AED 450 and above. One premium provider publishes AED 650.

The in-home premium is the clearest number on the page. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors in Dubai are quoted up to AED 500. Monthly in-home packages appear around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits, against about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. What the difference buys is travel, and in a city where a weekday cross-town drive costs an hour, that is the honest description of it.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on these pages, because the right number depends on board, subject, tier and how many weeks are left. The trial lesson is free with no condition beyond booking a time, and the rate for the specific subject is confirmed in that conversation rather than guessed from a table.

sections.heading: Online sessions against an in-home tutor for Year 11
paragraphs: The case for online delivery in IGCSE mock work rests on one thing: syllabus specificity. A competent generalist can help a Year 11 student revise. Only someone who teaches the specific code can tell you that the four marks lost on a 4CH1 question went because the mark scheme wanted a named observation rather than a correct conclusion. Dubai's in-home market is large and real, but it is geographically bounded, and a code-specific specialist is a narrow thing to find within driving distance.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. All UAE sessions are one-to-one over live video, which is the same model stated on every other country page on this site. For mock review the format has a practical edge beyond the tutor pool: tutor and student look at the same scanned script and the same mark scheme simultaneously, annotate it together, and the annotated copy is saved rather than left on a table. Over a six-week block that archive becomes the revision resource.

Where in-home genuinely wins is younger students who need physical presence to stay on task, households where screens are already a contested resource, and subjects with a hands-on element that cannot be shown on a screen. For a Year 11 student working through board-specific past papers eight weeks before the June series, the trade runs the other way, and the comparison below shows where.

Group revision courses are the third option and the cheapest per student. They suit a broad syllabus refresh for a student whose coverage is thin across the board. They do not suit mock follow-up, because mock follow-up is by definition about one student's particular pattern of lost marks, and that is not a thing a class of fifteen can be taught.

sections.heading: IGCSE grades, MoE equivalency and what comes after Year 11
paragraphs: IGCSE results do two jobs in the UAE. The first is sixth-form entry, which is set school by school in grades and is the reason tier matters. The second is Ministry of Education equivalency, the process by which a non-UAE school certificate is recognised here, and the rules on the British track are published and specific.

As reported in July 2026, the British track requires proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, together with a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last detail is worth stating because at least one provider ranking for these queries publishes a requirement of six IGCSE subjects, which is not the rule as reported.

Two cautions belong with that. Equivalency is a Ministry process; no tutoring service performs it, influences it or guarantees it, and anything suggesting otherwise is misdescribing a regulatory procedure. And the figures above are the British track only. There is no IB points threshold published in that same source, so no IB equivalency number should be quoted to you without a Ministry page behind it. Verify your own case on the Ministry's own channel.

For planning purposes, the practical takeaway after a mock is that the five-subject rule gives a floor and the sixth-form requirements give a ceiling, and they are different numbers. A student comfortably clearing the equivalency floor may still be short of the grades their chosen A Level or Diploma Higher Level subjects require, and the mock is where that gap is first visible while there is still a year of school left to close it.

sections.heading: Starting after a Dubai IGCSE mock, without the guesswork
paragraphs: What to send first: subject, board code, tier, the mock mark and how many weeks remain. If the code and tier are not to hand, send a photograph of the mock paper's front page, which usually carries both. With that we can say whether a specialist in that exact syllabus is available, and when the answer is no, we say no rather than offering an approximate match and hoping it holds.

The marked script transforms the first session. Without it, a trial lesson is a conversation about the subject in general. With it, the tutor has already mapped where the marks went and spends the hour on the pattern. Dubai schools generally return mocks within two to three weeks, and asking the subject teacher for the mark scheme alongside the script is an ordinary request that most departments grant without fuss.

The trial lesson is free and the only condition is finding a time. It exists to answer a narrow question: can this tutor teach this syllabus to this student, and will the student come back. A mock block collapses if the student is unwilling, so we would rather a family stop after a trial than commit to eight weeks on a bad match. If we think the fit is wrong, we say it before you do.

On what a tutor will and will not do: coursework and controlled assessment in IGCSE subjects must be the student's own work. A tutor can teach the underlying skill, explain the marking criteria and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. Nothing is written or edited to completion on their behalf. We also link to official Cambridge and Pearson timetable and syllabus pages rather than redistributing those documents, because that material belongs to the boards.

process.title: Send the board code, tier and mock mark
process.description: Subject, syllabus code, tier, the mark and the weeks remaining. A photograph of the mock paper's front page usually supplies the first two. We reply with whether a specialist in that exact syllabus is free, including when the answer is that they are not.

process.title: Send the marked script and mark scheme
process.description: The script is the most useful document in the exchange. The tutor maps the mark distribution before the first session, so the trial is spent on the actual leak rather than on finding it. Most departments supply the mark scheme on request.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One live session, no condition beyond booking it. The student works on a question from their own mock paper and decides whether to continue. If the match looks wrong to us, we will say so rather than let a block start badly.

process.title: Fix the plan to the school's real calendar
process.description: Frequency and length are set against the school's mock window, coursework deadlines, practical components and the winter break, not against a template. The plan states which weeks are already full, because those are the weeks a template assumes are free.

process.title: Check progress on marked evidence at week three
process.description: Halfway through, the diagnosis is tested against a fresh piece of marked work rather than against impressions. If it was wrong, the plan changes. If a different tutor is a better fit, that is arranged rather than argued about.

whyPoints.title: Board code before anything else
whyPoints.description: Work begins by confirming whether your child sits Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, 0620 or 4CH1. Past papers from the wrong board teach the wrong habits, and this is the most common avoidable waste in Dubai mock revision.

whyPoints.title: Tier treated as a decision, not a label
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended carry different grade ceilings. A very strong Core mock mark is evidence, and we tell families to take it to the school while an entry change is still administratively possible.

whyPoints.title: Specialists reachable from any community

whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, Cambridge or Pearson endorsement and claims none. We explain what each body does and link to its own pages so anything here can be checked independently.

faqs.question: When do Dubai schools run Year 11 IGCSE mocks?
faqs.answer: Most Dubai schools sit Year 11 mocks between November and January, with some running an additional Year 10 mock in the summer term. Dates are set school by school and neighbouring schools can differ by a fortnight, so confirm with your own school rather than with other parents. Scripts generally come back within two to three weeks. If you are planning a revision block, overlay the mock window on coursework and practical component deadlines first, because those almost always fall in the same weeks and a plan that ignores them will be abandoned by the second week.

faqs.question: The mock paper does not show a board name. How do I confirm the entry?
faqs.answer: The syllabus code is printed on the entry statement, usually on the front of the mock paper, and generally in the school's curriculum handbook for that subject. If none of those are to hand, the subject teacher will confirm it in one sentence. It matters because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different formula provision and question styles, and revising from the wrong board's past papers is the most common avoidable waste we see in Dubai mock preparation. Check it before buying any revision material.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended in practice?
faqs.answer: Tier sets the grades available. A Core entry, or Foundation in the Pearson wording, cannot reach the top grades however well the paper is answered; Extended or Higher can but contains harder content. The practical consequence shows up at sixth-form entry, where Dubai schools specify grades for A Level and IB Diploma Higher Level subjects, and some of those grades are unreachable from a Core paper. If a mock produced a very high Core mark, ask the school whether the entry can still move and by what date, because that deadline is administrative and earlier than the exam.

faqs.question: Does my child sit the February or March IGCSE series in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers the February/March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series, with June the main sitting and November available as a resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Any revision plan or deadline you have seen built around a February or March exam is built on the wrong country's calendar. Work from the timetable your school issues, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and the zone version of the timetable is the one that applies to your child.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 run from about AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits with travel inside the rate, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IGCSE and IB specialists. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Monthly comparisons in the market sit near AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for in-home blocks. Those are other providers' figures. Ours depends on board, subject, tier and weeks remaining, and is confirmed after the free trial.

faqs.question: Why is IGCSE tutoring cheaper than IB tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the specialist pool is wider. Many more teachers can teach IGCSE Chemistry competently than can mark IB Chemistry HL Paper 3 to criteria, and the market prices that scarcity. Unitors, for instance, publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour against AED 200 for IB. The gap narrows for the harder IGCSE codes: Additional Mathematics 0606 and Further Pure 4PM1 command closer to Diploma rates because far fewer tutors teach them. Tier also matters, with Extended and Higher work generally priced above Core across providers in this market.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our home in Dubai for mock revision?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. The argument for that is not cost, it is reach: an in-home arrangement restricts you to specialists willing to drive to your community, and a tutor who teaches your child's exact syllabus code may not be among them. Mock review also works particularly well on a shared screen, because tutor and student annotate the same scanned script together and the marked-up version is saved for later revision rather than left behind on paper.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Dubai students most often struggle with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and the sciences dominate our mock enquiries, with Chemistry the single most requested. The pattern is consistent: moles calculations and electrolysis in Chemistry, electricity and circuits in Physics, and transport in plants and homeostasis in Biology. In Mathematics the losses cluster in vectors, transformations and histograms, and in the last four questions of the Extended paper. English Language requests rise in January, when students who write fluently discover the reading-response questions reward precise reference to the passage rather than general comment.

faqs.question: How are science practical papers assessed if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The practical component is assessed by the school and the board, not by a tutor, so nothing changes about where your child does the experiments. Cambridge offers a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on the centre; Pearson assesses practical skills through its written papers. What online sessions do is the write-up: naming independent, dependent and control variables, describing apparatus precisely, and structuring a procedure so it could be repeated. That is a format to learn rather than an experiment to redo, and it is where most practical-paper marks are lost in Dubai mock scripts.

faqs.question: My child scored well in the mock. Is tutoring still worth it?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the script tells you. A very high mark on a Core paper is a reason to talk to the school about the tier rather than to buy hours. A strong Extended mark with marks lost on the final questions suggests a short technique block rather than a term's work. A strong mark where the mock scope was only part of the syllabus means the untested topics are still unknown. We would rather look at the paper and tell you that two sessions would do, or that none are needed, than sell a block against a good result.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should my child be tutored in at once?
faqs.answer: Two is usually the practical ceiling for a Dubai Year 11 student, and often one is enough. The limit is the student's week rather than availability: school, the KHDA mandatory subjects, coursework in progress and timed practice between sessions fill it quickly. Three subjects in parallel generally means none is done properly. If three genuinely need work, we would sequence them and tell you which to start with, usually the one where the mock showed a technique problem rather than a coverage gap, because technique repairs fastest.

faqs.question: During mock season, how far can a tutor go on coursework drafts?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits. A tutor can teach the underlying skill, explain the marking criteria, discuss the student's plan and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it, or edit it to completion, and any provider offering that is exposing your child to a malpractice finding with the board. A useful parent test is to ask the student to explain their own argument without notes a week after a session. If they cannot, the work was not theirs and the risk sits with them, not the tutor.

faqs.question: What if the mock covered only half the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Then the mark understates and overstates different things at once, and you need the scope before you read the result. Ask the subject teacher exactly which topics the mock paper covered. If it excluded late-taught content such as organic chemistry or transformations, the mock tells you nothing about those and a plan built on the mark alone will skip them entirely. If it covered the full syllabus, the mark is a much stronger signal and the gaps it exposes are real. This is the first question we ask when a family sends a mock result.

faqs.question: If the mock predicts a poor June result, is the November series a sensible plan?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both Cambridge and Pearson run a November series, and for UAE candidates that is the resit route after the June sitting. Pearson's published record shows the timelines involved: its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A resit decision is best made on the actual results statement and narrowed to specific papers rather than taken as a repeat of the whole year. Your school's examinations officer handles the entry, and entry deadlines sit well before the papers.

faqs.question: Should I check a mock-revision tutor's UAE permit before booking?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount with caution. A separate KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises, which is a different thing entirely.

dubai/igcse-mock-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Start with the code, the tier and the script
dubai/igcse-mock-exam-preparation.closingBody: Three pieces of information turn a mock result into a plan: which board your child is entered for, which tier, and where the marks actually went. Send the subject, the code, the mark and the weeks remaining, and we will tell you whether a specialist in that exact syllabus is free. Add the marked paper and the mark scheme and the first session starts from the leak rather than from introductions. The trial lesson is free and the only condition is finding a time that works. Everything runs one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The hourly rate is the smallest number in this decision
paragraphs: Most searches for October and November IGCSE preparation in Dubai come from one of two places: a June grade that was not enough, or a subject a school does not offer and a family has decided to enter privately. Both are second-attempt situations in the sense that matters, because neither has a class moving through a syllabus behind it. And in both, the price a family focuses on, the tutor's hourly rate, is the least consequential figure in the decision.

The costs that actually determine whether a November entry is worth making are three. The examination entry fee, which the exam centre sets and collects and which differs for a private candidate. The preparation block, which at published Dubai rates of AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist is a known quantity once the number of sessions is fixed. And the timing cost, which is that a November result is not confirmed until the middle of the following January.

That third cost is the one nobody prices and the one that most often makes the decision. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. A candidate sitting in November is therefore holding an unconfirmed grade through the whole winter, which has consequences for sixth-form places, university applications and in some cases for school progression. Knowing that before entering is worth more than any discount on an hourly rate.

The preparation itself is cheaper than families expect, for a specific reason. A resit candidate has already been taught the syllabus, so the loss is usually in the paper rather than in the knowledge: pacing, command terms, unwritten method, missing units, generic answers where a named context was given. Those are habits, and habits move in weeks rather than terms. A resit block of eight to ten sessions aimed at two components is often the whole intervention.

What makes resits expensive is spending that block in the wrong place. Re-covering a whole syllabus when the component marks show the loss was concentrated in one paper is the commonest waste in this market, and it happens because nobody asks for the component marks. Those are available and they change the plan completely, which is why the decision block comes before any teaching.

Sessions are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, since that is an India-only service. For this window that is practically useful as well as cheaper: resit candidates are often between schools, travelling, or starting something else alongside the entry, and a plan that survives a change of address is worth more than one tied to a weekly drive across the city.

The entry is private, the preparation is entirely external, and in the sciences the practical component needs specific arrangement with a centre.

dubai/igcse-october-november-exam-prepar.subjectsIntro: Resit decisions are made subject by subject, and the useful information is where the loss normally sits and how quickly it moves. Each entry names that rather than restating content a resit candidate already has.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The most commonly re-entered subject and the one that moves fastest, because method marks are recoverable without new learning. A resit candidate who starts writing the method out typically gains across every paper, and three marked attempts reveal whether the loss was method or pacing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Units, significant figures and stating the principle in use. On Cambridge codes the alternative-to-practical paper is often the component that carried the loss, and because it needs no laboratory it is the cheapest part of a resit to fix properly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation steps and equation conventions, including state symbols. Resit scripts commonly show correct chemistry scoring poorly because the working was not written. Four sessions on calculation types usually clears the pattern.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Accepted mark scheme wording and data interpretation. A resit candidate with a textbook and the published scheme can do much of this alone, so the sensible purchase is a small number of audited sessions rather than a weekly block.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Frequently re-entered because the grade is needed for progression. The loss is usually task type and word discipline rather than language, and the components respond well to a short block of timed attempts marked against the scheme.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing on audience, form and purpose is where a resit gains most. A candidate rewriting the same task twice, a fortnight apart, with the scheme beside both versions, can see structural improvement that reading model answers does not produce.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Generic answers that ignore the named firm or economy, and no judgement at the end of extended questions. Both are patterns, both are learnable quickly, and both make these subjects unusually good resit candidates.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Entered privately more often than most subjects, usually by students heading for mathematics-heavy A-Levels or Higher Level IB. Thin tutor coverage means booking the specialist early matters more here than the hourly figure does.

subjects.name: Home languages and second languages
subjects.description: A common private entry in Dubai, where a student speaks a language at home that their school does not examine. The content is largely present; the work is text type conventions, register and the specific task structures of that specification.

sections.heading: Who actually sits this window in Dubai
paragraphs: The October and November window serves a smaller and more specific population than the main summer series, and the advice written for the summer misleads most of it. The largest group is resit candidates: students who received an August grade that did not meet a sixth-form, university or family target and are re-entering one or two subjects. The second group is private candidates adding a subject their school does not offer. The third is students who arrived in Dubai mid-year or had an interrupted Year 11 and are using the window to buy preparation time.

What the first two groups share is the absence of a class. No teacher is setting work, no cohort provides comparison, no mock timetable exists, and the school's revision programme is running for a different year group entirely. Whatever structure the candidate had in Year 11 has gone, and a plan for this window has to replace it deliberately rather than assume it.

The third group is different and is often misadvised. A student who arrived in February with half a syllabus untaught is not a weak candidate; they are an under-taught one. Entering in June regardless, on the grounds that everyone else does, can produce a grade that then needs a resit anyway. Sitting in November with ten extra weeks of teaching, and a confirmed result in January, is sometimes the better arithmetic, and it deserves to be checked rather than dismissed.

Across all three, the decisive early question is administrative rather than academic: who will enter the candidate, by when, and at what fee. A student who has left Year 11 may no longer be an internal candidate at their old school, which turns a simple resit into a private entry with an earlier deadline. That is an August conversation, not an October one.

sections.heading: The timetable and the results lag, with published dates
paragraphs: This is the one section of this page where real dates can be given with a source, and it is worth stating them precisely because the pattern repeats. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and a November window. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October through to 19 November 2026. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series. The February and March series that appears in search results is offered to India only and is not available to a candidate sitting in the UAE.

The results lag is the number that changes decisions. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So the gap between sitting a November paper and holding a confirmed grade is roughly two months, which places it well into the following calendar year and after a good deal of the admissions cycle.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why the sensible practice is to open the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than to trust a date restated on a tutoring page. Dates get revised, and a revised date that a family did not see is indistinguishable from a wrong one. Cambridge adds the zone complication: every centre sits in one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and the board states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one.

The table works the window backwards from the papers, with the published dates where they exist and the shape where they do not. Use it to see where the preparation block actually fits, which is tighter than most families assume.

sections.heading: What a resit actually costs, all three lines
paragraphs: Families price a resit by the hourly rate and then discover two other costs. The first is the entry fee, which the exam centre sets and collects and which is higher and administratively heavier for a private candidate than for an internal one. No figure is published here because none could be sourced reliably for this page, and an invented number would be worse than none; the exams officer at the centre can give the current schedule in writing, and it is a reasonable question to ask before committing.

The second cost is the preparation block, and this is the predictable one. At published Dubai rates, a qualified online subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and a specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, with TutorChase at AED 270 and a premium named tier reaching AED 650 at BartyED. An eight to ten session block therefore runs roughly AED 1,200 to 4,500 depending on tier and scarcity. Those are the providers' figures, not IB Gram's.

The third cost is the timing, and it is the one that occasionally makes the whole decision. A November candidate does not hold a confirmed grade until the middle of the following January. If a sixth-form place, a university offer or a school progression decision depends on the grade, the institution has to be willing to wait, and that willingness must be confirmed in writing rather than assumed. Where it is not forthcoming, a resit aimed at that purpose cannot achieve it however well the preparation goes.

The table puts all three lines together, which is how the decision should be read. The cheapest option in the table is also the one families skip: a decision block that occasionally ends in advice not to enter at all.

sections.heading: Which subjects are worth re-entering, and the component arithmetic
paragraphs: A resit is worth making when the loss was concentrated and habit-shaped, and it is usually a poor investment when the loss was spread and content-shaped. That distinction is invisible in a subject grade and obvious in the component marks, which is why the component marks are the first thing to request. A candidate who lost most of their marks on one paper has a far stronger case than one who lost a handful on every component, even where both ended on the same grade.

The second part of the arithmetic is the type of loss. Marks lost to pacing, misread command terms, unwritten method, missing units and generic answers are habit losses, and eight to ten weeks is comfortably enough to change a habit. Marks lost because whole topics were never understood are content losses, and those need teaching time that competes directly with the habit work. A plan should state how many of each it is dealing with.

The third part is the ceiling. Where a component cannot be re-sat, or where a coursework or practical element carries forward, the achievable grade is capped by what the remaining components can contribute at their published weightings. That is a ten-minute calculation with the syllabus document in front of you, and it is the difference between a plan aimed at a reachable grade and one aimed at an impossible one.
The table runs the decision in order. A family that can answer all five rows has a real basis for entering or not entering, and the second answer saves far more than the decision block costs.
