sections.heading: Preparing with no class behind you
paragraphs: In October the school around a resit candidate is running a programme for a different year group. There is no revision timetable, no mock, no class and no cohort, and the candidate is frequently also starting something new: a sixth form, a foundation course, a job. The structure that carried them through Year 11, whatever its faults, is gone, and the single commonest reason a resit underperforms is not difficulty but drift.

Designing against drift takes four commitments and no extra money. One fixed weekly slot at the same time, kept even in a week where little was done. Work set between sessions that is marked rather than discussed, because marked work cannot be quietly skipped. A raw mark logged every fortnight so that drift is visible in week four rather than week nine. And a stated end date, so the block can be judged rather than extended.

The second half of the problem is honesty about available hours. A candidate who has started a sixth form in September does not have the evenings a Year 11 had. A plan written for twelve hours a week when four exist will fail and will be blamed on the student. Asking how many hours genuinely exist, and designing for that number, is unglamorous and is what separates a block that works from one that is abandoned in week five.

What the block should contain is narrow by design. Two components, a timed attempt every week, a one-page habit list, and nothing else. Re-covering a syllabus is both unaffordable in the time available and unnecessary where the content was already taught, and a provider proposing it for a resit has not looked at the component marks.
bullets: A fixed weekly slot held for the whole block
Work marked rather than discussed, every week
A raw mark logged fortnightly so drift shows early
Hours designed around the candidate's real availability

sections.heading: Private candidate logistics in Dubai
paragraphs: A private entry is an administrative project before it is an academic one, and the order matters. The candidate needs a centre willing to accept private entries for that specific subject and component, and that centre's internal deadline sits earlier than the board's published one. Availability is not guaranteed by subject: a centre that takes private entries for mathematics may not for a science with a practical component or for a less common language.

The science practical is the sharpest version of this problem. Where a specification assesses practical skills through a practical test rather than a written alternative, a private candidate needs physical access to a laboratory session that the centre must run. Not every centre offers it to private candidates. Confirm which component your child will be assessed on before paying for any tutoring in the subject, because the answer changes the preparation completely.

Fees for private entries are set by the centre and are typically higher than internal entries, reflecting the administration involved. No figure is published here because none could be sourced for this page. Ask for the schedule in writing, ask whether it includes any practical or coursework administration, and ask what the centre's refund position is if the candidate withdraws, since that is the question nobody thinks to ask until it matters.

One further detail worth settling early: how results are issued to a private candidate and who releases them. For an internal candidate the school handles it. For a private candidate the route runs through the centre, and knowing exactly how and when the grade will reach you is part of the planning rather than an afterthought, particularly where an institution is waiting on it.

sections.heading: What to refuse, and what to insist on
paragraphs: Refuse a full-syllabus resit plan before anybody has looked at the component marks. For a candidate who has already sat the course, a plan that proposes re-covering every topic is either lazy or priced to be long, and in either case it spends the available weeks on content that was not the problem. Ask instead which two components the plan targets and why, with the marked paper as the evidence.

Refuse any offer to supply past papers and mark schemes as downloads. Those documents belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and the practical risk to your child is larger than the legal one: privately circulated copies are frequently from superseded specifications or retyped with errors, so a candidate learns the wrong accepted wording. The board's own channels and the centre are the correct sources.

Insist on three things in writing. The number of sessions and the end date, so the block can be judged. Whether setting and marking work between sessions is included, because for a resit the marked timed attempt is the entire product. And an explicit statement of what the block will not reach, which is the sentence that distinguishes an honest plan from a hopeful one.

Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or source that published it, including Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED, and none of them is an IB Gram price. No entry fee, practical fee or group rate is quoted, because none could be sourced. There is no success rate, average improvement or satisfaction figure anywhere on this page, since none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method, and no tutor can promise a grade on an externally marked paper.

process.title: Request the component marks on results day
process.description: Not the subject grade, the component marks behind it. They show whether one paper carried the loss or whether it was spread across everything, and that single distinction decides whether a November entry is a narrow fix with a good case or a long rebuild with a weak one.

process.title: Settle the centre, deadline and fee
process.description: Find out who will enter the candidate, by when, and at what cost, and get it in writing. A student who has left Year 11 may now be a private candidate with an earlier deadline. For a science, confirm whether the assessment is a practical test or a written alternative, because the answer changes everything.

process.title: Take the decision block before entering
process.description: Two or three sessions in which the candidate sits one timed paper per target component and the tutor marks and classifies the losses. The output is a written estimate of recoverable marks against the target. Some candidates read it and do not enter, which is a good outcome for them.

process.title: Confirm the institution will wait
process.description: If a sixth-form place, a university offer or a progression decision depends on the grade, ask the institution in writing whether it will accept a result that is confirmed in the middle of January, and keep the reply. Where the answer is no, the entry cannot serve the purpose it was intended for.

process.title: Run a narrow block with weekly marked work
process.description: Eight to ten sessions on two components, a fixed weekly slot, a marked timed attempt every week, raw marks logged fortnightly, and a stated end date. Nothing else. Re-covering a syllabus is unaffordable in the weeks available and unnecessary where the content was already taught.

whyPoints.title: All three costs stated, not just the rate
whyPoints.description: The entry fee, the preparation block and the January results lag are set out together, because the third is often the cost that decides the matter. A quote that prices only the hours has left out the part most likely to make the entry pointless.

whyPoints.title: Component marks before any teaching
whyPoints.description: A resit plan is built from the component marks and one marked timed paper, not from the subject grade. That is how a block ends up targeting two components rather than a whole syllabus, which is both cheaper and considerably more likely to work.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the boards and dated
whyPoints.description: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are the published figures, cited as such, and the live official timetable is where you should check your own series.

whyPoints.title: Designed against drift
whyPoints.description: The common failure in a resit is not difficulty but a quiet second month. One fixed slot, work marked rather than discussed, a fortnightly raw mark and a stated end date are what make the difference, and they cost nothing extra.

whyPoints.title: Honest about entries we would not recommend
whyPoints.description: Where losses were spread across every component, where the target needs a component that cannot be re-sat, or where the institution will not wait for a January result, the honest answer is not to enter. Saying that costs a sale and is the correct advice.

faqs.question: Who sits the October and November IGCSE window in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Three groups, with different needs. Resit candidates re-entering one or two subjects after an August grade. Private candidates adding a subject their school does not teach, which in Dubai is commonly a home language, an additional mathematics option or a humanities subject dropped at option time. And students who arrived mid-year or had an interrupted Year 11 and are using the window to buy preparation time rather than to make a second attempt. Advice written for the summer series misleads the first two groups in particular, because neither has a class behind it.

faqs.question: What does a resit cost in total rather than per hour?
faqs.answer: Three lines. A decision block of two or three sessions at published Dubai rates is roughly AED 450 to 1,350. A preparation block of eight to ten sessions runs about AED 1,200 to 4,500 at the published bands of AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist. The examination entry fee is set by the centre and no figure is quoted here because none could be sourced. The fourth cost is not a fee: a confirmed grade only in the middle of January.

faqs.question: When exactly does the November timetable run?
faqs.answer: For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October through to 19 November 2026, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series. Cambridge runs its own November series. Because dates get revised, the correct practice is to open the live official timetable on the board's own site for your series rather than rely on a date restated elsewhere. Cambridge candidates must also use the timetable version for their centre's administrative zone, since the board states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who uses the wrong one.

faqs.question: Why do November results take until January?
faqs.answer: Marking, moderation and awarding run on the board's own cycle, and for this series that places the release well into the following calendar year. The published evidence is specific: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day. So the gap between sitting and knowing is roughly two months for November candidates against roughly ten weeks for June candidates, but the November gap lands in the middle of the admissions year rather than before it.

faqs.question: Will a sixth form or university wait for a January result?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it must be confirmed rather than assumed. Ask the institution directly, in writing, whether it will accept a result confirmed in the middle of January for the intake in question and by what date it needs it, then keep the reply. Admissions offices answer this routinely. Where the answer is no, a resit aimed at that place cannot achieve its purpose however well the preparation goes, and knowing that before paying an entry fee is worth considerably more than the fee itself.

faqs.question: Can my child resit one paper or must the whole subject be retaken?
faqs.answer: This depends on the board and the specification, and it is the question to put to the exam centre rather than to a tutoring site, because the answer determines the arithmetic. Where a component carries forward or cannot be re-sat, the achievable grade is capped by what the remaining components can contribute at their published weightings. That is a short calculation with the syllabus document in front of you, and it is how you find out whether the target grade is arithmetically available before committing to a block of preparation.

faqs.question: How do we enter as a private candidate for this window in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Find a centre that accepts private entries for the specific subject and component, and work to that centre's internal deadline, which sits earlier than the board's published one. Availability varies by subject, and a centre taking private mathematics entries may not take a science with a practical component or a less common language. Ask for the fee schedule in writing, ask whether it covers practical or coursework administration, and ask how results will be released to a private candidate and when.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to resit in November or wait for the following June?
faqs.answer: November is usually cheaper in preparation hours, because the content is still fresh and the block can be narrow. June is sometimes better in total value, because it allows a longer plan where content gaps are real and because the result lands inside the main admissions cycle rather than in the middle of January. The deciding factor is rarely money. It is whether the loss was habit-shaped, which November suits, or content-shaped, which it does not.

faqs.question: What do we do about the science practical as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Establish first which component your child will actually be assessed on, because specifications differ: some assess practical skills through a written alternative-to-practical paper and some through a practical test requiring laboratory access. Where a practical test applies, the centre has to run it and not every centre offers that to private candidates. Confirm this before paying for any tutoring in the subject, since a written alternative can be prepared for entirely at a desk while a practical test cannot.

faqs.question: There is no school revision programme in October. How do we build structure?
faqs.answer: Four commitments, none of which cost extra. One fixed weekly slot at the same time, kept even in a week where little was done. Work set between sessions that is marked rather than discussed, because marked work cannot be quietly skipped. A raw mark logged fortnightly so that drift becomes visible in week four rather than week nine. And a stated end date so the block can be judged. Then design the hours around what genuinely exists, especially if the candidate has started a sixth form or a job.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to our home in Dubai for November preparation?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that is an India-only service, and all sessions are delivered online over live video. For this window the online format solves a real problem rather than imposing one. A high proportion of candidates for this series have moved school, started a foundation course, begun working, or left the emirate entirely since June, and a plan that survives a change of city and a change of time zone is worth far more than one tied to a weekly drive.

faqs.question: How many weeks of preparation does a resit actually need?
faqs.answer: Eight to ten sessions across the weeks between an August result and the papers is the usual shape, and it is enough when the plan targets two components rather than a syllabus. Habit losses such as pacing, command terms, unwritten method and missing units change inside three marked timed attempts. Where whole topics were never understood, more time is needed and the plan should say how much of the available weeks those topics will consume, because they compete directly with the habit work that pays faster.

faqs.question: Does the November paper differ from the June one?
faqs.answer: Each series has its own papers, so a candidate is not sitting a recycled version of the June paper. The syllabus and the mark scheme conventions are shared, which means past papers from either series are legitimate practice. What differs around the paper matters more: there is no class behind the candidate, specialist tutor availability for a given component is thinner, and the result lands in the middle of the following January. Plan around those three rather than around any imagined difference in difficulty between the series.

faqs.question: Which subjects are worth re-entering and which are not?
faqs.answer: Worth re-entering: mathematics, where method marks recover quickly; the Cambridge science codes where the alternative-to-practical paper carried the loss, since it needs no laboratory; and business, economics, geography and history, where the losses are structural patterns learnable in a few marked questions. Weaker cases: subjects where marks were lost evenly across every component, subjects where whole topics were never understood, and any subject where the target grade needs a component that cannot be re-sat. The component marks tell you which category you are in.

faqs.question: What should we refuse to pay for in a resit block?
faqs.answer: Refuse a full-syllabus plan proposed before anybody has looked at the component marks, because it spends scarce weeks on content that was probably not the problem. Refuse any offer to supply past papers and mark schemes as downloads, since those belong to the boards and privately circulated copies are often from superseded specifications or retyped with errors. Insist instead on the number of sessions, the end date, whether marking is included, and an explicit written statement of what the block will not reach.

dubai/igcse-october-november-exam-prepar.closingBody: The order matters more than the budget. Ask for the component marks rather than the subject grade. Find out who will enter the candidate, by when and at what fee, and whether a science is assessed by a practical test or a written alternative. Ask the sixth form or university in writing whether a grade confirmed in the middle of January is acceptable, and keep the reply. Then take a short decision block, with one timed paper per target component marked and classified, and read the written estimate. If the target is reachable, a narrow eight to ten session block is usually the whole plan. If it is not, you have saved a term.

dubai/igcse-online-tuition.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IGCSE at Core and Extended tier across the Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications Dubai schools enter. Each one works to a named syllabus code, marks to the published scheme, and writes the session note your child revises from.

intro.heading: Judge tuition by what it leaves on the page, not by how the lesson felt
paragraphs: A Dubai parent paying for IGCSE support is buying a change in a grade that will be printed in August. The trouble is that almost nothing in a tutoring relationship reports on that directly. A lesson can be warm, well-paced and entirely useless. A tutor can be charming and never once mark a paper to a scheme. By the time the real evidence arrives, in the form of a results slip, the Year 11 is over and there is no second attempt before the UCAS or university-application cycle that depends on it.

So this page is organised around evidence. Not testimonials, not a promise about grades, but the specific artefacts a competent IGCSE session produces and the order in which they appear. In week one you should be holding a diagnostic: a timed section of a real past paper, marked, with the lost marks grouped by cause rather than by question number. By week four you should have a short written list of recurring errors and the first evidence that one of them has stopped recurring. By week ten you should be able to put two marked papers side by side and point at the difference.

Online delivery is what makes that trail practical rather than aspirational. A shared screen holds the paper, the mark scheme and the annotation in the same frame, and the file is still there the following week. A tutor working on paper in a living room in Arabian Ranches hands your child a sheet that is lost by Thursday. The same tutor working over video leaves a dated PDF. Nothing about that is a compromise forced by geography; it is simply a better record, and it is the reason the written trail on this page is possible at all.

There is a second reason Dubai families end up here. The city has 227 private schools and 17 different curricula running at once, and British-curriculum provision carries the largest share of enrolment. That density means the subject your child needs help with may be well covered by tutors living fifteen minutes away, or it may be covered by nobody within an hour's drive. Combined Science at Extended tier is easy to staff. Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics, or Edexcel International GCSE Further Pure Maths, is not. Online removes the drive from the equation entirely, so the match is made on the syllabus rather than on the map.

IB Gram arranges tuition for UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not run home visits in Dubai; that is a service we operate only in India, and saying so plainly is more useful than implying a tutor will appear at the door. What you get instead is a specialist in the exact tier and board your child is entered for, a timetable that survives a 7:20am school start, and a feedback record you can actually audit. The rest of this page sets out what that record contains, week by week.
bullets: Week one produces a marked diagnostic, not an introductory chat
Every paper is marked to the published scheme, with lost marks grouped by cause
Session notes are dated and cumulative, so term-on-term movement is visible
Core and Extended tier decisions are made from mock evidence, not from instinct

dubai/igcse-online-tuition.programmesIntro: Dubai schools enter IGCSE through two main boards and several routes into it. The programme your child sits determines the paper structure, the tier available and the retake calendar, so it is worth being precise about which one appears on the school report.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The most widely entered IGCSE route in Dubai's British-curriculum schools. Subjects carry four-digit syllabus codes - 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English - and most sciences and maths are tiered into Core and Extended. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series each year, and those are the two a UAE candidate sits; the February and March series is offered to India only. Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres sit the June series in the main, with November used mostly for retakes and private candidates. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so the first thing a tutor should ask a Dubai family for is the school's own timetable rather than a generic one found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The second major route, identified by codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics and 4CH1 Chemistry. Mathematics is tiered Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, and several specifications are available in a modular structure where units can be sat and banked across series. Exams run in May/June and November, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series.
programmes.countryNote: A number of Dubai schools mix boards by subject, entering Cambridge sciences alongside Edexcel Mathematics. Parents often discover this only when a tutor asks for the specification code. The November 2026 Edexcel International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which makes it a genuine retake window for a Dubai Year 12 who needs one grade lifted.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary into IGCSE
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE begins, assessed through Checkpoint tests offered in March, May and October. This is where the algebra, proportional reasoning and scientific-writing habits that IGCSE then assumes are either built or missed. A Year 9 who cannot rearrange a formula reliably will meet that gap again in 0580 Paper 4 and in every quantitative question in 0625.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this stage matters more than it looks, because mid-year arrivals are common. A student joining a British-curriculum school in Dubai from a CBSE or American background in Year 9 has usually met the content but not the command-term style, and Checkpoint results are the cheapest early warning a parent will get.

programmes.name: Post-IGCSE routes: A Level and IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE grades in Dubai are a gate rather than a destination. Most British-curriculum schools in the emirate require a grade 6 or 7 at IGCSE before admitting a student to the same subject at A Level, and IB Diploma Higher Level entry is usually pitched at a similar bar. The tier sat at IGCSE matters here: a Core-tier maths grade caps at grade 5 under Cambridge's tiering, which closes some sixth-form doors regardless of effort.
programmes.countryNote: Because Dubai offers both routes in volume - British schools dominate by enrolment, with International Baccalaureate schools taking a smaller share - the same IGCSE result can lead to an A Level block in Jumeirah or a Diploma at an IB school in Al Barsha. Getting the tier decision right in Year 10 protects both options.

dubai/igcse-online-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Dubai families most often ask about, with the tier structure and the part of the assessment where marks reliably go missing. Every one of them is taught one-to-one over live video.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended tier adds functions, transformations of graphs, vectors and more demanding trigonometry. Marks are lost less often on the hard topics than on unstructured working: an answer with no intermediate line scores zero where the method mark was available. A session here is usually spent making working legible and habitual rather than teaching new content.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Entered by a small number of Dubai schools for students heading to A Level Maths or Further Maths. Calculus, series and proof appear two years earlier than most students expect. This is the clearest example of a subject where the tutor pool within driving distance of any one Dubai community is thin, and an online match is the only realistic way to get a specialist.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity, electromagnetic induction and the practical paper account for most of the gap between a 6 and an 8. Candidates who can recite the formula still lose marks for unit conversion and for describing an experiment without naming the controlled variable. The Alternative to Practical paper rewards method vocabulary that is rarely taught explicitly in class.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic reaction pathways are the recurring pressure points. Extended tier asks for mole calculations with limiting reagents and percentage yield, where Core stops short. Equation balancing errors cascade: one wrong coefficient in part (a) removes the follow-through marks in parts (b) and (c) unless the working is clear enough for the examiner to award them.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem rather than the difficulty. Students who revise by reading lose marks on command terms: a question asking them to explain osmosis in a plant cell wants water potential and the cell wall named, not a description of water moving. Extended tier adds genetics and inheritance diagrams that must be drawn to convention.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Two IGCSE grades, or one double award, covering biology, chemistry and physics in less depth. Dubai students sitting this route are often aiming for a non-science A Level and need efficiency rather than extension: knowing precisely which sub-topics are on the paper and which are not is worth more than extra content.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading Paper 1 is where grades move. Directed-writing and summary questions carry specific mark tariffs for content points, and candidates who write beautifully but miss the point allocation cap themselves in the low 20s. Timing is the other half: the paper punishes students who over-invest in the first response.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.levels: Single tier · with or without spoken endorsement
subjects.description: A different specification from 0500, with a different mark profile, and Dubai schools enter both depending on the cohort. Students moved from 0510 to 0500 mid-course - a frequent occurrence in the emirate's transient school population - meet a reading paper that assumes two years of writing practice they have not had.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Data-response questions carry the available marks, and the usual loss is analysis without application: a correct textbook definition applied to no business in particular. Evaluation marks require a judgement with a reason attached. These are teachable in a handful of sessions, which makes them an unusually efficient place to put tuition hours.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: The written paper tests pseudocode, trace tables and data representation rather than coding fluency, and students who program confidently in Python still lose marks writing pseudocode to the syllabus convention. Dubai schools entering both Computer Science and ICT sometimes enter different boards for each, which changes the practical component entirely.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. IGCSE Arabic sits alongside that requirement rather than replacing it, and the two are often confused on a school report.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source-based questions and the extended response carry the marks. A student who knows the case study and writes it as narrative scores in the middle band; the top band needs the source interrogated, the provenance used and a conclusion that answers the question asked. Mark-scheme literacy moves these grades faster than content revision does.

dubai/igcse-online-tuition.regionsIntro: Online delivery means the tutor is matched to the syllabus rather than to the drive. These Dubai communities are listed because the school clusters around them shape when a session can realistically start, not because a tutor is based in any of them.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Apartment living, two school runs in opposite directions and a 6pm bottleneck on Sheikh Zayed Road. Sessions here work best at 4:30pm or after 7:30pm, and the evening slot is the one families keep.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Mudon
regions.note: Villa communities with long single-direction commutes. Year 11 students here often arrive home after 4pm with a sports fixture already in the diary, which pushes IGCSE revision into the 7pm to 9pm band on two fixed weeknights.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Dense British-curriculum provision within a few kilometres, which makes in-person tutoring look easy until a specific subject is needed. Families here most often ask for Extended Maths and 0500 English rather than general support.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Fast-growing school catchment with several schools opened in the last five years. Cohorts are young, so demand skews to Year 9 and Year 10 foundation work ahead of the IGCSE entry decision.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Established family districts on the Sharjah side of the city. The drive to a tutor in Jumeirah is the whole objection to in-person tuition here, and it disappears entirely once lessons run over video.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Apartment towers with working parents on long days. The practical constraint is a quiet room rather than travel, and sessions are frequently scheduled at 8pm once the household has settled.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: High turnover of residents, which means mid-year school transfers and students arriving part-way through a two-year IGCSE course. Diagnostic marking matters more here than anywhere else in the city.

regions.name: Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Schools and universities sitting side by side, with families who already treat online learning as normal. Requests cluster around Computer Science, ICT and Extended Maths.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
schoolClusters.note: The oldest concentration of British-curriculum secondary provision in Dubai, and the cluster where IGCSE entry policy is most settled. Students we support in these catchments are usually entered for Cambridge sciences with a mixed-board maths entry.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Dubai Hills and Tecom
schoolClusters.note: A newer and much larger cluster, including several schools that opened within the last decade. Cohorts are still working through their first full IGCSE cycles, which is why Year 10 tier decisions are the most common request from these catchments.

schoolClusters.city: Nad Al Sheba, Meydan and Sobha Hartland
schoolClusters.note: Villa communities built around schools rather than the other way round. Session timing here is set by the length of the commute home, and almost all of the IGCSE work we are asked for falls after 6:30pm.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
schoolClusters.note: Mixed-curriculum districts where British-curriculum, Indian-curriculum and American schools sit within the same few blocks. Families here often have children on two different boards at once, which complicates the revision calendar.

dubai/igcse-online-tuition.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every IGCSE request we receive from Dubai. All three run as live one-to-one or small-group video sessions; none of them involve a tutor travelling to a UAE address.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, year-round
modes.description: Two fixed slots a week per subject through Year 10 and Year 11, with the same tutor throughout. This is the format the evidence trail on this page assumes: a diagnostic in week one, a marked paper roughly every third session, and a cumulative note file the student revises from in the final term.
bullets: Same tutor across both IGCSE years where scheduling allows
Marked past-paper section at least every third session
Dated session note after every lesson, kept in one place
Tier review at the end of each term, with the mock evidence attached

modes.title: Exam-term intensive
modes.description: A compressed block in the eight to twelve weeks before a June series, built backwards from the paper dates. The emphasis shifts from content to timing, mark-scheme reading and the specific topics a student's own marked papers show as weak. Families who start late use this, and it is honest work provided nobody pretends a grade is being promised.
bullets: Plan built backwards from the school's own exam timetable
Timed sections under exam conditions, marked and returned
Topic list narrowed each week by what the marking shows
No claim about an outcome; the evidence is the deliverable

modes.title: Coursework and controlled-assessment support
modes.description: Where a Dubai school enters a subject with a coursework or practical component, sessions focus on method, structure and the assessment criteria. A tutor reads what the student has already produced and gives feedback on it. The student does the work; that boundary is not negotiable and it is what separates tuition from malpractice.
bullets: Criteria explained in the board's own language before drafting starts
Feedback on the student's own draft, never a substitute for it
Practical method and variable control rehearsed before a write-up
School deadlines, not ours, set the schedule

sections.heading: What an hour of IGCSE online tuition in Dubai actually contains
paragraphs: A session that produces evidence looks different from one that does not, and the difference is visible in the first ten minutes. A good lesson opens with the previous week's marked work on screen and a single question: which of these three errors happened again? That takes four minutes and it sets the agenda. A weaker lesson opens with 'what would you like to look at today?', which transfers the diagnostic job to a fifteen-year-old who does not have the mark scheme.

The middle forty minutes are spent on one topic, not four, and the topic is chosen by the marking rather than by the syllabus order. If a Year 11 lost six marks across two papers on mole ratios, the session is about mole ratios until the next timed question comes back clean. Dubai students are generally well taught and short of nothing but targeted practice; the content has usually been covered in class, and what has not happened is the fifty repetitions of the one calculation that still goes wrong under time pressure.

The last ten minutes produce the artefact. That is either a timed question to be done and submitted before the next lesson, or a short written note listing what changed and what did not. Over a term this accumulates into a document that is far more useful than any report card: it shows which errors stopped recurring and in which week. A parent reading it can tell the difference between a child who is working and a child who is being entertained.

Online delivery is what makes the artefact durable. The paper, the mark scheme and the annotation sit in one shared window, the file is saved rather than carried home, and nothing depends on a folder surviving a school bag. For a family in Dubai Marina or Mirdif, the other gain is simply that the hour is an hour: no twenty-minute buffer each side for a drive down Al Khail Road.
bullets: Opens with last week's marked work, not with an open question
One topic per session, chosen by the marking

sections.heading: The evidence a term of tuition should leave behind
paragraphs: Ask a prospective tutor what you will be able to look at in eight weeks' time. The answer separates the professionals from the pleasant. A tutor who has thought about it will describe specific documents; one who has not will describe a feeling. The table below lists what a Dubai family should expect to accumulate for a single IGCSE subject taken over one academic term, and roughly when each item appears.

None of these artefacts proves a grade will move. That is worth stating plainly, because the market around this query is full of people implying otherwise. What the artefacts do is make the work auditable: if an error pattern identified in week two is still present in week ten, something is wrong with the teaching, the frequency or the student's practice between sessions, and you can see which. That is a far more useful instrument than a monthly reassurance.

The other reason to insist on written evidence is continuity. Dubai's school population turns over constantly, and so does its tutoring market. A student who changes tutor, school or emirate mid-course loses nothing if the error log and the marked papers exist as files. A student whose entire tutoring history lived in one person's memory starts again from scratch, usually in the term when there is least time to spare.

There is a third use for the file, which parents discover at the sixth-form application stage. A head of department deciding whether to admit a student to A Level Chemistry or IB Higher Level Physics is making a judgement about trajectory, and a folder of dated marked papers showing a rising profile across two terms is a far better argument than a parent's account of how hard their child has worked. The same file answers the question a new school asks on transfer. Dubai families move schools more often than most, and the evidence travels.

sections.heading: Marking a past paper properly: the four passes that find the real problem
paragraphs: Most students mark their own work in one pass: right, wrong, move on. That tells them a score and nothing else. A score is the least useful number available, because two candidates on 41 out of 70 can need completely different teaching. The job of marking is to convert a score into a cause, and that takes four passes over the same script.

The first pass is the raw mark, done strictly to the published scheme with no generosity. The second pass labels each lost mark by cause: recall, method, arithmetic, command-term misreading, or time. The third pass groups the labels - if five of eleven lost marks are command-term misreadings, the subject knowledge is not the problem and a term of content revision would have been wasted money. The fourth pass picks exactly one cause to work on and finds three more questions that attack it.

This is where the published mark scheme earns its place in the session. Cambridge and Pearson schemes award method marks explicitly, and a Dubai student who writes only a final answer is discarding marks that were available regardless of whether the answer was right. Reading the scheme out loud, in the student's own script, is often the single intervention that moves a grade. It costs twenty minutes and it is boring, which is why it rarely happens unprompted.

We reference the boards' own published materials and link to them rather than reproducing them. Syllabuses, specimen papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge Assessment International Education and to Pearson, and they are available through cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com. A tutoring service that offers to supply you with a library of those documents is telling you something about how it treats rules in general.

Pass two: label every lost mark by cause
Pass three: group the causes and count them

sections.heading: A twelve-week ledger: what movement looks like in the Dubai Year 11 calendar
paragraphs: Progress in IGCSE is not smooth and it does not arrive in the first fortnight. It tends to appear as a step: three or four weeks of flat marks while an error pattern is being unlearned, then a visible jump when the corrected method survives time pressure. Parents who stop at week four because nothing has happened are usually stopping one week before something does.

The ledger below is a realistic shape for one subject across a twelve-week Dubai term, aligned to the way the emirate's British-curriculum schools run their year: a first half-term of content, a mock window, then the long run at papers. It is not a guarantee of anything. It is the pattern against which a slower or faster trajectory can be read, which is the only legitimate use of a schedule like this.

Two things routinely disrupt it, and both are local. The first is the mock timetable, which in many Dubai schools lands in November and again in late February, and which eats two weeks of tutoring time while producing the single most useful piece of evidence in the whole cycle. The second is Ramadan, which shortens the school day and moves family routines; sessions usually shift to post-Iftar slots and the plan has to absorb that rather than pretend it is not happening.

A third disruption is self-inflicted and worth naming. Families who see a flat week often respond by adding hours, which is the intervention least likely to work. If the error log says the problem is command-term misreading, a second weekly session of the same activity produces more misreading. The correct response to a flat week at the midpoint is to re-read the labels, not to buy more of the thing that is not working. That is the practical value of keeping the ledger at all: it converts an anxious decision into a readable one, and it usually saves money.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: reading the tier decision off the evidence
paragraphs: The tier decision is the most consequential thing a Dubai IGCSE parent will be asked about, and it is routinely made on sentiment. Under Cambridge tiering, Core-tier papers in subjects such as Mathematics and the sciences cap the grade available, while Extended papers reach the top grades but punish a student who is not secure in the underlying method. Pearson Edexcel uses Foundation and Higher for Mathematics in a similar way. A capped grade can close an A Level or IB Higher Level door two years later, which is why schools are usually conservative and parents are usually not.

Evidence resolves this better than argument. The question is not whether the student could cope with Extended content in principle, but what the marked papers show about method security and timing. A candidate who scores respectably on Extended questions when untimed and collapses under time pressure is a different case from one who cannot access the questions at all, and they need opposite decisions.

The table sets out what to look at. It is deliberately not a scoring system - the school holds the entry decision and knows the cohort - but it gives a Dubai parent the vocabulary to have the conversation with a head of department rather than simply accepting or resisting a recommendation. Bring two marked papers and an error log to that meeting and it becomes a different discussion.

One further local point belongs here. Because Dubai schools offer both A Level and IB Diploma routes in volume, the tier decision taken in Year 10 is really a decision about which sixth forms remain open in Year 12. A student planning an IB Diploma with Higher Level sciences needs the extension content and the grade range that only the higher tier provides, and a student heading for a non-science A Level block may genuinely be better served by securing a strong grade at the lower tier than by scraping the higher one. Ask the school for its entry requirement in writing before the tier is fixed.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson deadlines, counted backwards from the exam
paragraphs: Almost every competitor page on this query talks about exams without naming a single date. That is a strange omission, because the dates are the part parents cannot look up quickly and the part that produces real mistakes. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, forecast grades are due before the exam is sat, and a student who needs a retake has to decide long before the results that would tell them whether they need one.

The results dates make the arithmetic concrete, and they are the dates that decide which series is worth entering. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, early enough for a sixth-form place to be confirmed before term. Its November 2025 results, by contrast, reached students on 22 January 2026, after most of those conversations had finished. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 on the same pattern. Cambridge works to the same rhythm: the June series returns grades in August, the November series the following January, and the entry for either closes months before the papers, which is the part families never see coming.

Two cautions belong with that. First, Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong one; a Dubai family should work from the school's own timetable. Second, Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the official page is the reference rather than any date restated on a tutoring site, including this one.

Counted backwards, a Dubai Year 11 aiming at a June series should have a marked diagnostic in the autumn term, a mock-derived topic list by January, and paper-technique work running through March and April. A Year 12 who needs one IGCSE grade lifted for a sixth-form condition should be looking at a November series and should be told, honestly, that the entry deadline for it falls before the summer holiday ends.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing, subject by subject
paragraphs: Across the marked scripts that come out of these sessions, the losses cluster in a small number of places and they are not the places students expect. Very little is lost to genuine ignorance of a topic. Most is lost to four things: working that is not written down, command terms read as if they were synonyms, units and significant figures, and time spent in the wrong part of the paper.

In Mathematics, the single largest recoverable loss is unshown method. Cambridge and Pearson schemes allocate method marks explicitly, and a correct answer with no working can score full marks while a wrong answer with no working scores none - so the student who writes only answers is gambling. In Physics and Chemistry, unit conversion and the practical-method vocabulary of the Alternative to Practical paper are the standing problems; a candidate who writes 'measure the temperature' where the scheme wants the independent variable, the control and the repeat named has not understood what the question is for.

In the essay subjects the pattern inverts. English First Language candidates lose marks by writing well about the wrong thing: the summary question has a content-point tariff, and prose quality cannot substitute for the points. In Business Studies and Economics, the loss is analysis without application - a textbook definition correctly stated about no particular firm. In Geography and History, narrative instead of source interrogation. All of these are structural habits, which is good news, because habits respond to practice much faster than content gaps do.

That is why the marking method in this page's earlier section matters more than the hours booked. A student doing four hours a week of untargeted revision and a student doing ninety minutes a week against a labelled error log are not doing the same activity, and the second one is usually cheaper.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what an IGCSE tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: This matters more than it should, because the market around IGCSE and IB in the Gulf includes businesses that sell completed assessed work. One site in this search landscape openly advertises finished Internal Assessments. Buying one is not a shortcut; it is malpractice, it is detectable, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller.

The boundary is not complicated. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria in the board's own words, rehearse method, ask questions about a draft the student has written, point at where the criteria are not yet met, and set further practice. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, choose and develop an investigation on the student's behalf, or hand over model answers to be submitted. If a tutor cannot explain which side of that line a piece of help falls on, that is the answer.

For Dubai families this also has a practical dimension. Coursework and practical components vary by board and by subject, and schools hold internal deadlines months before the external ones. The useful tutoring intervention is early: criteria read before drafting starts, method rehearsed before a write-up, feedback on the student's own first attempt rather than a rescue in the final week. Rescue work is where the pressure to cross the line comes from.

We also do not distribute board materials. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables are published by Cambridge and Pearson and should be reached through their own sites. Referencing and linking them is legitimate; reproducing them as a download is not, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright one.

sections.heading: KHDA, Dubai's school market and what an inspection report tells a parent
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In the 2024-25 year the sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with UK-curriculum schools accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, US 14 per cent and International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

An inspection report is more useful to a tutoring decision than its headline band. The band - Outstanding down to Very Weak - is a summary, but the subject-level judgements underneath it tell you where a school is strong and where its results rest on a small number of teachers. A school rated highly overall can still have a weak year in one IGCSE science because a department changed hands, and that is precisely the situation in which external subject support earns its keep.

KHDA also sets requirements that sit alongside the licensed international curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Parents are often surprised to find these subjects competing for timetable space with IGCSE options; understanding the rule makes the timetable legible.

None of this means IB Gram holds any standing with KHDA. We are not approved, licensed or endorsed by the authority, we hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and we operate no premises in the UAE. The regulator is named here because knowing how it works helps a Dubai parent read a school report, not because it says anything about us.

sections.heading: Getting started, and the honest answer about availability
paragraphs: The first step is a free trial lesson, and the useful thing to ask of it is not whether your child liked the tutor. Ask what came out of it. A trial that produces a marked question, a named error pattern and a sentence about what the next four sessions would attack has told you something. A trial that produces a friendly conversation and an invoice has not.

Matching takes a syllabus code, a tier, a school and a timetable constraint. With those four things most IGCSE requests from Dubai can be matched within a few working days. Without them, matching is guesswork: 'IGCSE maths help' could mean Core 0580 foundation work for a Year 10 or Edexcel 4MA1 Higher paper technique for a Year 11 six weeks from a series, and no single tutor is the right answer to both.

Availability is not infinite and pretending otherwise is how tutoring goes wrong. Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English and Business Studies are well covered at both tiers. Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics, Computer Science at the top end, and the less commonly entered languages are thinner, and in those cases the honest options are a short wait for the right specialist, a different session pattern, or a recommendation that tuition is not the lever that will help. We would rather say that than fill a slot.

On delivery, to be unambiguous one last time: these are live one-to-one video lessons on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE - home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. What a Dubai family gets instead is a specialist matched to the exact syllabus their child is entered for, a timetable that does not depend on traffic, and a written record of what each hour produced.

process.title: Send the specifics
process.description: School, year group, subject, board and syllabus code if you have it, plus the two time windows that genuinely work on a Dubai school week. The code is on the school report or the exam entry letter, and it narrows the match more than any other single detail.

process.title: Free trial lesson
process.description: A live one-to-one video session with the proposed specialist. It includes a short timed question so there is something to mark, and it ends with a named error pattern and a proposed focus for the first month. No commitment follows automatically from it.

process.title: Baseline marking
process.description: A section of a real past paper, timed, marked strictly to the published scheme, with every lost mark labelled by cause. This is the number everything later is measured against, which is why it is taken before any teaching happens rather than after.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written trail
process.description: One or two fixed slots a week per subject. Every session leaves a dated note; roughly every third session leaves a marked piece of work. The notes accumulate into the file the student revises from in the final term.

process.title: Term review against the evidence
process.description: At the end of each term, the first and most recent marked papers are placed side by side, the error log is compared with its earlier version, and the tier recommendation is restated with the marks attached. If the evidence has not moved, the plan changes rather than the hours increasing.

process.title: Exam-term reset
process.description: Eight to twelve weeks out from the series, the plan is rebuilt backwards from the school's own timetable. Content work stops; timing, mark-scheme reading and the student's specific residual errors take the remaining sessions.

whyPoints.title: The marking is the product
whyPoints.description: Papers are marked to the published Cambridge or Pearson scheme, not to a tutor's impression, and lost marks are labelled by cause rather than counted. That is what makes a flat week interpretable instead of merely disappointing.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus, not the map
whyPoints.description: Because sessions run over video, the specialist is chosen for the board, tier and subject your child is actually entered for. A family in Mirdif gets the same access to an Additional Mathematics teacher as a family in Jumeirah.

whyPoints.title: A written record you can audit
whyPoints.description: Dated session notes and marked scripts accumulate as files. If a tutor, a school or an emirate changes mid-course, the history survives, which is unusually valuable in a city with Dubai's rate of school transfer.

whyPoints.title: Straight answers about limits
whyPoints.description: Some subjects are thinly covered and some problems are not tutoring problems. You will be told which, before you book, including when the honest recommendation is to spend the money elsewhere.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no invented satisfaction percentages, no self-awarded star ratings, and no suggestion of approval by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson. Market rates on this page are attributed to the sources that published them.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Dubai week
whyPoints.description: Session timing assumes a 7:20am school start, a long commute home in several communities, Friday as part of the weekend and a shortened school day during Ramadan. Plans absorb those rather than ignoring them.

faqs.question: How does a live online IGCSE lesson for a Dubai Year 11 student actually run from start to finish?
faqs.answer: It opens with last week's marked work on screen and one question: which of these errors happened again? That takes about four minutes. The middle of the hour is spent on a single topic chosen by the marking rather than by syllabus order, with the paper, the mark scheme and the annotation all visible in the same shared window. The last ten minutes produce something that exists afterwards - a timed question to submit before the next session, or a dated note listing what changed. Everything is saved, so the record survives the school bag and the term.

faqs.question: What should I be able to see after four weeks before I decide whether to continue?
faqs.answer: Four specific items. A marked diagnostic from week one with lost marks labelled by cause. An error log grouped by cause rather than by question number. Three or four dated session notes showing what was taught and what was set. And at least one piece of timed work attacking the largest error pattern. What you should not expect at four weeks is a visible grade jump: unlearning a method takes longer than learning one, and flat marks at week four are normal. Flat marks with no error log, however, mean the work is not being diagnosed at all.

faqs.question: Which syllabus codes should I check on my child's Dubai school report before booking anything?
faqs.answer: The four-digit Cambridge codes or the alphanumeric Pearson ones: 0580 or 4MA1 for Mathematics, 0625 or 4PH1 for Physics, 0620 or 4CH1 for Chemistry, 0610 or 4BI1 for Biology, 0500 or 0510 for English. They appear on the report, the options form or the exam entry letter. They matter because the papers, the tiering and the retake calendar differ between boards, and because many Dubai schools mix boards by subject - Cambridge sciences with an Edexcel maths entry is a common combination. A tutor who does not ask for the code is not planning around the paper your child will sit.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor mark a full past paper to the published mark scheme rather than just checking answers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the part of the work that matters most. Marking strictly to the scheme reveals method marks the student discarded by writing only final answers, which is the single largest recoverable loss in Mathematics and the quantitative sciences. The marking should then label each lost mark by cause - recall, method, arithmetic, command-term misreading or time - and group those labels, because five command-term errors out of eleven lost marks points at a different term of work than five recall errors. We link the official Cambridge and Pearson materials rather than redistributing them.

faqs.question: What does the Dubai market charge per hour for one-to-one IGCSE support online in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published market rates vary by tier. Budget online tutors and university students advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit broadly in the AED 150-300 band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors run around AED 200-450 and above, and premium named tutors are advertised higher still. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours. For IB Gram's own arrangement, start with the free trial lesson and a consultation.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a villa or apartment anywhere in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation to apologise for: it removes a 30 to 50 minute drive from both sides of the session, it lets us match a family in Mirdif or Al Furjan to a subject specialist who would never have been within reach, and it means the paper, the mark scheme and the annotation stay in one saved file rather than on a sheet that disappears by Thursday.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge final entries close relative to the exam my child will actually sit?
faqs.answer: Months earlier, which catches families out every year. The exam your child will actually sit is the June series or the November series, because Cambridge offers its February and March series to India only. For June, final entries close in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, and the forecast grade is submitted before the series opens; the exact dates sit on your centre's statement of entry. The November series runs through October and November with the same long lead time on its entry. Pearson's International GCSE series run in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Work from your school's own timetable, since Cambridge allocates centres to six zones.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education count towards equivalency, and at what grade?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published rule says. Equivalency is a Ministry process - verify your own case through the Ministry rather than through any tutoring service, including this one.

faqs.question: My child wants to move from Core to Extended Maths halfway through Year 10 - is that realistic?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the evidence decides it rather than enthusiasm. Look at two things in marked work. First, whether the student can access Extended questions at all when untimed, even for low marks - that tests reach. Second, how far the mark falls when the same questions are timed; a drop of more than roughly a fifth usually means method is not yet automatic. Bring two marked papers and an error log to the head of department, because the school holds the entry decision. The reason it matters is the grade ceiling: a Core-tier maths grade can close A Level and IB Higher Level doors two years later.

faqs.question: How is an IGCSE science practical assessed if my child only ever studies online?
faqs.answer: Most Dubai candidates sit the Alternative to Practical paper rather than a live practical, which tests experimental method on paper: identifying the independent and dependent variables, naming controls, reading instruments, spotting anomalous results and describing improvements. That paper is entirely teachable over video, and it is where a large share of science marks is lost, because the vocabulary it rewards is rarely taught explicitly. Where a school enters a component requiring practical work, that work happens at school under the school's supervision and the tutoring focus is method rehearsal and the write-up criteria beforehand.

faqs.question: What exactly may an IGCSE tutor do with a piece of assessed work my child has drafted?
faqs.answer: A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, ask questions about what the student has written, point out where a criterion is not yet met, rehearse method, and set further practice. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final form, choose and develop an investigation on the student's behalf, or hand over model answers to be submitted. One site in this search landscape sells finished Internal Assessments; that is malpractice and the consequence lands on the student. If a tutor cannot say which side of the line a request falls on, that is your answer.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with Dubai families need a permit from MoHRE?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system under the service 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount you see quoted is unverified.

faqs.question: Can online IGCSE sessions move to post-Iftar timings during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they usually should. Dubai schools run a shortened day during Ramadan, family routines shift and a 5pm session that worked in January is often the worst possible slot in March. The practical pattern is to move sessions to a post-Iftar window, reduce them slightly in length, and accept that the fortnight either side of Eid is for consolidation rather than new content. Because the lesson is delivered over video, moving the slot costs nothing - there is no drive to re-plan around - and the plan simply absorbs the change rather than pretending the calendar is the same all year.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for a niche IGCSE subject my child takes in Dubai?
faqs.answer: You get told. Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English, Business Studies and Economics are well covered at both tiers. Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics, Computer Science at the top end and the less commonly entered languages are thinner. In those cases the options are a short wait for the right specialist, a different session pattern such as fortnightly work with heavier independent practice, or a straight recommendation that tuition is not the lever that will help. Filling a slot with a tutor who does not know the specification wastes a term, and a term is what a Year 11 does not have.

faqs.question: How do I tell the difference between a tutor who knows the Cambridge specification and one who only knows the subject?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions before you book. Which syllabus code does my child's school enter, and what are the papers worth? Where do candidates lose marks on the paper my child is sitting, specifically? What will I be able to look at in eight weeks? A specification-literate tutor answers the first in a sentence, the second with a list of named topics and command-term traps, and the third with documents rather than feelings. Someone who knows the subject but not the paper will answer all three in general terms, and general terms are what cost marks.

dubai/igcse-online-tuition.closingHeading: Start with a marked paper, not a promise
dubai/igcse-online-tuition.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the question you ask any prospective tutor: what will I be able to look at in eight weeks? IGCSE online tuition in Dubai is worth paying for when it produces marked papers, a labelled error log and a dated record of what changed, and it is worth very little when it produces reassurance. Book the free trial lesson, bring the syllabus code and the tier, and judge the hour by what came out of it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around your child's school week.

dubai/igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: Every tutor below works the same way round: mark first, teach second. The first deliverable is a script annotated against the board's published mark scheme with the lost marks itemised by question, which is the document the whole block is then measured against. You keep it whether or not you continue.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE online tutor in Dubai should be able to show you
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements in Dubai are judged on feeling. The student says the sessions are helpful, the tutor says progress is good, and three months later a mock arrives and nobody can say whether the money did anything. The alternative is not more reporting; it is a small number of concrete artefacts that exist whether or not anyone feels good. An annotated script. A table of marks by paper section. A fortnightly note naming what moved. Those three documents answer the question a parent is actually asking, and they are the whole structure of this page.

The sequence matters as much as the artefacts. Teaching before marking is the default in this market and it is the wrong way round, because a tutor who has not seen a marked script is guessing at where the marks went. So the first ninety minutes of any arrangement here are spent on evidence rather than instruction: a recent paper is sat or supplied, marked question by question against the board's own published scheme, and the lost marks are sorted into categories — method not shown, command term misread, content absent, arithmetic slip, time ran out. That sort is the plan. Everything after it follows the marks.

What the evidence then looks like week by week is deliberately unglamorous. Each session opens by marking the timed set from the previous week, which produces a number. Each fortnight the section-mark table is updated, which produces a trend. At week six the student sits a full paper under timed conditions, which produces a comparison against the baseline. At week twelve there is a second full paper and a written summary of which sections moved, which did not, and what is left. Six written notes, two full marked papers, one section-mark table maintained throughout. That is the deliverable.

There are things this page deliberately does not claim, and the omissions are the point. No percentage of students improving, because publishing a statistic requires the sample size, the date and the method on the same page and we are not going to invent them. No grade promises, because no tutor can make one honestly and a promise with refund conditions attached is usually a promise engineered to be unreachable. No satisfaction score. No star rating. Several pages ranking for these searches publish review figures that contradict each other within the same page, and one publishes markup for questions that do not appear on the page at all.

On delivery, plainly, before you read further: tuition for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school week. Screens are shared both ways so a student's working is visible as it is written, scripts are annotated live and saved, and both parties keep the file. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For evidence-led work that is an advantage rather than a compromise, because every artefact the block produces is digital, dated and in one place rather than scattered across a notebook somebody left at school.
