intro.heading: Pricing IGCSE physics support topic by topic in Dubai
paragraphs: Physics marks do not leak evenly across the syllabus. In almost every marked paper we see from Dubai schools, the same handful of topics accounts for most of the loss, and the same three habits account for most of the rest. That makes the subject unusually easy to price honestly: a family is buying three or four topic repairs and a technique fix, not a term of general physics lessons, and the difference in cost is substantial.

The published Dubai rate bands supply the arithmetic. At the floor, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase quoting AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and market home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above.

Applied topic by topic, those numbers produce small, bounded purchases. Electricity, the topic Dubai students name most often, usually takes three or four sessions to put right if the underlying algebra is sound. Moments and equilibrium take two. Waves and refraction take three. Thermal physics takes two. A student with four problem topics is looking at ten to twelve sessions, not a year, and knowing that in advance protects a family from an open-ended arrangement.

Two administrative facts have to be established first, and most families do not have them to hand. The first is the syllabus: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 are different specifications with different paper structures. The second is which practical route the school has entered the student for, because Cambridge offers a practical test and an alternative-to-practical paper and they require genuinely different preparation.

Dubai's examination pattern matters too, and it is simpler than families fear. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. A student who needs more time than the summer allows has a real second route, which changes how a late diagnosis should be handled.

Delivery is stated once. Physics support for Dubai families runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school day. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Circuit diagrams, ray diagrams and graph work are all drawn and annotated on a shared screen, which keeps the working as revision material afterwards.

dubai/igcse-physics-tutor.programmesIntro: IGCSE Physics sits in a longer route through a Dubai school, and what is worth buying differs sharply by stage because the content is cumulative and the habits form early.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the course begins
programmes.description: The years where the mathematics physics depends on is either secured or not: rearranging formulae, standard form, units and prefixes, reading a gradient from a graph. None of that is physics, and all of it determines whether a student can access physics marks. A student who cannot confidently rearrange an equation will lose physics marks for two years.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families usually first consider physics help in Year 10, which is a term or two later than the useful moment. The cheapest intervention in this subject is three or four sessions in Year 9 on equation rearrangement, standard form and unit conversion, which costs little at the lower published bands and removes a recurring deduction from every subsequent paper.

programmes.name: Year 10, the content year
programmes.description: Most Dubai schools deliver the bulk of the syllabus in Year 10: general physics, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, atomic physics. Topics met once and not revisited become the Year 11 gaps. Practical work happens here too, which is where the skills tested by both practical routes are built, whether or not the student notices.
programmes.countryNote: The most useful thing a Dubai family can do in Year 10 is keep the returned topic tests. Schools assess as they teach, and a sequence of topic tests is a precise map of which topics are weak, available free, months before any mock. Families who bring that sequence to a first session get a plan in twenty minutes rather than two sessions.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: Revision, mocks and the series. Content has been taught at least once, so the work is diagnosis, topic repair and technique. This is also when the practical route becomes concrete: students entered for the practical test need laboratory technique and those entered for the alternative paper need to interpret other people's experiments on paper, which are different skills.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mock windows run from roughly late November to February depending on the school. A marked physics mock is the single most useful document in the two years, because it shows topic losses and habit losses separately. Acting on it in January leaves months; waiting until the spring term converts a topic repair job into triage.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level and IB Diploma physics
programmes.description: The IGCSE physics grade and tier decide whether A Level Physics or IB Physics at Higher Level is realistic. Both assume fluency with the algebra and graph work that IGCSE introduces, and both move quickly past it. A student who scraped through IGCSE physics by memorising will find the first term of either course difficult in a way that is avoidable.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai offers A Levels, the IB Diploma and American pathways within a small radius, and the physics entry requirement differs between them. Identifying the likely post-16 route during Year 10 and working backwards to the tier and grade needed is better planning than choosing a route after results, when the options have already narrowed.

dubai/igcse-physics-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics requests from Dubai families usually arrive with a maths or chemistry request attached, because the weaknesses are connected. These are the subjects most often bundled with an IGCSE physics enquiry.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Multiple choice and theory papers plus a practical route, covering motion and forces, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, and atomic physics. Marks are lost on equation rearrangement, units, unlabelled diagrams and extended answers that describe without explaining.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two written papers with practical skills assessed within them rather than in a separate practical examination. Content overlaps heavily with Cambridge but question style and the treatment of practical work differ enough that past papers should match the specification.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The subject underneath physics. Rearrangement, standard form, ratio, gradients and significant figures are maths skills tested in physics papers, and a student losing marks in both usually has one problem rather than two.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the quantitative discipline and the practical skills. Moles and concentration are proportional reasoning problems, and students who are weak on ratio lose marks in both sciences for the same underlying reason.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The third science in a triple-award timetable, lighter on calculation but still requiring graph interpretation, rate work and careful unit handling. Students taking all three sciences have a heavy practical load to coordinate.

subjects.name: Combined or Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: The route many Dubai students take instead of three separate sciences, with reduced content across all three disciplines. The physics content is a subset of 0625, so past-paper practice has to come from the right syllabus rather than the separate-science one.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger candidates and genuinely useful for physics, since the algebraic fluency it builds removes most of the rearrangement difficulty. It is also a substantial extra load in an examination year.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Shares logic and data representation with the electronics parts of physics. Students comfortable with binary and logic gates find the digital electronics content straightforward where others treat it as a separate subject.

subjects.name: Design and Technology
subjects.description: Overlaps with forces, materials and structures, and builds the habit of recording a method precisely. That habit transfers directly to the practical and alternative-to-practical routes in physics.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: An unexpected but real overlap in graph and data interpretation under examination conditions. Students who read graphs confidently in geography usually lose fewer marks on the physics graph questions, which carry a predictable share of the paper.

dubai/igcse-physics-tutor.modesIntro: Physics support is worth buying in one of three shapes, and the right one depends on which of the three kinds of loss a marked paper shows. All run over live video on Gulf Standard Time rather than at a Dubai address.

modes.title: Topic repair blocks
modes.description: Two to four sessions per problem topic, with the topic rebuilt from the underlying idea rather than patched with worked examples. Each block ends with a timed past-paper question from the correct specification, marked properly. The topic list is the plan and crossing items off it is the progress record.

Each block closes with a timed question from the right syllabus

modes.title: Technique and calculation discipline
modes.description: Short work on the three habits that cost marks regardless of topic: rearranging before substituting, carrying units through a calculation, and writing extended answers that explain rather than describe. Unglamorous, quick, and worth more across a whole paper than any single topic repair.
bullets: Rearrange, then substitute; never the other way round
Units carried through every line and stated in the answer
Significant figures and prefixes handled consistently
Extended answers practised against the command term

modes.title: Practical paper preparation, by route
modes.description: Separate preparation for the practical test and the alternative-to-practical paper, because they test different things. The practical test needs laboratory technique and real measurement discipline; the alternative paper needs the ability to read somebody else's experiment, spot the control variable and criticise a method on paper.
bullets: Route confirmed with the school before preparation begins
Alternative-to-practical worked through past papers specifically

sections.heading: The six topics that account for most lost physics marks, priced
paragraphs: Marked physics papers from Dubai schools show a consistent pattern. A small number of topics absorb most of the loss, and they are the same topics year after year, for structural reasons rather than because students are careless. Each one is taught once, each one depends on something taught earlier, and each one appears reliably in the papers.

Electricity leads the list, and it is the topic students name when asked. The difficulty is rarely the physics: it is that circuit questions require tracking several quantities through a system, which exposes any weakness in rearranging equations or in handling series and parallel relationships. Three or four sessions usually settles it, and the sessions are mostly algebra wearing a physics costume.

Moments and equilibrium is the second, and the cheapest to fix. Students who can take moments about a sensible point reliably gain the marks; students who cannot lose all of them in a question type that recurs. Two sessions is normal. Waves and refraction is the third, where ray diagrams and the geometry of refraction cause the trouble, and three sessions is typical. Thermal physics is the fourth, with specific heat capacity and latent heat questions being calculation discipline more than conceptual difficulty.

Pressure and density is the fifth, usually failing on unit conversion rather than on the physics, and atomic physics is the sixth, where half-life questions and nuclear equations are mechanical once the convention is clear. The table below puts session counts and AED totals against each one. None of the figures is an IB Gram price; the bands are the market's own published rates and the totals are arithmetic.

sections.heading: Paper 5 practical or Paper 6 alternative to practical: which is your child sitting?
paragraphs: This is the question Dubai parents ask most often about physics and get the least clear answer to. Cambridge offers two routes for the practical element: a practical test sat in a laboratory, and an alternative-to-practical written paper that examines practical understanding on paper. The school chooses, and candidates prepare very differently depending on the choice. Pearson's International GCSE Physics assesses practical skills within the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination.

The practical test requires laboratory technique: setting up apparatus, taking readings carefully, recording in a sensible table, spotting an anomalous result and knowing what to do about it. Preparation means doing experiments, which a tutor cannot replicate remotely and should not pretend to. What a tutor can do is drill the surrounding skills: table design, significant figures, plotting, drawing a line of best fit, and calculating a gradient with units.

The alternative-to-practical paper is a different animal and, for a tutor, a much more tractable one. It presents somebody else's experiment and asks the candidate to identify variables, criticise a method, read a scale, complete a table, plot and interpret. All of that is a written skill, examinable from past papers, and improvable in three or four sessions. Students entered for this route who spend their revision doing experiments are preparing for the wrong paper.

The practical consequence is a single question to the school: which practical paper is my child entered for? Families who do not ask often assume the laboratory route because it sounds more like physics, and then meet an alternative-to-practical paper full of method criticism they have never practised. Confirm the current paper structure and codes with the school and with the awarding body's own syllabus page rather than from summaries.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1: what actually differs
paragraphs: Two specifications dominate IGCSE physics entries in Dubai and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 is used widely across the emirate's Cambridge schools. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 is the main alternative. The content overlap is large, which lulls families into treating past papers as interchangeable, and the question style, mark allocation and practical treatment are different enough that they are not.

The structural differences matter most for revision planning. Cambridge separates the practical element into its own paper, either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, while Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Cambridge tiers into Core and Extended with supplement content examined only at Extended; a Core candidate revising Extended material is wasting time, and an Extended candidate revising only Core material is missing examinable content.

There are also Combined or Co-ordinated Sciences routes, where physics is a reduced subset taken alongside chemistry and biology in a single award. Students on those routes need past papers from the combined syllabus, not from separate-science 0625, because the content boundary differs and questions on excluded material are a waste of revision time.

The screening question for any tutor is therefore specific: which syllabus code and tier is my child entered for, and which practical paper? A tutor who answers in general terms about physics is working from assumptions. Confirm the live specification with the school and link to the awarding body's own page; no tutoring service should be distributing syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes itself, since those belong to the awarding body and the correct behaviour is to point at the official source.

sections.heading: Equations: which are given, which are not, and the rearrangement problem
paragraphs: A large share of physics marks turns on equation handling, and most of the loss has nothing to do with physics. Some equations are supplied in the examination and some must be recalled, and the boundary differs between specifications. A student who does not know which is which either wastes memorisation effort or arrives at a question unable to start.

The deeper problem is rearrangement. Students substitute numbers first and then try to rearrange an expression containing them, which multiplies the chances of an error and makes any mistake invisible. The habit worth installing is rearranging symbolically first, checking the rearrangement against units, and substituting last. It takes about two sessions to install and it reduces errors across every calculation topic simultaneously.

Units are the companion problem. Prefixes are the usual culprit: kilo, milli, micro and nano appear constantly, and a student who converts inconsistently produces answers that are correct by a factor of a thousand, which earns nothing. Carrying units through each line of working catches that automatically, which is the practical reason for insisting on it rather than treating it as neatness.

Significant figures and the instruction to give an answer to a stated accuracy complete the set. Questions that specify two significant figures are awarding a mark for following the instruction, and students routinely give four. These are the cheapest marks on any physics paper and the ones most often left behind, which is why a technique block is usually better value than a fifth topic repair.
bullets: Know which equations are supplied and which must be recalled
Rearrange symbolically first, substitute numbers last
Check a rearrangement against units before using it

Two sessions on these habits affects every calculation topic at once

sections.heading: Electricity, the topic Dubai students name most often
paragraphs: Ask a Dubai IGCSE physics candidate which topic they find hardest and electricity is the usual answer. It is worth unpacking why, because the honest diagnosis changes what the sessions should contain. Electricity is not conceptually harder than waves or thermal physics. What makes it feel harder is that a circuit question requires holding several related quantities in mind at once and moving between them.

In a series and parallel problem a candidate has to track current, potential difference and resistance across multiple components, deciding at each step which relationship applies. A student with secure algebra does this comfortably. A student whose algebra is shaky loses the thread halfway through, and the symptom presents as not understanding electricity when the cause is not being fluent with rearrangement and ratio.

The second genuine difficulty is representational. Circuit diagrams use conventions that have to be read accurately, and students who cannot reliably tell a series branch from a parallel one in an unfamiliar drawing are guessing. Practising reading circuits, redrawing them in a standard form, and identifying what is in series with what, is a visual skill that improves quickly with repetition on a shared screen.

What this means for a Dubai family's purchase is encouraging. Three or four sessions on electricity, with the first one spent confirming whether the problem is algebra or conventions, usually resolves it. Buying twenty sessions of general physics because electricity is hard is the expensive route to the same destination, and it is the arrangement most of this market will sell you.

sections.heading: The UAE exam series and what a late diagnosis can still do
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, which means a UAE candidate sits June or November and any advice referring to a February entry deadline is advice for a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

The November series is the fact that changes the economics of a late diagnosis. A Dubai student whose January mock comes back well below target has two options rather than one: compress the work into the months before the summer series, or plan properly for November with an extra five months. The second is often the better outcome and it is almost never mentioned by providers selling compressed revision programmes.

Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, which is the administrative fact that surprises families. For a sense of the cycle, Pearson's November International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026 in the current series, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Those dated examples are what make the pattern checkable rather than asserted.

One warning that specifically affects UAE candidates. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Revise from the timetable your school issued, and check the awarding body's live timetable page rather than a restated version.

sections.heading: Online physics tuition against the in-home market in Dubai
paragraphs: Physics involves drawing, and families reasonably ask whether that works over video. It does, better than the alternative in most respects, because a shared screen that both parties can draw on leaves the circuit diagram, the ray diagram and the graph in a file that can be reopened. The same work in an exercise book is somewhere in the house by revision season.

The in-home premium in Dubai is quantifiable. Bestimate puts home visits at AED 180 to 350 and market home tutors at AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Advertised monthly packages run AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. For topic repair work, eight shorter contacts across a month suit the subject better than four long ones, because each topic should finish with a timed question and a gap before the next one.

There is a specification argument too. Two awarding bodies, two tiers and two practical routes produce eight combinations, and the right tutor is one who knows your child's. Within a twenty-minute drive of a given Dubai community, the set of physics tutors who match that exact combination may be small. Over video the constraint disappears, which matters most for the alternative-to-practical paper, where specific past-paper familiarity does the work.

The honest case for presence remains for younger students who need supervision as much as teaching, and for practical technique, which no remote session replaces. Laboratory skill is built at school, in the laboratory, and a tutor who claims otherwise is overselling. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case; that service is part of our India offering only, and physics support here runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

sections.heading: What a Dubai family should ask before paying for physics help
paragraphs: The screening questions for this subject are short and they eliminate most of the field. Which syllabus code and tier is my child entered for. Which practical paper. Which three topics does the marked paper show as weakest. What would the first four sessions cover, specifically. A tutor who answers all four without hedging is worth booking; one who talks about physics in general is guessing.

The fifth question is about the permit. Any individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and warns that tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

There is a related point about school teachers specifically. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document, but the direction is clear and no family should be arranging tutoring with their own child's class teacher.

Finally, be sceptical of outcome claims. Nobody can guarantee a physics grade, and figures about percentages of students improving are meaningless without the number of students, the date and the method behind them. What a provider can honestly offer is a named topic list, a session estimate, a marked re-test, and a straight answer when the plan is not working.

process.title: Get three facts from the school
process.description: The syllabus code, the tier, and which practical paper your child is entered for. All three in writing. Revision shape depends on them and no tutor can supply them, which is why a tutor who does not ask is working from assumptions.

process.title: Send the marked papers and topic tests
process.description: A mock is ideal and a sequence of returned Year 10 topic tests is almost as good. Together they separate topic losses from habit losses, which is the distinction the whole plan rests on.

process.title: Agree a topic list and a habit list
process.description: Three or four named topics and the technique habits visible on the script. Both lists are short and both can be crossed off. An agreement to improve at physics in general cannot be checked by anyone.

process.title: Run short sessions over live video
process.description: Two shorter slots a week beat one long block for topic repair, because each topic should end with a timed question and a gap before the next. Sessions sit around the Dubai school day, mandatory subject lessons, sport and prayer times.

process.title: Re-test from the correct specification
process.description: Every few weeks, a timed past-paper question set from the right syllabus, marked properly. The lists shrink or they do not. If they do not after three re-tests, the plan changes rather than continuing by default.

whyPoints.title: Priced topic by topic
whyPoints.description: Six topics account for most lost marks, and each is priced with a session count and a modelled AED total at published market bands. A family can see that four problem topics is ten to twelve sessions rather than a year of lessons.

whyPoints.title: The practical route named explicitly
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's practical test and alternative-to-practical paper need different preparation, and Pearson assesses practical skill inside the written papers. Students entered for the alternative paper who spend revision doing experiments are preparing for the wrong examination.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes stated
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 differ in structure and question style, and Combined Sciences routes differ again. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole researched competitor cluster, which is how families end up with the wrong past papers.

whyPoints.title: Technique treated as the best value
whyPoints.description: Rearranging before substituting, carrying units, respecting stated accuracy. Two sessions on those habits affects every calculation topic simultaneously, which usually beats a fifth topic repair for the same money.

whyPoints.title: The November series named
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November, and the February and March Cambridge series is India-only. A late diagnosis has a genuine second route, and compressed revision programmes sold without mentioning it are incomplete advice.

whyPoints.title: No outcome claims
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees and no percentages about other students, because such figures mean nothing without the sample size, date and method. What is offered instead is a named list, an estimate, a marked re-test and a straight answer.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a practical exam for IGCSE Physics in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the school entered them for. Cambridge offers two routes: a practical test sat in a laboratory, and an alternative-to-practical written paper that examines practical understanding on paper. Pearson's International GCSE Physics assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead of through a separate practical examination. The two Cambridge routes need genuinely different preparation, so ask the school which paper appears on the entry. Families who assume the laboratory route and meet an alternative-to-practical paper full of method criticism are badly caught out.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to fix IGCSE physics electricity?
faqs.answer: Usually three or four, and the first should establish whether the problem is actually electricity. Circuit questions require tracking current, potential difference and resistance across several components, which exposes weak algebra rather than weak physics. A student whose rearrangement is shaky loses the thread halfway through and reports not understanding electricity. The other common cause is representational: being unable to tell reliably what is in series with what in an unfamiliar diagram, which improves quickly with practice redrawing circuits in standard form.

faqs.question: Which physics syllabus does my child's Dubai school use?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because it changes the revision material. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 are both widely used in the emirate, and Combined or Co-ordinated Sciences routes exist as well with a reduced physics subset. The content overlap is large enough to lull families into treating past papers as interchangeable, and the question style, mark allocations and practical treatment differ enough that they are not. Get the code and the tier in writing.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose physics marks after getting the physics right?
faqs.answer: Three habits account for most of it. Substituting numbers before rearranging, which multiplies errors and hides them. Inconsistent prefix conversion between kilo, milli, micro and nano, producing answers wrong by a factor of a thousand. And ignoring an instruction to give an answer to a stated accuracy, which is a mark awarded for following the instruction. Carrying units through every line of working catches the second automatically. Two sessions on these habits improves every calculation topic at once.

faqs.question: Does anyone come to our home in Dubai for physics lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Physics support for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with circuit diagrams, ray diagrams and graphs drawn on a shared screen and saved as files that are still available during revision. The in-home market here is real and quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with the tutor's travel inside the rate.

faqs.question: Can a tutor prepare my child for the practical test?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it is important to be straight about the limit. Laboratory technique, meaning setting up apparatus, taking careful readings and handling equipment, is built at school in the laboratory and no remote session replaces it. What a tutor can do is drill everything around it: designing a results table, significant figures, plotting, drawing a line of best fit, calculating a gradient with units, identifying an anomalous result and knowing what to do about it. Those carry a substantial share of the marks.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended in Cambridge physics?
faqs.answer: Extended covers the full syllabus including supplement content and carries the upper grade range; Core covers reduced content and is capped below the top grades. The practical consequence for revision is specific: a Core candidate working through Extended material is wasting time on content they will not be examined on, and an Extended candidate revising only Core material is leaving examinable topics untouched. The tier sits with the school, which has evidence from two years of assessment, and any conversation about it belongs in Year 10.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit IGCSE physics exams?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any guidance referring to a February entry deadline is written for a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that candidates must use the correct zone timetable, so always work from the version the school issued.

faqs.question: Is it worth waiting for the November series if the mock was poor?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and it is rarely offered as an option. A student whose January mock sits well below target can either compress the work into the months before the summer series or plan properly for November with roughly five extra months. The second frequently produces the better grade. The decision belongs with the school because it affects entries and post-16 applications, but it exists, and a provider selling a compressed revision programme without mentioning it is giving incomplete advice.

faqs.question: Could weak IGCSE maths be what is costing my child physics marks?
faqs.answer: Frequently. Rearranging formulae, standard form, ratio, gradients and significant figures are mathematics skills assessed inside a physics paper, and a student losing marks in both subjects usually has one underlying weakness rather than two. The tell is a marked script where the physics reasoning is sound and the arithmetic or the algebra breaks down. Fixing that in a few sessions aimed at the mathematics is cheaper and more effective than hiring separate tutors for physics, chemistry and maths to work around the same gap.

faqs.question: What does physics tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above on Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase quotes AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. At the floor, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Those are the providers' published figures, read in October 2026.

faqs.question: How early should physics support start?
faqs.answer: Year 9 is the best value, which surprises families. The IGCSE course assumes fluency with rearranging equations, standard form, units and prefixes and reading gradients from graphs, none of which is physics and all of which determines whether physics marks are accessible. Three or four sessions on those in Year 9, which sit comfortably at the lower published rate bands, remove a recurring deduction from every paper for the following two years. Year 10 is still good; the spring of Year 11 is triage.

faqs.question: Is it allowed for an IGCSE physics teacher to tutor their own class privately?
faqs.answer: That should be avoided, and in Abu Dhabi it is explicitly restricted. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document, but the direction is unambiguous and no family should be arranging private lessons with their own child's class teacher.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE physics tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system, and warns that tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties.

faqs.question: What if no physics tutor matches our specification and practical route?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of substituting quietly. Two awarding bodies, two tiers and two practical routes produce several combinations, and a specific match on the alternative-to-practical paper in the weeks after mock results can be narrower than families expect. The options are a start date in the future, a tutor who covers the content but not that exact route for interim topic repair, or a recommendation to wait until demand eases. Families should be told which of those is on offer.

dubai/igcse-physics-tutor.closingHeading: Three facts from the school, then a short topic list
dubai/igcse-physics-tutor.closingBody: Ask the school for the syllabus code, the tier and the practical paper, then send whatever marked physics work you have, including Year 10 topic tests. The free trial session turns that into two short lists: three or four topics to repair and the technique habits visible on the script. Both lists can be crossed off and checked, which is why we would rather sell ten sessions that finish than a year that does not. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are not part of our UAE service.

dubai/igcse-private-candidate-registrati.tutorsIntro: The tutors matched here teach IGCSE subjects to students sitting as private candidates, which is a different brief from school teaching: no coursework support from a department, no in-school practical, and a syllabus to cover alone in a defined number of weeks.

intro.heading: What a private candidate is actually paying for
paragraphs: A private candidate is a student who sits IGCSE examinations without being enrolled at the school that hosts them. In Dubai this comes up in four situations: a homeschooled student, a student who wants one extra subject their school does not offer, a student resitting a subject after leaving school, and a student whose family moved mid-cycle and whose new school will not enter them. Each of those has the same administrative shape and the same cost structure, and the cost structure is where families get caught out.

The money breaks into three parts. First, the examination entry fee, which the board sets per subject per series and the centre passes on. Second, the centre's own administration or registration fee, which is the centre's commercial decision and varies substantially between providers in Dubai. Third, any component surcharge — a practical examination, a speaking test, or a coursework alternative paper — which can turn a cheap subject into an expensive one. A family budgeting for 'five IGCSEs' using one figure multiplied by five will be wrong.

The second surprise is availability. Not every IGCSE subject is open to a private candidate, and the reason is structural rather than arbitrary. Subjects assessed partly through coursework marked by a school teacher cannot be entered privately in the normal way, because there is no teacher to mark it. Boards generally provide an alternative route — an additional written paper in place of coursework, or a practical examination in place of a teacher-assessed practical — but not for every subject and not in every series. The subject list a private candidate can realistically take is shorter than the published syllabus catalogue.

Third, the calendar. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and the February/March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai private candidate sits June or November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and private-candidate entries often close earlier at a given centre than school entries do, because the centre has to administer them. Late entry, where a centre allows it at all, carries a higher fee.

Fourth, logistics that only private candidates have to think about. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. A private candidate has no school checking that for them. The same applies to identification requirements, arrival times and what may be brought into the room.

IB Gram's role here is teaching, and it is worth being precise about the boundary. We are not an examination centre, we hold no board approval or accreditation, and we cannot register a candidate, host an examination or influence a centre's decision. We teach the syllabus, one-to-one, live over video on Gulf Standard Time, and we can explain the process set out on this page. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service.

dubai/igcse-private-candidate-registrati.programmesIntro: Private-candidate entry is an IGCSE and A Level phenomenon rather than an IB one, for a structural reason worth understanding before a family chooses a route.

programmes.name: International General Certificate of Secondary Education
programmes.description: Single-subject qualifications taken individually, which is exactly what makes private entry possible. Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers in many subjects, with Core capped at grade C or 5 and Extended reaching A* or 9. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is ungraded by tier in most subjects and assessed entirely by written examination in several, which can make it the easier board for a private candidate.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, IGCSE is the dominant pre-16 qualification among British-curriculum schools and the one most private candidates sit. The board a family chooses matters more than usual here: a subject with no coursework requirement is straightforward to enter privately, and one with a teacher-assessed component is not. Check the specific syllabus code, not the subject name.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Taken after IGCSE, in subjects at Advanced Subsidiary or full Advanced Level, and entered per subject in the same way. Practical sciences carry an examined practical component, which private candidates can usually sit at an approved centre but which needs confirming subject by subject and series by series before any teaching is planned.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant to Dubai private candidates for a specific reason: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five GCSE or IGCSE passes. A private candidate assembling a certificate portfolio needs to know that before choosing which subjects to sit.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the Creativity, Activity, Service strand, with each subject carrying internal assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The programme is assessed as a whole rather than subject by subject.
programmes.countryNote: The IB Diploma is not a private-candidate route in the way IGCSE is. It requires registration through an IB World School and carries internally assessed components in every subject, which means a school and a teacher of record. Families who want a flexible, subject-by-subject route to university entry are usually looking at IGCSE and A Level rather than the Diploma, and that is a real structural difference rather than a preference.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four lettered criteria per subject by the school, ending in the Grade 10 Personal Project. Assessment is internal in most years, with an optional external eAssessment route some schools use.
programmes.countryNote: Mentioned here because Dubai families sometimes compare MYP and IGCSE for the 14-16 window. The practical difference for anyone considering private entry is decisive: MYP is school-assessed and cannot be taken privately, while IGCSE is a set of individual qualifications that can. Families planning around flexibility usually end up on the IGCSE side of that line.

dubai/igcse-private-candidate-registrati.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones private candidates in Dubai most often ask about, with the specific thing that makes each one easy or awkward to enter without a school behind you.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The cleanest private-candidate subject in the catalogue: written papers only, no coursework, no practical, no spoken component. The tier decision is the real work, because Core caps the attainable grade and a student entered at the wrong tier cannot be moved after the deadline.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: A written-only extension subject that private candidates use to add weight to a portfolio. Content is considerably harder than IGCSE Mathematics and assumes the Extended syllabus is already secure, so it is a poor choice as a first private entry.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Available to private candidates but the practical component is the question to resolve first. Boards generally offer an alternative-to-practical written paper in place of a teacher-assessed practical, and a centre must be able to administer whichever route the entry uses. Confirm the component code before teaching starts.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same structure and same caution as Physics: the written theory papers are straightforward to enter and the practical component determines whether the subject is viable at a given centre in a given series. The alternative-to-practical route tests experimental understanding on paper rather than in a laboratory.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest-volume science syllabus and the one where private candidates most often underestimate the reading. Written papers plus a practical component with an alternative written route in most board specifications. Command-term discipline matters as much as recall.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Widely taken by Dubai private candidates and usually the most administratively complex, because the speaking component has to be arranged and conducted by the centre. Some centres offer it as an option rather than as standard, so ask before entering.

subjects.name: English Language (first language)
subjects.description: Written papers in most specifications, which makes it private-candidate friendly, with some routes offering a coursework alternative that a private candidate cannot use. Choose the examination-only route and check the component codes on the entry.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Possible privately but demanding, because set texts change by series and the student must work from the correct set text list for the series they are entered in. Getting that wrong is the single most expensive error available on this subject.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Written papers only in most specifications, making it a reliable private entry. The content is approachable and the marks sit in data-response and extended-answer technique, which is exactly what one-to-one teaching can build in a defined number of weeks.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Written papers in most routes, with some specifications offering a coursework option that private candidates cannot take. Popular as a fifth or sixth subject for portfolio purposes, and straightforward to teach to the examination rather than to a school scheme.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Check the specification carefully. Some routes include a practical programming component assessed by the centre, others a written paper on practical problem solving. The two are different entries and only one of them is routinely open to a private candidate.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language
subjects.description: Relevant for Dubai private candidates for both language and equivalency reasons, though note that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five subjects the UAE Ministry of Education counts for British-track equivalency. Check whether the specification includes a spoken component the centre must administer.

dubai/igcse-private-candidate-registrati.regionsIntro: A private candidate has to physically attend an examination centre, often on consecutive mornings, sometimes during the June heat. Where you live is a real variable in choosing a centre rather than a detail.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Tecom
regions.note: Central, well served by Metro and with several education providers in the immediate area. One of the easier bases from which to reach a range of candidate centres without a long drive on an examination morning.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Coastal and close to the older education belt, so travel to a centre is usually short. Street parking on examination mornings is the practical constraint rather than distance.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Metro-connected but at the far end of the line from some centres. A private candidate here should time the journey once, at the actual examination hour, before the first paper rather than on the day.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Eastern Dubai with a dense school presence nearby but fewer Metro options, so examination mornings mean driving. Worth checking the centre's arrival and identification requirements, since a late arrival is not recoverable.

regions.name: International City and Warsan
regions.note: Affordable and relatively distant from the central education corridor. A private candidate based here often finds the journey, not the syllabus, is what makes a five-subject series hard, and should choose a centre accordingly.

regions.name: Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to several institutions, which makes centre access unusually convenient. A useful base for a candidate sitting a full subject list across several consecutive mornings.

regions.name: Deira and Bur Dubai
regions.note: Older central Dubai, Metro-served, with short journeys to several long-established providers. Peak-hour traffic along the creek corridor is the thing to plan around on an examination morning.

regions.name: Dubai Hills and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Newer residential Dubai with good road access to the central corridor. Journeys are predictable outside peak hours, which matters for an afternoon paper more than a morning one.

sections.heading: What IGCSE private candidate entry costs in Dubai
paragraphs: A private candidate in Dubai pays per subject, to a centre, in three separable parts, and the total for a five-subject series is materially higher than families expect because only one of the three parts is the board's exam fee. The other two are the centre's own charges and any component surcharge, and both vary between centres in the same city.

We do not publish specific centre fee figures on this page, for a reason worth stating. Centre registration fees in Dubai are commercial and change by series, several centres quote only on enquiry, and a figure printed here would be out of date within a year and wrong for most readers immediately. What is useful instead is the structure, so that when you call three centres you know what to ask about and can compare quotes that are actually comparable.

Ask every centre the same five questions: the per-subject entry fee for the series you want; the centre's own registration or administration fee, and whether it is per candidate or per subject; whether any of your subjects carry a practical, speaking or alternative-paper surcharge; the private-candidate entry deadline, which is often earlier than the school deadline; and the late-entry fee if you miss it. Get the answers by email rather than by phone, because a quote you can re-read is a quote you can compare.

For context on where the rest of the money goes: tutoring to cover a full IGCSE syllabus privately is the larger cost in most cases. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 in the middle. A private candidate covering a full syllabus alone usually needs more than one hour a week, which is the honest arithmetic.

sections.heading: Which subjects a private candidate can actually enter
paragraphs: This is the question to settle before any money is spent on teaching, and it is settled by the component structure of the specific syllabus rather than by the subject name. The rule of thumb: a subject assessed entirely by written examination is straightforward to enter privately; a subject with a component that a school teacher must assess is not, unless the board provides an alternative route and the centre can administer it.

Written-only subjects are the safe ground. Mathematics, Additional Mathematics, Economics, Business Studies and most history and geography routes are assessed by papers a private candidate sits in the same room as everyone else. These are the subjects a portfolio should be built around, especially for a candidate assembling five passes for equivalency purposes.

The sciences sit in the middle. Physics, Chemistry and Biology all include a practical element, and boards generally provide an alternative-to-practical written paper in place of a teacher-assessed practical. That route is usually available to private candidates, but it is a different component code on the entry and the centre must be able to administer it. The alternative paper is not easier; it tests experimental understanding in writing, which is its own skill.

Languages are the awkward ones. English as a Second Language and most foreign-language specifications include a speaking component that the centre has to arrange and conduct, and not every Dubai centre offers it as standard. English Literature carries a different hazard: set texts change by series, and a candidate who prepares the wrong set text list has lost the subject. Computer Science splits the same way, with some routes carrying a centre-assessed practical component and others a written paper on practical problem solving.

The practical instruction is always the same. Find the syllabus code, read the assessment structure on the board's own site, then ask the centre in writing whether they administer that component for private candidates in the series you want. Do all three before booking a tutor.

sections.heading: The series, the deadline and the whole calendar counted backwards
paragraphs: A Dubai private candidate sits June or November with Cambridge International, and May/June or November with Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only. That single fact removes an option families sometimes plan around, and it is worth confirming before a teaching schedule is built, because a plan aimed at a February window is a plan aimed at nothing.

Pearson's published pattern shows the real shape of the calendar. The November International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January — November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June results come in August: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the correct practice is to work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date, because provisional timetables are revised.

For Cambridge the zone rule is the private candidate's specific hazard. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. A school student has an exams officer checking this. A private candidate has nobody, so ask the centre which zone it sits in and download that timetable.

Counted backwards from the papers, the planning order is: confirm the series, confirm the centre and its zone, confirm the private-candidate entry deadline with that centre, finalise the subject list including component routes, make the entry, then build the teaching schedule into the remaining weeks. Families routinely do this in the reverse order, start tutoring first, and discover a component or deadline problem with eight weeks to go.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel for a private candidate
paragraphs: The board choice matters more for a private candidate than for a school student, because a school student follows whatever their school entered them for and a private candidate chooses. The choice should be made on component structure and centre availability rather than on reputation, since both boards' IGCSE qualifications are widely recognised.

Cambridge International offers Core and Extended tiers in many subjects, which is a genuine decision with consequences: Core caps the attainable grade while Extended reaches the top of the scale, and a candidate entered at the wrong tier cannot be moved after the deadline. Cambridge also runs the zone timetable system, with six administrative zones and an explicit warning about using the wrong one. Its series for UAE candidates are June and November.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE assesses several subjects entirely by written examination, which can make it the simpler board for a private candidate, and it runs May/June and November series. Pearson's published timetables and results dates are well documented, which makes planning more predictable. Where a subject has no coursework component in the Pearson specification but does in the Cambridge one, that is a reason to prefer Pearson for that subject specifically.

A mixed portfolio is permissible and sometimes sensible: there is no requirement that all a candidate's IGCSEs come from one board. What matters is that the chosen centre administers every component for every subject in the series you want. A family that picks subjects across two boards without checking that is likely to find one subject orphaned, and the fix at that point is to defer it to the next series.

sections.heading: The five subjects UAE equivalency counts, and why the list matters here
paragraphs: A large share of Dubai private candidates are sitting IGCSEs with a specific destination in mind: a certificate portfolio that will satisfy UAE Ministry of Education equivalency when the time comes to apply to a university here. If that is the goal, the subject list should be chosen against the published requirements rather than against interest, because getting it wrong means sitting another series.

The published British-track requirements are specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is the detail families most often get wrong and which at least one page ranking in this market states incorrectly as six subjects.

For a private candidate that translates into a planning rule: build the five around written-examination subjects that are reliably open to private entry, and treat Arabic as an addition rather than as one of the five. It also means the A Level or AS Level requirement needs a plan of its own, since practical sciences at that level carry an examined practical component that must be confirmed with a centre.

Two cautions. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority run; they are not services IB Gram performs, influences or guarantees, and we describe them here only so a subject list can be planned sensibly. And nothing about tutoring is required for equivalency, for admission or for progression. Any provider who implies otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process they have no part in.

sections.heading: Teaching a full syllabus with no school behind you
paragraphs: This is the part of private candidacy that is genuinely harder than school, and it is not the exam. A school student gets a department: a scheme of work, a pace, mock exams set by someone else, a teacher who knows which topics the paper has favoured, and twenty-nine other students whose questions reveal gaps the student did not know they had. A private candidate has none of that and has to manufacture all of it.

The pacing problem is first. A full IGCSE syllabus is typically taught across two school years. A private candidate working towards a series eight months away is compressing that, and the only way to do it reliably is to build the schedule backwards from the paper date with topic coverage tracked in writing. The student should be able to see, at any point, what has been covered and what has not. Without that, the last six weeks become a discovery exercise.

The second problem is calibration. A school student finds out where they stand from mocks and class position. A private candidate finds out from timed past papers, marked properly against the official mark scheme, and the discipline of actually sitting them under time rather than reading them. This is where most private candidates lose marks they did not need to lose: they know the content and have never written three hours of it against a clock.

The third is the exam-technique layer that schools transmit almost accidentally — how long to spend on a six-mark question, what a command term expects, how the marks are distributed across a paper, what the examiner is actually looking for in a data-response answer. None of it is content and all of it is marks. For a private candidate it has to be taught explicitly, which is a good use of one-to-one time and a poor use of a group class.

Sit past papers under genuine timed conditions, not as reading exercises

sections.heading: Academic honesty and what a tutor may do for a private candidate
paragraphs: Private candidates are more exposed to this than school students, because they have no department watching and because some providers in this market will offer whatever is asked for. The boundary is the same and it is worth stating on this page specifically.

A tutor may teach the whole syllabus, explain the assessment structure and mark allocations, teach exam technique and command terms, set and mark past-paper work against the official mark scheme, give written feedback, and explain the registration process as this page does. That is the entirety of what a private candidate actually needs and it is a great deal of help.

A tutor may not sit any part of an examination, assist during one, produce work that will be submitted as the candidate's own, or supply board material that is not publicly released. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads — we reference them and link the official source. Any provider offering a private library of mark schemes or unreleased material is offering something that is both a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure for the candidate.

One more boundary specific to this page: IB Gram is not an examination centre and holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or any other body. We cannot register a candidate, host an examination, obtain a place at a full centre, or influence a centre's decision on components or deadlines. We teach the syllabus and we explain the process. The registration is between you and the centre.
