sections.heading: Permits, availability and scheduling in a Dubai year
paragraphs: On the legal position for whoever teaches you: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted to you as unverified.

On availability, the honest position: a private candidate's requirement is unusual because it is a whole syllabus rather than a weekly top-up, often at a higher weekly intensity, and sometimes in a subject with few local tutors. Mathematics, Economics, Business Studies and the sciences are reasonably covered. A full syllabus in a less-common language or in a subject with a specialist component is thinner, and a specific intensive slot cannot always be filled immediately. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base including IB and IGCSE specialists in India, delivered identically by live video on Gulf Standard Time. No home visits happen in the UAE.

On scheduling, a private candidate has one real advantage over a school student: no school day. That makes morning and early-afternoon sessions possible, which is when most people study better and when tutor availability is widest. A candidate who is not at school should be using those hours rather than defaulting to a 6pm slot built for people who are.

The UAE calendar still applies. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend. During Ramadan the productive window shifts, for many families to after Iftar, and it is better to agree that the slot moves for the month than to renegotiate weekly. Eid breaks are announced rather than fixed far ahead. And the June series sits in the Dubai summer, which is worth factoring into both revision conditions and the journey to the centre.
bullets: MoHRE permit: free, valid two years, two working days, no published fine schedule
Private candidates should use morning hours; tutor availability is widest then
Agree in advance that the slot moves after Iftar for Ramadan
The June series sits in the Dubai summer; plan the journey to the centre accordingly

process.title: Decide the series before anything else
process.description: June or November for Cambridge, May/June or November for Pearson. The February/March Cambridge series is India-only and not available to you in Dubai. Every subsequent decision, including the teaching schedule, is built backwards from this one date.

process.title: Shortlist centres and ask the five questions
process.description: Per-subject entry fee, centre administration fee and whether it is per subject or per candidate, component surcharges, the private-candidate deadline, and the late-entry position. Ask by email so the answers are comparable. Also ask which Cambridge zone the centre sits in.

process.title: Confirm each subject's component route
process.description: Find the syllabus code, read the assessment structure on the board's own site, then confirm in writing that the centre administers that component for private candidates in your series. Do this before booking any teaching, because it can remove a subject from your list.

process.title: Make the entry, then book the teaching
process.description: The entry is between you and the centre; we cannot make it for you and no tutor can. Once it is confirmed, the teaching schedule is built backwards from the paper dates with topic coverage tracked in writing, so you can see at any point what remains.

process.title: Timed papers from early, not from the end
process.description: Past papers under genuine timed conditions, marked against the official mark scheme, starting well before the final weeks. This is where private candidates make up the ground a school's mock exams would otherwise give them, and it is the single highest-value habit on this route.

process.title: Check the logistics before the first paper
process.description: Zone timetable downloaded, identification requirements confirmed, arrival time confirmed, journey timed at the actual examination hour. A late arrival or a wrong document is not recoverable, and no school is checking any of it on a private candidate's behalf.

whyPoints.title: We tell you the cost structure, not a made-up figure
whyPoints.description: Centre fees in Dubai are commercial, vary by provider and change by series, so a number printed here would be wrong for most readers. What we give you instead is the three-part structure and the five questions to ask, which is what makes three centre quotes comparable.

whyPoints.title: Component viability checked before teaching is sold
whyPoints.description: The commonest expensive mistake on this route is paying for teaching in a subject the candidate cannot actually enter at their chosen centre. We treat the component route as the first question rather than a detail, even where that shortens the subject list.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is not an examination centre. We hold no Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA or Ministry of Education approval, accreditation or partnership, we cannot register a candidate or host a paper, and we have no UAE office. All UAE teaching is online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the boards, with the ones we cannot verify left out
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's zone rule and series, Pearson's November timetable end date and its published results dates are cited from the boards. We publish no IB session date anywhere, because the IB's site blocks automated checking and a wrong date is worse than none.

whyPoints.title: A schedule built backwards with coverage in writing
whyPoints.description: A private candidate's real enemy is pacing, not difficulty. Teaching is planned from the paper date back, with topics tracked so the student can see what remains at any point. Without that the final six weeks become a discovery exercise about what was never covered.

whyPoints.title: Official material linked, never supplied
whyPoints.description: Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents are referenced and linked from the board's own site. We do not host or distribute them. A provider offering a private library of mark schemes or unreleased material is creating a copyright problem and a malpractice exposure for the candidate.

faqs.question: What does it cost to sit IGCSEs as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The total has three separable parts and only one is the board's fee. First, the per-subject examination entry fee. Second, the centre's own registration or administration charge, which is a commercial decision and varies between Dubai centres — ask whether it is per candidate or per subject, because across five subjects the difference is large. Third, any practical, speaking or alternative-paper surcharge, which can double the cost of a single science or language. We do not print centre figures here because they change by series and by provider; ask three centres the same questions by email and compare the written answers.

faqs.question: Can a private candidate in Dubai sit IGCSE Physics or Chemistry with the practical?
faqs.answer: Usually, but through a different route and only if the centre administers it. Both subjects include a practical element, and boards generally provide an alternative-to-practical written paper in place of a teacher-assessed practical. That is a different component code on the entry, and not every Dubai centre offers every component for private candidates in every series. The alternative paper is not easier: it tests apparatus choice, variable control, sources of error and data interpretation in writing. Confirm the component with the centre in writing before paying for any teaching in that subject.

faqs.question: Is the Cambridge February or March series available to a candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. The Cambridge International February/March series is offered to India only. A UAE candidate, private or school-entered, sits the June series or the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. This matters because families sometimes build a whole teaching schedule around a February window that does not exist for them, and discover it when the entry is attempted. Decide the series first, confirm it with the centre, and build the teaching plan backwards from the actual paper dates for that series.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are easiest to take without being at a school?
faqs.answer: The ones assessed entirely by written examination. Mathematics, Additional Mathematics, Economics, Business Studies and most history and geography routes are papers a private candidate sits in the same room as everyone else, with no teacher-assessed component to arrange. These should form the core of any portfolio, especially one being assembled for UAE equivalency. The awkward ones are languages with a speaking component the centre must conduct, English Literature where set texts change by series, and Computer Science where some routes carry a centre-assessed practical that is not routinely open to private candidates.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram register our child for the exams or host them?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is not an examination centre and holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or any other body. We cannot register a candidate, host a paper, obtain a place at a full centre, or influence a centre's decisions on components, deadlines or fees. What we do is teach the syllabus, one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time, and explain the process as set out on this page. The registration itself is a direct arrangement between you and the examination centre you choose.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge zone timetable and why does it matter more for a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. A school student has an exams officer checking this on their behalf. A private candidate has nobody, so it becomes your job. Ask the centre in writing which zone it sits in, download that specific timetable rather than a generic one, and check every paper date against it before the series begins.

faqs.question: How far ahead does a private candidate have to register in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Months, and often earlier than a school student would. Entry deadlines sit well before the papers in every series, and private-candidate deadlines at a given centre are frequently earlier still, because the centre has to administer the entry separately from its own cohort. Some centres do not accept late private entries at all, and where late entry is permitted it carries a higher fee. Confirm the exact date by email rather than by phone, and treat a verbal reassurance as worthless. Missing the deadline means waiting for the next series, which is months of delay.

faqs.question: Should a Dubai private candidate choose Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Choose on component structure and centre availability rather than reputation, since both are widely recognised. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE assesses several subjects entirely by written examination, which can make it simpler for a private candidate, and it runs May/June and November. Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers in many subjects, which is a real decision because Core caps the attainable grade and a tier cannot be changed after the deadline. A mixed portfolio across both boards is permitted, provided one centre administers every component you need in the series you want.

faqs.question: How many hours of teaching does a full IGCSE syllabus need from scratch?
faqs.answer: More than one hour a week, which is the honest answer families least like. A full IGCSE syllabus is normally taught across two school years, so a private candidate aiming at a series eight months away is compressing it. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor online in Dubai run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 in the middle. Expect to need above that for genuine full-syllabus coverage, and build the schedule backwards from the paper date.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE results reach a private candidate?
faqs.answer: On the same dates as everyone else in the series, through the centre. Pearson's published pattern is a useful guide: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A private candidate usually collects results from the centre rather than from a school, so confirm with the centre in advance how results will be issued and to whom. Note also that the enquiry-about-results window is short, so know the deadline before results day rather than after it.

faqs.question: Which five subjects should a private candidate take for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Build the five around written-examination subjects that are reliably open to private entry, and plan the A Level requirement separately. The published British-track requirements are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, so treat Arabic as an addition. Verify everything on moe.gov.ae; the Ministry runs this process and IB Gram has no part in it.

faqs.question: Do you come to our home in Dubai to teach a private candidate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE teaching is one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time. For a private candidate this is usually an advantage: full-syllabus coverage needs a specialist in that exact syllabus and often several sessions a week, and the pool of people who can do that in a given Dubai community at a given hour is far narrower than the pool available online. If you require a tutor physically present, we are not the right provider.

faqs.question: How does a private candidate know whether they are on track without mock exams?
faqs.answer: Timed past papers, marked against the official mark scheme, started early rather than saved for the end. This is the single habit that separates private candidates who do well from those who do not, because a school student gets calibration free from mocks and class position while a private candidate has to manufacture it. The discipline is to sit the paper under genuine time rather than reading it, then have it marked properly and the errors categorised by question type. Official papers and mark schemes are linked from the board's site; we do not reproduce or supply them.

faqs.question: Is a resit as a private candidate treated differently from a first entry?
faqs.answer: Administratively it is an ordinary entry: same deadline structure, same fees, same component requirements. Academically it should be treated completely differently. A resit candidate usually knows most of the content and is losing marks in two or three identifiable question types, so starting from the syllabus wastes money. The work should start from the previous paper performance where that is available, target the specific question types that cost marks, and run on timed practice rather than teaching. That makes a resit block shorter and cheaper than a full syllabus course, by design.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help during the examination or with submitted work?
faqs.answer: No, and the boundary needs to be clear before anything is booked. A tutor may teach the whole syllabus, explain the assessment structure and mark allocations, teach command terms and exam technique, set and mark past papers against the official mark scheme, and give written feedback. A tutor may not sit or assist in any part of an examination, produce work submitted as the candidate's own, or supply unreleased board material. Any provider offering a private library of mark schemes or unreleased papers is creating a copyright problem and a malpractice exposure that falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: What is the best time of day for a private candidate to study in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Mornings, and it is the one structural advantage of not being at school. A private candidate has no school day, so the hours when most people concentrate best and when tutor availability is widest are available, instead of a 6pm slot designed for people who have just finished a school run. The UAE week still applies — Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend — and during Ramadan the productive window shifts, for many families to after Iftar, which is better agreed in advance than renegotiated weekly. The June series sits in the Dubai summer, so plan both study conditions and the journey to the centre.

dubai/igcse-private-candidate-registrati.closingHeading: Settle the series, the centre and the components first
dubai/igcse-private-candidate-registrati.closingBody: Almost every expensive mistake on this route is administrative rather than academic: a subject the candidate cannot actually enter at their centre, a deadline that closed earlier than expected, or a plan built around the February series, which is India-only and not open to a Dubai candidate. Settle the series, choose the centre, ask the five questions by email, confirm each subject's component route, make the entry — and then book teaching against the remaining weeks. We teach the syllabus one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. We are not an examination centre, we hold no board approval, and we do not send tutors to UAE homes.

This page prices the whole thing: what each provider model charges, which extras get added afterwards, what an hourly contract exposes you to against a package, and how rates behave in exam season. dubai/igcse-private-tuition.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below carries a rate band rather than a slogan, set by subject scarcity, syllabus code and session length. The band is confirmed in writing before the free trial lesson, with the session length it is built around and anything that is charged on top stated in the same message.

intro.heading: What IGCSE private tuition in Dubai actually costs, line by line
paragraphs: Ask five Dubai providers for a price on the same Year 11 Extended Mathematics brief and you will get five numbers between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour. That fourteen-fold spread is not a market failing to settle; it is five different products sold under one phrase. One is a university student supervising homework. One is a tuition centre putting six students in a room. One is an agency placing a qualified subject teacher online. One is an independent tutor pricing in a forty-minute drive across the emirate. One is a named premium tutor with a waiting list. Comparing their headline rates tells you almost nothing, and that is the problem this page exists to solve.

Start with what the market publishes. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both read October 2026 — the budget online band. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200, which is roughly where a qualified subject tutor working online sits. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour including travel, and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 or more. TutorChase publishes AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

Then look at what the published rate leaves out, because this is where Dubai families are most often caught. Registration or placement fees charged once. Assessment or diagnostic fees charged before teaching starts. Material and past-paper charges, which are sometimes charges for documents the board publishes free. Travel surcharges by community, or travel priced inside an hour so that a sixty-minute visit delivers forty minutes of teaching. Cancellation windows of forty-eight or seventy-two hours that quietly convert a missed session into a paid one. Rescheduling limits per term. Report or progress-report fees. Peak-season premiums in the weeks before a series. Minimum commitments of ten or twenty sessions. Sibling rates that evaporate if session lengths differ. And the one nobody mentions until the invoice: whether the quoted figure is before or after VAT.

The third layer is contract shape, which matters more than the rate for most families. An hourly arrangement is the most expensive per session and carries almost no risk. A twenty-session package is cheaper per session and transfers the risk to you, because the exposure sits in the cancellation terms, the expiry date and who holds unused sessions if the match turns out to be wrong. A monthly subscription is the easiest to forget about, which is precisely why it is the model most likely to still be running in June for a student who stopped needing it in February. None of the three is wrong. Choosing one without reading the cancellation clause is.

On our own position and on delivery, plainly. IB Gram publishes no price list on this page, because an honest quote depends on subject scarcity, syllabus code and session length, and because a figure given before anyone has met your child is a figure about nothing. What we publish is the market with its sources attached, then one free 30-minute trial lesson — one per family, no card details — after which you get a written quote in AED naming the tutor, the session length and anything charged on top. Dubai lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

dubai/igcse-private-tuition.programmesIntro: Price behaves differently at each stage, because scarcity does. These four bands cover the stages a Dubai family buying IGCSE tuition is usually pricing across, including the one most providers never mention: entering a subject again, or for the first time, as a private candidate.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The two years that generate most tuition spend in Dubai. Pricing within IGCSE varies more by subject than by year: Extended Mathematics, the separate sciences and Additional Mathematics command the top of the qualified-tutor band, while Business, Economics and ICT sit below it because the tutor pool is wider. Year 11 spend typically runs 20 to 40 per cent above Year 10 for the same subject, driven by mock season and entry deadlines rather than by difficulty.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's scale is what creates the spread. The UK curriculum accounts for 37 per cent of enrolment across 227 private schools, so there are enough buyers to support a genuine budget tier and enough demand in exam term to support a premium one. Both tiers advertise with the same words, which is why comparing the included items matters more here than in a smaller market.

programmes.name: AS Level
programmes.description: Rates step up at AS, typically by 20 to 50 per cent over the same subject at IGCSE, because the pool of tutors competent at AS Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry is materially smaller. Families who have budgeted an IGCSE rate for two years are routinely surprised in Year 12. The step is worth planning for in the Year 11 budget rather than discovered in September.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at a grade no lower than E can substitute for one Advanced Level subject. That makes AS a route decision as well as an academic one, and it is the Ministry's process rather than a tuition provider's — verify the current wording on the official channel.

programmes.name: A Level
programmes.description: The highest band in the British-curriculum ladder, where premium and named-tutor pricing concentrates. Published figures in this market reach AED 650 an hour at the top end. The practical question for a Dubai family is whether the premium is buying scarce subject competence — Further Mathematics, Physics, Economics at the top grades — or simply reputation, and the test is whether the tutor can diagnose from a marked script in the trial.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's post-16 cohort splits between A Level and the IB Diploma, and the two markets price differently for the same hour of a tutor's time. A family holding quotes from both should compare what is included rather than the rates, because Diploma quotes often bundle Internal Assessment feedback time that A Level quotes do not.

programmes.name: Retakes and private candidate entry
programmes.ageRange: Any age · June and November series
programmes.description: The least-discussed and most often mispriced situation: a student retaking a subject, or entering one their school does not offer. Tuition for a retake is usually shorter and more intensive than a first attempt, because the content exists and the loss patterns are known from a real script. The separate cost is the examination entry itself, which is set by the centre and the board rather than by any tutor.
programmes.countryNote: A small number of licensed centres in Dubai accept private candidates, and each publishes its own fee schedule and deadlines. No entry-fee figure is quoted on this page because none has been verified from a centre's own current schedule — ask the centre directly, in writing, and confirm the series deadline at the same time.

dubai/igcse-private-tuition.subjectsIntro: Rates inside IGCSE are set by how many people in Dubai can teach the subject well, not by how hard it is. Each entry below names the syllabus codes and explains where that subject sits in the local price band and why, which is the part of pricing no provider explains.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Extended and Higher tier)
subjects.description: The single most demanded IGCSE subject in Dubai and consistently at the top of the qualified-tutor band. Extended and Higher-tier competence is a narrower skill than it appears, and Year 11 demand concentrates in the eight weeks after January mocks, which is exactly when the premium appears.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Priced above standard Mathematics because the tutor pool is small. Taken by stronger Dubai sets heading for A Level Mathematics, and the content — calculus, identities, series — is genuinely a different teaching job. Expect this to sit near the ceiling of the qualified-tutor band rather than the middle.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Top of the science band in Dubai, partly because competent physics teaching is scarce everywhere and partly because the practical component adds a second thing to teach. Rates for 0625 with the practical paper routinely exceed rates for the same tutor teaching Chemistry.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mid-to-upper science band. Supply in Dubai is better than physics, so rates sit slightly lower for equivalent experience. Demand peaks later in the year than mathematics, because chemistry problems tend to surface in the second mock rather than the first.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The widest supply of the three sciences and therefore the most competitive pricing. Worth noting that a cheaper biology rate does not mean a weaker tutor here — it reflects a larger pool rather than lower quality, which is the opposite of the assumption most families make.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Priced in the middle of the band, with a wide quality spread because almost anyone will offer it. The discriminating question for a Dubai family is whether the tutor marks to the board's own criteria rather than to a general sense of good writing, and that is testable in a trial.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification from First Language English and frequently confused with it in Dubai enquiries. Specialists in the second-language syllabus are scarcer than general English tutors, so a correctly matched tutor often costs more than the first quote a family receives.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: Among the scarcest specialisms in the Dubai market and priced accordingly, at or above the science band. KHDA requires Arabic first-language classes to be organised separately from the additional-language group, so the two are not interchangeable and should never be quoted as if they were.

subjects.name: Arabic as a foreign language
subjects.description: Better supplied than the first-language syllabus and priced closer to the middle of the band. The most common pricing error in Dubai Arabic enquiries is a first-language quote for an additional-language need, or the reverse, which is a difference of well over AED 100 an hour.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Below the science and mathematics bands because supply is wide. Technique rather than content drives the grade, which means short, cheap blocks are often genuinely sufficient — one of the few places in this market where the low quote and the right answer coincide.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Unusual pricing: wide supply of people who can code, narrow supply of people who can teach the specific theory terminology and pseudocode conventions the papers reward. The cheap end of this subject is cheap for a reason, and the trial lesson is where the difference shows.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Mid band, with a premium where a Dubai centre runs the coursework option, because support for coursework has to be delivered inside strict rules and fewer tutors will take it on. Always establish whether your school runs the coursework route before comparing quotes.

dubai/igcse-private-tuition.regionsTitle: Dubai communities, and what they do to a quote
dubai/igcse-private-tuition.regionsIntro: Where you live changes the price of in-home tuition and, less obviously, the price you are first quoted for online tuition. These are the Dubai communities where that effect is clearest, with the market behaviour we actually see from each.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: High-rise households where travel surcharges are low but parking and building access slow a visiting tutor down, so sixty-minute visits often deliver less teaching. Online quotes here start higher than the emirate average simply because providers assume a higher budget.

regions.name: The Greens, The Views and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Dense apartment communities with large Year 10 and 11 populations, which makes this one of the few parts of Dubai where group classes genuinely find students at the same level. Group pricing of AED 90 to 150 a student is realistic here rather than theoretical.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens, The Gardens and Al Furjan
regions.note: Price-sensitive, high-volume demand and the most competitive quoting in the emirate. It is also where the budget tier is most likely to be sold as something it is not, so the included-items comparison matters more here than anywhere else.

regions.name: Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Muhaisnah
regions.note: Established communities with strong Indian and British curriculum demand side by side. Independent tutors dominate and quote directly, often below agency rates, which puts the permit and syllabus-code checks squarely on the parent.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Villa communities at the top of the in-home band, where travel is priced in heavily and specialist availability is the real constraint rather than cost. Families here most often end up online for scarce subjects after trying to book locally.

regions.name: Town Square, Remraam and Dubailand
regions.note: Long drives from where most Dubai tutors live, which shows up as a travel surcharge of AED 50 to 150 an hour or as a flat refusal. The gap between the in-home and online quote is wider here than in any other cluster.

regions.name: Motor City, Sports City and Arjan
regions.note: Mid-fee school catchments with steady Year 11 demand and heavy use of twenty-session packages. The cancellation and expiry terms on those packages are the single most useful thing to read before signing in this community.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and International City
regions.note: Long bus runs mean late weekday starts and a weekend-heavy timetable, and weekend slots carry a premium with several providers. Asking whether the weekend rate differs from the weekday rate is worth doing before a package is priced.

schoolClusters.note: Schools where in-school academic support is substantial and private tuition is bought selectively, usually for one subject in Year 11. Quotes from this cluster tend to be for short, targeted blocks rather than year-long arrangements, which is also the cheapest way to buy tuition.

sections.heading: What each provider model charges in Dubai, and what is inside the figure
paragraphs: A Dubai family holding five quotes is usually comparing five different products. The table below separates them by model, states the AED band each publishes, names the source and the month it was read, and lists what is typically inside and outside the figure. That last pair of columns is where the real comparison happens, because two quotes 40 per cent apart can represent identical value once travel, materials and cancellation terms are accounted for.

The budget online tier is real and has a legitimate use. At AED 33 to 65 an hour, which is where Tutopiya and EdFlik publish their entry rates, you are buying supervision and reassurance: somebody sitting with a student while they work, keeping them on task, answering questions as they arise. For a Year 10 student who simply does not start homework, that can be exactly the right purchase. What it does not buy is diagnosis against a syllabus code or marking to a board scheme, and families who expect that from a budget rate are disappointed by the product rather than cheated by it.

The qualified-tutor band, roughly AED 150 to AED 300 online, is where most genuine IGCSE teaching sits. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase publishes AED 270. Above that, the premium tier reaches AED 650 at the top of the published Dubai market. The honest observation about the premium tier is that it buys scarcity reliably and competence only sometimes — a named tutor with a waiting list is priced by demand, and demand is not a measure of teaching.

In-home visiting rates look higher than online rates and are often the same thing with travel inside them. Bestimate's 2026 table gives AED 180 to AED 350 an hour including travel, and independent listings run from AED 200 to AED 500. When you strip the travel out, the teaching component of a AED 300 visit is frequently in the same band as a AED 200 online session. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai — home visits are a service we offer only in India — so the comparison here is offered as market information rather than as an option we sell.

sections.heading: The eleven extras that change the real hourly cost
paragraphs: The gap between a quoted rate and what a Dubai family actually pays per hour of teaching is typically 10 to 35 per cent, and almost all of it sits in items that are perfectly legitimate and simply were not mentioned. None of the eleven below is a scam. Each is a real cost somebody has to carry. The problem is that they are disclosed at different points in the sales process by different providers, which makes the quotes incomparable unless you ask.

Two of them deserve particular attention because they are the largest. The first is travel inside the hour: a visiting tutor booked for sixty minutes who arrives late from Downtown and leaves on time has delivered forty-five minutes, so the effective rate is a third higher than quoted. Ask whether the hour starts at the agreed time or on arrival. The second is the cancellation window. A seventy-two-hour cancellation policy, applied to a Year 11 student with a changing fixture list and a mock timetable, converts several sessions a term into paid absences. Both are negotiable before signing and immovable afterwards.

The material charge is worth a separate warning. Board syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are published by Cambridge and Pearson on their own sites and should be read there; a charge for supplying them is a charge for something the board already provides, and redistributing those documents is a copyright matter. A charge for a provider's own written notes or question banks is a different and reasonable thing. Establish which one you are being billed for.

On VAT, the only statement this page will make is a narrow one. UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees is not something a tutoring site should assert without a Federal Tax Authority citation, and this page has none. What you can and should insist on is clarity about the specific quote in front of you: ask whether the figure is inclusive or exclusive of VAT, and ask for the answer in the same written message as the rate. A provider that will not put that in writing has told you something useful.

sections.heading: Hourly, block or term: three contracts and what each exposes you to
paragraphs: Most Dubai families think they are choosing a tutor. They are also choosing a contract, and the contract decides what happens in the two situations that actually arise: the match is wrong, or the need ends earlier than expected. Both are common. Neither is a failure. A sensible contract makes both cheap.

Paying per session is the most expensive per hour and the correct default for a first arrangement. Nothing is held in advance, stopping costs one session's notice, and the provider carries the risk of being good enough to be rebooked. The reason families move away from it is a discount, and the discount is real — but it is the price of accepting the risk transfer, and that trade only makes sense once the match has proved itself.

A package transfers risk in three specific places, and all three are readable before signing. Who holds unused sessions if you stop, whether the package expires on a date or on completion, and whether sessions are transferable between siblings or subjects. A twenty-session package at a 15 per cent discount that expires in ninety days, bought in October for a student whose need closes in January, is a bad purchase at a good rate. The version with no expiry and transferability is a good purchase at the same rate.

Monthly subscriptions are the most comfortable and the most likely to overrun. The failure mode is simple and we see it constantly: nobody cancels. A plan bought in October for a Year 11 mock problem is still billing in June, long after the problem closed, because reviewing it requires an awkward conversation. Our own answer to that is a written half-term review with an explicit stop recommendation, and we say stop when stopping is right. Any model can be run honestly; the subscription is the one that needs a review date built in.

sections.heading: Tuition spend against a Dubai school-fee year
paragraphs: Tuition is easier to judge next to the school bill than on its own, and 2026-27 is an unusually clean year in which to do it. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For most Dubai families this is the first flat fee year in some time, which makes a tuition decision a decision about new money rather than about a rising baseline.

The arithmetic below converts the market mid-band into the spend patterns Dubai IGCSE families actually choose. It assumes AED 220 an hour, a thirty-four-week academic year, and no extras, and it is arithmetic rather than an IB Gram price. The striking thing when it is laid out is how much cheaper a targeted block is than a year-long weekly slot, and how rarely families choose the block. Two subjects weekly across Year 11 is roughly AED 15,000; two targeted blocks that close the actual loss patterns are roughly a fifth of that.

The pattern that gives the best return in our experience is not the cheapest or the dearest. It is a marked diagnostic, then a short block against the named patterns, then a stop, then a second short block in the term before the series. Total spend lands near the middle of the table and the hours sit where the marks are. The pattern that gives the worst return is the open weekly slot with no named target, which is also the easiest to sell and the hardest to end.

One more line in the budget that most families miss entirely: examination entry for any subject taken outside the school's own entry. Private candidate entry is priced by the centre, not the tutor, and each Dubai centre publishes its own schedule and deadlines. No figure appears here because none has been verified from a centre's current schedule. If a retake or an extra subject is in your plan, get that number in writing early, because the entry deadline usually falls months before the paper.

sections.heading: Does paying more buy a better IGCSE grade?
paragraphs: Not reliably, and the market data makes that unusually easy to see. Published Dubai rates for the same described service span fourteenfold. If price tracked outcome, the AED 650 tutor would be roughly fourteen times as effective as the AED 45 one, which nobody believes. What price tracks in this market is scarcity, demand and overhead — and scarcity is only sometimes a proxy for competence.

Three things do correlate with grade movement, and none of them appears in a rate. The first is whether the tutor works from the correct syllabus code and the board's own mark scheme. A tutor teaching 0580 content to a 4MA1 candidate will be pleasant, expensive and off-target. The second is whether a marked script came before the teaching, because that is the only way the hours get aimed. The third is whether the student completes the work between sessions — the single strongest predictor we see, in every format and at every price point.

There is one legitimate reason to pay the top of the band, and it is scarcity rather than quality. Arabic as a first language, Additional Mathematics, and physics at the top grades have genuinely thin supply in Dubai. If your need is one of those, the premium is the market clearing and there is no clever way around it. If your need is Business Studies technique or English exam structure, paying premium rates is paying for availability you do not need.

What this means practically is that the trial lesson is worth more than the rate card. In thirty minutes a competent tutor will ask for the syllabus code, look at a marked script, and name a loss pattern with the marks it costs. One who talks about motivation and potential for thirty minutes has shown you something too. That test costs nothing and discriminates better than any price signal in this market.

sections.heading: What to send when you ask five Dubai providers for a quote
paragraphs: Most quotes in this market are vague because the brief was vague. A provider given a subject and a year group has to price the uncertainty, and prices it upwards. A provider given a precise brief can price precisely, and the quotes you receive become comparable with each other for the first time.

Send seven things in one message: the exam board and the four-digit or alphanumeric syllabus code from the entry statement; the tier, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher; the exam series you are working towards; the current mark or grade and the target; a recent marked paper if you have one; the session length you want and three possible weekly slots in Gulf Standard Time; and the format, which for Dubai families means online one-to-one. That single message removes most of the ambiguity that inflates a quote.

Then ask five questions and compare the answers rather than the rates. What is inside the hourly figure and what is billed on top. What is the cancellation window and how many reschedules a term. Is the figure inclusive or exclusive of VAT. What happens if the match is wrong — specifically, is there a replacement arrangement and what happens to anything prepaid. And who exactly will teach the session, by name and subject background, because an agency quoting a rate and matching later is quoting a rate for an unknown tutor.

One last filter that costs nothing. Ask whether the provider holds any regulatory approval and listen carefully to the answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years; a business with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. Those are specific, checkable things. A provider implying a regulator endorses its teaching has either a permit number to show you or a problem. IB Gram holds no such permit and claims none.
bullets: Send the board, the code, the tier and the series in the first message
Send the current mark, the target and a marked paper if one exists
Ask what is billed on top, and get the VAT position in writing
Ask who will teach, by name and subject background, before agreeing a rate
Ask about the replacement arrangement before you need it, not after

sections.heading: When the match is wrong, and what should happen to the money
paragraphs: Roughly one arrangement in six does not work, in any market and at any price. The student does not engage, the tutor's pace is wrong, the subject turns out to be a different problem from the one described. This is normal and it is the situation most tuition contracts handle worst, because the commercial incentive runs towards keeping the slot rather than fixing the match.

What a reasonable arrangement looks like: the problem is raised after two sessions rather than endured for a term, a different tutor is offered without a new registration fee, nothing prepaid is lost, and the written diagnostic travels with the student so the new tutor does not restart from zero. What an unreasonable arrangement looks like: a package expiring on a date, no replacement without a fresh fee, and prepaid sessions locked to a tutor you have decided against.

This page does not offer a refund tied to a grade outcome, and you should be sceptical of any page that does. Published grade promises either come with refund terms nobody honours or with conditions that make them unreachable, and either way the provider is selling certainty it does not have. No tutor can promise a grade; what can be promised is a named target, written feedback, and an honest statement when the arrangement has stopped producing anything.

Our own practice, stated so you can hold us to it: the trial is free and takes no card details; nothing is prepaid unless you choose a block; a block has an end condition rather than an expiry date; if a match is wrong we change the tutor and the written diagnostic goes with the student; and at every half-term review we say whether to continue, reduce or stop. Saying stop is part of the service, not a loss of business, and the alternative is billing a Dubai family through June for a problem that closed in February.

sections.heading: The Dubai tuition year: when demand and prices move
paragraphs: Tuition pricing in Dubai is seasonal, and knowing the shape of the year is worth real money. Demand has three peaks and two troughs, and both the rate you are quoted and the availability of a scarce specialist move with them. Buying in a trough and holding the slot is a legitimate strategy that almost nobody uses.

The first peak follows the first set of school assessments in the autumn term, when reports arrive and families act. The second and largest follows January mocks, which is when Extended Mathematics and physics specialists disappear and premiums appear. The third is the short, intense window immediately before a May or June series, which is largely triage buying at the worst prices. The troughs are the long summer and the weeks either side of the December break, when availability is widest.

Ramadan sits across this pattern and changes the shape of the week rather than the price. School hours shorten, evenings reorganise around Iftar, and a fixed late-afternoon slot that worked in February often stops working. Families either move to a post-Iftar slot, shift to late-morning weekend sessions, or pause for the month and use the spring break as a block. A provider that cannot accommodate the move will quietly cost you four weeks of continuity, which is a real cost even if no invoice shows it.

The table maps the year as a buying calendar. Use it the way a Dubai family actually can: book scarce specialisms in the trough before you need them, avoid committing to a long package at a peak rate, and plan Ramadan and the long summer explicitly in the contract rather than discovering how they are billed.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor in Dubai, and what that costs them
paragraphs: Permit status belongs in a pricing conversation because it is part of what a parent is buying, and because the market contains a persistent myth that the permit is expensive and therefore baked into high rates. It is not. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years. Any rate justified to you by permit costs is justified by something that does not exist.

Eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists the process as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the official route, and it is the one to point an independent tutor towards rather than around.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published — the ministry did not specify amounts — so treat any figure circulating online with scepticism rather than repeating it. A separate and much heavier regime applies to a business with premises and staff, which requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

Two Dubai-specific consequences for a buyer. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school; that is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it before relying on the exact wording, but no reputable arrangement markets your child's own teacher privately. And no provider in this market, including IB Gram, should be describing itself as regulator-endorsed. We hold no permit, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education or any examination board, and nothing on this site should be read as claiming one.

faqs.question: What is the real hourly cost of IGCSE private tuition in Dubai once extras are added?
faqs.answer: Take the quoted rate and add 10 to 35 per cent for most arrangements. The published bands read in October 2026 run AED 33 to 65 for budget online platforms, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 350 for a visiting tutor including travel, and up to AED 650 for a premium named tutor. On top sit registration or diagnostic fees, material charges, travel inside the hour, community surcharges, cancellation windows that convert absences into paid sessions, peak-season premiums, weekend rates, report fees and the VAT position. Ask for all of them in the same written message as the rate.

faqs.question: Is a twenty-session package genuinely cheaper than paying by the hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Per session, yes, usually by 10 to 20 per cent. In total, only if you use it. A package transfers risk to you in three readable places: whether unused sessions remain yours if you stop, whether it expires on a date or on completion, and whether sessions transfer between siblings or subjects. A discounted package expiring in ninety days, bought in October for a need that closes in January, costs more than paying hourly. Start by the session for three or four weeks, then convert to a block with an end condition rather than an expiry date if the need is genuinely sustained.

faqs.question: Does a Dubai tuition quote include VAT, and how do I get that confirmed?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask for the answer in writing in the same message as the rate. This page will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and we have none to offer; what matters practically is whether the specific figure quoted to you is inclusive or exclusive, which only the provider can tell you. A difference of up to five per cent on a year of weekly sessions is real money. A provider unwilling to put the VAT position in writing alongside the rate has told you something useful about how the rest of the billing will work.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are dearest to tutor in Dubai, and is that about difficulty?
faqs.answer: It is about supply, not difficulty. Arabic as a first language, Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics, Extended and Higher-tier Mathematics, and physics at the top grades all sit at the ceiling of the Dubai band because the pool of people who teach them well is thin. Biology sits lower with the widest supply of the three sciences, which reflects availability rather than weaker tutors. Business Studies, Economics and ICT sit lower still. If your need is one of the scarce subjects, the premium is the market clearing and there is no clever way around it.

faqs.question: Do Dubai tutoring rates rise in the weeks before a May or June series?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically by 10 to 25 per cent, and the scarce specialists disappear entirely. The pattern is predictable: demand rises after autumn assessments, peaks sharply after January mocks, and spikes again in the short window before the papers. Availability is widest in the long summer and the weeks either side of the December break, when rates are at their lowest and tutor choice at its widest. A Dubai family that books a scarce specialism in a trough and holds the slot through the peak pays less and gets a better tutor, which is a straightforward strategy almost nobody uses.

faqs.question: What should I include when I ask several Dubai providers for a quote?
faqs.answer: Seven items in one message: exam board; syllabus code from the entry statement; tier, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher; the exam series you are working towards; the current mark and the target; a recent marked paper if you have one; and three possible weekly slots in Gulf Standard Time with the session length you want. A provider given a subject and a year group has to price the uncertainty and prices it upwards. A precise brief produces precise quotes, which is the only way five quotes become comparable with one another rather than five different products.

faqs.question: What happens to my money if the tutor turns out to be wrong for my child?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the contract you signed, which is why it is worth asking before you need the answer. A reasonable arrangement replaces the tutor without a new registration fee, loses nothing prepaid, and passes the written diagnostic to the new tutor so nothing restarts from zero. An unreasonable one locks prepaid sessions to a tutor you have decided against and charges a fresh fee for a replacement. Raise a mismatch after two sessions rather than enduring a term — roughly one arrangement in six does not work, in every market and at every price point, and it is not a failure.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE in Dubai as a private candidate, and what does entry cost?
faqs.answer: A small number of licensed centres in Dubai accept private candidates, which is the route for a retake or for a subject the school does not offer. Entry fees are set by the centre and the board, not by any tutor, and each centre publishes its own schedule and deadlines. No figure appears on this page because none has been verified from a centre's current schedule, so ask the centre directly and in writing. Confirm the entry deadline in the same message, because in the UAE a private candidate sits the June series or the November series and the entry for either closes months before the first paper - Cambridge's June entries close in the spring, and Pearson's November 2026 papers, which ran to 19 November 2026, were entered well before the autumn term. A late enquiry does not cost a few days; it costs a whole series and six months of waiting.

faqs.question: Is a Dubai tuition centre group class better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: At AED 70 to 150 a student against AED 150 to 300 for one-to-one online, the arithmetic looks obvious and the condition attached is not. A group only works when the students are genuinely at the same point, because the pace is set by the group rather than by your child. In dense apartment communities with large year groups that condition is often met; in low-density villa communities it usually is not. Factor in the second commute on top of the school run, any registration fee and term minimum, and whether written feedback on your child's own work is included at all.

faqs.question: Why is an independent Dubai tutor sometimes more expensive than an agency?
faqs.answer: Because the independent is pricing one person's scarce time while an agency is pricing a pool. An independent with a full timetable in a scarce subject has no reason to discount, and listings in this market run from AED 200 to AED 500 an hour. What the higher independent rate does not usually include is a replacement arrangement if the match fails, written progress reporting, or anyone to escalate to. That is the real trade: a direct relationship at a direct price, with the permit check, the syllabus-code check and the recovery plan all sitting with you.

faqs.question: How much should a Dubai family budget for a full IGCSE year across two subjects?
faqs.answer: At the market mid-band of about AED 220 an hour, two subjects weekly across a thirty-four-week year is roughly AED 15,000 before extras. The same money spent differently buys considerably more: a marked diagnostic, a ten-session block against the named loss patterns, a stop, and an eight-session block before the series comes to roughly AED 4,400. That is the pattern with the best return we see, because the hours sit where the marks are. The worst return is the open weekly slot with no written target, which is the easiest arrangement to sell and the hardest to end.

faqs.question: Are the monthly in-home packages advertised around AED 1,599 good value?
faqs.answer: Published monthly packages in this market include AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits and around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Per hour of teaching those are roughly AED 200 to 225 and AED 100 respectively, so the comparison depends on what the hour contains. Travel is inside the visiting figure whether itemised or not, and a sixty-minute visit that starts late delivers less than sixty minutes of teaching — ask whether the hour starts on arrival or at the agreed time. For scarce subjects the deciding factor is usually not price but which specialists will travel to your community at that hour.

faqs.question: Does paying a higher hourly rate actually move an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. Published Dubai rates for the same described service span fourteenfold, and nobody believes the top tutor is fourteen times as effective. Price tracks scarcity, demand and overhead. Three things do track grade movement: whether the tutor works from the correct syllabus code and the board's own mark scheme, whether a marked script came before the teaching so the hours are aimed, and whether the student completes the work between sessions. Test the first two in the free trial by watching whether the tutor asks for the code and names a loss pattern from the script.

faqs.question: Can we pause during Ramadan and the summer without losing paid sessions?
faqs.answer: That depends on the contract, and it is worth settling before either arrives. Ramadan changes the shape of the week rather than the price: school hours shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so a fixed late-afternoon slot often stops working. Families move to a post-Iftar slot, switch to late-morning weekend sessions, or pause and use the spring break as a block. Our own practice is that holiday and Ramadan weeks are agreed in advance rather than invoiced by default, and a fixed block carries an end condition rather than an expiry date, so pausing does not consume prepaid value.

faqs.question: Should a diagnostic assessment be free, or is paying for one reasonable?
faqs.answer: Both models exist in Dubai and some providers charge AED 100 to 300 for an initial assessment. Paying is not unreasonable where the output is substantial — a marked script against the board's published scheme, the loss patterns named with the marks each costs, and a written tier recommendation you can take to the school. Paying for a twenty-minute conversation that produces a sales quote is unreasonable. Ask what document you receive and whether it is yours to keep regardless of whether you book. Our own written diagnostic and the thirty-minute trial lesson are free, one trial per family, with no card details taken.

dubai/igcse-private-tuition.closingHeading: Send the brief, collect five comparable quotes
dubai/igcse-private-tuition.closingBody: Write one message containing the exam board, the syllabus code, the tier, the series, the current mark, the target and three possible weekly slots in Gulf Standard Time, and send it to us and to anyone else you are considering. You will get back a written diagnostic if you include a marked paper, a free 30-minute trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the subject, and a quote naming that tutor, the session length and everything billed on top including the VAT position. One trial per family, no card details. Dubai lessons run one-to-one over live video, and if the honest answer is a short block rather than a year, that is what the quote will say.

dubai/igcse-private-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below works to one named syllabus and marks against the published scheme rather than from memory. Where a subject is tiered, the tutor states on day one which tier the papers they are preparing for belong to, because Core and Extended reward different answers to the same question.

intro.heading: The question to ask a tutor is not how experienced they are, it is what they can show you
paragraphs: Most tutoring conversations in Dubai start in the wrong place. A parent asks about qualifications and years of experience, gets reassuring answers, books a block of ten hours, and then has no way to tell in week six whether the money is working. Experience is a weak predictor. What a tutor produces each week is a strong one, and it can be inspected by a parent with no subject knowledge at all.

This page is built on that idea. An IGCSE private tutor working properly generates artefacts: a marked script with annotations tied to the mark scheme, a named error with a count attached, a timed paper with the time stamps written on it, a draft with comments that ask questions rather than supply answers. Those things either exist after three sessions or they do not. If they do not, no amount of rapport explains the gap.

The reason this matters more at IGCSE than at almost any other stage is that IGCSE marks are unusually legible. Every paper is marked against a published scheme. Every command word has an agreed meaning. "State" takes one line, "describe" takes the what, "explain" takes the why, and "suggest" takes a reasoned answer to a situation the examiner has not seen before. A specialist reading your child's script can sort fourteen lost marks into categories in minutes and tell you which three are cheapest to recover. A generalist tells you the child needs to revise more.

There is a second reason evidence beats reputation in this particular market. Dubai has 227 private schools and 387,441 private-school pupils as of 2024-25, with 37% of that enrolment on a UK curriculum, so the IGCSE cohort here is large and the tutoring supply that serves it is uneven. Plenty of people in this city will teach maths competently. Far fewer can read a marked Paper 4 and tell you that nine of the fourteen lost marks were technique and process, which recover in weeks, while only three sat in content, which takes months. The two tutors look identical on a profile page and produce completely different terms.

IB Gram delivers this as live one-to-one video tuition on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a Dubai address; home visits are something we offer only in India. For evidence-led work the online format is actively better, not a compromise: the script sits on a shared screen, annotated live, with both the answer and the mark scheme visible at once. That is nearer to how an examiner reads a paper than two people leaning over one piece of A4.

Below is the machinery. How a marked script gets read, which command words cost Dubai cohorts the most marks, what a twelve-week ledger looks like, what a predicted grade actually rests on, where the line sits on coursework feedback, what the market charges in dirhams and which published source says so, and what the evidence looks like when the right decision is to change tutor or stop. Nothing on this page promises a grade, because no tutor controls one.

dubai/igcse-private-tutor.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different at each stage. In Key Stage 3 it is fluency data; across IGCSE it is marks against a scheme; after Year 11 it is whether the grade cleared a published threshold. A tutor should be able to say which of the three they are producing.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the entries are set
programmes.description: The evidence that matters here is fluency, measured rather than described. Timed arithmetic and algebra checks, a reading-comprehension score, and a written piece marked for structure. These produce a baseline that the Year 9 set placement can be argued against later, which is the only stage at which a tier decision can be influenced cheaply.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools take pupils in mid-Key Stage from CBSE, American and other systems most years. A child arriving from CBSE Year 8 has usually met more algebra and fewer extended written answers. Three timed baseline tasks in the first fortnight tell you which of those two gaps you are dealing with, instead of a term of impressions.

programmes.name: Years 10 and 11, the two examined years
programmes.description: Evidence becomes marks. Each paper is marked against the board's published scheme, so a lost mark has a documented reason. A tutor's weekly output across these two years should be a marked question, a running error count, and periodically a full paper sat to time. Mock results are useful only when the raw mark is recorded alongside the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is a two-board city, with Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel entries sitting in the same friendship group. Evidence is board-specific: a mark scheme for Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 does not describe Pearson 4MA1 Paper 2. Any tutor producing evidence against the wrong scheme is producing a convincing-looking document that means nothing.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma entry after Year 11
programmes.description: The evidence here is the published threshold. Dubai sixth forms set subject-level entry criteria, commonly a 6 or B in the same subject for A Level and a spread of strong grades plus writing stamina for the IB Diploma. Tuition in Year 11 should be aimed at a stated number rather than at general improvement, because the number is what the admissions spreadsheet reads.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Families planning a UAE university route should check the five counted subjects before Year 11 entries are locked.

dubai/igcse-private-tutor.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, what evidence of progress actually looks like. A tutor who cannot name the artefact they produce in a subject is unlikely to be producing one.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The artefact is a marked Paper 4 with method marks circled separately from answer marks. The useful count is process errors: rounding mid-calculation, missing units, sign slips. Three papers with a tally produce a number that a fifteen-year-old will argue with far less than they argue with advice.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Evidence here is a circuit question marked twice, before and after a fortnight of potential-divider work. Electricity and magnetism are where the marks sit and where the recall decays, so a cold retest two weeks later is the only honest check that teaching landed.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and electrolysis half-equations are countable. The artefact is a sheet of ten equations with balanced charges checked, dated, and repeated cold. Progress is the drop in unbalanced equations, not the student's reported confidence.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Almost all recoverable marks are vocabulary precision. Evidence is the student's own sentence rewritten next to the mark-scheme wording, kept and compared a month later. Water potential, enzyme graph description and genetics notation are the three reliable sources of lost marks.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990, 0510 second language)
subjects.description: The summary task and directed writing are both marked against clear criteria, which makes them the most auditable components on the timetable. Evidence is a summary scored twice: once as written, once after the lifting of phrasing has been removed.

subjects.name: English Literature (Cambridge 0475 / 0992)
subjects.description: Evidence is an essay plan next to the band descriptors, with the quotations counted. Candidates who write everything they know about a character can see the problem immediately when the plan is scored against the question actually set.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study evaluation marks are the ones routinely left unclaimed. The artefact is an answer with the stimulus quotations highlighted and the justified recommendation marked separately, so the student sees which half of the answer earned the band.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the explicit link from diagram to argument. Evidence is a marked diagram with axis labels and shifts checked, then the same diagram reproduced from blank a week later, which is where the real retention gap shows.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / 0984)
subjects.description: Trace tables are self-marking, which makes them ideal evidence. A student who completes a trace table correctly has demonstrably understood the algorithm. Hexadecimal and two's complement conversions are mechanical and should reach near-perfect accuracy under timed conditions.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 in stronger Dubai sets. Evidence is notation discipline: calculus written correctly, not just answered correctly. The common failure is treating 0606 as harder 0580, and a marked script makes that visible in one session.

modes.description: One 60-minute session a week, structured the same way every time: ten minutes reviewing the marked work set last week, thirty minutes on the error currently being tracked, twenty minutes on the school's live topic. The record builds slowly and reliably, and after six weeks there is enough data to say whether the approach is working.

The unit of work becomes a whole paper rather than a topic: sat to time, marked against the published scheme, then taken apart question by question with the losses sorted into technique, process, timing and content. Evidence accumulates fast enough to redirect the plan mid-block.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE private tutor in Dubai should be able to show you after three sessions
paragraphs: After three sessions with an IGCSE private tutor in Dubai you should hold four things. A marked piece of your child's work with annotations that reference the mark scheme. A named error, stated specifically enough to count. A number: how often that error occurred across the work seen so far. And a sentence about what happens next, in which the error is the subject rather than the child's attitude.

If those four things exist, the tuition is auditable. You do not need to understand chemistry to look at a sheet that says "unbalanced ionic equations: 7 of 10 in week one, 4 of 10 in week three" and know what is going on. If they do not exist, you are buying company. Pleasant company, often, and sometimes useful for confidence, but not something that can be shown to have moved marks.

The reason tutors avoid this is that it creates accountability in both directions. A tracked count that does not fall after four weeks is an argument the tutor has to answer. Most will prefer to report that your child is improving in confidence, which may even be true, and which cannot be checked. Our position is that the count gets shown to the parent whether it moved or not, and a flat count triggers a change in approach rather than a reassurance.

A note on what three sessions is not enough for. It is not enough to move a grade, and anyone presenting it that way is overselling. Genuine content gaps need six to ten sessions per significant topic. Three sessions is enough to produce a diagnosis you can trust and to see whether your child actually talks to this tutor, which are the two things that should be settled before you commit money to a block.
bullets: A marked script with scheme-referenced annotations, not a grade and a sentence
One error named precisely enough to be counted
The count itself, across all work seen so far
A next step whose subject is the error, not the child's effort

sections.heading: Reading a marked script: command words and the marks hiding behind them
paragraphs: The single most common reason a Dubai IGCSE candidate who knows the material scores below their understanding is that they answer a different question from the one the command word asked. This is not a vague risk. It is countable, it is visible on any marked script, and it is the cheapest category of mark to recover because no new content has to be learned.

Command words are specified. "State" or "give" wants a short factual answer with no reasoning; writing a paragraph wastes time without adding marks. "Describe" wants what happens, in order. "Explain" wants why, and a description scores nothing against an explain mark scheme no matter how accurate it is. "Suggest" signals an unfamiliar context and is marked on reasoning rather than recall, which is why candidates who leave it blank are leaving the most forgiving marks on the paper. "Calculate" wants working, because the method marks are awarded before the answer is reached.

The session technique is simple and it works on fifteen-year-olds. Put the student's own answer on one side of the screen and the published mark scheme on the other. Ask them to award themselves the marks. Nearly every student is stricter than the examiner on content and far more generous than the examiner on form. Watching themselves fail to award a mark they thought they had earned does more in ten minutes than a term of being told to read the question carefully.

This is also where board differences bite. A Cambridge mark scheme and a Pearson mark scheme for the same topic credit different wording, and the number of marks per question differs. A tutor marking Pearson work against a Cambridge scheme produces a document that looks like evidence and is not. Establishing the board before the first marking exercise is not administrative tidiness; it determines whether the evidence means anything.
