sections.heading: The first session, and how a mock paper gets taken apart
paragraphs: A first session that teaches content is a wasted session. Nobody yet knows which content to teach. The first hour reads evidence, and the most useful evidence is the most recent mock with the marks on it. If the script is not available, we set a past paper and mark it ourselves before any teaching happens, because a plan built on a report card grade is a plan built on a summary of a summary.

The reading happens in a fixed order. First, total marks lost and where on the paper they sit, because a cluster at the end is a timing problem rather than a knowledge problem. Second, each lost mark gets a category: technique, process, timing or content. Third, the categories get a mark total. Fourth, the totals get ranked. The resulting list is the plan, in order, and it frequently surprises the family because the topic they were worried about is rarely the one costing the most marks.

A worked example from a typical 0580 Extended Paper 4 script. Fourteen marks lost: five to rounding and unit errors spread across the paper, four to two blank questions in the final section, three to a genuinely unlearned topic, and two to method marks forfeited by writing only answers. The family had asked for help with the unlearned topic, which is worth three marks. Process and timing together are worth nine, and both respond faster. Starting with the unlearned topic would have felt responsive and returned the least.

The output of the first session is written, goes to the parent, and is short: the ranked category list with mark totals, the single error we will track first, a target count, and the fortnight by which we expect it to move. Everything after that is execution against a document you can check. If a tutor cannot produce that document after reading a script, the diagnosis did not happen.
bullets: Marked script read before any content is taught
Every lost mark assigned to technique, process, timing or content
Categories ranked by marks available, not by parental concern
A written one-page diagnosis with a target count and a review date

sections.heading: Twelve weeks, measured: the ledger a Dubai parent can audit
paragraphs: A term of tuition should leave a document behind. Not a folder of worksheets, a ledger: what was marked each week, what the tracked count was, and what changed. The point of writing it down is that memory is kind to tuition. Everyone remembers the session where something clicked. Nobody remembers the four weeks where a count sat still.

The shape below is what a maths or science term typically looks like. Weeks one to two diagnose and set the baseline. Weeks three to six attack the highest-value error category, usually process or technique, because those return marks fastest. Weeks seven to nine move to content gaps, which are slower. Weeks ten to twelve run full timed papers, which test whether the earlier gains survive under pressure. They often do not at first, which is exactly why that block exists.

What a parent does with the ledger is ask one question every fortnight: did the number move. If it did, continue. If it did not, the conversation is about why, and the honest answers are a narrow set. The error was misdiagnosed. The independent work between sessions is not happening. The tutor's explanation is not landing with this particular child. Or the gap is genuinely content-shaped and needs more weeks than estimated. Each of those has a different response, and none of them is "keep going and hope".

The ledger also solves a problem families do not anticipate: tutor changes. Tutors move cities, change jobs, and occasionally turn out to be the wrong fit in week five. When the record exists, the next tutor starts from the diagnosis rather than redoing it, which saves two to three sessions. We keep the record with the family's file and hand it over on request, and we delete marked work when asked.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, mocks and raw marks: what the school's number rests on
paragraphs: A predicted grade is a professional judgement, not a measurement, and it is produced under constraints parents rarely see. Dubai schools generate them from internal assessment data, set placement and teacher judgement, usually in a short window and for a whole cohort at once. They are frequently accurate. When they are not, the family needs to know what evidence sits underneath before challenging anything.

The question that cuts through is about raw marks. A mock grade is a raw mark converted using some set of grade boundaries, and boundaries are set per series, per paper, after the exam. A mock marked against last year's boundaries produces an indicative grade, not a prediction. So the useful request to a head of department is not "can the prediction change", it is "what raw mark did my child score, out of what total, and which series boundaries were applied". That is a factual question with a factual answer.

Raw marks also make progress legible in a way grades do not. A child who moves from 94 to 112 out of 130 has gained eighteen marks and may still be sitting in the same grade band, which looks like no progress on a report card and is in fact substantial. The reverse happens too: a one-mark move can cross a boundary and flatter a term of work that achieved very little. Tracking marks protects a family from both illusions.

For forecast grades there is a hard date in the calendar, and it belongs to whichever series your child is in. A UAE candidate sits June or November, so for a June candidate the sequence is an entry closing in the spring, a forecast submitted before the series opens, and papers in June; your examinations officer can give you the exact submission date for that series. The implication is the same either way: the conversation about a prediction belongs in the autumn term, while there is still a term of evidence left to gather. By the time the forecast is submitted, the evidence that would have changed it needed to already exist.

sections.heading: Coursework and assignment drafts: what feedback may do, and where it stops
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry a component the student produces outside an exam hall. Wherever that exists, there is a line, and the line is not negotiable. A tutor may teach the skills the component needs, explain the assessment criteria in plain language, discuss the student's chosen approach, question their reasoning, and respond to a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not produce assessed material, rewrite a draft into a submittable state, or supply sentences for a student to hand in.

The practical test we use is whether the feedback could be read aloud to the student's teacher without anybody being uncomfortable. "Your second paragraph asserts a conclusion your data does not support; which figure would you need to show to support it?" passes. Handing over a corrected paragraph does not. The first builds the skill the criteria are actually assessing. The second transfers the mark to the tutor and exposes the student to a malpractice finding they, not the tutor, will carry.

This market has a specific problem that makes the boundary worth stating loudly. One site competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. Families encountering that offer sometimes assume it is normal and that everyone does a version of it quietly. They should not. It is an academic-integrity breach, it is the kind of thing boards investigate, and the student is the one who faces the consequence.

Our process makes the boundary auditable rather than merely asserted. Feedback is logged, so the trail of advice can be read in order. Sessions on a coursework component are scheduled against the school's internal deadlines so the work is produced over time rather than assembled at the end. And the boundary is written down and sent to the parent before the first draft session, because the moment to agree it is before anyone is under deadline pressure.

sections.heading: What a private tutor costs in Dubai, and what the extra dirhams actually buy
paragraphs: The Dubai market publishes rates unevenly, so here are the bands with their sources, as of October 2026. Budget online tutoring advertises from AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180-500 inclusive of travel, per Bestimate at 180-350 and independent home tutors at 200-500.

Above that, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named or examiner-badged tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650. Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end, 600-1,200 mid-range and 1,000-2,000 plus for specialist exam-year work.

What the extra dirhams buy, in evidence terms, is mark-scheme literacy. A tutor at the bottom of the range usually knows the subject and not the scheme, which means they can explain content and cannot tell you that nine of fourteen lost marks were technique. That is a real distinction and it is most of the price gap. The upper bands exist because syllabus-specific marking experience is scarce, and scarcity in a small market prices accordingly.

A note on the in-home premium. The AED 180-500 band for visits is partly a travel bill, and travel is the one component of a tutoring fee that produces no teaching. IB Gram prices against the online bands rather than the in-home bands because nobody is driving anywhere. We do not publish a rate card on this page: the figure depends on subject scarcity, tier and session length, and the consultation after the free first lesson is where you get it. Any page quoting you a specific dirham figure as our price is not ours.

sections.heading: KHDA inspection bands, and what a school report tells you about tuition
paragraphs: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it inspects private schools on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The report is public, it is detailed, and most families read only the headline band. The useful part sits further in, in the subject-level and phase-level judgements, because a school can be Very Good overall and have an inconsistent department in exactly the subject your child is struggling with.

That is the connection to tuition, and it is a practical one. If the inspection report flags attainment in a subject as acceptable while the rest of the school sits higher, a child in that subject is being taught in a department under scrutiny. Tuition in that subject is more likely to be worth the money than tuition in a subject where the department is strong and the child's problem is attitude or organisation.

The band also tells you something about how to read the school's own predicted grades. A department with inconsistent internal assessment produces predictions with wider error bars, which makes raw marks and external past-paper evidence more valuable. A strong department's prediction is usually well calibrated, and a parent who disputes it with a tutor's opinion rather than with marks will get nowhere, correctly.

One thing an inspection band is not is a statement about any individual child or any tutor. We name KHDA here because it is the regulator and because its reports are a free, public, well-evidenced source that families underuse. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, endorsed or licensed by KHDA, holds no permit from it, and operates no premises in the UAE. An operation with premises here would require a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific thing issued to training institutes, and we do not hold one or claim to.

sections.heading: When the evidence says change the tutor, change the plan, or stop
paragraphs: An evidence-led arrangement has to be willing to produce an unwelcome answer, or it is not evidence-led. The count either moved or it did not, and when it has not moved after four to six weeks of consistent work there are only a few honest explanations. Confronting them is cheaper in week six than in month five.

The first is misdiagnosis. The error being tracked was not the one costing the marks, which happens most often when a family's stated concern overrode the ranked list. The fix is re-reading the script and re-ranking, and it costs one session. The second is independent work not happening between sessions, which no amount of tutoring hours compensates for; a child who does nothing for six days and sits a lesson on the seventh will plateau. That is a scheduling and expectation conversation, not a teaching one.

The third is personal fit, and it is more common than the industry admits. A tutor can be technically excellent and simply not land with a particular fifteen-year-old. The signal is a student who answers in monosyllables, does not bring questions, and performs better on independent work than in sessions. When we see that, we propose a different tutor and the ledger transfers, so nothing is restarted from zero.

The fourth answer is the one nobody advertises: sometimes the right decision is to stop. A child carrying nine subjects, a coursework backlog and three tuition slots a week is not short of teaching. Dropping a session and sleeping is occasionally the intervention with the highest return. We would rather say that and keep a family's trust than sell hours into a timetable that is already full. If a subject's marks are genuinely secure, the honest recommendation is to spend the money elsewhere or not at all.

process.title: Send the marked script, not the report
process.description: The most recent paper with the marks and annotations on it is worth more than a term of grades. If none exists, the first task is a set past paper, marked by us against the published scheme, before any teaching is planned. A diagnosis built on a report card is a summary of a summary.

process.title: Confirm board, code, tier and scale from school documents
process.description: Cambridge or Pearson, which syllabus code, Core or Extended, A*-G or 9-1. Dubai runs both boards inside the same neighbourhood, and evidence marked against the wrong scheme looks convincing and means nothing. We take these four facts from the school's own paperwork.

process.title: Free first lesson, then a written diagnosis
process.description: A full session with the proposed tutor at no cost, with no card details needed to book. Afterwards you receive the ranked category list with mark totals, the first error to be tracked, a target count and the review date. That page is the contract the rest of the term is measured against.

process.title: Weekly marked work, fortnightly count review
process.description: Every session returns a marked question and updates the count. Every two weeks the count is compared with the previous fortnight and sent to you whether it improved or not. A flat count is information, and it changes the plan rather than producing a reassuring email.

process.title: Decide at the review point
process.description: At week six and week twelve there is a decision, taken from the ledger: continue, change approach, change tutor, or stop. We put the recommendation in writing with the numbers that support it, including when the recommendation is that further sessions in this subject are not the best use of your money.

whyPoints.title: Marking against the published scheme, every week
whyPoints.description: Work is marked to the board's own scheme rather than from a tutor's memory of what good looks like. That is what makes a lost mark explainable, and it is the capability that separates a subject-knowledgeable tutor from one who can tell you which fourteen marks went where.

whyPoints.title: One error, counted, until it stops
whyPoints.description: Fortnightly counts rather than termly impressions. A student who sees their own rounding-error tally fall from seven to two argues with it far less than with advice, and a parent who sees a flat tally has grounds to ask for a change of approach without any subject knowledge.

whyPoints.title: The specialist you need, not the one within driving distance
whyPoints.description: Live video means a family in Mirdif and a family in Dubai Hills choose from the same specialists. Additional Mathematics 0606 and top-band Computer Science 0478 are scarce in any single catchment and reachable from all of them, which is the practical advantage of not sending anyone anywhere.

whyPoints.title: A boundary on coursework we put in writing first
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria explanation, questions and feedback on the student's own draft. Not replacement text, not a rewrite to submission standard. One competitor in this market sells finished Internal Assessments; the student carries that risk, not the seller, which is why we set the line before the deadline pressure starts.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed, no figures about ourselves
whyPoints.description: Market rates carry the provider and the date. Regulator rules carry the authority. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no average grade gain and no star rating, because we cannot show you the underlying data for any of them and a number without its method is worth nothing.

whyPoints.title: Records that transfer and delete on request
whyPoints.description: The diagnosis is the expensive part of tuition and it should not be redone when a tutor changes. The ledger stays with your file and moves to the next tutor on request. Marked work is kept only while it is useful to the plan and deleted when you ask.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE private tutor in Dubai hand over after the first three sessions?
faqs.answer: Four things. A marked piece of your child's work with annotations tied to the published mark scheme. One error named precisely enough to count, such as unbalanced ionic equations or rounding mid-calculation. The count of that error across the work seen so far. And a next step whose subject is the error rather than the child's effort. Those four exist after three sessions or they do not. Three sessions is not long enough to move a grade, and anyone implying otherwise is overselling, but it is long enough to produce a diagnosis you can check.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but the marks do not show it. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Usually command words. IGCSE schemes credit specific forms of answer, and a correct description scores nothing against an explain mark. "State" wants one line, "explain" wants a causal link, "suggest" wants reasoning about an unfamiliar context, and "calculate" wants working because method marks come before the answer. The fastest diagnostic is to put your child's answer beside the mark scheme and ask them to award their own marks. Most students are stricter than the examiner on content and far more generous on form, and seeing that happen is more persuasive than being told.

faqs.question: How do I check a mock grade rather than just accepting it?
faqs.answer: Ask for the raw mark and the boundaries. A mock grade is a raw mark converted using some set of grade boundaries, and boundaries are set per series after the exam, so a mock marked against last year's boundaries gives an indicative grade rather than a prediction. The precise request is: what mark did my child score, out of what total, on which paper, and which series boundaries were applied. Raw marks also show progress a grade band can hide, since eighteen extra marks can look like no movement on a report card.

faqs.question: Can tuition change a predicted grade, and when is it too late to try?
faqs.answer: Tuition cannot change a prediction; evidence can, and the timing is tight. Cambridge publishes a forecast-grade submission date for each series, and for a June candidate in the UAE that falls after the spring entry deadline and before the papers, while a November candidate's forecast goes in during the autumn. For either series, the evidence that would revise a judgement has to exist before the school submits, which in practice makes the autumn term the right one for this conversation. The evidence that works is marked work at the target standard under timed conditions, handed to the department, not a letter explaining that your child is trying hard.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do with my child's coursework draft?
faqs.answer: Teach the skills, explain the criteria in plain words, discuss the approach, question the reasoning, and respond to what the student has written. Not produce assessed material, not rewrite a draft to submission standard, and not supply sentences to be handed in. Our working test is whether the feedback could be read aloud to the class teacher without discomfort. "Your conclusion asserts more than your data supports; which figure would you need?" passes that test. A corrected paragraph does not, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Is it normal for tutoring sites in Dubai to offer finished assessments?
faqs.answer: It happens, and it is not normal practice; it is an integrity breach. At least one site competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Boards investigate this, and the student carries the consequence rather than the seller. If any provider offers to supply work for submission, that is the point to stop the conversation. We put the boundary in writing before the first draft session and log every comment, so the sequence of advice given can be read in order by anyone who asks.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for an evidence-led IGCSE tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market bands as of October 2026 put budget online tutoring at AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The practical difference along that scale is mark-scheme literacy rather than subject knowledge. Those are the providers' own figures, not ours; our rate depends on subject scarcity and tier and comes after the free first lesson.

faqs.question: Why do in-home rates in Dubai sit so much higher than online ones?
faqs.answer: Travel is inside the fee. Published in-home bands run AED 180-500 an hour, per Bestimate at 180-350 and independent tutors at 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor online. The difference is largely a car on Al Khail Road, which produces no teaching. It also shrinks the pool to whoever will make the drive at 5pm, which is how a family needing Cambridge 0620 Extended ends up with a general science graduate. We price against the online bands because nobody is driving anywhere.

faqs.question: How does a KHDA inspection report help me decide about tuition?
faqs.answer: Read past the headline band to the subject and phase judgements. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and a school can sit at Very Good overall while one department is flagged as inconsistent. If that department teaches the subject your child is struggling in, tuition there is more likely to pay than in a subject where the department is strong and the real problem is organisation. The reports are public and free, and most families use only the first page.

faqs.question: What do I do if the tracked count has not moved in six weeks?
faqs.answer: Treat it as information and ask for a review. There are four honest explanations and each has a different fix. The error was misdiagnosed, which costs one session to re-rank. Independent work is not happening between sessions, which is a scheduling conversation rather than a teaching one. The tutor is not landing with this particular child, in which case we propose someone else and the ledger transfers. Or the gap is content-shaped and needs more weeks than estimated. The wrong response is another month of the same with encouragement.

faqs.question: Will we have to start from scratch if we change tutor?
faqs.answer: No, provided the record exists. The diagnosis is the expensive part of tuition, typically two or three sessions of reading scripts and ranking error categories. We keep the ledger with your family's file, so a new tutor opens with the ranked list, the tracked error and the count history rather than rebuilding it. That usually saves two to three sessions. Marked work is held only while it is useful to the plan, and we delete it when you ask, including the scripts and the session notes.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor actually see enough to mark my child's work properly?
faqs.answer: More than in a shared-desk arrangement, in practice. The script sits on screen with the mark scheme next to it, annotated live, so both the answer and the criteria are visible to tutor and student at once. Written work is photographed or shared before the session and marked beforehand, which means session time goes on the conversation rather than on reading. The part online cannot do is handle apparatus, which belongs to the school; we plan around the school's practical schedule rather than pretending to replace it.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 and nothing is wrong yet. Is tuition premature?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the cheapest point to act, for a specific reason: tier entries are not locked. In tiered Cambridge subjects a Core entry caps the achievable grade, and the decision usually follows set placement rather than an explicit conversation. Evidence produced in Year 10, meaning Extended-standard work under timed conditions, is the argument that moves a department before final entries close. Waiting until a Year 11 mock looks wrong means arguing after the window. A diagnostic in Year 10 is also genuinely allowed to conclude that nothing needs doing.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two subjects for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking rather than assuming. Maths and physics overlap enough that one specialist often covers both well, and the shared algebra and graph-work diagnosis saves time. Chemistry and biology are less interchangeable than families expect, because the recoverable marks sit in different places: calculation discipline in one, vocabulary precision in the other. We would rather put two specialists on two subjects than stretch one tutor into a subject where they can explain the content but not the mark scheme.

faqs.question: What does the free first IGCSE lesson include, and what is the catch?
faqs.answer: A full-length session with the proposed tutor, working on real questions from your child's own board and tier, followed by a written diagnosis if a marked script was supplied. No card details are needed to book it and there is no obligation afterwards. The condition is simply that it is one lesson per family, with the tutor we propose. The purpose is to test two things money should not be spent discovering later: whether your child talks to this adult, and whether the tutor can read a script.

dubai/igcse-private-tutor.closingHeading: Send a marked paper and see what comes back
dubai/igcse-private-tutor.closingBody: The fastest way to judge any tutor, including ours, is to hand over a marked script and read what they produce from it. Send the last paper your child sat with the marks on it, tell us the board, syllabus code and tier, and take the free first lesson with the specialist we propose. Afterwards you get one page: the ranked list of where the marks went, which category each loss falls into, the first error we would track, and the fortnight by which we expect its count to fall. If that page does not convince you, nothing has been spent. If the tutor is not right for your child, say so and we propose someone else.

dubai/igcse-resit-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work with resit candidates, which is diagnostic work rather than course teaching. Each starts from the component breakdown and the board's own mark scheme, and each marks written work so progress is visible rather than asserted.

intro.heading: A resit plan stands on two documents
paragraphs: The first document is the statement of results broken down by component. A grade alone tells you almost nothing about whether a resit will move it. A breakdown tells you which paper lost the marks, how far below the boundary the candidate sat, and whether the shortfall was spread evenly or concentrated in one component. Those three facts decide whether a resit is a five-week job, a five-month job, or the wrong instrument altogether. Your school's examinations officer can obtain the breakdown, and it is the first thing to ask for rather than the second.

The second document is written confirmation of the entry route. A resit has to be entered through a school or a registered examination centre, and not every Dubai school will enter a former student. Several centres in the emirate accept private candidates, and the practical questions are which boards they offer, whether they can accommodate a subject with a practical or coursework component, and what the entry deadline is. Verify all of that directly with the centre, because availability and board coverage differ and change.

Once both documents exist, the work is narrow. Resit candidates rarely need a whole course retaught. They need the specific marks the breakdown identified, recovered through marked practice on the board's own papers. The habit this page argues for is evidencing that movement month by month: a marked paper at the start, a marked paper in the middle, a marked paper near the end, with the mark on each recorded. A resit plan without that trail is a plan running on hope.

Dubai adds two practical factors. The June series is the main UAE sitting and November is the resit route, with results from a November series reaching students in the following January: Pearson's record shows November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. That timing matters if a sixth-form place or a Ministry of Education equivalency submission depends on the grade, because the gap between sitting and result is months rather than weeks. Confirm the current series timetable from the board's own page rather than from any restated date.

One more decision belongs at the start, which is how many subjects go into the plan. Most resit candidates are carrying something else at the same time: a sixth-form timetable, a Diploma, or a job. Spreading the available hours across three subjects reliably produces no visible movement in any of them, while one subject chosen on the breakdown usually moves. The criterion is recoverable marks per hour, not which grade looks worst on the certificate.

All UAE sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For resit candidates the format earns its place twice: the candidate is often no longer on a school timetable and has daytime availability, and the specialist needed is defined by a syllabus code rather than by proximity.

dubai/igcse-resit-tutor.programmesIntro: A resit decision looks different depending on what the grade is needed for. Here is how each stage treats it.

programmes.name: Year 11 candidates resitting
programmes.description: Students still in school who sat in June and want to improve in November. Usually the simplest route, because the school is already the registering centre and the subject teacher can supply mark schemes and the component breakdown without difficulty.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary in how readily they enter current students for a November resit alongside starting sixth form, and some discourage it on workload grounds. Ask the examinations officer early, because the entry deadline for the November series falls well before the papers and the sixth-form term will already be underway.

programmes.name: Sixth-form students resitting
programmes.description: Candidates already in A Level or Diploma courses who need a specific IGCSE grade for a subject prerequisite, a university requirement or an equivalency submission. The constraint is time: the resit competes with a full post-16 timetable.
programmes.countryNote: This is the most common Dubai resit case we see, and the one where narrowing matters most. A Year 12 student carrying three A Levels or six Diploma subjects cannot resit three IGCSEs well. One subject, chosen because the breakdown shows recoverable marks, is the plan that works.

programmes.name: Private candidates
programmes.description: Candidates entering independently through a registered examination centre rather than through a school. The route exists in Dubai, and the questions are which boards a centre offers, whether practical or coursework components can be accommodated, and what the deadlines are.
programmes.countryNote: Private entry is also the route used by adults completing the five subjects required for a Ministry of Education equivalency submission on the British track. Centres differ in board coverage, so confirm with the centre directly before planning around a particular syllabus code.

programmes.name: Resitting for equivalency
programmes.description: As reported in July 2026, the British track for Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels.
programmes.countryNote: A candidate short of the five-subject count is in a different position from one chasing a high grade: the target is a pass rather than a top band, which usually means a much shorter plan. Equivalency is a Ministry process and no tutoring provider performs, influences or guarantees it. Verify your own requirements through the official channel.

dubai/igcse-resit-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below is what a November run can realistically achieve in each subject, with the codes to confirm on the entry.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Moves well where the breakdown shows unwritten method or blank final questions. A candidate who was weak across algebra and geometry needs most of a course, which a single term rarely delivers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and electrolysis are the recoverable marks. Organic chemistry is often taught late in a school course, so a June candidate may have met it thinly, which a resit run can genuinely fix.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit and prefix discipline and equation selection respond quickly. Electricity is the usual topic gap. Confirm with the centre how the practical or alternative-to-practical component is handled for a resit.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Among the strongest resit subjects, because most marks are lost to command-term shape rather than missing content. Learning the required answer structures moves a grade without new material.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Marks come back through precise quotation and analysis of effect, and through controlled register in directed writing. Six to ten weeks of marked timed responses is the usual shape.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: The summary task and the listening paper are where the marks sit. Word limits and own-words requirements are applied strictly, and candidates lose marks for content they did understand.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Fast movers in a resit window. A supported judgement in the evaluation question and accurate diagrams between them account for most of the recoverable marks.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are learnable in a few weeks. Candidates who code competently often lose marks purely on the format the mark scheme requires.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: A harder resit because the questions are long and interdependent, so partial method earns little. Realistic only where the breakdown shows the content was broadly secure.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Note that they are excluded from the five subjects counted for equivalency on the British track.

dubai/igcse-resit-tutor.regionsIntro: Resit candidates are often between institutions or carrying a post-16 timetable. Here is how that looks across the communities we hear from.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Established British schools, so most candidates here resit through their own school. The examinations officer can usually supply the component breakdown within days.

regions.name: Al Barsha and The Greens

sections.heading: What the component breakdown proves
paragraphs: A grade is a summary. The breakdown is the evidence, and it answers the only question that matters before entering a resit: how many marks are actually recoverable. A candidate three marks below a boundary with one weak paper and two strong ones is a different proposition from a candidate thirty marks below with the shortfall spread evenly, and the two should not buy the same plan.

Read it in three passes. First, the distance to the boundary, which tells you the size of the job in marks rather than in feelings. Second, the distribution across papers, which tells you where the job is. Third, where available, the pattern within a paper: blank questions indicate pacing or coverage, low marks on long questions indicate technique, and uniformly middling marks indicate shallow knowledge across the syllabus.

That third reading is the one that changes plans. Blank final questions on a Mathematics paper usually mean a pacing problem, which is weeks of timed practice rather than a term of teaching. Correct content scoring half marks in Biology means command terms, which is faster still. Uniformly middling marks across every topic is the expensive case, because it means the content was never secure and a term may not be enough.

The table below is how we present the reading back to a family. It is deliberately quantitative, because a resit decision made on a feeling about how June went is the decision most likely to waste a term. Ask the examinations officer for the breakdown before any tutoring conversation; it is a routine request and it usually arrives within days.

sections.heading: Where to sit a resit in Dubai
paragraphs: No plan survives without an entry. A resit is entered through a school or a registered examination centre, and the candidate's original school is the first place to ask. Some Dubai schools enter former students routinely and others decline, usually on capacity grounds, so get the answer in writing rather than assuming. Where the school declines, the examinations officer can normally describe the route through another centre.

Several centres in Dubai accept private candidates, and the questions to ask are specific. Which boards do they offer, because Cambridge and Pearson coverage differs by centre. Can they accommodate a subject with a practical or a coursework component, which is the constraint that most often rules a subject out for a private candidate. What is the entry deadline, which sits well before the papers. And what the total entry cost is, which the centre quotes and which we do not publish because it varies and an invented figure would mislead.

The practical-component question deserves emphasis. For a science resit, how the practical element is assessed depends on the board and the centre: Cambridge offers a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on the centre, and Pearson assesses practical skills within its written papers. A private candidate needs to know which applies before committing, because the answer changes both the revision plan and whether the subject can be sat at that centre at all.

Two further checks are worth making in the same conversation. Confirm the syllabus code the centre will enter, since it may differ from the one the candidate studied, and confirm which grading scale results are reported on, because UAE centres use both A* to G and 9 to 1. Neither question is difficult and both change what the candidate should be revising.

sections.heading: The November series counted backwards
paragraphs: A resit run is short, so the calendar does most of the work. Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only and has no application to a UAE candidate. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For a UAE resit the November series is the route, and the entry deadline sits months before the papers.

Pearson's published record shows the shape of the tail clearly. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so plan from the live official timetable rather than from any restatement, including this page's.

That January results date is the most consequential fact on this page for Dubai families. If a sixth-form place, a university condition or a Ministry equivalency submission depends on the resit grade, the decision-maker will not see it until the new year. Check with the institution or the authority whether that timing works before entering, because a grade that arrives after a deadline has no value to the thing it was meant to achieve.

One Cambridge administrative detail matters too. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct zone version of the timetable, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The centre handles this; the candidate's job is to work from the timetable the centre issues.

sections.heading: Evidencing grade movement month by month
paragraphs: The argument of this page is that a resit plan should be auditable. A candidate who cannot show, in marks, that the work is landing is a candidate whose family will discover in November whether the term was worth it. That is avoidable: papers are available, mark schemes exist, and a marked paper produces a number.

The method is simple and we use it on every resit run. A full paper is sat under timed conditions in the first fortnight, marked against the board's scheme, and the mark recorded. The content work then proceeds against the gaps that paper confirmed. A second full paper is sat at roughly the halfway point and marked the same way. A third is sat in the final fortnight. Three numbers, on comparable papers, marked to the same scheme.

What the three numbers show is usually one of four things. Steady improvement, in which case the plan continues. No movement despite the work, in which case the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes rather than intensifies. Movement that stalls, which normally means the easy technique marks were recovered and the remaining gap is content. Or a mark already above the target, which means sessions can stop and the money can stay in the family's pocket.

That last outcome happens more often than families expect, particularly where the June result was a pacing failure rather than a knowledge one. We raise it when the evidence shows it. A provider with no marking habit has no way of knowing, which is one reason marking should be part of a resit plan rather than an extra.

sections.heading: What a Dubai resit costs, and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: Two costs sit on a resit: the entry and the tutoring. The entry is quoted by the school or centre and varies, and we publish no figure for it because an invented number would be worse than none. The tutoring can be priced from published market data, and the useful discipline here is to check each figure against the provider that published it rather than taking any aggregate on trust, including ours.

Published Dubai rates read in October 2026: Tutopiya lists from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; qualified online subject tutors run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; IGCSE and IB specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and one premium provider at AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. Monthly comparators include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

For a resit the band should follow the diagnosis. A candidate recovering command-term marks in Biology needs someone who knows the mark scheme, which is the mid band at minimum. A candidate who simply will not sit down and work through past papers may be adequately served at the budget band, and paying specialist rates for supervision is waste. A candidate chasing a top grade on a difficult code needs the specialist band. Matching the band to the job is the part of this decision that saves the most money.

What a parent can verify, and should: the provider's own published rate page with the date read, the syllabus code the tutor teaches, whether marking is included or extra, the entry deadline from the centre in writing, and the marked papers from the sessions themselves. Everything on that list is checkable. Any claim that is not checkable, including satisfaction percentages and star ratings with no sample or date, should be treated as decoration.

sections.heading: Why resit work is delivered online here
paragraphs: Resit candidates make the clearest case for the format. They need a specialist in one syllabus code, their availability is irregular, they are frequently carrying a post-16 timetable or working, and some are no longer in Dubai at all. Matching on the code rather than on the postcode is the only sensible approach, and it is why IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India; all UAE sessions are one-to-one over live video.

There is a specific evidence advantage as well. Marked papers are annotated on a shared screen and saved, so the three checkpoint papers and every marked question in between exist as documents the family can look at. The whole argument of this page is auditability, and a trail of annotated papers is what auditability looks like in practice. Work done on paper at a kitchen table leaves no comparable record.

The in-home premium also looks different on a short, deadline-bound run. Published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour carry travel inside them, and a resit candidate frequently has daytime availability that an in-home tutor cannot use because they are teaching elsewhere. Online, daytime slots are genuinely available, and they widen the specialist pool more than any other single factor.

The honest exception, as always, is the candidate who will not work without someone present. That is a real pattern and worth naming rather than pretending away. But a resit requires independent practice between sessions whatever the delivery format, so a candidate who cannot work alone needs a different conversation about habits before anyone is hired.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and what nobody can promise
paragraphs: Three cautions. The first is that any coursework or controlled assessment in scope must be the candidate's own work. A tutor can teach the skill, explain the criteria, discuss a plan and give feedback on a draft the candidate wrote; a tutor cannot write it, rewrite it or edit it to completion. Boards investigate malpractice, and a finding can void a grade or an entire entry, which on a resit means losing the thing the resit was for.

The second is practical components, which are a centre question rather than a teaching one. How a science practical element is handled for a resit depends on the board and the centre, and for a private candidate it is the most common reason a subject cannot be sat where they hoped. Settle it with the centre before entering, because no amount of revision fixes an entry that was never possible.

The third is that no provider can promise a grade. Boundaries are set by the boards after each series and move with the paper, and they are published afterwards rather than in advance. A provider quoting the mark that will earn a grade is guessing. What a resit plan can honestly offer is recovery of the marks the breakdown identified, evidenced by marked papers along the way, which is the part anyone can act on.

On materials, we link to Cambridge and Pearson's own timetable and syllabus pages rather than redistributing papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables, which belong to the boards. The candidate's school or centre is the right source for official copies, and a provider offering a downloadable bank of board material is telling you something about its judgement.

sections.heading: Starting a resit plan with the evidence in hand
paragraphs: Send three things: the statement of results with the component breakdown, the subject and syllabus code, and what the grade is needed for and by when. The third item decides more than the first two. A grade needed for a sixth-form place in September is a different problem from one needed for an equivalency submission with no fixed date, and the November results timing makes that distinction decisive.

The first session reads the breakdown against the mark scheme and gives a view in marks: how many look recoverable, in which paper, and over what period. Sometimes the answer is that a re-mark enquiry should come first. Sometimes it is that one subject is worth resitting and the second is not. Occasionally it is that the June result was a pacing failure and six weeks of timed practice will do, which is a much smaller purchase than the family came for.

The trial lesson is free and carries no condition beyond booking a time. For a resit we spend it on a real question from the paper that lost the marks, because that is the quickest way to separate technique from content, and those two carry very different costs and timescales.

From there the plan runs monthly with three marked checkpoint papers, and it is reviewed on those numbers rather than on impressions. If the marks are not moving, the diagnosis changes rather than the intensity. If they pass the target early, we say so and stop. Either way the family can see the evidence, which is the point of the whole arrangement.

faqs.question: When can my child resit an IGCSE in the UAE?
faqs.answer: In the November series, which is the resit route for UAE candidates; the June series is the main sitting. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE also runs in November. The timing consequence matters: Pearson's record shows November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026, so a November grade is known in the new year rather than within weeks. Work from the board's live official timetable and the centre's own letter rather than any restated date.

faqs.question: What should I ask for before deciding on a resit?
faqs.answer: The statement of results broken down by component, which the examinations officer can obtain and which usually arrives within days. It tells you how far below the boundary the candidate sat, which paper lost the marks, and whether the shortfall was concentrated or spread. Three marks below in one paper is a different proposition from thirty marks below across all of them, and the two should not buy the same plan. A resit decision made without the breakdown is the most common way a Dubai family wastes a term.

faqs.question: Can my child resit through our own school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is the simplest route because the school is already a centre and can supply the breakdown and mark schemes easily. Some Dubai schools decline to enter former students, usually on capacity grounds, so ask the examinations officer and get the answer in writing. Where the school declines, the officer can normally describe the route through another school or a registered examination centre. Do this first, because the November entry deadline falls well before the papers and no revision plan survives a missed entry.

faqs.question: How do private candidates enter an IGCSE resit in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Through a registered examination centre rather than a school, and the questions to ask that centre are specific: which boards it offers, whether it can accommodate a subject with a practical or coursework component, what the entry deadline is, which syllabus code it will enter, and the total cost. Board coverage differs by centre and changes, so verify directly rather than relying on any third-party list. The practical-component question is the one that most often rules a science subject out for a private candidate, so settle it before paying.

faqs.question: How many marks can a resit realistically recover?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the breakdown shows. Blank questions at the end of a paper indicate pacing, which timed practice fixes in weeks. Correct content scoring half marks indicates command terms, which is faster still. One paper far below the others indicates paper-specific technique, which is a defined job. Uniformly middling marks across every topic indicate content that was never secure, and a single series may not be enough for that. We estimate recoverable marks per paper in the first session rather than quoting a general improvement.

faqs.question: How do we know the resit work is actually landing?
faqs.answer: By marking full papers. We sit a complete paper under timed conditions in the first fortnight, mark it to the board's scheme and record the mark, then repeat at the midpoint and again near the end. Three numbers on comparable papers show whether the plan is working while there is still time to change it. Steady movement means continue; no movement means the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes rather than intensifies; passing the target early means stopping. A plan with no marking habit cannot tell you any of this.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects resit best in a single term?
faqs.answer: Biology, Economics, Business Studies and Computer Science, because their recoverable marks are structural: command-term shape, a supported judgement, pseudocode conventions. English Language responds to six to ten weeks of marked timed responses. Mathematics moves quickly where the losses were unwritten method or blank final questions and slowly where algebra and geometry were never secure. Additional Mathematics and Further Pure are the hardest, because long interdependent questions give little credit for partial method, so they need the content to have been broadly sound.

faqs.question: Will a November grade arrive in time for a sixth-form place?
faqs.answer: Check with the institution before entering, because the answer is often no. Pearson's published record shows November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026, so a November grade lands in the new year. If a Dubai sixth form wants the grade before a September start, a November resit cannot supply it, and the useful conversation is with the school about conditional entry or an alternative subject. If the grade is for an equivalency submission with no fixed date, the timing matters much less.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework for a resit subject?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits. A tutor can teach the underlying skill, explain the marking criteria, discuss the plan and give feedback on a draft the candidate has written. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it or edit it to completion. Boards investigate malpractice and a finding can void the entry, which on a resit means losing the grade the whole term was for. A useful test is whether the candidate can explain their own argument without notes a week later; if they cannot, the work was not theirs.

faqs.question: Do you come to our home in Dubai for resit sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Resit candidates are the strongest case for that: they need a specialist in one specific syllabus code, their availability is irregular, and many have daytime hours free because they are no longer on a school timetable. Daytime availability widens the specialist pool considerably. Published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour also carry travel inside them, which buys movement rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What does a resit cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Two lines. The entry fee is quoted per subject by the school or centre and varies, so ask for it in writing with the deadline; we publish no figure because an invented one would mislead. Tutoring at published Dubai rates read in October 2026 runs AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists. Ask whether marking of full papers is included, because on a resit the marking is the evidence you are buying.

faqs.question: Is it worth resitting just to raise one grade for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the plan is much smaller than families expect. As reported in July 2026, the Ministry of Education's British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. A candidate short of the count needs a pass rather than a top band, which usually means weeks of narrowed work on the highest-mark topics. Equivalency itself is a Ministry process that no tutoring provider performs or guarantees, so verify your own requirements officially.

faqs.question: Should we try a re-mark before entering a resit?
faqs.answer: If the candidate was close to a boundary, yes, and quickly. Enquiries about results run through the school within short windows that start from the results release, and they are cheaper and faster than entering a resit. Dubai examinations officers handle these requests routinely. It will not help a candidate who was well below the boundary, but for one a few marks short it can resolve the problem entirely, which makes it the first call rather than a fallback after a term has been booked.

faqs.question: How many subjects should a candidate resit at once?
faqs.answer: Usually one, occasionally two, and rarely more. Most resit candidates are carrying something else: a sixth-form timetable, a Diploma, a job. A Year 12 student with three A Levels cannot resit three IGCSEs well, and spreading the available hours across several subjects reliably produces no visible movement in any of them. The breakdown decides which subject to choose, and the criterion is recoverable marks per hour rather than which grade looks worst on the certificate.

dubai/igcse-resit-tutor.closingBody: Ask the examinations officer for the component breakdown, and ask a centre in writing which board and code it will enter your child for and by when. With those two documents a resit plan can be built in marks rather than in hope: how many are recoverable, in which paper, and over how many weeks. Send them with the subject and what the grade is needed for, and the first session will give you that reading, including when the answer is a re-mark or no resit at all. The trial lesson is free, one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Nine subjects, one term: the triage problem
paragraphs: A Dubai Year 11 student sitting nine or ten IGCSEs has roughly the same number of revision weeks as a student sitting five, and no plan makes that arithmetic disappear. The most consequential revision decision a family makes is therefore not which provider to use but which subjects get real attention and which get maintenance. Families who refuse that decision end up giving every subject a thin slice, which is the one approach that reliably moves nothing.

Triage needs three pieces of information per subject, and all three are free. The first is the current marked position: not the predicted grade but the actual mock mark and where it sat relative to the boundary. The second is what the grade is for, because a subject needed for a sixth-form prerequisite or for the five-subject Ministry of Education equivalency count carries different weight from one taken for breadth. The third is how recoverable the marks are, which depends on whether the losses were technique or content.

Put those together and a ranking usually falls out quickly. Subjects a few marks below a needed threshold, with technique losses, go to the top: they are cheap to move and the move matters. Subjects already comfortably above what they are needed for go to maintenance. Subjects far below with broad content gaps are the hard cases, and the honest question is whether any amount of revision in the time available changes the outcome, or whether the November series is the better plan.

Dubai adds its own constraints to the week. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and those lessons continue through the revision term. School-run revision sessions, where they exist, are usually timetabled after school. What remains is the revision week a plan can actually use, and it is smaller than the one families write on a first draft.

There is a second decision hiding inside the first, which is what each chosen subject gets. Content coverage, command-term correction, timed pacing work and practical write-up technique are four different activities with different costs and different timescales, and a subject does not need all four. A student losing marks to answer shape in Biology does not need the syllabus retaught, and a student who has genuinely not learned electrolysis will not be rescued by more past papers. Matching the activity to the evidence is what keeps a nine-subject plan affordable.

IB Gram works one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not run group classes in the UAE, and IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Where a group course or the school's own revision sessions are the better purchase for a particular subject, we will say so, because on a nine-subject timetable most subjects should not be bought at all.

programmes.name: Year 10

programmes.countryNote: A Year 10 summer assessment is the best early signal on tier in Dubai, and it arrives while a change from Core to Extended is still administratively straightforward. Revision bought in Year 10 is cheaper and more decisive than the same money spent in the Year 11 spring, and almost nobody buys it.

programmes.name: Year 11, autumn to mocks
programmes.description: The content is still being completed in some subjects while mocks approach in others. Revision in this window should follow the school's scheme of work rather than the whole syllabus, because topics not yet taught cannot be revised.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mock windows run from November to January and differ between neighbouring schools by weeks. A revision plan copied from a friend at another school will be aimed at the wrong fortnight, which is a common and avoidable waste in this emirate.

programmes.name: Year 11, mocks to the June series
programmes.description: The real revision term. Marked mocks make triage possible for the first time, coursework and practical components fall due, and the final weeks should be full papers under timed conditions rather than topic coverage.
programmes.countryNote: This is when the Dubai revision market is loudest and when choosing becomes hardest. The spring break usually sits close enough to the June series that it should be spent on marked full papers, not on a topic course, and that distinction is worth more than any provider comparison.

programmes.name: After the papers
programmes.description: Results arrive in August for the June series, and the November series is available as a resit route. Decisions at that point should be made on the component breakdown rather than on the grade, and narrowed to specific papers.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's published record shows June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. That January timing matters if a Dubai sixth-form place or an equivalency submission depends on a resit grade.

dubai/igcse-revision-classes.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects Dubai families bring to us most, with the revision activity that actually moves each one.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Topic retrieval works for the standard content; the recoverable marks are usually in written method and in the final questions of the longer paper, which need timed practice with marking rather than more exercises.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Heaviest content load of the sciences for most Dubai cohorts. Moles calculations and electrolysis repay topic revision; qualitative analysis repays learning the exact terms the mark scheme names.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits are where most marks go. Unit and prefix discipline is a checklist habit, and the practical write-up conventions can be learned in two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The subject where command-term drills return the most marks per hour. Content revision alone moves little, because the usual loss is correct knowledge presented in the wrong answer shape.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Cannot be revised by reading notes. Progress comes from marked timed responses, with attention to precise quotation and to register in directed writing.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: The summary task rewards strict adherence to word limits and own-words requirements. Listening paper marks are lost to answering from context rather than from what was actually said.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagrams respond to drill; the evaluation question responds to structure. Together they are the largest block of quickly recoverable marks available at IGCSE.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are format learning rather than programming. A competent coder can gain several marks in a fortnight by writing algorithms the way the scheme expects.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case-study and source-skill subjects where revision means practising the specific question formats. Content recall alone leaves the higher-mark questions unaddressed.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. They take timetable space through the revision term and are excluded from the five subjects counted for equivalency.

sections.heading: How to triage nine subjects in one evening
paragraphs: Triage is a two-column exercise and it takes about an hour at a kitchen table. In the first column, for each subject, write the most recent marked mark and how far it sat below or above the grade the student needs. In the second, write what that grade is needed for: a sixth-form prerequisite, a university requirement, the five-subject equivalency count, or nothing in particular. Subjects with a large gap and a real requirement come first.

Then add a third judgement, which is where a marked paper is worth more than a report: how recoverable are the missing marks. Blank questions at the end of a paper mean pacing, which is weeks of work. Correct content scoring part marks means command terms, which is days. Low marks spread evenly across every topic mean the content was never secure, which is months. Two subjects with identical gaps can therefore sit at opposite ends of the ranking.

The output is usually three subjects for real attention, two or three for maintenance, and the rest left to school teaching and the student's own retrieval practice. That feels uncomfortable to write down and it is the single most useful document in a Dubai Year 11. Without it, revision defaults to whichever subject the student feels worst about that week, which is rarely the one where marks are cheapest to recover.

One important exception belongs in the ranking. A subject needed to complete the five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or 3 for the Ministry of Education's British equivalency track has a floor rather than a target, and Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from that count. Getting a borderline subject over a pass line can therefore be more valuable than lifting a strong subject one grade, and it is usually much faster work.

sections.heading: A revision week a Dubai Year 11 can actually hold
paragraphs: Most revision timetables fail because they are written for a week that does not exist. A Dubai Year 11 student is in school until mid-afternoon, has the KHDA mandatory subjects on the timetable, often has school-run revision after hours, and has a commute that in some communities is an hour each way. The honest planning unit is therefore four to six usable evening hours a week plus the weekend, not twenty.

Within that, the highest-return structure is short, frequent and retrieval-based rather than long and passive. Reading notes feels productive and produces little; answering questions from memory and then checking produces most of the gain. Forty minutes of recall practice in a subject, three times across a fortnight, beats a single three-hour session on the same material, and it fits a school week far better.

Full papers need protecting separately, because they cannot be done in forty-minute slices. One full paper a week at the real duration, at the weekend, marked, with the errors worked through on a weekday, is the pattern that produces visible movement in the spring term. That single paper plus its follow-up is worth more than four evenings of reading, and it is the activity families most often skip because it is uncomfortable.

The table sets out a workable shape. It deliberately assigns fewer subjects than a student sits, because that is the consequence of triage. It also protects two evenings entirely, which is not generosity: a Year 11 revising seven evenings a week in February is a Year 11 who stops revising in April.

sections.heading: Revising for the right board
paragraphs: Dubai schools use both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, sometimes in the same building for different subjects, and the two are not interchangeable for revision purposes. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ in paper structure, in formula provision and in question style. A term spent on the wrong board's past papers teaches habits that the real paper will not reward.

The code is printed on the entry statement, usually on the front of a mock paper, and generally in the school's subject handbook. If none is to hand, the subject teacher confirms it in a sentence. We ask for it before the first session, because it determines which papers are worth sitting and which revision guides are worth owning. Families often discover their child sits different boards for different subjects, which means the revision shelf needs to match subject by subject.

Pearson also runs a modular route in some subjects, where units can be sat across sessions rather than all at the end, while Cambridge is terminal by default. For revision planning that changes what is at stake in a given series: a modular candidate may hold a banked unit result, which alters where the remaining hours should go. Nobody can plan that without knowing which structure applies.

Two practical checks belong alongside the code. Confirm the tier, because in tiered subjects the lower tier carries a grade ceiling and revising for a top grade from a Core or Foundation entry is wasted effort. And confirm which grading scale the school reports on, since UAE centres use both A* to G and 9 to 1, so the target itself may be ambiguous until asked about.

sections.heading: What group courses cost per subject, and when they pay
paragraphs: Group courses look most attractive precisely when a student has nine subjects, because the arithmetic of one-to-one across that many is impossible for most households. That instinct is right in part. A group course divides a tutor's fee across the room, which is real value when what the student needs is content coverage in a subject they have genuinely not learned.

Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 set the frame. One-to-one with a qualified online subject tutor runs AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visits are AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. Budget online providers publish from AED 33 to 65. Monthly comparators in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Group formats sit below the one-to-one figures per student by a margin that depends on class size.

The useful test is what the subject needs. Content coverage, taught to a room, is a legitimate group product and often the right purchase for a Dubai student who has fallen behind in a science. Command-term correction, method presentation, pacing, and the evaluation paragraph in Economics are individual findings from an individual script, and a class cannot address them because it does not know they exist. Buying a course to fix an individual pattern is how families end up paying twice.

Count the hidden costs before comparing. A centre course involves travel at the worst hour of a Dubai weekday, holiday courses are usually prepaid so a missed day is still a paid day, and a mixed-curriculum room may spend part of its time on material outside your child's specification. Against that, the cheapest revision in the emirate is the school's own sessions, which are usually included in fees and matched to the department's teaching, and which many families never ask about.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the components nobody revises
paragraphs: Every revision plan we see arrives with the written papers covered and the other components missing. In the sciences, practical skills are assessed either through a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper with Cambridge depending on the centre, and within the written papers with Pearson. Either way, marks go on naming independent, dependent and control variables, describing apparatus precisely, and writing a procedure that could be repeated. That is a format to learn, and two or three sessions covers it.

Where coursework or controlled assessment exists, it must be the student's own work. A tutor can teach the skill, explain the marking criteria, discuss a plan and give feedback on a draft the student wrote; a tutor cannot write it, rewrite it or edit it to completion. Boards investigate malpractice and a finding can void a grade or a whole entry. One provider ranking in this sector sells completed assessed work in a different qualification at around AED 3,750, which is the same category of offer and the same exposure for the student.

Speaking and listening components in languages have their own arrangements, set by the centre, and they are frequently left out of revision entirely because they do not look like a paper. Ask the subject teacher when they fall and what they require. A student who has revised three written papers and not prepared for an oral has left marks on the table in the easiest component to prepare for.

On materials, we link to Cambridge and Pearson's own syllabus and timetable pages rather than redistributing papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables, which belong to the boards. The school holds official copies and the subject teacher is the right route to the school's own mock papers. A provider offering a downloadable bank of board material is making a choice worth noticing.
