sections.heading: A past-paper routine that fits a commuting household
paragraphs: The most common reason science tutoring underperforms is not the teaching. It is that the work between sessions does not get done, and in a household where a pupil is home at five after a commute there is a real reason for that. So the routine has to fit the week that exists.

What works is short, timed and marked. One past-paper question set per science per week under a clock, rather than an hour of open revision. Timing is the operative constraint: a candidate who spends fourteen minutes on a six-mark question will not finish, and unanswered questions score nothing regardless of understanding. Twenty-five minutes with a clock running teaches more than ninety minutes without one, and it fits into an evening that starts late.

The second element is marking against the published scheme rather than against a sense of whether the answer looked right. This is the habit that changes results, because it shows a student where credit actually sits: a named variable, a unit, a construction line, a stated comparison. Candidates who learn to read a mark scheme start writing for the marker instead of writing what they know, and in science that shift alone is often worth a grade.

The third is sequencing by paper rather than by topic. In Cambridge sciences the losses are frequently concentrated in one paper — very often the alternative-to-practical, because nobody revised it — and a term spent on theory content will not touch that. Mark the mock paper by paper before deciding what to revise. In a household with limited evening hours, that ordering is the difference between a term that moves a grade and a term that confirms one.

sections.heading: Two sciences, one evening: how to prioritise
paragraphs: Al Barari families frequently need two sciences supported at once in Year 11, and the evening does not stretch. The question is how to allocate a limited number of hours, and the answer is usually not to split them evenly.

Start by finding the shared cause. Where physics and chemistry are both weak, the common factor is often quantitative: rearranging, standard form, units and significant figures. One tutor covering both will see that the physics difficulty and the chemistry difficulty are the same algebra problem, whereas two separate tutors will each diagnose within their own subject and both teach content. A short block on the quantitative handling can lift both sciences at once, which is better value than two parallel content programmes.

Where the causes genuinely differ, prioritise by distance from the grade boundary rather than by weakness. A science sitting two marks below a boundary repays an hour far better than one sitting fifteen below, and the marked mock tells you which is which. It feels counterintuitive to spend the time on the stronger subject, and it is usually the right call when the goal is the overall profile rather than fixing the thing that worries the student most.

Where three sciences all need attention, the honest answer is that term-time cannot absorb it. Sequence them: one science weekly in term and the others covered in a holiday block, then rotate. Three weekly sessions plus school homework produces a pupil too tired to complete the set work, and the set work is where the improvement happens. We will say this rather than take the larger booking, because an exhausted candidate does not improve and the family concludes tutoring does not work.

Monthly, at one session a week, market estimates run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid tier, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages show around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits — roughly double the money for half the sessions, with the premium going to travel rather than teaching.

In science the figure to think about is per subject, because that is how the commitment actually scales. Two sciences at one session a week each at the mid band is AED 1,200 to AED 2,400 a month, which is a materially different decision from one. That arithmetic is the strongest argument for the prioritisation section above: finding a shared quantitative cause and treating it once is cheaper than running two parallel programmes, and frequently works better.

For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion. The school bill is flat; tutoring is the variable line. sections.heading: Permits, papers and the limits of what we supply
paragraphs: In a villa community this size a science tutor usually arrives by referral from another family, and that is exactly the route which skips the one check worth making. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated and most Dubai parents have not been told. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. The categories allowed to hold it are broad enough to cover almost anyone a neighbour would recommend: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. So the question to put to a recommended Chemistry tutor is not how many Al Barari families they already teach, but whether their permit is current.

MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system, so a tutor who says the permit is costly or optional is wrong twice. No fine amount appears on this page: Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and the figure circulating online could not be verified. IB Gram is also not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and nobody in this market should imply such a thing without a permit number.

On materials, the limit is firm. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works through questions from legitimately obtained material and teaches the candidate to read a mark scheme themselves, which is more durable: a student who understands where credit is awarded writes differently on the next paper, while one handed answers does not.

Two further claims to treat sceptically. Examiner status, which we do not use as a selling point for anyone whose current status cannot be evidenced and which gives no access to marking, boundaries or unseen papers. And grade guarantees, which we will not offer because nobody controls the outcome. What we will give you after a marked diagnostic is a categorised account of where the marks are going, paper by paper, and an honest view of which categories the remaining weeks can close.

sections.heading: Bridging into A Level and IB sciences
paragraphs: The summer after IGCSE is the most underused tutoring window in a school career, and in the sciences it is worth more than in any other subject area. A Level sciences and IB Higher Level sciences both begin at pace, and both assume quantitative fluency and extended-writing ability that a comfortable IGCSE pass does not demonstrate.

The specific gaps are predictable. In physics, the Diploma and A Level both treat fields and rates with a mathematical depth that IGCSE does not approach, and students arrive able to use equations without reasoning from relationships. In chemistry, organic work shifts from product recall to mechanism reasoning, and energetics becomes quantitative where IGCSE left it descriptive. In biology, the volume of precise terminology rises sharply and the assessment rewards extended explanation rather than short answers.

The second predictable gap is practical and investigative. Both A Level and the IB Diploma require individual investigative work assessed against criteria, and an IGCSE candidate who only ever sat an alternative-to-practical paper has never designed anything. Teaching variables, controls, uncertainty and evaluation before Year 12 begins means the student's first investigation is not also their first attempt at the skills it requires.

Six to eight sessions across a summer covers most of this, which is a small commitment against a two-year course. Where the pupil took a combined award rather than separate sciences and intends to continue, the block matters more and should be longer, because the content gap is genuine rather than a matter of pace. Ask the school directly what their sixth form expects, since separate sciences at the higher tier are commonly assumed.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science award is my child actually taking?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer, because there are at least four possibilities and they are not interchangeable. Separate sciences means three IGCSEs with three sets of papers. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 is a single award across all three sciences. Cambridge Co-ordinated Science 0654 is a double award. The Pearson Edexcel Science Double Award 4SD0 is a different double award again. Content volume, paper structure and reporting all differ, and a tutor cannot plan a course without knowing which one your child sits.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a practical exam or a written alternative?
faqs.answer: In Cambridge sciences it depends on what the centre enters: either a practical test conducted in the school laboratory under exam conditions, or an alternative-to-practical written paper examining experimental skills on paper. Ask the exams officer which. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences set no separate practical paper and assess practical skills inside the two written papers instead. The answer matters because the alternative-to-practical paper is a distinct skill set that needs explicit teaching rather than general revision.

faqs.question: Can experimental skills be taught over video?
faqs.answer: The paper-based ones, yes, and better than most families expect. Identifying variables, justifying repeat readings, handling anomalies, choosing apparatus with an appropriate resolution, naming a specific source of error rather than saying human error, and reading scales accurately are question types following a learnable formula. They are the most predictable marks in the subject and the least revised. What a screen cannot supply is apparatus familiarity, which your child's school provides and which no tutor substitutes for in any format.

faqs.question: Is a combined science award easier than separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Lighter in volume and identical in standard, which is a distinction families often miss. A combined award covers reduced content in each science but is examined with the same command-term precision and the same calculation discipline, so a pupil told the course is easier can still be caught out by how the marks are awarded. The more important consequence is forward-looking: A Level and IB Higher Level sciences commonly assume separate-science content, so check what your school's sixth form expects before the award is chosen.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to an Al Barari villa?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run only in India and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. For the written and practical-skills papers the format costs very little, because the work is marked questions, worked calculations with visible steps and a shared screen. Practical laboratory work happens at school in either case, and we say so rather than implying a tutor could run experiments at your home.

faqs.question: Where do IGCSE physics candidates lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: Describing a graph when the question asked for an explanation, which costs marks in every topic rather than one. Then refraction and ray diagrams, where credit attaches to construction lines and to measuring from the normal rather than the surface, so a candidate who measures wrongly loses the whole question. Then unit prefixes in the wave equation, where kilohertz and megahertz quietly cost a mark each time they appear. Each of those takes one to three sessions, which is why technique work often beats more content revision.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose chemistry marks on calculations they can do?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, both fixable. Concentration units: moles per cubic decimetre against moles per cubic centimetre decides more questions than conceptual understanding does, and it bleeds through every titration and solution question. And missing working: mark schemes credit the steps, so a candidate who shows nothing loses the entire question when an early rounding choice compounds through a multi-step calculation. The pupils most affected are the quick ones who have been praised for mental arithmetic, and two to three weeks of enforced working changes it.

faqs.question: How should we handle two weak sciences with only one free evening?
faqs.answer: Find the shared cause first. Where physics and chemistry are both weak the common factor is usually quantitative — rearranging, standard form, units, significant figures — and one tutor across both will see that rather than diagnosing separately within each subject. A short block on the quantitative handling can lift both at once. Where the causes genuinely differ, prioritise by distance from the grade boundary rather than by severity, because a science two marks below a boundary repays an hour far better than one fifteen below.

faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget and student tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for qualified subject tutors online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or above for specialists. Monthly at one session a week that is roughly AED 240 to AED 600, AED 600 to AED 1,200, or AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. faqs.question: What revision routine works when my child gets home at five?
faqs.answer: Short, timed and marked. One past-paper question set per science per week under a clock beats an hour of open revision, because timing is where the marks go: a candidate spending fourteen minutes on a six-mark question will not finish the paper. Then mark it against the published scheme rather than against a feeling about whether it looked right, so the student sees where credit actually sits. Sequence by paper rather than by topic, because the losses are often concentrated in one paper.

faqs.question: Which biology topics are worth most late in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Inheritance, because drawing the cross instead of reasoning in prose recovers method marks immediately and takes one session. Then the precise distinctions between diffusion, osmosis and active transport, which the mark scheme separates and candidates conflate under pressure. Then data-interpretation on enzymes and photosynthesis, where the answer wanted is the limiting factor that produced the graph's shape rather than a description of the shape. All three are technique rather than content, so they fit the weeks when content teaching has stopped being realistic.

faqs.answer: Six to eight bridging sessions, more if your child took a combined award and intends to continue. A Level and IB Higher Level sciences both start at pace and assume quantitative fluency and extended writing that a comfortable IGCSE pass does not demonstrate. Both also require individual investigative work assessed against criteria, and a candidate who only ever sat an alternative-to-practical paper has never designed anything. Teaching variables, controls, uncertainty and evaluation before Year 12 means the first investigation is not also the first attempt.

The February and March series is offered to India only, so any UAE-facing page quoting a March window is wrong about your country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

The private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of pages quoting amounts. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance, and ask any agency the same question.

faqs.question: Will a tutor give us mark schemes and past papers to keep?
faqs.answer: No. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works through questions from legitimately obtained material and teaches your child to read a mark scheme themselves, so they can see where credit is awarded rather than being handed answers. In science that shift is worth a great deal, because the marks sit in named variables, units and construction lines rather than in the final figure.

intro.heading: Four routes, and only one of them is your child's
paragraphs: The phrase IGCSE science covers four quite different qualifications, and a family in Al Barsha comparing tutors without knowing which one applies is comparing the wrong thing. The first route is separate sciences: three qualifications, three grades, with Cambridge codes 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology, or the Pearson equivalents 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. The second is a co-ordinated double award, Cambridge 0654, which covers all three disciplines and is reported as a double award. The third is a single combined award, Cambridge 0653, covering all three in less depth for one grade. The fourth is the Pearson Science Double Award, 4SD0, which covers all three and awards two grades.

The differences are not academic hair-splitting. They change which topics are in scope, how many papers are sat, how many grades appear on a certificate, and what a sixth form will accept for A Level entry in a science. A student on a combined route who has been working through separate-science revision material has been revising content their syllabus excludes, which is a term of effort pointed at the wrong target. A student on separate sciences who has been using co-ordinated resources has gaps they do not know about.

This page therefore runs two comparisons. The first is between the routes, because that is the comparison that changes a grade. The second is between districts, because that is the comparison parents in Al Barsha actually ask about: Al Barsha 1 against Al Barsha South, against Al Barsha Heights, against Al Sufouh and Dubai Hills. The honest result of the second comparison is that what varies by district is which routes the local schools tend to offer, and what does not vary is the syllabus, the papers or the pool of people who can teach them.

There is a third comparison worth making and it sits inside the sciences themselves. Physics, chemistry and biology fail students in different ways. Physics loses marks in circuit analysis and in converting a graph gradient into a physical quantity with units. Chemistry loses them in moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables. Biology loses them to command-term imprecision: describing when an explanation was asked for, naming a structure without its function. A tutor who treats science as one subject will apply one method to three different problems.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as one-to-one online tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. For the sciences that distinction has a specific shape: hands-on laboratory work belongs to the school, which holds the equipment and the supervision requirement, while the examined practical component on most Cambridge routes is the alternative-to-practical paper, which is a written paper and is taught better with a shared screen than at a bench.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-barsha.programmesIntro: These are the four routes, described by structure rather than by difficulty, because structure is what decides which past papers a session should use and which topics are safely out of scope.

programmes.name: Separate sciences: Cambridge 0625, 0620, 0610
programmes.description: Three qualifications and three grades. Each is entered at Core or Extended tier and each sits a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component, which is either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Core candidates take Paper 1 and Paper 3; Extended candidates take Paper 2 and Paper 4. This is the route most sixth forms prefer for A Level science entry, because it evidences depth in the specific subject.
programmes.countryNote: The British-pathway schools in Al Barsha 1 and Al Sufouh concentrate their strongest science sets here. A student on separate sciences has three syllabuses and three sets of past papers, which is also why families on this route most often end up buying support in two subjects rather than one and should decide in advance how many they are willing to fund.

programmes.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences, Double Award
programmes.description: All three disciplines in one syllabus, reported as a double award, entered at Core or Extended with the same paper architecture as the separate sciences. Content is genuinely narrower than three separate syllabuses: specific topics are out of scope, and knowing exactly which ones saves a term of misdirected revision. Confirm with the centre how the award is reported on the certificate.
programmes.countryNote: This is a common route in Dubai schools balancing a broad curriculum against timetable pressure. The practical risk for an Al Barsha family is resource mismatch: online revision material is overwhelmingly written for separate sciences, so a 0654 candidate working alone will almost certainly revise material their papers will not ask about.

programmes.name: Cambridge Combined Science
programmes.description: All three disciplines in less depth for a single grade, entered at Core or Extended. It is a legitimate route for a student whose strengths lie elsewhere and whose post-sixteen plans do not require a science A Level. Scope is the defining feature: a substantial amount of what appears in separate-science past papers is simply not examinable here.
programmes.countryNote: Where a student in this catchment is entered for 0653 and hopes to take a science at A Level, that conversation should happen with the school early rather than after results. Sixth forms set their own entry requirements and several will want evidence from a separate science or a double award rather than a single combined grade.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel Science Double Award
programmes.description: Pearson's double-award route, covering biology, chemistry and physics and awarding two grades. Papers, mark-scheme conventions and question styles follow Pearson practice rather than Cambridge, and Pearson publishes its own assessment materials and timetables. A tutor who has only taught Cambridge will mark against the wrong expectations for working and presentation.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Barsha schools run Pearson for some subjects and Cambridge for others, which produces split-board profiles within a single student's timetable. The statement of entry is the only reliable source for which board applies to the sciences, and it is worth reading before any tutoring rate is agreed.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-barsha.subjectsIntro: The sciences fail students in different ways, and the entries below name the specific failure points in each discipline alongside the codes. This is the level of detail a route comparison has to reach to be useful.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Electricity and circuit analysis cause the most trouble, followed by any question requiring a graph gradient to be converted into a physical quantity with its unit. Moments and density questions are reliable marks for a prepared candidate. Extended-tier questions on electromagnetic induction and on the gas laws reward precise sequencing rather than recall.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables concentrate the losses. Organic chemistry is typically learned as a list of names rather than reaction types, so students recognise an alcohol and cannot predict what it does. Extended electrolysis questions want half-equations written correctly rather than described.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Content volume rather than conceptual depth. Marks go to imprecise command-term responses: describing when the paper asked for an explanation, or naming a structure without its function. Transport in plants, enzymes and genetics crosses all reward exact vocabulary, and magnification calculations are easy marks for a numerate candidate.

subjects.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: The same three disciplines with a defined narrower scope. The single most valuable thing a tutor can do in the first session is mark the boundary: which separate-science topics are out of scope, so the student stops revising them. That conversation regularly saves more time than any amount of teaching.

subjects.name: Cambridge Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: The narrowest route, awarding one grade. Students and parents frequently work from separate-science resources here, which is the costliest resource mismatch available in IGCSE science. Establishing scope from the current syllabus document, which the school holds, is the first step rather than an afterthought.

subjects.name: Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: Pearson's own structure and conventions across the three disciplines. Its question styles build context across multi-part questions and its presentational expectations differ from Cambridge. A candidate trained on Cambridge papers will lose a few marks a paper for reasons unconnected to science knowledge.

subjects.name: The alternative-to-practical paper
subjects.description: Assesses experimental literacy in writing: reading a scale correctly, identifying a control variable, recognising why a result is anomalous, and drawing a line of best fit the data supports. It is the most trainable component in the whole route and the one students most reliably arrive at unprepared, because it does not feel like revision.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The sciences assume rearranging formulae, handling standard form, and proportional reasoning. A student losing science marks to algebra rather than to science has one problem presenting as three, and closing it in a single place is cheaper than closing it in physics, chemistry and biology separately.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics (0606 · 4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the sciences by students heading for engineering or medicine. Relevant here because a school entering a student for Additional Mathematics is usually also entering them for separate sciences, so the two route decisions tend to travel together.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in every Dubai private school, in every district. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited.

sections.heading: The four science routes compared
paragraphs: This is the comparison that changes a grade, and it should be settled before any tutor is chosen. The table below sets the four routes side by side on the dimensions that matter: codes, paper architecture, grades awarded, scope and what each route typically permits at sixteen. Entry details should be confirmed from the statement of entry and from the centre, because schools enter different sets differently and a sibling's route is not evidence of your child's.

The paper architecture is worth understanding in its own right. On the Cambridge separate sciences and on 0654, Core candidates sit a multiple-choice Paper 1 and a theory Paper 3, while Extended candidates sit a multiple-choice Paper 2 and a theory Paper 4. Both tiers then sit a practical component, which is either Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, depending on what the centre enters candidates for. Pearson's routes use their own paper structures and their own conventions.

The scope column is the one that costs money when it is ignored. On 0654 and 0653 a defined set of separate-science topics is simply not examinable, and almost all freely available revision material online is written for separate sciences. A student on a combined route revising from that material is doing real work that the papers will not reward, and nobody notices until a mock. Establishing scope from the current syllabus document, which the school holds, is a two-session job and it is the best value available on these routes.

The post-sixteen column should be read with care rather than treated as a rule. Sixth forms set their own entry requirements and those vary, including between schools in this catchment. The pattern is that separate sciences evidence depth in a specific subject and are the most straightforward route into a science A Level, that double awards are widely but not universally accepted, and that a single combined grade is the hardest case. Where a student on a combined route wants a science A Level, that conversation belongs with the school now rather than after results.

sections.heading: Al Barsha against the next district over: what route availability does
paragraphs: Now the comparison parents actually make. Al Barsha 1 against Al Barsha South, against Al Barsha Heights, against Al Sufouh and Dubai Hills. The honest answer for science tutoring is that one thing differs between them and two things do not, and the thing that differs is upstream of tutoring entirely.

What differs is route availability, because it follows the schools. The British-pathway schools concentrated in Al Barsha 1 and in the Al Sufouh strip are where separate-science entries cluster. Al Barsha South contains an IB continuum school, Dwight School Dubai, so a family there may be comparing MYP sciences against IGCSE rather than comparing two IGCSE routes. American-curriculum schools in the cluster enter students for other qualifications entirely. So a family choosing a district is, indirectly, choosing a likely route, and that is a real consideration when choosing a school.

What does not differ is the syllabus and the tutor pool. Cambridge sets 0625, 0620, 0610, 0654 and 0653, and Pearson sets its own codes, and none of them varies by postcode. The number of people in Dubai who have taught 0654 specifically, and who can state its scope boundary without looking it up, is small; Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, and the co-ordinated routes are a minority within that. Dividing a small specialist population by district produces a very small one.

The table below makes the district comparison concrete, with the one column that genuinely varies alongside the columns that do not. The honest conclusion is the same as it would be for any subject here: compare districts for schools, commute and household fit, and do not compare them for access to a tutor. IB Gram delivers UAE lessons as one-to-one online tuition over live video and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India, which is what makes the access identical across the set.

sections.heading: Three sciences, three failure modes
paragraphs: A tutor who treats science as a single subject will bring one method to three different problems. The three disciplines lose marks in characteristically different places, and knowing which one is costing your child is more useful than knowing their overall science grade.

Physics losses cluster in two places. The first is electricity, specifically circuit analysis where a student has to reason about what happens to current and potential difference when a component changes rather than apply a remembered formula. The second is graph work: converting a gradient into a physical quantity with its correct unit, which appears across mechanics, electricity and thermal physics. Both are reasoning habits and both respond to deliberate practice rather than to re-reading notes.

Chemistry losses are more arithmetic in character. Moles calculations, concentration work and empirical formula questions depend on proportional reasoning the student may be shaky on in mathematics too. Ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables reward precise recall of a small body of specific material, which is efficiently learned and rarely learned efficiently. Organic chemistry taught as a list of names rather than as reaction types is the single most common structural weakness at Extended tier.

Biology losses are almost entirely linguistic. The content volume is high and the conceptual demand is lower than in the other two, so marks go to imprecision: a description offered where an explanation was required, a structure named without its function, a process described without its purpose. Command-term discipline is therefore the highest-return work in biology, and it is work a student can continue alone once it has been taught once. sections.heading: The alternative-to-practical paper, which almost nobody prepares for
paragraphs: On the Cambridge science routes the practical component is either Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, depending on what the centre enters candidates for. Many Dubai centres use the alternative, and it is the most neglected component on the whole route. It does not feel like revision, it is not covered by most online revision material in any depth, and students arrive at it having done no specific preparation.

What it assesses is experimental literacy in writing. Reading a scale or an instrument correctly and recording to an appropriate precision. Identifying the independent, dependent and control variables in an unfamiliar method. Recognising why a particular result is anomalous rather than merely different. Drawing a line of best fit that the data supports rather than one that joins the first and last points. Suggesting an improvement that would actually address the weakness identified rather than a generic one.

Every item on that list is trainable, and the training transfers across all three disciplines, which makes it unusually good value on a separate-sciences route where a family is funding help in two subjects. Three or four focused sessions on practical-paper technique improves the practical component in physics, chemistry and biology simultaneously. Few requests in IGCSE science have that property.

One important clarification on delivery. Hands-on laboratory work belongs to the school, which holds the equipment, the technician support and the safety and supervision requirements, and no tutoring arrangement should claim to replace it. The alternative-to-practical paper, however, is a written paper. Working through it with the question, the student's own attempt and the published mark scheme on one shared screen is a format that suits the task better than a bench does, and the session can be recorded for revision.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson for the sciences
paragraphs: Several Al Barsha schools run Pearson for some subjects and Cambridge for others, which means the board for the sciences cannot be assumed from the board for mathematics. The statement of entry is the only reliable source, and reading it before agreeing any tutoring rate is free.

The structural differences matter for teaching. Cambridge separate sciences and 0654 use tiered entry with a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component, with Core candidates on Papers 1 and 3 and Extended candidates on Papers 2 and 4. Pearson's separate sciences, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, use two written papers per subject with their own conventions, and the 4SD0 Double Award covers all three disciplines and awards two grades. Pearson publishes its own assessment materials, and those are the ones a Pearson candidate should be working from.

Session timing also differs by board and it affects planning. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge's exams officers' guide is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer for the zone and the dated timetable together.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and those can be revised, so the live official timetable should be the reference rather than any restatement of it. The February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply to candidates in Dubai.

sections.heading: Why the route decision outweighs the neighbourhood
paragraphs: Pulling the two comparisons together produces a clear ranking. The route your child is entered for changes which topics are examinable, how many papers they sit, how many grades they receive and what a sixth form will accept. The district you live in changes which routes the nearby schools tend to offer and what time a session can start. The first of those decides a science grade. The second decides a diary entry.

That ordering has a practical consequence for how a family spends. The highest-return purchase on a combined or co-ordinated route is two sessions establishing scope from the current syllabus document, because it stops months of misdirected revision. The highest-return purchase on a separate-sciences route is usually practical-paper technique, because it improves three subjects at once. Neither of those is what a parent typically asks for, and neither depends on anybody being able to drive to Al Barsha South.

There is one case where moving district genuinely changed the qualification, and it is worth naming because it is common in Dubai Hills and Al Barsha South. A student who transfers school mid-course can land on a different science route than the one they left: separate sciences to a double award, or a double award to separate sciences. The second direction is the dangerous one, because the student now needs content their previous syllabus excluded and nobody has flagged it. One diagnostic session mapping what was taught against what the new route requires is the cheapest fix available.

Beyond that, the useful framing for an Al Barsha family is that the science questions are route questions and the district questions are schooling questions. Pick the school on programme fit, commute and the things families normally weigh. Then read the statement of entry, establish the route and the tier, and buy support against that. The people who can teach it are reachable from every district in this comparison on identical terms.

sections.heading: What it costs, and the claims to check in any district
paragraphs: Market rates, read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers who publish them. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to AED 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, usually delivered by current university students. Unitors publishes from AED 150 for IGCSE for qualified online subject tutors. TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate places specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Bestimate quotes in-home visits including travel at AED 180 to AED 350, independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutors. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. None of this is an IB Gram price list.

The specific arithmetic that bites on a separate-sciences route is the subject count. Supporting two of the three sciences at one weekly session each on the mid band is roughly AED 1,200 to AED 2,400 a month, and three is AED 1,800 to AED 3,600. That is the pattern families drift into between October and February as each mock produces a new worry. Deciding in advance how many sciences will be funded, and accepting the others will be what they will be, is a cost control and usually an academic one too, because the student's week is finite.

On claims, three checks apply identically in every district. The permit: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Accreditation: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does so there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those bodies regulate schools. IB Gram holds no accreditation from any of them, nor from Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. And materials: syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes belong to the awarding bodies and should be referenced and linked at source rather than redistributed as downloads.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science route is my child in Al Barsha actually on?
faqs.answer: One of four, and the statement of entry says which. Separate sciences means three qualifications and three grades, Cambridge 0625, 0620 and 0610 or the Pearson equivalents. Cambridge 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences covers all three and is reported as a double award. Cambridge 0653 Combined Science covers all three in less depth for one grade. Pearson 4SD0 Science Double Award covers all three and awards two grades. Schools enter different sets differently, so a sibling's route is not evidence of your child's.

faqs.question: What is the difference between co-ordinated and combined science?
faqs.answer: Depth and the number of grades. Cambridge 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences covers all three disciplines and is reported as a double award; Cambridge 0653 Combined Science covers them in less depth for a single grade. Both have a defined scope that excludes topics the separate sciences include, which matters enormously for revision because almost all freely available material online is written for separate sciences. Confirm with the centre how the award is reported, since that is what a sixth form will read.

faqs.question: Will a double award be accepted for A Level science?
faqs.answer: Often, and it depends on the sixth form rather than on a general rule. Schools set their own entry requirements and those vary between schools in this catchment. The pattern is that separate sciences are the most straightforward route into a science A Level because they evidence depth in the specific subject, double awards are widely but not universally accepted, and a single combined grade is the hardest case. If your child is on a combined route and wants a science A Level, raise it with the school now rather than after results.

faqs.question: On the Cambridge science routes, what is Paper 6 assessing?
faqs.answer: Experimental literacy in writing rather than manual skill. Reading a scale or instrument to an appropriate precision. Identifying independent, dependent and control variables in an unfamiliar method. Recognising why a particular result is anomalous rather than simply different. Drawing a line of best fit the data supports instead of joining the first and last points. Suggesting an improvement that addresses the weakness identified. All of it is trainable in three or four sessions, and the technique transfers across all three sciences at once.

faqs.question: Does my child sit Paper 5 or Paper 6 for the practical?
faqs.answer: The centre decides, so ask the exams officer. Paper 5 is the practical test and Paper 6 is the alternative to practical, and many Dubai centres use the alternative. The technique required differs between them, so a tutor should know which applies before planning practical sessions. This is a one-line answer that nobody volunteers, and getting it wrong means practising the wrong kind of preparation for a component that forms part of every science grade on the route.

faqs.question: Is it easier to find a science tutor in Al Barsha 1 than in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: No. What differs between these districts is which routes the local schools tend to offer: separate-science entries cluster at the British-pathway schools in Al Barsha 1 and the Al Sufouh strip, while Al Barsha South contains an IB continuum school where some students meet MYP sciences rather than IGCSE. The syllabus, the papers and the pool of people who have taught 0654 or 4SD0 do not vary by postcode, and that pool is small across the whole emirate.

faqs.question: My child moved school and the science route changed. What now?
faqs.answer: Buy one diagnostic session before anything else, especially if the change was from a combined or co-ordinated route onto separate sciences. In that direction the student now needs content their previous syllabus excluded, and neither school will have flagged it because each assumes the other covered it. One session maps what was actually taught against what the new route requires, and produces a written gap list with a week count. Mid-course arrivals are most common in Dubai Hills and Al Barsha South.

faqs.question: How many of the three sciences should we pay for support in?
faqs.answer: Decide the number before October rather than during February. Two sciences at one weekly session each on the mid band of AED 150 to AED 300 is roughly AED 1,200 to AED 2,400 a month, and three is AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 plus eleven commitments in a student's week. Those are market figures read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers who publish them. Supporting fewer subjects properly beats supporting more thinly, and the student's available evenings are a real limit.

faqs.question: Where does my child lose marks in IGCSE physics specifically?
faqs.answer: Two places reliably. Circuit analysis, where the question asks what happens to current and potential difference when a component changes rather than inviting a remembered formula. And graph work, where a gradient has to be converted into a physical quantity with its correct unit, which appears across mechanics, electricity and thermal physics. Both are reasoning habits rather than knowledge gaps, which is why re-reading notes does not help and deliberate practice with past questions does.

faqs.question: Why does organic chemistry cause so much trouble at Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Because it is usually learned as a list of names rather than as a set of reaction types. A student can identify an alcohol and still be unable to predict what it does, because they have memorised labels instead of behaviour. The fix is to reorganise the material by reaction type, which takes two or three sessions and then supports itself. The related loss is electrolysis, where Extended questions want half-equations written correctly rather than described in words.

faqs.question: Is biology just memorisation, and can a tutor help with that?
faqs.answer: The volume is high and the conceptual demand is lower than in physics or chemistry, but the marks are not lost to memory. They are lost to imprecision: a description offered where an explanation was required, a structure named without its function, a process described without its purpose. Command-term discipline is the highest-return work in biology, it takes two or three sessions to teach, and a student can then continue it alone. Magnification calculations are easy marks for a numerate candidate.

faqs.question: Which exam series will an Al Barsha science candidate sit?
faqs.answer: June or November. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with an explicit warning that the correct zone timetable must be used. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. The February and March series is offered to India only.

faqs.question: Can online lessons cover science practical work?
faqs.answer: Not the hands-on part, which belongs to the school with its equipment, technician support and supervision requirements. What online lessons cover well is everything the examination actually assesses on most Cambridge routes, because the alternative-to-practical paper is written. Working through it with the question, the student's own attempt and the published mark scheme on one shared screen suits the task better than a bench does, and the session can be recorded for revision. Any provider claiming to run practicals for a Dubai family should be questioned.

faqs.question: Do science tutors in Dubai need a permit, and does it affect the price?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it costs nothing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. No fine schedule is published, so no fine amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Should we buy separate-science revision guides for a 0654 candidate?
faqs.answer: Not without first establishing the scope boundary. Cambridge 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences has a defined narrower scope than three separate syllabuses, and separate-science material covers topics the 0654 papers will not ask about. A student working from that material does real work that earns nothing, and nobody notices until a mock. Two sessions reading the scope off the current syllabus document, which the school holds, is the most cost-effective purchase available on this route.

faqs.question: Which single piece of science work improves all three subjects?
faqs.answer: Practical-paper technique, on the Cambridge routes. Scale reading, variable identification, recognising a genuine anomaly, lines of best fit judged against the data, and improvements that address the weakness found all appear in the physics, chemistry and biology practical components alike. Three or four sessions therefore pay three times, which is unusual in IGCSE science. The second candidate is units and significant figures discipline, which takes one or two sessions and recurs on every paper a student will sit.

intro.heading: Four neighbourhoods, four school mixes, one answer
paragraphs: A parent in Al Barsha South who starts searching for science support usually widens the search within a day. Would Dubai Marina have more tutors. Would a Jumeirah Village agency be cheaper. Does Dubai Hills, with its newer schools and higher fee band, have better people. These are reasonable questions and they all have answers, so this page sets out the comparison honestly rather than asserting that one location wins.

Start with what actually differs between them. Al Barsha South is five numbered sub-communities of villas and mid-rise apartments sitting inside a ring of established British-curriculum schools, which means a short school run and a large local Year 10 and Year 11 cohort. Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Beach Residence are vertical, international and transient, with few schools inside the towers and most children bussed inland. Jumeirah Village Circle and Triangle are dense, newer and mixed, with families from a wide fee range sharing the same bus routes. Dubai Hills Estate is newer again, lower density, higher fee band, with its own schools and an easier afternoon run. Those are real differences and they change the commute, the school options and the price of a villa. They do not change what an IGCSE science student needs.

The reason they do not is that the binding constraint in this subject is not distance. It is the syllabus code. A student doing Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a Double Award sits different papers from a student doing Cambridge Physics 0625 as a separate science, and both sit different papers again from a student on Pearson Edexcel 4PH1, which assesses practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical or alternative-to-practical component. A tutor who is excellent at one of those and vague about the others will set the wrong practice, and that error costs the same number of marks in Marina as it does in Al Barsha South.

The second constraint is the window. Across all four neighbourhoods, school buses deliver secondary students home between roughly 3.30pm and 4.15pm, and an in-person tutor has to arrive after that and before the evening collapses. Within a drivable radius of any one of these communities, the number of people who both know 0654 Extended Paper 4 as a document and are free at 4.45pm on a Tuesday is small. Across the network, with no drive attached at either end, it is not. That single fact is why the recommendation does not change by postcode.

What does change by neighbourhood is which schools the student is competing against for a sixth-form place, which exam board their cohort is entered for, and how much time the school run leaves. Those are worth knowing, and the comparison table further down sets them out side by side. What the comparison should not be used for is choosing a tutor by proximity, because proximity is the one variable in this subject that carries no educational value at all.

Cambridge separate sciences add a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson does not, assessing practical understanding inside the theory papers instead.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools carry 37% of Dubai's private-school enrolment, the largest share of any curriculum, and almost all of them enter Year 11 for international GCSE sciences. Within the Al Barsha South ring the board varies school to school, and at least two schools in this cluster enter different science routes within the same year group depending on set.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The alternative at the same ages, assessed on four criteria out of 8 each rather than on papers: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Students arrive in an IGCSE class with better experimental design instincts and weaker exam-answer discipline.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within a short drive of Al Barsha South run MYP instead of IGCSE, which produces transfers in both directions each September. A student moving into IGCSE science for Year 11 has one term to learn a mark scheme they have never met, and that is distinct work from general science support.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Where strong IGCSE science grades lead for students staying in the IB system: Biology, Chemistry, Physics and others at Standard or Higher Level, with a Scientific Investigation worth 20% of the subject grade. Diploma sciences assume the quantitative fluency that IGCSE Extended builds and Core does not.

A student in Al Barsha South intending to take a Diploma science at Higher Level should be on an Extended or Higher tier at IGCSE, since a Core entry caps the grade below most sixth-form entry requirements.

programmes.name: A Level Sciences
programmes.description: The other post-16 route in this cluster, with practical skills assessed separately from theory. A Level Biology, Chemistry and Physics each assume the whole of the Extended or Higher IGCSE content as background, and the common first-term shock is the volume of quantitative work rather than the difficulty of the concepts.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools near Al Barsha South offer A Level sciences, and sixth-form entry commonly asks for a 6 or 7 at IGCSE in the subject. Students who took a Double Award rather than separate sciences sometimes find one specific A Level - usually Physics - harder to enter, which is a reason to check entry requirements in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-barsha-s.subjectsIntro: Science on this page means three subjects and several routes. Below are the areas where students across all four neighbourhoods lose reachable marks, with what the examiner is actually looking for in each.

subjects.name: Biology: transport in plants and animals
subjects.description: Xylem and phloem, transpiration, the heart and the double circulatory system. Marks go on describing a structure when the question asked for a function, and on omitting the direction a substance moves.

subjects.name: Biology: enzymes and the effect of variables
subjects.description: Rate against temperature and pH, denaturation, and the experimental design questions built around them. Students name the variable without saying how it would be controlled, which is where the design mark sits.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance diagrams
subjects.description: Punnett squares, ratios, codominance and sex linkage. The error is almost always notation rather than understanding: parental genotypes written without defining the allele symbols first.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles, formulae and reacting masses
subjects.description: The quantitative spine of the whole syllabus. A student who cannot carry a mole calculation through three steps will lose marks on acids, electrolysis and energetics questions that look nothing like stoichiometry.

subjects.name: Chemistry: electrolysis and electrode products
subjects.description: Predicting products at each electrode for molten and aqueous electrolytes, with half equations. The aqueous case is where students guess, because the rules about which ion is discharged are learned loosely.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic chemistry and homologous series
subjects.description: Alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids, polymers and the tests that distinguish them. Displayed formulae must show every bond, and a skeletal shortcut loses the mark however correct the molecule is.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, motion and graph interpretation
subjects.description: Distance-time and velocity-time graphs, gradient and area under the curve. The area-under-a-velocity-time-graph question is answered as a gradient more often than any other misread in the paper.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity, circuits and series-parallel reasoning
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance combinations and the reasoning about what happens when one component changes. Students know the equations and stall on the qualitative reasoning the paper actually asks for.

subjects.name: Physics: waves, refraction and ray diagrams
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, total internal reflection and lens diagrams. Ray diagram marks are awarded for construction lines and arrows, which students routinely omit while drawing the correct image.

subjects.name: Practical skills: Paper 5 and Paper 6
subjects.description: The practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, worth around a fifth of the Cambridge grade. It tests tables, graph plotting, anomalies, variables and improvements, and it is the most predictable paper in the whole set and the least practised.

subjects.name: Command terms across all three sciences
subjects.description: Describe, explain, suggest, compare and calculate each demand a different answer shape. A correct idea written as a description where an explanation was asked earns nothing, and this single habit accounts for a large share of avoidable loss.

subjects.name: Multi-step calculations with unit changes
subjects.description: Converting between units mid-calculation and carrying significant figures honestly. The physics papers punish this hardest, and the chemistry papers hide it inside mole work where the slip is harder to spot.

sections.heading: Al Barsha South against Marina, JVC and Dubai Hills, side by side
paragraphs: The comparison is worth doing properly because parents do it anyway, usually with worse information. Four things genuinely differ between these communities: the schools within reach, the exam boards those schools enter, what time a secondary student actually gets home, and the fee band of the local provision. Everything else that gets discussed - the quality of local tutors, the availability of specialists, whether one area is better served - turns out on inspection to be a function of who happens to live there this year, which is not a basis for a two-year plan.

Al Barsha South has the shortest school run of the four, because three established British-curriculum schools sit inside or on the edge of it. That produces the largest local Year 11 science cohort and, as a side effect, the most competition for the early-evening tutoring slot. Dubai Marina and JBR have the longest effective run despite being compact, because almost no secondary school sits inside the towers. Jumeirah Village has the widest spread of boards within a single building, which defeats any area-level assumption about what children there are sitting. Dubai Hills has the easiest afternoon and the highest fee band, and its science cohorts sit the same papers as everyone else.

Where this lands is a conclusion a location page is not supposed to reach: for IGCSE science, the neighbourhood is close to irrelevant. What matters is the syllabus code, the tier, and whether the tutor knows the specific paper. A family in Dubai Hills and a family in Al Barsha South whose children both sit Cambridge 0654 Extended need identical work, and a family in Al Barsha South whose child sits Pearson 4PH1 needs different work from their next-door neighbour on Cambridge 0625. The useful question is never where the tutor is. It is which paper they have marked.

sections.heading: Which science route your child is on, and why the label hides it
paragraphs: Science is the subject where the label on the school report tells a parent least. Three different routes sit under it. Separate sciences means three syllabuses and three grades. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a Double Award: one course, one grade, counted as two IGCSEs for most purposes. Combined Science 0653 is a Single Award, one grade counting once. A parent who knows only that their child does science cannot tell which of the three they are on, and all three have different papers.

Boards differ as much as routes. Cambridge separate sciences run a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper at the entered tier, and then either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper. The practical component is worth roughly a fifth of the grade, and because it is partly predictable - tables, graph plotting, anomalies, variables, suggested improvements - it is the cheapest component in the entire set to improve. Pearson's International GCSE sciences, 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, take a different approach: there is no separate practical or alternative-to-practical paper, and practical understanding is examined inside the theory papers instead.

That single difference changes what revision should look like. A Cambridge 0625 student who never practises Paper 6 is leaving a fifth of their grade to chance on a paper that rehearses almost identically every series. A Pearson 4PH1 student who spends sessions on alternative-to-practical questions is practising for a paper they will not sit. Both students look diligent and only one is aimed correctly. Finding out which applies costs nothing: the board, the syllabus code and the tier appear on the school's exam entry confirmation, and that document is the single most useful thing a parent can forward before a first session.

sections.heading: Where science marks go: the same four leaks in every neighbourhood
paragraphs: Mark a set of IGCSE science papers from four different Dubai communities and the pattern does not sort by postcode. It sorts by habit. Four leaks account for most of the avoidable loss, and they appear in the same proportions whether the student lives in a Marina tower or an Al Barsha South villa.

The first is command-term mismatch. Describe, explain, suggest, compare and calculate each demand a different answer shape, and a correct idea written as a description where an explanation was wanted earns nothing. The second is the unclaimed working mark: multi-step calculations in physics and chemistry carry method marks, and a student who writes only the final answer forfeits them whenever the arithmetic slips. The third is the practical paper nobody rehearsed, which on Cambridge routes is roughly a fifth of the grade sitting untouched. The fourth is the diagram mark: ray diagrams need construction lines and arrows, genetic crosses need allele symbols defined, and circuit answers need the component named rather than pointed at.

What makes this useful is that all four are habits rather than knowledge gaps, which means they move fast. Command terms respond to about three weeks of consistent correction. Working marks respond to the student marking their own script against the official scheme aloud. The practical paper responds to four or five past papers worked under timed conditions. Diagram marks respond to a checklist. None of this requires re-teaching content, which is why a student whose mocks came back lower than their topic tests can often recover a meaningful part of that gap without learning a single new fact.

sections.heading: What science tutoring costs across these four areas
paragraphs: Take the market from the bottom up, since that is the end most families start at. The cheapest published online rates in Dubai are Tutopiya's, from AED 33 to 52 an hour, and EdFlik's, from AED 45 to 65. At that level the tutor is typically a university student, and what the money buys is supervision and homework company rather than syllabus-code knowledge. For a Year 9 student who simply will not sit down, that may be exactly the right purchase. For a Year 11 student on Cambridge 0654 Extended eight weeks from a paper, it is not.

The next band up is where IGCSE science support actually lives. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. The step from the budget band into this one is the step from someone who can help with homework to someone who knows which paper your child sits and what its mark scheme rewards. Above it, BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium examiner-led work, which buys scarcity; whether it buys more than that depends on the individual and on whether the credential can actually be evidenced.

Separately, the travel line. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and home tutors up to AED 500, against the same providers' online bands for comparable tutors. The difference is the car. Monthly packages visible in this market run AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Those figures are each provider's own published numbers as of October 2026, not IB Gram's. Worth noting against them that KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, so a tutoring line added this year is not landing on top of a fee increase. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page; the free trial lesson comes first.

sections.heading: Online against in-home, judged on the science rather than on convenience
paragraphs: Stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one to one over live video, and visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. That needs saying on a page reached by searching for someone local, and the comparison then deserves to be made honestly rather than argued backwards from the limitation.

The in-home case for science is real in one specific respect: physical apparatus. A tutor in the room can put a thermometer, a measuring cylinder or a circuit in a student's hands, and for a nervous Year 10 that has value. What it cannot do is widen the pool. An in-home tutor has to live within a workable drive of the student and be free in the hour after the school bus, and across all four of the neighbourhoods compared above that narrows the field sharply once you add the requirement of knowing Cambridge 0654 Extended Paper 6 or Pearson 4CH1 specifically.

For the components that carry the marks, video turns out to be a close substitute. The Cambridge practical paper is a written paper about practical work, not a practical, so it is rehearsed on paper either way. Graph plotting, anomaly identification and variable control are all screen-shareable. Diagram conventions are easier to correct on a shared whiteboard than over a student's shoulder, because both parties are looking at the same magnified line. And sessions can be recorded, so a student can rewatch an electrolysis explanation at the point they lost it. The honest trade is this: in-home buys apparatus and presence from a smaller local pool at a travel premium; online buys the specialist in the exact paper, plus a recording, and asks the family for a desk and an open door.

sections.heading: The series, the zone, and counting backwards from the papers
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, which means any revision plan pointing at a spring exam window has been built for the wrong country. Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. That is the school's responsibility, but it is a fair question to ask at a parents' evening.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations run in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including for later years, which is exactly why every date here should be confirmed against the live official timetable rather than taken from a tutoring page.

The planning value is in the backwards count. Working from the first paper: the final eight to ten weeks are technique and timed papers, because content learned in that window is unreliable under pressure. The term before that is the last efficient period for closing genuine content gaps. Mocks sit before that again and are the first honest signal of the grade. Entry and tier decisions sit earliest of all and are the ones with the longest consequences, since a Core or Foundation entry caps the grade regardless of how well the student performs on the day. A family in any of these four neighbourhoods starting in September has a content term and a technique term. A family starting in March for a June series has a technique term only, and the plan should say so rather than pretend otherwise.

sections.heading: KHDA, permits and the two checks worth making before you pay anyone
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a report per school across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, broken down by subject and phase. For a family comparing schools across Al Barsha South, Jumeirah Village and Dubai Hills, those reports are the only independent evidence available, and the secondary-science attainment line is the one that matters for a Year 11 student. Context: Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering 17 curricula, with seven new schools opening for 2026-27 creating 16,846 places after enrolment rose 6% during 2025-26.

The second check is the tutor's permit. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time via the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is invented.

Two related points. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school; these are press-reported positions worth verifying against the current policy document, but the direction is clear and applies to the convenient option of hiring your child's own science teacher. And an operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram runs no UAE centre and holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB.

sections.heading: Honesty boundaries, and what we will not do with your child's work
paragraphs: IGCSE sciences at both boards are examined by written paper, which removes most of the coursework risk that shadows Diploma and A Level tutoring. The boundary still matters, because students in this cluster often carry subjects that do involve assessed work, and because the practical components invite a particular kind of shortcut. The rule we apply everywhere: a tutor teaches, explains, marks and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not produce the work.

In practice that means a tutor may work a past-paper question through with a student, mark their attempt against the published scheme, explain exactly which line earned which mark, set comparable questions on different material, and model a method on a question the student is not submitting. A tutor may not sit with a student during a timed school assessment, supply answers to anything that will be handed in, write or part-write coursework, or edit a piece of work into a submittable state. Providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments. That is an integrity breach, the consequences land on the student rather than the seller, and it is not something IB Gram offers at any price.

There is a second boundary around materials, and for a science family it is reassuring rather than restrictive. We reference Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables and link to the board's own page; we do not reproduce or supply them as downloads. Everything a student needs for 0610, 0620, 0625, 0654, 4BI1, 4CH1 or 4PH1 preparation is published free by the board itself. What a good tutor adds is knowing which question to set next and how to mark it honestly, which is not something a private library can substitute for.
