sections.heading: Getting started, and what we will tell you that others will not
paragraphs: The first step is a free trial lesson, and it begins with one document: the school's exam entry confirmation, which carries the board, the syllabus code and the tier. With that in hand the trial becomes a diagnostic rather than a demonstration. The student works a section of the correct past paper live, the tutor marks it against the published scheme while the student watches, and the four leaks are counted. What a parent receives afterwards is a topic-accuracy list and a straight view on whether one science or three need support, and whether one session a week or two is the right place to start.

Matching takes a few days rather than minutes, because the match is to a code. Cambridge 0620 Extended, 0625 Extended and 0654 requests fill quickly, as do the main Pearson codes. The requests that stall are narrower: a Single Award route combined with a specific practical-paper focus and one fixed slot, for instance. When that happens we say so. The options are to wait a week, to move the slot, or to begin with a strong generalist on a clearly stated interim basis, and we will tell you which one is on the table rather than placing someone and describing them as a specialist.

One more thing worth saying on a page built around a comparison. If after reading this you conclude that your child's science problem is really a school-fit problem, or a timetable problem, or a tier-entry problem, then the right next step is a conversation with the school rather than a tutoring contract. Tier entry in particular is a school decision with a hard consequence - a capped grade - and it deserves marked evidence rather than a tutor's reassurance. We would rather tell a family that before they pay for a month of lessons than after.

faqs.question: Would my child get a better science tutor in Dubai Marina or Dubai Hills than in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: No, and the comparison is worth making rather than dismissing. These communities genuinely differ in school options, commute and fee band: Al Barsha South has the shortest school run and the largest local cohort, Marina has almost no secondary provision inside its towers, Jumeirah Village spreads several exam boards across single buildings, and Dubai Hills has the easiest afternoon. None of that changes what a science student needs, which is a tutor who knows their exact syllabus code and tier. Proximity is the one variable in this subject that carries no educational value.

faqs.question: What is the difference between separate sciences, Double Award and Combined Science?
faqs.answer: Separate sciences means three syllabuses and three grades - for Cambridge, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a Double Award: one course, one grade, counted as two IGCSEs. Combined Science 0653 is a Single Award counting once. The routes cover overlapping content at different depths and sit different papers, and they also carry different implications for sixth-form entry, since some A Level science courses prefer the separate route. Check which one your child is entered for on the school's exam entry confirmation rather than assuming from the timetable.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a practical exam for IGCSE science in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board. Cambridge separate sciences and Co-ordinated Sciences include either a practical test or a written alternative-to-practical paper, worth roughly a fifth of the grade. Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE sciences take a different approach and assess practical understanding inside the written theory papers, with no separate practical component. This distinction decides what revision should look like: a Cambridge candidate who never practises the alternative-to-practical paper is leaving a fifth of the grade unrehearsed, and a Pearson candidate practising those papers is preparing for an exam they will not sit.

faqs.question: Which single science component is easiest to improve quickly?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge routes, the practical test or alternative-to-practical paper, without much competition. It is worth about a fifth of the grade and it rehearses almost identically each series: tables with correct headings and units, graph plotting and line of best fit, identifying an anomaly, naming independent and control variables, and suggesting an improvement that would actually address a named problem. Four or five past practical papers worked under timed conditions will move it, and most schools are too pressed for curriculum time to drill it properly. It is the cheapest set of marks in the course.

faqs.question: My child's topic tests are fine but the mock paper was poor. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Usually habit rather than knowledge. Topic tests examine one idea in a familiar format; a full paper examines command terms, timing, diagram conventions and multi-step working all at once. Four leaks account for most of the gap: answering a describe question when explain was asked, writing a final answer with no working so method marks go unclaimed, leaving diagram marks on the table through missing arrows and labels, and running out of time on the last pages. All four respond to a few weeks of correction without any new content, which is why this kind of drop is often the fastest to recover.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for IGCSE science tutoring in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates spread very widely. The cheapest online bands are Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, typically university-student tutors offering supervision rather than syllabus knowledge. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 table puts IGCSE, IB and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350. BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium examiner-led work. Those are each provider's own figures, not IB Gram's; we run a free trial first.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all three sciences for my child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being sceptical. A tutor with a genuine background in one science can usually teach IGCSE level in a second competently, and the third is where claims start to stretch. For a student on Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, a single well-matched tutor is often the right arrangement because the course itself is integrated. For a student on three separate sciences who is behind in all three, two tutors with a written rotation generally works better than one covering everything. Ask which science the tutor actually studied beyond school level.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to our home in Al Barsha South or JVC?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. UAE lessons are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For science the in-home advantage is apparatus in the student's hands, which is real for a nervous younger student. Against that, the Cambridge practical paper is itself a written paper about practical work, so it is rehearsed on paper either way, and widening past the drive is what makes a code-specific specialist available at all.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE science exams happen for a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a plan built around a spring window is built for another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and results reaching students in January. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six timetable zones and warns that the correct zone version must be used. Confirm every date on the board's live timetable.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to start science tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10, for a reason that has nothing to do with selling more lessons. Year 10 is the only period when learning new content is genuinely efficient, because there is time for it to settle and be tested twice. By the middle of Year 11 most schools have finished the content and moved to revision, so a gap that opens then will not be retaught and the tutoring has to run two tracks at once. Starting in Year 10 also means the tier decision - Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher - can be made on evidence from marked papers rather than on a guess.

faqs.question: How do I check that a science tutor is legally allowed to work in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the permit, not a profile. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is issued through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service with no fee and a stated two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. u.ae states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule is published, so any specific figure quoted at you is invented.

faqs.question: Why does the exam entry confirmation matter more than the school report?
faqs.answer: Because the report describes your child and the entry confirmation describes the examination. It carries the board, the syllabus code and the tier, and those three facts decide what practice is useful. A Pearson 4CH1 candidate and a Cambridge 0620 Extended candidate taking the same lessons are being prepared for different papers, and one of them is being prepared wrongly. The confirmation also reveals a capped entry early enough to challenge it: a Core or Foundation entry limits the grade regardless of performance, and that is a school conversation worth having in Year 10.

faqs.question: Can we pause science sessions during school exams or over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we would usually recommend it. A student sitting internal examinations does not gain from a tutoring session the same evening, so sessions pause and the slot is held rather than lost. Summer works the same way, with the exception of students entering Year 11 who have a known content gap, where a short summer block is genuinely more efficient than trying to close it alongside term-time revision. Sessions also shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan for families who prefer it. The one period we advise against pausing is the eight weeks before the papers.

faqs.question: What if the problem turns out to be the school rather than my child?
faqs.answer: Then we will say so, and the right next step is the school rather than a tutoring contract. KHDA inspects every Dubai private school annually and publishes a report broken down by subject and phase, so a school rated Good overall may be rated Acceptable for secondary science attainment, and a note that internal assessment data does not match external outcomes explains a predicted grade that never arrives. Dubai had 227 private schools in 2024-25 with seven more opening for 2026-27, so department-level variation between neighbouring schools is normal rather than scandalous.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for my child's exact syllabus code?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting quietly. The mainstream codes - Cambridge 0620 and 0625 Extended, 0654, the main Pearson suite - usually match within a few days. The requests that stall are narrow: a Single Award route combined with a practical-paper focus and one fixed evening slot, for instance. The honest options then are to wait a week, to move the slot, or to start with a strong generalist on a clearly stated interim basis. What we will not do is place a general science tutor and present them as a code specialist, which is standard practice in this market.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-barsha-s.closingHeading: Send the entry confirmation, and let the paper decide the plan

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-furjan.tutorsIntro: These are the science tutors an Al Furjan family is matched with for Years 9 to 11. Each works to one board and one award, and can say whether your child's entry carries a laboratory paper or the written alternative.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one afternoon
paragraphs: A student taking Biology, Chemistry and Physics as separate IGCSEs has three departments setting homework, three sets of practical write-ups and three revision loads, all landing inside the same week. In Al Furjan that week begins late. The school buses loop across the Quortaj, Masakin, Dar and Murooj districts, so arrival runs from 15:20 to 16:10, and a Year 11 student who stayed for a revision clinic is home closer to 16:30.

The arithmetic that follows is the reason this page exists. If three sciences each need attention and the usable evening starts at 17:00, then a single ninety-minute tutoring session covering everything is not a plan. What works in this community is targeted: one science at a time, chosen on the evidence of marked work, in a slot that holds through fixtures and traffic, with the other two carried by school teaching and set work.

The second question is what your child is actually entered for, because science entries vary more than any other subject area. Some schools enter the three separate sciences: Cambridge 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, or the Pearson equivalents 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Others enter Cambridge 0654 Coordinated Sciences as a double award, or 0653 Combined Science as a single award. Pearson offers Double and Single Award routes too.

That distinction changes everything downstream: how much content there is, how the papers are structured, how a weakness in one discipline affects the others, and what post-16 study it allows. A tutor who does not know which award your child sits is working blind, and a parent who does not know is unable to judge the advice they receive. The school's exams officer holds the entry list that settles it.

IB Gram matches on the board and the award, and delivers every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. The practical benefit for a family here is scheduling flexibility: an 18:30 session is routine over video and effectively impossible for someone driving into the villa districts in evening traffic.

What follows covers the awards side by side, how to schedule three sciences in a week shaped by the Al Furjan bus, what the practical and data papers actually examine, where marks go in each discipline, and what happens when one science drags a double award down. UAE candidates sit the June and November series; Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so any plan quoting a February exam window to a Dubai family is working from another country's calendar. The document that matters is your school's own zone timetable, since Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong version can cost a candidate an exam.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-furjan.programmesIntro: Science support divides into four stages in this corridor, and each needs something different. The handover into Year 10 is where most of the trouble starts.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 science, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The three years where practical and processing habits form, or fail to. Four things matter: reading an instrument to the right precision, tabulating with units in the headings, plotting a sensible scale with a line of best fit, and naming a control variable with a reason. None is assessed externally and all four are examined from Year 10 onward in every science.
programmes.countryNote: Year 7 to 9 students in Al Furjan are home earlier than exam-year students, often by 16:00, so a 16:30 slot works comfortably. This is the cheapest stage to buy support and the one skipped. A term spent on practical technique in Year 9 pays back across three sciences for two years, which is a better return than anything available in Year 11.

programmes.name: IGCSE sciences, Years 10 to 11
programmes.description: Either three separate sciences, a double award covering all three disciplines, or a single combined award. Entries carry either a laboratory examination or a written alternative-to-practical paper, depending on board and school. Most lost marks are procedural: units misplaced, graphs badly scaled, methods described without controls named, anomalies identified but not explained.
programmes.countryNote: This is where nearly all Al Furjan enquiries sit. Year 10 students are home between 15:40 and 16:10 on local routes; Year 11 students with revision clinics are later. The workable pattern is one science at a time in a 17:00 or 17:30 slot, rotating focus by term according to which discipline the marked work says is weakest.

programmes.name: Double and single award science
programmes.description: Cambridge 0654 Coordinated Sciences is a double award and 0653 Combined Science a single award; Pearson runs Double and Single Award routes. Content is reduced relative to three separate sciences, but all three disciplines still appear in the papers, so a student weak in one carries that weakness into every paper rather than into one grade.
programmes.countryNote: This is the entry decision Al Furjan families understand least well, and it has post-16 consequences. Some schools require separate sciences for Advanced Level study in a science subject, and IB Diploma Higher Level science entry often expects the same. Checking what the intended post-16 school asks for, in Year 10, is worth more than any amount of Year 11 revision.

programmes.name: Advanced Level or IB Diploma sciences
programmes.description: Both routes normally require grade 6 or 7 in the relevant science and both expect quantitative handling that IGCSE does not demand: uncertainty propagation, extended written explanation built from a named principle, and independent investigation design. The gap is procedural and mathematical rather than conceptual.
programmes.countryNote: Families in this corridor usually change schools for the IB Diploma, since full Diploma provision nearby is limited. Four to six bridging sessions over the summer on uncertainty, graph work and extended response removes one of the variables from a first term that already includes a new school and a new teaching style.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-furjan.subjectsIntro: Science requests from this corridor cover the three disciplines and the combined awards. Each note names the code to check on the entry list and where that subject's marks actually go.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, genetics, ecology and human physiology. Punishes imprecise language above all: an answer saying a value increases, without naming the mechanism and direction, scores nothing. Genetic crosses and the required practical techniques are the two areas where a few sessions change the grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Atomic structure, bonding, moles and stoichiometry, organic chemistry and chemical tests. Mole calculations and the chemical tests account for most lost marks. Tests must be answered as an observation plus a conclusion, because the paper asks what would be seen and what it shows, and credits each separately.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves, thermal physics and radioactivity. Graph gradients, unit conversion and describing an experiment without naming controls are the reliable losses. Electricity is the topic students report as hardest and is rarely where their marks are actually going.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences, double award
subjects.description: All three disciplines in a reduced-content double award. The structural risk is that a weakness in one discipline appears in every paper rather than in one grade, so a student strong in biology and weak in physics scores below their biology ability across the whole award.

subjects.name: Combined Science, single award
subjects.description: A single award covering all three disciplines with further reduced content. Suits a student whose strengths lie outside science, and it needs checking against post-16 plans: some schools will not accept it as preparation for Advanced Level study in a science subject.

subjects.name: Double and Single Award Science
subjects.description: Pearson offers Double and Single Award routes alongside the separate 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 entries. Paper structure and practical assessment differ from the Cambridge equivalents, which is why the board as well as the award has to be confirmed before any revision plan is built.

subjects.name: Practical and alternative-to-practical skills
subjects.description: Depending on the entry, a candidate sits either a laboratory examination or a written paper testing the same skills: reading instruments, tabulating, plotting, identifying anomalies and describing methods with controls named. Narrow, trainable, examined, and the best value per session in the whole science syllabus.

subjects.name: Data handling and graph work
subjects.description: Units in table headings rather than cells, scales that fill the grid, lines of best fit read for gradient rather than dot-to-dot plotting, and anomalies explained rather than circled. Each is a mark, the set of them is often a grade, and none requires a laboratory to practise.

subjects.name: Mathematics within the sciences
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, percentages, ratios, standard form and unit conversion. A student who understands the science and stalls on the arithmetic needs mathematics support rather than more science, and one session with a marked paper distinguishes the two cases reliably.

subjects.name: Scientific writing and command terms
subjects.description: Describe, explain, suggest and compare each require a different answer shape, and a knowledgeable answer to the wrong command earns little. Written answers marked against the command used, then rewritten once, is slower work than content review and the reason it moves grades.

subjects.name: Additional science reading for post-16
subjects.description: For students heading to Advanced Level or IB Diploma sciences, the summer gap is uncertainty treatment, extended explanation and investigation design. Four to six sessions covers it and is far cheaper than catching up in the first post-16 term.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. They sit on the same timetable as three sciences, which is part of why the Al Furjan week is as full as it is.

sections.heading: Separate sciences, double award or single award
paragraphs: This is the first thing to establish and the thing families most often cannot answer. Cambridge enters separate sciences as 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics; Coordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award; and Combined Science 0653 as a single award. Pearson Edexcel enters separate sciences as 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with Double and Single Award routes alongside. The school's exams officer holds the entry list that names which applies.

The practical differences go beyond content volume. In a combined or coordinated award, all three disciplines appear within the same papers, so a student who is strong in biology and weak in physics does not get a good biology grade and a poor physics grade. They get one grade pulled down by the physics content inside every paper. That structural fact changes where tutoring hours should go.

With separate sciences the opposite applies: each grade stands alone, so a weak discipline is contained. That makes separate entries more forgiving of unevenness and more demanding in total workload, which is the trade-off a Year 9 family is actually making when the school asks for option choices. Three separate sciences means three sets of homework in an afternoon that starts at 17:00.

The post-16 consequence is the part worth checking early. Some schools require separate sciences before accepting a science at Advanced Level, and IB Diploma Higher Level science entry often expects the same. The reliable method is asking the intended post-16 school what it requires, in Year 10, while the entry can still be influenced. Finding out in Year 11 leaves nothing to decide.

sections.heading: Fitting three sciences into an Al Furjan week
paragraphs: Start with the real timings. Buses serving the Al Furjan villas arrive between 15:20 and 16:10 depending on the district and the school, with Year 11 students staying for revision clinics home closer to 16:30. Students travelling the Al Barsha or Al Khail corridor arrive later still. After a snack and a change of clothes the usable study window runs from about 17:00 to 20:30, and school homework has first claim on it.

Within that window, three sciences cannot each get a tutored session. What works is choosing one discipline at a time on the evidence of the paper-level breakdown, running a weekly session on it, and reviewing the choice each term. Depth in the weakest subject moves a grade; a weekly rotation across all three moves nothing, because nothing gets enough continuity to stick.

The exception is the practical and data skills block, which is genuinely three-for-one. Instrument reading, tabulation, plotting, anomaly explanation and method description with controls named are examined in all three sciences in similar form. Four to six sessions on those improves marks across biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously, which is the only shortcut available in this subject area and the one most families never hear about.

On placement: book the slot that survives a bad afternoon rather than a good one. A fixture, a clinic and a traffic delay will each happen. Families who book optimistically lose two sessions a month, and over a term in three sciences that is a significant share of the support they paid for. Online delivery helps here too, since a missed session can move to the next evening rather than the next week.

sections.heading: The practical paper, and why it is the cheapest grade on offer
paragraphs: Every science entry assesses practical skill, either through a laboratory examination or through a written alternative-to-practical paper that tests the same competencies on paper. Which applies depends on the board and the school's entry, and it is worth asking, because the preparation differs in form though not in content. What does not differ is how predictable the marks are.

The skills are narrow. Reading an instrument to the precision it supports. Tabulating results with the unit in the heading rather than in the cells. Choosing a scale so the plotted data fills most of the grid. Drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points. Identifying an anomaly and explaining it rather than circling it. Naming a control variable and saying how it was controlled. Stating a conclusion that answers the hypothesis.

Each of those is worth marks, none requires a laboratory to practise, and together they frequently amount to a grade. For a student taking a coordinated or combined award, the same skills are examined across all three disciplines in the same paper, so the return is multiplied. This is why a practical skills block is the single best-value purchase in IGCSE science support.

The errors are consistent across every cohort we see, which is itself informative: units written into the cells, a graph occupying a quarter of the grid, a method claiming the temperature was kept the same without saying how, an anomaly noticed and left unexplained, and a conclusion that restates the data instead of answering the question. A tutor who starts there rather than with content is reading the evidence correctly.

sections.heading: Where marks go in each of the three sciences
paragraphs: Asking which topics are hardest produces the same answer in every household: electricity in physics, moles in chemistry, genetics in biology. Asking where the marks actually go produces something more useful, because it is specific and mostly fixable. The losses differ by discipline and a tutor should be able to name them for the subject they are teaching before any content is covered.

In biology the dominant loss is imprecise language. The subject requires naming a mechanism and a direction, so an answer stating that something increases earns nothing even when the student understands the process. Genetic crosses are the second area, lost on notation and layout rather than on understanding, and the required practical techniques are the third. All three respond quickly to marked written practice.

In chemistry the losses are mole arithmetic and chemical tests. Everything quantitative routes through moles, so weakness there shows up as poor marks in topics the student understands. Chemical tests are lost because they were learned as a list: the paper asks what would be seen and what that shows, and credits the observation and the conclusion separately, so a list-based answer collects half the marks at best.

In physics the losses are mathematical and procedural. Gradients read from plotted points rather than from the line of best fit. Unit conversion errors, particularly with prefixes. Experiment descriptions with no control variables named. Electricity is reported as the hardest topic and is usually not where the marks are going, which is a good example of why a plan should be built from a marked paper rather than from a student's sense of difficulty.

sections.heading: When one science drags a double award down
paragraphs: In a coordinated or combined award, all three disciplines appear inside the same papers, which produces a specific and common pattern: a student who is comfortable in two sciences and struggling in one scores below their ability across the entire award. There is no separate grade for the strong subjects to protect them. This is the single most useful diagnostic fact about double award science and it is rarely explained to parents.

The implication for tutoring is that the weak discipline is the whole job. Where a family with three separate entries might reasonably split hours across subjects, a double award family should concentrate on the one discipline costing marks in every paper. Spreading hours evenly in that situation is the most expensive way to make no difference, and it is what most generic revision plans do.

Identifying which discipline is responsible needs the paper-level breakdown, which schools hold and often do not send out. A grade 5 in a coordinated award can come from weak physics content inside every paper, from poor practical skills applied across all three disciplines, or from command-term errors in extended answers. Those three need entirely different interventions, and guessing between them wastes a term.

There is also a timing point. If the award looks wrong for the student's post-16 intentions, that is a Year 10 conversation with the school rather than a Year 11 one, because entries close months before the papers. A tutor reading marked work in the autumn of Year 10 can give a parent a view in time to act. The same reading in the spring of Year 11 is information rather than a decision.

sections.heading: The June series, three sciences deep
paragraphs: A student sitting three separate sciences has a different exam fortnight from one sitting a single award, and planning for it belongs in the autumn rather than in May. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

That makes the school's own zone timetable the planning document, not a generic one downloaded from the internet. For a three-science candidate it shows how the papers stack: how many sit in the same week, whether two land on one day, and where the gaps fall. Those gaps are where the last useful revision happens, and knowing them in advance changes how the preceding months are used.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Published dates give a sense of the calendar's reach: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and keep their dates; forward planning should use the live official timetable.

Counted backwards, the year has a clear shape for a science candidate. Entries close months ahead and fix the award and tier. Practical or coursework components complete before the written papers. Mocks sit in the winter. Study leave frees the afternoon for whole papers. Then the series, results in August for June entries, and a narrow window to consider a November resit. A family that maps this in September spends less for a better result.

sections.heading: What a science tutor will not do
paragraphs: Science entries involve work produced in school, and some providers in this market treat that as an opportunity. One advertises completed internal assessments for the IB at a fixed price, and the same logic gets applied to school science coursework. The consequence falls on the student: submitted work that is not their own is malpractice, and the entry or the grade is what is at risk rather than the seller's revenue.

The legitimate work is substantial. A tutor can teach the practical technique the task requires, explain what each part of the assessment rewards, question a method until the controls make sense, show how a published write-up is structured, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. That is teaching, and in the sciences most of the recoverable marks live inside it because the losses are procedural.

What a tutor must not do is write, rewrite, process the student's results, supply content for a submission, or outline a piece for the student to fill in. IB Gram tutors state that at the first session of any coursework block and give feedback in writing, so that a school asking what support was received gets an answer that holds up. A tutor who does not raise that boundary is one to be careful with.

On materials, we do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are cited and linked, and sessions work from what the school has issued. We also do not guarantee grades in any science, and we do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence of current status, since examiner status confers no access to marking or paper content in any case.

whyPoints.description: We ask for the paper-level breakdown before recommending anything. In a double award that single document distinguishes a physics content gap from a practical skills gap from a command-term problem, and those need three different plans.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the workload
whyPoints.description: Three sciences cannot all be tutored in one weekly session, and we say so rather than selling a session that passes shallowly over everything. Depth in the weakest discipline moves a grade; a weekly rotation across three moves nothing.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is India-only. No completed coursework, no reproduced mark schemes, no grade guarantees. If no specialist is free for your board and slot, we say so instead of substituting one.

faqs.question: Is my child in Al Furjan taking three separate sciences or a combined award?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the entry list, which names the board, the codes and the award. Cambridge enters separate sciences as 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, Coordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award, and Combined Science 0653 as a single award. Pearson runs 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 alongside Double and Single Award routes. The distinction matters because in a combined award a weak discipline appears in every paper rather than being contained in one grade.

faqs.question: How can three sciences be covered in one tutoring session a week?
faqs.answer: They cannot, and a provider claiming otherwise is selling a session that passes shallowly over everything. What works is one discipline at a time, chosen from the paper-level breakdown, with the choice reviewed each term and switched when the evidence changes. The exception is a practical and data skills block, which genuinely improves all three at once because the same competencies are examined in each. Four to six sessions on those is the only real shortcut in IGCSE science.

faqs.question: Why is the practical paper the best value work in IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Because the skills are narrow, examined and rarely practised. Reading an instrument to the right precision, putting units in the table heading, scaling a graph so the data fills the grid, drawing a line of best fit, naming a control variable with a method for controlling it, explaining an anomaly, and stating a conclusion that answers the hypothesis. Each is a mark, the set is often a grade, and none needs a laboratory. In a combined award the same skills earn marks across all three disciplines.

faqs.question: My child has a grade 5 in Coordinated Sciences. What do I ask the school?
faqs.answer: For the paper-level breakdown, and specifically which discipline and which skill is responsible. A grade 5 in a double award can come from weak physics content appearing in every paper, from poor practical skills applied across all three disciplines, or from command-term errors in extended answers. Those three need entirely different interventions, and guessing between them wastes a term. Schools hold this detail and frequently do not send it out unless a parent asks directly.

faqs.question: Does a single or double award limit what my child can study at 16?
faqs.answer: It can. Some schools require separate sciences before accepting a science subject at Advanced Level, and IB Diploma Higher Level science entry often expects the same. A single combined award is frequently insufficient for continuing with a science. The reliable method is to ask the intended post-16 school directly what it requires, in Year 10, while the entry can still be influenced. Finding out in the spring of Year 11 leaves nothing to decide, because entries closed months earlier.

faqs.question: What time can a science session start for a Year 11 student in the villa districts?
faqs.answer: Usually 17:00, and 18:00 if your child travels the Al Barsha or Al Khail corridor. Buses serving Al Furjan arrive between 15:20 and 16:10 depending on district and school, and Year 11 students staying for revision clinics are home closer to 16:30. Children on Dubai Investments Park or Green Community routes can start at 15:50. Book the slot that holds after a fixture and a traffic delay rather than the one that works on a quick afternoon.

faqs.question: Where do biology marks actually go wrong?
faqs.answer: In language precision above everything. Biology requires naming a mechanism and a direction, so an answer saying that a value increases earns nothing even when the student understands the process perfectly. The second area is genetic crosses, lost on notation and layout rather than on understanding, and the third is the required practical techniques. All three respond quickly to marked written practice, which is slower work for a tutor than talking through content and the reason it moves grades.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose chemistry marks on the chemical tests?
faqs.answer: Because the tests were learned as a list. The paper asks what would be seen and what that shows, and credits the observation and the conclusion separately, so a student who recalls a list of results collects half the available marks at best. The other reliable chemistry loss is mole arithmetic, which everything quantitative routes through; weakness there shows up as poor marks in topics the student genuinely understands. Two to four sessions of pure arithmetic practice usually settles that one.

faqs.question: Is electricity really the hardest physics topic for IGCSE students?
faqs.answer: It is the topic most students name and usually not where their marks are going. The actual physics losses are procedural: gradients read from plotted points instead of from the line of best fit, unit conversion errors with prefixes, and experiment descriptions with no control variables named. That gap between where a student feels weak and where the marks go is the main argument for building a plan from a marked paper rather than from the student's sense of difficulty.

faqs.question: When do UAE candidates sit IGCSE science exams?
faqs.answer: In the June series and the November series. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so a plan built around a February window uses another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct zone timetable, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: How should a three-science candidate use the zone timetable?
faqs.answer: As the planning document for the final term. It shows how the papers stack: how many sit in the same week, whether two land on one day, and where the gaps fall. Those gaps are where the last useful revision happens, and knowing them months ahead changes how the preceding term is used. Get it from the school rather than downloading a generic timetable, because the zone version is the one that applies to your child's centre.

faqs.question: Should we use one tutor for biology, chemistry and physics, or three?
faqs.answer: For practical and data skills, yes, and that is the efficient case, because those competencies are shared across the disciplines. For content at Year 11 level it is worth checking rather than assuming: marking a biology explanation and marking a physics calculation are different skills, and a tutor comfortable in two disciplines and stretched in the third will show it. Where one tutor genuinely covers all three to the level needed we will say so, and where they do not we will say that too.

faqs.question: What is the best use of study leave for a science student?
faqs.answer: Whole timed papers, marked, with errors grouped by cause rather than by topic, and the practical skills work finished before study leave rather than during it. Three sessions a week is a workable intensity once the school day has gone. What does not work is a full syllabus review across three sciences, because there is no time to consolidate it. Book this fortnight months ahead; it is the most contested period in the Dubai tutoring year.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic alongside three sciences in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. That sits on the same timetable as three sciences, which is a large part of why the Al Furjan week is as full as it is and why one tutored session has to be chosen carefully.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write up my child's school science coursework?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the technique the task requires, explain what each part rewards, question a method until the controls make sense, show how a published write-up is structured, and give written feedback on your child's own draft. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it, process the results or supply content for the submission. That boundary is stated at the first session of any coursework block and feedback is given in writing, so a school asking what help was received gets a clear answer.

faqs.question: What should a Year 9 family in this corridor do before science options are chosen?
faqs.answer: Two things, both free. Ask the intended post-16 school what science entries it requires, since that determines whether separate sciences are necessary. Then spend a term on practical and processing technique: instrument reading, tabulation, plotting, control variables. Those habits are examined from Year 10 onward in every science entry and are never formally taught again. A term in Year 9 on them pays back across three subjects for two years, which no Year 11 intervention can match.

intro.heading: The honest answer to "does anyone near me know this syllabus" starts with naming the syllabus
paragraphs: Parents in Al Garhoud searching for an IGCSE science tutor are usually asking whether anyone reachable actually understands the course their child is sitting. It is the right question, and it cannot be answered until the course is named. IGCSE science is not one qualification. It is a family of them, and a Dubai school may enter pupils for any of seven realistic combinations across two boards. A tutor who knows Cambridge separate Physics inside out is not automatically the right tutor for a Pearson Edexcel Double Award candidate, and six weeks of mismatched past papers is six weeks gone.

Here is the shape of it. Cambridge runs separate Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625; Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award covering all three; Combined Science 0653 as a single award; and Physical Science 0652 covering chemistry and physics only. Pearson Edexcel runs separate Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1; Science Double Award 4SD0; and Human Biology 4HB1. Each of these has its own paper structure, its own content depth, its own tiering arrangement where one exists, and its own practical or Alternative to Practical component. Schools around Al Garhoud, Festival City and Oud Metha use different ones, and some use more than one for different cohorts.

That is the first thing a competent tutor will ask you, and the first thing to be suspicious about if they do not. The second question is which papers your child is entered for, because a route like Co-ordinated Sciences compresses three subjects into a double award, meaning the content is broader and shallower than separate sciences and the revision strategy has to be different. A pupil who prepares for 0654 by working through separate-science past papers will spend time on material that is not on their syllabus while missing the breadth the actual papers demand.

The third is the practical component. Most IGCSE science routes assess experimental skills, and in the UAE many candidates sit an Alternative to Practical written paper rather than a laboratory examination. That paper tests the same reasoning, reading apparatus diagrams, identifying variables, spotting sources of error, interpreting a results table, but it tests it in writing, and it is a distinct skill that is routinely under-prepared. Confirm with the school which route your child's centre uses, because it changes what the last six weeks should look like.

Lessons here are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For a subject family this fragmented that matters practically rather than philosophically: matching on geography means accepting whoever teaches science within a short drive of the airport perimeter, while matching online means finding someone who teaches your child's specific code every week.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: Science tutoring is efficient when it targets a named paper and a named weakness. These are the strands Al Garhoud families most often buy time on, across the biology, chemistry and physics content of the IGCSE routes.

subjects.name: Biology: transport, respiration and photosynthesis
subjects.description: High-yield content that is reliably examined and reliably half-learned. Marks go on explaining a process in sequence rather than naming it, and candidates lose them by describing what happens without giving the reason the question asked for.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics, inheritance and variation
subjects.description: Punnett square questions are mechanical and should be free marks; they are lost to careless labelling of gametes and to confusing genotype with phenotype in the final answer. Extended content on variation and selection needs precise use of terminology.

subjects.name: Biology: human physiology and homeostasis
subjects.description: Negative feedback questions require a loop described in order, and partial answers earn partial marks. Students who learn diagrams without the sequence tend to produce answers that contain the right words in the wrong causal order.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles, formulae and equations
subjects.description: The quantitative spine of the subject and the single best use of early tutoring hours. An insecure mole concept corrupts titration, yield and concentration work for the rest of the course, and it is fixable in three or four focused sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry: rates, energetics and reversible reactions
subjects.description: Collision theory explanations are marked for the named factor and its effect, not for enthusiasm. Le Chatelier-style reversible reaction questions want a direction and a reason, and the reason is where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and separation techniques
subjects.description: Homologous series, functional groups and the standard reactions are learnable and should be secure. Separation technique questions reward a candidate who can justify the method chosen from the properties of the mixture rather than recite a list.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, motion and moments
subjects.description: Free-body reasoning and moments questions are lost to diagrams drawn carelessly rather than to misunderstood physics. Every subsequent line of working inherits an omitted force, so the diagram is the mark-bearing step.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The most common loss point in IGCSE physics. Series and parallel reasoning, potential difference versus current, and component behaviour appear as questions requiring argument rather than formula substitution, and roughly half the available marks go to explanation.

subjects.name: Physics: waves, light and sound
subjects.description: Ray diagrams must be drawn to a convention and are marked against it. Refraction and total internal reflection questions reward accurate construction; candidates who sketch freehand lose marks they understood perfectly well.

subjects.name: Experimental skills and the Alternative to Practical paper
subjects.description: A distinct skill and the most under-prepared component across every science route. It tests reading apparatus diagrams, identifying independent and dependent variables, naming a source of error and suggesting an improvement, all in writing and under time pressure.

subjects.name: Graph work, tables and data interpretation
subjects.description: Plotting accurately, choosing a sensible scale, drawing a line of best fit and reading a value from a curve. These carry marks on every science paper, transfer across all three subjects, and are usually quicker to fix than any content topic.

subjects.name: Command terms and answer length
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, calculate and compare each demand a different answer shape. The cheapest grade movement in the final term is teaching a candidate to read the command term and write the required number of points, rather than writing more.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE science is your child actually taking?
paragraphs: This is the section to read before any other. The phrase IGCSE science covers at least seven distinct entries, and the differences are not cosmetic. They affect how many papers a pupil sits, how deep the content goes, what grade is available, and what past papers are useful. A tutor who starts teaching before this is settled is guessing, and so are you.

The practical step is one email to the school's exams officer asking for the syllabus code and the paper numbers your child is entered for. Most schools answer within a day. The codes are short and unambiguous, and once you have them every other decision becomes simple: you can find the live syllabus on the board's own site, you can tell a tutor exactly what you need, and you can check that the past papers being used are the right ones.

The route also changes the shape of the problem. Separate sciences give depth in each subject and three sets of papers to prepare. Co-ordinated Sciences compresses all three into a double award, which means broader coverage at shallower depth and a different revision strategy: a candidate who knows a few topics very well and others not at all is more exposed on a coordinated paper than on a separate one, because the paper samples across everything. Combined Science as a single award narrows further again.

The table below sets the routes side by side. Treat it as an orientation rather than a specification: paper structures are revised, and the authoritative source is the live syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com plus your own school's entry information. What the table is for is making sure the conversation with a prospective tutor starts in the right place.

sections.heading: Who can actually teach three sciences well, and who cannot
paragraphs: The second honest answer on this page is about the tutor rather than the syllabus. A great many people can teach one IGCSE science to Extended standard. Rather fewer can teach two. Very few can teach all three convincingly at that depth, and a tutor who claims all three without qualification is worth probing rather than dismissing. The probe is simple: ask which of the three they teach most weeks, and ask the same question about the one they mention last.

This matters most for coordinated and double award candidates, because their weakness is usually spread across subjects rather than concentrated in one. The instinct is to find a single tutor for the whole award. The better arrangement is often two tutors with a shared plan, each covering what they teach every week, with the graph work, data interpretation and command-term technique taught once by whichever of them does it best and applied across all three. That is cheaper than it sounds, because those transferable skills are a single block rather than three.

For separate science candidates the calculation is different. A pupil losing marks in physics and secure in biology and chemistry needs one tutor for one subject, and the honest advice is to buy that rather than a three-subject package. Packages are sold because they are easier to sell, not because a pupil needs them. A single weekly lesson on the subject that is actually costing marks, plus independent past-paper work in the other two, is usually the right purchase.

Availability shapes this too, and it is worth stating plainly rather than implying unlimited supply. Biology and chemistry coverage at IGCSE level is comfortable. Physics at Extended depth is tighter, particularly in the contested 16:30 to 17:30 slots. Where no UAE-based tutor covers a specific combination, the tutor may be based elsewhere teaching into Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed rather than concealed. Parts of this market route UAE enquiries to non-UAE phone numbers without saying where the teaching happens; stating the position is a low bar and worth clearing.

sections.heading: The Alternative to Practical paper nobody prepares for
paragraphs: Every IGCSE science route assesses experimental skills, and in UAE centres a large share of candidates sit an Alternative to Practical written paper rather than a laboratory examination. It is the most predictable source of lost marks in the whole science entry, for a straightforward reason: it is nobody's priority. Content revision feels like revision. Practical paper technique feels like a detail, right up to the point where a candidate loses a dozen marks on it.

What the paper actually asks is narrow and very learnable. Read an apparatus diagram and say what it is for. Identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables in a described experiment. Complete a results table with correct headings and units. Plot and interpret a graph. Name a specific source of error, not a vague one, and suggest an improvement that would actually address it. Evaluate whether a conclusion is supported by the data provided. That list is the whole paper, and it barely changes between series.

The errors are equally predictable. Candidates write that the experiment was affected by human error, which earns nothing because it names no mechanism. They give an improvement that does not address the error they just named. They omit units from a table heading. They draw a line of best fit through the first and last points rather than through the data. All of these are habits, and habits respond to four or five sessions of deliberate practice better than to any amount of content revision.

The scheduling advice is simple: put the practical paper block six to eight weeks out, not in the final fortnight. By then the content revision is competing with every other subject, and a technique block is the first thing to be dropped. Six weeks out it is still possible to build a habit, and the habit survives the final rush. Confirm with the school which component your child's centre uses, because it determines whether this block is essential or irrelevant.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE science marks are lost, subject by subject
paragraphs: Generic revision advice is not much use because the losses are specific and they repeat. What follows is the pattern across the three sciences as it shows up on marked scripts, and it is the list a tutor should be able to produce from your child's own paper rather than from a general impression.

In biology, the losses are linguistic more than conceptual. Questions ask for an explanation and receive a description. Processes are named rather than sequenced. Genetics questions, which should be free marks, are lost to careless labelling and to answering with a genotype where a phenotype was asked for. A pupil who knows the biology and writes in the wrong register can be two grades below their understanding.

In chemistry, the losses are quantitative. The mole concept is the hinge: insecure there and titration, yield, concentration and empirical formula work all become unreliable. Balancing equations under time pressure is the other reliable loss, along with rate questions answered with enthusiasm rather than with the named factor and its effect on collision frequency.

In physics, the losses are procedural. Diagrams drawn carelessly, so that every later line of working inherits a missing force. Ray diagrams sketched freehand when the mark scheme wants a construction. Circuit explanations that substitute into a formula where the question asked for reasoning about potential difference. And across all three subjects, the command term ignored, which is the single most common and most fixable error on any science paper.

sections.heading: Core, Extended and the grade ceiling in each science
paragraphs: Several IGCSE science routes are tiered, and the tier caps the grade. On Cambridge separate sciences, Core candidates sit a different paper combination from Extended candidates and the available grade range differs, with Extended giving access to the top grades. The same logic applies across the coordinated and combined routes. Pearson Edexcel's science entries are structured differently, and some are untiered, which is one more reason the code matters before anything else.

The decision is usually made by the school, often in Year 9 or early Year 10, on internal evidence. The argument for the lower tier is genuine: a pupil placed above their level sits harder papers, scores less on each, and can finish below where a confident lower-tier candidate would have landed. The question is always whether a particular pupil is at their ceiling or whether two or three specific weaknesses, typically numeracy within science, graph work and explanation register, are holding down a result otherwise within reach.

That is diagnosable in a single sitting. Give the pupil a lower-tier paper and a higher-tier paper on the same afternoon and look at where the marks fall rather than at the totals. A pupil who scores well on the first and collapses on identifiable question types in the second has a repairable gap. A pupil losing marks evenly across both is at their level, and the honest advice is to secure a strong grade on the lower route rather than gamble.

The post-16 consequence is worth knowing before the decision is made rather than after. Sixth forms set their own entry expectations for A Level and Diploma sciences, and a coordinated or combined route does not close them off but does change the bridging work required. Ask the sixth form, in writing, what they expect for each science. That answer, obtained in Year 9 or 10, is worth more than any amount of tutoring bought in Year 11 to repair a decision nobody checked.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs around Al Garhoud, and what you can verify yourself
paragraphs: Start with what a parent can check independently, because that is the part no tutoring page controls. Published Dubai rates are public. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik quoting AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. In-home one-to-one visits, which carry the tutor's travel, are quoted at AED 180 to 500, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table shows a common range of AED 180 to 350. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named tutors higher, with BartyED at AED 650.

For IGCSE science, the qualified subject tutor band is usually the right one. The specialist premium earns its keep in Diploma Higher Level work and in narrow combinations; for a Year 11 candidate on a known syllabus code with identifiable loss points, what you are buying is diagnosis and board-specific past-paper work, and that sits comfortably in the AED 150 to 300 range. Where families overspend is in buying three subjects when one is the problem, and in buying hours before the syllabus code has been confirmed.

Monthly shapes are easier to budget than hourly rates. Packages advertised in the Dubai market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market. Set that against school fees, which KHDA confirmed in May 2026 would not rise in Dubai for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package.

Every figure above belongs to the provider or dataset that published it; none is IB Gram's price, and no fixed price list appears on these pages because the rate depends on level and session length. What is fixed is that the first lesson is a free trial, so the judgement about whether a tutor knows your child's specific syllabus is made by watching one lesson rather than by reading a profile.

sections.heading: The exam series, the practical component and counting backwards
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so a Garhoud family planning a resit is planning for November rather than for the spring. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, with explicit guidance that using the wrong zone's version is the candidate's own risk and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for a missed exam on that basis.

Pearson's pattern is published on their support pages and is easier to cite. International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead, including for the November series ahead of you, and those get revised, so the live PDF is the only version worth planning around.

Working backwards from the papers, the science-specific milestones are these. The syllabus code and paper entries should be confirmed in writing by the start of Year 11 at the latest. The content should be covered once before the school mocks, usually in January or February for a June series. The mock scripts should be reviewed line by line in the six weeks after, which is the single most productive tutoring block in the whole year. The practical or Alternative to Practical technique block belongs six to eight weeks before the papers. And the final fortnight is for timed papers from the correct board and route, not for new content.

For a resit, the planning happens in the summer. A November entry gives roughly four months, and the efficient use of them is to work from the papers that lost marks rather than to re-teach the course. A candidate who dropped a grade on the Alternative to Practical paper and on explanation register in biology does not need the syllabus again; they need those two things repaired, which is a materially shorter and cheaper piece of work.

sections.heading: Permits, approvals and claims worth checking
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists the route as private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the app, website or e-services. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so ignore any page quoting an amount.

Two claims deserve a check. The first is approval by a regulator. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, which is a specific thing with a specific process. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises, and claims no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A page describing its tutors as approved by one of those bodies is describing something that does not exist.

The second is the offer to supply syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads. These are the boards' copyright material. The right behaviour is to reference them and link the official source, which is what this page does, and the wrong behaviour is to host them. A provider distributing board material is telling you something about how carefully they handle other rules too.

Beyond that, the useful checks are the free ones. Email the school for the syllabus code. Read the school's inspection report on the regulator's own site. Run the free trial as an assessment by sending a marked script beforehand and asking the tutor to name the specific loss points. A tutor who can do that in one lesson has demonstrated the only thing that matters, and no rating on any page substitutes for it.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE science syllabus my child in Al Garhoud is sitting?
faqs.answer: Email the school's exams officer and ask for the syllabus code and the paper numbers your child is entered for, plus whether the centre uses a practical or an Alternative to Practical component. Most schools answer within a day. The codes are unambiguous: Cambridge separate sciences are 0610, 0620 and 0625, Co-ordinated Sciences is 0654 and Combined Science 0653, while Pearson Edexcel runs 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and Science Double Award 4SD0. Once you have the code you can find the live syllabus on the board's own site and be certain any past papers used are the right ones.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Co-ordinated Sciences and separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Co-ordinated Sciences covers biology, chemistry and physics as a double award, giving two grades, with broader coverage at shallower depth than three separate courses. Separate sciences give three grades and full depth in each. The practical consequence for revision is significant: a coordinated paper samples across all three subjects, so a candidate who knows some topics very well and others not at all is more exposed than on a separate-science paper. It is not an easier route, it is a differently shaped one, and the revision strategy has to match.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach all three IGCSE sciences to Extended standard?
faqs.answer: Some can, but fewer than claim to, and it is worth probing rather than assuming. Ask which of the three they teach most weeks, then ask the same question about the one they mentioned last; the second answer is the informative one. For a coordinated or double award candidate whose weakness is spread across subjects, two tutors with a shared plan often works better, with the transferable skills, graph work, data interpretation and command terms, taught once by whichever does it best and applied to all three.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to a home in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. The practical argument is the pool. Matching on geography means accepting whoever teaches science within a short drive of the airport perimeter, which is a small set for a specific syllabus code. Matching online means finding a tutor who teaches your child's exact specification every week. Published in-home rates in Dubai also run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online.

faqs.question: What is the Alternative to Practical paper and how do we prepare for it?
faqs.answer: It is a written paper that assesses experimental skills in place of a laboratory examination, used by many UAE centres. It asks candidates to read apparatus diagrams, identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, complete a results table with correct headings and units, plot and interpret a graph, name a specific source of error and suggest an improvement that addresses it, and judge whether a conclusion is supported by the data. Four or five sessions of deliberate practice, booked six to eight weeks before the papers, is the whole preparation, and it is the component most often skipped.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter lose marks in biology when she knows the content?
faqs.answer: Almost always register rather than knowledge. Biology mark schemes reward explanation, and a large share of candidates give descriptions: they name a process without sequencing it or without giving the reason the question asked for. Genetics questions, which should be reliable marks, go the same way through careless gamete labelling or answering with a genotype where a phenotype was wanted. A pupil who understands the biology and writes in the wrong register can sit two grades below their understanding. Rewriting past answers against the mark scheme wording fixes it in two or three sessions.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science do Dubai pupils need the most help with?
faqs.answer: Physics, and within physics the electricity and circuits topic. The reason is that the questions require reasoning about potential difference, series and parallel behaviour and component characteristics rather than formula substitution, and roughly half the available marks go to explanation. Chemistry is second, and there the problem is almost always quantitative: an insecure mole concept propagates into titration, yield and concentration work for the rest of the course. Biology produces the fewest requests and the most avoidable losses, because the gap there is in how answers are written.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE science tutor cost around Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: The qualified subject tutor band is the relevant one, quoted in Dubai at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Below that, budget online tutoring is advertised from about AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65. Above it, IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and more, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits, which carry travel inside the rate, run AED 180 to 500. Those are market rates published by those providers, not IB Gram's price, and the first lesson here is a free trial.

faqs.question: Should we book all three sciences or just the weakest one?
faqs.answer: Usually just the weakest one. A single weekly lesson on the science that is actually costing marks, combined with independent past-paper work in the other two, is the efficient purchase for most separate-science candidates. Three-subject packages are sold because they are simpler to sell rather than because pupils need them, and they triple the weekly load at a point when time is the scarce resource. The exception is a coordinated or double award candidate whose weakness is genuinely spread, where a rotation across the three with a shared plan makes sense.

faqs.question: Does Core or Extended science change what grade my child can get?
faqs.answer: On the tiered Cambridge routes, yes. Core and Extended candidates sit different paper combinations and the available grade range differs, with Extended giving access to the top grades. Pearson Edexcel structures its science entries differently and some are untiered, which is one more reason to get the code from the school first. The decision is usually made internally in Year 9 or early Year 10. Whether a pupil is genuinely at their ceiling is diagnosable in one sitting by comparing performance on a lower-tier and a higher-tier paper and looking at where the marks fall.

faqs.question: Which exam series do IGCSE science candidates in Dubai sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so there is no spring resit route for a pupil in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with separate timetables and warns that using the wrong one is the candidate's risk, so take the dates from your school's exams officer.

faqs.question: My son has eight weeks before his science papers. What should we spend them on?
faqs.answer: Timed past papers from the correct board and route, reviewed line by line against the mark scheme, plus a block on the Alternative to Practical or practical component if his centre uses one. Not new content. The highest-yield items in eight weeks are command-term discipline, which is roughly an hour's work with permanent effect, graph and data interpretation, which transfers across all three sciences, and the two or three named loss points his last script actually shows. Re-teaching the syllabus in eight weeks achieves less than repairing four specific habits.

faqs.question: If he does Co-ordinated Sciences, can he still take A Level or Diploma sciences?
faqs.answer: It does not close the door, but it changes the bridging work. A double award candidate has met the concepts at less depth than a separate-science candidate, and the gap shows in the first term of a post-16 course. Ask the sixth form in writing what they expect for each science, and get that answer in Year 9 or 10 rather than after the entry decision. Where the route is already settled, six to ten weeks of targeted summer work on the specific topics the double award treated lightly is the efficient fix.

faqs.question: Do science tutors working with Al Garhoud families need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists the application as private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted on a tutoring site.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give us past papers and mark schemes to work from?
faqs.answer: A tutor should direct you to the official source rather than supply copies. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright material, and distributing them is not something a careful provider does. The right behaviour is to cite and link cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com, and to point you to your school's exams officer for the authoritative entry and timetable information. A provider hosting board material is telling you something about how it handles other rules too.

faqs.question: What time can a science lesson start for a pupil living in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: On a club-free day, 16:15 or 16:30. Secondary schools in and around Al Garhoud, Festival City and Oud Metha finish between 14:00 and 15:00, activity clubs extend two or three afternoons to about 16:00, and a bus loop through Garhoud, Al Rigga or Al Mamzar adds twenty-five to fifty minutes. On club days 17:15 is more realistic. Thursday suits a longer session because Friday mornings start later at most schools, and Saturday morning is the only window where a full timed paper plus a proper review fits comfortably.
