Send one email to the school's exams officer asking for the code, the paper numbers and whether the centre uses a practical or Alternative to Practical component. Then send that code with a photograph of a recent marked script. The first lesson is free and is used to name the two or three places marks are actually going. Buy the science that is costing marks rather than a package, and book the practical technique block six to eight weeks out.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-habtoor-.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach IGCSE science to examination rather than in general. Most cover two of the three disciplines to a high level and are honest about the third, because a student revising three sciences in eight weeks is better served by two specialists than by one generalist claiming all three.

intro.heading: Three sciences, two or three grades, and one revision term
paragraphs: The phrase IGCSE science hides a decision most parents in Al Habtoor City were never formally told about. Depending on the school and the set, a Year 11 student is sitting either three separate science qualifications, a double award worth two grades, or a single combined award worth one. Those are different syllabuses with different codes, different paper structures and very different volumes of content. A family asking how long revision will take cannot be answered until that is established, and the answer is on the examination entry rather than in the school newsletter.

Cambridge runs separate sciences as Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625. It also runs Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, a double award covering all three disciplines for two grades, and Combined Science 0653, a single award for one. Pearson Edexcel runs separate International GCSEs as 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, and a Science Double Award as 4SD0. Each route has its own past-paper library, and a student practising on the wrong one is working hard in a dialect nobody is speaking in the hall.

Practical work is the second thing families get wrong. Nobody sits a laboratory examination in front of a tutor, and online delivery changes nothing about how practical skills are assessed. Cambridge separate sciences examine practical skills either through a practical test or through an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the alternative route is what most international centres use. That paper is examinable technique: reading a measuring instrument, identifying a variable, spotting what is wrong with a described method, drawing a table before the data arrives. Those are taught on paper, and they are among the most reliably recoverable marks in the subject.

The third problem is arithmetic rather than science. Three subjects in one term is a scheduling problem, and the usual outcome of leaving it unplanned is that the strongest subject gets revised because it is pleasant and the weakest gets avoided because it is not. A written plan that allocates the weeks across three sciences by marked evidence rather than by preference is most of the value of hiring anybody. We start there, with a marked paper from each discipline, before any teaching happens.

Al Habtoor City is a cluster of residential towers and hotels on Sheikh Zayed Road, between Business Bay and Al Safa, with the Dubai Water Canal along one side. No school sits inside the development, so students here travel out to Al Safa, Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim, Al Barsha or the Al Quoz axis each morning and come back in the afternoon through the worst of the traffic. IB Gram works with these families online, one-to-one, over live video. Home visits are an India-only service; we do not send tutors to UAE addresses, and for a household juggling three sciences the ability to put a biology session on Monday and a physics session on Wednesday without two car journeys is the practical argument.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-habtoor-.programmesIntro: Science requests from these towers come in at three stages, and the right work is different in each. The stage matters more than the subject, because the volume of content at IGCSE is what makes timing decisive.

programmes.name: IGCSE Sciences, separate or awarded together
programmes.description: The two-year course ending in the June or November series. Separate sciences give three grades and carry the most content; the co-ordinated double award gives two grades across all three disciplines; the combined single award gives one. Tutoring divides between content recall, calculation method and the practical-skills paper, and the proportions should follow a marked script rather than a general plan.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools near Al Safa and Jumeirah usually set the route in Year 9 or early Year 10, often by set rather than by choice, and parents frequently learn which route their child is on from a mock timetable. Ask the science department for the codes on the entry. A double-award student revising separate-science papers is doing more work than the examination will ever ask for.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9 science, before the route is set
programmes.description: The years in which the triple or double decision is effectively made, usually on set performance. The skills that decide it are not scientific: rearranging a formula, handling standard form, reading a graph, converting units. Work at this stage is cheap, unglamorous and changes which route the school offers, which is a far larger effect than a grade boost in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Al Habtoor City has a high proportion of families who arrived in Dubai mid-phase, and a Year 8 or 9 arriving from another system is often placed on evidence that reflects unfamiliarity rather than ability. If the long-term aim is separate sciences and then Diploma or A Level sciences, the conversation with the school belongs in Year 9, not after the first Year 10 report.

programmes.name: What the science route allows afterwards
programmes.description: The route taken at sixteen shapes the options at seventeen. Schools in Al Safa, Al Barsha and Al Sufouh split into A Level and IB Diploma pathways, and higher-level sciences in either assume a particular depth of prior study. Separate sciences are the comfortable preparation; a double award can work, and it usually needs deliberate bridging work in the summer between.
programmes.countryNote: Where a student is aiming at medicine, engineering or a physical-science degree, check the published entry requirements of the actual universities rather than relying on general advice. UAE and overseas institutions differ in what they specify, and the requirement is usually about the post-16 qualification, with the IGCSE route mattering because of what it makes achievable.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-habtoor-.subjectsIntro: These are the science codes we are asked to cover from this part of Dubai, with what each one actually demands. The code is the thing to confirm before any revision plan is built.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and vocabulary-dependent. Marks are lost on imprecise terminology and on long-answer questions where the required number of distinct points was never counted.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles, concentration and yield are proportional reasoning in disguise. State symbols and charges carry marks, and they are treated as wrong rather than untidy when omitted.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: The science that punishes weak algebra hardest: rearranging formulae, standard form, reading a gradient. Students strong in biology often struggle here for purely mathematical reasons.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: All three disciplines for two grades. Less content than three separates, and the same practical and calculation demands, so revision has to be planned across disciplines rather than within them.

subjects.name: Combined Science (Cambridge 0653)
subjects.description: One grade across the three disciplines. Timing is the main enemy in the papers, and timing responds to pacing practice rather than to more content teaching.

subjects.name: Biology (Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Pearson's separate biology, with question wording noticeably different from Cambridge. Students who revise on the wrong board's papers lose marks to phrasing rather than knowledge.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Calculator use throughout shifts the risk from arithmetic to rounding and interpretation. The practical-skills content is examined in writing rather than in a laboratory.

subjects.name: Physics (Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Formula-driven and graph-heavy. The transferable gain for a student heading to Diploma or A Level physics is algebraic fluency, which is worth building deliberately.

subjects.name: Science Double Award (Pearson 4SD0)
subjects.description: Two grades across the three disciplines on Pearson's route. The content is narrower than three separates and the examination technique demands are identical.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: Frequently the real cause of a science problem. Rearrangement, ratio and standard form appear inside physics and chemistry questions, and repairing them lifts two grades at once.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-habtoor-.modesIntro: Three shapes of science support cover nearly every request from Al Habtoor City. All run online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

modes.title: One discipline, weekly
modes.description: The most common arrangement: a weekly session in the single science that is dragging the set of grades down, usually physics for algebraic reasons or biology for terminology reasons. Running one subject properly beats running three thinly, and in most cases fixing the weakest discipline also lifts the other two because the underlying skill was shared.
bullets: A written coverage map against the specification for that code
Short retrieval work between sessions rather than long problem sets
Calculation method taught as method, then mixed so the student must choose
Practical-skills questions included from the first month

modes.title: Split-subject timetable
modes.description: For students who genuinely need two or three sciences, usually in the final term. Different tutors on different evenings, with one written plan shared between them so nobody is teaching the same thing twice and the practical paper is not left to whoever remembers it. Households find the coordination more valuable than the teaching, because it removes the avoidance problem.
bullets: One plan across disciplines, allocating weeks by marked evidence
Two or three fixed evenings, never two sessions in one night
A shared error tally so patterns across subjects are visible
The practical-skills paper assigned explicitly to one tutor

modes.title: Pre-series paper block
modes.description: An eight-week run before the June or November series, structured backwards from the examination. Diagnosis and the two worst topics first, then whole papers under time, then two weeks of error elimination with nothing new introduced. For three sciences this is where the written allocation matters most, because there is no slack left to absorb a bad week.
bullets: Week one is a marked paper in each discipline being sat
Two priority topics per subject, written down and not quietly changed
Papers marked against the published scheme, not by impression
The final fortnight adds no new content by design

sections.heading: Triple, double or combined: the decision, the deadline and the consequences
paragraphs: This is the first question to settle and it is settled by the examination entry, not by what anyone remembers being told. Separate sciences produce three grades and carry the largest content load. A co-ordinated or double award produces two grades across the same three disciplines with less content. A combined single award produces one grade. All three are legitimate routes, all three are respected, and they are not interchangeable for revision purposes because the past papers differ.

Schools usually make the decision in Year 9 or early Year 10, and often by set placement rather than by family choice. That timing is the part worth acting on. If your child is aiming at Diploma or A Level sciences and is currently placed on a double-award route, the conversation with the department belongs in Year 9 while sets are still fluid. By the spring of Year 11 the entry is lodged and the question has become how to get the best out of the route taken, which is a different and smaller conversation.

The consequences run in two directions. Separate sciences are the more comfortable preparation for higher-level study, because the depth is closer to what post-16 courses assume. A double award is a perfectly workable base and typically needs a short, deliberate bridging block in the summer before Year 12, concentrating on the specific content the separates covered and the double award did not. Nobody should treat a double award as a closed door, and nobody should pretend the gap does not exist either.

The table below sets out the routes with their codes and what each implies for a revision plan. Confirm the codes with your school's examinations officer before using it. A single email asking which syllabus numbers appear on your child's entry removes the largest source of wasted revision time in this subject.

sections.heading: Practical skills without a laboratory: how that paper is actually examined
paragraphs: Families worry about practical science and online tutoring, and the worry is aimed at the wrong thing. Practical work for coursework purposes happens in the school laboratory under the school's supervision, and no tutor of any kind participates in it. What a tutor can affect is the examination of practical skills, and that is a written paper. Cambridge separate sciences assess practical skills either through a practical test or through an alternative-to-practical written paper, and most international centres use the alternative route. Pearson examines practical knowledge within its written papers.

That paper is one of the most trainable components in IGCSE science, and it is routinely under-prepared because it looks like laboratory work. The questions are predictable in type: read a scale or an instrument to the correct precision, identify the independent and dependent variables in a described method, state what should be controlled, spot the flaw in somebody else's procedure, complete a results table with appropriate headings and units, plot and interpret a graph, and suggest an improvement that addresses the actual weakness rather than a generic one.

Each of those is teachable on paper, in a session, with the student writing while the tutor watches. Reading a measuring cylinder to the right precision is a skill practised on a diagram. Table headings with units are a habit. Identifying a controlled variable is a routine applied to a sentence. We build practical questions into sessions from the first month rather than saving them for the final fortnight, because they are the component where a student can gain the most for the least content work.

One honest caution: a student who has never handled apparatus will still find some questions unfamiliar, and the school laboratory is where that is remedied. If your child has missed laboratory sessions, raise it with the science department rather than with us. What we can do is make sure the written component is not where marks are lost, and that is most of the practical marks on the papers most Dubai centres sit.
bullets: Most international centres use the alternative-to-practical written route
Question types are predictable: precision, variables, flaws, tables, graphs, improvements
Table headings with units and correct precision are habits, not knowledge
Improvements must address the specific weakness described, not a generic one
Missed laboratory time is a conversation for the school, not for a tutor

sections.heading: Eight weeks, three sciences: how the term is actually allocated
paragraphs: A student sitting three sciences in the same series has roughly the same number of free evenings as a student sitting one, and the usual failure is not laziness but allocation. Left to themselves, students revise the subject they enjoy and avoid the one that frightens them, which is precisely the inversion of what the marks require. The fix is a written allocation based on marked papers in each discipline, agreed at the start and reviewed once in the middle, not renegotiated every week.

The allocation should be unequal. If the marked evidence says physics is twelve marks behind where biology is three marks behind, physics gets most of the weeks. That is uncomfortable for a student who finds physics unpleasant, which is exactly why it needs to be written down and shared with the household rather than left to good intentions. Parents can help here more than they expect, simply by holding the plan rather than policing the hours.

The table below is the shape we use for an eight-week pre-series block across three sciences. It is a template rather than a prescription, and the specific topics come from the marked papers. The two features that matter are that each discipline gets whole-paper practice under time at least twice, and that the last two weeks introduce nothing new in any subject. Students resist that second rule and it is the one that most reliably protects a grade.

A note on dates: the milestones are fixed and the dates are not. Cambridge IGCSE runs in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only, so a Dubai family should disregard any date they see attached to it. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Get the zone-correct timetable from the school.

sections.heading: Where marks go in each of the three sciences
paragraphs: The three disciplines fail in different ways, which is why a single revision method underperforms across them. In biology the dominant loss is terminology and point-counting. A six-mark question wants six distinct scoring points, and a student who writes three good points at length scores three. Teaching a student to count their points before writing, and to use the precise term rather than an approximation of it, recovers marks faster than rereading the textbook.

In chemistry the dominant loss is method selection and notation. A student who can perform a mole calculation on request but does not recognise that a question requires one has a selection problem, repaired by mixed practice rather than more worked examples. Alongside that, state symbols, charges and balanced equations carry marks that students read as presentation. They are not presentation, and the fix is mechanical, which means it holds under pressure.

In physics the dominant loss is mathematical. Rearranging a formula with the unknown on the wrong side, standard form, unit prefixes, and reading a gradient from a drawn line rather than from two plotted points. A student who is genuinely strong in biology and weak in physics usually has a maths problem wearing a physics costume, and the honest diagnosis is worth more than a term of physics content revision. It also explains why repairing it lifts the chemistry grade at the same time.

Across all three, two losses recur. Instruction-reading: an answer in the wrong units, to the wrong precision, or answering a different question from the one asked. And pacing: marks surrendered to questions never reached. Both are procedural, both are measurable from a marked script, and both are cheaper to fix than any content gap.
bullets: Biology: count the scoring points before writing; use the precise term
Chemistry: method selection by mixed practice; state symbols and charges are marks
Physics: rearrangement, standard form, prefixes, gradients from the line
All three: units, precision and reading the actual question asked
All three: an agreed order of attack so no question is left unseen

sections.heading: What Dubai charges for science support, and what three subjects costs
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages examined for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. The figures below are market rates taken from published provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai tutoring-cost table, each attributed, so that you can judge a quote you have been given. They are not an IB Gram price list, and nothing on this page should be read as our fee.

The arithmetic that matters for a science family is per-subject rather than per-hour. One weekly session in a single discipline sits in the published mid band of roughly AED 600-1,200 a month; the same arrangement across three disciplines multiplies that, which is the point at which most families reconsider whether all three genuinely need paid support. In our experience they usually do not. Fixing the weakest discipline, which is frequently physics for mathematical reasons, lifts the other two because the underlying skill was shared.

The in-home premium is worth naming precisely because it is where the money goes without buying teaching. Home visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180-500 an hour against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, with published monthly packages around AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits and about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. For three sciences the difference is not marginal: it is the gap between supporting one subject and supporting all three.

For context on where tutoring sits in a Dubai education budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are therefore the fixed part of the budget this year and tutoring is the moving part, which is an argument for deciding the size and duration of a block up front rather than renewing it monthly by default.

sections.heading: Three sciences, one apartment, four weekday evenings
paragraphs: Al Habtoor City students leave the towers each morning for schools in Al Safa, Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim, Al Barsha or across Sheikh Zayed Road on the Al Quoz axis. The afternoon return puts most of them home between 15:45 and 16:45 depending on the day and the route. After the lift, a change and something to eat, the first slot that survives a difficult traffic evening is around 17:30. A household trying to fit three sciences into that week has four usable weekday evenings and one weekend, and the plan has to respect that rather than pretending otherwise.

Two rules make it work. Never put two sessions in one evening: the second is attended rather than used, and the student remembers almost none of it. And keep each discipline on the same night each week, so the household knows Wednesday is physics without negotiating it. Those two decisions do more for consistency than any choice of tutor, and they are entirely within a family's control.

Study conditions in a tower apartment need a small amount of preparation. A hard surface rather than a sofa, squared paper, a ruler, the student's own calculator rather than a phone, and headphones so the rest of the household is not in the lesson. The camera is angled at the page, because watching the working appear is where the diagnosis happens in every science. Where two siblings share a space, staggered slots on different evenings work and a shared session does not.

Ramadan shifts the timetable for a few weeks each year and Dubai schools adjust their hours. For a three-science student the sensible adjustment is fewer and shorter sessions rather than the same load pushed later, with work set between sessions reduced accordingly. We agree that revised timetable before the month begins, because those weeks often sit close to a mock series and improvising through them tends to cost the weakest subject first.
bullets: Sessions from 17:30 survive a Sheikh Zayed Road afternoon; earlier ones get rescheduled
One science per evening, same night each week
Hard surface, squared paper, a real calculator, headphones, camera on the page
Siblings get staggered slots, not a shared session
Ramadan: fewer and shorter sessions, agreed before the month starts

sections.heading: Equivalency, the five-subject count and why the science route matters later
paragraphs: Families in Dubai planning for UAE university entry eventually meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process, and science choices intersect with it. For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which does not match the published rule.

How a double award counts towards that total is exactly the kind of detail that should be confirmed with the Ministry or the attestation authority rather than taken from any page, including this one. Equivalency is a regulatory process that IB Gram does not perform, influence or guarantee, and the only safe route is the official channel. What we can say is that the question is worth asking in Year 10, when the route can still be adjusted, rather than after results.

For the American track the published requirements are different: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold appears in the source we rely on, so no IB equivalency figure should be published without a reading from the Ministry's own site. We would rather leave a gap than fill it with an unverified number.

The broader point for a science family is that the IGCSE route is a gateway rather than a destination. It determines how comfortable the post-16 sciences will feel, which in turn determines what a university application can credibly aim at. That is an argument for getting the route right at fourteen and for treating a weak third science in Year 11 as a problem worth solving rather than tolerating.
bullets: British track: five IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3
Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from that count of five
Plus one A Level at E, or two AS Levels at E
American track: IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 reading and writing; SAT Math 450
Confirm how a double award counts with the Ministry, not with a tutoring page

sections.heading: Permits, honest limits and what to verify for yourself
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with the application made through its smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any figure you see quoted should be treated as unverified.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page here will imply one. We operate no office or centre in the UAE, we do not run home visits anywhere in the Emirates, we do not enter candidates for examinations, and we do not perform equivalency. Those statements exist because competitors in this market imply the opposite, and because a parent deserves to know what they are buying.

On what a tutor may do: teach, explain, set work, mark it and give feedback on the student's own writing. IGCSE sciences include no written coursework in the way the Diploma does, so the question arises less often, but the principle stands for any school-assessed task. A provider offering to supply finished work is offering your child a malpractice risk rather than a service. We also do not reproduce or supply board-owned syllabuses, papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we link them, and your child's school has legitimate access through its own subscriptions.

What to verify independently: the syllabus codes on the entry with your school's examinations officer; the zone-correct examination timetable with the same person; the school's inspection judgements on KHDA's own site rather than from a summary; and any individual tutor's permit status directly. Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK; Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education.

process.title: Get the codes before anything else
process.description: One email to the examinations officer asking which syllabus numbers appear on your child's science entry, and which tier. That single answer determines which past papers are useful, how much content exists, and whether the practical component is a test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Everything else we do is built on it.

process.title: One marked paper per discipline
process.description: We ask for a recent marked paper in each science your child sits. Three marked scripts take twenty minutes to read and tell us where the marks are actually going: terminology in biology, method selection in chemistry, algebra in physics, or instruction-reading across all three. Without them, any allocation of weeks is guesswork dressed up as a plan.

process.title: Free trial lesson in the weakest subject
process.description: The first session is free and is spent in whichever discipline the scripts identify as furthest behind, working through real questions rather than discussing services. You receive a short written note afterwards naming the two priority topics and the error patterns, and that note is yours whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Agree a written allocation and fixed evenings
process.description: Weeks are allocated unequally according to the marked evidence, written down, and shared with the household. Each discipline keeps the same evening each week, and no evening carries two sessions. This is the part families most often skip and the part that most reliably determines whether the block finishes.

process.title: Review once, properly, at week four
process.description: A second paper in the priority subject is sat and marked at week four, and the error tally compared with week one. If the pattern has not moved we change the approach or the tutor rather than defending either. If the evidence says a subject needs the November series instead, we say so while the entry decision is still open.

whyPoints.title: The weakest science is identified before anything is sold
whyPoints.description: Three marked scripts and twenty minutes usually show that one discipline is dragging the set, and that its cause is shared with a second. Fixing that one subject often lifts two grades, which is a cheaper and more honest recommendation than three weekly sessions.

whyPoints.title: Specialists per discipline, not a generalist across three
whyPoints.description: Online matching selects on who has taught a specific syllabus to examination rather than on who can reach a tower in the evening. For a student sitting three sciences that means two tutors on two evenings with one shared plan, which is what the subject actually requires.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper is treated as examinable technique
whyPoints.description: Precision reading, variable identification, table headings, flaw spotting and improvement suggestions are built into sessions from the first month. It is the component most often left to the final fortnight and one of the most reliably recoverable on the paper.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: This page names Dubai market bands in dirhams and says who published each. Three of six competitor pages in this market publish nothing at all, and one asks the price in its own FAQ and then declines to answer. You should be able to tell whether a quote is ordinary before you take a call.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is treated as a fact
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the Cambridge February and March series is India-only and has no bearing on a Dubai entry. We also insist on the zone-correct timetable from the school, because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong one.

whyPoints.title: Plain about what we are not
whyPoints.description: A tutor-matching platform with no board or regulator approval, no UAE premises, and no home-visit service in the Emirates. Where this page names KHDA, MoHRE or the Ministry, it is to explain what they do and point you at their own pages rather than to borrow their standing.

faqs.question: Is my child in Al Habtoor City taking triple or double award science?
faqs.answer: The entry answers it, not the school newsletter. Ask the examinations officer which syllabus codes appear on your child's science entry. Cambridge separate sciences are 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, giving three grades; 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences is a double award giving two; 0653 Combined Science is a single award giving one. Pearson equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for separates and 4SD0 for the Science Double Award. The codes decide how much content exists and which past papers are worth sitting, so getting them in writing is the first useful step in any revision plan.

faqs.question: Can practical science be taught if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The examinable part can, and that is what affects the grade. Laboratory work for school purposes happens in the school laboratory under the school's supervision, and no tutor takes part in it. What tutoring affects is the written assessment of practical skills, which most international centres sit as an alternative-to-practical paper. Those questions are predictable: reading an instrument to the right precision, identifying variables, spotting the flaw in a method, completing a results table with units, plotting and interpreting a graph, and suggesting a specific improvement. All of that is taught on paper, and it is among the most recoverable marks available.

faqs.question: Do you send science tutors to apartments in Al Habtoor City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we provide in India only. Science sessions for these towers run one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For a household covering two or three disciplines the format is the practical answer rather than a compromise: a biology session on Monday and a physics session on Wednesday involve no car journeys, each discipline is taught by someone who actually teaches that syllabus, and no session is lost to Sheikh Zayed Road at the wrong hour.

faqs.question: Which science should we pay for if we can only fund one?
faqs.answer: Usually the one furthest behind on marked evidence, which in practice is often physics. The reason is mathematical: rearranging formulae, standard form, unit prefixes and reading gradients are maths skills examined in a physics paper, and the same weaknesses quietly damage chemistry calculations too. Repairing them therefore lifts two grades rather than one. Biology is more often a terminology and point-counting problem, which a disciplined student can address with the right method and less supervision. Send us one marked paper per subject and we will tell you which single discipline gives the best return.

faqs.question: How do you fit three sciences into a Year 11 week in these towers?
faqs.answer: With a written allocation and two firm rules. The allocation comes from marked papers and is deliberately unequal: the subject twelve marks behind gets more weeks than the one three marks behind. The first rule is one science per evening, because a second session in the same night is attended rather than used. The second is the same discipline on the same night each week, so nothing is renegotiated. Students left to allocate their own time revise the subject they enjoy and avoid the one they fear, which is the exact inversion of what the marks need.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE science candidates in Dubai actually sit their papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE runs a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Dubai centres typically enter the main Year 11 cohort for the summer window and use November as the resit route. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so disregard any date you see attached to it. One practical detail matters: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: My child is on double award but wants to study science after sixteen. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Not a closed door, and not something to ignore either. A double award covers all three disciplines with less content than three separates, so a student moving into A Level or Diploma sciences meets some material for the first time that a separates student has already seen. The practical answer is a short, deliberate bridging block in the summer before Year 12, aimed specifically at the content the separates covered. Ask the post-16 science department what they assume students arrive knowing, then close that list. Doing it in the summer is far cheaper than discovering it in the second term.

faqs.question: What does science tutoring cost for a family in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates put a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and an IGCSE specialist at about AED 200-450 or more. Monthly figures from the Bestimate Dubai table run around AED 600-1,200 for mid-band weekly support in one subject. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180-500 an hour because the fee carries the journey, with packages around AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. The multiplication across three sciences is what makes most families choose one discipline properly rather than three thinly. Those figures are the market with sources, not our price list.

faqs.question: Why does a strong biology student struggle with IGCSE physics papers?
faqs.answer: Nine times out of ten it is maths rather than science. Physics requires rearranging formulae with the unknown on the wrong side, fluency with standard form and unit prefixes, and reading a gradient from a drawn line rather than from two plotted points. Biology asks for precise terminology and well-counted long answers, which rewards a different kind of diligence. A student strong in one and weak in the other usually has a specific algebra gap that a few weeks of targeted work closes, and closing it improves chemistry calculations at the same time. That is why we diagnose from scripts rather than from subject labels.

faqs.question: How many marks does a six-mark biology answer actually need?
faqs.answer: Six distinct scoring points, which is not the same as six sentences or a thorough paragraph. Students lose marks here by writing three strong points at length and assuming quality substitutes for coverage. The method is mechanical: read the mark allocation, plan that many separate points in the margin, then write them using the precise terminology rather than an approximation. Two sessions of this on the student's own answers usually changes the habit, and the gain shows up across every long-answer question in the paper rather than only in the topic that was being revised.

faqs.question: Can we do a short marking clinic instead of weekly science lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some students it is the better purchase. The student sits papers independently, we mark them line by line against the published scheme, and a shorter session covers only the error pattern. It costs less per week than teaching, suits a self-directed Year 11 student who does not need company, and is a sensible way to keep an eye on the two stronger sciences while the weakest one gets proper weekly attention. It is also the honest recommendation for a student who is already working hard and stuck in the same grade band.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education count a double award as one subject or two?
faqs.answer: That is a question for the Ministry or the attestation authority rather than for any tutoring page. What is published for the British track is the overall shape: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus either one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at E. Equivalency is a regulatory process that we do not perform or influence. Ask it in Year 10 while the science route can still be adjusted, and get the answer from the official channel.

faqs.question: What equipment does an online science session need in a tower apartment?
faqs.answer: Less than people expect. A hard surface rather than a sofa, squared paper and a ruler for graph work, the student's own calculator rather than a phone, and headphones so the rest of the household is not part of the lesson. The camera is angled at the page rather than the face, because watching the working appear is where every science diagnosis happens. Ten minutes of setting this up before the first session removes most of the friction families anticipate. Where two siblings share the space, staggered evenings work and a shared session does not.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for a specific science syllabus?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot with whoever is free. Mainstream requests such as Extended 0620 or 4PH1 are usually matched quickly. Narrower ones, such as 0653 Combined Science or the practical test route rather than the alternative-to-practical paper, draw on a smaller group, and the honest options are a different time, a short wait for the right tutor, or a marking clinic in the meantime so the weeks are not wasted. We also tell you where a tutor is based before you book, rather than after.

intro.heading: The question nobody answers straight
paragraphs: A parent in Al Jaddaf types 'IGCSE science tutor near me' because they want to know whether anyone within reach genuinely knows the course their child is taking. It is a reasonable question and the Dubai market answers it badly. Agency pages list subjects and areas, publish a photograph of a smiling tutor, and never mention a syllabus code. The implicit promise is that science is science. It is not, and the difference shows up in the first marked paper.

Here is what the question really means. A Year 11 student sitting Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 at Extended tier is examined on a specific set of supplement content, with a six-mark extended-response style and an alternative-to-practical paper that asks for apparatus judgement. A student sitting Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1 meets a different paper structure and a different balance of recall and application. A student on Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three sciences in a reduced form, and a tutor who teaches full Biology will over-teach half of it and miss the parts that are actually examined.

So the honest answer to the question as asked is this: whether somebody who lives near Al Jaddaf knows your child's syllabus is almost entirely a matter of luck. The creek corridor is not a science-tutoring district. The schools here run a spread of boards, families arrive from a dozen school systems, and the tutor who happens to live two towers over may teach the national curriculum, or the American sequence, or Cambridge Biology but not the Co-ordinated route your child is actually on. Proximity is not evidence of anything.

Which is why we stopped matching on geography. Open delivery to live video and the pool changes from the people who will drive to the creek at 17:00 to everybody who teaches your child's exact specification and is free in the Gulf evening. That is not a sales argument about convenience. It is the difference between a tutor who recognises the mark scheme and one who is reading it for the first time alongside your child, at the same hourly rate.

What follows is practical: how to find out which syllabus your child is on, what each route examines, how practical skills are assessed without coursework, the ten-minute conversation that tells you whether a tutor knows the specification, and which exam series UAE candidates actually sit. There is a tier decision hiding in the Cambridge routes that carries a grade ceiling, and most families only hear about it after entries have closed, so that gets a section of its own. The exam calendar section exists because this market gets it wrong often enough to be dangerous: the February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only, and a Dubai parent handed those dates has been given the wrong country's timetable to plan around. Lessons are delivered one to one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.programmesIntro: IGCSE science is not one qualification. Dubai schools run at least three distinct shapes of it, and the shape decides what a tutor needs to know before the first session.

programmes.name: Separate sciences: Biology, Chemistry, Physics
programmes.description: Three qualifications, each with its own papers and its own grade. On the Cambridge route these are Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625; on the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE route they are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. A student takes three sets of papers and receives three grades, which is the route most British-curriculum schools in Dubai use for students heading towards A Level or IB Diploma sciences.
programmes.countryNote: This is the most common route at the larger British campuses near Al Jaddaf and south of the creek. The practical consequence for tutoring is that three separate specialists usually beat one generalist. A tutor strong on Physics 0625 may be merely adequate on Biology 0610, where the examined skill is precise terminology rather than calculation, and the difference is visible in the marks within a term.

programmes.name: Co-ordinated Sciences, double award
programmes.description: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 covers biology, chemistry and physics in a single qualification that counts as two IGCSEs. Content is reduced relative to the three separate syllabuses but the papers still examine all three disciplines, including an alternative-to-practical or practical component. It suits students taking a broad subject spread who still need credible science qualifications.
programmes.countryNote: Co-ordinated Sciences is where the mismatch between tutor and syllabus does the most damage in Dubai. A tutor teaching from the full Biology 0610 scheme will spend hours on content that is not examined on 0654 and skip the way the paper sequences across disciplines. Families pay full rate for partly irrelevant teaching, and the first indication is a mock result that does not reflect the hours put in.

programmes.name: Combined Science, single award
programmes.description: A single-award route, Cambridge Combined Science 0653 or the Edexcel Science (Double Award) 4SC1 depending on the school, covering all three disciplines at a lighter content load and yielding one grade. Schools use it where a student's timetable or prior attainment makes three separate sciences unrealistic, and it still provides a recognised science qualification at 16.
programmes.countryNote: The important planning point for an Al Jaddaf family is what each route leaves open. Progression to A Level or IB Diploma sciences is generally smoother from separate sciences or Co-ordinated than from single-award Combined, though schools set their own entry criteria. Ask the head of science directly what their own sixth form requires before assuming any route is sufficient; the answer varies between campuses in the same emirate.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.subjectsIntro: Below are the science areas Al Jaddaf families ask for most, with what each one actually examines and where the marks leak away. Syllabus codes are given because they are the thing a tutor must match.

subjects.name: Biology, Cambridge 0610
subjects.description: Characteristics of living organisms, cells, enzymes, transport, respiration, coordination, reproduction, inheritance and ecology. Marks are lost on imprecise terminology more than on misunderstanding: writing that a substance moves in rather than naming diffusion down a concentration gradient costs the mark every time.

subjects.name: Biology, Edexcel 4BI1
subjects.description: Similar content territory to Cambridge but a different paper structure and a different balance of recall against data interpretation. Students moving between the two boards mid-course, which happens often in Dubai, need the paper technique retaught even though the biology itself is familiar.

subjects.name: Chemistry, Cambridge 0620
subjects.description: Particulate nature of matter, atoms and bonding, stoichiometry, electrochemistry, energetics, rates, acids and bases, the periodic table, metals and organic chemistry. Stoichiometry is where the grade is decided; a correct method on an unbalanced equation loses every subsequent mark.

subjects.name: Chemistry, Edexcel 4CH1
subjects.description: Comparable content with its own question style, including a distinctive approach to calculation-heavy items. The recurring loss on either board is the same: students who can recite a definition but cannot apply it to an unfamiliar substance in a data table.

subjects.name: Physics, Cambridge 0625
subjects.description: Motion, forces and energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, nuclear physics and space physics. Multi-step problems are the differentiator between grades; students who can recall every formula still stall when two have to be chained together under time pressure.

subjects.name: Physics, Edexcel 4PH1
subjects.description: Similar syllabus territory with its own formula sheet conventions and paper split. Unit conversion is the quiet killer on both boards, particularly where a question gives a value in centimetres and the relationship demands metres without saying so.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: All three disciplines in one double-award qualification with reduced content. Requires a tutor working from the 0654 syllabus specifically, because the examined subset is not simply the easier parts of the three separate courses and the papers move between disciplines within a single question set.

subjects.name: Practical and data skills
subjects.description: Apparatus identification, variable control, plotting, anomalies, and improving a described method. Examined through the alternative-to-practical paper on most Cambridge routes. Rarely taught as a distinct skill in a crowded school scheme, and therefore unusually responsive to a short tutoring block.

subjects.name: Scientific terminology and command words
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest and compare each demand a different answer length and structure. A student who understands the science and writes one line for a four-mark explain question has a technique problem, not a knowledge problem, and only marked scripts reveal it.

sections.heading: First find out which syllabus your child is actually on
paragraphs: Before you look for a tutor, spend five minutes establishing what is being sat. Most Al Jaddaf parents cannot name their child's syllabus code, which is not a failing on their part; schools rarely volunteer it. But hiring a science tutor without it is like booking a translator without naming the language, and it is the single most common reason tutoring money is wasted on this subject in Dubai.

Three places hold the answer. The student's exercise book or revision guide usually carries the code on the cover. The school's curriculum page or the head of science will confirm it in one email. And if entries have been made, the statement of entry from the exam centre names the syllabus and the components precisely. Any of those takes a few minutes and settles the matter completely.

Why it matters so much is a question of examined content rather than difficulty. Cambridge Biology 0610 at Extended tier and Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 overlap substantially but are not the same examined subset, and the papers are structured differently. Pearson Edexcel 4BI1 covers broadly similar biology with a different paper split and a different balance of recall against data handling. A tutor teaching the wrong one of those three is not teaching badly; they are teaching a different course competently.

The table below sets out the routes you are most likely to encounter in this part of Dubai. Take the code to a prospective tutor and ask them to describe the paper structure from memory. A tutor who has taught it will do so without hesitating. One who asks you to send the specification is telling you something useful, and it is better to know in the first conversation than in the third month.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and the ceiling nobody mentions
paragraphs: On the Cambridge science syllabuses there is a tier decision, and it carries a consequence families are often not told about until the entries are made. Core and Extended are not two levels of difficulty applied to the same paper; they are different papers drawing on different content, and the Core tier carries a grade ceiling. A student entered for Core cannot access the top grades regardless of how well they perform, which is a reasonable arrangement for some students and a quietly closed door for others.

The tier decision is usually made by the school in Year 10 or early Year 11, on the basis of internal assessment. That is sensible and usually right. It becomes a problem when a student's attainment changes after the decision, which is precisely what effective tutoring is supposed to achieve. A student who moves from borderline to comfortable in the autumn of Year 11, and who is still entered for Core, has gained nothing from the improvement in grade terms.

The practical move for an Al Jaddaf family is to ask three questions early. Which tier is my child provisionally entered for? When is the final entry decision made? And what would need to be true for that decision to change? Those questions cost nothing and they are the whole of what parents can usefully do about a tier ceiling. Asking them in November is useful; asking them in March is usually too late, because final entries have gone.

Edexcel's International GCSE sciences are single-tier, which removes the decision entirely and is one reason some Dubai schools prefer them. If your child is on 4BI1, 4CH1 or 4PH1 there is no tier to worry about. The trade-off is that the single paper set has to serve the full ability range, so the easier marks and the harder marks sit in the same paper and time management matters more.

sections.heading: How practical skills are examined when there is no coursework
paragraphs: Parents who sat GCSEs themselves often assume there is a practical coursework component carrying marks, and on most IGCSE science routes in Dubai there is not. What exists instead is a paper that examines practical reasoning without a laboratory: the alternative-to-practical component, where a student is shown an apparatus diagram, given a method and a table of readings, and asked to make judgements about it.

This component is strange and it is strangely underprepared. The questions ask which variable should be controlled and why, how to improve a described method, which reading is anomalous and what might have caused it, how to plot and what the gradient represents. None of that is content knowledge in the ordinary sense, so a student who has revised every topic can still arrive at that paper without a technique for it. A crowded school scheme of work rarely has room to teach it as a skill in its own right.

For a tutoring budget this is the best-value block in the whole qualification. The content is small, the examined skill is learnable, the marks are substantial, and almost nobody arrives prepared. Four to eight sessions working through practical papers from the correct specification, with every attempt marked, reliably moves marks in a way that another pass through the content does not. Ask any prospective tutor whether they teach this component specifically; a vague answer is the answer.

Where a school does run a practical component, the arrangement differs by board and by centre, so the school is the only reliable source on how it is assessed for your child. What a tutor can do either way is build the reasoning: controlled variables, repeats, anomalies, resolution of instruments and sensible improvements. That reasoning serves the examined paper, the school's own practicals, and the internal assessment work that follows at A Level or in the Diploma.

sections.heading: Four questions that reveal whether a tutor knows the specification
paragraphs: You can establish in about ten minutes whether somebody has actually taught your child's science specification, and it does not require you to know any science yourself. The method is to ask questions whose answers are specific to the course rather than to the subject. A tutor who has taught the specification answers immediately and concretely. A tutor who has not gives you generalities about building confidence.

Ask first what the paper structure is for the code your child is sitting. How many papers, what each one contains, how long. Somebody who has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended knows this the way a driver knows their route. Ask second where students most often lose marks on that paper, and listen for whether the answer is specific. The useful reply names something diagnosable: unbalanced equations before a calculation, hydrogen bonding named without the molecules, unit conversion from centimetres.

Ask third how they handle the alternative-to-practical component, if the route has one. This question separates tutors sharply, because the component requires a different kind of teaching and many people simply skip it. Ask fourth what proportion of a session the student spends writing. The right answer for IGCSE science is most of it, and a tutor who has taught exam classes will say so without being prompted.

Then there is one question that is not about competence but about honesty: what will you do if my child is behind by March? A tutor who says they will prioritise the highest-yield topics and accept that some content will go uncovered is telling you the truth about what is possible. A tutor who promises to cover everything and secure a particular grade is making a promise nobody in this market can keep, and grade guarantees are not something any responsible provider offers.

sections.heading: What proximity actually buys, and what it costs
paragraphs: Suppose a genuinely good tutor for Cambridge 0654 lives in Al Quoz and will travel to Al Jaddaf. The market rate for that is published: Bestimate records in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors across Dubai advertising AED 200 to 500. Against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, as published by Unitors at IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150, the premium is clear and it buys the journey.

The journey itself is the hidden cost. A tutor arriving at the creek for 17:00 leaves around 16:15 and is not free again until past 19:00, so one paid hour consumes three hours of their working day. That shows in the rate, and it also shows in flexibility: a session that needs moving cannot simply move, because the trip has already been committed to the day's plan. Families in Nad Al Sheba and Meydan see this most sharply, which is why in-home quotes further out sit at the upper end of the published range.

The larger cost is the one nobody prices. Restricting yourself to tutors who will drive to Al Jaddaf on a Tuesday evening shrinks the set of candidates to a handful, and nothing about that handful guarantees one of them teaches Co-ordinated Sciences 0654. You have optimised for the wrong variable. The thing that moves marks is whether the tutor knows the specification; the thing proximity optimises is travel time, which affects nobody's grade.

To be plain about what is and is not on offer: IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE. Teaching for UAE families is delivered one to one over live video, screen-shared, with tutor and student annotating the same apparatus diagram or the same data table. In-home visiting is a service we operate only in India. The in-home AED figures above are the market's published rates, quoted so you can compare them, not an offer we make.

sections.heading: The school cluster around Al Jaddaf and what it means for matching
paragraphs: Al Jaddaf sits in an unusual position for a Dubai neighbourhood. It is not a single-school community. The creek corridor between Dubai Healthcare City and Ras Al Khor draws families towards IB continuum provision on one side, British campuses inland, Indian-curriculum schools in the older districts, and American provision across the water at Festival City. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK curricula at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent.

That spread has a direct consequence for anyone looking for a science tutor here. In a district built around one large British school, a local tutor has probably taught that school's specification. Around Al Jaddaf there is no such default. Two students living in the same tower may be on Cambridge Extended separate sciences and Edexcel Double Award respectively, and they need different teaching.

It also means the school's own position is worth checking before you buy anything. KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Published inspection reports frequently identify the subject departments where attainment lags, which is free, specific information about whether science at your child's school is a general weakness or your child's individual difficulty. Those two situations call for different responses.

Dubai's intake continues to grow: the 2026-27 year adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family budgeting tutoring, a flat fee year is the context in which that spending sits.

sections.heading: Exam series, entries and the calendar UAE candidates actually sit
paragraphs: This is where Dubai tutoring providers get things wrong most often, and the error is consequential because parents act on dates. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only. A provider quoting a Dubai family February exam dates or a November entry deadline for a February sitting has handed them the wrong country's calendar.

Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. That is a real risk and it is entirely avoidable: the school's exams officer knows the centre's zone, and the correct timetable is the only one worth printing.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November each year. As a verified example of how far entry deadlines sit ahead of papers, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series and those can be revised, so the live official timetable is the only version to rely on.

For planning purposes, the useful habit is counting backwards from the series rather than forwards from today. Final entries close months before the papers. Mocks sit roughly a term before. If a tier decision is in play, it is made before entries. A family that maps those four points onto a calendar in the autumn knows exactly when a tutoring block needs to start, which is almost always earlier than instinct suggests.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what happens if nobody fits
paragraphs: The sequence is short and the first step is the one that does the work. Send the syllabus code, the most recent marked science paper, and the school. From those three things a tutor can tell you what is actually wrong, which is usually more specific than the family expected: terminology precision in biology, balancing before calculation in chemistry, unit conversion in physics, or answer length across all three.

We then propose a tutor who teaches that specification, with their boards and codes stated rather than implied. A free trial lesson runs before any payment, working on a real question from your child's own past paper rather than a generic assessment. If the match is wrong you say so and we propose another, and nothing has been spent. That is the whole arrangement; there is no registration fee and no commitment attached to the trial.

On availability, we would rather be blunt than optimistic. Some combinations are genuinely scarce. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 taught properly, or a single tutor covering two sciences on different boards, may not have a free slot in the Gulf evening window during a busy term. When that happens we say so instead of quietly substituting a generalist at the same rate, which is the standard practice in this market and the reason families lose terms. Usually we can offer a different time, a tutor in another time zone whose hours overlap the UAE evening, or a start a fortnight out.

The information we ask for is limited to what the match requires: a parent's name and contact details, the student's year group, the subjects and the syllabus codes. That exists to find a tutor and arrange the trial lesson, it is not sold on, and you can ask for it to be deleted at any point; the privacy notice linked from every page explains how. We do not ask for a child's photograph, school report or grade history to arrange a trial.
