process.title: Find the syllabus code
process.description: Check the revision guide cover, ask the head of science, or read the statement of entry. Five minutes here determines whether every subsequent hour is spent on the right course. Without it, a tutor is guessing which of three plausible specifications your child is sitting.

process.title: Send a marked science paper
process.description: A marked script shows the pattern in ten minutes: whether marks go on terminology, on calculation setup, on unit handling, or on answers too short for the marks offered. Those are four different fixes of four different lengths, and guessing between them is expensive.

process.title: Get a code-matched tutor
process.description: We name a tutor who teaches that board and that syllabus, with the tier and the practical component stated. If the student is on Co-ordinated Sciences we say so explicitly, because teaching from the separate-science schemes wastes hours on unexamined content.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: The trial runs on a question from your child's own paper. You hear whether the tutor talks about the specification or about confidence, and the student decides whether the explanation lands. No payment is taken before this and nothing follows automatically.

process.title: Review on re-marked work
process.description: Progress is judged on re-marked questions in the same topic, not on how the sessions felt. If marks have not moved after a block, the approach changes or the tutor does. That review is the step that prevents a year of pleasant sessions and a flat mock result.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 are three different courses with three different papers. A tutor is proposed because they teach yours, which is the variable that actually moves marks.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper taken seriously
whyPoints.description: The alternative-to-practical component is examined, learnable and almost universally underprepared, because a crowded school scheme has no room to teach it as a skill. It is the best-value block in the qualification and we treat it as one.

whyPoints.title: A test you can run yourself
whyPoints.description: Four questions on this page let you establish in ten minutes whether a tutor has taught the specification, without knowing any science. Use them on us and on anybody else you are considering.

whyPoints.title: Dates that are right for the UAE
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit Cambridge June and November; the February and March series is India only. Providers quoting Dubai parents February dates are working from the wrong country's calendar, and a parent can act on a wrong date.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed, not concealed
whyPoints.description: When no code-matched tutor has a slot in the Gulf evening, we say so and offer an alternative time, tutor or start date. Substituting a generalist at a specialist rate is how a family loses both the fees and the term.

faqs.question: How do I find out which science syllabus my child in Al Jaddaf is sitting?
faqs.answer: Three sources settle it in minutes. The code is usually printed on the cover of the revision guide or exercise book. The head of science will confirm it in one email, and a school's curriculum page often lists it. Once entries are made, the statement of entry from the exam centre names the syllabus and every component precisely. Do this before contacting any tutor. Hiring a science tutor without the code is the most common way families in this corridor waste money, because Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 are three different courses with three different papers.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who lives near the creek better than one teaching over video?
faqs.answer: Only if they happen to teach your child's exact specification, and nothing about living nearby makes that more likely. Al Jaddaf is not a single-school community: the creek corridor draws families towards IB continuum provision, British campuses inland, Indian-curriculum schools in the older districts and American schooling across the water. Two students in the same tower may be on different boards. Restricting your search to tutors who will drive to the creek on a Tuesday reduces your choice to a handful, none of whom is guaranteed to know Co-ordinated Sciences 0654. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: What is Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and does it need a different tutor?
faqs.answer: It is a Cambridge double-award qualification covering biology, chemistry and physics in one, counting as two IGCSEs, with content reduced relative to the three separate syllabuses. And yes, it needs a tutor working from the 0654 syllabus specifically. The examined subset is not simply the easier parts of 0610, 0620 and 0625, and the papers move between disciplines within a question set. A tutor teaching from the full separate-science schemes will spend paid hours on content that is not examined while skipping how the paper is actually structured.

faqs.question: Does the Core tier really cap my son's grade?
faqs.answer: Yes. On the Cambridge science syllabuses, Core and Extended are different papers drawing on different content, and the Core tier does not give access to the top grades however well a candidate performs. Schools usually decide the tier in Year 10 or early Year 11 from internal assessment, which is reasonable, but it becomes a problem if attainment improves afterwards. Ask three things in the autumn: which tier is he provisionally entered for, when is the final entry decision made, and what would need to be true for it to change. Asking in March is normally too late.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE sciences interchangeable for a tutor?
faqs.answer: No, though the underlying science overlaps heavily. The paper structures differ, the balance between recall and data interpretation differs, and Edexcel's International GCSE sciences are single-tier while Cambridge has a Core and Extended split. Students who move between boards mid-course, which happens regularly in Dubai when a family changes school, usually find the science familiar and the paper technique unfamiliar. That technique has to be retaught deliberately. Ask any prospective tutor to describe the paper structure for your child's code from memory; hesitation is informative.

faqs.question: Why does the alternative-to-practical paper matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because it is examined, learnable, and almost nobody arrives prepared for it. The questions show an apparatus diagram, a method and a table of readings, then ask which variable to control and why, how to improve the method, which reading is anomalous and what caused it. None of that is content recall, so a student who has revised every topic can still have no technique for the paper. A crowded school scheme rarely teaches it as a skill in its own right, which makes four to eight marked practical-paper sessions the best-value block in the qualification.

faqs.question: Should we use one tutor for all three sciences or three separate ones?
faqs.answer: Three separate specialists, where the budget allows, because the subjects fail for different reasons. Biology marks turn on terminology precision: writing that a substance moves in rather than naming diffusion down a concentration gradient loses the mark. Physics marks turn on chaining formulae and converting units under time pressure. Chemistry turns on balancing before calculating. A tutor strong in one is often merely adequate in another, and it costs the same per hour either way. Start with the subject where the marked paper shows the clearest pattern.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE science exams actually happen for a Dubai candidate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai family given February dates has the wrong country's calendar. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, since it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and in November. Your school's exams officer holds the zone-correct official timetable.

faqs.question: My daughter revises for hours and her science marks do not move. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because she is revising content while losing marks on something else. Three patterns dominate. Answers too short for the mark allocation, where a four-mark explain question receives one line: that is command-word discipline, not knowledge. Correct method applied to an unbalanced equation, which loses every subsequent mark. And unit conversion, where a value is given in centimetres and the relationship wants metres. None of these improves with more content revision, and all three are visible on a marked script within minutes, which is why a tutor should ask for one first.

faqs.question: How many sessions does IGCSE science support usually take?
faqs.answer: A single diagnosable technique fault, such as command-word discipline or practical-paper reasoning, is typically a four to six session block with a re-marked script as evidence at the end. Unfinished content takes roughly a session per topic plus practice. A student well below target across all components usually needs a weekly slot over a year rather than a block. Anyone quoting a session count before reading a marked paper is guessing, and that guess is how a four-session need becomes a twelve-session invoice. Ask for the diagnosis before agreeing hours.

faqs.question: Do science tutors in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The u.ae guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time via its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can a tutor at my child's own school give private lessons?
faqs.answer: Not to their own students, in Abu Dhabi at least, and the principle is worth knowing wherever you live. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify against the current policy document. The practical point for a Dubai parent is that a school teacher offering to tutor your child privately is a situation worth asking questions about rather than accepting gratefully.

faqs.question: What does online science teaching look like in practice?
faqs.answer: A shared screen, the student's own past paper open, and both people annotating it. The tutor marks an attempt live, shows where the mark scheme awarded nothing and why, and the student rewrites the answer on the spot. Apparatus diagrams, graphs and data tables all work better magnified on a screen than passed across a table. The practical work itself happens at school, where the equipment and the technician are. What the format changes is which tutor you can reach: anyone teaching your child's specification who is free in the Gulf evening.

faqs.question: What if you cannot find a tutor for our exact specification?
faqs.answer: We tell you. Some combinations are genuinely thin, particularly Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 taught properly, or one tutor covering two sciences across different boards, and in a busy term the right person may have no slot in the Gulf evening window. The standard practice in this market is to substitute a generalist at the same rate and say nothing, which costs a family the fees and the term. Instead we will normally offer a different time, a tutor whose time zone overlaps the UAE evening, or a start a fortnight out, and occasionally the honest answer is no.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-khail-ga.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach to a named syllabus code and mark against the published scheme. Each starts by looking at a practical-skills question rather than a content topic, because that is where the most recoverable marks in IGCSE science usually sit.

intro.heading: The marks are often in the paper nobody revises
paragraphs: When a family asks for science help, the request is almost always about content: my child does not understand electricity, or organic chemistry, or genetics. Sometimes that is right. More often a marked paper shows that the content marks are broadly there and the losses are concentrated in the practical-skills questions, in reading apparatus to the correct precision, in describing a standard experiment, and in handling a data table. Those are the marks almost nobody revises, because they do not look like a topic.

Most international centres examine practical skills through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory test. That paper is predictable in a way content papers are not. It asks the student to read a scale, identify variables, find the flaw in a described method, complete a results table with headings and units, plot and interpret a graph, and suggest an improvement that addresses the specific weakness described. Six question types, all trainable, and the training is on paper rather than at a bench.

The second underweighted area is the set of standard experiments. Every syllabus expects candidates to be able to describe a small number of classic investigations: measuring the rate of a reaction, testing for ions and gases, investigating the resistance of a wire, testing a food sample, finding the focal length of a lens, investigating osmosis in plant tissue. These come up as describe-the-method questions, and students who have done the experiment once and never articulated it lose marks they could have banked.

Al Khail Gate is a mid-rise residential community in the Al Quoz district, strung along Al Khail Road between the Al Quoz industrial areas and the Dubai Hills and Al Barsha South developments. It is a practical, affordability-conscious neighbourhood where children travel to a wide spread of schools by bus, and where the study table is usually shared. Those two facts shape what a sensible science arrangement looks like more than any pedagogical preference does.

There is a budget point too, and it deserves a direct answer rather than a brochure. Published Dubai bands run from roughly AED 45 an hour for budget online tutoring to roughly AED 500 for an in-home specialist visit, which is a tenfold spread. A fixed budget spread across three sciences buys three arrangements that diagnose nothing. The same money spent on one subject, chosen from a marked script, usually lifts more than one grade, because the weakest science is frequently weak for a reason it shares with another.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. For practical-skills work the format is genuinely well suited, because the entire exercise is reading diagrams, annotating tables and plotting graphs with somebody watching the page.

sections.heading: The practical-skills paper, question type by question type
paragraphs: Families worry that online tutoring cannot help with practical science, and the worry is aimed at the wrong thing. Laboratory work for school purposes happens in the school laboratory under the school's supervision and no tutor of any kind takes part in it. What tutoring affects is the written assessment of practical skills, and at most international centres that is an alternative-to-practical paper rather than a bench test.

That paper is the most predictable component in the whole qualification. Six question types account for nearly all of it, they recur across biology, chemistry and physics, and each is a procedure rather than a piece of knowledge. Reading a scale or an instrument to the correct precision. Identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables in a described method. Finding the flaw in somebody else's procedure. Constructing a results table with correct headings and units. Plotting and interpreting a graph. Suggesting an improvement that addresses the specific weakness described rather than a generic one.

The last of those is where students lose most, and the reason is instructive. Asked how a method could be improved, students write repeat the experiment and take an average, which is sometimes right and frequently irrelevant to the weakness the question described. A question that has just told you the temperature was not controlled is asking about temperature control. Reading the stem for the stated weakness and addressing that specific thing is a two-session habit with a direct mark return.

The table sets out the six types with the procedure and the usual error. A parent can use it with a past practical-skills paper in front of them to see which types their child handles and which they do not, which is a better basis for a conversation with any tutor than a general sense that science is going badly.

sections.heading: Apparatus, precision and the reading errors that cost marks
paragraphs: Precision is content in science papers, not presentation. An instrument has a smallest division and a measurement is entitled to a precision related to it, and an answer quoted more precisely or less precisely than that loses the mark. Students treat this as pedantry and examiners treat it as the point, because an experimental result that overstates its own precision is a wrong result.

The related skill is knowing what each instrument is for and what its limitations are. A measuring cylinder, a burette and a pipette do not measure volume equally well, and a question that asks which to use is asking about precision rather than about preference. A thermometer read at the wrong angle introduces a systematic error. A balance that is not zeroed produces a consistent offset that a repeat will not detect, which is why the distinction between random and systematic error is worth teaching as a distinction rather than as vocabulary.

That distinction is examinable in a practical way. A random error is reduced by repeating and averaging. A systematic error is not, and a student who offers repetition as a remedy for a zero offset has shown the examiner they do not understand the difference. Teaching the two side by side, with a named example of each, takes one session and shows up repeatedly on the paper.

The table lists the instruments that come up most with their precision considerations and the error each invites. We work through it with diagrams on screen, asking the student to state the reading and then justify the precision they chose, which is exactly the form the question takes.

sections.heading: The standard experiments every candidate is expected to describe
paragraphs: Each science syllabus assumes familiarity with a small set of classic investigations, and questions regularly ask a student to describe the method, state what would be measured, or identify what is being controlled. Students who performed the experiment once in Year 10 and never articulated it lose marks that were entirely bankable, because describing a method is a rehearsable task rather than a recall lottery.

The list is short enough to prepare properly. In biology: testing a food sample for starch, reducing sugar, protein and fat; investigating osmosis in plant tissue; investigating the effect of temperature or pH on enzyme activity; investigating the rate of transpiration. In chemistry: tests for common gases and ions; measuring the rate of a reaction by gas collection or by a change in appearance; a titration; separation techniques. In physics: the resistance of a wire; finding the focal length of a converging lens; determining density; timing a pendulum.

The useful exercise with a student is to require the description from memory, in a fixed structure: the aim, the independent variable and how it is changed, the dependent variable and how it is measured, the controlled variables, the apparatus, the method in numbered steps, and the expected result. Doing that for six experiments across a term is a few sessions of work and it converts a whole class of question from uncertain to reliable.

The table lists the experiments with what each one is really testing in an examination context and the trap attached to it. Note how often the trap is about control rather than about procedure, which is the examiners' actual interest: they are checking whether the student understands why the method is built the way it is.

sections.heading: Graphs and data handling across the three sciences
paragraphs: Graph work carries marks in all three sciences and it is manual rather than conceptual, which means it improves with supervised practice far faster than with unsupervised practice. The student cannot see their own plotting errors; a tutor watching the page can. The elements are consistent: choose a scale that uses most of the grid, label both axes with quantity and unit, plot accurately, draw a line rather than joining points, and read any gradient from the line rather than from two data points.

The gradient is where marks disappear most often and the fix is specific. Read it from the line, use as large a triangle as the line allows, show the triangle on the graph, and quote the result with units. Each of those is a mark somewhere. A gradient quoted without units is incomplete regardless of its value, and a gradient read from two plotted points rather than from the drawn line defeats the purpose of drawing a line of best fit at all.

Data tables carry their own marks. The heading carries the quantity and the unit, the values carry a consistent number of decimal places down each column, and processed columns show what was calculated. A table that puts units beside each value rather than in the heading loses marks for presentation that is actually content, and the habit is worth correcting early because it appears in every data question for the rest of the course.

The final piece is interpretation. A question asking what the graph shows wants a statement about the relationship, ideally quantified, not a description of the line's appearance. Students who write the line goes up have described rather than interpreted. Teaching a fixed phrasing, where the relationship is stated with the direction and, where possible, the proportionality, is a small intervention that transfers to every data question in all three sciences.

sections.heading: Which science to fund first, from this community's perspective
paragraphs: Al Khail Gate is a practical, affordability-conscious community, and the honest question for most families here is not which tutor but how to spend a fixed amount well. Published Dubai bands span roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, AED 200 to 450 or more for a specialist, and AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the fee. Monthly estimates run about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band for one weekly subject.

Those figures come from published provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table, and they are the market rather than our price list. We publish them because most pages competing for this search publish nothing: three of the six examined for this project quote no figure at all, and one asks the price in its own list of questions and declines to answer. A family with a fixed budget cannot allocate it without knowing the bands.

The allocation answer is usually one subject rather than three, and usually the one a marked paper identifies rather than the one that feels hardest. Physics is frequently the right single choice because its losses are mathematical and the same weaknesses damage chemistry calculations, so fixing it lifts two grades. The exception is where the marked papers show practical-skills losses across all three, in which case a practical-skills block is the better purchase because it benefits every science at once for the price of one.

Group classes are plentiful and cheap in this part of Dubai and they do real work: content coverage for a student who is simply behind on material, and structure for a week that needs it. What they cannot do is read one student's script against a mark scheme. The combination that serves a fixed budget best is often group content coverage plus periodic one-to-one marking, which costs less than weekly private teaching and targets better than extra group hours.

sections.heading: Al Khail Road, school buses and a shared study table
paragraphs: Students in this community travel to a wide spread of schools, mostly by bus, and the routes are long because the schools are dispersed across Al Quoz, Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills and the Dubailand belt. The practical consequence is that arrival times vary more here than in a neighbourhood with a school at its centre. Students at Al Quoz schools are often home by 15:30; students travelling to Motor City or Sports City arrive considerably later.

The honest advice is to set the session time from the actual bus arrival rather than from the school's finish time, and then add forty minutes for food and a change of clothes. For most families here that puts the reliable slot at 17:00 to 17:30, and later for the longer routes. A slot booked optimistically early is a slot that gets rescheduled by the third week, and in a subject with as much content as science a rescheduled session is a lost week rather than a lost hour.

Study space needs a short conversation rather than being left to chance. The table is usually shared, so headphones are equipment rather than a luxury, a hard surface matters, and squared paper, a ruler and the student's own calculator rather than a phone should be in place before the first session. The camera is angled at the page, because in practical-skills work the whole exercise is reading diagrams, building tables and plotting graphs with somebody watching.

Where siblings share a room, staggered evenings work and a shared session does not, because two students at different stages in one hour means one is supervised while the other is taught. Ramadan shifts the pattern for several weeks and schools adjust hours; the arrangement that works is fewer and shorter sessions moved to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, agreed before the month begins rather than improvised through it.

Add forty minutes for food and a change before any session starts
Headphones, hard surface, squared paper, own calculator, camera on the page

sections.heading: Routes, codes and the series
paragraphs: Three things on the examination entry decide what revision should contain and none of them is the subject name. The route: separate sciences for three grades, a co-ordinated or double award for two, or a combined award for one. The code: Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 for separates, 0654 for co-ordinated and 0653 for combined; Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for separates and 4SD0 for the double award. And the tier, where Cambridge entries are Core or Extended with a capped ceiling on Core.

One email to the examinations officer requesting the route, the codes and the tiers removes the largest source of wasted revision time in this qualification. A double-award student working through separate-science material is doing more work than the examination will ask for; a Core-tier student revising Extended content is doing work that cannot be rewarded; an Extended student revising only Core content is under-prepared. All three happen regularly and all three are preventable with one message.

On the series: Cambridge IGCSE runs in June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Those are the windows available to a UAE candidate. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, which is worth stating clearly in a community where many families have direct experience of the Indian system. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson's published pattern shows the shape of a surrounding year: its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official document is what a family should plan from rather than a restatement anywhere else.
bullets: Confirm the route, the codes and the tiers in one email
A double-award student should not be revising separate-science material
UAE candidates sit June and November; February and March is India-only
Ask the school for the zone-correct Cambridge timetable and keep it

sections.heading: Permits, honest limits and what to verify
paragraphs: Al Khail Gate households tend to ask this in a practical register: is the neighbour who teaches chemistry on Friday mornings allowed to charge for it. He is, provided he holds a private tuition work permit, and the list of who may hold one is wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The permit arrived with Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and stands for two years free of charge. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with the application made through its smart app, website and e-services system, so the cost of being in order is an evening of form-filling. Tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Since no fine schedule is published, any specific amount should be treated as unverified, and that includes amounts quoted with great confidence in a community group chat.

Four things this site does not do, since each of them gets asked here. Nobody visits your flat: there are no home visits anywhere in the Emirates, and no office, centre or branch in the UAE either, which is also why there is no KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. That is the document a Dubai operation with premises must hold, and premises are precisely what is absent. Candidates are not entered for examinations from here; your child's school or a registered examination centre does that. Ministry equivalency is not performed here either, whatever a listing elsewhere suggests. And there is no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, on this page or on any other page of this site.

Two further limits, one on documents and one on numbers. Documents: the official syllabus, the specimen papers and the published timetable are linked and quoted from here, never reproduced, and board-owned past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are not offered as downloads by this site. A school holds legitimate access to all of it through its own subscriptions, which means the practical papers your child ought to be drilling are a request to the head of science rather than a hunt for a file. Numbers: every figure above carries a source you can follow for yourself, and you will find no success rate, no satisfaction score and no star rating anywhere on this page, because the data that would support any of them does not exist here.

Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Inspection reports live on the regulator's own site, and that is where to read them rather than in anybody's summary, including ours.

faqs.question: Can practical science be taught usefully if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The examinable part can, and that is what affects the grade. Laboratory work for school purposes happens at school under the school's supervision and no tutor takes part in it. What tutoring affects is the written assessment of practical skills, which most international centres sit as an alternative-to-practical paper. Six question types cover nearly all of it: reading an instrument to the correct precision, identifying variables, spotting a flaw in a method, building a results table, plotting and interpreting a graph, and suggesting an improvement that addresses the stated weakness.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send science tutors to homes in Al Khail Gate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. Science sessions here are one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For practical-skills work in particular the format suits the task, since the entire exercise is reading diagrams, annotating results tables and plotting graphs with somebody watching the page. It also means no session is lost to the Al Khail Road afternoon.

faqs.question: Why does my child write repeat and take an average for every improvement question?
faqs.answer: Because it is a safe-sounding answer that was learned once and applied everywhere. It is sometimes correct and frequently irrelevant to the weakness the question described. If the stem has just told you that temperature was not controlled, the question is about temperature control, and repetition will not address it. The habit worth building is to re-read the stem, name the stated weakness, and address that specific thing. It takes about two sessions and it shows up on every practical paper afterwards.

faqs.question: What are the standard experiments our child should be able to describe?
faqs.answer: A short and learnable list. In biology: the food tests for starch, reducing sugar, protein and fat; osmosis in plant tissue; the effect of temperature or pH on enzyme activity; and transpiration. In chemistry: tests for common gases and ions; measuring a reaction rate by gas collection; a titration; and separation techniques. In physics: the resistance of a wire; the focal length of a converging lens; determining density; and timing a pendulum. Practise describing each from memory using a fixed structure, and a whole class of question becomes reliable.

faqs.question: How precisely should a reading be given?
faqs.answer: To a precision appropriate to the instrument's smallest division, and no more. Quoting more decimal places than the instrument supports is an overstatement of accuracy and examiners treat it as wrong. Quoting fewer discards information. The related skill is knowing which instrument suits which measurement: a measuring cylinder, a burette and a pipette do not measure volume equally well, and a question asking which to use is asking about precision rather than preference. Both are examinable and both are quick to teach.

faqs.question: What is the difference between random and systematic error in an exam answer?
faqs.answer: A random error scatters results around the true value and is reduced by repeating and averaging. A systematic error shifts every result in the same direction and is not, which is why a student who offers repetition as a remedy for an unzeroed balance has told the examiner they do not understand the distinction. Teaching the two side by side with a named example of each takes one session, and it converts a commonly dropped mark into a reliable one because the question recurs in all three sciences.

faqs.question: If we can fund one science, which gives the best return?
faqs.answer: Usually the one a marked paper identifies rather than the one that feels hardest, and often that is physics, because its losses are mathematical and the same weaknesses damage chemistry calculations. Fixing it therefore lifts two grades. The exception is where the marked papers show practical-skills losses across all three disciplines, in which case a practical-skills block is better value, because the six question types recur in every science and a short block benefits all of them for the price of one subject.

faqs.question: What does science tutoring cost for a family in this community?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai bands run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 or more for a specialist, and AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the fee. Monthly estimates run about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band for one weekly subject. Those figures come from published provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table rather than from us. We quote after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a local centre good enough for science?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, often yes, and this part of Dubai has plenty of affordable options. A group class works where a student is simply behind on material and needs structure in the week. What it cannot do is read one student's script against a mark scheme and identify that the losses sit in practical-skills procedures and graph work rather than in content. On a fixed budget the best combination is frequently group content coverage plus periodic one-to-one marking, which targets better than extra group hours.

faqs.question: How do we find out whether our child is on separate or double-award science?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer for the route, the syllabus codes and the tiers. Cambridge separates are 0610, 0620 and 0625 giving three grades; 0654 co-ordinated sciences is a double award giving two; 0653 combined gives one. Pearson equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for separates and 4SD0 for the double award. The route determines how much content exists, and a double-award student revising separate-science material is doing more work than the examination will ever ask for.

faqs.question: What time should sessions start given the bus journey?
faqs.answer: Set it from the actual bus arrival rather than the school finish time, then add about forty minutes for food and a change of clothes. Students attending Al Quoz schools are often home by 15:30 and can manage an earlier slot; students travelling to Motor City, Sports City or the outer Dubailand communities arrive considerably later. For most families here the reliable window is 17:00 to 17:30 or after. A slot booked optimistically early gets rescheduled by the third week, and in science that costs a week rather than an hour.

faqs.question: Why do graph marks keep disappearing?
faqs.answer: Four reasons, all manual. A scale that uses only a corner of the grid. Points joined dot to dot instead of a line of best fit being drawn. A gradient read from two plotted points rather than from the drawn line. And a gradient quoted without units, which is incomplete regardless of its value. Each of those is a mark somewhere and each improves faster with somebody watching the page than with unsupervised practice, because a student cannot see their own plotting errors as they make them.

faqs.question: Our child moved into IGCSE science from another system. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With an audit rather than teaching. One session goes through the specification topic by topic to establish what the previous school covered and to what depth, compared against the new department's teaching order. Transfers arrive unevenly rather than uniformly behind, and the audit usually produces three or four real gaps plus a technique problem rather than a whole syllabus. It also prevents weeks spent covering material the student already holds, which is the standard offer a transferring family receives.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor working with an Al Khail Gate family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount you read as unverified. Asking about the permit is a reasonable question in any arrangement.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one short evening, and a timetable to build
paragraphs: An IGCSE candidate on a triple-award timetable in Al Khawaneej is carrying three examined sciences at once, each with its own homework, its own practical lessons and its own assessment cycle. They are also travelling. The community holds primary provision and a Dubai Schools campus, so secondary students go out to Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais or further, and they arrive home late enough that the usable working window on a school night is roughly ninety minutes once a break and a meal have happened.

That combination produces a particular kind of week. Science homework arrives from three directions and is done in whichever order the deadlines force, which means the subject with the most organised teacher gets the most attention and the others get whatever is left. Over two years this quietly shapes a set of results that has very little to do with the student's actual aptitude in each science, and a great deal to do with which teacher sets work on which day.

The remedy is dull and effective: allocate the hours deliberately instead of letting deadlines allocate them. That means knowing which science's work suits a tired weekday evening and which needs a rested weekend morning, where the practical lessons fall and what they leave to be written up, and when each subject's assessments cluster. None of this is about teaching. It is about timetabling, and it is the single most useful thing a family in this catchment can do before buying any tutoring at all. Do it with the three subject outlines side by side, because the clustering only becomes visible once they are on the same page.

There is a second decision in the background, which is whether a student should be carrying three sciences in the first place. Triple award and double award are different workloads with different consequences for sixth form, and the choice is often made on the basis of ambition rather than on the basis of hours available. A student doing two sciences well is in a better position for science A Levels or Diploma sciences than a student doing three badly, and that conversation is worth having before Year 11 rather than during it.

The rest of this page works through all of it: the weekly load, the slot allocation, how the school run shapes when science homework lands, the triple against double decision, how practical skills are examined in writing, revision that genuinely fits ninety minutes, and keeping one loss log across three subjects instead of three separate impressions. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India.

Science is taken either as three separate subjects, awarding three grades, or as a coordinated or combined award covering a defined subset and awarding one or two. Some syllabuses are tiered, and the tier caps the available grade. Practical skills are generally assessed in writing for international candidates.
programmes.countryNote: UK-curriculum schools held thirty-seven per cent of Dubai private enrolment in 2024-25, the largest share of any curriculum, so this is the qualification most Al Khawaneej secondary students sit. Boards vary school by school, so confirm yours from the statement of entry.

programmes.name: AS and A Level sciences
programmes.description: The common next step for a science student here. A Level sciences assume the higher IGCSE tier as their starting point, and in practice they assume the separate-science content rather than the combined subset, which makes the Year 10 award decision consequential two years later.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme sciences
programmes.description: The alternative, where sciences are taken at Higher or Standard Level alongside an independent investigation in each. Receiving schools commonly expect the higher IGCSE tier for Higher Level science entry, and the quantitative step up is sharper than students expect in the first term.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-khawanee.subjectsIntro: The three sciences and the subjects around them, described by what each demands of an evening rather than by content. That is the information a family building a weekly timetable actually needs.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: High recall volume and strict command-term discipline. The only one of the three that genuinely works in twenty-minute blocks on a tired evening, because retrieval practice is short by nature and benefits from frequency rather than from length.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Splits in two for timetabling purposes. Mole arithmetic and definitional recall tolerate a tired slot; ionic equations and organic pathways need a clearer head, so the subject is best divided across two different kinds of session.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The least tolerant of tiredness, because it needs sustained problem-solving and careful algebra. Physics belongs in the best slot of the week, and a Physics session booked straight after a long bus run is usually an hour spent copying worked solutions.

subjects.name: Coordinated or combined science
subjects.description: All three sciences compressed into fewer papers with one or two grades. The content is a defined subset, so the timetabling problem is genuinely lighter, and teaching separate-science material to a combined candidate wastes evenings on topics that will not appear.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject that silently decides science marks. Rearrangement, standard form and graph work appear in every science paper, so twenty minutes a week of context-free algebra practice raises marks in all three sciences at once.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Relevant because extended science answers are written answers. A student who cannot sustain a two-sentence causal explanation in English loses science marks that have nothing to do with their science, and the fix belongs in the English slot.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Shares the logical decomposition that physics problem-solving uses, and its practical component rewards documenting what was actually done. Often taken alongside three sciences, which makes the weekly load heavier than most parents realise.

subjects.name: Environmental Management
subjects.description: Substantial overlap with biology and chemistry on ecosystems, pollution and resources, and it rewards the same data-interpretation skill the science papers test. Reasonable value as a fourth science-adjacent subject if the hours exist.

subjects.name: Additional or Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger mathematicians and useful preparation for A Level sciences. Worth considering only where the weekly load genuinely allows it, since it competes directly with science revision for the same short evenings.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and it occupies timetable and homework hours that any honest science plan has to account for. It is excluded from the five-subject count for British-track equivalency.

sections.heading: The load: three sciences against the hours that exist
paragraphs: Write it down before deciding anything. A triple-award candidate in Al Khawaneej has five school evenings, of which one or two go to co-curricular commitments or a late arrival, leaving three or four with a usable window of about ninety minutes after a break and a meal. Add a weekend and the honest weekly total for independent academic work is perhaps six to nine hours, and that total covers every subject on the timetable rather than only the sciences.

Three sciences setting homework independently will consume most of it without any revision happening at all. That is the structural problem, and it explains the pattern families describe: a diligent student who completes everything set and still arrives at mocks with no secure knowledge of anything. Completing homework is not revision, and three sciences generate enough homework to fill the week while leaving the actual learning undone.

The table sets the arithmetic out. It is deliberately unflattering, because the version of this calculation that helps is the one that produces a decision. Most families who do it conclude one of two things: either the sciences need a deliberate rotation across one weekly slot rather than three separate commitments, or the student should not be carrying three sciences at all. Both are reasonable conclusions and both are much cheaper to reach in Year 10 than in the final term of Year 11. Reaching it early also means the student is part of the decision rather than its subject, which matters more than parents expect at fifteen.
bullets: Three or four usable weekday evenings, not five
Six to nine honest weekly hours, covering every subject
Three sciences' homework can fill that with no revision at all
Completing set work is not the same as learning the material

sections.heading: Which science belongs in which slot
paragraphs: The three sciences do not make the same demands on attention, and matching them to the available slots is free. Most families do the opposite by accident, giving physics the weekday evening after a ninety-minute bus ride because that is when the homework is due, and leaving the weekend for whichever subject feels least threatening.

Biology suits a tired evening better than the other two, because its work is largely retrieval and retrieval is short by nature. Twenty minutes of self-testing on a topic, three times in a week, outperforms a single ninety-minute reading session by a wide margin, and a tired student can still do it. Chemistry divides: mole arithmetic and definitional recall tolerate a tired slot once the method is secure, while ionic equations and organic pathways need a clearer head. Physics belongs in the best hour of the week, because sustained problem-solving collapses when attention is low and the student ends up copying worked solutions, which teaches recognition rather than recall.

The table below is the allocation worth trying for a fortnight. The pattern it produces for a long-run student is usually a weekend morning for physics, short biology retrieval on two or three weekday evenings, and chemistry split between the two depending on the topic. It costs nothing to rearrange and it routinely produces more than an additional tutored hour would. Try the allocation for a fortnight and ask your child which evenings felt productive; the answer is usually clearer than any theory about study habits.

sections.heading: What the school run does to when science work happens
paragraphs: The number that governs everything is not when the school day ends. It is when the student is at a desk, fed, and capable of thinking. Between those two points sit the bus departure, the multi-stop route, the arrival in Al Khawaneej and the twenty to thirty minutes of break and food that cannot be skipped without wasting the hour that follows.

For a student travelling to the Mirdif cluster that chain is manageable. For one on a route to Al Qusais or deep into Al Warqa it can consume an hour and a half, and on days with an after-school commitment it consumes the evening. A plan built on the published end of the school day will therefore fail, and it will fail in a way that looks like the student lacking commitment rather than like the plan being wrong.

Measure it for one week, writing down only the final number: the time the first page was genuinely open. Five numbers give you the real window. Then build the science week inside it, put physics at the weekend, and treat activity days as days with no academic work beyond submission deadlines. One further point specific to this catchment: multi-stop routes make arrival time variable, so a tutored slot needs a buffer rather than a precise start, and a session that begins fifteen minutes late is better than one the student arrives at breathless. A buffer also removes an argument from the week, which has its own value.
bullets: Four different times exist; only the last one is useful
The break and meal cannot be skipped without wasting the hour

sections.heading: Triple award or double: an hours decision rather than an ambition one
paragraphs: Carrying three separate sciences is a choice, and in this catchment it is often made without the hours being counted. The alternative, a coordinated or combined award, covers a defined subset of all three sciences and awards one or two grades instead of three. The subset is genuinely smaller rather than merely easier, which is precisely why it is a reasonable choice for a student whose week cannot hold three full syllabuses.

The honest comparison is this. A student doing two sciences well, or a combined award securely, is in a better position for sixth-form science than a student doing three sciences badly, because sixth-form entry depends on grades achieved rather than on subjects attempted. The caution runs the other way too: some A Level and Diploma science routes expect separate-science grades, so the decision has to be checked against the destination rather than made on workload alone.

Three questions settle it. How many hours does your child actually have, measured rather than assumed. What do the sixth forms and programmes you are considering require, in writing. And what does the current evidence from marked papers say about whether three syllabuses are being held or three are being half-held. Ask those before entries are fixed. Once the series has been sat the award structure is a fact on the certificate, and a student who half-held three sciences has three mediocre grades rather than two good ones. The question is uncomfortable and the answer is usually visible in a marked paper rather than in a conversation.

sections.heading: Practicals at school, practical papers in writing
paragraphs: International IGCSE candidates generally demonstrate practical skills in writing rather than in a laboratory, which produces a paper that asks about experiments the candidate never performed. Students find this strange; it is in fact the most predictable paper they will sit, because the question types recur relentlessly across all three sciences.

The recurring types are a short list. Identify which variable was changed and which were held constant. Read a measurement to an appropriate precision and give its unit. Explain why one result does not fit the pattern. Suggest a single improvement to the method. Draw or complete a results table correctly. Each of these can be practised against unfamiliar methods without any apparatus, and a student who has done twenty of them will do them reliably under exam conditions.

The improvement question is where vague answers lose marks and it is worth teaching explicitly. Saying the experiment should be repeated earns little. Saying that repeating it and taking a mean would reduce the effect of random error in the timing measurement earns the mark, because it names the error and the mechanism. Anomaly questions work identically: the mark is for a specific plausible cause tied to the method described, not for noticing that one point sits above the others. For a family with limited hours this is excellent value, because the work applies to biology, chemistry and physics at the same time. Confirm with your exams officer exactly how practical skills are assessed on your child's syllabus, because the arrangement is board-specific.
bullets: Questions concern experiments the candidate did not perform
The question types recur across all three sciences
Improvement answers must name the error and the mechanism
One block of practice pays into all three subjects

sections.heading: Revision that genuinely fits ninety minutes
paragraphs: Most revision advice assumes an evening that an Al Khawaneej student does not have. What works in ninety minutes is different from what works in four hours, and the difference is not about doing less of the same thing. It is about choosing methods whose return per minute is high and whose start-up cost is low.

Re-reading notes has almost no return and a very low start-up cost, which is exactly why students default to it. Self-testing from memory has a high return and a slightly higher start-up cost, because it requires covering the notes and tolerating the discomfort of not knowing. Past-paper questions under time pressure have the highest return and the highest start-up cost, which is why they belong in the weekend slot rather than at the end of a long day. Matching method to slot is the whole skill.

The table gives the allocation. Two habits are worth building regardless of slot. The first is marking your own work against the published scheme before anyone else sees it, which teaches what the examiner rewards faster than being told ever will. The second is logging what was lost by cause rather than by topic, because causes transfer across every paper and topics only pay if they reappear. Material should come from the school and the boards' own published pages; IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables. Neither habit requires a tutor to be present, which makes them the right things to establish first.

sections.heading: One loss log across three sciences
paragraphs: Families carrying three sciences usually end up with three separate impressions: biology is fine, chemistry is a worry, physics is a disaster. Impressions are not actionable. A single loss log across all three subjects is, and it almost always reveals that the three sciences are failing for the same two or three reasons rather than for nine different ones.

The method is simple. After every marked piece of science work, write down each lost mark with its cause rather than its topic: a missing unit, a command term answered descriptively, a mole conversion, an algebraic rearrangement, a precision error, running out of time. Keep them all in one place regardless of subject. After six pieces of work, count. Two or three causes will dominate across all three sciences, and those are what the next block of work should attack.

This changes what tutoring is for. Instead of three subjects each needing attention, there is a short list of transferable faults, and fixing one of them raises marks in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously. Unit discipline is the clearest example: a student who stops omitting units gains marks in every quantitative question in all three papers. For a family with six to nine honest hours a week, that kind of leverage is not a nicety. It is the only way the arithmetic works. Start the log in whatever is to hand; a page in the back of a notebook works as well as anything designed for it, and the only rule that matters is that all three sciences go in the same place.
bullets: One log, all three sciences, causes rather than topics
Two or three causes usually dominate across all three subjects
Fixing a cause raises marks in every science at once
Count after six pieces of work rather than reacting to each one

sections.heading: Starting, and what is disclosed about availability
paragraphs: Send four things. The statement of entry showing the board, the codes and whether the entry is separate sciences or a combined award, plus the tier where one applies. The most recent marked script in each science if available, or at least one. The school's assessment dates for the term. And the measured weekday time your child is genuinely able to work, from a week of writing down when the first page was actually open.

Then a free trial lesson, one-to-one over live video. Ask the tutor to read the marked work and say what the dominant loss causes are across the sciences rather than which topics need revising. That is the answer that makes a ninety-minute week workable, and a tutor who gives it has understood the actual problem. If the hour produces a list of topics instead, the plan it leads to will not fit the hours available.

The disclosure, before you ask. Coverage is held by board and syllabus rather than by the word science, and a tutor who covers all three sciences at the required tier on your child's board is a narrower category than it sounds. In some weeks nobody UAE-based fits that description with a slot that suits an Al Khawaneej timetable. Where that happens you will be told, and offered a specialist based elsewhere teaching the same syllabus over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time, or two tutors working to one plan if that serves better. Nothing is substituted quietly, and no competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

whyPoints.description: Three sciences against six to nine honest weekly hours is the real problem in this catchment, and the arithmetic comes first. A plan allocating three tutored hours a week to a ninety-minute evening is a plan that lapses by week eight.

faqs.question: How does a triple-award science student in Al Khawaneej fit three subjects into one evening?
faqs.answer: They do not, and planning as though they can is what produces a diligent student with nothing securely learned. A student here has three or four usable weekday evenings of about ninety minutes after travel, a break and a meal, plus a weekend, giving six to nine honest weekly hours for every subject rather than only the sciences. Three sciences' homework can consume that entirely. The workable approach is a deliberate allocation: short biology retrieval on weekday evenings, physics at the weekend, chemistry split by topic.

faqs.question: Which science should get the weekend morning?
faqs.answer: Physics, in almost every case. It needs sustained problem-solving and careful algebra, and a tired student working on physics ends up copying worked solutions, which builds recognition rather than the ability to start a question cold. Biology is the opposite: its work is retrieval, which is short by nature and tolerates tiredness, so twenty-minute self-testing blocks on weekday evenings suit it better than a long weekend session. Chemistry divides, with calculation tolerating a tired slot and organic reasoning needing a clearer head.

faqs.question: Should my child take three separate sciences or a combined award?
faqs.answer: Count the hours and check the destination before deciding. A combined or coordinated award covers a defined subset of all three sciences and awards fewer grades, and it is a sound choice for a student whose week cannot hold three full syllabuses, because sixth-form entry depends on grades achieved rather than subjects attempted. The caution is that some A Level and Diploma science routes expect separate-science grades, so ask the receiving sixth form in writing what it requires before entries are fixed.

faqs.question: Why does my child finish all the science homework and still do badly in tests?
faqs.answer: Because completing set work is not revision, and three sciences generate enough homework to fill a short week while leaving the learning undone. Homework is practice and diagnostic information; a test requires retrieval from memory, which is a different activity. The change that helps is small and specific: protect two or three twenty-minute blocks a week for self-testing from memory with the notes covered, and treat them as non-negotiable rather than as what happens if the homework finishes early.

faqs.question: How are practical skills examined if my child does not sit a laboratory exam?
faqs.answer: In writing, generally, for international candidates, which produces questions about experiments the candidate never performed. The question types recur across all three sciences: identify which variable changed and which were controlled, read a measurement to the right precision with its unit, explain an anomaly, suggest one improvement, complete a results table. These are learnable without apparatus and respond strongly to practice against unfamiliar methods. Confirm the exact arrangement for your child's syllabus with the school's exams officer, since it is board-specific.

faqs.question: What makes an improvement answer earn the mark?
faqs.answer: Naming the error and the mechanism rather than the action. Saying the experiment should be repeated earns little. Saying that repeating it and taking a mean would reduce the effect of random error in the timing measurement earns the mark, because it identifies what kind of error exists and how the change addresses it. Anomaly questions work the same way: the credit is for a specific plausible cause tied to the method described, not for observing that one result does not fit the pattern.

faqs.question: Is it better to tutor one science or all three?
faqs.answer: One, in most Al Khawaneej households, with the subject chosen from marked papers rather than from which feels worst. Three weekly tutored sessions do not fit a ninety-minute weekday evening and will be attended inconsistently before lapsing. The alternative that works is one weekly slot rotating across the sciences according to what is coming next, with a single tutor holding the whole picture and one loss log covering all three subjects rather than three separate impressions.

faqs.question: What is a loss log and why keep one across all three sciences?
faqs.answer: A written record of every lost mark by its cause rather than its topic: a missing unit, a command term answered descriptively, a mole conversion, a rearrangement, a precision error, running out of time. Kept in one place across biology, chemistry and physics, it almost always shows that the three subjects are failing for two or three shared reasons rather than nine separate ones. Fixing unit discipline, for instance, raises marks in every quantitative question across all three papers simultaneously.

faqs.question: How much does maths affect my child's science grades?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect, and the effect is largest in physics. Rearrangement, standard form, ratio and graph work appear inside science questions, so a student who handles them slowly spends their attention on the algebra rather than on the science and loses marks that look like science failures. Twenty minutes a week of context-free algebra practice, with no science attached, raises marks across all three subjects. It is the cheapest intervention available for a family short of hours.

faqs.question: What should we do on days with after-school activities?
faqs.answer: Treat them as days with no academic work beyond submission deadlines. A student travelling back to Al Khawaneej after a commitment has no usable window left, and a session booked there will be attended badly or cancelled late, which damages the arrangement as well as wasting the hour. Put the tutored slot on a clear evening early in the school week so there are days left to act on the feedback, and keep the demanding work for a weekend morning.

faqs.question: Does the bus route really change what we should plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, materially. A student travelling to the Mirdif cluster keeps a usable evening; one on a route to Al Qusais or deep into Al Warqa can lose an hour and a half door to door, and multi-stop routes make the arrival time variable rather than fixed. The practical consequences are two: build the science week from three or four evenings rather than five, and give a tutored slot a buffer instead of a precise start, because a session beginning fifteen minutes late beats one the student arrives at breathless.

faqs.question: When should a Year 10 science student start getting help?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the better of the two years for it, because the problems at that stage are foundations rather than topics, and foundations take a term rather than a fortnight. A syllabus audit against the actual codes, marking each statement secure, shaky or unmet, takes two or three sessions and usually shows the gap is narrower than it feels. Starting then also establishes the marking and loss-log habits before the pressure arrives, which is when they are hardest to build and most valuable.

faqs.question: Where should science past papers and mark schemes come from?
faqs.answer: From the school, which holds the material it is entitled to use, and from the boards' own published pages. Files circulating in parent groups are frequently from the wrong code, the wrong tier or an outdated specification, and an outdated syllabus is worse than none because it looks authoritative while quietly adding or removing topics. IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables; sessions work from official material the school already provides.

faqs.question: What should an Al Khawaneej family send before a first science session?
faqs.answer: Four things. The statement of entry showing board, syllabus codes, whether the entry is separate sciences or a combined award, and the tier where one applies. At least one recent marked science script with teacher comments intact. The school's assessment dates for the term. And the measured weekday time your child is genuinely able to work, from a week of noting when the first page was actually open. Those four make the trial hour a diagnosis rather than an introduction.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-khawanee.closingHeading: Build the week, then buy the hour
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-khawanee.closingBody: Three sciences and a long school run is a timetabling problem before it is a teaching one. Measure the real evening for a week, give physics the weekend morning, keep biology in short repeated blocks, split chemistry by topic, and put every lost mark in one log by cause rather than by subject. Then buy a single rotating slot rather than three commitments the week cannot hold. intro.heading: Three sciences, one commute, and about four usable hours a week
paragraphs: Start with the week rather than the syllabus, because the week is what defeats most science tutoring plans in this neighbourhood. A Year 11 student in Al Mamzar on a British curriculum is almost certainly commuting - the schools immediately around here predominantly teach CBSE or the Ministry curriculum, and Indian-curriculum schools account for 26 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment with a far higher local share. So the day ends somewhere else and the journey home happens in the worst hour of the afternoon.

Count what is actually left. School finishes between roughly 2.30pm and 3.30pm depending on the cluster. The journey back takes fifteen minutes from Al Qusais and up to fifty from across the creek, with real variance rather than a fixed figure. Add an activity on one or two afternoons, homework across eight or nine subjects, and prayer times. What remains, realistically, is three or four hours a week in which a student can concentrate on something that is not school homework - and that is the budget to allocate across biology, chemistry and physics.

Three sciences into three or four hours does not divide well, which is why the sequencing question matters more here than the teaching question. A family that buys three weekly sessions ends up with six hours of tuition on top of a full timetable, and the first thing to stop is the independent practice that converts teaching into marks. The result is a student who is busier, more tired, and no closer to a grade. One science at a time, chosen deliberately and finished, produces more from a quarter of the money.

Choosing which science to take first is not a matter of which grade looks worst. It is a matter of which marks are cheapest to recover, and that is visible in a marked paper. There is also a prior question worth five minutes: whether the real problem is science at all. Proportion, equation rearrangement, standard form, unit conversion and graph reading are examined inside all three sciences, and a student weak there loses marks in every one and concludes they are bad at science generally.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Mamzar or anywhere else in the UAE; a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. On a commuting timetable that is not a marketing preference, it is the practical difference between a session that happens at the same time every week and one that depends on two uncertain arrivals - the student's and the tutor's - lining up on the same stretch of Al Ittihad Road.

What follows is ordered to be acted on. The first section writes out the week slot by slot with an honest reliability rating for each, from this neighbourhood. The second gives the five-minute test to run at the kitchen table before any science is chosen, and then orders the possible targets by return per session. After that: why sequencing beats running three sciences in parallel, what the practical component actually assesses and what no tutor can teach, how Ramadan and the November series reshape the revision window, and the cost arithmetic of three subjects from a district where visiting travel is longer than average.
