dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-mamzar.programmesIntro: Science decisions made at fourteen shape what is possible at sixteen and eighteen. These are the stages an Al Mamzar family is planning across, with the local consideration at each.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 science, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Combined science teaching across three years, ending in the triple or double award recommendation. Nothing is externally examined, so weak proportion and unit work travel undetected into Year 10 - and because this is also the stage when many families in this district transfer between curricula, those gaps can come from a change of system rather than from the student.
programmes.countryNote: In Deira and Al Qusais, curriculum transfers happen in both directions and often mid-key-stage. A student moving from CBSE science into a British curriculum in Year 8 or 9 usually arrives strong on content and unfamiliar with investigation, variable control and extended written explanation - which is the opposite of the gap families expect and a different thing to buy.

programmes.name: IGCSE sciences, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Triple award means three syllabuses and three grades: Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Double award - Cambridge 0654 or Pearson's Science Double Award - covers all three disciplines at reduced depth for two grades. Practical skills are assessed by practical test, by a written alternative, or within the written papers depending on board and centre.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track a student needs five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five. Sciences usually form part of that count. One competing tutoring site tells UAE parents six subjects are required; check the Ministry's own pages first.

programmes.name: A Level sciences, Years 12 and 13
programmes.description: Entry normally requires the separate science at the upper tier, often at grade 7 or above. Departments are frequently unwilling to admit double-award students to A Level chemistry or physics because the content coverage is materially thinner, and in a commuting household that can also narrow which schools are practical for sixth form.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Mamzar family the post-16 question has a travel dimension as well as an academic one. If the nearest school offering A Level sciences sits across the creek, a two-year commitment to that journey at seventeen is a real factor, and it is worth weighing while the Year 11 subject plan is still open rather than afterwards.

programmes.name: The CBSE science comparison, locally
programmes.description: Most schools near Al Mamzar teach CBSE, so families here often weigh a British-curriculum science commute against a CBSE place nearby. The assessment difference matters for tutoring: CBSE rewards accurate recall against a defined syllabus, while IGCSE sciences reward command-term discipline, extended explanation and precise practical writing.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence is that local tutoring supply in this district is strongest in CBSE science and in Arabic, because that is where local demand sits. A household with one IGCSE child and one CBSE child usually needs two different arrangements, and insisting on one produces a compromise that serves neither well.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-mamzar.subjectsIntro: These are the science syllabuses and immediate neighbours Al Mamzar families ask about, with the component that decides the grade named.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The largest content volume of the three, which is why revision tends to go broad and shallow. Extended responses need the specification's own terms, so a biologically correct answer in everyday language frequently scores nothing.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables are the reliable losses, and organic arrives last. The analysis tables are a memorisation task students keep deferring, and they are among the cheapest marks available.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity on unfamiliar circuits is the worst case at Extended tier, because students learn worked examples rather than a reduction method. Graph gradients are calculated correctly and their physical meaning left unstated.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences, Double Award (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Two grades covering all three disciplines at reduced depth. Chosen for timetable reasons more often than for academic ones, and its effect on post-16 science access is usually discovered during the Year 11 conversation rather than before.

subjects.name: Combined Science, Single Award (Cambridge 0653)
subjects.description: One grade and the lowest content volume of the three structures. Workable where science is not a post-16 destination and a genuine obstacle where it is, so it should be confirmed against intended A Level choices.

subjects.name: Practical test and alternative-to-practical papers
subjects.description: The most under-prepared component in IGCSE science. The written version is precision writing: describing a method, naming variables, reading apparatus to the correct resolution, spotting a flaw and suggesting a targeted improvement.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject that silently decides science grades. Proportion, rearrangement, standard form and graph work appear inside every science paper, which is why a student failing three sciences usually has one problem.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside by students heading for A Level sciences. It brings algebraic fluency and calculus forward a year and makes the post-16 science transition noticeably smoother, and it is routinely taught in fewer hours than it needs.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Relevant to science grades in this district more than families expect. Extended science responses are marked on precise written explanation, and a student working in a second language loses marks on expression rather than on understanding.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Local supply for the first-language pathway is strong in this district, unlike for the sciences.

sections.heading: The week, written out, with the hours that actually exist
paragraphs: Most tutoring plans fail on arithmetic rather than on pedagogy, so it is worth doing the arithmetic. A Year 11 science student commuting from a school in Al Garhoud or across the creek is not home and settled until somewhere between 3.45pm and 4.30pm, with real week-to-week variance. Homework across eight or nine subjects consumes two to three hours most evenings. Prayer times, dinner and an activity on one or two afternoons take the rest.

What that leaves is three or four hours a week of genuinely usable attention outside school homework, and a weekend morning. That is the budget. Any plan that assumes more than that will be abandoned by the third week of term, and the usual way it gets abandoned is that the student stops doing the between-session work first, which is the part that actually produces marks.

The practical consequence is that the slot has to be chosen for reliability and the content has to be chosen for yield. A session placed at 5pm against a creek commute will routinely start late and finish at the same time, which turns a sixty-minute lesson into forty with the first ten spent restarting. A session placed at 7.30pm starts on time every week because it depends on nothing. On a commuting timetable the second is worth more than the first even though it looks worse on paper.

The weekend block is the piece families in this district most often leave out. A longer Saturday or Sunday morning session is the only realistic time to sit a full timed science paper and review it in the same sitting, and without that there is no diagnosis - only an impression. Used alongside one weekday session it gives a Year 11 student both consistency and genuine measurement, and it depends on no road at all.

sections.heading: Which science to fix first, and the test that comes before all three
paragraphs: Before choosing a science, run a five-minute test at the kitchen table. Write down an unfamiliar formula - anything with three or four symbols the student has not seen - and ask them to make a given symbol the subject. No science, no context. Then ask them to convert a figure into standard form, and to read the gradient off a printed graph and say what it means physically.

If any of that is slow or uncertain, the science grades are a symptom. Proportion, rearrangement, standard form, unit conversion and graph reading are examined inside biology, chemistry and physics alike, and a student weak there loses marks in all three while concluding they are bad at science. Two sessions on that, with no subject content attached, lifts every science paper at once and is the best-value purchase available in this subject area.

If the quantitative test is clean, then the choice between sciences is made from marked papers rather than from grades. The question is not which grade is worst but where the cheapest marks are. A paper losing twelve marks to the qualitative analysis tables in chemistry is cheaper to fix than one losing twelve marks spread across every biology topic, because the first is a defined memorisation task and the second is a revision-method problem that takes a term.

The table below orders the options by return per session, which is the order a limited budget should follow. It is written to be read against a marked script. The point of ordering it this way is that most families work top-down from the worst grade, and the worst grade is frequently the most expensive one to move.

sections.heading: Sequencing, not parallelising, three sciences
paragraphs: The instinct when a report shows three weak science grades is to buy three tutors, and it is the single most common way science tutoring money is wasted in this catchment. Three weekly sessions is six hours of tuition a week on top of a full timetable and a commute, and the student has three or four usable hours. Something has to give, and what gives is always the independent practice.

That matters because independent practice is where the marks come from. A tutor can explain circuit reduction clearly in forty minutes, and the student will still lose circuit marks unless they then work through fifteen unfamiliar networks alone. Tutoring that consumes the time in which that practice would have happened is not neutral - it actively reduces the return on itself, which is why more is frequently worse.

Sequencing solves it. Take one science, run a block of six to eight sessions with a timed paper at each end, finish, and then decide whether the next block is worth buying. The decision at the end of the first block is genuinely informative: if the targeted marks moved, the method works and the second block is a good bet. If they did not, something is wrong with the match or the diagnosis, and buying two more tutors would have compounded the error rather than hedging it.

There is one case for running two at once: both sciences are genuinely weak, the papers are within two terms, and the student has the capacity. Even then, two specialists on different evenings beats one generalist covering both, because biology, chemistry and physics fail for different reasons. With online delivery the second appointment adds no travel for anybody, which is the one respect in which this catchment's geography stops mattering.

sections.heading: The practical component when the school laboratory is the only laboratory
paragraphs: Practical skills are assessed in every IGCSE science, either through a practical test, through a written alternative-to-practical paper, or within the written papers depending on the board and the centre. Which applies to your child is a question for the school, and it is worth asking early because the three require different preparation and a student prepared for the wrong one has prepared for nothing.

The honest limitation of any tutoring arrangement - online or in-home - is that apparatus cannot be handled in a lesson. A tutor cannot show a student how a burette behaves at the endpoint, how a micrometer feels when over-tightened, or why an ammeter reading drifts. That learning happens in the school laboratory, and laboratory provision differs between schools in this district, which is a fair question to ask on a school tour rather than to discover in Year 11.

What tutoring can do is the part the written papers actually assess, which is mostly not dexterity. Describing a method precisely enough that another student could follow it. Naming the independent, dependent and control variables and saying how each is controlled. Reading apparatus to the correct resolution and recording to a consistent number of decimal places. Identifying a flaw in a described procedure and suggesting a targeted improvement rather than a generic one.

All of that is precision writing applied to science, marked on specific wording, and it improves faster than content work because the body of technique is small. It also transfers completely between biology, chemistry and physics, which makes it unusually efficient for a triple-award student with limited hours. Two sessions, with answers written, marked strictly against official schemes and rewritten, generally recovers more marks per hour than anything else available.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar and where the revision window actually sits
paragraphs: The UAE academic year has features that reshape a revision plan, and science revision is particularly sensitive to them because it needs sustained concentration rather than short bursts. School days shorten during Ramadan, afternoons become unproductive for most students, and the usual after-school hour is the worst hour of the day rather than a neutral one.

The practical response is to move the whole timetable rather than to persist and lose sessions. A session at 9pm or 9.30pm after Iftar is frequently the most alert hour available, and because delivery is online there is nothing to rearrange beyond a calendar entry and nobody driving at an awkward hour. Families in this district who plan that shift in advance keep their session count intact; families who improvise lose three or four weeks of it.

The timing matters because Ramadan falls close to the run-up to the summer papers in the current cycle, which is exactly when a Year 11 science student should be rotating through whole timed papers. Losing that block is expensive in a way that losing an equivalent block in October would not be. Planning the shift in January rather than discovering it in March is the difference.

The calendar also has a second half that most revision advice ignores. UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June series and the November series - the February/March series is offered to India only - and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. For a science student who misses a grade in the summer, the November route exists, entries close well before the late-October start, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Deciding in advance what grade would justify a resit makes that a short conversation rather than a scramble.

Online, the budget end starts at roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour with Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik, which generally means a university student. A qualified subject tutor online is published from around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist work is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above.

In-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price. For three sciences that travel is paid three times if three different specialists visit, or the family accepts one generalist covering all three - which is the usual outcome and the reason in-home science tutoring across a triple award rarely works well. Advertised packages run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Read monthly, published estimates for a weekly one-hour session in Dubai run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Multiply any of those by three and the number stops being a tutoring decision and becomes a household-budget decision. Sequencing one science at a time keeps it in the first category.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page, because a figure quoted without knowing the award structure, the number of sciences and the frequency is a number rather than information. sections.heading: Materials, honesty and the one thing you can verify
paragraphs: IGCSE sciences carry practical and, in some syllabuses, coursework components, which is where the honesty line gets tested. A tutor may teach content, explain what a mark scheme rewards, model a method on a different question, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, finish or edit assessed work to completion, including when it is described as polishing.

The consequence is asymmetric. The school signs an authentication that the work is the candidate's own, and if that is untrue the sanction falls on the student while the provider keeps the fee. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price. Recognising that trade for what it is matters more than any rule, because the rule is enforced against the student and nobody else.

Materials follow the same principle. We reference Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes, cite them, and link out to the boards. We do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads, because they are the boards' copyright and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. A tutor who opens with an offer of a mark-scheme folder has told you how they work before the first lesson.

The verifiable thing is the permit, and almost nobody asks. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so treat quoted penalty figures as unverified.

sections.heading: KHDA, the timetable squeeze and the Sharjah boundary
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The sector ran 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment and Indian at 26. Inspection reports are public and comment on teaching quality by subject, which makes them the most useful comparison of science provision between two schools in this district.

The mandatory UAE subjects shape every timetable regardless of curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated against a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and at least twenty-five minutes is advised for any mandatory subject lesson.

Three separate sciences need roughly half again as many periods as a double award, and in a Year 10 timetable that also has to fit the mandatory subjects, mathematics, English and two or three options, triple award is rationed. That is the structural reason behind a pattern families in this district notice without diagnosing: triple award is offered to fewer students than want it, and where it is offered the periods can be tighter than the content needs.

The Sharjah boundary matters here specifically. Al Mamzar sits minutes from it, and some families in this neighbourhood have children at schools regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than KHDA. Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval rather than only inspection sits with the emirate. For completeness: ADEK covers Abu Dhabi, the Department of Knowledge covers Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

process.title: Run the five-minute test at home
process.description: An unfamiliar formula to rearrange, a figure into standard form, a gradient read off a printed graph and explained. If any of it is slow, the first two sessions are quantitative ones and they pay in all three sciences rather than one.

process.title: Tell us the school and the journey
process.description: Which school, in which cluster, and how the student travels. That determines whether an afternoon slot is realistic or whether the evening is the only one that will hold through a term, and it is the question most providers skip.

process.title: Send marked papers from each science
process.description: Three marked scripts show whether this is one problem or three, and where the cheapest marks are. The distribution of lost marks across content, quantitative error, command terms, practical technique and time is what sets the order.

process.title: Confirm the award structure and the practical route
process.description: Triple, double or single award, the syllabus codes, and whether the centre enters a practical test or the written alternative. One email, and it prevents preparing for the wrong component entirely.

process.title: Take one science, finish the block
process.description: Six to eight sessions with a timed paper at each end, then a decision. We would rather you buy one block that works than three that collectively remove the practice time the marks depend on.

process.title: Book the weekend slot for diagnosis
process.description: A longer weekend session is the only realistic time to sit a full paper and review it in the same sitting. We build those in at the start and end of a block so progress is measured rather than reported.

whyPoints.title: The week is planned before the syllabus
whyPoints.description: We work out how many concentrating hours a commuting student actually has, then allocate them. Plans that assume twelve hours a week get abandoned by week three, and the independent practice goes first.

whyPoints.title: One problem, not three
whyPoints.description: Three weak science grades usually share a quantitative cause. We test it with no subject content attached before selling subject hours, because fixing it lifts biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously.

whyPoints.title: Sequenced, not parallel
whyPoints.description: One science, one block, a timed paper at each end, then a decision. It costs a third of three tutors and produces more, because the student keeps the hours in which practice happens.

whyPoints.title: Slots chosen for reliability
whyPoints.description: A 7.30pm session that starts on time every week is worth more than a 5pm session that starts late half the time. On a creek commute that is not a preference, it is arithmetic.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Method description, variables, apparatus resolution and evaluation are precision writing marked on specific words, they improve fast, and they transfer across all three sciences at once.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the laboratory limit
whyPoints.description: Apparatus handling belongs in the school laboratory and no tutoring arrangement replaces it. What we do is the analysis and the writing, which is what the written papers actually assess.

faqs.question: How many science sessions a week can a commuting Year 11 student in Al Mamzar actually manage?
faqs.answer: Realistically two, plus a weekend block. Once school finishing times, a journey of fifteen to fifty minutes depending on the cluster, homework across eight or nine subjects, prayer times and an activity or two are accounted for, there are three or four hours of genuinely usable attention left in a week. A plan built on more than that gets abandoned by the third week of term, and what gets dropped first is the independent practice that converts teaching into marks.

faqs.question: My son is weak in biology, chemistry and physics. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a five-minute test, not with a science. Write down an unfamiliar formula and ask him to make a given symbol the subject; ask for a figure in standard form; ask him to read a gradient off a printed graph and say what it means. If any of that is slow, the science grades are a symptom, because proportion, rearrangement and graph reading are examined inside all three subjects. Two sessions on that, with no science attached, lifts every paper at once.

faqs.question: Is the 4.30pm slot realistic if school is in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. A finish between 2.30pm and 3.15pm across the creek means a journey of thirty to fifty minutes back to Al Mamzar at that hour, with a swing of twenty-five minutes or more week to week. A 5pm booking against that becomes a forty-minute session with ten unproductive minutes at the start, often enough to make the slot unreliable. A 7.30pm session depends on no road at all, which is why it holds through a whole term in this catchment.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all three sciences for a triple-award student here?
faqs.answer: At Core tier or in Year 10, reasonably well. At Extended tier in Year 11, the three fail for different reasons - chemistry's mole system and analysis tables, physics's circuit reduction, biology's specification vocabulary - and are taught best by people who teach them. Where two sciences genuinely need attention at once, two specialists on two evenings beats one generalist across both, and with online delivery the second appointment costs nobody any travel.

faqs.question: Which part of the science papers is most under-prepared?
faqs.answer: The practical component, almost always. Cambridge assesses practical skills through a practical test or a written alternative depending on syllabus and centre, and Pearson assesses them within the written papers in several subjects. The written version asks for a precisely described method, named and controlled variables, apparatus read to the correct resolution, a flaw identified and a targeted improvement. It is precision writing marked on specific words, it improves quickly, and it transfers across all three sciences.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor come to the house in Al Mamzar?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Mamzar, in Dubai, or anywhere else in the UAE - a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For three sciences the in-home arithmetic is particularly poor: published visiting rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and three specialists means that travel is paid three times.

faqs.question: How should we handle the Ramadan weeks for science revision?
faqs.answer: Move the whole timetable in advance rather than improvising week by week. School days shorten, afternoons become unproductive, and a session at 9pm or 9.30pm after Iftar is frequently the most alert hour available. Because the lessons are online there is nothing to rearrange beyond a calendar entry. The timing matters because Ramadan currently falls close to the run-up to the summer papers, which is exactly when a Year 11 student should be rotating through whole timed papers.

faqs.question: My daughter's school only offers double award. Does that limit her?
faqs.answer: For post-16 science, yes, and it is a structural limit rather than an academic one. A Level chemistry and physics departments and Diploma Higher Level sciences generally expect the separate subject, and many are reluctant to admit double-award students. If a science destination matters, the options are to make an evidence-based case for a triple-award place while timetabling still allows it, or to plan a route that accepts the double-award outcome. Both work; discovering it in Year 13 does not.

faqs.question: What does a full science tutoring plan cost from this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether you sequence or parallelise. Published monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session in Dubai run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a qualified subject tutor and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Multiply by three and it becomes a household-budget decision rather than a tutoring one. One science at a time keeps it in the first category and usually produces more. Our trial and consultation are free.

faqs.question: Is a local tuition centre a better option for science here?
faqs.answer: For Year 10 routine and consolidation it often is, and we would rather say so. Centres in Al Qusais and Deira offer structure, supervision, a peer group and a lower cost per student. The limitation is that a group has to share a board and a tier to be taught efficiently, and in this district the group is often mixed in both, so the overlap gets taught. Once a marked paper identifies a specific narrow gap, a group setting cannot address it.

faqs.question: My child came from a CBSE school. What is actually different in IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Not the content, mostly - the assessment. IGCSE sciences reward command-term discipline, extended written explanation and precise practical writing, where CBSE rewards accurate recall against a defined syllabus. A student who knew the material well in Class 9 can lose marks in Year 10 for answering the topic rather than the question, or for describing where the question said explain. A term on command terms, six-mark structure and practical method writing closes most of it.

faqs.question: Should we plan a November resit for a science before the summer results come?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the window afterwards is short. Decide in advance what grade would justify a resit in each science so the decision takes minutes. UAE Cambridge candidates sit June and November, and Pearson International GCSE runs May/June and November. Entries for November close well before the late-October start, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Ask the exams officer for the paper-level breakdown: a near-miss on one paper is a far better resit case than a uniform shortfall.

faqs.question: Does the school's laboratory matter if we are getting tutoring anyway?
faqs.answer: Yes, because no tutoring arrangement replaces it. Apparatus handling - how a burette behaves at the endpoint, how a micrometer feels over-tightened, why an ammeter drifts - is learned in the school laboratory and nowhere else, and provision differs between schools in this district. It is a fair question on a school tour. What tutoring covers is the analysis and the writing the papers actually assess, which is the larger share of the available practical marks.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free for the science and tier we need?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting someone who does not teach it. Some requirements are genuinely thin - a particular Cambridge syllabus version mid-revision, or practical-paper technique in the fortnight before the papers. When that happens you get three straight answers: how long a match realistically takes, whether the quantitative work would address part of the problem meanwhile, and whether a local centre or the school's own department is the better route for now.

Then send marked papers from each science and tell us which school and which journey. With those three things the plan is usually obvious, and it is almost always one science rather than three.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-manara.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors an Al Manara science enquiry is matched against: teachers who ask which science route and which code before anything else, because the answer decides whether one person can cover the whole thing. intro.heading: "Science" is not one purchase
paragraphs: The word on the enquiry is almost always "science", and it hides the most consequential fact about the cost. A Year 10 student in a Dubai school may be taking three separate sciences, each a full qualification with its own papers - Cambridge 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Or they may be taking Cambridge Combined Sciences 0653, three subjects compressed into one qualification. Or Coordinated Sciences 0654, or Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0, which is two qualifications across three subject areas. Those are not variations. They are different products with different budgets.

On the separate route you have three syllabuses, three sets of papers and three sets of topic gaps. One tutor can sometimes cover all three competently, and more often covers one well and two adequately - which is fine if your child's problem is in the one, and expensive if it is not. On the Combined or Coordinated route you have a single qualification with shallower content and identical exam-technique demands, where one tutor genuinely can hold the whole thing, and where students frequently arrive with weaker practical reasoning because fewer laboratory sessions were run.

So the first question is not what an hour costs; it is which route and which code. Ask the school in writing, because it also tells you something a tutor needs: whether the route is tiered. Cambridge Combined and Coordinated Sciences are tiered Core and Extended, and a Core entry caps all three science strands at once - a single entry decision affecting three subjects, which is the largest piece of arithmetic on this page and costs nothing to check.

With that established, here is the market, every figure attributed to whoever published it. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Named specialists are quoted AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table at 200-450+, and BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 independently. Monthly packages run about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Multiply those by three subjects and the problem becomes obvious. A family buying weekly support in biology, chemistry and physics at mid-market rates is looking at the specialist monthly band for the sciences alone, before anything else in the week is paid for. That is almost never necessary and almost always what happens by default, because each subject gets bought separately as each report arrives.

Al Manara's geography shapes the in-home end of the range. The neighbourhood sits inland on Al Wasl Road and Umm Suqeim Street between two school clusters, so a tutor driving to a villa here comes from Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or further through afternoon traffic. IB Gram does not sell that: home visits are a service we run only in India, and for an Al Manara family lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

programmes.name: Three separate IGCSE sciences
programmes.description: Cambridge 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 - three full qualifications with three sets of papers. programmes.name: Cambridge Combined Sciences

programmes.countryNote: Common in Dubai for students who do not intend to carry three sciences forward, and genuinely sensible for them. One tutor can hold the whole qualification, which makes it the cheapest science route to support properly - provided the tier has been checked first.

programmes.name: Cambridge Coordinated Sciences
programmes.description: A double award covering the three sciences with more depth than Combined, tiered Core and Extended, and worth two qualifications. It sits between Combined and the separate sciences in both content and workload, and it keeps more post-16 doors open than Combined does.

programmes.name: Pearson Science Double Award

Paper structures and practical assessment arrangements differ from the Cambridge equivalents, which is why a tutor's board familiarity matters as much here as anywhere else in the IGCSE system.
programmes.countryNote: Used by the Pearson-entering schools in Al Manara's radius. Past-paper practice must be on the correct board: a student revising with Cambridge papers for a Pearson route is practising unfamiliar question styles and timing, which wastes the single best preparation tool available.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-manara.subjectsIntro: Below, the science components Al Manara families ask about, with what each costs in attention. The honest point is that these are not equally expensive to fix.

subjects.name: Biology content volume
subjects.description: The hardest science to move with one weekly hour, because the problem is usually volume rather than difficulty. Terminology is marked tightly - "the cell takes it in" earns nothing where the scheme wants active transport against a concentration gradient. Better suited to a concentrated holiday block than to a term of weekly sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The highest-yield single topic in IGCSE science, because it decides the chemistry grade and because the arithmetic discipline it builds pays back in physics calculations too. Marks go on significant figures, limiting reagents and percentage yield confused with atom economy.

subjects.name: Chemistry explanation quality
subjects.description: Answers that describe an observation where the mark scheme wants a reason. State symbols omitted. Electrolysis questions answered without reference to the species actually present. All habits rather than knowledge gaps, which makes them cheap to fix and visible on a paper total.

subjects.name: Physics electricity
subjects.description: Where most physics marks disappear across every board. The failure is usually arithmetic rather than conceptual - a correct formula, a correct substitution, then a unit left unconverted or a rearrangement slip. Circuit reasoning questions reward a systematic approach that takes two sessions to install.

subjects.name: Physics waves and optics
subjects.description: Ray diagrams marked on construction accuracy rather than on the final answer, and wave calculations where the frequency and period relationship gets inverted under time pressure. Diagram technique is fast to teach and routinely untaught.

subjects.name: Graph and data skills
subjects.description: Axes chosen sensibly, scales that use the grid, points plotted accurately, a line of best fit justified, a gradient taken from large intervals. These marks appear on every science paper and in both practical assessment formats, which makes this the single most transferable thing to buy.

subjects.name: Method evaluation
subjects.description: Reading a described method and identifying its actual flaw, naming the controlled variables, explaining why a result is anomalous. Entirely paper-based skill, assessed heavily on written practical papers, and almost never taught explicitly in a crowded Year 10 timetable.

subjects.name: Required practicals and apparatus reasoning
subjects.description: Where a route uses a practical examination, the apparatus work belongs in the school laboratory. What can be prepared remotely is the sequence, the readings to take, the precision expected and the common procedural errors - which is most of where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline
subjects.description: State is not explain, describe is not compare, suggest asks for a plausible scientific reason. A fluent answer to the wrong command term is capped before its science is read, and one long answer rewritten properly teaches more than ten attempted badly.

subjects.name: Paper timing and allocation
subjects.description: Minutes allocated by marks, nothing left blank, and the longer questions attempted rather than abandoned. For a student whose content is largely there, this is the highest-return few hours in the whole subject and it costs the lowest rate tier.

subjects.name: Formula recall and units
subjects.description: Which formulae are given and which must be known differs by board and route, and students routinely assume wrongly. Unit conversion errors are the quiet mark-killer in physics calculations, and a session enforcing them line by line changes a paper total.

subjects.name: Science vocabulary for second-language students
subjects.description: Common in Dubai classrooms and frequently misread as a science gap. A student who understands the process and cannot produce the precise term loses the same marks as one who does not understand it, and the fix is targeted vocabulary work rather than content re-teaching.

sections.heading: One tutor or three? The arithmetic
paragraphs: This is the question that determines the bill, and it has a genuine answer rather than a sales answer. On the Combined, Coordinated or Double Award routes, one tutor can cover the whole qualification. The content is shallower in each strand, the papers are shared or closely related, and the most valuable work - graph skills, method evaluation, command terms, unit discipline - is common across all three. Buying three tutors for a single qualification is paying three times for one job.

On the separate-sciences route the honest answer is more nuanced. A science teacher's subject specialism is real: a chemist is a chemist, and the mechanism-level reasoning in chemistry or the mathematical confidence in physics is not interchangeable. But at IGCSE level the depth required is well inside what a trained science teacher covers, and most can teach two of the three to a high standard and the third competently. The practical question is which of your child's three sciences has the problem.

That question is answered by marked papers, not by reports. Across three sciences a student's lost marks are frequently the same marks in all three - graph construction, a described method whose flaw they cannot spot, command terms misread, units unconverted. If that is the pattern, one tutor addressing shared technique improves three sets of marks and costs a third of three weekly commitments. If instead the losses are genuinely subject-specific - stoichiometry in chemistry, electricity in physics, terminology volume in biology - then they should be bought as separate blocks in order of return, not as three parallel subscriptions.

The default pattern, and the expensive one, is subject-by-subject purchasing as each report arrives: physics help in October, chemistry help in January, biology help in March, all running concurrently by spring. sections.heading: The tier that caps three subjects at once
paragraphs: Cambridge Combined Sciences 0653 and Coordinated Sciences 0654 are tiered Core and Extended, and here the tier does something unusually consequential: a Core entry caps the grade for all three science strands simultaneously. One entry decision, three subjects' worth of ceiling. Very few pages in this market mention tiering at all, and none that were researched mention this particular effect.

The implication for a budget is direct. A family spending months of fees to lift a Core science candidate into the top band is spending on an outcome the entry has excluded across all three strands. The reverse error exists too: a student entered for Extended who is not yet fluent faces questions pitched above their current level in three subject areas at once, and loses marks across a whole paper in a way that content teaching does not recover.

On the separate-sciences route, Cambridge tiers each science individually, which means a student can be Core in one and Extended in another - a flexibility worth knowing about, because it allows a sensible asymmetric entry for a student strong in physics and struggling in biology. Pearson's international sciences are single tier, so the question does not arise in the same form, and the full grade range is available to every candidate.

The action is the same in all cases and it is free: ask the school, in writing, which route, which codes and which tier. Then ask what the mocks predict on each tier and what would have to change by the entry deadline. A specialist reading a marked mock can separate marks lost to fixable technique from marks lost to the paper being pitched above the student's fluency, which is the whole of the decision and takes one session.

sections.heading: What preparation is worth paying for, by practical format
paragraphs: Science routes handle practical assessment differently, and this is where money gets spent on the wrong thing more often than anywhere else in the subject. Some routes use a practical examination. Some use a written alternative-to-practical paper assessing the same skills entirely on paper - identifying variables, evaluating a described method, constructing a results table with correct headings and units, plotting and interpreting a graph, explaining an anomaly. The content being tested overlaps. The preparation that helps does not.

If your child sits a written alternative paper, the useful work is paper-based and transfers perfectly to a shared screen: reading a method and finding its actual flaw, building a table before data arrives, plotting and taking a gradient from large intervals, explaining why a point is anomalous rather than reciting "human error". That is a fast-moving, teachable skill set, and a term of apparatus rehearsal in a kitchen does nothing for it. Paying for the latter is a waste that happens routinely.

If your child sits a practical examination, the apparatus work belongs in the school laboratory and no tutor can substitute for it over video - anybody claiming otherwise is overselling. What can genuinely be prepared remotely is the thinking: the sequence of the procedure, which readings to take and to what precision, the common procedural errors, and how to record and process the results. That is most of where the marks sit even in a practical examination.

The first step, then, is to find out which format applies, from the school rather than from a tutor's assumption. It is one question and it redirects the entire preparation plan. For families considering private-candidate entry after a mid-year move, practical arrangements are set by the board and the examination centre and they constrain which science components a private candidate can sit at all - ask the centre directly and in writing before building a plan around it.

sections.heading: The Dubai rate card, read per qualification
paragraphs: Here is the market with the name attached to every figure, then the multiplication nobody does. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named specialists run AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table showing 200-450+ and BartyED publishing AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted AED 180-350 by Bestimate, up to AED 500 independently.

Now the multiplication. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240-600 at the budget tier, AED 600-1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Those figures are per subject. A family running three weekly science hours at the mid-range tier is therefore in the AED 1,800-3,600 monthly region for sciences alone, before mathematics, English or anything else. Almost nobody intends that; plenty of households arrive there one report at a time.

The alternatives are cheaper and usually better. One tutor across a Combined or Coordinated qualification is a single rate. One shared-skills block addressing graph work, method evaluation and command terms improves three sets of marks for the price of one subject. Defined blocks on the diagnosed science, taken in sequence rather than in parallel, cost a fraction of three subscriptions and end with a decision rather than drifting.

The in-home premium applies on top of all of it and compounds with the number of subjects. Published packages run about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits - half the contact days for roughly twice the outlay, per subject. For science, where the marks sit in graphs, tables and annotated method evaluation on a shared screen, the premium buys a drive from Al Barsha rather than better teaching. Where supervision is the real need it is worth paying for; IB Gram does not sell it, because home visits are a service we run only in India.

sections.heading: Five places science money disappears in Dubai
paragraphs: First, three parallel weekly subscriptions when the losses are shared. This is the big one and it bears restating: if a student is losing graph marks, method-evaluation marks and command-term marks in all three sciences, those are one problem presenting three times, and one tutor fixes it once at one rate.

Second, paying for apparatus rehearsal when the route uses a written alternative paper. It is a specific, common and entirely avoidable waste, and the check is one question to the school about which practical format applies. Families buy it in good faith, usually after a teacher mentions that practical skills are assessed, without establishing that on their child's route those skills are assessed on paper rather than at a bench. Several weeks of equipment-based sessions can be bought before anybody notices that the examination does not involve equipment at all.

Third, buying biology weekly when the problem is volume. Biology's difficulty is the sheer quantity of precise terminology, and a single weekly hour cannot deliver content at the rate needed - it can only teach technique and vocabulary strategy. For volume problems a concentrated holiday block does more per dirham, and a tutor who says so is reducing the bill.

Fourth, group classes for a tiered, multi-route subject. A centre class containing Core and Extended candidates on Combined and separate routes across two boards can only deliver generic science. It is cheaper per hour and often worth less per hour, though it can work for common content revision before mocks. Fifth, the in-home premium multiplied by three subjects: AED 180-500 against AED 150-300, per science, where the difference is a car in Al Wasl Road traffic rather than better teaching.

sections.heading: Which science to fund, given where your child is going
paragraphs: When the budget only stretches to one science, the destination should decide which. A student heading for A Level or IB Higher Level sciences needs the subject they intend to continue secured, because the step up assumes fluency rather than familiarity - and in Dubai, post-16 specialist tuition is quoted at AED 200-450 and above, so fluency built at IGCSE rates is fluency not bought twice.

Chemistry is usually the highest-leverage choice on that basis. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary science and many biological and engineering programmes specify chemistry, frequently at an advanced level, and chemistry's calculation discipline pays back in physics as well. A student who can handle moles reliably is a student whose physics arithmetic also improves, which makes it the one subject whose hours visibly benefit another.

Physics is the right choice where the loss is mathematical rather than conceptual, because the fix transfers directly to mathematics and to chemistry calculations. Biology is the right choice where it is the intended post-16 subject, and the honest caveat is that it needs more hours or a concentrated block rather than a weekly trickle, because volume does not respond to an hour a week.

Two cautions for UAE destinations. Ministry of Education equivalency is a regulatory process run by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, not something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for it. The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject figure, which does not match the sourced requirement - and option choices get made on numbers like that.

sections.heading: Counting backwards to the series
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate in Dubai, which matters because a wrong exam window handed to a parent destroys a real revision plan.

One Cambridge detail affects science planning directly, since science candidates often sit the largest number of papers. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer which zone your centre is in, in writing.

For Pearson, International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official timetable rather than from restated dates, including these.

Counted backwards for sciences specifically, the phases are: route, codes and tier confirmed first; practical format established; steady work or a diagnosed block through Years 10 and 11; the mock round read from the marked scripts rather than the percentages; then timed papers on the correct board in the final weeks. The table adds the ownership column, because knowing who sets a deadline is most of meeting it.

sections.heading: Checking the tutor costs nothing
paragraphs: Before you fund a first hour of biology, chemistry or physics, two checks cost you nothing but a message. Start with the licence, because a science tutor who arrives at an Al Manara villa with a box of practice papers is carrying out regulated work. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the permit in question is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. No fine schedule is published anywhere, which matters to you in one practical way: if a tutor or an agency quotes a dirham figure for the penalty, they have invented it, and the invention tells you how the rest of their claims were assembled.

Eligibility is the part worth knowing before you judge an answer, because the science tutors offered around Al Manara come from every category on MoHRE's list: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. A current school science teacher qualifies. So does the engineering undergraduate who tutors physics in the evenings. The route is identical for all of them, and it is MoHRE's own service page titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Two working days and no fee is the entire barrier, so a tutor teaching three sciences a week without a permit has chosen not to have one.

The second check is the arrangement itself. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat it as press-reported and verify against the current policy document, but decline the arrangement where your child's own science teacher is paid privately.

And the claims to refuse. No individual tutor in Dubai is KHDA-approved, because that status does not exist for individuals - KHDA regulates schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises in the emirate. Nobody holds Cambridge or Pearson accreditation as a private tutor. No provider should supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those should be referenced and linked. And where a science route includes an assessed component, a tutor may teach, explain the criteria, mark practice work and comment on a draft the student wrote - never write, complete or edit a submission.

sections.heading: A first block that earns its fee
paragraphs: Eight sessions with a shape, for an Al Manara student losing science marks. Session one is diagnosis across all three sciences at once, which is the part most families skip: the marked papers from biology, chemistry and physics are read together, and the lost marks are sorted into shared technique, subject-specific content, and tier or fluency problems. That comparison is what reveals whether you need one tutor or three, and it cannot be done from reports.

Sessions two to four take the shared technique, because it is the highest return available: graph construction with sensible axes and a justified line of best fit, reading a described method and naming its flaw, building a results table before data arrives, command terms against real mark schemes, and unit discipline enforced line by line. Those marks appear in every science paper, so three sets of marks move at once.

Sessions five to seven take whichever subject-specific gap the diagnosis named - stoichiometry in chemistry, electricity in physics, terminology precision in biology - one at a time, with practice set between sessions and marked at the next. Session eight is a full paper on the correct board under time, dissected into a written error list the student keeps and rereads before the real thing.

Then a decision gets made rather than a subscription continuing. Some students need a second block on another science. Some need the holiday block for biology volume. Some turn out to be in a tier conversation with the school rather than a tutoring one, and should be told so plainly. The free trial lesson means the diagnostic session costs nothing, and no block is agreed until after it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover biology, chemistry and physics for an Al Manara student?
faqs.answer: On a Combined, Coordinated or Double Award route, yes - it is one qualification with shared technique demands, and buying three tutors for it is paying three times for one job. On the separate-sciences route it depends on where the marks are going. If the losses are the same in all three - graph construction, method evaluation, command terms, units - one tutor fixes one problem and three sets of marks move. If they are genuinely subject-specific, buy defined blocks in sequence rather than three parallel weekly hours, which costs a fraction and usually achieves more.

faqs.question: How do I find out which science route my child is actually on?
faqs.answer: Ask the school in writing, and ask for the codes. Cambridge Combined Sciences is 0653 and Coordinated Sciences is 0654; separate sciences are 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics. Pearson runs 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 separately and 4SD0 as the Science Double Award. Do not infer the route from the textbook on the shelf, because schools change provision and a student who joined mid-course may have covered material from two. While you are asking, request the tier and the practical assessment format too.

faqs.question: Why does a Core science entry matter more than a Core maths entry?
faqs.answer: Because it caps three subjects at once. Cambridge Combined Sciences 0653 and Coordinated Sciences 0654 are tiered Core and Extended, and a Core entry ceilings the grade across all three science strands simultaneously - one entry decision with three subjects' worth of consequence. No researched competitor page in this market mentions this. On the separate-sciences route Cambridge tiers each science individually, which usefully allows an asymmetric entry: Extended in physics, Core in biology, for a student whose strengths differ that way.

faqs.question: What does three weekly science hours actually cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: More than most families intend. Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240-600 at the budget tier, AED 600-1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work - and those figures are per subject. Three mid-range weekly science hours therefore lands around AED 1,800-3,600 a month for sciences alone, before mathematics or English. Households rarely decide on that; they arrive there one report at a time, buying physics in October, chemistry in January and biology in March.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for practical rehearsal if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the assessment format, and this is the most routine waste in science tutoring. If your child's route uses a written alternative-to-practical paper, the marks come from evaluating a described method, naming controlled variables, building tables, plotting graphs and explaining anomalies - all paper-based and all better on a shared screen than across a table. If the route uses a practical examination, apparatus technique belongs in the school laboratory and no tutor can substitute for it, though the sequence, precision and common procedural errors prepare well remotely.

faqs.question: Which science should we fund if the budget only covers one?
faqs.answer: Usually the one your child intends to continue post-16, because that subject gets bought twice otherwise - post-16 specialist tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 200-450 and above. Beyond that, chemistry is often the highest-leverage choice: it is specified by medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary science and many biological and engineering programmes, and its calculation discipline visibly improves physics arithmetic too. Physics is the right pick where the loss is mathematical rather than conceptual. Biology needs a concentrated block rather than a weekly hour, because the problem is volume.

faqs.question: Why is biology the hardest science to fix with one hour a week?
faqs.answer: Because the difficulty is volume rather than conceptual depth, and an hour a week cannot deliver content at the rate required. The syllabus marks terminology tightly - "the cell takes it in" earns nothing where the scheme wants active transport against a concentration gradient - so the gap is a large quantity of precise vocabulary and mechanism detail. What a weekly hour can do is teach vocabulary strategy, data-question technique and command-term discipline. For the volume itself, a concentrated block in a Dubai school break does far more per dirham.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to a villa in Al Manara?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. For an Al Manara family lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the marked paper, the graph being plotted and the method being evaluated are visible to both sides, and the annotated work stays with the student. For science that is well suited rather than compromised, and across three subjects it also avoids paying the in-home premium three times over.

faqs.question: Why is in-home science tuition quoted higher here than online?
faqs.answer: Because an hour of teaching takes about two and a half hours to deliver. Al Manara sits inland on Al Wasl Road between two school clusters, so a tutor drives in from Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or further through afternoon traffic, parks on a villa street, and reverses the journey. Bestimate's 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500, against AED 150-300 online. The premium is the price of a car. It buys supervision, which genuinely helps some students, and not better science teaching.

faqs.question: Are science group classes at a Dubai centre good value?
faqs.answer: For common content revision before mocks, sometimes. For diagnosed work, rarely, because a centre class can contain Core and Extended candidates on Combined and separate routes across two different boards, which means only generic science can be delivered. Nobody in that room can address one student's route, code, tier or practical format. It is cheaper per hour and often worth less per hour. A centre with premises in Dubai also operates under a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different licence from an individual tutor's MoHRE permit.

faqs.question: What should we send so a first science session is not wasted?
faqs.answer: The route and codes from the school, the tier, the practical assessment format, and the most recent marked papers from all three sciences rather than just the weakest one. That last point matters more than it sounds: comparing lost marks across three subjects is what reveals whether this is one shared technique problem appearing three times or three separate gaps - and that distinction is the biggest number in the whole budget. It takes ten minutes to gather and saves a session of discovery.

faqs.question: Does a Combined Sciences student need less exam technique than a separate-sciences student?
faqs.answer: No, and this catches families out. Combined and Coordinated Sciences cover shallower content but the exam technique demands are identical: the same graph construction, the same method evaluation, the same command terms, the same unit discipline. Students on these routes often arrive with weaker practical reasoning as well, because fewer laboratory sessions were run across the compressed course. So the technique work that transfers across all three strands is arguably better value here than on the separate route, since one qualification benefits entirely.

faqs.question: Which exam series will a Dubai science candidate sit?
faqs.answer: The June series or the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Science candidates often sit the most papers of anyone, so confirm which of Cambridge's six administrative zones your centre is in, because Cambridge warns that using the wrong zone timetable is the candidate's risk.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry actually count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five, for the British track. The published guidance requires passing five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject figure, which does not match the sourced requirement - and option choices get made on numbers like that. Verify on moe.gov.ae; no tutoring provider performs equivalency.

faqs.question: What does a well-spent first block of eight science sessions contain?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis across all three sciences first, from marked papers rather than reports, sorting the losses into shared technique, subject-specific content, and tier or fluency problems. Then three sessions on shared technique - graph construction, method evaluation, command terms, unit discipline - because those marks appear in every science paper and three sets move at once. Then two or three on the diagnosed subject gap, one at a time with practice set and marked. Then a full paper on the correct board under time, dissected into a written error list, and a decision rather than a rollover.

intro.heading: Three qualifications, one week, one calendar
paragraphs: A student taking triple science at IGCSE is not taking one subject with three parts. They are entered for three separate qualifications, each with its own code, its own papers, its own practical assessment arrangement and its own place in the examination timetable. Cambridge Biology is 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625; the Pearson equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Three entries, three sets of past papers, three mark schemes.

What families underestimate is the arithmetic that follows. If a student has two evenings a week available for science revision across the whole of Year 11, that is roughly one evening per two sciences, and the third gets whatever is left. In practice what happens is that the science the student dislikes most absorbs the attention, the one they find easiest is neglected on the assumption it will hold, and the third drifts. By the mock it is usually the neglected one that has slipped, and nobody planned for that because nobody planned at all.

The calendar compounds it. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Three sciences sit inside the same window, often within days of each other, so a plan that works for one subject in isolation can collapse when the three are scheduled against each other.

A warning that belongs early. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only - UAE candidates sit June and November. Cambridge's Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests do run in March, May and October, which is a separate thing and part of why so much tutoring content written for Gulf parents quotes the wrong window. A family planning a science run-in toward February has three subjects aimed at the wrong month.

Reading your own position in this belt takes one document. Several schools around Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai split science entries between Cambridge and Pearson by subject or by teaching group, so one child can be Cambridge in Biology and Pearson in Physics - two paper sets, two question styles and two administrative timelines for one student. Others enter candidates for Co-ordinated Sciences as a double award rather than three separate qualifications, which changes the content set entirely. The entry statement names all of it in a few lines, and almost no family has read it.

So this page plans the week and the terms rather than teaching the content. How to split a week across three sciences deliberately. How the practical-assessment route your centre entered changes what has to be prepared and when. A term-by-term shape for a double or triple science student. What to prioritise when the weeks run short, with the reasoning stated rather than implied. And what a resit across three subjects actually involves, in weeks as well as in dirhams.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-mankhool.programmesIntro: Which science qualifications your child is entered for determines how many weeks of work exist and how they have to be divided. Four arrangements are common across the schools these districts feed.

programmes.name: Separate sciences: Biology, Chemistry and Physics
programmes.description: Three qualifications, three codes, three paper sets. The full content depth in each, which is what post-sixteen science courses assume. It is also three times the revision load and three practical assessment arrangements, and the planning problem is real rather than theoretical.
programmes.countryNote: The majority arrangement for students in this belt heading toward A Level sciences, the IB Diploma sciences, or medical and engineering routes. The practical consequence for a family in Al Mankhool is that a single weekly science hour cannot serve three subjects, and pretending otherwise produces a term where each gets twenty minutes.

programmes.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences, double award
programmes.description: All three sciences in a double award, covering less depth in each than the separate qualifications. It solves the timetable problem and limits what can be assumed afterwards, which matters where a student intends a post-sixteen science course at Higher Level or A Level.
programmes.countryNote: Worth confirming before paying for three separate science tutors, because the content set is different and the past papers are a separate series. Also worth checking against what the receiving school requires: post-sixteen science courses state entry requirements in named qualifications, not in general science terms.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences
programmes.description: Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1, each with its own paper structure and question style distinct from Cambridge. Exams are available in May/June and November each year, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series so dates can be revised.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools around Al Mankhool split entries between boards by subject, so a student can be Cambridge in one science and Pearson in another. That means two administrative timelines and two paper sets in the same household, and it is the single most common planning surprise in this belt.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Science taught as an integrated subject group and assessed against four criteria on a 1-8 scale rather than by terminal papers in most schools. There is no board calendar and no entry deadline, which makes the planning problem completely different.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant because households in these districts often have children on both routes. An MYP student's support can be scheduled purely around school deadlines, whereas an IGCSE triple-science sibling is counting weeks to a fixed series in three subjects at once.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-mankhool.subjectsIntro: The three sciences are not equally difficult to revise and they do not fail in the same way, which is the basis for splitting a week sensibly rather than evenly.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The highest content volume and the subject most often revised badly, because reading notes feels productive. Marks go on data interpretation, on definition precision, and on describing a process in the correct order. More content time, more written practice.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: A split subject: mechanical calculation work on moles and formulae, plus explanation questions on bonding and reactivity. The two halves need different kinds of practice, and students usually find one comfortable and neglect the other.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: The least content-heavy and the most technique-dependent of the three. Electricity and electromagnetism produce the largest losses, usually on explain questions answered as descriptions. Less content time, more structured-question practice.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: A different content set from the separate sciences with its own papers, so practice must come from the correct series. Depth is limited, which is the thing to check against the receiving school's post-sixteen entry requirements.

subjects.name: Combined Science (Cambridge 0653)
subjects.description: A further reduced science provision where the timetable will not fit more. Students on this route who later want a post-sixteen science course need the gap closed deliberately and early, usually across a summer rather than a term.

subjects.name: The alternative-to-practical paper
subjects.levels: Where the centre has entered it
subjects.description: A written paper on practical reasoning, with recurring question types: variables, controls, sources of error, reading scales, suggesting improvements. Schools often cover it late because laboratory time goes to the practical work, so it is reliably under-prepared.

subjects.name: The practical examination route
subjects.levels: Where the centre has entered it
subjects.description: A laboratory assessment rather than a written one, which changes what needs preparing and where. The apparatus and supervision are the school's; what a tutor adds is the written reasoning and the recording discipline around it.

subjects.name: Mathematical handling inside science
subjects.description: Rearrangement, unit conversion, significant figures, reading gradients, and percentage and ratio work. Frequently the real gap behind a science problem, and quicker to fix as a short block than through more science teaching.

subjects.name: The six-mark extended response
subjects.description: The question type where grades are decided across all three subjects. Marked on linked causal points rather than on volume of correct facts. The skill transfers between the sciences, which makes it the most efficient thing to teach a triple-science student.

subjects.name: Environmental Management (Cambridge 0680)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the sciences at some schools in this belt, with a strong data and case-study component. It rewards structured evaluation rather than recall, and a short block on answer structure usually moves it more than content work does.
