sections.heading: Splitting one week across three sciences
paragraphs: Start from the honest total. Ask how many hours a week your child genuinely has for science outside school once homework, the mandatory subjects, other GCSEs, travel and sleep are accounted for. In this belt the realistic answer in Year 11 is often two to four hours, and three sciences have to fit in it. That number, not an aspiration, is what a plan should be built on.

Then split it deliberately rather than evenly, because the three subjects do not need equal time. Biology carries the highest content volume and benefits most from sustained reading combined with written question practice. Chemistry divides into mechanical calculation work and explanation questions, and most students are comfortable with one half and neglect the other. Physics is the least content-heavy and the most technique-dependent, so it needs proportionally less content time and more structured-question practice.

Write the split down. An unstated allocation becomes an emotional one: the student spends the time on whichever subject frightened them most recently, the subject they find easiest is neglected on the assumption that it will hold, and by the mock it is the neglected one that slipped. A written rotation, reviewed after each mock, prevents the most common failure in a triple-science year without requiring any additional hours.

One practical note on how to hold the split. Where the week allows only one session, a stated rotation is better than three fragments: a full hour on one science, with work set for the other two, beats twenty minutes each. Twenty minutes cannot contain a timed question and a proper marking conversation, which are the two things that actually move a science grade.

sections.heading: The practical route the centre entered changes the plan
paragraphs: Practical skills are assessed in IGCSE science either through a practical examination or through the alternative-to-practical written paper, and which one applies depends on the centre's entry rather than on the subject. It is written on the entry statement and it materially changes what needs preparing, where and when. A family that does not know which route applies is preparing for one of two different things by guesswork.

Where the alternative-to-practical paper applies, the preparation is written and it is entirely teachable outside a laboratory. The paper has recurring question types: identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables precisely; explain why holding a particular variable constant protects the conclusion; name a specific source of error and its effect on the result; propose a concrete change to method or apparatus; read a scale with appropriate precision; suggest an improvement that addresses a named limitation. Each has a right shape of answer, and schools cover it late because laboratory time goes to the practical work itself.

Where the practical examination route applies, the apparatus, the supervision and the handling experience are the school's and cannot be bought elsewhere. What a tutor adds is the written and recording discipline around it: tabulating results properly, deciding on repeats, recording to an appropriate precision, and knowing what the examiner wants to see written down. That is a real contribution and it is not a substitute for laboratory time.
The table sets out the two routes against what each demands. Confirm your child's from the entry statement, which names it alongside the subject code.

sections.heading: A term-by-term shape for a multi-science year
paragraphs: Three sciences across two years will not organise themselves, and the default - revise each in syllabus order when it feels urgent - produces three incomplete passes and no reliable marks. A term-by-term shape avoids that, and it needs only to be written down once at the start of Year 10 and reviewed after each mock.

The principle is that technique comes early and content comes continuously. The shared skills - the six-mark response, command verbs, units and significant figures, practical-reasoning question types - should be taught once, early, because they pay in all three subjects simultaneously for the rest of the course. Content work then runs alongside the school's teaching, with the rotation adjusted by what the marked scripts show rather than by anxiety.

Year 11 changes the balance rather than the structure. Papers replace content as the main activity, and the shared-technique slot becomes an audit slot: three marked scripts to read rather than one, with the four causes of lost marks counted separately for each subject. That comparison across three sciences is unusually informative, because a student whose method marks are fine in Chemistry and poor in Physics has a subject-specific habit rather than a general one.

There is one more reason to write the shape down at the start of Year 10 rather than improvising. In this belt a large share of students change campus at sixteen, so the science grades they leave Year 11 with are also an admissions document for a school whose requirements the family has not yet read. Knowing in Year 10 which sciences the intended post-sixteen route will name turns an abstract plan into a set of priorities, and it costs one email to the receiving school to find out.

sections.heading: Triage: which science to prioritise when the weeks run short
paragraphs: Eight weeks before a series, a triple-science student with three unfinished subjects has a genuine allocation problem and it needs a decision rather than a hope. The instinct is to divide the remaining weeks equally, which produces three partial improvements and often no grade change in any subject. A deliberate ranking produces fewer improvements that are large enough to count.

Three criteria decide the ranking. First, where the recoverable marks are: a subject where the student nearly knows the material and is losing marks on structure or method is far more recoverable than one where whole topics are missing. Second, what the next stage requires: a student heading for a post-sixteen Chemistry course has more at stake in Chemistry than in Biology, and the receiving school states its requirements in named subjects. Third, which subject is closest to a tier or grade boundary, where a small movement changes the outcome.

Physics is frequently the highest-yield late subject in this belt, for a specific reason: it has the lowest content volume and the highest share of losses coming from technique, particularly explain questions answered as descriptions. A student who knows physics and writes descriptions can gain substantially in a few weeks. Biology is usually the lowest-yield late subject, because its losses are more often genuine content volume, which cannot be installed quickly.

What should be protected regardless of ranking is the shared slot. The six-mark response, the command verbs and the units discipline pay in all three subjects simultaneously, which makes them the most efficient use of a short run-in. sections.heading: Where the marks go, differently in each science
paragraphs: The three sciences share a mark-scheme philosophy and fail in distinguishable ways, and knowing the difference lets a session be aimed rather than general. In Biology the content volume is high and so is the temptation to revise by reading. The marks go on describing a process in the correct sequence, on the precision of definitions, and on interpreting data the student has not seen before. A student who has read the textbook twice and never written a timed answer will underperform relative to their knowledge.

In Chemistry the losses split cleanly. On the calculation side they are procedural: dropped units, premature rounding, a concentration confused with an amount, a formula misremembered under pressure. On the explanation side they are structural: a correct set of facts about a reaction presented in no particular order, where the scheme wanted cause connected to effect. Most students are comfortable with one side and avoid the other, and a tutor's first job is to find out which.

In Physics the dominant loss is the command verb. Explain, describe, state and calculate demand different responses, and a student who writes a description where an explanation was asked for can know the physics perfectly and score two marks from four. Electricity and electromagnetism concentrate these losses, partly because the reasoning chains are longer and partly because students struggle to reason about what happens elsewhere in a circuit when one component changes.

Across all three sits the six-mark extended response, which is where grades are decided and which behaves identically in each subject: marked on linked causal points rather than on volume of correct content. Three well-ordered sentences outscore eight unordered true ones. This is the single most efficient thing to teach a triple-science student, because the skill transfers intact between all three qualifications.

sections.heading: Separate or co-ordinated: a decision with a deadline
paragraphs: Some of the pressure in a triple-science year is structural. Three separate sciences is a heavy load, and where it does not fit, Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award or Combined Science 0653 as a single award covers all three with less depth. Those are legitimate routes and they solve a real timetable problem. They also limit what a post-sixteen science course can assume, and that is the trade to understand before choosing.

The constraint is that the decision is taken at entry stage and is set by the school. By the time a family concludes in the spring of Year 11 that three separate sciences was too much, the entry has been made and the amendment window has closed. The conversation to have, in Year 10 or early Year 11, is with the school about load and with the receiving institution about what it will require.

That second conversation is the one families skip. Post-sixteen science courses state entry requirements in named qualifications and specific grades, and a school offering A Level Chemistry or Diploma Higher Level Chemistry may ask for something that a double award does not provide. Asking directly, before the entry is made, costs nothing and prevents the situation where a student holds a perfectly respectable science qualification that does not open the door they wanted.

Where three separate sciences is the right load but is going badly, the alternative to changing the entry is changing the plan: a written weekly split, a protected shared-technique slot, and triage by recoverable marks rather than equal division. That is usually more effective than a structural change made in a panic, and it keeps the depth that the next stage requires.

sections.heading: Resitting across three subjects
paragraphs: A science that goes wrong in the June series can usually be retaken in November, and for a triple-science student the decision has an extra dimension: which subject, and whether more than one. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 Pearson final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

Three practical constraints shape the decision. The entry fee, which where a student sits as a private candidate is set by the approved examination centre rather than by the board, so it has to be confirmed in writing with the centre per subject rather than estimated. The autumn workload, because a resit block runs alongside the start of a post-sixteen course, which is the busiest term in a student's life so far. And the result date: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to students on 20 August 2026 - so an autumn resit does not meet a December deadline however well it goes.

The advantage of a resit block is that it is more targeted than the original preparation. The student has sat the real paper in that subject, knows what it felt like, and can usually name which questions they recognised and could not finish. That turns the block into specific repair rather than general revision, and it is often shorter than families expect. Resitting two sciences at once, however, reinstates the allocation problem in a term with less room than Year 11 had.

Where a resit is under consideration, settle the entry and the centre fee first, then scope the block, then check the result date against whatever deadline prompted the question. Doing it in that order prevents the common outcome of a well-prepared resit whose result arrives after the decision it was meant to influence.

sections.heading: Three subjects, one budget
paragraphs: A triple-science student is the case where buying a weekly hour per subject is most tempting and least often affordable, so the allocation question is financial as well as temporal. Three weekly specialist hours is a substantial monthly commitment, and in most cases a shared-technique block plus one targeted single-science repair achieves more for less, because the shared skills improve all three qualifications at once.

Multiply each published band by three and the budget question largely answers itself. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts qualified online tuition at AED 150 to 300 an hour, which is AED 450 to 900 for one week of three single hours. Its specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level band of AED 200 to 450 or more becomes AED 600 to 1,350 a week, and its in-home one-to-one figure of AED 180 to 350 including travel becomes AED 540 to 1,050 before anybody has opened a past paper. Named rates sit inside those bands: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150, TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650, while home tutors are quoted up to AED 500 an hour including travel. Only the entry platforms survive the multiplication, Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, and a triple-science candidate who buys three cheap hours has bought the one thing these three qualifications do not reward. Each figure is attributed to the provider that published it and was read in October 2026. None of those is an IB Gram price.

The monthly view decides most families' plans. One Dubai provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, near AED 100 an hour. In-home monthly packages are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, near AED 200 to 225 for the same eight hours. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support - and a triple-science student buying one hour per subject at the specialist rate is at the top of that range or beyond it.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Sessions for Al Mankhool students run one-to-one over live video. For a three-subject plan the format has a specific practical benefit: three different specialists can run in consecutive hours or on different days without anybody travelling, which an in-home arrangement cannot do economically across three subjects.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the periods inside the day
paragraphs: Two things a parent can establish before committing to any of this. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because the permit is free, no part of a quoted rate is a permit fee being recovered. Operating without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so nobody should be quoting an amount.

Second, the school's inspection report, which for a science family is directly useful because it comments on science provision. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes reports on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. If science teaching is named as a strength, the school's own revision support may cover ground you were about to buy, and the private hour belongs on technique. Across the country, ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates there, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

A tutoring business with premises in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, no regulator accreditation and no UAE office, and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; those are published and owned by the boards and your child's school holds the current versions.

Finally, the periods that squeeze a three-science week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year or April 2026 where the year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Those periods sit inside the school day, which is part of why the honest weekly science total in Year 11 is two to four hours rather than the larger figure a timetable implies. Ramadan compresses it further, and the sensible move is to agree in advance that sessions shift to a post-Iftar slot for that period and return afterwards.

faqs.question: How should a triple-science student in Al Mankhool divide their revision week?
faqs.answer: Start from the honest total - in Year 11 in this belt, usually two to four hours a week outside school once homework, the mandatory subjects and travel are accounted for. Then split it deliberately rather than evenly: Biology takes the largest share because its content volume is highest, Chemistry a third split between calculations and explanations, Physics the smallest because its losses are mostly technique. Protect one session in four for the shared skills. Write the rotation down, because an unstated allocation becomes an emotional one.

faqs.question: Which science usually slips in a triple-science year, and why?
faqs.answer: The one the student finds easiest, because it gets neglected on the assumption it will hold while attention goes to whichever subject was most frightening that week. By the mock it is the neglected subject that has moved backwards, and nobody planned for it because nobody planned at all. A written rotation reviewed after each mock prevents this without requiring any additional hours, which makes it the cheapest intervention available in a three-science year.

faqs.question: What is the most efficient thing to teach a student sitting three sciences?
faqs.answer: The skills that pay in all three at once. The six-mark extended response behaves identically in Biology, Chemistry and Physics: it is marked on linked causal points rather than on volume of correct content, so three well-ordered sentences outscore eight unordered true ones. Command verbs, significant figures and unit discipline transfer the same way, as do the alternative-to-practical question types. One block of sessions on those improves three qualifications simultaneously.

faqs.question: How do we find out whether our child sits a practical exam or the written alternative?
faqs.answer: It is on the school's entry statement alongside the subject code, and it changes the preparation materially. Where the alternative-to-practical paper applies, the work is written and fully teachable outside a laboratory, with recurring question types on variables, controls, sources of error, reading scales and suggesting improvements. Where the practical examination route applies, the apparatus and supervision are the school's and a tutor adds recording and tabulating discipline. Ask in the autumn rather than the spring: schools cover the written paper late.

faqs.question: Which science is worth prioritising if only a few weeks remain?
faqs.answer: Usually Physics, because it has the lowest content volume and the highest share of losses coming from technique - particularly explain questions answered as descriptions. Chemistry calculations come next, being mechanical and drillable. Biology content gaps are the poorest late target, because the losses there are more often genuine volume and volume cannot be installed quickly. Rank by recoverable marks and by what the next stage requires, and protect the shared-technique slot whatever the ranking.

faqs.question: Is it worth hiring three separate science tutors?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and mainly for budget reasons rather than principle. Three weekly specialist hours is at or beyond the top of the published monthly bands for exam-year support, and in most cases a shared-technique block plus one targeted single-science repair achieves more for less, because the shared skills improve all three qualifications. Where three specialists genuinely are needed, online delivery lets them run on different days or consecutively without anybody travelling, which is not economic in-home across three subjects.

faqs.question: What do we do with three marked mock scripts?
faqs.answer: Audit each separately into four causes - content not known, method not shown, question misread, time ran out - and then compare across the three. That comparison is unusually informative. A student whose method marks are fine in Chemistry and poor in Physics has a Physics-specific habit rather than a general one, and the repair is different. A student losing marks to the clock in all three has a paper-strategy problem. Then adjust the written rotation from the counts.

faqs.question: Should my child take separate sciences or Co-ordinated Sciences?
faqs.answer: It is a load decision with a downstream consequence, and it is taken at entry stage by the school rather than in the spring of Year 11. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award, or Combined Science 0653 as a single award, solve a genuine timetable problem and limit what a post-sixteen science course can assume. Ask the receiving school what it requires, by named qualification, before the entry is made - a respectable science qualification that does not open the intended door is the outcome to avoid.

faqs.question: Which exam series do science candidates in Dubai sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only. Cambridge's Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests do run in March, May and October, which is a separate thing and part of why the confusion persists.

faqs.question: Can one science be retaken in November without the others?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is usually the sensible version. A single-subject resit block is targeted, because the student has sat the real paper and can name which questions they recognised and could not finish. Resitting two sciences at once reinstates the allocation problem in an autumn term that already contains the start of a post-sixteen course. Settle the entry and the centre's fee per subject in writing first, then scope the block, then check the result date against whatever deadline prompted the question.

faqs.question: When will a November science resit result actually arrive?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. So a summer result is available before a September start and an autumn result is not. If the reason for the resit is a school or university deadline in December, a November sitting does not meet it however well the student performs, and that should be established before the entry is made.

faqs.question: With three sciences in one window, does the timetable zone matter?
faqs.answer: Because the timetable differs between zones, and with three sciences in the same window that matters more than usual. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Take the dates from the school's entry statement and the board's live timetable rather than from a PDF found through a search engine.

faqs.question: My child reads their biology notes constantly and still underperforms. Why?
faqs.answer: Because reading produces recognition and the paper tests retrieval and writing. Biology's marks go on describing a process in the correct sequence, on the precision of definitions, and on interpreting data the student has not seen before - none of which improves by re-reading. The fix is written, timed answers marked against the official scheme, which feels much worse and works. A student who has read the textbook twice and never written a timed answer will underperform relative to what they actually know.

faqs.question: What does science tuition for three subjects cost in this market?
faqs.answer: Budget by the month rather than the hour. Published Dubai rates are AED 33 to 65 at the budget end from Tutopiya and EdFlik, AED 150 upward from Unitors for IGCSE, AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tuition and AED 200 to 450 or more for specialist provision on Bestimate's 2026 table, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. Bestimate's monthly estimate for specialist exam-year support is AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more, and one hour per science at that rate sits at or above the top of it.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory subject block really reduce science study time?
faqs.answer: It reduces the time available more than families account for. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Those periods sit inside the school day alongside three sciences and everything else, which is why the honest weekly total outside school is two to four hours.

faqs.question: How do three subjects keep running through Ramadan and term breaks?
faqs.answer: By counting them out of the plan before it is agreed, and by moving the slot deliberately. Term breaks, public holidays, Ramadan and the school's own mock windows remove sessions, so a notional eight-week plan in the UAE academic year routinely delivers six - and across three subjects that loss is three partial plans rather than one. For Ramadan, agree in advance that sessions shift to a post-Iftar time and return afterwards, which preserves a rotation that would otherwise simply stop for a month.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-mankhool.closingHeading: Count the hours, write the split, protect the shared slot
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-mankhool.closingBody: Three sciences do not fit in a week that was not divided on purpose. Ask the school for the entry statement for all three subjects, so you know the boards, codes, tiers and practical routes. Count the hours your child genuinely has outside school, which in Year 11 is usually fewer than it feels. Then write a rotation down, keep one session in four for the skills that pay in all three subjects, and bring three marked scripts to a free trial lesson so the split can be adjusted from evidence rather than from anxiety. Sessions run one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Find the syllabus code before you find the tutor
paragraphs: Science at IGCSE is not one qualification. A student in the Al Mizhar catchment might be sitting three separate sciences, each with its own syllabus and its own papers. They might be sitting a coordinated or combined award that compresses all three into fewer papers and one or two grades. They might be entered at Core tier, with a lower grade ceiling, or at Extended. They might be with Cambridge International or with Pearson Edexcel, and the two boards structure the practical assessment differently. The word on the school report is the same in all of those cases.

This matters because a tutoring plan built on the wrong assumption wastes the first month. A tutor teaching separate-science content to a student on a combined award covers material the student will never be examined on, which is frustrating and expensive. A tutor preparing a Core-tier candidate on Extended-only topics does the same thing in reverse. And a tutor who has only taught one board's practical paper will prepare a student for the wrong style of question, because the way a board asks about an experiment the candidate never performed is specific to that board.

So the first thing to do, before any search for a tutor at all, is to find the code. It is on the entry confirmation the school sends, on the statement of entry, and usually on the front of a past paper the student has been given. Cambridge codes are four digits: Biology, Chemistry and Physics each have their own, the coordinated and combined awards have theirs. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look different again. Ten minutes finding the right one saves a month of approximate teaching.

The second thing is the tier, where one exists. Core and Extended are not difficulty settings applied to the same exam; they are different papers covering overlapping but unequal content, and Core entry limits the grade a candidate can be awarded. Parents are often not told this plainly, and it comes up in conversations about university or Diploma entry two years later, when the entry decision cannot be revisited. Ask the school directly what grade ceiling applies to your child's tier and grading scale. The answer should come in writing, from the exams officer rather than the class teacher, because it is their record to confirm.

The rest of this page is about the syllabus and the marks: what each paper asks for, where the mark schemes catch students out in each of the three sciences, how to use a past paper so that it produces improvement rather than a score, and when the exam series fall for a UAE candidate. IB Gram teaches this one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-mizhar.subjectsIntro: These are the science syllabuses and their close neighbours as Al Mizhar families actually meet them. Where a code is given, check it against your child's statement of entry rather than assuming.

subjects.name: Biology, separate award
subjects.description: Characteristics of living organisms, cells, transport, respiration, co-ordination, reproduction, inheritance, ecology. Marks are lost on command terms: a question asking to explain is answered with a description, and a question asking for two differences receives one difference twice in different words.

subjects.name: Chemistry, separate award
subjects.description: States of matter, atoms and bonding, stoichiometry, electrochemistry, energetics, rates, acids and bases, the periodic table, organic chemistry. The single biggest mark loss is mole arithmetic, closely followed by ionic equations written with the charges unbalanced.

subjects.name: Physics, separate award
subjects.description: Motion and forces, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, nuclear physics. Students lose marks by giving answers without units, by using the wrong form of a rearranged relationship, and by describing a graph rather than extracting a value from it.

subjects.name: Coordinated or combined science
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics compressed into fewer papers, awarding one or two grades rather than three. Content is a defined subset of the separate syllabuses, so teaching separate-science material to a combined candidate wastes time on topics that will never be examined.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject that silently determines science marks. Rearrangement, standard form, ratio and graph work appear in every science paper. A student losing physics marks is very often losing them in the algebra rather than in the physics.

subjects.name: Additional or Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger mathematicians alongside the main course and useful preparation for A Level or Diploma sciences. Worth considering for a student aiming at Higher Level Physics, because the algebraic fluency is exactly what that course assumes.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Relevant to science because extended-response marks depend on precise written explanation. Students who cannot sustain a two-sentence causal explanation in English lose science marks that have nothing to do with their scientific understanding.

subjects.name: Environmental Management
subjects.description: Overlaps substantially with biology and chemistry content on ecosystems, pollution and resources. Often taken as a fourth science-adjacent subject, and it rewards the same data-interpretation skill the science papers test.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Chosen by many science students in this catchment. Shares the logical decomposition that physics problem-solving uses, and its practical component demands the same habit of documenting what was actually done rather than what was intended.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. Worth noting here because it occupies timetable hours that compete with science revision, and because it is excluded from the five-subject count used for Ministry of Education British-track equivalency.

sections.heading: The syllabus codes, and why the wrong one costs a month
paragraphs: A code is a four-digit number for Cambridge International and a different format for Pearson Edexcel, and it is the only reliable description of what your child will be examined on. Two students in the same year group at the same school in Mirdif can be entered for different awards, and a tutor who assumes rather than checks will build the wrong plan. The code appears on the statement of entry, on the school's entry confirmation and on the front page of any past paper the student has been issued.

The distinction that catches most families is between separate sciences and a coordinated or combined award. Separate entry means three syllabuses, three sets of papers and three grades. A coordinated or combined award covers a defined subset of all three sciences and awards one or two grades instead. The subset is genuinely smaller, not merely easier, so teaching separate-science content to a combined candidate spends hours on material that will not appear. Confirm which award your child holds before the first lesson.

The second distinction is the board. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both run international GCSE science qualifications, and their question styles and practical assessment arrangements differ. A tutor fluent in one board's style will prepare a student competently for the content and imperfectly for the paper. Ask any prospective tutor which board and which code they teach, and treat a vague answer as the answer. sections.heading: Core against Extended: the grade ceiling parents are rarely told about
paragraphs: Where a science syllabus is tiered, a candidate is entered at Core or at Extended, and the two are not the same exam at two difficulty levels. They are different papers covering overlapping content, and Core entry limits the highest grade that can be awarded. That limit is the whole point of the decision, and it is the part of the conversation that most often does not happen. A family discovers it two years later, when a sixth-form entry requirement or a Diploma science prerequisite turns out to sit above the ceiling.

There are good reasons to enter at Core. A student who would be overwhelmed by Extended content and score nothing is better served by a tier they can succeed in, and a secure Core grade is worth more than a collapsed Extended attempt. The reason to have the conversation deliberately is that the decision has a shelf life: once the entry is made and the series sat, it is a fact on the certificate. If the student is close to the boundary, it is worth asking what would need to change for Extended entry to be realistic, and whether a term of focused support could achieve it.

Ask the school three questions in writing. What tier is my child entered for, in each science. What is the highest grade available at that tier under the grading scale in use. And what would need to change for the other tier to be appropriate. Those three answers, together, are the only basis on which the decision should be made. sections.heading: The practical paper: questions about experiments nobody performed in the exam
paragraphs: Every IGCSE science award assesses practical skills, and in most arrangements a UAE candidate does that in writing rather than in a laboratory. This produces a paper that students find strange and that is, in fact, highly predictable. It asks a small set of recurring things: which variable was changed, which was kept constant, how a measurement should be read and to what precision, why one result does not fit, and what single change would improve the method.

Because the patterns recur, the paper rewards preparation disproportionately. A student who has practised identifying the independent and dependent variables in twenty unfamiliar experiments will do it reliably in the exam, regardless of whether they ever ran that experiment. A student who has only done practicals in class, and has never been asked to write about someone else's method, meets the question style for the first time under timed conditions and loses marks that have nothing to do with their laboratory ability.

The improvement question deserves separate attention because it is where vague answers go to die. Saying the experiment should be repeated earns little; saying that repeating it and taking a mean would reduce the effect of random error in the timing measurement earns the mark, because it names the error and the mechanism. Anomaly questions work the same way: the mark is for a plausible, specific cause tied to the method described, not for observing that one point is higher than the others. These are learnable in a handful of sessions and they are worth more than another pass through content.

sections.heading: Biology and Chemistry: where the mark schemes catch students out
paragraphs: Biology at IGCSE loses marks to command terms more than to ignorance. A question that says describe wants observable detail; a question that says explain wants the because. Students who have learned the content thoroughly still answer explain questions descriptively and score half. The second recurring loss is the two-differences question, answered with one difference stated twice in different words, which earns one mark. The third is naming a process without naming where it happens, when the mark scheme requires both.

Chemistry's losses are more arithmetic. Mole calculations are the largest single source, and within them the recurring errors are failing to convert volumes into the right unit, identifying the limiting reagent by mass rather than by amount, and quoting an answer to more figures than the data supports. Ionic equations are the second source: students write them with the species correct and the charges unbalanced, which is not a careless slip in the mark scheme's eyes but a wrong equation. Tests for ions and gases are the third, and they are pure recall, which makes them the cheapest marks on the paper to secure.

Both subjects reward a specific habit that very few students have: marking their own work against the published scheme before anyone else sees it. A candidate who marks their own answer and discovers the scheme wanted the word because, or wanted a unit, or wanted the location as well as the process, learns something that no amount of being told will teach. In a one-to-one session the most useful hour is often the student marking and the tutor auditing the marking, rather than the tutor explaining content the student already half knows.

sections.heading: Physics: units, rearrangement and reading a graph for a value
paragraphs: IGCSE Physics punishes carelessness more visibly than the other two sciences, because so much of it is quantitative and the mark schemes are specific. Three losses recur. Answers given without units, which can lose a mark on a question the student otherwise answered correctly. Rearrangement errors, where the physics was understood and the algebra was not, and the wrong form of the relationship produced a confident wrong number. And graph questions answered by describing the shape when the question asked for a value read off the axis.

The rearrangement problem is the one worth attacking first, because it is not a physics problem at all. A student who cannot reliably make a chosen quantity the subject of a relationship will fail physics questions for mathematical reasons throughout the course, and will keep failing them however much physics is revised. Twenty minutes a week of pure rearrangement practice, with no physics context, fixes this faster than any amount of topic teaching. It also improves chemistry calculations at the same time.

Graph work needs the same mechanical treatment. Read what is being asked: a value, a gradient, a trend, or a comparison. If a value, go to the axis and read it, with the unit. If a gradient, choose two widely separated points on the line rather than two data points, and show the subtraction. If a trend, name the relationship rather than saying it goes up. These are habits, not insights, and habits are exactly what responds to a weekly one-to-one slot that keeps checking them.

sections.heading: How to use a past paper so that it produces marks
paragraphs: Most students use past papers as a thermometer. They sit one, score it, feel either reassured or alarmed, and move on to the next. That produces a series of measurements and almost no improvement. A past paper is useful only if what happens after it is more work than the paper itself, and the procedure below is what that looks like in practice.

The central move is that the student marks their own script against the published scheme before anyone else looks at it, and the tutor then checks the marking rather than the answers. This is uncomfortable for a week and transformative afterwards, because it forces the student to read the scheme as the examiner does. A student who has marked ten of their own scripts knows that explain needs a causal link, that a unit is part of the answer, and that two differences means two distinct differences. Being told those things does not work; discovering them while losing your own marks does.

The second move is to log the losses by cause rather than by topic. A student who writes down that they lost four marks this week to missing units, three to command terms and two to rearrangement has a list they can act on. A student who writes down that they are bad at electricity has a mood. Over six papers the log shows which causes are shrinking and which are not, and that is what a monthly review should look at. Paper material should come from the school and from the boards' own published pages; IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables.

sections.heading: The exam series a UAE candidate actually sits
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs its IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests at other points in the year. There is an additional early-year series, and it is offered to India only. A UAE candidate sits June, with November available as the resit route. Any revision plan built around the India-only sitting is built on a date that does not apply to your child, and that error has appeared on advice pages aimed at Gulf parents.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and its exams officers' guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A parent cannot resolve this; the school's exams officer can, in one email. Ask which zone your child's centre sits in and work from that timetable.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and in November each year. For the November 2026 series the final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results reach students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and those can be revised, so plan from the live official timetable rather than from any date restated on a page like this one.

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens if the right syllabus specialist is not free
paragraphs: The first step is the code. Send the statement of entry, or a photograph of the front page of a past paper the school issued, and the plan can be built on fact rather than on the word science. Then a marked script, ideally the most recent one with the teacher's annotations left on it, because that is where the diagnosis comes from. Ten minutes of preparation by a parent saves a full session of guessing.

Then a free trial lesson, one-to-one over live video, used as a diagnostic rather than a demonstration. Ask the tutor to work through the marked script and tell you where the marks went and why. A tutor who can name the causes, missing units, command terms, mole conversions, within the hour is worth booking. A tutor who talks about their experience and their approach is not answering the question. Say early if the match is wrong; week one is the cheapest time to change.

The disclosure, before you ask for it: specialist coverage is by board and by syllabus, not by the word science, and there are weeks when no UAE-based tutor for a particular code has an evening slot that fits an eastern-suburbs timetable. Where that happens you will be told, and offered a specialist based elsewhere teaching the same syllabus over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time. What you will not get is a general science tutor presented as a specialist in your child's code, because that is the specific failure this whole page is written to prevent.

process.title: Send the code, not the subject name
process.description: Statement of entry or the front page of an issued past paper. Board, syllabus code, award type and tier. Everything in the teaching plan follows from these four facts, and all four are wrong often enough that checking is never wasted effort.

process.title: Send a marked script
process.description: The most recent marked paper or test with the teacher's comments intact. This is where the diagnosis comes from, and it converts the first session from an introduction into a piece of work. A script from before the last holiday is still more useful than none.

process.title: Free trial used as a diagnostic
process.description: One hour, one-to-one over live video, with the script read in advance. Ask the tutor to name the causes of the lost marks. You should leave the hour with a list of causes and a plan for the first block, not with an impression of a nice person.

process.title: Set the past-paper discipline early
process.description: Timed paper, student marks it first, tutor audits the marking, losses logged by cause. Establishing this in the first fortnight is worth more than any amount of content teaching, and it is the habit that keeps working after the tutoring ends.

process.title: Review the loss log monthly
process.description: Look at whether the causes are shrinking: fewer missing units, fewer command-term errors, fewer rearrangement failures. If a cause has not moved in four weeks, the method changes rather than the hours increasing.

whyPoints.title: The code comes first
whyPoints.description: Teaching starts from the confirmed board, syllabus code, award type and tier. Competitor pages reviewed for this project mention almost no syllabus codes at all, and a plan built on the word science wastes the first month on content that will not be examined.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes, read by the student
whyPoints.description: Sessions build the habit of the student marking their own script against the published scheme while the tutor audits the marking. It is uncomfortable for a fortnight and it changes results, because it teaches what the examiner rewards.

whyPoints.title: Losses tracked by cause
whyPoints.description: Missing units, command terms, mole conversions and rearrangement are causes. Electricity is not a cause, it is a topic. Logging by cause produces a list a student can act on and a review that shows whether anything is actually improving.

whyPoints.title: Series and timetable handled honestly
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The early-year Cambridge sitting is offered to India only, and this page says so, because advice aimed at Gulf parents has got it wrong before now.

whyPoints.title: Official material only
whyPoints.description: Sessions work from the papers and syllabus documents the school holds and from the boards' own published pages. IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated by syllabus
whyPoints.description: Availability is disclosed per board and per code rather than per subject. If no UAE-based specialist for your child's syllabus is free, you are told and offered a specialist elsewhere on Gulf Standard Time instead of a quiet substitution.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE science syllabus my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Look at the statement of entry the school issues, the entry confirmation email, or the front page of any past paper the school has given your child. You are looking for four facts: the exam board, the syllabus code, whether the entry is for separate sciences or a coordinated or combined award, and the tier where the syllabus is tiered. If any of those is unclear, email the exams officer rather than the class teacher; it is their record and they can answer it in a line.

faqs.question: What is the difference between separate sciences and a combined science award?
faqs.answer: Separate entry means three syllabuses, three sets of papers and three grades. A coordinated or combined award covers a defined subset of biology, chemistry and physics and awards one or two grades instead. The subset is genuinely smaller rather than simply easier, so a tutor teaching separate-science content to a combined candidate spends hours on topics that will never be examined. It also matters for sixth-form entry, because some science A Level and Diploma requirements are written in terms of separate-science grades.

faqs.question: Does Core tier entry limit the grade my child can get?
faqs.answer: Yes, where a syllabus is tiered. Core and Extended are different papers covering overlapping content, and Core entry caps the highest grade available. Ask the school in writing for the exact ceiling under the grading scale in use, because it varies and it is not reversible once the series is sat. There are sound reasons to enter at Core, and a secure Core grade beats a collapsed Extended attempt, but the decision should be made deliberately and before entries close rather than discovered two years later.

faqs.question: How is the practical work assessed if my child studies science online?
faqs.answer: The practical component is generally assessed in writing rather than in a laboratory for international candidates, which means the paper asks about experiments the candidate did not perform. The questions follow recurring patterns: identify the variables, read a measurement to the right precision, explain an anomaly, suggest one improvement that names the error and its mechanism. Those patterns are learnable without equipment, and practising them against twenty unfamiliar methods is worth more than another pass through content. Confirm the exact arrangement with your child's exams officer.

faqs.question: Which science does my child lose the most marks in without realising?
faqs.answer: Usually physics, and usually for mathematical reasons rather than scientific ones. The recurring losses are answers given without units, rearrangement errors where the physics was understood and the algebra was not, and graph questions answered by describing a shape when a value was wanted. Twenty minutes a week of pure rearrangement practice with no physics context fixes more physics marks than an equivalent amount of topic revision, and it improves chemistry calculations at the same time.

faqs.question: Why does my child write a full page in biology and still score half marks?
faqs.answer: Almost always command terms. A describe question wants observable detail; an explain question wants the causal because. A student who has learned the content thoroughly can answer an explain question descriptively, at length, and score half. The second recurring loss is a two-differences question answered with one difference stated twice in different words. The third is naming a process without naming where it happens when the scheme asks for both. These are diagnosable in one session from a marked script.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches Cambridge science also prepare an Edexcel candidate?
faqs.answer: On content, largely yes. On the paper, with more caution. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel structure their international GCSE science qualifications differently, their question styles differ and their practical assessment arrangements are not identical. A tutor fluent in one board prepares a student competently for the subject and imperfectly for the exam. Ask any prospective tutor which board and which code they teach, and treat a vague answer as the answer. Matching the board is worth more than matching the postcode.

faqs.question: Which exam series will an Al Mizhar science candidate actually be entered for?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series for international candidates, and UAE schools use June as the main sitting with November available as a resit route. Cambridge also offers an early-year series to India only, so any plan built around that sitting does not apply to a UAE candidate. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. Your school's exams officer holds the centre's own dates, including the entry deadline, which falls months before the papers.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge timetable zone matter for a Dubai centre?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each. Its exams officers' guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is not something a parent can resolve from a public page. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in, then work only from that timetable.

faqs.question: How many science past papers should my child do before the series?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families imagine, done properly. Six papers with a full procedure after each one beat twenty papers scored and filed. The procedure is what matters: sit it timed, mark it against the scheme yourself before anyone else sees it, have the marking audited, log the losses by cause rather than by topic, and re-answer only the questions that were lost. A student who has marked six of their own scripts has learned more about the examiner than a student who has sat twenty.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE science grades count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, alongside one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that six subjects are needed, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channels; equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring provider performs.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 and already behind. Is it too early or too late to start?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the best time there is, because the problem is usually a foundation rather than a topic, and foundations take a term rather than a fortnight. A syllabus audit against the actual code, marking each statement as secure, shaky or unmet, takes two or three sessions and usually shows the gap is narrower than it feels. Starting now also means the past-paper marking discipline is established before the pressure arrives, which is when it is most useful and hardest to build.

faqs.question: Where should we get IGCSE science past papers and mark schemes from?
faqs.answer: From the school, which holds the material it is entitled to use, and from the boards' own published pages. Files circulating in parent groups are frequently out of date, and an old syllabus is worse than none because it looks authoritative and quietly removes or adds topics. IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables; sessions work from the official material the school provides, with links out to the boards' current pages.

faqs.question: What should an Al Mizhar family send before a first science session?
faqs.answer: Five things, and they take a quarter of an hour. The statement of entry showing board, code, award and tier. The most recent marked science paper with teacher comments left on. The topic the class is covering now and the next assessment date. Whether the practical component has been discussed in class. And the realistic weekday time your child walks in the door, because a slot booked for the moment the bus arrives buys a tired student rather than a working one.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-mizhar.closingHeading: Start from the syllabus, not from the subject name
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-mizhar.closingBody: Science on a school report is four unanswered questions: which board, which code, separate or combined, and which tier. Answer those and a tutoring plan becomes specific instead of approximate. Send the statement of entry and the most recent marked script, take a free trial lesson as a diagnostic, and ask the tutor to name the causes of the lost marks rather than the topics. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, timed for when a student travelling home across eastern Dubai can actually concentrate.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-muteena.tutorsIntro: The science tutors here teach to one board and one paper set at a time. The first question in every enquiry is which series the student is entered for and what the school's mock date is, because those two facts decide whether the next block is content teaching or examination behaviour.

intro.heading: Where your child actually is in the IGCSE science year
paragraphs: Most tutoring enquiries about IGCSE science start with a worry and no date attached. The honest first step is to put the date in. A Year 10 in the autumn term has eighteen months and can afford to rebuild foundations. A Year 11 eight weeks from a paper has time for examination behaviour and nothing else. A student who sat June papers and was disappointed is looking at the November series and has an entirely different problem, which is choosing what to re-sit. These three families need different tutors, different session lengths and different numbers of hours, and a page that answers all three identically is not answering any of them.

The calendar is fixed and public. Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and both are open to UAE candidates. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route available to a student in Al Muteena, and any provider telling a Dubai parent otherwise is giving them a date they cannot use. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations run in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

Results land at predictable distances from the papers. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November results arrive in the following January: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entries close months before the papers, because the centre has to declare candidates, tiers and options before a timetable is finalised. That is the whole reason a tier conversation in the spring term matters more than extra hours in the summer.

Science complicates the picture because a Year 11 is rarely sitting one subject. Cambridge candidates may be entered for three single sciences, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology, or for 0654 Coordinated Sciences as a double award, or for 0653 Combined Science as a single award. Pearson candidates may sit 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 separately or 4SD0 Double Award Science. Each of those carries its own paper structure, and the practical component differs between the boards. A plan that does not name the codes is guessing.

Al Muteena sits in the older half of Dubai, near Deira, with most of the relevant secondaries a short bus ride away in Al Garhoud and Al Qusais. IB Gram teaches students here one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own past papers and mark schemes shared on screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. That means a session can be held at 7am before school in the final fortnight, which is a scheduling option no visiting tutor realistically offers.

The rest of this page is organised as a countdown. What the series actually are, what each science paper set contains, which practical paper the school entered, what the final eight weeks should contain week by week, what the market charges and what a parent can verify about it.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-muteena.programmesIntro: Three stages of the science timetable produce different enquiries from this part of Dubai, and the stage matters more than the subject. These are the groups a science tutor in Al Muteena actually works with.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the course starts
programmes.description: The year in which schools decide tier and route: three single sciences, a double award or a combined award. That decision shapes what a student can apply for later, and it is made on Year 9 evidence. Work at this stage is about the mathematics science depends on, and about writing explanations that answer the question asked.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools run a British academic year from late August to early July, so route decisions for Year 10 are typically taken in the spring. A family in Al Muteena who wants three single sciences should be asking what evidence the school needs by February rather than appealing in June.

programmes.name: Year 10, the content year
programmes.description: The year with room to repair foundations. Content taught now is examined eighteen months later, so retention is the challenge and retrieval practice is the answer. This is also the only point at which a student can comfortably change tier or route on the strength of improved work rather than hope.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 in a Dubai school includes the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the science timetable, so the realistic independent study window for most Al Muteena households is the weekend plus two weekday evenings. Planning for that honestly produces a schedule that survives the term.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: Mocks in the first half, papers in the second, and a steadily shrinking set of options. Content teaching gives way to paper technique, command terms, practical paper preparation and timing. The highest-value work here is marking the student's own answers against the published scheme and acting on what it shows.
programmes.countryNote: A Year 11 in Al Muteena is typically entered through their own school, which holds the entry and the tier. Private candidates sit at an approved examination centre in Dubai instead and must confirm their own deadlines with that centre well before the series opens.

programmes.name: November resit candidates
programmes.description: A different problem entirely: deciding which papers to re-sit, what grade movement is realistic, and how to use a short autumn window. The content is already taught, so the work is diagnostic from the actual result and the question-level feedback, then targeted repair on the two or three areas that cost the most.
programmes.countryNote: The November series is the resit route available in the UAE, since the February/March series is offered to India only. Re-entry deadlines sit well before the papers, so the decision has to be made in the weeks after August results rather than in October.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-muteena.subjectsIntro: Science is three subjects and up to nine papers depending on the entry. These are the specific areas Al Muteena students bring most often, with what the examination asks of each.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Series and parallel circuits, potential dividers, resistance calculations and circuit diagram interpretation. This is the most reliably weak topic in IGCSE physics, and it is fixable because the questions are formulaic once the student reads circuits rather than recognising them.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, motion and moments
subjects.description: Speed-time graphs, Newton's laws, momentum at Extended level and moments about a pivot. Graph questions carry marks for reading values accurately from the grid, which students lose through approximation rather than misunderstanding.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Relative formula mass, moles, concentration and reacting-mass calculations. Extended candidates meet these throughout the paper, and the mark loss is unit discipline rather than chemistry, so a layout change often recovers several marks immediately.

subjects.name: Chemistry: rates, equilibrium and energetics
subjects.description: Collision theory, the effect of concentration and temperature, reversible reactions and exothermic or endothermic changes. Explanation questions are marked for mechanism, so answers that describe what happens without saying why earn little.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and respiration
subjects.description: Transport in plants and humans, gas exchange, aerobic and anaerobic respiration. Marks are lost in questions asking students to apply a process to an unfamiliar organism or experiment, which is a reading skill as much as a biological one.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Monohybrid crosses, Punnett squares, probability of outcomes and the vocabulary of alleles and genotypes. Students who learn the terminology precisely gain marks that students using everyday language lose, even with the biology understood.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Double or single award covering all three sciences in one qualification with a reduced content load. The syllabus is not simply the three single sciences shortened, so revising from single-science resources leads students into content they are not examined on and away from content they are.

subjects.name: The practical component
subjects.levels: Paper 5, Paper 6, or within written papers
subjects.description: Cambridge single sciences assess practical skills in a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper worth a fifth of the grade. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead. Which applies changes revision completely, and parents rarely know which their child is entered for.

subjects.name: Command terms and explanation structure
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest and calculate each have a defined expectation. Science papers hand out marks for answering at the right depth, and a four-mark explain answered as a one-line description is the most common single loss across all three subjects.

subjects.name: Graphs, tables and data handling
subjects.description: Plotting accurately, drawing a line of best fit, reading intermediate values and describing a trend with reference to the data. This is trainable in two or three sessions and appears in every science paper, which makes it the best-value late repair available.

sections.heading: The two series a UAE candidate can actually sit
paragraphs: Everything in a science plan hangs off which series the student is entered for, so this comes first. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only. A student in Al Muteena therefore has June and November, and nothing else.

That restriction has a practical edge. An earlier version of the research behind these pages offered the February and March key dates as a worked example, and pages went out quoting a February examination window and a late-November entry deadline to UAE parents. A wrong date is worse than a thin page, because a parent acts on it. If any provider gives you a February series date for a Dubai school, that is a reason to doubt everything else on their page.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Results follow at known intervals: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates keep their years here because they are citations, and the year is what makes them checkable.

One further Cambridge rule matters and almost nobody mentions it. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. A parent downloading a timetable from a general search result rather than from the school is taking a risk for no reason.

sections.heading: Which science papers is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: Parents are often surprised by how much this question matters. A Year 11 may be entered for three single sciences, a double award or a single combined award, under one of two boards, at one of two tiers. Each combination has a different paper structure, a different practical arrangement and a different amount of content, and revising from the wrong set of resources is one of the most expensive mistakes available in the final term.

On the Cambridge side, the single sciences carry the codes 0625 for Physics, 0620 for Chemistry and 0610 for Biology. Coordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award covering all three, and Combined Science 0653 is a single award. The double and combined awards are not simply the single syllabuses shortened: content is selected, so a student revising physics from 0625 material while entered for 0654 will study topics they are not examined on and miss emphasis they are.

On the Pearson side, the single sciences are 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, with 4SD0 Double Award Science as the combined route. The structural difference parents notice most is the practical arrangement: Cambridge single sciences assess practical skills in a separate paper, while Pearson assesses them inside the written papers. That single difference changes the final month of revision substantially.

The first action for any family in this cluster is to find the examination entry letter and read the codes on it. Then check the paper structure against the board's own published specification, because syllabus versions change and a tutor working from an old one will prepare the wrong things. This is a five-minute task that routinely improves a revision plan more than an extra month of sessions.

sections.heading: The practical paper nobody asks about until March
paragraphs: For Cambridge single sciences the practical component is worth a fifth of the grade, and there is usually a choice the school made on the student's behalf: a practical test taken in a laboratory, or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Parents almost never know which, and students frequently revise as though the component does not exist because it is the one part of the course with no obvious textbook chapter.

The two options demand different preparation. A practical test rewards apparatus familiarity, measurement technique and the discipline of recording readings as they are taken. An alternative-to-practical paper rewards the ability to read a described experiment, identify the variable being controlled, criticise a method and process somebody else's results. Both reward table layout and graph discipline, which is why those two skills are the best use of a late session.

Pearson's arrangement is different: practical skills are assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate component. That does not make them less important, it makes them harder to see. A student who has never deliberately practised method criticism will meet it embedded in a longer question and treat it as a comprehension exercise rather than a technique with marks attached.

The action here is specific and takes one email: ask the school which practical component each science is entered for, then plan accordingly. In the final eight weeks, two sessions spent on the practical paper format are usually worth more than two spent on content, because the format is unfamiliar and formats are learnable.

sections.heading: The last eight weeks, week by week
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the shortest window that reliably changes a science grade, and it only does so if the plan is specific. The mistake families make is to attempt a full syllabus sweep, which spreads attention so thinly that nothing is secured. The better approach is to accept that some topics will be left alone, and to spend the window on the behaviours that cost marks across every topic at once.

Week one is diagnosis: the last two marked papers, read against the published mark scheme, with the losses counted by cause rather than by topic. Most students discover that two or three habits account for more lost marks than any content gap. Weeks two to four attack those habits, alongside the two topics with the clearest return, which is usually electricity in physics, moles in chemistry and genetics vocabulary in biology.

Weeks five and six turn to the practical component and to data handling, because both are learnable formats and both appear in every paper. Weeks seven and eight are full timed papers under something close to examination conditions, marked properly, with the final sessions spent on the specific question types still going wrong. Nothing new is introduced in the last fortnight, because new content at that point displaces practice of content already known.

The plan in the table is a template rather than a prescription, and the dates it hangs on are the school's: the mock result, the entry confirmation and the first paper. A tutor who cannot tell you which week of this countdown your child is in does not have a plan.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs in Dubai, and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: Rates in this market are published inconsistently, and three of the six most visible competitor pages quote no price at all. What can be verified is worth stating with its source. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to AED 52. The Bestimate rate survey for Dubai places specialist tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 or more and in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 350.

The verifiable part is the method, not just the number. Each of those figures sits on a page a parent can open, which is what makes it useful; a rate quoted without a source is just a claim. Monthly, Bestimate estimates roughly AED 240 to AED 600 for budget tutoring on a weekly one-hour pattern, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Science has a specific cost feature: a family often needs more than one subject. Three single sciences with three different weak topics is not one tutoring request, and a provider who implies one tutor covers physics, chemistry and biology at Extended level with equal depth is overstating. Sometimes one tutor genuinely can, more often two is the honest answer, and that doubles the budget conversation. Asking about it early is better than discovering it in April.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly table on this page, because the hours a student needs depend entirely on the window remaining and on how many subjects are involved. The arrangement is a free trial lesson, a written diagnosis and then a plan sized to both. Every figure above belongs to the provider or survey named with it.
