sections.heading: Online sessions, early-morning slots and the Deira commute
paragraphs: The scheduling argument matters more for science than for most subjects, because a Year 11 sitting three sciences needs more sessions in the same week than a student sitting one subject. Four sessions a week across two tutors is a logistics problem for any family, and it is the point at which in-home delivery usually breaks down: two tutors, two commutes, two arrival times that depend on Al Ittihad Road.

Online removes that entirely. Sessions can be stacked on a weekend morning, split across two evenings, or placed at 7am before school in the final fortnight, which is a slot no visiting tutor would offer. Nothing travels, so nothing is late, and a session that was going to be cancelled because of traffic simply happens. For an eight-week countdown where consistency is the whole point, that reliability is the substance of the argument rather than a convenience.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. Lessons for Al Muteena families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with past papers and mark schemes shared on screen and sessions recorded for later review. In-home science tutoring is available locally from independent tutors and agencies at published market rates, and for a younger student who will not stay on task without someone in the room it may be the better choice.

sections.heading: The UAE calendar that sits on top of the exam calendar
paragraphs: A science countdown in Dubai does not run on the board's calendar alone. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 the equivalent date for schools whose year begins in April. Instructional time for those subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those are real weekly hours that cannot be moved to make room for revision.

Ramadan then reshapes the school day across the emirate and moves household routines substantially, with study time shifting to late evening after Iftar for many families. A plan that ignores it either fails during the month or quietly stops. The workable approach is to reschedule into post-Iftar slots for the month and to treat it as a different kind of term rather than a lost one.

Eid holidays, winter and spring breaks, National Day and the school's own mock window all compete for the same weeks. Mapping those dates before buying any hours is unglamorous and it is the single most useful planning act available to a family in this cluster. What remains after the mapping is the real revision window, and sizing the plan to it is why some plans survive twelve weeks and others collapse in week three.

The regulator context is worth one sentence for completeness. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no permit or approval from any of them and should never be described as approved by one.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam series can a student in Al Muteena actually be entered for?
faqs.answer: June and November with Cambridge, and May/June or November with Pearson Edexcel. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not available to a candidate in Dubai. This matters because at least one earlier wave of tutoring content circulated February dates and a late-November entry deadline to UAE parents, which is a date a family might act on. If a provider offers you a February series date for a Dubai school, treat the rest of their information with caution and check the school's own entry letter.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE results arrive for the June and November sittings?
faqs.answer: June results come about two months after the papers and November results in the following January. For Pearson, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those gaps matter for planning: a student disappointed in August has only a few weeks to decide on November re-entries, because entry deadlines sit well before the papers. The decision therefore has to be made soon after results rather than in October.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits 0625 or 0654 for physics?
faqs.answer: Read the examination entry letter from the school; the syllabus code is on it. Cambridge single sciences are 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology. Coordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award and Combined Science 0653 a single award, and neither is simply the single syllabus shortened, because content is selected. A student revising from 0625 resources while entered for 0654 will study material they are not examined on. It is a five-minute check that frequently improves a revision plan more than an extra month of sessions.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and does my child sit it?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge single sciences, practical skills are assessed either in a laboratory practical test or in an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the component is worth a fifth of the grade. The school chooses which, and parents usually do not know. The two need different preparation: a practical test rewards apparatus technique, while the alternative paper rewards reading a described method, identifying controlled variables and criticising a procedure. Ask the school by email which each science is entered for, then plan the final weeks around the answer.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks long enough to change an IGCSE science grade?
faqs.answer: It is long enough to change examination behaviour, which is where most recoverable marks sit, and too short for a syllabus sweep. A realistic eight weeks starts with diagnosis from two marked papers, spends weeks two to four on the two or three habits costing most marks, uses weeks five and six on practical format and data handling, and finishes with full timed papers. Some topics get left alone deliberately. Nobody can promise a grade in eight weeks, and any provider who does should be questioned closely.

faqs.question: Which science topics give the fastest improvement for a Year 11 in Deira?
faqs.answer: Electricity and circuits in physics, moles and reacting masses in chemistry, and genetics vocabulary in biology, with graph and data handling cutting across all three. Those four have something in common: the questions are formulaic once the student reads the problem properly, so improvement comes quickly and holds. Topics that depend on long chains of reasoning move more slowly and are poor choices in a short window. A diagnosis from marked papers usually confirms this list with one or two personal additions.

faqs.question: Does my Year 11 need separate tutors for physics, chemistry and biology?
faqs.answer: Sometimes one tutor covers two of them well at Extended level, and sometimes the honest answer is two specialists. Any provider implying that one person teaches all three at equal depth is overstating, and the cost consequence is real because it doubles a budget. The question to ask during matching is which papers the tutor has actually marked at the level you need. Settling this at the start avoids the conversation in April where a plan turns out to be half the size it needed to be.

faqs.question: Can sessions happen before school for a 7am slot in the final weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online delivery is the reason it is practical. A visiting tutor will not realistically arrive in Al Muteena at 7am, but a video session at that hour costs nobody a commute. In the final fortnight before a series, some students work far better early than after a full school day, and a short morning session on one paper type can be the most productive thirty minutes of the day. The slot is agreed with the family and held, so it becomes routine rather than an occasional effort.

faqs.question: Does someone travel to our home in Al Muteena for science lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with past papers and mark schemes shared on screen. In-home science tutoring is available from independent tutors and agencies at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. For a three-science Year 11 needing four sessions a week, the practical problem with visits is two tutors, two commutes and two traffic-dependent arrival times.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE science tutoring cost per hour in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: Published figures range widely. Unitors advertises IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. At the lower end EdFlik lists from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to AED 52. The Bestimate rate survey for Dubai puts specialist tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 or more and in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 350. Each of those sits on a page you can open, which is what makes them worth quoting.

faqs.question: My child sat June papers and did badly. Should we re-enter for November?
faqs.answer: Decide on evidence rather than disappointment, and decide quickly, because re-entry deadlines fall well before the papers. Start with the actual result and any question-level feedback the school can supply, then identify which papers are realistically movable in an autumn window. Re-sitting everything is rarely the right answer; re-sitting the one or two papers with clear, specific losses often is. The content is already taught, so the work is targeted repair rather than a second full course, and that is a different and shorter plan.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect an IGCSE science revision plan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The school day shortens across the emirate and household routines change substantially, with study time moving to late evening after Iftar for many families. Sessions can be rescheduled into post-Iftar slots for the month rather than forced into a timetable nobody can keep. The sensible approach is to map Ramadan, Eid, the winter and spring breaks, National Day and the school mock window before buying any hours, then size the plan to what is left. Plans built without that mapping tend to stop in week three.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory UAE subjects reduce the time available for science revision?
faqs.answer: They occupy fixed weekly hours, so yes, and a plan has to account for it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum licensed, with KHDA requiring implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For most households in this cluster that leaves the weekend plus two weekday evenings as the realistic independent study window, which is sufficient if the work is targeted rather than open-ended.

faqs.question: Who regulates the school my child sits these papers at?
faqs.answer: In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. That distinction matters for families in Al Nahda who may use schools on both sides of the Sharjah boundary. IB Gram holds no permit or approval from any of these bodies and does not claim one.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-nahda.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics for students in Al Nahda, Al Qusais and across the Sharjah border, on both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications, in evening and weekend slots.

intro.heading: When does an IGCSE science session actually fit into an Al Nahda week?
paragraphs: Start with the clock rather than the syllabus, because the clock is what decides whether tutoring happens at all. Schools serving Al Nahda, Al Qusais and Al Twar finish between roughly 2pm and 3.30pm depending on the provider and the year group. A bus route through this part of Dubai adds twenty to forty minutes, and a parent collecting by car at 2.45pm on Al Nahda Road in term time will not be home by three. Add a snack and the first attempt at homework, and the earliest a Year 10 student is genuinely able to concentrate on a new chemistry topic is somewhere around 5pm.

That leaves two usable windows on a weekday. The first runs from about 5pm to 6.30pm, before the evening meal and before a parent gets home from work in Deira or Sharjah. It is the better window for teaching new content, because the student is tired but not finished. The second runs from about 7.30pm to 9pm, after the meal, and it is the better window for practice and past-paper work, which needs less from the student than new material does. Trying to teach bonding at 9.15pm is a waste of an hour nobody enjoys.

The third option, and the one most families under-use, is Saturday morning. Al Nahda households tend to commit Saturday afternoons and Fridays to family and prayer, which leaves Saturday from 9am to noon almost entirely free and the student at their freshest of the week. A single ninety-minute Saturday session covering new content, with a short weekday slot later for practice, outperforms two tired weekday hours for most Year 10 and Year 11 students. We say this on the first call because it is the cheapest improvement available and it costs nothing to try.

The science subject matters too. Three separate sciences at Extended tier is a different weekly load from double award or co-ordinated science, and it changes how much tutoring is useful. A student taking Biology, Chemistry and Physics separately is sitting six or more papers; a student on a combined route is sitting fewer, with less content in each. Tutoring the wrong route is a common and expensive error in this district, because the school's own naming of the course does not always make the entry obvious to a parent.

One thing to state plainly before the detail. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE science tuition for an Al Nahda family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for diagrams, calculations and marked past papers. For a timetabling problem this specific, that is the point: nothing has to be driven anywhere, so a 5pm slot really starts at 5pm and a cancelled session does not waste anyone's fuel.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-nahda.programmesIntro: Science at 16 sits at a junction, and which route a student takes changes both the papers and the weekly rhythm. These are the four routes Al Nahda families encounter.

programmes.name: IGCSE separate sciences
programmes.description: Biology, Chemistry and Physics taken as three qualifications, each with its own papers. The heaviest option by content and the one university-bound science students usually need. Extended tier at Cambridge, or the untiered Pearson Edexcel International GCSE science qualifications, gives access to the full grade range.
programmes.countryNote: Most of the British-curriculum provision serving Al Nahda and Al Qusais runs separate sciences from Year 10 for the stronger sets. The practical consequence for families here is three subject teachers, three homework streams and three sets of past papers, which is why tutoring usually targets one science at a time rather than all three.

programmes.name: Co-ordinated or combined science
programmes.description: One or two qualifications covering all three sciences with reduced content in each. Fewer papers, a lighter weekly load, and a sensible route for a student whose strengths lie elsewhere. It does restrict some post-16 science choices, so the decision deserves a conversation rather than a default.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in this part of Dubai place students on co-ordinated science without the name making it obvious on a report card. Ask the school which codes your child is entered for; it is a one-line email and it prevents a term of tutoring aimed at content your child will never be examined on.

programmes.name: IB Diploma sciences after IGCSE
programmes.description: Biology, Chemistry and Physics at Standard or Higher Level, assessed by two papers and a Scientific Investigation worth about a fifth of the grade. Extended-tier IGCSE is reasonable preparation for Standard Level and thin preparation for Higher Level quantitative work.
programmes.countryNote: Al Nahda students have real access to this route, with IB continuum provision in Al Twar and Diploma provision in Al Garhoud. A student who wants it should be entered for separate sciences at Extended tier, which is a Year 9 decision rather than a Year 11 one.

programmes.name: AS and A Level sciences after IGCSE
programmes.description: The more common post-16 route in the British-curriculum schools around Al Nahda. Three or four subjects studied in depth, with AS content typically examined at the end of Year 12 and A2 at the end of Year 13, depending on the school's modular choices.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-nahda.subjectsIntro: Science tutoring in Al Nahda rarely means all three sciences at once. These are the subjects and components families here ask for, and what each one actually demands.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to revise badly. Marks go in questions that ask students to explain a mechanism rather than name a structure, and in data questions where a trend is described instead of accounted for.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The science most often tutored in this district. Moles and reacting-mass calculations are the usual block, followed by electrolysis products at the wrong electrode and ionic equations with charges left unbalanced.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fewer facts, more technique. Nearly all lost marks trace to unit conversion, to rearranging an equation after substituting rather than before, and to answers given without the unit the question demanded.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: All three sciences in reduced depth across a double award. Tutoring has to be aimed at the right specification, because a student revising separate-science content is learning material their paper will not ask for.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The hidden dependency. Rearranging formulae, standard form, ratio and percentage work appear throughout physics and chemistry, and a science grade is frequently capped by a maths weakness rather than a science one.

subjects.name: Practical and alternative-to-practical skills
subjects.description: A distinct examined skill set: identifying variables, reading instruments to the right precision, spotting an anomaly, and improving a method. It is examined even where the school does not sit the hands-on paper.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Frequently requested alongside science in Al Nahda, where many students are strong scientists working in a second language. Long-answer science marks are often lost to phrasing rather than to understanding.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger sets as a bridge towards A Level maths or physics. Useful preparation for quantitative physics, and a sensible alternative to extra science hours for a student already secure on content.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A common fourth option in this cluster. Its algorithmic discipline transfers neatly to multi-step calculation, where the habit of defining each step before computing prevents most arithmetic losses.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. It occupies timetable space families should account for when planning evening sessions.

sections.heading: The Al Nahda school day, and the slots that survive it
paragraphs: The usable tutoring window in this district is narrower than parents expect, and the reason is cumulative rather than dramatic. A 2.30pm finish plus a bus route through Al Qusais and Al Nahda puts a child at the door around 3.15pm. Changing, eating and a first pass at the school's own homework takes until about 4.45pm. The student is then available, genuinely tired, for roughly ninety minutes before the evening meal. After the meal there is a second window, shorter and less sharp, until about 9pm.

Within those windows the ordering matters more than the total. New content needs the earlier slot, because learning something unfamiliar demands attention a nine o'clock student does not have. Past-paper practice, calculation layout and command-word drilling survive the later slot perfectly well, because the thinking is recall and technique rather than construction. Families who get this the wrong way round conclude that tutoring does not work for their child, when what failed was the scheduling.

Saturday mornings are the lever almost nobody pulls. In Al Nahda households the week's commitments cluster on Friday and on Saturday afternoon, which leaves Saturday from nine until noon free and the student at their best. A ninety-minute Saturday session for new teaching, paired with a short weekday practice slot, is the schedule we recommend most often for Year 10 and Year 11 science in this district. It also survives a bad week, because an unexpected school event rarely lands on Saturday morning.

The table below gives the shape of the day across this cluster. Finish times vary by school and by year group and are given as the band families report rather than as a published figure, so confirm your own school's time on its calendar. What is worth noticing is the spread: the earliest and latest finishes in this cluster are about ninety minutes apart, which is enough that a single district-wide tutoring slot cannot work for everyone.

sections.heading: Three separate sciences, or co-ordinated? The entry decides the tutoring
paragraphs: Before buying any science tutoring, establish what your child is entered for. The question sounds administrative and it is the single most consequential fact in the plan. A student entered for Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences sits a double award covering all three sciences in reduced depth. A student entered for separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics sits three qualifications and six or more papers. The content lists are different, the paper structures are different, and revising the wrong one wastes the whole term.

Schools do not always make this visible to parents. A report card that says Science with a single grade may describe either route. The reliable test is the entry code, which the examinations officer can give you in a sentence: Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 for separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics, or 0654 for Co-ordinated Sciences, with the equivalent Pearson Edexcel codes being 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Ask for the codes and the tier, and the tutoring plan writes itself.

The decision also has consequences past 16, which is why it is worth revisiting rather than accepting. Separate sciences at Extended tier keep the Diploma Higher Level and A Level science routes open. Co-ordinated science keeps most other routes open and reduces the weekly load substantially, which for a student whose strengths are elsewhere is a sensible trade rather than a demotion. What does not work is a student on a combined route whose family assumes a Higher Level science is still straightforwardly available two years later.

Where tutoring helps most is different on each route. On separate sciences the gain is usually depth in one subject, taken one at a time, because three simultaneous science tutors produce a student with no evenings. On a co-ordinated route the gain is usually breadth and paper technique, because the content per topic is thinner and the marks are lost in how questions are read rather than in what is known.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: find out which, because the papers differ
paragraphs: Two boards dominate IGCSE science in this part of Dubai, and they do not examine identically. Cambridge International runs IGCSE with a Core and Extended tier structure in several subjects and offers separate practical routes. Pearson Edexcel runs its International GCSE sciences untiered, with its own paper structure. Both are accepted by universities and both appear within a few hundred metres of each other in Al Nahda, because the schools here made independent choices.

A tutor who teaches the wrong board gets most of the content right and the specifics wrong, and the specifics are where the marks are. Question styles differ, the way practical skills are examined differs, and the balance between recall and application differs. A student drilled on one board's past papers for a term will walk into the other board's paper and find the phrasing unfamiliar at exactly the moment unfamiliarity is most expensive.

There is a second detail that catches UAE families specifically. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. If you are checking dates yourself, get the zone from your child's examinations officer first. Pearson publishes its own timetables, including provisional ones ahead of each series, so always read the live official document rather than a date restated on a tutoring page.

The table lists the codes families in this cluster most often turn out to be entered for. Treat it as a prompt for the one email you need to send to the examinations officer, not as a statement about your child's school. The codes are what make the rest of the plan correct.

sections.heading: How practical science is examined when the lab is at school and the tutor is on screen
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how practical work can be tutored over video. The answer is that the practical component is an examined skill set rather than a set of experiments, and the skills are taught on paper far more efficiently than in a lab. Students are asked to identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, read instruments to an appropriate precision, record results in a table with correct headings and units, plot a graph with a sensible scale, spot an anomalous point and say what to do about it, and suggest an improvement to a method that is specific rather than generic.

Every one of those is examinable from a written description of an experiment the student has never performed, which is exactly how the alternative-to-practical route works. Over a shared screen, a tutor can put an unfamiliar method in front of a student, ask them to identify the flaw, and mark the answer against the published criteria in the same session. That cycle, repeated six or seven times, moves performance on this component more than any amount of time holding a burette.

The commonest lost marks here are specific and easy to name. Students write improve accuracy instead of naming the measurement to repeat. They plot a graph with an awkward scale that costs a mark before any data is read. They record a result to a precision the instrument does not support. They identify an anomaly and then include it in the line of best fit anyway. None of these is a knowledge gap, and none of them needs a laboratory to fix.

Check which practical route your child's school uses, because it changes what to practise. Some centres enter candidates for a hands-on practical paper and others for the written alternative, and the preparation differs. The school's examinations officer will tell you in one line, and that one line determines whether the tutoring should focus on apparatus handling and observation recording or on the written analysis of somebody else's method.

sections.heading: The exam series counted backwards from an Al Nahda evening
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market counts the calendar backwards, and it is the most useful thing a parent can be given. UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, and a page that tells a Dubai family otherwise has handed them a date they might act on. Within the June and November structure, every meaningful deadline sits months before the paper, which is why families who start planning in the spring have already missed several decisions.

Dates are set by the board and revised, so the only safe instruction is to read the live official timetable. What can be stated usefully is the pattern. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking facts, and they tell you how long the gap between paper and result actually is.

Working backwards from that pattern gives an Al Nahda family a usable plan. Final entries close long before the papers, and the entry decision includes tier and specification, so it is the point at which a mistaken co-ordinated-versus-separate entry becomes permanent. School mocks typically fall a term ahead of the series and are the best available predictor. The practical or alternative-to-practical paper has its own preparation and is usually the component families notice last. The resit route is the other series, which for a June candidate means November and a result in January.

The table sets this out as milestones rather than dates, with who controls each one. Add your own school's internal dates from its calendar, and the plan stops being guesswork. The one date worth writing on the fridge is the final entry deadline, because it is the only one that cannot be recovered afterwards.

sections.heading: Ramadan, UAE term dates and the revision weeks you actually have
paragraphs: The UAE academic calendar does not distribute revision time evenly, and Al Nahda families feel this more than most because many run a household on Ramadan hours while children sit British-curriculum exams on a European calendar. School days shorten during Ramadan, energy patterns shift, and the useful study window moves from late afternoon to after Iftar. Pretending otherwise produces a revision plan that collapses in week two.

The practical adjustment is straightforward once it is planned rather than improvised. Sessions move to a post-Iftar slot, typically from around 8.30pm, and they get shorter and more focused: forty-five minutes of past-paper work rather than ninety minutes of new content. New teaching moves to the weekend mornings, which stay workable. Students who shift deliberately lose almost nothing; students who try to hold a 5pm weekday slot through Ramadan lose a month.

The second calendar feature worth planning around is the Sharjah boundary. Al Nahda families frequently hold a school place on one side of the line and an address on the other. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA; Sharjah private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Term dates and mock windows are not guaranteed to align, so revision pacing has to follow your own school rather than the neighbourhood pattern.

Travel is the third factor. Many households in this district spend part of the summer and part of the winter break abroad, which is an opportunity rather than a problem when lessons are delivered over video: a session can follow the family and continue through a trip, which is impossible for any arrangement that depends on somebody arriving at a UAE address. Tell us the travel dates at the start and the plan absorbs them instead of breaking around them.

sections.heading: What a term of IGCSE science costs in this market, monthly first
paragraphs: Parents think in months, not in hours, so start there. Advertised monthly packages in the Dubai market run at around AED 799 for eight online sessions, and at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's rate survey puts monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those bands are the honest frame for a decision; the hourly figures underneath them are useful mainly for comparing like with like.

Converted to hours, the same market reads as follows. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at about AED 200 to 450, TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one, which carries travel inside the rate, is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. Every figure here is a market rate attributed to whoever published it, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

For a timetabling problem the monthly comparison is the one that exposes the real trade. Eight online sessions a month at the mid band and four two-hour in-home sessions a month cost roughly the same, but the first gives eight contact points spread across the week and the second gives four long ones that must survive Dubai traffic. For IGCSE science, where the gain comes from frequent short practice rather than from long teaching blocks, the eight-point pattern usually wins on the same budget.

One piece of context worth holding. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Household education spending is therefore flat on the school line this year, which is the right moment to decide deliberately what the tutoring line should be rather than letting it accumulate by the hour.

sections.heading: Three schedules that survive a real Al Nahda term
paragraphs: The first schedule suits a Year 10 student who is coping but drifting. One ninety-minute Saturday morning session for new content, aligned to the school's scheme of work, plus one forty-five-minute weekday slot in the later window for past-paper questions. Two contact points, under three hours a week, and the weekday slot can be moved without destroying the plan because the teaching has already happened on Saturday.

The second suits a Year 11 student with a specific weakness in one science. A dated block of eight to ten sessions, twice a week in the later window, aimed at one subject and one paper. The block is scoped at the start against the school's mock dates, with an honest assessment of what is recoverable in the time. When it ends, it ends; families who want to continue decide then rather than drifting into an open commitment.

The third suits a student taking three separate sciences who is overloaded rather than weak. Here the intervention is sequencing rather than teaching: one science at a time, four weeks each, in rotation, so that no week ever contains three science tutors. This is the schedule we recommend most often to Al Nahda families with a strong student on the separate-science route, and the one parents are most surprised by, because the instinct is to add hours when the real problem is that the week has none left.

Whichever shape fits, two rules hold. Protect the evening meal, because sessions scheduled across it get cancelled and cancelled sessions kill momentum. And decide the Ramadan arrangement in advance rather than in week one, moving to a shorter post-Iftar slot and pushing new teaching to the weekend. A schedule that anticipates the year it has to survive is worth more than a schedule that is ideal in October.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE science session realistically start in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: Later than most parents plan for. Schools in this cluster finish between about 2pm and 3.30pm, a bus route through Al Qusais and Al Nahda adds twenty to forty minutes, and changing, eating and the school's own homework take until roughly 4.45pm. That gives a usable early window of about 5pm to 6.30pm for new content and a second window from about 7.30pm to 9pm for practice. Saturday morning from nine until noon is the strongest slot of the week and the one most families overlook entirely.

faqs.question: Is Saturday morning really better than a weekday evening for science tutoring?
faqs.answer: For teaching new content, usually yes. The student is rested, nothing else is competing for the slot, and in most Al Nahda households Saturday afternoon and Friday carry the week's commitments while Saturday morning is free. The pattern we recommend most often is a ninety-minute Saturday session for new material plus a short weekday slot in the later window for past papers. It also survives a bad week, because an unexpected school event rarely falls on a Saturday morning.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits separate sciences or co-ordinated science?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer for the entry codes. Cambridge uses 0610 for Biology, 0620 for Chemistry and 0625 for Physics as separate qualifications, and 0654 for Co-ordinated Sciences as a double award; the Pearson Edexcel equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. A report card showing a single Science grade can describe either route, so the code is the only reliable answer. Get it before buying tutoring, because revising separate-science content for a co-ordinated paper wastes an entire term.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to our flat in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE science tuition for an Al Nahda family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for diagrams, calculations and marked past papers. For a scheduling problem this tight that is an advantage rather than a compromise: a 5pm slot begins at 5pm whatever Al Nahda Road is doing, and the session follows the family if they travel.

faqs.question: Can practical science be taught without a lab at home?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the practical component examines skills rather than experiments. Students are assessed on identifying variables, reading instruments to an appropriate precision, tabulating with correct headings and units, choosing a sensible graph scale, spotting anomalies and suggesting specific improvements to a method. Every one of those is examinable from a written description of an experiment nobody performed, which is exactly how the alternative-to-practical route works. Over a shared screen a tutor can set an unfamiliar method, mark the answer against the criteria and repeat the cycle weekly.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Al Nahda sit?
faqs.answer: The June series or the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so it does not apply to a UAE candidate. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Read the live official timetable rather than a date quoted on any tutoring page, and at Cambridge get your centre's zone from the examinations officer first.

faqs.question: Does the exam timetable differ depending on which centre my child sits at?
faqs.answer: Because every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. For a family checking dates independently this is the detail that matters: ask your child's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in, then read that version of the timetable from Cambridge's own site rather than a copy elsewhere.

faqs.question: How long after the papers do IGCSE results arrive?
faqs.answer: Longer than families expect, and it differs by series. As published facts: Pearson Edexcel June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. So a June candidate waits roughly two and a half months and a November candidate about two months. Knowing the date in advance matters because the resit route is the other series, which is a decision with its own deadline.

faqs.question: Which science do Al Nahda families ask for most, and why?
faqs.answer: Chemistry, by a clear margin, and almost always for the same reason: moles. Reacting-mass and concentration calculations are the first point in the course where a student cannot pass by remembering, and a child who has coasted on recall through Year 9 meets a genuine wall. The other two recurring requests are electrolysis, where products end up assigned to the wrong electrode, and ionic equations with charges left unbalanced. All three are fixable in a handful of sessions once the underlying arithmetic is secure.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover biology, chemistry and physics together?
faqs.answer: Some can, and at co-ordinated-science level that often works well because the content per topic is thinner and the gains come from paper technique that transfers across all three. On the separate-science route it is usually the wrong plan. Depth in Extended-tier chemistry and depth in Extended-tier physics are different specialisms, and a tutor stretched across both tends to teach the one they know better. For separate sciences we normally suggest one subject at a time, four weeks each, in rotation.

faqs.question: What happens to science tutoring during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It moves rather than stops. School days shorten, energy patterns change, and the usable study window shifts to after Iftar, typically from around 8.30pm. Sessions get shorter and more focused, forty-five minutes of past-paper work rather than ninety minutes of new teaching, and new content moves to weekend mornings, which stay workable throughout. Decide this before Ramadan rather than during week one. Families who plan the shift lose almost nothing; families who try to defend a 5pm weekday slot lose most of a month.

faqs.question: How much should I budget each month for IGCSE science tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The market's own monthly figures are the clearest guide. Advertised packages run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's survey puts weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240 to 600 monthly at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. These are market rates attributed to their publishers and read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices; the trial lesson costs nothing.

faqs.question: Is a weekly hour enough, or does my child need two?
faqs.answer: One weekly session is enough for a student who understands the content and loses marks on technique, because the learning happens in the practice between lessons and an hour leaves room for it. Two sessions suit a real content gap, or a Year 11 student working through a specific paper under a deadline. Beyond two hours a week the limiting factor stops being teaching time and becomes independent practice, so additional hours buy less and less. Frequent short sessions beat occasional long ones in science.

faqs.question: Our school is in Sharjah but we live in Al Nahda. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: For planning, yes. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, while Sharjah private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The two emirates do not guarantee identical term dates, so mock windows and half-terms can fall in different weeks. Tell us which school your child attends and revision is paced to its calendar. A tutor whose other students are all on the opposite side of the boundary may otherwise revise to the wrong week.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic education count towards the equivalency subject total?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is wrong. Verify the current rule through the Ministry of Education's own channel before acting; IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: What should I ask before booking a science tutor in this area?
faqs.answer: Six questions. Which board and specification do you teach, and at which tier? Which practical route does my child's school use, and have you prepared students for that route? Which papers will you work through before the mock? What happens in the session when my child cannot do something? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid for two years? And can we trial the slot I actually intend to use, rather than a convenient one? Vague answers to any of these are the signal.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-nahda.closingHeading: Start with the timetable, then book the tutor
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-nahda.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE science tutor in Al Nahda, send three things: your child's school, the entry codes from the examinations officer, and what time the school day actually ends. From those we will propose a schedule that fits the real afternoon in this district rather than an idealised one, with new teaching in the early window or on Saturday morning and practice later in the evening. The trial lesson is free, runs in the slot you intend to keep, and needs no card details. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and if the slot turns out not to work we move it rather than defend it.

intro.heading: IGCSE science is three different qualifications, not one subject
paragraphs: Parents in Al Quoz searching for an IGCSE science tutor are usually responding to a particular kind of trouble. The grades are fine in one science and poor in another, or they are mediocre across all three, and the student says the honest thing: there is too much of it. That is not a complaint about ability. It is an accurate description of a breadth problem, and breadth problems are solved by sequencing rather than by working harder.

The first thing to establish is which award your child is sitting, because Dubai schools use three different routes and families often do not know which one applies. Separate sciences means three full IGCSEs, in Biology, Chemistry and Physics, with three sets of papers. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences, 0654, gives two awards covering all three sciences. Cambridge Combined Science, 0653, gives one. The content depth, the number of papers and the post-16 doors differ in each case.

The second thing is how practical work is assessed, which surprises families coming from systems with laboratory examinations. In these qualifications practical skills are examined on paper. A student has to describe a method precisely enough for a stranger to repeat it, identify variables, read apparatus correctly and evaluate a procedure, all in writing. That is a trainable writing skill rather than a laboratory one, and it is routinely the weakest paper in the set.

The third is sequencing. Three sciences, or one award covering three, cannot be revised simultaneously in the eight weeks before a series. Students who try end up with uneven coverage and a predictable gap in whichever science was taught first and revised last. A deliberate rotation, with timed papers in each science at planned intervals, is worth more than any amount of additional study time applied without a plan.

Al Quoz itself contributes one practical constraint worth planning around. The district holds its housing in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3 between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, with the rest given to warehouses, workshops, showrooms and the Alserkal Avenue arts spaces, and children travel outwards to school in several directions. A weekday session realistically starts between 5pm and 5.30pm rather than the 4.30pm that districts with schools inside them manage, which in a three-science household usually means one slot has to sit at the weekend.

The premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one IGCSE science tuition into Al Quoz homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, with working and diagrams shared and annotated on screen. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run in India only. For a household running three sciences that is useful in a specific way, because three different specialists can take three different evenings without three cars crossing Al Khail Road.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-quoz.subjectsIntro: Science support in Al Quoz is organised by where the marks go. Below are the areas across the three sciences that most often need work, each with the error that recurs in marked scripts.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and exchange
subjects.description: Diffusion, osmosis, circulation and gas exchange. Marks go on explanations that describe a structure without linking it to the function the question asked about, which is the single most common biology failure across both boards.

subjects.name: Biology: inheritance and variation
subjects.description: Genetic crosses, variation and selection. Students lose marks by producing a correct Punnett square without stating the ratio or the probability the question requested, and by using the words gene and allele interchangeably in written answers.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The arithmetic underneath most of the chemistry marks. Errors are almost never conceptual: a ratio inverted, a limiting reagent ignored, or units dropped partway through a multi-step calculation that was otherwise sound.

subjects.name: Chemistry: rates, energetics and equilibrium
subjects.description: Collision theory, exothermic and endothermic changes and reversible reactions. The characteristic error is predicting correctly and then explaining the prediction by restating it, instead of by reference to the change that caused it.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and analysis
subjects.description: Homologous series, basic reactions and identification tests. Answers that name a correct product without the balanced equation, or a correct test without its observation, score nothing in most schemes even when the chemistry was understood.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The topic Al Quoz students name most often. The difficulty is reasoning rather than recall: saying what happens to current and potential difference when one component changes requires holding the whole circuit in mind, and no formula substitutes for that.

subjects.name: Physics: waves and energy
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, the electromagnetic spectrum and energy transfer. Diagrams are marked on specified features, so a qualitatively correct ray diagram without the labelled angles or normal line loses most of its marks.

subjects.name: Practical skills on paper
subjects.description: Describing a method reproducibly, identifying independent, dependent and control variables, reading apparatus and evaluating a procedure. Reliably the weakest paper in the set, and the most improvable, because it is a writing skill with a finite set of conventions.

subjects.name: Command terms across the sciences
subjects.description: Describe, explain, suggest, compare and evaluate each demand a different response shape, and a correct fact in the wrong shape earns nothing. Because the conventions are shared across all three sciences, fixing this once pays three times over.

subjects.name: Data handling and graphs
subjects.description: Tables, graph plotting, line of best fit, gradients and conclusions supported by the data. Shared across the sciences, frequently taught in a hurry in each one separately, and therefore the most efficient single block of work available.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE science tutor in Al Quoz must confirm first
paragraphs: An IGCSE science tutor in Al Quoz means one-to-one science teaching at home on a weekday evening. IB Gram delivers that as a live online session into Al Quoz homes on Gulf Standard Time, with diagrams and working shared and annotated on screen. No tutor is sent to a UAE address, because in-person home visits are a service we run only in India.

Three things have to be established before any teaching is useful, and the first is the award. Separate sciences, Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 and Cambridge Combined Science 0653 are three different qualifications with different papers and different content depth. A tutor practising separate-science past papers with a Combined Science candidate is teaching material that will not appear, which wastes the block and damages confidence at the same time.

The second is the board and the tier. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers, assess practical skills differently and use different tier vocabulary. Departments choose independently, so a single student can sit Cambridge for one science and Edexcel for another. The code is printed on the school's assessment paperwork and the subject teacher will confirm it in a line.

The third is which of the three sciences is actually the problem, and the answer is frequently none of them individually. A student losing marks on command terms or on practical method writing loses them in all three subjects, which looks like general science weakness and is one fixable convention. Reading two marked scripts from different sciences usually makes that obvious within minutes, and it changes the plan from three blocks to one.

sections.heading: Separate sciences, Coordinated and Combined compared
paragraphs: This comparison is absent from every competitor page researched for this market, which is surprising, because it is the decision that most shapes a Dubai student's science outcome. The three routes differ in how many qualifications are awarded, how deep the content goes, how many papers are sat and what remains possible at 16.

The post-16 column is the one families should read first and usually read last. A Combined Science award does not position a student for A Level Biology, Chemistry or Physics, or for the equivalent IB Higher Level courses, regardless of the grade achieved. Coordinated Sciences sits in between and should be discussed explicitly with the school rather than assumed either way. Separate sciences keep everything open at the cost of the heaviest examination load.

The load question is real and should not be dismissed. Three sciences in a timetable that also carries mathematics, English, the UAE mandatory subjects of Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and two or three options, is a lot of examined content for a fifteen-year-old. A student doing three sciences badly has worse options at 16 than a student doing Coordinated Sciences well, so the honest conversation is about capacity rather than ambition.

Whatever the route, the practice set must match it exactly. This is the most common avoidable error in science tutoring in Dubai: a well-meaning tutor working from separate-science papers with a Coordinated candidate, or from Extended papers with a Core entry. Confirm the award, the board and the tier before the first session, and ask the tutor to state which they are using.

sections.heading: Practical skills examined on paper
paragraphs: Families arriving from systems with laboratory examinations are frequently surprised by this, and the surprise costs marks. In these qualifications practical skills are assessed in writing. The student describes a method, identifies variables, reads apparatus from a diagram, processes data and evaluates a procedure, all on paper, with no equipment in front of them.

That makes it a writing skill with a finite set of conventions, which is good news, because finite skills can be taught to completion. The method must be reproducible: a stranger reading it should be able to repeat the experiment without asking a question. Variables must be named as independent, dependent and controlled, not merely mentioned. Readings must be given to the precision the apparatus supports. Evaluation must identify a specific weakness in this procedure rather than a generic limitation that would apply to any experiment.

It is reliably the weakest paper in the set, for a structural reason rather than through anyone's fault: it is the paper schools have least time to practise, because practising it properly means marking extended written answers rather than ticking right answers. Students therefore meet it in a mock, score poorly, and conclude they are weak at science.

Four sessions usually changes it substantially, and the gain applies across all three sciences at once because the conventions are shared. That makes it, along with command terms, the highest-return science work available to an Al Quoz family, and it requires no new content at all.

sections.heading: Sequencing three sciences in the weeks before a series
paragraphs: This is where most science revision fails, and it fails for an arithmetic reason rather than a motivational one. Three sciences cannot be revised simultaneously in eight weeks. A student who tries covers everything thinly, and the thinnest coverage lands on whichever science was taught first and therefore feels most distant.

A rotation fixes it, and the rotation has to be written down. The principle is simple: the weakest science gets the first slot and the last slot, each science gets a timed paper at planned intervals, and no science goes more than two weeks without contact. Writing it down matters because an unwritten plan silently becomes a plan to revise whichever subject feels most frightening this week, which is always the same subject.

The table below is a workable eight-week shape for a three-science student. Adapt it to your own school's mock window and entry dates, which the exams officer holds. For Cambridge, a candidate in Dubai sits the June series with November as the resit route, since the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May and June, and November, and both boards revise provisional timetables, so use the official live document.

One more rule, and it is the one students resist. The timed paper comes before the revision of that topic, not after. A paper taken cold tells you what to revise; a paper taken after revision tells you that you revised. The first is information and the second is reassurance, and only one of them changes a grade.

sections.heading: Three sciences, one budget
paragraphs: A household carrying three sciences can turn a reasonable hourly rate into an unreasonable monthly total very quickly, simply by buying one weekly session in each subject without asking whether that is what the problem needs. So this section compares approaches on monthly cost rather than on hourly rate.

The market, attributed and dated October 2026. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270. Budget online provision starts at Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

Now the comparison. Three weekly sessions, one per science, is the most expensive approach and frequently not the most effective, because in many cases the actual deficit is a shared convention rather than three separate content gaps. A single shared-skills block of four to six sessions costs roughly a third as much and improves all three subjects at once. Where one science genuinely needs content work, a targeted single-science block is added on top of that rather than instead of it.

For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year. Tutoring is the variable line in an education budget, and in a three-science year it is the line most likely to drift, which is why every block on this page has a stated end.

sections.heading: The science grade, equivalency and what comes at 16
paragraphs: Science entries do two separate jobs in the UAE, and families usually meet them months apart. The first is post-16 progression, already covered: depth of prior study decides what A Level and IB Higher Level sciences are available, and a shallower award closes routes regardless of the grade. The second is Ministry of Education equivalency, which decides what a UAE university or employer will accept.

The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Note what this means for science routes: a Combined Science award is one subject in that count, while separate sciences are three, which can matter for a student whose option choices are otherwise thin.

One competitor page currently ranking in this market tells UAE parents six IGCSE subjects are required. That is wrong, and it is the kind of error a family acts on by making a child sit an extra subject they did not need. The American track runs on test scores instead, with SAT Math 450 or above required before applying and English proficiency satisfied by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450. For the IB, no points threshold appears in the source we read, so none is published here.

Two cautions as always. IB Gram does not perform, submit or expedite equivalency and tutoring is not required for it; it is a process families complete through the official channel. And requirements change, so verify the current position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before planning a subject list around any figure.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Quoz, and the limits we state
paragraphs: Send five things: the award, the board and tier for each science, the school, and the last two marked scripts from two different sciences. That last detail matters, because comparing scripts across subjects is what reveals whether the deficit is shared or specific, and that single piece of information changes the plan from three blocks to one.

What will not be claimed. No grade promise, because no honest provider can make one. No suggestion that tutoring is required for equivalency, admission or progression, which would be a false claim about a regulatory process. No regulator or board approval: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office or centre. No satisfaction statistics, because a figure without its sample, date and method is decoration.

A disclosed limit: in the weeks before a series, early-evening slots are genuinely constrained, and a household wanting three different science specialists on three consecutive evenings is asking a lot of a peak window. When it cannot be done you are told, offered a workable alternative shape, and given a realistic view of when the slots open. Nobody general is substituted for a specialist you asked for.

Finally, two facts worth asking of any provider. Individuals offering private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with those operating without one subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted. And board past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents are Cambridge's and Pearson's copyright, so we cite and link them rather than supplying them as downloads.

process.title: Confirm the award before anything else
process.description: Separate sciences, Coordinated 0654 and Combined 0653 are three different qualifications with different papers and depths. Practising the wrong one wastes the block and dents confidence at the same time, and the school's assessment paperwork states which applies.

process.title: Send scripts from two different sciences
process.description: This is the step that saves the most money. If the same error appears in biology and in physics, the deficit is a shared convention and one block fixes three subjects. If the errors are unrelated, you have one topic problem in one science, which is also short.

process.title: Free trial lesson as a diagnosis
process.description: One live session with shared annotation before any payment. By the end you should know whether you are buying a shared-skills block, a single-science repair or both, and roughly how many sessions each needs.

process.title: Write the rotation down
process.description: Three sciences need a written rotation with timed papers at planned intervals, because an unwritten plan quietly becomes a plan to revise whichever subject feels most alarming this week. Weakest science first and last; nothing left untouched for more than two weeks.

process.title: Verify with a timed paper, then stop
process.description: Each block ends with a paper under examination conditions in the subject worked on. If the logged error has gone, stopping is the right recommendation. A three-science household is where open-ended arrangements become expensive fastest.

whyPoints.title: The award is established first
whyPoints.description: Separate sciences, Coordinated 0654 and Combined 0653 differ in depth, papers and post-16 position. No competitor page researched for this market compares them, and practising the wrong route's papers is the most common avoidable error in Dubai science tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Shared deficits found before separate ones
whyPoints.description: Command terms, practical method writing and graph conventions are shared across biology, chemistry and physics. Fixing one convention improves three subjects, which is why scripts from two different sciences are worth more than two scripts from one.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Practical skills are examined in writing, with a finite set of conventions: reproducible method, classified variables, justified precision, specific evaluation. It is reliably the weakest paper in the set and among the most improvable.

whyPoints.title: Rotation instead of simultaneous revision
whyPoints.description: Three sciences cannot be revised at once in eight weeks, and the gap always lands on whichever was taught first. A written rotation with cold timed papers at intervals prevents the predictable failure.

whyPoints.title: Costs compared monthly, with sources
whyPoints.description: Indicative monthly AED figures from Bestimate's 2026 estimates and providers' published rates, dated October 2026, set against what each approach achieves rather than against an unnamed competitor.

whyPoints.title: The equivalency arithmetic stated correctly
whyPoints.description: Five GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 excluding Arabic and Islamic education, with Combined Science counting as one subject and separate sciences as three. A ranking competitor publishes six subjects, which is wrong.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Combined, Coordinated and separate sciences?
faqs.answer: They are three different qualifications. Separate sciences give three full IGCSEs with three paper sets and the deepest content. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 gives two awards covering all three sciences at intermediate depth. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 gives a single award at the shallowest depth. The post-16 consequence is the important part: a Combined award does not position a student for A Level or IB Higher Level sciences regardless of the grade, and Coordinated should be discussed explicitly with the school.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor come to our Al Quoz home?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach IGCSE science one-to-one into Al Quoz homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with diagrams and working annotated on a shared screen, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. For a household running three sciences this helps in a specific way: three specialists can take three evenings without three cars crossing Al Khail Road at five o'clock.

faqs.question: Our child has never sat a lab exam. What does the practical paper test?
faqs.answer: Practical skills in these qualifications are examined on paper, not in a laboratory session, so online tutoring and school laboratory work serve different purposes. The paper asks the student to describe a method reproducibly, classify independent, dependent and controlled variables, read apparatus to the correct precision, process data and evaluate a specific weakness in the procedure. That is a writing skill with finite conventions, and it is both the weakest paper in most sets and among the most improvable.

faqs.question: My child is weak across all three sciences. Do we need three tutors?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and finding out is free. Send marked scripts from two different sciences. If the same error appears in both, such as describing where the question said explain, or a method that assumes the reader was present, the deficit is a shared convention and one block of four to six sessions improves all three subjects. If the errors are unrelated, you have one topic problem in one science, which is a three to five session fix. Either answer is cheaper than three weekly sessions.

faqs.question: How should three sciences be revised in the final eight weeks?
faqs.answer: On a written rotation, never simultaneously. The weakest science takes the first slot and the last, each science gets a timed paper at planned intervals, and nothing goes more than two weeks without contact. Write it down, because an unwritten plan becomes a plan to revise whichever subject feels most alarming this week, which is always the same one. And take the timed paper before revising that topic, not after: a cold paper is information, a revised one is reassurance.

faqs.question: Which science topic causes the most trouble in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: Electricity and circuits in physics, consistently. The difficulty is reasoning rather than recall: saying what happens to current and potential difference when one component changes requires holding the whole circuit in mind, and a student who has memorised every relationship can still fail that question. Chemistry's equivalent is moles and stoichiometry, where errors are almost always a ratio inverted or a limiting reagent ignored. Biology's is explanation that describes a structure without linking it to function.

faqs.question: Is Combined Science a problem for a child who might want medicine?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a conversation to have before the entry is confirmed rather than in Year 12. A Combined Science award does not position a student for A Level Biology or Chemistry, or for the equivalent IB Higher Level courses, and medical and related applications commonly expect chemistry at Higher Level or A Level alongside biology. If that pathway is a genuine possibility, the route conversation belongs with the head of science now, with the honest capacity question included.

faqs.question: Does the exam board matter for IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal in Year 11. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers, weight topics differently, use different tier vocabulary and frame practical skills assessment differently, even where the content overlaps heavily. Departments choose independently, so a single student can sit Cambridge for one science and Edexcel for another. Check the code per science on the school's assessment paperwork, and ask any prospective tutor which codes they are building practice from.

faqs.question: What does science tutoring cost monthly for a three-science student?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the deficit is shared or specific, which is why diagnosis is the first step. A shared-skills block of four to six sessions over six weeks runs roughly AED 600 to 1,200 monthly at mid-market rates. A single-science targeted block of three to five sessions is similar. Both together, in an examination year, runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more per Bestimate's 2026 estimates. Three separate weekly sessions is the most expensive option and often not the most effective.

faqs.question: Does my child really need to classify variables explicitly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the marks say so. Mentioning a variable is not the same as naming it independent, dependent or controlled, and schemes frequently award the mark only for the classification. The same applies to evaluation: a generic statement about human error earns nothing, while naming a specific weakness in this procedure and what it did to the result earns the mark. These are conventions rather than insights, and a student can learn all of them in four sessions.

faqs.question: Can we start science support partway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families do, but the work has to be targeted rather than broad. Pick the shared conventions first, because they pay across three subjects immediately, then one topic per science from the marked scripts. What a mid-year start cannot do is cover three sciences comprehensively, so the honest plan secures the achievable grades rather than chasing complete coverage. The rotation table on this page is the shape to adapt to whatever weeks remain.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects count towards UAE equivalency if we take Combined Science?
faqs.answer: Combined Science is a single award and therefore one subject in the count, while separate sciences give three. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. That arithmetic matters for a student whose option choices are otherwise thin, and it should be verified on moe.gov.ae before it is planned around.

faqs.question: Is the November series available if June goes badly in a science?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run a November series, and for a candidate sitting in Dubai that is the resit route; the February and March series is offered to India only. A November attempt is easier to plan than a first attempt, because you have the actual script and grade and can identify the two or three topics that cost it. Entry is arranged by the school's exams officer and is worth discussing as soon as results arrive.

faqs.question: Should the weakest science get all the attention?
faqs.answer: It should get the most, not all of it. Put the weakest science in the first and last slots of the rotation and give it the repeat contact, but do not let either of the others go more than two weeks without a session or a timed paper, because the gap that appears in a results sheet is usually in the subject that felt safe. The arithmetic of three sciences is unforgiving: attention withdrawn entirely from one is a grade withdrawn from one.
