intro.heading: What science tuition costs around Al Quoz 4, and what it buys
paragraphs: A family in Al Quoz 4 asking about IGCSE science tuition will be quoted anything from AED 45 to AED 650 an hour depending on who answers the phone. Nothing on most providers' pages explains the spread, and three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all. One of them asks the cost question in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. That is not a pricing strategy; it is a reason to make the first call elsewhere.

The spread is real and it maps onto something. At the bottom sits a university student working through set homework with your child. At the top sits a scarce specialist in the final term before an exam series. Both are legitimate purchases and they solve different problems. The expensive mistake is buying the first when the problem needs the second, or the second when the problem was never academic in the first place.

Where money gets wasted in this neighbourhood follows a pattern. Families pay for general science support when the mark loss is concentrated in one paper. They pay for two-hour sessions because the package was sold that way, when a fifteen-year-old loses focus at seventy minutes. They pay a travel premium for a tutor crossing Dubai to reach Al Quoz 4 and attribute the higher rate to higher quality. And they pay for months of topic revision while leaving the alternative-to-practical paper, worth a fifth of the grade, entirely untouched.

On delivery, the honest position: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Science lessons for Al Quoz 4 families are delivered live online, one-to-one, with a shared whiteboard and a camera on the student's working. The cost consequence is straightforward. An hour of teaching stays an hour of teaching rather than an hour of teaching plus ninety minutes of driving that somebody has to pay for.

What makes the biggest difference to a bill is not the hourly rate but the diagnosis. A student entered for Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 who is losing most of their marks on Paper 6 needs perhaps six focused sessions, not a year of weekly lessons. A student who has been placed on Core when they could manage Extended needs a conversation with the school rather than a tutor. Both of those save a family real money, and neither is a conversation most providers are keen to have.

Dubai context helps too. KHDA figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula, with UK curriculum the largest share of enrolment. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. For many households the flat school bill is exactly what makes a weekly science session affordable, which is worth knowing when planning a two-year spend rather than a monthly one.

sections.heading: Five ways science tuition money is wasted in this neighbourhood
paragraphs: The first and largest waste is buying a subject when the problem is a paper. A Cambridge science grade is 30% multiple choice, 50% theory and 20% practical or alternative to practical. A student losing most of their marks on Paper 6 does not need a year of topic revision; they need six sessions on apparatus diagrams, variable control and table conventions. Families routinely spend ten times what the fix requires because nobody looked at the component breakdown.

The second is the wrong board. Cambridge and Pearson structure their papers differently and assess practical skills differently. A tutor drilling Cambridge 0625 past papers with a student entered for Pearson 4PH1 is teaching real physics and the wrong exam. Ask the school which board each science is entered with, and do not assume it is the same for all three, because frequently it is not.

The third is session length sold as value. Two-hour sessions appear in several published packages in this market. A fifteen-year-old's useful attention in a one-to-one science session runs to about seventy minutes, and the final fifty are mostly expensive company. Two sixty-minute sessions on separate days produce more than one two-hour block at the same cost, and the research on spacing has said so for a long time.

The fourth is paying a travel premium and reading it as quality. The in-home band sits above the equivalent online band because somebody is driving to Al Quoz 4 in late-afternoon traffic. That is a real cost and it is honestly charged, but it buys a journey. The fifth waste is the slowest: continuing a weekly arrangement for a year after the original problem was solved, because nobody set an exit point. A block with a defined end is cheaper than an open arrangement with good intentions.

sections.heading: The papers you are actually paying to improve
paragraphs: A Cambridge science entry at Extended tier is three papers. The multiple-choice paper carries 30% of the grade, the theory paper 50%, and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper 20%. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 follows the same pattern as Papers 2, 4 and 6. Those three numbers should govern where tuition money goes, and in practice they almost never do.

The theory paper deserves the largest share because it carries half the grade, but it is also the component where improvement is slowest, since it rewards accumulated content across the whole syllabus. The multiple-choice paper responds faster than families expect: much of the mark loss there is misreading the stem or eliminating two options and guessing between the remaining pair, and both are trainable in a few timed sets with every wrong option reviewed rather than just the right one identified.

The practical component is the one with the best return per hour spent. It tests a limited and highly predictable set of skills: drawing apparatus correctly, identifying independent and controlled variables, setting out a results table, plotting and reading a graph, and suggesting a specific improvement rather than a generic one. Students are rarely taught these as skills in their own right, which means the marks are sitting there for anyone who spends six sessions on them.

Tier choice sits underneath all of this. Core and Extended are different papers with different grade ceilings. A student placed on Core who could cope with Extended has had their maximum grade decided for them, and that decision is reviewable with the school while there is still time. It is the one conversation that can change an outcome without any tuition spend at all, and it is worth having before signing up for anything.

sections.heading: Paper 6 is where the cheap marks are
paragraphs: If a family in Al Quoz 4 can only afford a short block of science tuition, the alternative-to-practical paper is where to spend it. It is worth 20% of a Cambridge science grade, it tests a narrow and repetitive skill set, and it is the component schools have least curriculum time for, because practical lessons are usually spent doing the practical rather than rehearsing how it would be written up in an exam.

The question types recur almost without variation. Draw the apparatus you would use. Name the independent variable and two variables to keep constant. Complete the results table with appropriate headings and units. Plot the points and draw a line of best fit. Read a value from the graph. State one source of error and one specific improvement. A student who has practised each of those a dozen times answers them quickly and accurately, and a student who has not loses marks on every one.

The traps are small and consistent. Apparatus drawn in perspective rather than as a labelled section. Variables confused with measurements. A table with units in the cells rather than the header. A line of best fit drawn through the first and last points rather than through the trend. An improvement stated as 'repeat the experiment' or 'be more careful', neither of which earns a mark. Each of these is a correctable habit, not a gap in understanding.

For a student sitting the practical test rather than the alternative, the same skills apply with the added pressure of doing them in a room under time. The teaching is similar; the rehearsal differs. Either way, a block aimed squarely at this component is the clearest example in IGCSE science of a small spend with a measurable, predictable effect on a grade.

sections.heading: The journey, priced: online against in-home for Al Quoz 4
paragraphs: This page targets a search that assumes a tutor arriving in person, so the comparison should be made properly rather than avoided. In-home science tuition in Dubai is a real market with real practitioners. It costs more per hour at the same quality tier, and the difference is the drive. For Al Quoz 4, which sits in a mainly commercial district with few resident tutors, nearly every in-home quote is a travel quote.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; home tutoring is an India-only service. Every lesson for a family here runs live online, one-to-one. The reason is partly cost and mostly supply: once the radius narrows to a tutor who can reach Al Quoz 4 by five o'clock, the person available is whoever is available, and for a specific Pearson science specification that is often nobody suitable.

The practical difference in a science lesson is smaller than people expect. A shared whiteboard handles apparatus diagrams and graph work better than paper, because both people can draw on the same figure. A camera on the student's written answers gives the tutor the same view a tutor at the table would have. The school lab remains the school lab in both cases; no visiting tutor brings one.

What online removes from the bill is the travel premium, and what it removes from the week is the risk. A session at 17:00 that depends on a drive from the other side of the city is a session that will be late sometimes. A session at 17:00 that depends on a laptop is not. Over a two-year IGCSE run, that reliability is worth more than most families estimate in advance.

sections.heading: Two years of science, costed in context
paragraphs: A family planning IGCSE science spend should look at the two-year figure rather than the hourly rate, because that is the decision actually being made. One weekly hour of mid-market online tuition across Years 10 and 11, excluding holidays, is on the order of AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month on Bestimate's estimates. Specialist exam-year support in Year 11 runs higher, AED 1,000 to over AED 2,000 a month. A finite component block is a fraction of either.

That sits against a school bill that is not rising this year: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Private provision in the emirate is also expanding, with seven new private schools and 16,846 new places announced for the 2026-27 intake and enrolment up 6% during 2025-26.

There are costs beyond tuition worth putting on the same page. Exam entry fees are payable through the school or, for a private candidate, through an exam centre, and they vary by board and subject count. Resit entries for the November series are a separate fee. Past papers and the syllabus document itself are published free by the boards, and no tutor should be charging for them or supplying copies; the correct route is to reference and link the official page.

Set against those, the most cost-effective interventions are unglamorous. Review the tier entry with the school. Confirm the board for each science. Spend a short block on the practical component. Then, if a weekly arrangement is still needed, set a review point at the end of a term rather than letting it run. A family that does those four things usually spends less and sees more movement than one that signs up for a year on the first phone call.

sections.heading: Permits, paperwork and what to ask before paying a deposit
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE operates under a permit regime. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through its app, website or e-services. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published; Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify amounts, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different matter and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific thing issued to specific organisations and should never be implied by a platform that does not hold one. IB Gram does not.

Before paying a deposit, four questions are worth asking any science tutor. Which board and syllabus code has your child's school entered them for, and have you taught it? Which component do you think the marks are being lost on, and what evidence are you using? What is the agreed end point of this arrangement? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit? A provider who answers the second question with a testimonial rather than a component is telling you something useful.

One further caution worth stating because competitors in this market breach it: no tutor may write, complete or produce assessed coursework, and no tutor should be supplying board-published past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Reference them and link the official source. A service offering to produce a student's work is selling them a malpractice finding, and the consequence lands on the child.

process.title: Confirm the board and the code
process.description: Get the syllabus code for each science from the school's entry list: 0610, 0620, 0625, 0654 for Cambridge, or 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4SD0 for Pearson. Tutoring priced before this is tutoring priced blind, and drilling the wrong board's papers is the most common avoidable waste.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a description
process.description: A marked mock or topic test shows which component is leaking marks and whether the cause is content, arithmetic, command-term reading or timing. Three pages of real working tells a tutor more than a paragraph of explanation, and it often shortens the plan.

process.title: Take a free trial and ask for a diagnosis
process.description: The trial lesson is live, one-to-one, and in the slot you intend to use. At the end, ask the tutor to name the component and the specific habit costing marks. A clear answer is the thing you are buying; a vague one is a reason to try somebody else.

process.title: Buy a block with an end point
process.description: Agree how many sessions, aimed at what, and what will be different at the end. A finite block against a known weighting is both cheaper and easier to judge than an open weekly arrangement that nobody reviews until the exam.

whyPoints.title: Prices published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names who published it and which tier it sits in. Three of the best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and one asks the question in its own list of questions and then declines to answer.

whyPoints.title: Component diagnosis before a plan
whyPoints.description: A Cambridge science grade is 30%, 50% and 20% across three papers. We work out which of the three is losing marks before recommending anything, because that single step is what separates a six-session block from a two-year arrangement.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper taught deliberately
whyPoints.description: Alternative to practical carries a fifth of the grade and is the component schools have least time for. Apparatus diagrams, variable identification, table conventions and graph work are taught as skills with their own drills.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the hourly rate
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live online, so nothing is priced for a drive across Dubai to Al Quoz 4. The published in-home band sits above the online band for exactly that reason, and the difference is a journey rather than better teaching.

whyPoints.title: An agreed stopping point
whyPoints.description: We would rather recommend eight sessions that work than a year that drifts. Open arrangements are how families end up spending far more than the original problem required, and setting the end point at the start prevents it.

faqs.question: How much should IGCSE science tuition cost in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: Published rates span a wide band, and the band maps onto what you get. Budget online tuition runs around AED 33 to AED 150 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 and EdFlik from AED 45. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium provision reaches AED 650, as BartyED publishes. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to AED 500 because they include travel.

faqs.question: Which part of an IGCSE science grade is cheapest to improve?
faqs.answer: The alternative-to-practical paper, by a clear margin. It carries 20% of a Cambridge science grade and tests a narrow, repetitive skill set: drawing apparatus, naming independent and controlled variables, setting out a results table with units in the headers, plotting a line of best fit, reading a value off a graph, and suggesting a specific improvement rather than a generic one. Schools have little curriculum time for it because practical lessons are spent doing practicals. Six to eight focused sessions usually show up directly in the mark.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home science tutor in Al Quoz 4 quoted more per hour?
faqs.answer: Travel. Al Quoz 4 is a residential pocket inside a largely commercial district with few resident tutors, so nearly every in-home quote includes a drive across Dubai in late-afternoon traffic. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500, against AED 150 to AED 300 for an equivalent qualified tutor online. The premium is honestly charged and it buys a journey rather than better science teaching.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send science tutors to homes in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Science lessons for Al Quoz 4 families are delivered live online, one-to-one, with a shared whiteboard both people can draw on and a camera on the student's written working. For apparatus diagrams and graph work the shared whiteboard is arguably better than paper. The school laboratory stays the school laboratory either way, since no visiting tutor brings one.

faqs.question: Is Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 easier to tutor than three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Cheaper, usually, rather than easier. The double award covers biology, chemistry and physics at reduced depth in one qualification worth two grades, examined as Papers 2, 4 and 6. One tutor can realistically cover all three disciplines at that depth, where three separate sciences at Extended often genuinely need two or three different people. The risk with 0654 is thin coverage across many topics, so the work goes topic-by-topic against the syllabus checklist rather than chapter-by-chapter through a textbook.

faqs.question: Do we need to know the syllabus code before booking?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single cheapest thing you can do. Cambridge codes are 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences and 0653 Combined Science; Pearson's are 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4SD0 for the double award. The boards structure papers differently and assess practical skills differently, so a tutor drilling Cambridge past papers with a Pearson candidate is teaching real science against the wrong exam. Ask the school for the entry list, and do not assume all three sciences use the same board.

faqs.question: Are two-hour science sessions better value than two short ones?
faqs.answer: Rarely, for this age group. Several published packages in this market are sold as two-hour visits, and the length is presented as value. A fifteen-year-old's productive attention in a one-to-one science session runs to roughly seventy minutes, after which the remaining time is expensive company. Two sixty-minute sessions on separate days cost about the same and produce more, because the material is revisited rather than crammed. Ask for the shorter format even when the longer one is offered as a discount.

faqs.question: Can the school change my child from Core to Extended?
faqs.answer: It is a conversation worth having, and it costs nothing. Core and Extended are different papers with different grade ceilings, so a Core entry caps the maximum grade available regardless of how well the student performs. Schools make the tier decision on evidence from Year 10, and that evidence can be revisited while there is still time to switch. For a student heading towards A Level or Diploma sciences, Extended is the content those courses assume. Raise it before committing to any tuition spend.

faqs.question: What does a Year 10 and Year 11 science plan cost in total?
faqs.answer: Plan against the monthly figure rather than the hourly rate. Bestimate's estimates for one weekly hour are roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to over AED 2,000 for specialist exam-year support. Across two academic years that is a substantial commitment, which is why a finite block aimed at one component is often the better first purchase. KHDA confirmed no private school fee increase in Dubai for 2026-27, which helps the overall household arithmetic.

faqs.question: Should we pay for past papers or mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor offering to supply them is a warning sign. Cambridge and Pearson publish syllabus documents and past materials through their own channels, and reproducing or redistributing them is a copyright matter rather than a service. The correct approach is to reference the official page and link to it. What you are paying a tutor for is the marking conversation afterwards: why this answer earned two marks out of four, and what the mark scheme actually wanted the student to write.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover physics, chemistry and biology for Year 11?
faqs.answer: At Co-ordinated Sciences depth, usually yes. At separate-science Extended depth it is less realistic, and a tutor who claims equal strength in all three at that level is worth questioning. The practical compromise most Al Quoz 4 families reach is one tutor for the two sciences that share mathematical demands, physics and chemistry, with biology handled separately or left alone if the marks there are already secure. The decision should follow the marked papers rather than convenience.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a licence, and should we check?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it takes one question. The UAE private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with a two-working-day completion time listed on MoHRE's own service page. Teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 can all apply. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no amounts have been published.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams run for a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only, so it has no place in a Dubai plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and must use the timetable for its own zone. Check the live official timetable, because entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers themselves.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE equivalency process require?
faqs.answer: Five, not six. For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure. Verify the current rule through the Ministry's own channel before acting on it.

We will give you the component, the habit costing the marks and an honest estimate of how many sessions it takes — including the cases where the answer is very few.

intro.heading: Science tutoring is a three-subject bill, and that is the whole budgeting problem
paragraphs: A family pricing maths support has one subject to pay for. A family in Al Qusais pricing science has either two or three, depending on a decision the school made about the entry, and the arithmetic changes completely between those two cases. One hour a week of biology, chemistry and physics at the mid-market Dubai rate of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour becomes three hours a week - somewhere between AED 1,800 and AED 3,600 a month if nothing is trimmed. That is more than most households intended to spend on tutoring in total.

So the first useful move is not to find a tutor. It is to establish exactly what your child is entered for. A Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences entry under code 0654 produces a double award - two GCSE grades - from one combined course, and a separate-sciences entry under 0610, 0620 and 0625 produces three. Pearson's equivalent routes are the separate 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 specifications, or Science Double Award under 4SD0. The number of codes on the timetable tells you how many subjects you are actually buying help for.

The second move is to accept that the three sciences do not need equal hours. Across the Al Qusais students we see, the distribution of difficulty is consistent and lopsided. Physics causes the most trouble because it is the most mathematical and the least forgiving of weak algebra. Chemistry causes the second most, concentrated in moles, equations and energy. Biology causes the least in terms of understanding and the most in terms of marks lost to imprecise written answers. A budget split evenly across three subjects is almost always the wrong split.

The third is that some of the most common science purchases in Dubai do not buy marks. Paid past-paper collections when the boards publish specimen material freely. Group revision courses sold by the term and taught across all three sciences at once. Weekly sessions with no marked written output, where nobody can say at the end of a month which topics were closed. And tutoring bought in April for a June series, which can repair technique and cannot build two years of content. Each is set out on this page with the cheaper alternative beside it.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE science to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a three-subject bill the format matters financially as well as practically: the published Dubai in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour includes the tutor's round trip, and multiplying a travel premium by three subjects is how a science budget doubles without anybody choosing it.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-qusais.subjectsIntro: Families search for an IGCSE science tutor in Al Qusais and then name something far more specific. These are the requests that come up most across the three subjects, with the hours each typically takes.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Series and parallel reasoning, potential dividers, power and energy calculations. The most consistently mishandled area in IGCSE physics because it combines algebra with a model students have not visualised. Typically four to six focused sessions, and it pays back across several questions a paper.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, motion and moments
subjects.description: Graph interpretation for distance and velocity, Newton's laws applied to simple systems, moments and equilibrium. Marks are lost to unit conversion and to gradients read without units rather than to the physics itself, which makes this cheap to repair.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The quantitative spine of the course and the dividing line between a 6 and an 8 for most Al Qusais students. Limiting reagents, percentage yield, concentration and gas volumes. Responds to short, frequent drills with immediate marking far better than to explanation.

subjects.name: Chemistry: equations and reactivity
subjects.description: Balancing, ionic equations, the reactivity series, acids and bases and electrolysis. Students who have memorised outcomes without the pattern cannot predict an unfamiliar case, and the papers increasingly ask them to. Three to five sessions usually shifts it.

subjects.name: Biology: written precision
subjects.description: Biology marks are lost in language more than in understanding. Describe against explain, named structures, the direction of a gradient, and answers that stop one step short of the mark point. Drilling against the published mark scheme is the only reliable fix, and it is quick.

subjects.name: Biology: transport, respiration and photosynthesis
subjects.description: The three process-heavy topics where diagrams are reproduced correctly and the explanation that carries the marks is missing. Teaching each as a sequence of causes rather than a labelled diagram changes how students answer unfamiliar versions of the question.

subjects.name: Practical skills and the practical papers
subjects.description: Reading a measuring instrument, tabulating results with consistent decimal places, plotting a graph that earns the plotting marks, and suggesting a genuine improvement. Whether your child sits a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper changes the preparation entirely.

subjects.name: Graph and data skills across all three sciences
subjects.description: One skill, three subjects, and the highest-leverage purchase on this page. Choosing axes, scaling sensibly, drawing a best-fit line, taking a gradient with units and describing a trend in the words the mark scheme wants. Two or three sessions serve biology, chemistry and physics at once.

sections.heading: Double award or triple: the entry decision that sets your science bill
paragraphs: Before pricing anything, find out how many science grades your child is being entered for. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences, syllabus 0654, is a double award: one combined course covering biology, chemistry and physics that produces two GCSE grades. Cambridge Combined Science, 0653, is a single award from a similar combined course. Separate sciences under 0610 for biology, 0620 for chemistry and 0625 for physics produce three grades and cover more content in each. Pearson's routes mirror this with 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 separately, or Science Double Award under 4SD0.

The tutoring consequence is direct. A double-award student has one body of content taught as a combined course, so a competent general science tutor can genuinely cover it and two hours a week is a credible plan. A separate-sciences student has three bodies of content, each going further, and the specialisms begin to matter - the person who is excellent on biology explanation marks is not automatically the person to fix circuit reasoning.

There is a sixth-form consequence too, and it is the one that should drive the decision rather than the tutoring cost. Separate sciences cover more and are the smoother route into IB Diploma or A Level sciences. A double award is accepted by many sixth forms but leaves more content to close in the first term of Year 12. If a science-heavy Diploma is the plan, the money is better spent making a separate-science entry work than on remediating a double award two years later.

The decision usually belongs to the school rather than the family, and some schools stream students between routes during Year 10. Ask the head of science in writing which entry your child is on, when it becomes final, and what evidence the decision rests on. Then buy one diagnostic in the weakest subject before that date, because a marked paper is better evidence than a conversation.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, multiplied across three subjects
paragraphs: The useful way to read published rates on a science page is per month per subject, because that is the number that triples. Bestimate's Dubai rate table, read in October 2026, estimates weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000-plus for specialist exam-year support. Those are per subject. Take the mid-market band and run three subjects weekly and the monthly figure sits between AED 1,800 and AED 3,600 before anybody discusses quality.

Hourly figures behind those monthly bands: budget online platforms staffed largely by university students advertise from the low double digits, with Tutopiya published from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 across the Dubai market, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Named exam specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270, with BartyED at AED 650 for premium named tutors.

In-home visits are where a three-subject plan becomes genuinely expensive. Published Dubai in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors asking AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in the market are around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against about AED 799 for eight online sessions - and if that in-home package covers one subject, covering three means absorbing the travel premium three times over.

Every figure above is a published market rate belonging to the provider named, read in October 2026. None is an IB Gram price. We do not print a rate card on these pages because the honest number depends on how many subjects, which codes and how many weeks remain. The free trial lesson is one lesson with one matched tutor, with the fee discussed afterwards, and for a three-subject enquiry we would use it on whichever subject the diagnostic says is worst.

sections.heading: Three sciences, one budget: how to split the hours without wasting them
paragraphs: An even split is the default and it is usually wrong. Buy a diagnostic in each subject first - one marked paper or a substantial section of one, against the published scheme, producing a written list of named weaknesses per subject. That costs three sessions and it almost always reveals that the three subjects are not equally broken. Across the Al Qusais students we see, physics and chemistry absorb more hours than biology, but which of those two leads varies by student and cannot be guessed.

The second principle is to sequence rather than parallelise where the budget is tight. Three simultaneous weekly slots means three tutors setting homework into the same evenings, which is how a plan collapses in week four. Taking the weakest subject for six to eight weeks, closing its list, then moving to the next, costs a third as much per month and usually produces more because the student is only carrying one extra set of work at a time.

The third is to buy the shared skill once. Axes, scaling, best-fit lines, gradients with units, tabulating with consistent decimal places and describing a trend in mark-scheme language are the same skills in biology, chemistry and physics. Two or three sessions on them improves all three subjects, and almost nobody sells it that way because it is hard to bill repeatedly. It is nevertheless the best value purchase available on this page.

The fourth is to protect the biology budget from over-spending. Biology is rarely a comprehension problem and frequently a language problem: describe against explain, answers that stop one step short of the mark point, named structures omitted. That responds to a short drilling block against published schemes rather than to a year of weekly teaching, and families who allocate biology an equal third of the budget usually find they bought less than they thought.

sections.heading: The practical papers, and why your child's route changes the preparation
paragraphs: Cambridge separate sciences assess practical skills through either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and which one your child sits is a centre-level arrangement rather than a student choice. This is one of the least-discussed cost factors in science tutoring, because the two routes need genuinely different preparation and a tutor who does not ask which applies will prepare for the wrong one.

A student on the practical-test route needs apparatus familiarity: reading a measuring cylinder or thermometer correctly, setting up a circuit without wasting time, taking repeat readings, and recording in a table with consistent decimal places. Much of that happens in the school laboratory and cannot be replicated at home, which is why the tutoring contribution there is about planning, tabulating and interpreting rather than about handling equipment.

A student on the alternative-to-practical route needs something closer to a comprehension skill: reading a described method, spotting the controlled variable, identifying the source of error that actually matters, completing a results table, plotting from given data and proposing a genuine improvement rather than a generic one. This is highly trainable online and one of the most reliably improvable components in the whole entry.

Pearson's separate specifications assess practical skills within the written papers rather than through a separate practical component, which changes the balance again. The honest summary is that practical marks are easier to gain than most families assume and are usually left untouched because nobody checked which route applied. Two sessions spent on the correct route is better value than ten spent on content a student already half-knows.

sections.heading: Where Al Qusais families waste money on science tutoring
paragraphs: The first and largest waste is buying three weekly slots before any diagnosis. It feels thorough and it produces three homework streams into the same two available evenings, with no written list anywhere to say what is being fixed. Three diagnostic sessions cost a fraction of a month of that arrangement and usually show that one subject needs real work, one needs a short drilling block and one needs nothing yet.

The second is paying for past papers and notes. The boards publish specimen and past material, schools distribute it, and paying for a collection buys convenience rather than content. The product worth paying for is marking: a paper marked against the published scheme by someone who can explain why an answer that looks right earned nothing. A hundred unmarked papers rehearse a student's existing habits.

The third is the all-subjects group revision course sold by the term. For a student near a grade boundary who needs structured reminding it can work. For a student whose physics problem is algebraic rearrangement it cannot, because the class cannot stop. And when it covers all three sciences in rotation, each subject gets a third of the attention for the full term price.

The fourth is starting in April. Eight weeks before a June series is enough to repair technique, drill the quantitative spine of chemistry and train the alternative-to-practical paper. It is not enough to build two years of content across three subjects, and a provider implying otherwise is selling reassurance. The fifth is tutoring on the wrong entry route - paying for extended-tier content when the entry is core, or preparing for a practical test when the centre sits the alternative paper.

sections.heading: Series, entries and the exam logistics a tutoring plan has to respect
paragraphs: Dates matter to a science budget because entries close months before papers are sat, and a family that discovers a deadline late can end up paying for a resit cycle. For Cambridge candidates in the UAE the series are June and November. The February and March series is offered to India only, so no Al Qusais family should be planning around a March examination - a point worth stating because incorrect advice on this circulates widely in Gulf parenting groups.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are available in May/June and November. The November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any session planning should work from the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than from a restated date anywhere, this page included.

Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is the school's administrative responsibility rather than a parent's, and it is worth knowing exists if your child's timetable looks different from a classmate's at another school.

For tutoring, the planning consequence is simple. A June series means the useful content window closes around the Easter break, with the final weeks reserved for timed papers and correction. A November resit route exists and should be treated as a route rather than a safety net, because the content has to be held for an extra two terms. Confirm every date with the school's examinations officer.

paragraphs: We match a tutor per subject and per syllabus code, and lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The first lesson is a free trial with the matched tutor - one lesson, fee discussed afterwards rather than before. There is no office, centre or branch in the Emirates, no tutor is sent to a UAE address, and home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated identically on every UAE page on this site, which is the only way a reader can check that it is a policy rather than a sales line.

We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing here implies one. Where a regulator appears it is to explain what it does. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and KHDA inspects schools rather than tutors.

We publish no success rate, no star rating, no student headcount and no claimed grade improvement, because none of those could be produced on request. The verifiable figures on this page are other providers' prices, attributed and dated, plus Dubai's own published market data: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, 17 curricula offered, and an enrolment split of 37% UK curriculum, 26% Indian, 14% US and 7% International Baccalaureate.

On permits: private tutoring here is regulated, and a parent should ask. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published - so disregard any specific amount quoted online. Ask our tutors the same question you would ask anyone else's.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to tutor all three IGCSE sciences in Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: At the published mid-market Dubai band of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, three weekly hours lands between about AED 1,800 and AED 3,600 a month, read against Bestimate's October 2026 estimates of AED 600 to 1,200 a month per subject at that level. Very few families should spend that. Three diagnostic sessions usually show one subject needs real hours, one needs a short drilling block and one needs nothing yet, which cuts the monthly figure to a third or less without cutting the outcome.

faqs.question: Is a double-award science entry cheaper to tutor than three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Materially, yes. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences under 0654 is one combined course producing two grades, so a competent general science tutor can genuinely cover it and one to two hours a week is a credible plan. Separate sciences under 0610, 0620 and 0625 are three bodies of content going further in each, where specialisms start to matter. The decision should still be driven by sixth-form plans rather than by tutoring cost, because separate sciences are the smoother route into Diploma or A Level sciences.

faqs.question: Which of the three sciences should we spend the tutoring budget on?
faqs.answer: Buy a diagnostic in each before deciding, because the answer varies by student and cannot be guessed from report grades. The pattern across Al Qusais students is that physics and chemistry absorb more hours than biology - physics because it is the most mathematical and least forgiving of weak algebra, chemistry because of moles, equations and energy. Biology is usually a language problem rather than a comprehension one, which a short block drilling against published mark schemes fixes faster and more cheaply than weekly teaching.

faqs.question: Why is my child good at biology in class but losing marks in the exam?
faqs.answer: Almost always language rather than understanding. Biology mark schemes reward precision: describe against explain, the named structure rather than a general one, the direction of a gradient stated explicitly, and an answer that reaches the mark point rather than stopping one step short. A student can hold the biology correctly and write an answer worth half the marks. Drilling answers against the published scheme, with someone explaining why a sensible-looking response earned nothing, is the only reliable fix and it works quickly.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child sits Paper 5 or Paper 6?
faqs.answer: It changes the preparation entirely, and most tutors never ask. Paper 5 is a practical test in the laboratory, where the value a tutor adds is in planning, tabulating with consistent decimal places, repeats and interpretation rather than in equipment handling. Paper 6 is the alternative-to-practical written paper: reading a described method, identifying the controlled variable and the error that actually matters, completing tables, plotting from given data and proposing a real improvement. The second is highly trainable online and usually left untouched.

faqs.question: Should we buy a group science revision course in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Buy it second, after diagnosis, and know what it can do. A group course works for a student near a grade boundary who needs structured reminding across the syllabus. It cannot work for a student whose physics problem is algebraic rearrangement, because the class cannot stop for one person. When a course rotates across all three sciences for a term fee, each subject receives a third of the attention - which is reasonable value only if all three are genuinely weak in the same way.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful thing an Al Qusais family can buy for science?
faqs.answer: Three diagnostics - one per subject - and then nothing else until you have read them. One marked paper or substantial section per subject, against the published scheme, producing a written list of named weaknesses with the marks lost attached. At mid-market rates that is roughly AED 450 to 900 once, and you keep the documents whoever teaches afterwards. The second cheapest is a two-session block on axes, graphs, gradients and trend description, because that single purchase improves all three sciences at once.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child's IGCSE sciences be sat in?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge candidates in the UAE, the June series with November available as a resit route. The February and March series is offered to India only, so plans built around a March science examination in Dubai are built on incorrect information. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences run May/June and November; the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Work from the board's live timetable.

faqs.question: Is three weekly science slots too much for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes - not because of the hours but because of the homework. Three tutors setting work into the same two available evenings, on top of school homework and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies load that all Dubai private schools carry, is how a plan is abandoned in week four. Sequencing one subject at a time for six to eight weeks costs a third as much per month and generally achieves more, because the student is carrying one extra stream rather than three.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach biology, chemistry and physics at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For a double-award entry, often yes, and it is a sensible economy - one relationship, one homework stream, one diagnosis. For separate sciences at extended tier it is less likely to hold up, because the specialisms diverge: the person strongest on biology explanation marks is not automatically the one to repair circuit reasoning or stoichiometry. Ask a prospective tutor which of the three they have taught to extended tier most recently, and listen for whether they volunteer the one they are weakest on.

faqs.question: We are starting in April before a June series. What can tutoring realistically do?
faqs.answer: Repair technique and drill the most mark-dense routines, which is worth real money. In eight weeks a student can be trained on command words and complete mark-point answers, drilled on moles and stoichiometry, taught the alternative-to-practical paper properly and given timed practice with correction. What eight weeks cannot do is build two years of content across three subjects, and anybody suggesting otherwise is selling reassurance. Narrow the plan to one or two subjects and accept the trade-off deliberately.

faqs.question: How do we check an IGCSE science tutor in Dubai is permitted to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask directly. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a working tutor has no financial reason to be without one. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat quoted amounts as unverified.

faqs.question: Do you send science tutors to homes in Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson we arrange is one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we operate only in India, stated the same way on every UAE page we publish. The Dubai market does supply in-home science tutors at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel. The arithmetic worth seeing is that replicating an in-home arrangement across three sciences means paying the travel premium three times, which is how a science budget doubles without anybody choosing it.

faqs.question: What does a science diagnostic session actually give us?
faqs.answer: A marked paper or substantial section per subject, sat under something close to timed conditions, assessed against the published scheme, and converted into a written list of three to six named weaknesses with the marks lost beside each. It will usually also give a view on whether the current tier and entry route are right. You keep the document whether you continue with us, hand it to another tutor or decide no weekly tutoring is needed yet. Almost nobody in this market sells it on its own.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one slot, and a decision nobody helps you make
paragraphs: Families searching for a science tutor in this district are rarely asking about one subject. A Year 10 or Year 11 student is carrying biology, chemistry and physics, either as three separate IGCSEs or as a combined award, and something has gone wrong in at least one of them. The household has the money and the evening for roughly one weekly hour. The question is which science that hour should buy, and almost nobody answers it, because answering it honestly means telling a parent not to buy two more hours.

The geography makes the constraint tighter here than in some districts. Al Rashidiya sits between Dubai International Airport, Al Garhoud and Nad Al Hamar and has no secondary school of its own. Its students travel: a short run north into the Garhoud cluster, or east along Algeria Street towards Mirdif, Al Mizhar and Al Warqa, where collecting bus routes take the better part of forty minutes once school finishes. A student home at 4.15pm has one usable hour before the evening belongs to the family, and three sciences cannot share it.

So this page is a decision aid before it is anything else. Which award is your child entered for, and does that change the answer. Which of the three sciences is actually losing the marks, as opposed to which one feels hardest. Which of them has a practical component that needs separate attention. And what the realistic cost looks like if two subjects genuinely need support rather than one.

The second thing worth saying plainly is that a science tutor is not a thing. Biology, chemistry and physics fail differently: biology on terminology and volume, chemistry on mole arithmetic, physics on circuits and on reasoning from a model. Somebody good at all three to IGCSE standard exists, but somebody good at one of them is both commoner and better, and on a single funded hour the specialist wins. We list our tutors by subject rather than as science generalists for exactly that reason.

There is also a cheaper answer than any of the three subjects, and it is worth knowing before you spend. A large part of what separates a grade 5 from a grade 7 in all three sciences is not content at all but the discipline of answering the command term that was used, writing an explanation where an explanation is asked for, and referring to the data in a conclusion. That skill is taught once and collects marks in biology, chemistry and physics at the same time, which makes it the best-value purchase available to a Year 11 student two terms from a series.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one lessons over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the slot set from your child's real arrival home. Home visits are an India-only service; nobody is driving to an address in the UAE, which means the travel time that would otherwise come out of the hour stays in the lesson. The rest of this page is the detail: the awards, the practical components by board, the triage between three subjects, the market rates in dirhams with every figure attributed, and the exam calendar read backwards from the entry deadline.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap. Students revise the whole syllabus thinly and then lose the long-answer marks that want precise terminology: osmosis explained without water potential, enzymes without the active site. Writing to the command term is worth more here than another pass through the textbook.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles decide the grade. A student who can explain the method but cannot move between mass, moles and concentration in fifteen seconds loses marks across every paper. Organic chemistry and the reactivity series reward memory; stoichiometry rewards practice, which is the part students skip.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity, and series and parallel circuits in particular, separates students more reliably than any other topic. The second recurring loss is the practical component, which asks students to criticise an experiment they did not run, and that is a learned written skill rather than recall.

subjects.name: Combined and co-ordinated science routes
subjects.description: A reduced content load across all three sciences producing fewer grades. Sensible for many students and a real constraint for anyone heading towards A Level or Higher Level sciences, because the depth that a sixth-form course assumes may not have been covered. Check the award before planning a post-16 route.

subjects.name: Practical and alternative-to-practical skills
subjects.description: Reading a described method, identifying control variables, criticising a procedure and interpreting someone else's results. Cambridge assesses this in a dedicated component; Pearson examines it inside the main written papers. Either way it is practised on past questions, not learned from a textbook.

subjects.name: Graph work and data handling in science
subjects.description: Plotting accurately, drawing a line of best fit that is defensible, reading a gradient and stating what it means physically or biologically. Mechanical marks available in all three subjects, routinely lost to rushed axes and to conclusions that do not refer to the data.

subjects.name: Scientific explanation and command terms
subjects.description: The difference between describe, explain, suggest and compare, and what each one has to contain to earn its marks. This is the single highest-yield piece of work across all three sciences and it covers no new content whatsoever, which makes it the obvious first purchase late in Year 11.

subjects.name: The maths inside the sciences
subjects.description: Rearranging a formula, handling standard form, percentages and ratios, and significant figures. A student whose science marks drop in calculation questions usually has a maths problem wearing a science costume, and three sessions on rearrangement does more than ten on content.

subjects.name: Required practical knowledge and apparatus
subjects.description: Knowing what a named piece of apparatus does, what a standard test for an ion or a gas looks like, and what a sensible range of readings is. Finite, learnable content that appears every series, and routinely under-revised because it feels like trivia.

subjects.name: Extended-response questions in biology
subjects.description: The six-mark style questions that reward a structured answer using the correct terminology in the correct order. Students who know the biology still lose half the marks by writing a general paragraph instead of addressing each element the question asks for.

subjects.name: Triple-science time management
subjects.description: Not a topic but the real problem for many Year 11 students: three sciences, three sets of past papers and a finite number of evenings. Planning which subject gets which evening is work a tutor should do with a family rather than leave to chance.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory subjects alongside science
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside IGCSE in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it is licensed for. They occupy timetable space, which is relevant when a family is calculating how many tutoring hours a Year 11 week can genuinely hold.

modes.description: The default recommendation and the one most families should start with. Pick the subject where the marks are actually leaving, book one specialist for one fixed weekday, and leave the other two sciences to the school for now. A specialist hour in the failing subject moves a grade; a divided hour across three sciences moves none, and this is the single most common mistake in this market.

A full hour in biology this week and a full hour in chemistry next week keeps both tutors working on something substantial, where two half-hours achieve the arrival and departure and little else. sections.heading: Triple, double or combined: find out before you spend anything
paragraphs: The first question is not which science to tutor. It is which award your child is entered for, because the answer changes what the tutoring is trying to achieve. A triple-award student sits three separate sciences with three separate syllabus codes and receives three grades. A combined or co-ordinated student covers a reduced content load and receives fewer grades from it.

Neither route is better in the abstract. The combined route is a sensible decision for a great many students and removes a real workload problem. What it also does, quietly, is change what a sixth form can offer afterwards, because A Level and Higher Level science courses assume a depth of prior content that a reduced route may not have covered. A student can be formally eligible and practically underprepared, and that gap is discovered in the first term of Year 12 rather than at the point the award was chosen.

The practical consequence for tutoring is about target rather than effort. For a triple-award student aiming at A Level chemistry, the work is depth in chemistry. For a combined-science student whose problem is that the physics content inside the award is thin, the work is different and may be preparatory rather than remedial. A tutor who does not ask which award is in play is guessing.

Get the award and the codes from the statement of entry, which the school issues ahead of each series and which most parents have never opened. Your exams officer will send it. Bring it to the first conversation with any tutor, and confirm the current paper structure on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than from any summary, this page included.

sections.heading: Which of the three sciences should the one funded hour go to?
paragraphs: This is the question the page exists to answer, and the answer is almost never the subject that feels hardest. Feelings follow the teacher, the class and the last test; marks follow a pattern. Get three marked papers, one per science, and the choice usually makes itself in ten minutes.

Look for the shape of the loss rather than the total. Biology marks lost in long-answer questions point at terminology and command-term technique, which is cheap to fix and lifts the other two sciences at the same time. Chemistry marks lost in calculations point at mole fluency, which is pure practice and responds within weeks. Physics marks lost in circuits or in the practical component point at a specific conceptual topic and a specific written skill, both of which need a physics specialist rather than a general science tutor.

Then weigh what the grade is for. A student who needs chemistry for a medicine-adjacent route and biology only as a third subject should fund chemistry even if biology looks worse on the report, because the consequence of each grade is different. A student with no science route in mind should fund whichever subject is closest to a grade boundary, because that is where an hour buys the most.

The table sets out the triage we actually use. Run it with marked papers in front of you rather than with impressions, and be prepared for the answer to be a subject your child has not complained about.

sections.heading: The practical component, and why the board matters
paragraphs: Science practical assessment is the place where Cambridge and Pearson diverge most, and it is also the place where families most often buy the wrong preparation. A tutor who has drilled Cambridge alternative-to-practical questions for years has a genuinely valuable skill that does not map onto the Pearson arrangement, where practical understanding is examined inside the main written papers.

What the Cambridge component actually asks for is worth understanding, because it surprises parents. It does not test whether a student can perform an experiment. It tests whether they can read a described method, identify the variables that should have been controlled, criticise the procedure, suggest an improvement and interpret results they did not generate. Those are written skills with a learnable structure, and a student who has done twenty of them is in a different position from one who has done two.

This has a convenient consequence. Because the component is a written skill rather than a laboratory skill, it is taught perfectly well over a shared screen with past questions open. The actual laboratory work, apparatus and safety supervision remain the school's responsibility, as they always were, and no tutor is bringing equipment into an Al Rashidiya villa.

Ask any prospective science tutor which board's practical arrangement they have taught and how many series of it. The answer separates a specialist from somebody who will teach the content and leave the component to chance, which is where a meaningful share of science marks quietly goes.

sections.heading: What a science hour costs in this corridor, and what three would cost
paragraphs: The arithmetic families actually face is not the hourly rate but the hourly rate multiplied by three, and that is where decisions are really made. Here are the published Dubai figures, each read on the provider's own public page so you can open it and check.

EdFlik advertises budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya's published panel starting lower again. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Named IGCSE specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table reaching the top of that band. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home one to one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 because the rate carries a round trip through the Garhoud interchange or Algeria Street.

Multiply the specialist band by three weekly hours and the monthly figure becomes a number most households will not sustain, which is precisely why the triage section above matters more than the rate comparison. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support, and those are per subject. Monthly packages seen locally sit around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours.

None of these is an IB Gram price and we publish no rate card on these pages. The practical conclusion is the uncomfortable one: for most families the right purchase is one specialist hour in the subject the marked papers identify, plus a technique block that lifts all three, rather than three diluted arrangements nobody can afford to keep.

sections.heading: The weekday the lesson sits on, and the two evenings of practice
paragraphs: Scheduling is a money question, because a session that does not happen costs the same as one that does. For Al Rashidiya families the slot has to be set from the arrival home on a bad afternoon rather than the earliest time that ever worked, and the difference between those two choices is whether the arrangement still exists in February.

Garhoud-direction families can hold 4.30pm reliably. Mirdif, Al Mizhar and Al Warqa bus routes need 5.30pm or later, with Al Warqa and Al Khawaneej students often better served by a weekend morning. Add recovery time: a student off a forty-minute bus in Dubai heat needs food and twenty minutes before they are any use on a six-mark biology question.

Around the lesson, put the practice on two separate evenings rather than one. All three sciences reward frequency, and in chemistry specifically mole arithmetic only becomes automatic through repetition. Twenty minutes twice beats ninety minutes once by a wide margin, and the tutor's written note should name the practice specifically so that it is checkable rather than aspirational.

Plan the exceptions in advance. During Ramadan school days are shortened and household routines move to the evening, so the slot usually shifts to after iftar; because no tutor is travelling, that change costs a message. Holiday weeks suit a short defined block on one topic better than a weekly slot limping through while the family is away.

One more scheduling point that is specific to triple science. Three subjects means three sets of past papers competing for the same evenings in the final two terms, and left to chance a student will revise whichever subject has the nearest test rather than the one that needs the hours. Write the week down once, give each science a named evening, and the tutor can then work inside a plan rather than against one. It takes twenty minutes in October and saves a term of improvisation.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the science entry deadline
paragraphs: The date that catches families out is the entry rather than the exam. A school submits entries months before the first paper, and that submission fixes the tier and the series. A tier discovered to be wrong in February is wrong for that series, whatever is bought afterwards.

Get the series right first. UAE candidates sit the June and the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a March window is built for another country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask which zone your centre sits in.

For dated examples, Pearson's published record is the checkable one. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates, which is why they are safe to use as a shape rather than as a promise.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so open the live official timetable rather than relying on any restated date, including this one. For a triple-science student the practical reading of the table is that three subjects' revision has to be sequenced across the same window, which is another argument for deciding early which one gets the funded hour.

sections.heading: What a science tutor may and may not do with school work
paragraphs: IGCSE science carries less assessed coursework than it once did, which simplifies the honesty question without removing it. School investigations, projects and internally marked tasks still exist, and the boundary is the same one every board applies.

A tutor may teach the method, work a comparable example, question a student about their own attempt and point out where the reasoning does not hold. A tutor may not write, complete, redo or edit to completion any piece of work the student submits. The practical test for a parent requires no science: if the feedback reads as sentences your child could copy in, the line has been crossed, and if it reads as questions they must go and answer, it has not.

It is worth knowing what is on sale nearby. One page in the researched competitor set advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price, which is an academic-integrity breach and an examination malpractice trigger, and the student bears the consequence rather than the seller. Any offer of that kind should end a conversation rather than start a negotiation.

We also decline to reproduce or supply board material. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are available from them or through the school. Pointing a parent at the official page is both the lawful answer and the more useful one, because the official page is current while a file circulating in a school parent group is often from a superseded specification.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we will say about availability
paragraphs: Send four things. The board and syllabus codes from the statement of entry, including the award. Photographs of marked papers in all three sciences if you have them, or in the weakest two if not. Whether a specific science is needed for a post-16 route. And the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon.

With those, the triage takes one conversation rather than a term of trial and error, and the recommendation will sometimes be to fund a subject your child has not complained about. The free trial lesson then runs forty minutes on a past question in that subject, with your child working and the tutor teaching, and afterwards you receive a written read on the loss pattern and the weeks it implies.

Sometimes the honest answer is about availability rather than approach. Late-evening Gulf Standard Time slots fill first and weekend mornings fill during exam terms, and a specialist in a particular board's practical component requested close to a series may not be free. We will give a realistic match time rather than filling the hour with a general science tutor, because the wrong tutor in the right slot costs the fee and the weeks.

What we need is limited to what matching requires: board, codes, award, year group, school if you want its sequence followed, and a contact for scheduling. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history across every subject. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data we hold and the privacy link on this page sets out what is kept and how to have it removed.
