faqs.question: My child does all three sciences and we can only afford one tutor. Which one?
faqs.answer: Decide from marked papers rather than from which subject feels hardest. Long answers scoring half marks across all three point at command-term technique, which can be taught once and lifts every science. Chemistry calculation losses point at mole fluency, which is pure practice. Physics circuit losses point at a specific conceptual topic needing a physics specialist. Then weigh what each grade is for: a chemistry grade needed for a medicine-adjacent route outranks an untidy biology grade. If no route is in mind, fund whichever subject sits closest to a boundary.

faqs.question: Is there such a thing as a good science tutor for all three subjects?
faqs.answer: At IGCSE standard, yes, such people exist, and on one funded hour a specialist still beats them. The three sciences fail for different reasons: biology on terminology and the structure of extended answers, chemistry on mole arithmetic that is understood but not automatic, physics on circuits and on reasoning from a model. A specialist recognises the pattern in a marked paper within two minutes. An all-rounder teaches content competently and often misses the specific thing costing the marks.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is on triple or combined science?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry, which the school issues ahead of each series, names the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject and shows whether three separate sciences are entered or a combined or co-ordinated route. Your exams officer will send a copy. It matters beyond labelling: combined routes cover a reduced content load, and while a student may be formally eligible for an A Level science afterwards, they can be practically underprepared, and that gap is discovered in Year 12.

faqs.question: Does a combined science award stop my child taking A Level sciences?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and it may make them harder. A Level and Higher Level science courses assume a depth of prior content, and a reduced route may not have covered it, so a student can meet an entry requirement on paper and struggle in the first term. The right move is to ask the specific sixth form what it expects from a combined-science entrant and what it recommends covering over the summer. Ask before the award is chosen if you can, and in Year 11 if you cannot.

faqs.question: What exactly does the Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper test?
faqs.answer: Not whether a student can perform an experiment. It gives them a described method and asks them to identify which variables should have been controlled, criticise the procedure, suggest an improvement and interpret results they did not generate. That is a written skill with a learnable structure, and a student who has attempted twenty of these questions is in a different position from one who has attempted two. It is also why online tutoring suits it: a shared screen with past questions open is exactly the right setting.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson science?
faqs.answer: For choosing a tutor, yes. Practical assessment is where the two diverge most: Cambridge sets a dedicated practical or alternative-to-practical component, while Pearson examines practical understanding inside the main written papers. A tutor experienced in one arrangement is not automatically useful in the other, and past papers do not transfer. Ask which board and how many series they have taught it, and confirm the current structure on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than from any third-party summary.

faqs.question: What would it cost to fund all three sciences weekly?
faqs.answer: More than most households will sustain, which is the honest reason this page is a triage rather than a shop. Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support, and those figures are per subject. Three specialist subjects means three times the specialist monthly band. One specialist hour plus a technique block that lifts all three is the arrangement most families should buy.

faqs.question: Would a technique block really help all three sciences at once?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most underused purchase in this market. Command-term discipline, knowing what describe, explain, suggest and compare each have to contain, plus graph work and conclusions that refer to the data, are the same skills in biology, chemistry and physics. A six-to-ten session block teaching them across all three covers no new content and lifts marks in every paper. For a Year 11 student two terms from a series, it is usually better value than content teaching in any single subject.

faqs.question: What time should a science lesson start if my child buses back from Al Warqa?
faqs.answer: Later than you want, or on a weekend morning. Al Warqa routes are among the longest in this part of Dubai and students arrive home around half past four, flat. A 5pm lesson is being taught to somebody who is still on the bus mentally. For these families 6.30pm or 7pm works if the house is quiet, and a Saturday or Sunday morning works better still. The comparison is not one hour against another; it is a rested student against an exhausted one.

faqs.question: How much practice should go alongside a weekly science lesson?
faqs.answer: Twenty to thirty minutes on two separate evenings rather than ninety minutes once. All three sciences reward frequency, and in chemistry the mole arithmetic only becomes automatic through repetition. The practice should be named specifically in the tutor's written note after each lesson, so you can check it happened rather than hope. Put it on evenings that are genuinely free: not after a long fixture, not on the heaviest homework night, and not on the evening the lesson itself sits.

faqs.question: My child says biology is just too much to remember. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually, and not by more revision. Biology's content volume tempts students into one thin pass over everything, which produces recall good enough for short questions and useless for the extended-response ones where the marks concentrate. The fix is structural: learn the terminology precisely for a smaller number of topics, and practise building answers that address each element a question asks for in order. That is technique work, it covers no new content, and it typically shows up within four or five sessions.

faqs.question: Can a science tutor help with my child's school investigation?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary. A tutor may teach the method, work a comparable example, question your child about their own attempt and point out where the reasoning does not hold. A tutor may not write, complete, redo or edit to completion any work your child submits. The test needs no science on your part: feedback as questions they must answer is correct, feedback as sentences they could copy in is not. One page in this search result sells completed Internal Assessments, and the student carries the malpractice risk.

faqs.question: Do you give out science past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are not ours to reproduce or distribute. We teach against the codes your child is entered for and point you to the board's own site or to the school. That is also the more useful answer, because the official page is current while files circulating in school parent groups are frequently from superseded specifications and will quietly send a student to the wrong question styles.

faqs.question: Which series will my child sit, and when do results arrive?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so ignore any plan built around a March window. For dated shape, Pearson's published record is checkable: the International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always open the live official timetable, because provisional versions are revised before each series.

faqs.question: What should we send you before the first science lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things. The board, syllabus codes and award from the statement of entry. Marked papers in as many of the three sciences as you have. Whether any specific science is needed for a post-16 route, because that changes the recommendation. And the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history; UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data held and the privacy link explains it.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-rashidiy.closingHeading: Fund one science properly rather than three thinly
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-rashidiy.closingBody: The decision that matters for an Al Rashidiya family is not which tutor but which subject. Get the statement of entry so you know the award and the codes, collect a marked paper in each science, and look at the shape of the loss rather than the total. If the long answers are weak across all three, buy technique and it lifts everything. If the chemistry calculations are the problem, buy chemistry. Then set the slot from the afternoon your child actually gets home at the worst, and take the free trial lesson in that one subject. One hour spent in the right place moves a grade; the same hour split three ways moves nothing.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-safa.tutorsIntro: Science at IGCSE is three subjects wearing one label. The tutors below are matched one subject at a time, by syllabus code and by the paper your child is weakest on, rather than by who happens to live closest to Al Safa.

intro.heading: Start from the date on the exam entry form, not from the last report card
paragraphs: Parents in Al Safa usually start looking for an IGCSE science tutor in Al Safa in one of three weeks of the year: the week mock results come home, the week the school asks for Core or Extended tier decisions, and the week the final entry deadline is announced. All three are calendar events. None of them is really about whether your child is good at science. They are about whether there is enough time left to change a grade, and how that time should be spent.

That matters because science at IGCSE is not one subject. Cambridge Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 are three separate syllabuses with three separate mark schemes, and a child can be two grades apart across them. Pearson Edexcel runs its own versions with its own codes, 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. A tutor who is strong on organic chemistry is not automatically useful on electromagnetic induction. The first job of a term plan is deciding which of the three subjects actually earns the hours, and that decision has to be made from paper-level evidence rather than an overall percentage.

The second thing the calendar forces is honesty about scope. Eight weeks of one weekly session is roughly eight hours of teaching plus whatever the student does between lessons. Eight hours will not rebuild two years of physics. It will comfortably repair one topic family, drill one paper format and fix the habits that lose marks everywhere, which in practice is where most of the grade sits. A plan that promises everything in eight weeks is a plan nobody has counted.

The third is sequencing. Revision that happens in the wrong order wastes the window. Alternative-to-practical skills, for example, improve fast and improve across all three sciences at once, because the same planning, variables and graph-drawing conventions are examined in Biology, Chemistry and Physics. Topic content improves slowly and only helps the topic it covers. Early in a window you buy the transferable skills; late in a window you buy past papers under timed conditions. Getting that order backwards is the single most common way a family spends real money and sees no movement.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one tuition over live video to families in Al Safa. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. That is stated plainly here because it changes what you are choosing between: not a tutor who lives nearby against a tutor who does not, but a tutor who teaches your child's exact syllabus against whoever can reach Al Safa by 5pm on a Tuesday. On a three-syllabus subject like science, that difference is the whole decision.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-safa.subjectsIntro: Science is booked subject by subject, paper by paper. These are the components Al Safa families most often ask for, with what each one assesses and where the marks tend to leak.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: Marks are lost less on recall than on command terms. 'Explain' needs a mechanism, 'describe' needs the trend, and 'suggest' expects applied reasoning about an unfamiliar organism. Transport, respiration and homeostasis are the topics where a student who 'knows it' still scores two out of five.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: The quantitative half decides the grade. Moles, concentration, titration arithmetic and yield calculations are mechanical once drilled and catastrophic when they are not. Electrolysis and the reactivity series reward precise half-equations rather than general description.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves separate grades. Series and parallel circuits, potential dividers and the difference between current, potential difference and resistance account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, usually because the student is pattern-matching to a remembered question instead of reading the circuit drawn.

subjects.name: Alternative to Practical (Paper 6)
subjects.description: The highest-return component to tutor and the most ignored. It tests experiment planning, controlling variables, reading instruments, tabulating results and drawing a line of best fit. The conventions are shared across Biology, Chemistry and Physics, so improvement in one subject carries straight into the other two.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: One grade covering all three disciplines, with reduced content per subject and a different paper structure from separate sciences. Students who moved from combined to separate mid-course carry specific gaps, and a tutor needs the school's scheme of work to find them rather than guessing.

subjects.name: Mathematics inside science
subjects.description: Rearranging equations, standard form, unit conversion, percentage change and gradients. Weak science grades in Al Safa are frequently weak arithmetic grades in disguise, and a short block here lifts all three sciences at once rather than one of them.

subjects.name: Extended-response technique
subjects.description: The six-mark questions where candidates write a paragraph and score two. Students are taught to plan against the mark allocation, to use the subject's vocabulary rather than paraphrase, and to answer the question actually asked instead of the adjacent one they revised.

subjects.name: Past-paper diagnosis
subjects.description: Working through papers from the exact syllabus code and series, marked against the official mark scheme, then sorted into error types rather than topics. A student who loses marks to misread questions needs a different intervention from one who loses them to unlearned content.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE, alongside science)
subjects.description: Frequently booked in the same term as science because the two share the quantitative base. sections.heading: What an IGCSE science tutor in Al Safa is being asked to fix this term
paragraphs: An IGCSE science tutor in Al Safa is hired, nine times out of ten, to move one or two of three subjects by one or two grades inside a fixed number of weeks. That is the whole brief. Everything else follows from counting the weeks and then deciding which of Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 the hours go to.

The counting part is simple and almost nobody does it. Take the date of the first science paper in your child's series. Subtract the school's own mock window, the half-term break and the week of the Eid or winter holiday if they fall inside the period. What remains is the number of teaching hours actually available. A family that starts in the first week of a term with a weekly session has perhaps twelve usable hours before a June series; a family that starts after the mocks has five. Those are different plans, not the same plan with less of it.

The deciding part is where paper-level evidence replaces instinct. A school report that says 'working towards grade 5 in science' tells you nothing actionable. A marked Paper 4 tells you that eleven of the lost marks were in quantitative chemistry, six were command-term failures spread across topics, and four were on a single unlearned topic. The first of those is a four-session fix, the second is a habit, and the third is twenty minutes. Without that breakdown, the hours get spread evenly across three syllabuses and nothing moves far enough to change a grade.

The honest limit is worth stating as well. Science grades move reliably when there is a specific, diagnosable gap and at least six weeks. They move less reliably when a student is near their ceiling in all three subjects, when the real problem is attendance or sleep, or when the family wants three subjects lifted simultaneously on one session a week. A tutor who tells you which of those you are in before taking money is worth more than one who agrees to everything.

sections.heading: The exam series, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit two series a year. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that 'it is essential that you use the correct version of the timetable for your zone' because Cambridge 'cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam' after a zone mix-up. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only and is not available to candidates in the UAE, so ignore any revision plan built around it.

The pattern that matters more than the exact dates is the gap between the entry deadline and the exam. Entries close months in advance, which means the decision about which tier and which subjects your child is entered for is made long before anybody knows how the revision went. For the Pearson November 2026 series the final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results landed with students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series, including the November series a full year out, and revises those drafts more than once, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning against.

Read backwards, that produces a usable shape for an Al Safa family. Entry decisions and tier confirmation happen roughly five to six months before the papers. Mocks sit eight to twelve weeks out and are the last honest diagnostic before the real thing. The final eight weeks are for timed papers and error elimination, not new content. Results arrive two to three months after the papers, and the enquiry-about-results and retake windows open immediately after that, which is why a family hoping to resit in the next series has to decide quickly rather than wait for the next school term.

The practical consequence is that the best eight weeks of tutoring your money can buy are the eight weeks before mocks, not the eight before the exam. Mock results drive predicted grades, predicted grades drive sixth-form and university conversations, and a child who fixes their paper technique before mocks gets a better prediction and a calmer final term. Families who arrive after mocks can still move a grade; they just have fewer options about how.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, three sciences: what the plan actually contains
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the standard unit because it is long enough for a habit to change and short enough that a family can see the end of it. With two sessions a week that is sixteen hours of teaching; with one it is eight. The plan below assumes the shorter version, because that is what most Al Safa families start with, and it assumes the student does roughly the same amount again between sessions.

Weeks one to three go to shared skills. Alternative-to-practical conventions, graph plotting, significant figures, rearranging equations and the discipline of reading what a question asks before answering it. These are taught once and used in all three sciences, which is the only way eight hours touches three subjects honestly. A student who cannot draw a line of best fit is losing marks in Biology, Chemistry and Physics simultaneously, and fixing that costs one session.

Weeks four to six go to the one topic family the diagnostic named. For Chemistry that is usually moles and concentration; for Physics, circuits; for Biology, the processes where a mechanism is required rather than a description. The work here is narrow on purpose. One topic family taught to the point of fluency produces a bigger grade movement than six topics revisited briefly, because partially-known topics are exactly what the mark scheme punishes.

Weeks seven and eight go to timed papers and nothing else. Full papers from the exact syllabus code, marked hard, with every lost mark classified as content, technique or misreading. Then the same error types retested the following week. No new content is introduced in this block however tempting it looks, because a topic learned in week eight is not reliable in week nine and the time spent on it comes out of paper practice that is.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: a decision with a deadline attached
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE sciences are tiered. Core caps the grade available; Extended does not. The school decides which tier a candidate is entered for, and that entry is made months before the exam, which makes the tier conversation a calendar event rather than an academic one. Once entries close, the ceiling is fixed for that series regardless of how the final ten weeks of revision go.

The consequence sits two years later. AS and A Level sciences assume Extended-tier content and Extended-tier quantitative fluency. A student entered for Core because they were borderline in Year 10 can find the A Level route closed at 16 by a decision taken at 14, usually without the family understanding that was what was being decided. Dubai schools vary in how early and how firmly they tier, so the useful question at a parent evening in Al Safa is not 'how is she doing' but 'which tier is she currently on track for, and what would move her'.

What actually moves a borderline student onto Extended is rarely more biology. It is the arithmetic inside science: rearranging a formula, handling standard form, converting units, reading a gradient. Those are the skills Extended papers assume and Core papers mostly avoid. A short block on them during Year 9 or early Year 10 costs a fraction of a two-year tutoring programme and changes the tier question while it is still open.

If the entry has already been made at Core, the honest position is that this series has a ceiling and the work should aim at the top of it, with the Extended conversation moved to the next series or to the bridging year. Pretending otherwise wastes a term. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, so a student on an Edexcel code faces a different version of this question: one paper set, no ceiling, and a wider grade range to defend.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE science marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Most lost marks in IGCSE science are not lost to ignorance. They are lost in four repeatable ways, and all four are visible on a marked paper if somebody bothers to classify them. Knowing which of the four a student is in changes the plan completely, which is why the diagnostic session exists.

The first is command-term failure. A question says 'explain' and the student describes. The content is right and the marks are not awarded, because 'explain' requires a because, a mechanism, a causal link. This costs a grade on its own in Biology more often than in the other two sciences, and it is a two-session fix because it is a reading habit rather than missing knowledge.

The second is quantitative collapse. The student knows that concentration is moles over volume and still cannot get through a three-step titration calculation under time pressure, because each individual step is slow. Speed here is not a nicety; a candidate who takes four minutes on a two-minute calculation runs out of paper. Drill is the only remedy and it works quickly.

The third is pattern-matching. The student recognises a circuit that looks like one they revised, answers the remembered question, and ignores the detail that was changed. Physics punishes this hardest. The fix is forcing annotation of the actual diagram before any calculation begins. The fourth is the six-mark extended response, where a paragraph of correct general knowledge scores two of six because it was not planned against the mark allocation. Teaching a student to count the marks and plan that many distinct points is mechanical and reliable.

sections.heading: Practical science when the lessons are online
paragraphs: The reasonable question about online science tuition is what happens to the practical work. The answer is specific rather than reassuring: the practical component most IGCSE candidates in Dubai sit is Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which is a written paper about experiments rather than an experiment. It is examined on planning, variable control, instrument reading, tabulation, graph work and evaluation. Every one of those is taught better with a shared screen, a mark scheme and a real candidate response than with a beaker.

Where a school enters candidates for the practical test rather than the alternative, the hands-on work belongs to the school laboratory and always has; no tutor in any format substitutes for it. What a tutor contributes is the surrounding competence: knowing what the examiner wants recorded, how many significant figures the data justifies, why the anomalous point is circled and excluded from the line, and what an 'improvement' answer has to name. Students routinely perform an experiment competently and then lose half the marks writing it up.

The online format has one concrete advantage here that is worth stating plainly. Marking a graph is a visual, iterative activity, and a shared screen with an annotated PDF is closer to how an examiner works than a tutor leaning over a kitchen table. Past papers, mark schemes and the student's own marked work sit side by side, the session is recorded for revision, and the same material is available again the night before the exam.

Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and a page that implied otherwise would be selling something we do not run. For a science family in Al Safa the trade is explicit: you give up a person in the room, and you get a specialist in the specific syllabus code and the specific paper your child is losing marks on.

sections.heading: What a term of science support costs in this market
paragraphs: Price a term rather than an hour and the market gets easier to read. An eight-week block at one session a week is eight hours; the same block at two sessions is sixteen. Multiply the hourly band by those numbers and the difference between tiers of tutor stops being abstract. Eight hours at the budget end of the Dubai market is a few hundred dirhams; eight hours of named-examiner teaching is several thousand. Both are sold as 'science tutoring in Dubai'.

The published figures, attributed to whoever published them, run like this. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which is the budget online band where tutors are often university students. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200, which is the qualified-subject-tutor band. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, home tutors generally at AED 200 to 500, and specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED sits at AED 650. Monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

Those are market rates from the sources named, not IB Gram's price list. Three of the six ranking pages in this search publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays a tutor in. The reason to publish the bands is that they let you check a quote: a tutor asking AED 400 an hour for Year 10 single-subject science is asking at the specialist exam-year rate for work that is not specialist exam-year work, and you can now see that.

What the number should be judged against is the plan, not the hour. Sixteen hours spent on a diagnosed topic family and paper technique is worth more than forty hours of general science revision at a lower rate, and both have a price you can calculate before you start. Ask any tutor for the eight-week plan in writing and the cost of it in total. A tutor who cannot produce that is selling hours rather than an outcome, and hours are the thing families in Al Safa most often over-buy.

Market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's table and up to AED 500 for home tutors generally, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The gap is largely travel. A tutor crossing Dubai to Al Safa for a 5pm session on Al Wasl Road is committing ninety minutes of unpaid time to deliver sixty minutes of teaching, and that arithmetic is inside the hourly rate whether or not anybody says so.

What the premium buys is a person in the room, which genuinely helps some students: younger children, students who will not engage with a screen, and families who want the session visible from the kitchen. What it costs is not only money. It narrows the tutor pool to whoever can reach your address at the hour you need, and on a three-syllabus subject that is a sharp constraint. There are not many Chemistry 0620 specialists in Dubai; there are fewer who can be on Al Wasl Road at 5pm on a Tuesday in term time; and the intersection of those two sets is where the compromise happens.

The scheduling cost compounds in the pre-exam weeks, which is exactly when the sessions matter most. A travelling tutor can hold perhaps four sessions in an afternoon, so the 4.30pm and 5pm slots every family wants are allocated by who booked first in September. Sessions get cancelled for traffic. Rescheduling means finding another slot that works for the drive as well as the student. Online, the constraint is only the student's own timetable.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, coursework and what a science tutor may not do
paragraphs: IGCSE science carries less assessed coursework than the IB, but the honesty line still matters and the market in this search includes providers who cross it. One site in this cluster sells completed IB Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is not a grey area. Submitting work a student did not produce is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

What a science tutor may legitimately do is teach, model, question and give feedback. A tutor may work through a past-paper question, mark a student's own attempt against the official scheme, explain why three marks were withheld and set a comparable question to test whether the explanation landed. A tutor may teach the structure of a practical write-up and critique the student's draft. A tutor may not produce the write-up, dictate it line by line, or edit it until the words are the tutor's rather than the student's.

There is also a copyright line that tidy operations respect. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. We reference them and link to the official source; we do not host or redistribute them, and a tutor offering a drive full of boards' material is telling you something about how else they operate.

The regulatory position in Dubai is worth knowing too. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-based: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount can be quoted. Applications go through the MoHRE service 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for school staff bar paid tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar.

sections.heading: KHDA, mandatory subjects and the week your child actually has
paragraphs: Any science plan for an Al Safa family has to fit a real week, and in Dubai that week contains more than the licensed curriculum. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and it requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of which international curriculum the school is licensed for, with those requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Federal rules say the same thing from above: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the Ministry's general regulations.

The detail is specific enough to plan around. KHDA requires separate classes by group: 'For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.' Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

For a Year 11 student in Al Safa taking three separate sciences plus maths plus the mandatory subjects, the timetable is close to full before any tutoring is added. That is the real argument for a narrow eight-week block rather than an open-ended weekly commitment across three sciences: the hours have to come from somewhere, and in exam year they come out of sleep or revision. One diagnosed subject, taught properly for eight weeks, is more deliverable than three subjects taught thinly for a year.

The wider market context is useful for judging what a tutoring budget is being set against. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the exam should IGCSE science tutoring in Al Safa start?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks before your child's school mocks is the highest-value window, not eight weeks before the real papers. Mocks set predicted grades, and a student whose paper technique is fixed before mocks gets a better prediction and a calmer final term. If you have already passed mocks, six to eight weeks before the series still allows one topic family to be repaired and paper technique to be drilled. Under four weeks, the honest plan is timed papers and error elimination only, because new content learned that late is not reliable under exam pressure.

faqs.question: Which exam series do IGCSE science candidates in Dubai actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only and is not available to UAE candidates, so revision plans built around it are planning for the wrong country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school's exams officer which zone your centre is in.

faqs.question: Do we need separate tutors for Biology, Chemistry and Physics?
faqs.answer: Usually for two of the three, rarely for all three at once. Each is a distinct syllabus with its own mark scheme, and a tutor strong on organic chemistry is not automatically useful on electromagnetic induction. What changes the calculation is that the shared skills block, roughly the first three weeks of a plan, lifts all three sciences at once: command terms, graph work, significant figures and the alternative-to-practical conventions are examined identically across them. Most families start with one specialist on the weakest subject and add a second only if the diagnostic says the hours are justified.

faqs.question: What does Paper 6 test, and can it really be taught online?
faqs.answer: Paper 6 is the alternative to practical. It is a written paper about experiments, examining planning, variable control, reading instruments, tabulating results, plotting graphs, drawing lines of best fit and answering evaluation and improvement questions. None of it requires apparatus, and all of it requires a mark scheme and a real candidate response to work against. A shared screen with an annotated PDF is closer to how an examiner marks than a tutor leaning over a table, and the conventions transfer directly between Biology, Chemistry and Physics, which makes it the cheapest measurable gain in the subject.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Core science. Can a tutor get them onto Extended?
faqs.answer: Not for a series whose entries have already closed, because the tier is fixed at entry and so is the grade ceiling. For that series the sensible aim is the top of the Core range. For the next series, or during Year 9 and early Year 10, the tier question is open and the thing that usually moves a borderline student is the arithmetic inside science rather than more biology: rearranging formulae, standard form, unit conversion and reading gradients. A short block on those is far cheaper than a two-year programme and changes the conversation while the school can still act on it.

intro.heading: Which IGCSE science is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IGCSE science tutor assumes they are shopping for one thing. They are not. Within Cambridge alone, a Dubai school can enter a student for separate Chemistry (0620), Physics (0625) and Biology (0610), or for Co-ordinated Sciences as a double award (0654), or for Combined Science as a single award (0653). Pearson Edexcel runs its own separate sciences — 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1 — plus Science Double Award (4SD0) and Science Single Award (4SC0). Those routes have different paper structures, different content depth, and they produce different certificates.

That matters immediately, because a tutor prepared on separate-science resources for a Combined Science candidate will spend part of every session on content outside the student's syllabus. The student will not know. The parent will not know. It will show up as slow progress and be attributed to effort. This is the most common quiet failure in IGCSE science tutoring and it is entirely avoidable with one email to the school office.

The email asks three things: which science route is my child entered for, which syllabus codes, and which tier where tiering applies. The answer is on the statement of entry the school issues. Three lines, and the matching problem disappears. Send those lines with your first enquiry and the first session can be spent on diagnosis rather than on working out what is being taught.

The second thing a Satwa family needs to understand is the practical arrangement, because it varies and because it carries marks. Cambridge includes an alternative-to-practical paper for candidates not sitting a laboratory examination, and answering it well is a distinct taught skill: reading a scale correctly, identifying a control variable, explaining an anomaly, describing a method in procedural rather than narrative language. Students who know the science fluently lose marks on this paper because nobody taught the paper. A tutor who treats it as a by-product of content knowledge has misunderstood where those marks sit.

Geography adds a third factor. Al Satwa has almost no private schools inside it; children travel out to Oud Metha, Al Mankhool, Jumeirah, Al Safa, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim. Across those clusters, different schools make different science entry choices, which is why a neighbour's recommendation is a poor guide. The tutor who was excellent for the child next door may have been excellent at a different qualification.

Lessons from IB Gram are one-to-one and delivered live online to Al Satwa on Gulf Standard Time, with the first one free so the diagnosis costs nothing. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The trade is stated plainly: no person in the room, and a tutor matched to the exact syllabus code rather than to whoever teaches science within a short drive of Satwa.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and qualitative analysis
subjects.description: Reaction pathways and the observation language a qualitative test demands. Marks go on precise wording — white precipitate, soluble in excess — and students who describe loosely lose them. The combined routes carry a reduced version, so practising on separate-science questions wastes time.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The highest single source of lost marks in IGCSE physics. The difficulty is explaining why a reading changes when a component is altered, which requires a chain of reasoning rather than a calculation. Series and parallel reasoning rewards drawing before calculating.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, moments and motion
subjects.description: Moments questions are lost in the arithmetic of distances from a pivot rather than in the principle. Graph interpretation — distance-time against velocity-time — is a recurring examiner favourite and a recurring student confusion that one focused session usually settles.

subjects.name: Biology: enzymes, transport and osmosis
subjects.description: Explanation-heavy topics where Extended-tier questions demand reasoning rather than description. Students who describe what a graph shows and never say why lose the upper band consistently. Osmosis answers need the water-potential logic written out, not implied.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Genetic crosses are procedural and therefore quick to repair once the layout is drilled. The common loss is inconsistent notation rather than misunderstanding, and that is a half-session fix with a disproportionate return on a paper.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science routes
subjects.description: Two distinct routes that look alike on a timetable and are not alike on a paper. Content depth is reduced relative to separate sciences and the paper structure differs. A tutor using separate-science past papers for these candidates is preparing for a harder exam than the one being sat.

subjects.name: Pearson Science Double and Single Award
subjects.description: Pearson's equivalents of the combined routes, with their own specification and paper arrangement. Formula and data provision differs from Cambridge, which changes what has to be memorised. Always work from the actual specification rather than from a generic revision list.

subjects.name: Practical skills and the alternative-to-practical paper
subjects.description: Reading a scale to the right precision, identifying independent, dependent and control variables, explaining an anomaly, and writing a method as a numbered procedure. This is examinable technique and it is the most reliably neglected part of IGCSE science support.

subjects.name: Command words and mark-scheme language
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest and compare each demand a different response shape, and the mark scheme awards accordingly. Students who answer every question in the same register leave marks on every paper. A short repeated drill shifts grades faster than more content.

sections.heading: IGCSE science is at least six qualifications
paragraphs: There is no such thing as the IGCSE science syllabus. There are separate sciences, a double award and a single award, in each of two boards, and a Dubai school may use any of them. Each has its own code, its own paper structure and its own content depth, and the certificate at the end says something different. A family that does not know which one applies is not in a position to buy the right help.

The practical consequence is sharp. Content depth in Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences (0654) and Combined Science (0653) is reduced relative to the separate sciences, and the paper structure differs. A tutor working from 0620 chemistry past papers with a 0653 candidate is drilling harder questions on a wider syllabus than the student will sit. Some of that is harmless, much of it is wasted time, and some of it actively damages confidence for no examinable return.

The reverse error is just as common and more costly. A triple-science candidate given combined-route material arrives at the real paper under-prepared on depth. Because the topics are recognisable, nobody notices until a mock. By then a term has gone.

The table below lists the routes a Dubai school realistically enters students for. Take it to the school office with one question — which of these is my child on — and write the answer down. Then check that the tutor's past papers match it in the first session, which takes thirty seconds and is the single highest-value check available to a parent in this subject.

sections.heading: Four questions that test whether a tutor knows your variant
paragraphs: You do not need to understand the science to test a science tutor. You need four questions whose answers depend on knowing the specific route your child is on, and a sense of what a real answer sounds like. Ask them in the free trial lesson, where they cost nothing, and judge the specificity rather than the confidence.

The first question is simply which code the tutor thinks they are teaching. A specialist asks you before you ask them, because they know the answer changes what they prepare. Somebody who says 'IGCSE science is all much the same' has told you they do not plan to check.

The second and third probe depth: what content is in the separate sciences and not in the combined route, and how the practical skills are assessed on your child's papers. A tutor who can describe what drops out of the combined routes has taught both. A tutor who describes the alternative-to-practical paper as 'just the theory of experiments' has not taught it, because the paper has a distinct question grammar that has to be drilled.

The fourth is about your school specifically: what has the class covered so far, and when is the next assessment? A tutor who wants that information will teach against the school's sequence rather than against a generic plan. A tutor who proposes starting at the beginning of the syllabus in February is about to spend your money repeating October.

sections.heading: The practical paper nobody teaches
paragraphs: Cambridge includes an alternative-to-practical paper for candidates not sitting a laboratory examination, and it is the most reliably neglected component in IGCSE science. Students who can recite the content lose marks here because the paper examines a separate set of skills, and those skills are taught by drilling the question types rather than by knowing more science.

What the paper actually asks for is narrow and learnable. Read a scale to the correct precision, including judging where a needle or meniscus sits between marks. Identify the independent, dependent and control variables in a described experiment, which students confuse with astonishing consistency. Explain an anomalous result, which requires naming a plausible mechanism rather than saying the student made a mistake. Suggest an improvement that addresses the actual weakness in the method described. And write a method as a numbered procedure with quantities and repeats, not as a narrative.

Each of those is a pattern with a mark-scheme preference, and each is practised rather than understood. Four to six sessions on the question types will usually move a student from losing most of these marks to collecting most of them, and the block applies across chemistry, physics and biology simultaneously — which makes it the most efficient block available on a combined or double-award route.

One thing a tutor cannot replace is the laboratory itself. Practical work belongs to the school, and nobody should imply otherwise. What support can do is prepare a student for the laboratory session — the variables, the precision, the repeats — and then work with the data the student actually collected, which is both honest and where the assessed marks sit.
bullets: Scale reading to the correct precision, including between marks
Independent, dependent and control variables named correctly
Anomalies explained by mechanism, not by blaming the experimenter
Improvements that address the stated weakness in the method
Methods written as numbered procedures with quantities and repeats

sections.heading: Where the marks go in each of the three sciences
paragraphs: Each science loses marks in its own characteristic way, and a tutor who cannot name the pattern for your child's subject after reading one marked script is not worth a weekly slot. In chemistry the losses concentrate in calculation: limiting-reagent work abandoned part way, mole arithmetic attempted without a plan, and qualitative analysis answers written in loose language where the mark scheme wants precise observation terms.

In physics the dominant loss is electricity, and specifically the explanation questions. Marks are awarded for a chain of reasoning — this increases, so this decreases, so the reading falls — and students who know the answer write the conclusion and skip the chain. Moments and graph interpretation follow close behind, and both are arithmetic and convention problems rather than conceptual ones.

In biology the loss is in the gap between describing and explaining. Extended-tier questions ask why, and students answer what. Osmosis, enzyme graphs and transport in plants all reward a written logic that most students carry in their heads and never put on paper. Genetics is the exception: it is procedural, and once the cross layout is drilled, the marks come reliably.

Across all three, command words account for a quiet and substantial loss. State, describe, explain, suggest and compare each require a different response shape, and a student who answers every question in the same register leaves marks on every paper. It is the cheapest drill in the subject and it is almost never taught deliberately.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson for the same science
paragraphs: Parents often assume the board is interchangeable because the subject name is the same. It is not, and the differences are practical. Formula and data provision differs, which changes what has to be memorised. Paper structures differ. Some Pearson subjects operate modular assessment where units can be sat across series, which changes when support is best concentrated. Cambridge tiers several sciences into Core and Extended; Pearson's arrangement differs by subject.

The board is chosen by the school, not by the family, so this is not a decision to agonise over. It is a fact to establish and then respect. The question to ask is simply which board and which code, and then to confirm that the tutor's practice material matches. A tutor who shrugs at the board question is going to hand your child the wrong past papers.

The modular point deserves emphasis because it changes the shape of a plan. Where a route allows units to be sat across series, support concentrated in the weeks before each unit outperforms an even spread across two years. Where assessment is terminal, the opposite is true and a steady build with a pre-series intensive is better. Getting this wrong wastes months of effort on a correct-sounding schedule.

On materials: syllabus documents, specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. The right behaviour for any tutor or platform is to reference them and link the official source rather than hosting copies, which is why this page points to cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com instead of offering downloads.

sections.heading: What science support costs, and whether one tutor can cover three
paragraphs: Market rates in Dubai, as of October 2026, run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget online end — Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel, Bestimate putting the usual range at AED 180 to 350. The premium named tier begins near AED 500, with BartyED at AED 650. Those figures belong to the providers named, not to IB Gram.

The three-sciences question is where families lose money, and the answer depends entirely on the route. On a combined or double-award route, one tutor covering all three strands at the reduced depth those routes require is the right and cheaper arrangement. On a triple separate-science route, one tutor with equal depth in chemistry, physics and biology is uncommon, and paying a single generalist to cover all three is usually worse value than paying a specialist for the one subject in trouble.

That distinction has a direct budget consequence. A family with a triple-science candidate who funds three weekly slots is spending at specialist rates on coverage rather than on diagnosis, and two of the three subjects are often not where the marks are going. Rotating a single slot by diagnosis — chemistry this term, physics next — costs a third as much and addresses the actual problem.

The practical-paper block is the exception that applies to everyone. Because the skills it teaches cut across all three sciences at once, four to six sessions there serve the whole entry regardless of route. For a double-award candidate in particular it is the most efficient science spend available.

sections.heading: The June and November series, and the resit decision
paragraphs: Science entries are made months before the exams, and the decisions that matter are locked by those deadlines. Working backwards from a series produces a plan; working forwards from the current report card produces a reaction. For a Satwa family the useful milestones are the entry deadline, the mock window, the point eight to twelve weeks out, and the results release.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. One question to the school office — which zone is our centre in — removes a real and avoidable risk.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For the June 2026 series, results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so read the live official timetable rather than any restatement, including this one.

The resit decision is the one that catches families out. A November entry has to be made shortly after June results arrive, which is exactly when a household is least organised. Drafting the resit plan before results day — which subject, at which tier, and on what evidence — turns a scramble into a decision. It costs nothing to prepare and it is the difference between a planned retake and a missed deadline.

sections.heading: Permits, approvals and what nobody can promise
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a parent is entitled to ask about it. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears on this page, and any site quoting one is quoting something it cannot source.

On regulators: in Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is ADEK; in Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority; in Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. KHDA inspects schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises. It does not accredit individual tutors, so there is no such thing as a KHDA-approved science tutor. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, claims none, and has no UAE office.

Two final things nobody should be telling you. No tutor can promise a grade, a number of marks or an improvement in an externally assessed examination. And tutoring is not required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression — the British-track equivalency rule is five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five, and nothing about that process requires a tutor.

sections.heading: Starting, and the coverage limit stated honestly
paragraphs: Getting started is three lines and one free lesson. The three lines are the school and year group, the science route with its codes and tier from the statement of entry, and what the last piece of marked work looked like. With those, the free session goes on diagnosis instead of on introductions, and you end it with named topics you can plan against.

Cover is not uniform and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. Separate-science specialists at Extended tier are the widest pool. Double and single award routes are narrower, because fewer tutors have deliberately taught the reduced-depth specifications and many simply teach separate-science content at them, which is the mismatch this whole page is about. A specific subject combined with a fixed weekday hour is narrower still.

The honest options when the right person is not free are a short wait, which is usually weeks and almost always better than the wrong match; a different weekly slot, because a different hour is a different market; or a tutor outside the UAE working on Gulf Standard Time for the same code. What should not happen is a separate-science tutor taking a 0653 candidate without adjusting the material, which is invisible for about six weeks and costs a term.

One last note on coursework and assessed work, which applies even though most IGCSE science routes have no written coursework component. A tutor may teach content, explain assessment criteria in the board's own words, model a method on a different example, and give feedback on work the student wrote. A tutor may not write, complete, rewrite or edit assessed work to completion. One operator visible in this market sells finished Internal Assessments; the consequence of that lands on the student, not on the seller.

process.title: Email the school for the route and the codes
process.description: Three lines back: which science route, which syllabus codes, and which tier where tiering applies. It is on the statement of entry. This single email is the highest-value thing a parent can do in this subject, because it is what stops a tutor preparing for a different exam.

process.title: Check the past papers in the first session
process.description: Ask the tutor to show you which past paper they are working from and confirm the code on it matches your child's. Thirty seconds, and it catches the most common and most expensive mismatch in IGCSE science tutoring before any money is spent.

process.title: Use the free lesson for a diagnosis
process.description: Bring a marked script. The session should end with named topics: the mole calculations are the gap, the command words are costing a mark per question, the practical paper has never been practised. That list is the plan. Enthusiasm with no named topics is not.

process.title: Buy the practical-paper block early
process.description: Four to six sessions on scale reading, variables, anomalies and method writing. It applies across all three sciences at once, which makes it the most efficient block on any route, and it is the part schools most often leave to assumption.

process.title: Draft the resit plan before results day
process.description: Which subject, at which tier, and on what evidence. A November entry has to be made shortly after June results arrive, and families who decide in advance make a decision while families who do not make a scramble.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the route, not the word 'science'
whyPoints.description: 0620, 0625, 0610, 0653, 0654, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1, 4SD0 and 4SC0 are different qualifications with different depth and different papers. The match is built from the code on the statement of entry.

whyPoints.title: You get the verification questions
whyPoints.description: Four questions published on this page that test whether a tutor knows your child's variant, with the strong and weak answers written out. They cost nothing to ask inside a free lesson, of any tutor in this market including ours.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper is taught as a skill
whyPoints.description: Scale precision, variable identification, anomaly explanation and method as procedure, drilled on real question types. It is examinable, it cuts across all three sciences, and it is the most reliably neglected part of IGCSE science support.

whyPoints.title: Honest advice on three sciences or one
whyPoints.description: On a combined route, one tutor across all three strands is right and cheaper. On triple separate sciences, a specialist for the subject in trouble beats a generalist for all three. Funding three weekly slots is usually paying for coverage rather than diagnosis.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider that published it, with a date. Three of the six most visible competitors in this market publish no price and two quote US dollars.

whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. If presence in the room is the requirement, this is not the right service.

faqs.question: How can an Al Satwa parent check which IGCSE science route their child is sitting?
faqs.answer: Email the school office and ask three things: which science route, which syllabus codes, and which tier where tiering applies. The answer is printed on the statement of entry issued for the series. You are likely to hear one of Cambridge separate sciences (0620, 0625, 0610), Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences double award (0654), Cambridge Combined Science single award (0653), or the Pearson equivalents — 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1 separately, 4SD0 double or 4SC0 single. Write the answer down; it determines which past papers are the right practice material.

faqs.question: Co-ordinated Sciences or three separate sciences - what actually changes for my child?
faqs.answer: Content depth and the number of grades. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences (0654) is a double award covering all three sciences at reduced depth relative to the separate syllabuses, and the paper structure differs accordingly. Separate sciences (0620, 0625, 0610) go deeper in each subject and produce three distinct grades. Neither is better in the abstract; what matters is which one the school entered your child for, because a tutor drilling separate-science questions with a double-award candidate is preparing for a harder and wider exam than the one being sat.

faqs.question: Can one tutor really cover chemistry, physics and biology?
faqs.answer: On a combined or double-award route, yes, and it is the right arrangement — the content is reduced and coherent across the strands, and it is one slot to schedule rather than three. On a triple separate-science route, equal depth in all three is uncommon, and paying one generalist to cover all three is usually worse value than paying a specialist for the subject the diagnosis names. Rotating a single slot by diagnosis — chemistry this term, physics next — costs far less than three weekly commitments and addresses the actual gap.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and why does it cost so many marks?
faqs.answer: Cambridge includes it for candidates not sitting a laboratory examination, and it tests a distinct set of skills rather than content: reading a scale to the right precision, naming independent, dependent and control variables, explaining an anomaly by mechanism, suggesting an improvement that addresses the stated weakness, and writing a method as a numbered procedure. Students who know the science fluently lose marks here because nobody taught the paper. Four to six sessions on the question types usually flips it, and the block applies across all three sciences at once.

faqs.question: My son knows the biology and still gets 5s. What is he doing wrong?
faqs.answer: Most likely answering 'what' when the question asks 'why'. Extended-tier biology awards marks for a written chain of reasoning, and students who describe what a graph shows without explaining the mechanism lose the upper band consistently. Osmosis, enzyme activity and transport in plants all reward logic put on paper rather than held in the head. The second common cause is command words: state, describe, explain, suggest and compare each need a different response shape, and a student who answers every question in the same register leaves marks on every paper.

faqs.question: Which topic loses the most marks in IGCSE physics?
faqs.answer: Electricity, and specifically the explanation questions rather than the calculations. Marks are awarded for a chain of reasoning — the resistance rises, so the current falls, so the reading on the ammeter drops — and students who know the outcome write the conclusion and skip the chain the mark scheme is paying for. Series and parallel questions reward drawing the circuit before calculating anything. Moments and the distinction between distance-time and velocity-time graphs follow close behind, and both are convention and arithmetic problems rather than conceptual ones.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my daughter's school uses Cambridge or Pearson for science?
faqs.answer: It matters for practice material, not for quality. Formula and data provision differs between the boards, which changes what has to be memorised. Paper structures differ. Some Pearson subjects operate modular assessment where units can be sat across series, which changes whether support should be spread or concentrated before each unit. The board is chosen by the school rather than by you, so the task is simply to establish which it is and confirm the tutor's past papers match. A tutor who shrugs at the board question will hand your child the wrong papers.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE science tutor cost in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: Market figures as of October 2026: budget online runs about AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified online subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Those belong to the providers named, not to IB Gram; here the first lesson is free, so the diagnosis costs nothing before anything is priced.

faqs.question: Is there any point tutoring science online when the practicals happen at school?
faqs.answer: The laboratory belongs to the school and nobody should suggest otherwise. What online support does is handle the part that carries the marks: preparing the student for the session — variables, precision, repeats — and then working with the data the student actually collected. For Cambridge candidates it also covers the alternative-to-practical paper, which is examinable technique rather than hands-on work and which is the single largest neglected mark pool in IGCSE science. A shared screen with a past-paper question on it is genuinely the right tool for that.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to a home in Al Satwa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Sessions for Al Satwa families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen so diagrams, calculations and past-paper questions are visible and annotated. The trade is explicit: you lose a person in the room and gain a tutor matched to your child's exact syllabus code. Given how many distinct science routes exist, that match matters more in this subject than in most.

faqs.question: What time can a science lesson start for a Satwa family?
faqs.answer: Around 17:00 for the Oud Metha, Al Mankhool and Jumeirah runs, and 18:00 for Al Safa, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim. Al Satwa has almost no secondary schools inside it, so every child commutes, and looping bus routes regularly turn a 15:00 finish into a 16:15 arrival. Set the slot at least forty-five minutes after the latest arrival you have actually seen in the past fortnight. A time chosen from the published school finish slips by fifteen minutes a week and disappears by the third month.

faqs.question: When should we decide about a November resit in science?
faqs.answer: Before June results arrive, not after. A November entry has to be made shortly after results day, which is exactly when a household is least organised, so the decision gets made under time pressure or missed entirely. Draft it in advance: which subject, at which tier, and on what evidence from the mocks and the school's own assessments. Pearson's November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a resit shifts the whole timeline into the following year.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge exam zone and does it affect science papers?
faqs.answer: It affects every Cambridge paper, science included. Cambridge allocates each exam centre to one of six administrative zones and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That is a serious, entirely avoidable risk sitting behind one question to the school office. Ask which zone the centre is in, write it down, and read that zone's timetable rather than the first one a search returns.

faqs.question: Do science grades count towards UAE equivalency, and how many do I need?
faqs.answer: On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Sciences can sit inside that count, but how a double award is treated against three separate grades should be checked against the authority's own guidance rather than assumed. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced rule is five. Equivalency is an official process, not something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees.

faqs.question: Should I be looking for a KHDA-approved science tutor?
faqs.answer: No, because that credential does not exist for individuals. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai: it inspects schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises. It does not accredit individual private tutors, so the phrase should make you cautious about whoever used it. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation and claims none. What does exist is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free for two years and which you can ask to see.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for my child's exact science route?
faqs.answer: You should be told, not quietly matched. Separate-science specialists at Extended tier are the widest pool; double and single award routes are narrower, because fewer tutors have deliberately taught the reduced-depth specifications rather than simply delivering separate-science content at them. The honest choices are a short wait for the right person, a different weekly slot that opens a wider pool, or a tutor outside the UAE working on Gulf Standard Time for the same code. A mismatch on route is invisible for six weeks and costs a term.

Ask which route, which codes and which tier, and write the answer down. Then take the free first lesson, bring a marked script, and ask the tutor to show you the past paper they are working from so you can check the code on it matches. That thirty-second check catches the most common and most expensive mismatch in IGCSE science support. Lessons for Al Satwa families are one-to-one and delivered live online on Gulf Standard Time.
