dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-sufouh.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors who teach Cambridge and Edexcel International GCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics to students at schools around Al Sufouh, Knowledge Park and Al Barsha. Each one works to a named syllabus code, not to a general idea of school science.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE science search in Al Sufouh is usually really about
paragraphs: Parents in Al Sufouh rarely start looking for a science tutor because their child dislikes science. They start looking in the second half of Year 10, when the first set of real past-paper marks comes home and the gap between what the student knows and what the mark scheme rewards becomes visible. A child who can explain photosynthesis out loud scores four of a possible six because the answer named the product but not the condition. A child who understands circuits loses the last two marks of a question because the working was not set out. That is not a knowledge problem and no amount of re-reading the textbook fixes it.

The second reason is structural. Most British-curriculum schools in this corridor run three separate sciences for some students and a co-ordinated or combined course for others, and the decision about which route a child takes is made in Year 9 on the basis of Year 9 evidence. By the middle of Year 10 that decision has consequences. A student on Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is sitting one grade for three subjects; a student on 0610, 0620 and 0625 is sitting three. The content overlaps but the papers, the mark tariffs and the depth expected in a six-mark answer do not.

The third reason is timing, and it is the one nobody writes about. A secondary day in Al Sufouh typically ends between 14:45 and 15:30. Co-curricular activities, squad training and school transport push the real arrival home to somewhere between 16:00 and 17:15 depending on which school, which day and which direction the traffic on Al Sufouh Road is moving. A tutor who has to drive to the villa arrives inside that window, waits, and bills for the wait. A live video session at 17:00 or 19:30 starts at 17:00 or 19:30.

What a science tutor is for, in practical terms, is the distance between understanding and marks. That distance is measurable. It shows up as command-term failure, where a student describes when the question said explain. It shows up in the practical papers, where the candidate who has never written a method with a controlled variable named loses four marks that have nothing to do with chemistry. It shows up in the data questions, where a correct calculation arrives without a unit. All three are teachable in weeks, not years, and all three are invisible in a school report that says the student is working at expectation.

This page is written from the Al Sufouh school day outwards. It names the schools this neighbourhood feeds, the syllabus codes those schools enter candidates for, the realistic window a weekday session fits into, and what the Dubai market charges for science support at this level. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. The comparison further down the page sets out why that is the better deal for a family here rather than a compromise.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-sufouh.programmesIntro: An IGCSE science tutor in Al Sufouh works across four routes, and which one your child is on changes everything about the plan. The route is printed on the statement of entry, not on the school report, so the first question in a trial lesson is always which code the school has entered the candidate for.

programmes.name: Cambridge Single Sciences (0610, 0620, 0625)
programmes.description: Three separate qualifications, three separate grades. Each follows the same assessment shape: a multiple-choice paper worth 30% of the grade, a written theory paper worth 50%, and a practical component worth 20%. Candidates sit either the Core papers or the Extended papers, never a mixture, and the tier decision caps the grade available. This is the route most selective schools in the Al Sufouh corridor use for students heading towards Higher Level sciences or A Level.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this route is the usual precondition for IB Diploma Higher Level Biology, Chemistry or Physics at sixteen. Schools along Al Sufouh Road that run both an IGCSE and a Diploma pathway treat three separate science grades as the evidence for Higher Level entry, so the tier your child sits in Year 10 has a direct effect on Year 12 option blocks.

programmes.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences (Double Award)
programmes.description: One course, two IGCSE grades, covering biology, chemistry and physics content at reduced depth. The papers follow the same 30-50-20 split as the single sciences but the theory paper is longer and ranges across all three disciplines in a single sitting. Students who manage content well but struggle to hold three separate specifications in their head often do better here than on three separate subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Double Award is common at Dubai schools that want every student to leave with science qualifications without forcing three timetable blocks. It satisfies the Ministry of Education equivalency count as two of the five accredited subjects for the British track, and it keeps A Level science open, though a student moving to Higher Level Chemistry from 0654 has a genuine content gap to close over the summer.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Sciences
programmes.description: Edexcel runs its international sciences without a practical examination. Practical skills are assessed inside the written papers instead, which changes the revision entirely: there is no Paper 6 to practise, but there are extended method-and-evaluation questions embedded in Paper 1 and Paper 2. Codes are 4BI1 for biology, 4CH1 for chemistry, 4PH1 for physics, with 4SD0 as the Double Award.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools entered candidates with Edexcel specifically because the November series and the absence of a practical exam suit a two-site or mid-year intake. Parents in Al Sufouh with children at two different schools are frequently running a Cambridge child and an Edexcel child at the same time, and the two need different past-paper diets.

programmes.name: The route after sixteen: Diploma sciences or A Level
programmes.description: The reason IGCSE science marks matter beyond the certificate is that they decide the sixth-form door. Higher Level Diploma sciences and A Level sciences both assume a student can set out a method, handle uncertainty in data and write an extended explanation. A student who scraped a grade by learning recall questions will meet that assumption in the first month of Year 12 rather than at the exam.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students apply to UK, UAE, Canadian and Australian universities from the same cohort, and the science prerequisite differs for each. Medicine routes generally expect Chemistry at the higher tier; engineering routes expect Physics with Mathematics. Al Sufouh families often discover this during the Year 11 options conversation, which is late.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-sufouh.subjectsIntro: An IGCSE science tutor in Al Sufouh is asked for one of these ten things far more often than anything else. Each is diagnosable in a first session, and each has a known place where marks are lost rather than a vague difficulty.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Marks go missing in the long-answer questions on transport, respiration and inheritance, where a student writes a correct process with no reference to the specific organism or condition the stem named. Genetic-cross questions need the gamete row shown, not implied. The Extended tier adds plant transport detail and the nitrogen cycle.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and reacting masses are where the grade is decided. The common failure is not the arithmetic but the chain: mass to moles, moles to ratio, ratio to the wanted substance, back to mass. Students who learn each step separately stall when a question requires four of them without signposting. Organic naming and the ionic-equation rules are the other two reliable losses.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity is the section that most often produces the gap between a strong student and a strong mark. Series and parallel reasoning collapses when a question changes one resistance and asks what happens everywhere else. Momentum, pressure in fluids and the ray-diagram conventions for lenses are the other three places where method marks are left on the page.

subjects.name: IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: The difficulty is breadth under time pressure. A single theory paper moves from a food-web question to an electrolysis calculation to a wave diagram, and students who revise one discipline at a time have never practised that switching. Past-paper work for 0654 has to be done whole-paper, not topic by topic.

subjects.name: IGCSE Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: One grade from all three sciences at the lightest depth on offer. The route is appropriate for a student whose future does not require a science prerequisite, and inappropriate for one who intends to take a science at Higher Level. Deciding which of those two a child is turns out to be the most useful thing a tutor does in Year 10.

subjects.name: Practical skills: Cambridge Paper 5
subjects.description: The practical test is twenty per cent of a Cambridge single-science grade and is marked on method discipline rather than scientific insight. Candidates lose marks for a table drawn without units in the header, for a graph scaled so the plotted points occupy a third of the grid, and for a conclusion that restates the data instead of answering the question.

subjects.name: Practical skills: Cambridge Paper 6
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper tests the same skills on paper. It rewards a candidate who can name the dependent, independent and controlled variables in a described experiment, identify the source of error that actually matters, and suggest an improvement that is specific rather than the word more. All three are drillable in four to six sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics inside science papers
subjects.description: Rearranging, standard form, percentage change and gradient from a graph carry marks in all three sciences, and a student who is comfortable in a maths lesson is often not comfortable when the same skill arrives inside a physics stem. Working this separately is faster than treating it as a physics problem.

subjects.name: Command terms and tariffs
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, compare and calculate each demand a different shape of answer, and the mark tariff tells the candidate how many distinct points are wanted. A session spent mapping tariff to point count typically recovers more marks per hour than any amount of content revision.

subjects.name: Tier placement: Core or Extended
subjects.description: Core papers cap the grade available; Extended papers carry content a borderline student may not reach. Schools make this call on internal evidence, and it can usually be revisited before entries close. Testing which tier a child is actually on, using the two sets of past papers side by side, is a single-session job with a two-year consequence.

sections.heading: The Al Sufouh school day, and the hour a session can actually start
paragraphs: A weekday session has to fit between the end of school and the point where a fifteen-year-old stops being able to learn anything. In Al Sufouh that window is narrower than parents expect. Secondary days in this corridor typically finish between 14:45 and 15:30. Co-curricular blocks, squad training and school transport then push the real arrival home to somewhere between 16:00 and 17:15, depending on the school, the day and whether Al Sufouh Road is moving. Add a meal and the honest start time for a weekday session is 17:00 at the earliest for most households, and 19:00 for many.

This is the arithmetic that decides whether tutoring works or quietly stops. A family books a 16:00 slot in September because that is when the school day ends on paper. Through October the student arrives at 16:20, then 16:35, then misses one because of a fixture. By November the slot has moved twice and the sense that tutoring is another thing to manage has set in. Booking the slot the household can actually keep, even if it is later than ideal, is worth more than booking the slot that looks best on the calendar.

A tutor who travels makes this worse rather than better, and not through any fault of their own. Someone driving from Al Quoz or Jumeirah to a villa in Al Sufouh at five in the afternoon is in the same traffic as everybody else, and the arrangement has to absorb that somewhere: either the tutor arrives early and waits, or arrives late and the session is short, or the rate carries the travel. A live video session has none of that. The tutor is at a desk, the student is at a desk, and the hour that was booked is the hour that is taught.

The second thing the online format buys in this particular neighbourhood is subject match. Al Sufouh is well served for general science support. It is not well served for a tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended Paper 4 for several years and knows where the mole questions in the recent series went wrong. Restricting the search to people who can reach your villa by half past five restricts it to a handful of candidates; removing the drive widens it to anyone awake in a compatible time zone.

sections.heading: Which science route your child is on, and what each one actually assesses
paragraphs: Before a single topic is taught, the route needs establishing, because the four routes are assessed differently enough that revision advice for one is wrong for another. The route is not reliably recoverable from a school report. It is on the statement of entry, where a four-digit Cambridge code or a Pearson code appears next to the subject name, and it is worth finding before the first session rather than during it.

Cambridge single sciences share one shape. A multiple-choice paper carries thirty per cent of the grade, a written theory paper carries fifty, and a practical component carries twenty. Candidates sit either the Core set or the Extended set, and the tier caps the grade available. The practical twenty per cent splits two ways: some centres enter candidates for Paper 5, a laboratory test, and others for Paper 6, which tests the same skills on paper. Which one your child sits changes what the last six weeks of revision should contain, and a surprising number of families do not know the answer.

Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 awards two grades from one course and keeps the same weighting split, but the theory paper roams across biology, chemistry and physics in a single sitting. Students who revise discipline by discipline have never rehearsed the switching that paper demands, and they lose time rather than knowledge. The fix is whole-paper practice early, which feels premature in January and is not.

Pearson Edexcel runs its international sciences without a practical examination at all, assessing practical skills inside the written papers instead. For an Edexcel candidate there is no Paper 6 to drill, but there are extended method and evaluation questions embedded in the theory papers that a Cambridge-focused revision plan would miss entirely. Any tutor working with a child in Al Sufouh needs to know which of these two worlds the student lives in. The codes on the entry statement settle it in ten seconds.

sections.heading: The practical paper is a fifth of the grade and almost nobody practises it
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of a Cambridge single-science grade sits in the practical component, and it is the part of the course least likely to be revised. The reason is simple: it does not feel like science. Paper 6 does not ask what happens in a reaction. It asks a candidate to read a described experiment, name the variables, tabulate given results, plot them, identify the limitation that matters and suggest a specific improvement. None of that is in the textbook chapters a student revises from.

The marks lost here are mechanical and therefore recoverable quickly. A table drawn without units in the column headers loses a mark regardless of the numbers in it. A graph scaled so the points occupy the lower-left quarter of the grid loses the scale mark. A line of best fit drawn through every point rather than through the trend loses another. A conclusion that restates the readings instead of answering the question asked loses the final one or two. Four or five marks on a forty-mark paper is a grade boundary for many candidates, and none of those marks required knowing any chemistry.

The variable question is the one worth the most teaching time. A candidate who can write, in one sentence each, what was changed, what was measured and what was held the same has banked marks on every version of this paper for the last decade. Students who answer in general terms, saying the temperature was kept the same without saying how, get partial credit. Students who name the method of control get all of it. This is a sentence structure, not a concept, and it is learnable in one session and then rehearsed.

Where Paper 5 is sat instead, the same skills are tested with apparatus in front of the candidate and the clock running. That adds time pressure and the discipline of recording as you go rather than at the end. It does not change the underlying marking. A student who can write a controlled method on paper can write one in a laboratory; a student who cannot will not discover the skill under exam conditions.
bullets: Units belong in the table header, not next to each reading
Scale the axes so plotted points fill at least half the grid
Name the method of control, not just the controlled variable
An improvement must be specific; the word more earns nothing

sections.heading: Where science marks actually go, subject by subject
paragraphs: A school report that says a student is working at expectation tells a parent nothing actionable. A past paper marked question by question tells them everything. Across the students we see from this part of Dubai, the losses cluster in the same places, and they are the same places every year because they are features of the assessment rather than of the child.

In biology, the extended-response questions on transport, respiration and inheritance are where strong students underperform. The pattern is a correct general process written without reference to the specific organism, tissue or condition the question named. A six-mark question on water movement in a named plant under a named condition wants the condition in the answer. Genetic crosses need the gamete row shown on the page; a correct final ratio with the working omitted scores less than a wrong ratio with the method visible.

In chemistry, moles decide the grade. Not the arithmetic, which most students can do, but the chain of steps: mass to moles, moles to the reacting ratio, ratio to the substance the question asked about, back to a mass or a volume. Each step is taught separately in school and most students can perform each one. Assembling four of them when the question does not signpost the sequence is the skill, and it is practised by doing twenty of them in a row with the steps written out, not by re-reading the chapter.

In physics, electricity produces the widest gap between understanding and marks. A student can explain series and parallel circuits accurately and still fail a question that changes one resistance and asks what happens to the current elsewhere, because that requires reasoning through consequences rather than recalling a rule. Momentum calculations lose marks to unstated direction. Lens ray diagrams lose marks to construction lines drawn without arrows. Each of these is a specific, small, teachable fix, and together they are often two grades.

sections.heading: What IGCSE science tutoring costs around Al Sufouh
paragraphs: Start from the cheapest end rather than the premium end, because that is where most families begin and where most of the disappointment happens. Published rates from online platforms serving Dubai start low: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. At that level a parent is buying a university student or a recent graduate who knows the subject and does not know the mark scheme. For a Year 9 student who needs homework supervision that can be perfectly adequate. For a Year 11 candidate six weeks from a written paper, the thing being bought is mark-scheme literacy, and it is not available at that price.

The next band up is where IGCSE science support actually sits. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200; the broader market for a qualified subject tutor working online runs roughly AED 150 to 300. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors are quoted between AED 200 and AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey showing AED 200 to 450 plus. At the top, named or examiner-level tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED quoted at AED 650.

In-home visits are the band that distorts the comparison. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions are commonly advertised against AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. The difference is not teaching quality. It is a car, a driver's time and the risk that the hour gets compressed by traffic. In Al Sufouh, with the tram corridor and the Palm access road in the mix, that premium buys the household less than it does in a compact European city.

These are market figures, published by the companies named and by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, not IB Gram prices. We do not publish a science rate card on this page because the right number depends on tier, subject count and how many weeks remain. What a parent can verify independently is the band: three or four quotes from different provider models, each asked for the rate per sixty minutes rather than per session, will land inside the ranges above. Set the KHDA announcement of no private-school fee increase for 2026-27 alongside them when you are working out what the household can carry.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for a science student in this neighbourhood
paragraphs: This page targets a search that includes the word tutor and is read by parents who may well have meant someone at the dining table. The honest answer is that in-home tutoring is a real service in Dubai, that the market prices it between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 an hour, and that IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all. Home visits are something we run only in India. What follows is the case for the format we do deliver, made on its merits rather than by dismissing the alternative.

For science specifically, the online format has three concrete advantages that have nothing to do with cost. The first is the shared screen. A mole calculation worked in a shared document, with the four steps labelled, survives the session; a calculation worked on a notepad on a kitchen table is gone by Thursday. The second is the mark scheme. Reading a mark scheme alongside the student's own attempt, both visible to both people at once, is the exercise that moves marks, and it is awkward to do over one printed copy. The third is recording: a student can replay the five minutes where the electrolysis explanation finally landed.

The fourth advantage is the one that matters most in Al Sufouh and is the hardest to see from a search results page. Choosing a tutor who can reach your door by half past five means choosing from the people who happen to live nearby and are free at that hour. Choosing a tutor who appears on a screen means choosing the person who has taught the specific paper your child is sitting. For single-science Extended candidates, and especially for chemistry, the difference between those two pools is the difference between help and the right help.

There are students for whom a physical presence is the deciding factor, and a parent who knows that about their child should act on it. For everyone else, the thing to test is not the format in the abstract but one hour of actual teaching. Our trial lesson exists for that: one session, no card details taken, with a short written note afterwards saying what the tutor found. If the format does not suit the child, that is a useful thing to have learned in an hour rather than a term.

sections.heading: The Cambridge and Edexcel session calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: Nothing in the competitor set names a session or a deadline, which is odd, because the calendar is what makes tutoring urgent or not. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so a candidate in Dubai sits June or November and nothing else. Getting this right matters more than it sounds: a family planning around a spring series is planning around a date their child will not sit.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For results, Pearson's recent pattern is instructive: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November entry therefore means a January result, which is the detail that decides whether a resit can be reported to a university in time.

The other thing worth knowing is zoning. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs between them. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A parent in Al Sufouh should take the timetable from their own child's school rather than from a search result, because a zone mismatch is a missed paper.

Counted backwards from a June series, the useful milestones are these. Entries close months ahead, set by the centre and not negotiable afterwards; the tier decision is locked at that point. School mocks land in the winter term and are the last honest diagnostic before the real thing. Practical components are scheduled separately from theory papers, sometimes weeks apart. Specific dates move between series, so every one of them should be read off the live official timetable rather than a page like this one.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and the permit question
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. A parent in Al Sufouh reading an inspection report should treat the science judgement and the attainment-versus-progress distinction as the useful parts; a school can be judged strong overall while a particular subject sits a band lower.

The context behind the market is worth knowing too. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private-school fees for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Seven new private schools join the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places.

Alongside the licensed international curriculum, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval. A science-focused plan has to fit around those timetabled hours rather than pretend they are not there.

On tutoring itself: private tuition in the UAE is permit-based. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE app, website and e-services system. IB Gram holds no KHDA, MoE or MoHRE accreditation and makes no such claim.

sections.heading: What a science tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: IGCSE science carries less internally assessed coursework than the Diploma does, which makes this section shorter but not less important, because many Al Sufouh households are running an IGCSE child and a Diploma sibling at the same time and the rules differ. For IGCSE science, the assessment is almost entirely external: written papers and a practical component sat under supervision. There is no extended piece of writing to be improperly helped with, which removes the biggest integrity risk in one stroke.

Where the line does matter is in school-set work that feeds a predicted grade, and in the Diploma Internal Assessment if the student moves on to Higher Level science. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain a mark scheme, model a worked example on a different question and give feedback on the student's own attempt. A tutor may not write the Internal Assessment, draft the analysis, or produce a conclusion for the student to submit. One company in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. That is a malpractice trigger for the student, with consequences that outlast any grade.

The practical distinction is simple enough to apply. If the output is in the student's words and the tutor has commented on it, that is teaching. If the output contains sentences the tutor supplied, it is not the student's work, regardless of how the file was shared. A good tutor says so at the start and refuses the request when it comes, which it occasionally does, usually from the parent rather than the student and usually in April.

On materials: past papers and mark schemes are published by the boards and should be taken from their own sites. We reference and link them; we do not reproduce or supply syllabus documents, papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. For Cambridge codes that is cambridgeinternational.org and for Edexcel codes qualifications.pearson.com, and for the version of the specification your child is actually sitting, the school's examinations officer is the fastest route.

sections.heading: Starting mid-year, and what happens if the specialist is busy
paragraphs: Most science enquiries from Al Sufouh arrive at two moments: after the winter mock results and in the eight weeks before a June series. Both are late and both are workable, but they call for different plans. After mocks there is time to fix causes, which means variable-writing, mole chains, electricity reasoning and command-term discipline, in that order of return per hour. Eight weeks out there is time to fix symptoms, which means paper-by-paper drilling on the two topics that cost the most marks and leaving the rest alone.

The sequence is the same either way. A trial lesson diagnoses, using past-paper questions on the Core and Extended tiers so the tier itself gets tested rather than assumed. A written note follows within a day, naming the specific losses and what the first block of sessions will address. Then a weekly slot the household can genuinely keep, in the window the school day leaves rather than the one that looks tidiest, and a review at the school's next assessment point against evidence rather than impression.

Availability deserves an honest answer, because no competitor in this market gives one. Core demand from this neighbourhood is Cambridge Extended Biology, Chemistry and Physics, and that is well covered with UAE-hours tutors. Narrow requests are not always instant: Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 whole-paper specialists, Edexcel 4CH1 at short notice in the fortnight before a series, and anyone needed at exactly 16:00 GST on a Sunday can take several days to match. When no suitable UAE-hours tutor is free, we say so and offer the nearest workable slot rather than putting a generalist in front of a Year 11 candidate.

The trial lesson is free and the condition is stated here rather than in small print: one session per student, no payment details collected beforehand, and no obligation afterwards. If the written note that follows does not describe your child recognisably, that is the signal to stop. Families in Al Sufouh who book a diagnostic and nothing else, then take the written recommendation into a school options meeting, have used this well.

process.title: Send the subject, the code and the year group
process.description: The single most useful thing you can send is the syllabus code from the statement of entry: 0620, 0654, 4CH1. With the code, the year group and the school, a tutor can be matched to the exact paper your child sits rather than to the subject in general. The school's examinations officer will confirm the code in a sentence if you do not have it.

process.title: Book the trial in the slot you can actually keep
process.description: Pick the hour that survives a late bus and an activity block, not the one that looks neatest. For most Al Sufouh households that is 17:30 or 19:00 GST on a weekday, or a weekend morning if the work is whole-paper practice. One free trial session per student, with no payment details collected beforehand.

process.title: Read the written note the next day
process.description: After the trial the tutor sends a short written note: which tier the evidence supports, where the marks were going, and what the first block of sessions will target. It is written to be shown to the school. If it does not describe your child recognisably, say so and we will change the tutor or tell you tutoring is not the issue.

process.title: Run a weekly slot and review at the school's own checkpoints
process.description: Sessions follow the school's topic order with the tutor staying a fortnight ahead of the class. Progress is measured at the school's own assessment points using marked past-paper questions, not at intervals we invent. If three checkpoints pass without movement, the plan changes rather than continuing.

process.title: Switch to paper drilling in the final term
process.description: Six to eight weeks out, the weekly session changes shape: whole questions under timed conditions, mark scheme opened afterwards, and the practical component drilled on its own. This is the point at which knowing whether your child sits Paper 5 or Paper 6 stops being trivia.

whyPoints.title: The hour booked is the hour taught
whyPoints.description: No travel means no compression. A session at 17:30 starts at 17:30 whether or not Al Sufouh Road is moving, and if the school bus is late the start can shift by ten minutes with a message rather than costing the session. Over a two-term engagement that difference is several hours of actual teaching.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 Extended and Edexcel 4CH1 are both IGCSE chemistry and they are not the same job. Tutors are matched to the paper your child sits, including whether the practical component is Paper 5 or Paper 6, because the last six weeks of revision depend on that answer.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes read, not described
whyPoints.description: The exercise that moves a science grade is reading the official mark scheme against the student's own attempt, line by line, and seeing where the point was awarded. On a shared screen both people see both documents at once. It is the single most repeatable improvement available in IGCSE science.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE science session realistically start in Al Sufouh?
faqs.answer: Secondary days in this corridor typically finish between 14:45 and 15:30, but co-curricular blocks and school transport push most students home between 16:00 and 17:15. Add a meal and the honest answer for a weekday is 17:00 at the earliest, with 17:30 and 19:00 the two slots that hold best across a full term. Families on Palm Jumeirah or in Emirates Hills usually find 19:30 safer because it removes the trunk-road variable entirely. Book the hour your household can keep rather than the one that looks tidiest, because a slot that drifts twice in October tends to be abandoned by November.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE science syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: The code is on the statement of entry, which the school issues ahead of the series. It appears next to the subject name as a four-digit Cambridge number such as 0620 or 0654, or as a Pearson code such as 4CH1. If you do not have the statement, the school's examinations officer will confirm it in one email, and it is worth asking before the first tutoring session rather than during it. The code determines whether there is a practical examination, whether your child sits Core or Extended papers, and which past papers are the right ones to work from.

faqs.question: Does my child sit Paper 5 or Paper 6 for the Cambridge science practical?
faqs.answer: That depends on what the centre entered, and it is the question most families cannot answer. Paper 5 is a laboratory test with apparatus; Paper 6 is the alternative to practical, which tests the same skills on paper. Both carry twenty per cent of a single-science grade. The school's examinations officer knows which one is on the entry. The answer changes the final six weeks of revision substantially: Paper 6 rewards drilled variable-writing, tabulation and graph discipline, while Paper 5 adds the pressure of recording as you go with a clock running.

faqs.question: Is Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 easier than taking three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: It is less content at less depth, which is not the same as easier. 0654 awards two grades from one course and keeps the thirty, fifty, twenty weighting split, but the theory paper moves between biology, chemistry and physics within a single sitting. Students who revise one discipline at a time have never rehearsed that switching and lose time rather than knowledge. The route suits a student who handles breadth well and struggles to hold three specifications separately. A student heading for Higher Level Chemistry will have a real content gap to close over the summer.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Core to Extended papers, or the other way?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, until the centre confirms entries, after which the tier is locked. The decision is made by the school on internal evidence and it can normally be revisited if the evidence changes. What makes the conversation productive is data: Core and Extended past-paper questions on the same topics, attempted and marked, so the discussion is about what the child can actually do rather than about confidence. A single diagnostic session produces that, and the written note from it is designed to be taken into a school meeting.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand the science but still lose marks in the written papers?
faqs.answer: Because the papers reward a particular shape of answer, and that shape is a separate skill from the content. The command term tells the candidate what kind of answer is wanted and the mark tariff tells them how many distinct points to make. A student who describes when the question said explain writes something true that earns nothing. Units left off a calculation, a genetic cross without the gamete row, an electricity answer that recalls a rule instead of reasoning through a change: all of these are cases of knowing the science and not showing it in the form the mark scheme can credit.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE science tutoring cost in Dubai in 2026?
faqs.answer: Budget online platforms publish from AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from 33 to 52 and EdFlik from 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor working online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists are quoted between AED 200 and 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 500 including travel, per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table. These are market figures published by those providers, not IB Gram prices; the right number for your family depends on tier, subject count and weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Are tutors in Dubai required to hold a permit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE operates under a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified. The official route is MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold the permit.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Dubai actually sit for Cambridge IGCSE?
faqs.answer: June or November. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so it does not apply to a candidate in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Take the actual dates from your own school, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and the timetable differs between them.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting science tutoring eight weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the plan has to change shape. Eight weeks is not enough to fix underlying causes across three sciences, and trying produces a plan that touches everything and improves nothing. What eight weeks does allow is targeted work on the two topics costing the most marks, plus the practical component, which is twenty per cent of a Cambridge single-science grade and is the part least likely to have been revised. A first session should identify those three targets from marked past-paper evidence and ignore the rest of the specification deliberately.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in Al Sufouh?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market here is real and priced at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, so if a physical presence is the deciding factor for your child, that option exists elsewhere. For science specifically, the shared screen, the mark scheme read side by side and the choice of a tutor who has taught your child's exact paper tend to matter more than the room.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle biology, chemistry and physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being careful about it. A tutor can reasonably cover two sciences at Core level or support all three on general study skills and command-term discipline. At Extended level, and particularly in the final two terms, each science has its own mark-scheme habits and its own traps, and a specialist in one is rarely equally sharp in the others. Most families we work with use one tutor for the science that is genuinely weak and leave the other two alone, which is cheaper and usually produces more movement.

faqs.question: My child studies online, so how is the practical work covered?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge candidates the practical component is sat at the school as the examination centre, either as Paper 5 with apparatus or as Paper 6 on paper, and nothing about online tutoring changes that. What tutoring covers is the assessed skill: naming the independent, dependent and controlled variables with the method of control stated, tabulating with units in the header, scaling axes properly, drawing a trend line, and writing a conclusion that answers the question. Edexcel candidates sit no practical examination at all, so the same skills are drilled inside the theory papers instead.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson include, and what is the catch?
faqs.answer: One session per student, taught by the tutor who would take the weekly slot, with no payment details collected beforehand and no obligation afterwards. The tutor works through past-paper questions at both tiers so the session produces evidence rather than a chat, and a short written note follows within a day naming where the marks were going and what a first block would target. The note is written so it can be shown to the school. The condition is simply one trial per student; if the note does not describe your child recognisably, that is the signal to stop.

faqs.question: Which Al Sufouh schools do your students come from?
faqs.answer: Students we support near Al Sufouh attend schools across the Al Sufouh Road and Knowledge Park corridor and the Al Barsha cluster just inland, including Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School, Regent International School, Dubai American Academy and, a short drive inland, American School of Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha and Dubai International Academy Al Barsha. Those schools are named as context for the neighbourhood, not as clients or partners; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them. What matters operationally is which board each one enters candidates with, because siblings at two schools often need two different past-paper diets.

faqs.question: How will I know whether the science tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: By marks on marked work at the school's own assessment points, not by a feeling at the end of a session. After each session the tutor sends a short written note. At each school checkpoint the question asked is whether the specific losses named in the diagnostic note have reduced, measured on past-paper questions rather than on class tests of varying difficulty. If three consecutive checkpoints show no movement, the plan is wrong and should change: a different tutor, a different target, or an honest conversation about whether tutoring is addressing the real problem.

If the note does not describe your child, stop there. If it does, the weekly slot runs against the school's own assessment points, and six weeks before the series the work changes shape to timed papers and the practical component.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-twar.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics for Year 10 and Year 11 students in Al Twar, Al Qusais and Mirdif, on Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications, in evening and weekend slots.

intro.heading: How do three sciences fit into one Al Twar week?
paragraphs: Start with the arithmetic rather than the teaching. A student entered for Biology, Chemistry and Physics as separate qualifications is sitting six or more papers, has three subject teachers setting work independently, and in science subjects will also be producing practical work whenever a laboratory happens to be free. None of those three teachers knows what the other two set on Tuesday. The result is a week in which the science workload is genuinely heavy and wholly unpredictable.

Then add the Al Twar afternoon. Schools in this cluster finish between roughly 2pm and 3.30pm, and Al Twar sits towards the end of most bus loops, so add thirty to forty-five minutes. By the time a Year 10 student has changed, eaten and made a first pass at whatever the three science teachers set, it is well past five. The usable window runs to about 6.30pm before the evening meal, and then from about 7.30pm to nine. Families with a school place in Mirdif, Al Garhoud or Festival City should assume the earlier window does not exist.

The instinct at this point is to add tutors, one per science. It is the most common and most expensive mistake families in this district make, and it fails for a scheduling reason rather than a financial one. Three weekly science tutors means three sessions and three sets of work between sessions, dropped into a week that had no spare capacity before they arrived. The student then does none of it properly and all three tutors conclude the problem is motivation.

The arrangement that works is rotation. One science at a time, four weeks each, in sequence, so that no week ever contains more than one tutoring commitment on top of school. Over a term each science gets a concentrated block rather than a thin trickle, which suits science content because it is organised in topics rather than in continuous sequences. This is the recommendation that surprises Al Twar parents most, and it is the one we make most often. It also costs less than the arrangement it replaces, which is why it is worth hearing from a tutoring service rather than only from another parent.

One thing to state plainly. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE science tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for diagrams, calculations and marked past papers. In a rotation that has to move when a practical write-up lands, that matters: a session shifts by a day at no cost to anyone, which is impossible once somebody has set off across the city. The rest of this page sets out the rotation, the practical routes and what each option costs.

sections.heading: Separate or combined: the entry that sets the weekly load
paragraphs: Before buying anything, establish which science entry your child holds, because it determines both the content and the weight of the week. A student entered for three separate sciences sits six or more papers across Biology, Chemistry and Physics, each with its own theory and practical components. A student on a combined or co-ordinated route, such as Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences as a double award, sits fewer papers with reduced content in each. The difference in weekly workload is substantial and the difference in revision material is total.

Report cards do not always reveal which one applies. A single Science grade can describe either route. The reliable answer is the entry code from the examinations officer: Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 for separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics, 0654 for Co-ordinated Sciences, or the Pearson Edexcel equivalents 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Ask for the codes and the tier where tiering applies, and the whole plan becomes correct for the cost of one email.

The post-16 consequence is worth raising in Year 10 rather than Year 11. Separate sciences at the upper tier keep A Level science and IB Higher Level science routes open. A combined route keeps most other routes open and reduces the weekly load materially, which for a student whose direction lies elsewhere is a sensible trade rather than a demotion. What does not work is a family assuming that a Higher Level science remains straightforwardly available two years after a combined entry.

Where tutoring helps differs by route, which is why the entry has to be established first. On separate sciences the gain is depth in one subject at a time, taken in rotation, because three simultaneous science tutors produce a student with no evenings. On a combined route the gain is paper technique across all three, because the content per topic is thinner and marks are lost in how questions are read rather than in what is known.

sections.heading: Paper 5 or Paper 6: which practical route your centre uses
paragraphs: Cambridge science candidates sit one of two practical components and they require genuinely different preparation. The Practical Test is a hands-on examination in a laboratory: following and sometimes adapting a method under time pressure, handling apparatus, and recording observations precisely. The Alternative to Practical is a written paper about experimental method and data, answerable from a description of an experiment the candidate never performed. Which one applies is a decision made by the centre, not by the student, and most parents have never been told which.

Ask the examinations officer, because the preparation diverges. For the Practical Test, the useful work is procedural and precision-focused: reading a thermometer or burette to the right resolution, recording what was seen rather than what was expected, and managing time when a method has several stages. For the Alternative to Practical, the useful work is written analysis: identifying variables, spotting the flaw in somebody else's method, choosing a sensible graph scale, dealing with an anomaly and proposing an improvement that names a specific measurement rather than saying improve accuracy.

Both routes are coachable on screen, which parents reasonably doubt about the hands-on one. The written analysis half is obviously so. For the Practical Test, what can be taught remotely is everything except the muscle memory: the logic of the method, what to record and to what precision, how to lay out a results table before starting, and how to manage the clock. That is most of the mark, and the apparatus handling is what the school's own practical lessons are for.

The commonest lost marks on either route are the same handful, and none of them is a knowledge gap. Students write improve accuracy instead of naming the measurement to repeat. They plot with an awkward scale and lose a mark before any data is read. They record to a precision the instrument cannot support. They identify an anomaly and then include it in the line of best fit anyway. Four or five marked sets, and the pattern changes.

sections.heading: A four-week rotation that fits an Al Twar week
paragraphs: The rotation is the practical answer to a three-science week, and it is simple enough to describe in a paragraph. Pick the science currently costing most marks and give it four weeks of weekly sessions with short practice sets between them. Then move to the next, and then the third. Over a twelve-week term each science has had a concentrated block, and in no single week has the student carried more than one tutoring commitment on top of school.

It works because science content is modular. A four-week block on chemistry moles, electrolysis and ionic equations finishes a job: the student leaves it able to do something they could not do before. Four weeks later, when physics comes round, the chemistry does not evaporate, because the work was consolidated rather than sampled. Compare that with three parallel weekly sessions, each producing a practice set the student has no time to attempt, which consolidates nothing in any subject.

The order matters and should be chosen on evidence rather than on which subject the student complains about. Ask each science teacher which topic is costing marks; they will usually tell you plainly. Chemistry generally needs the most hours because moles cannot be remembered, physics the fewest because its faults are technique, and biology the least diagnostic attention because marked data-question practice does most of the work. That is a typical ordering, not a rule.

Build two pieces of slack into the rotation. First, the right to move a session by a day when a practical write-up lands, which in a three-science week will happen most weeks. Second, a spare week at the end of each block to absorb a school event. A rotation with no slack collapses in the first busy fortnight, and the family concludes the plan did not work when what failed was the absence of margin.

sections.heading: Why three science tutors is the wrong answer
paragraphs: It is the arrangement families reach for and it fails predictably. Three weekly science sessions in a week that already contains three science homework streams produces four or five hours of additional commitment, plus three sets of practice work. A Year 10 student in Al Twar who is home at 3.15pm and has a fixed evening meal does not have that capacity. So the practice work does not get done, and practice is where science learning actually happens. The sessions keep going ahead, the invoices keep arriving, and nothing moves.

There is a second failure that is less obvious. Three tutors each see one subject and nobody sees the pattern. If a student is losing marks in all three sciences because their rearrangement and unit handling are weak, which is extremely common, then three science tutors will each treat it as a science problem in their own subject. A rotation with one tutor, or one tutor who takes two of the three, notices that the fault is mathematical and says so. That single observation saves more than the arrangement costs.

The third problem is financial and quiet. Three weekly sessions at the published mid band of AED 150 to 300 an hour is roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600 a month on Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly sessions, for an arrangement whose practice component is not happening. The same budget spent on one rotating science, plus a budget-tier tutor to mark practice sets, does considerably more. Families rarely compare the two because the second option looks like less.

There is a case for two concurrent sciences, and it is worth naming so this does not read as a rule. A Year 11 student with a genuine gap in two subjects and a mock in six weeks may need both at once, accepting that the practice will be thinner. That is a deliberate trade made with the clock in mind, which is different from adding a third tutor in October because a report card was disappointing.

sections.heading: Reading three science grades on one report
paragraphs: Grading across three sciences can be genuinely confusing, and the confusion leads families to fund the wrong subject. Cambridge IGCSE sciences are reported on A* to G in their standard syllabus variants and on 9 to 1 in the numbered variants a school may have entered instead. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are reported on 9 to 1. A single report can therefore carry letters for one science and numbers for another, with no change in performance behind the difference.

Internal reporting adds a second layer. Many schools publish working-at or predicted grades during Year 10 on their own scale, which need not map onto either published scale. A working-at 5 in a school's internal system is not necessarily a 5 at the end, and only the school can explain its own mapping. Ask for that explanation in writing; it is usually a paragraph and it changes how every subsequent report reads.

Tiering is the third layer and the one with consequences. Where a Cambridge science is entered at Core rather than Extended, the achievable grade is capped, so a student reported near the top of Core is not near the top of the subject. For post-16 planning that distinction matters, because A Level and Diploma Higher Level prerequisites are expressed on the full scale. Pearson Edexcel runs its International GCSE sciences untiered, which removes the issue in those subjects.

The practical instruction before buying tutoring is to get three things in writing: which scale each science is reported on, the tier where tiering applies, and what the school's internal grades mean relative to the published scale. Then the rotation can be ordered against the real position rather than the apparent one. Families regularly discover at this point that the science they were about to fund is fine and another one is not.

sections.heading: Mock season, and what a science block should contain
paragraphs: Mock season changes the shape of the week rather than its weight. The school day fills with timed papers and revision sessions, so the early evening window effectively disappears and the student's own revision takes the later one. A tutoring arrangement built for ordinary term time does not survive that unaltered, and the usual outcome is three or four cancelled sessions and a lost month at the worst possible point in Year 11.

The adjustment is to move teaching to Saturday morning and convert the weekday slot into a short marking session on one timed paper. That is a different product from a teaching session and it is the right one for the period: the student is already revising, and what they need is somebody to tell them accurately where the marks went. Marking one paper properly, with the pattern named, is worth more in that fortnight than an hour of new content.

Choose two sciences rather than three for a mock block, and choose them on evidence. Ask each teacher what is recoverable; they will usually be frank. A block aimed at two sciences where marks can realistically move produces a better result than one spread across three where it cannot. A tutor who tells you everything is fixable in six weeks is selling comfort; one who names which two papers can move is giving you something to act on.

The practical component deserves its own fortnight inside the block, because it is the part schools least often drill separately and the part that transfers across all three sciences. Four or five marked sets on the route your centre enters for will change performance on that paper in every science at once, which makes it the most efficient fortnight available in the whole mock run.

sections.heading: What three sciences cost per month in this market
paragraphs: Think in months, because that is how the decision is actually made. Bestimate's 2026 survey puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Run three sciences in parallel at the mid band and you are at AED 1,800 to 3,600 a month. Run one at a time in rotation and you are at AED 600 to 1,200, with the remaining capacity available for a budget-tier tutor to mark practice sets.

The hourly bands behind those figures, read in October 2026 and attributed to their publishers: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate and up to AED 500 with independent home tutors; and BartyED advertising AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages appear at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The rotation plus budget-marking combination is the one worth costing properly, because it is both cheaper and better for a three-science student. One mid-band science session a week plus a weekly budget-tier session to mark practice from all three sciences comes to roughly AED 840 to 1,800 a month. That is less than three parallel mid-band sessions and it solves the problem parallel sessions create, which is that nobody was checking whether the practice happened.

Context for an Al Twar household. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the school line flat, a family can set a science tutoring figure for two years and hold it, which matters more with three sciences than with one. None of the figures here is an IB Gram price; the trial lesson is free.

sections.heading: Prayer times, Ramadan and a three-science week
paragraphs: With three sciences the week has less tolerance for a badly placed slot than usual, so the constraints are worth settling at the booking stage rather than being worked around later. A session that reliably runs into Maghrib will be cut short or cancelled; one scheduled to finish before it or start after it simply holds. Because lessons run over live video, moving a slot by thirty or forty minutes for a whole term is an administrative change rather than a logistical one.

Ramadan needs a planned shift rather than an improvised one. School days shorten, household rhythms change, and the useful study window moves to after Iftar, typically from around 8.30pm. The adjustment that works is a shorter, sharper session, forty-five minutes of marked past-paper work rather than ninety minutes of new content, with new teaching moved to weekend mornings. For a rotation, Ramadan is usually the right time to run the practical-component block, because written analysis is less demanding than new content.

Travel is the third factor. Many Al Twar households are away for part of the long break and part of the winter holiday. Over video a session can follow the family rather than pausing, which with three sciences is more valuable than it sounds: a rotation that stops for three weeks loses its sequence, and restarting it costs a block. Tell us the travel dates when the plan is made and the rotation is built around them.

One further scheduling note specific to this cluster. Al Twar families sometimes hold a school place across the Sharjah boundary, where private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than KHDA, and term dates and mock windows can differ by a week. With three sciences and a rotation, a week's difference in the mock date changes which block should be running when. Tell us the school by name and the plan follows its calendar rather than the district average.

faqs.question: How many tutoring hours do three separate sciences need each week?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families assume, because the limit is the week rather than the subject count. One tutoring session a week, rotating between the sciences in four-week blocks, is the arrangement that works for most separate-science students in this district. Three parallel weekly sessions produce four or five hours of commitment plus three practice sets in a week that had no spare capacity, so the practice stops happening, and practice is where science learning actually occurs.

faqs.question: Should we rotate the sciences or tutor all three at once?
faqs.answer: Rotate, in almost every case. Science content is modular, so a concentrated four-week block on chemistry moles and electrolysis finishes a job the student leaves able to do, while a thin weekly trickle across three subjects consolidates nothing in any of them. Rotation also keeps the week to one tutoring commitment at a time. Order the rotation by asking each science teacher which topic is costing marks, rather than by which subject your child finds least pleasant.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a science tutor to our home in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE science tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for diagrams, calculations and marked past papers. For a three-science rotation that has to move when a practical write-up lands, that is the practical advantage: a session shifts by a day at no cost to anybody, which is impossible once somebody has set off across the city.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Practical Test and the Alternative to Practical?
faqs.answer: The Practical Test is a hands-on examination in a laboratory: following and sometimes adapting a method under time pressure, handling apparatus and recording observations precisely. The Alternative to Practical is a written paper about experimental method and data, answerable from a description of an experiment the candidate never performed. The centre decides which route your child sits, so ask the examinations officer. The preparation differs: procedural precision for one, written flaw-spotting and data analysis for the other.

faqs.question: Can the hands-on practical paper be prepared for online?
faqs.answer: Most of it, yes, with one honest exception. What transfers on screen is the logic of the method, what to record and to what precision, how to lay out a results table before starting, and how to manage the clock across a multi-stage procedure. That accounts for a large share of the marks. What cannot be taught remotely is the muscle memory of handling apparatus, and that is exactly what your child's school practical lessons provide. The two halves complement each other rather than competing.

faqs.question: Which science should we fund first?
faqs.answer: Ask the three teachers, then follow the evidence rather than the complaints. Typically chemistry needs the most hours, because moles, reacting masses and concentration cannot be remembered and have to be understood. Physics needs the fewest, because its losses are technique: units, rearrangement order and missing units in the final answer. Biology needs the least diagnostic attention, because marked application and data-question practice does most of the work. That is the usual ordering, not a rule for your child.

faqs.question: Why are my son's marks low in all three sciences at once?
faqs.answer: Very often because of one underlying fault rather than three subject gaps, and the fault is usually mathematical. Rearranging a formula after substituting rather than before, handling standard form, and ratio and percentage work all appear throughout chemistry, physics and biology. Three separate science tutors will each treat this as a problem in their own subject. One tutor, or a rotation, sees it once and names it, which is frequently the single most valuable observation in the whole arrangement.

faqs.question: My report shows letters for one science and numbers for another. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the boards and syllabus variants differ. Cambridge IGCSE sciences are reported on A* to G in the standard variants and on 9 to 1 in the numbered variants a school may have entered, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are reported on 9 to 1. A single report can therefore carry both with no difference in performance behind it. Many schools also add internal working-at grades on their own scale. Ask the school which scale each science uses and how its internal grades map on.

faqs.question: Does a double award in science close off A Level sciences?
faqs.answer: It can restrict some routes, which is why it deserves a conversation rather than a default. A combined or co-ordinated route covers all three sciences in reduced depth and reduces the weekly load materially, which for a student heading in a non-science direction is a sensible trade. Separate sciences at the upper tier keep A Level and Diploma Higher Level science open. Raise it in Year 9 or Year 10 with the school, and ask specifically what their own sixth form requires for science entry.

faqs.question: How should a science plan change during mock season?
faqs.answer: Invert it. The school week fills with timed papers and revision, so the early evening window disappears and the student's own revision takes the later one. Move teaching to Saturday morning and convert the weekday slot into a short session marking one timed paper, which is a different product and the right one for the period. Target two sciences rather than three, chosen by asking each teacher what is realistically recoverable, and give the practical component its own fortnight.

faqs.question: What does a three-science tutoring plan cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Three parallel mid-band sessions come to roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600 a month on Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates of AED 600 to 1,200 per weekly session. A rotation of one science at a time is AED 600 to 1,200. Adding a weekly budget-tier session to mark practice from all three sciences, at the published AED 45 to 65 of EdFlik or AED 33 to 52 of Tutopiya, brings the total to roughly AED 840 to 1,800. These are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for someone just to mark practice work?
faqs.answer: With three sciences, frequently yes, and it is the most under-used purchase in this market. The reason parallel tutoring fails is that nobody checks whether the practice happened or what it showed. A budget-tier tutor at the published AED 45 to 65 an hour, marking one set from each science weekly and reporting the pattern, costs little and closes exactly that gap. It is also a job the budget band does genuinely well, which is not true of diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can science sessions be arranged around prayer times?
faqs.answer: Yes, and with three sciences it is worth settling at the booking stage rather than adjusting later, because the week has little tolerance for a badly placed slot. A session that reliably runs into Maghrib gets cut short or cancelled, while one scheduled to finish before it or start after it simply holds for the term. Since lessons run over live video, moving a slot by thirty or forty minutes involves no travel to re-plan and is an administrative change.

faqs.question: Does a rotation have to pause when we travel?
faqs.answer: No, and keeping it running matters more with three sciences than with one. Because lessons are delivered over live video on Gulf Standard Time, a session can follow the family through a trip rather than stopping and restarting cold. A rotation that pauses for three weeks loses its sequence, and recovering that costs most of a block. Tell us the travel dates when the plan is made, including a reduced frequency across the break if that suits, and the rotation is built around them.

faqs.question: Our school is across the Sharjah boundary. Does that affect the plan?
faqs.answer: With a rotation, yes, specifically through the calendar. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, while Sharjah private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Term dates and mock windows can differ by a week, and a week's difference changes which block should be running when. Tell us the school by name and the rotation follows its calendar rather than the district average.

faqs.question: How do I judge whether a science tutor is worth keeping after a block?
faqs.answer: At the end of a four-week block, ask two questions. First, can your child now do something specific they could not do four weeks ago, named precisely rather than described as improved confidence? Second, did the tutor tell you anything you did not know, such as that the real fault was mathematical or that the practical route needed separate work? A block that produces a named capability and one useful observation has earned the next one. Vague progress reports have not.

Each has marked to the published schemes and can tell you, after one session, whether the problem is content, written technique or the practical component nobody revised.

intro.heading: What science tutoring costs an Al Warqa family, and what it buys
paragraphs: Start with the bill rather than the brochure. A single IGCSE science subject supported once a week by a qualified online tutor runs from AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month at the market rates Dubai providers publish. Three separate sciences, taught by three people, triple that figure without tripling the result. Most Al Warqa families who come to us are already spending somewhere in that range and cannot say which of the three subjects the money is actually improving. That is the problem this page is built to solve: not whether to spend, but where.

Al Warqa sits in the eastern half of Dubai, within a short drive of some of the largest year groups in the emirate. The schools around Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Mirdif run cohorts where a science teacher may see well over a hundred and fifty students a week. Content coverage in those rooms is generally thorough. What is scarce is the thing that converts a grade: somebody reading your child's written answer, line by line, against the mark scheme, and saying why the second mark was not awarded. You are not buying missing information. You are buying marking attention.

That distinction decides the price you should pay. A budget tutor at the bottom of the Dubai market, from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, will re-explain electrolysis or the eye perfectly well. Re-explanation is not usually the gap. A tutor at AED 150 to AED 300 who has marked Paper 4 scripts can look at a six-mark answer about osmosis and identify that the candidate described the direction of movement but never named the water potential gradient, which is where the final two marks lived. The price difference between those two tutors is often smaller than the difference in what they change.

The second place money disappears in Al Warqa is the practical component. Cambridge puts a fifth of the final science grade into either Paper 5, a hands-on practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical. Families almost never buy tutoring for it. Students arrive at the paper having drawn perhaps four graphs in two years, with no habit of labelling axes with quantity and unit, and lose marks that required no scientific knowledge at all. An hour a fortnight on tables, graphs, anomalies and variable control is the cheapest grade movement available in the whole subject.

The third is timing. Science tutoring bought in the final six weeks before the June series is the most expensive version of itself, because the only thing left to do is damage limitation on three subjects at once. The same money spent across Year 10 and the first two terms of Year 11 buys tier decisions made on evidence, Extended-only topics taught when they appear rather than in a panic, and a Paper 6 habit built slowly. We would rather tell you that in October than take a larger fee in April.

Everything that follows is priced, sourced and specific to the eastern suburbs. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. The comparison table further down shows what the in-home premium costs in this part of Dubai and what it actually buys, so you can make that call with the numbers in front of you.
