dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-warqa.programmesIntro: Al Warqa schools run the IGCSE sciences on four distinct routes, and the route decides both the ceiling available to your child and the number of tutoring hours the family ends up paying for. Identify yours before you buy anything.

programmes.name: IGCSE Science, Core tier
programmes.description: The Core syllabus covers the main content of each science without the supplement topics. Candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3 alongside a practical component. The highest grade available is a C, which is the single most important thing a parent should know before paying for a year of tutoring on this route. Core suits a student whose arithmetic and reading speed make the Extended papers a genuine risk, not a student who has simply had a weak year.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools finalise tier entries with Cambridge months before the papers, and the deadline sits with the school's exams officer rather than with the family. If your child is on Core and aiming for A Level sciences, the conversation with the head of science in Al Warqa needs to happen in the autumn term of Year 11 at the latest, because after entries close the ceiling is fixed whatever tutoring you buy.

programmes.name: IGCSE Science, Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended adds the supplement content and opens grades A* to E. Candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4 with the same practical component. The supplement material is where tutoring earns its fee, because large Dubai cohorts frequently teach it last and fastest. Extended Physics 0625 carries the heaviest mathematical load of the three, and students who are weak in 0580 Mathematics tend to lose Physics marks that look like physics failures and are not.
programmes.countryNote: In the big Al Warqa and Al Qusais schools the Extended set can run to several hundred candidates, so written feedback on long answers is rationed by arithmetic rather than by willingness. That is the specific gap an outside tutor fills here, and it is why we price Extended support around marking volume rather than around teaching hours.

programmes.name: Co-ordinated Sciences, Double Award
programmes.description: Cambridge 0654 teaches biology, chemistry and physics as one subject and reports a double grade, counting as two subjects on a transcript. The content is lighter than three separate sciences but broader than one. For a family budget this is the most efficient route on the board: two subjects of credit for one tutoring slot a week, with a single tutor holding the whole picture rather than three people each seeing a third of it.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the eastern suburbs place their middle sets on 0654 and their target sets on three separate sciences, which means siblings in the same Al Warqa villa can be on different routes with different paper counts. Check the code printed on your child's exam entry statement before assuming you know which one they are on.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Science
programmes.description: Pearson runs single and double award science alongside separate Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1. The structural difference that matters to a tutor is practical assessment: Pearson examines practical skills inside the written papers rather than in a separate paper. A student moving between a Cambridge school and a Pearson school mid-course therefore gains or loses a whole component, and the revision plan has to be rebuilt rather than translated.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes its International GCSE timetables for a May/June and a November series, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January. Entry and resit planning for UAE candidates should be read off the live Pearson timetable page rather than off any date restated on a tutoring site.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-warqa.subjectsIntro: These are the science codes we see most often on exam entry statements in the eastern suburbs, with the part of each that costs families the most marks. Ask your child's exams officer which code appears against their name; it is printed, and it changes everything a tutor should be doing.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: The content is accessible and the marks are lost in precision. Transport in plants, enzymes and homeostasis are examined through six-mark explanations where a candidate must name the gradient, the surface, the hormone and the direction. Describing the process in general terms earns one mark of four. Biology is the cheapest science to improve and the easiest to coast on.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis products and organic naming carry most of the Extended losses. The arithmetic is not hard; the layout is. Candidates who write a chain of numbers with no units and no working get nothing when the final answer is wrong, and full marks when it is right, which makes marks volatile in a way that a few marked papers will fix.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The most mathematically demanding of the three. Moments, circuits, pressure and the wave equations require rearrangement under time pressure, and the commonest loss in Dubai scripts is a correct method with a dropped prefix — milli, kilo, centi — rather than a conceptual error. Electricity and magnetism are usually taught late and revised least.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: One syllabus, three disciplines, a double grade. The risk is uneven coverage: a student who is comfortable in biology can hide a complete gap in physics behind a middling overall mark. A tutor on 0654 should be diagnosing by discipline from the first session, not by paper.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: A single-subject route covering all three sciences in less depth. It appears on transcripts as one science, which matters for the Ministry of Education equivalency count and for A Level entry. Families sometimes discover this late; it is worth checking against the school's own progression requirements in Year 10.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them. The question style rewards longer connected prose than Cambridge does, so a student switching boards often keeps scoring at the same level of knowledge and a lower level of mark, purely because the answers are too short.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Quantitative chemistry and practical method questions dominate the difference from Cambridge. There is no separate alternative-to-practical component, so method, apparatus and safety reasoning appear without warning among the theory questions and are frequently answered in one line where three were wanted.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two papers, the longer carrying the larger share of the grade. Equation recall is heavier than many students expect, and the practical-skills questions embedded in the written papers are where Dubai candidates taught mainly through demonstrations tend to lose the most.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Included here because it is a science cost. Rearranging formulae, standard form, ratio and graph interpretation are physics and chemistry skills with a maths label. Families paying for separate physics help when the real fault is 0580 algebra are paying twice for one problem.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken by target sets in some eastern-suburb schools alongside the three sciences. It raises the total paper count substantially in one exam season, and the scheduling consequence for a Year 11 revision plan is usually underestimated when the subject is chosen in Year 9.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE science tutor in Al Warqa actually costs
paragraphs: Dubai publishes more tutoring prices than any parent realises, just not in one place. Reading across the providers that do quote, in October 2026, the market for an hour of IGCSE science support ran from AED 45 at the budget end to AED 650 at the top. The spread is not quality alone; it is a mixture of the tutor's qualification, whether anybody drives anywhere, and whether written work gets marked outside the hour you pay for. The table sets out each band with the provider that published it, so you can check the figure rather than take ours.

Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency an Al Warqa family transacts in. That is why the bands below are worth more than any claim about value. IB Gram does not operate a published price list on these pages; what we can do honestly is show you what the market charges, tell you which band a particular problem actually needs, and let the trial session establish the rest.

The practical reading of this table is narrower than it looks. Most Al Warqa science problems live in the middle band. A student who understands respiration but writes four-word answers does not need an examiner at AED 650; they need somebody at AED 200 who will mark twelve long answers properly. Conversely, a Year 11 candidate sitting three Extended sciences with a tier decision still unmade is poorly served by a AED 60 undergraduate, however patient, because the judgement being bought is the expensive part, not the explanation.

sections.heading: Three sciences or a double award: the arithmetic nobody does first
paragraphs: The single largest variable in an Al Warqa science bill is not the hourly rate. It is how many sciences your child sits and whether one person or three is being paid to support them. A student on 0610, 0620 and 0625 with a weekly tutor for each is buying twelve hours a month. The same student on Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 with one tutor is buying four to eight, and the transcript still shows two subjects rather than one. Over the two years of the course that gap is substantial.

Families rarely run this calculation before they start, because tutoring is bought subject by subject as each report arrives. Biology slips in October, so a biology tutor appears. Chemistry slips in February, so a chemistry tutor appears. By June there are three people, three invoices, three sets of diagnosis covering the same graph-drawing weakness, and nobody holding the whole revision calendar. The waste is not in any one hour; it is in the duplication.

Our recommendation for triple-science students in the eastern suburbs is one lead science tutor with the authority to move the hour where the need is. Graph skills, command verbs, units and significant figures are shared across all three syllabuses and should be taught once. Discipline-specific gaps — organic mechanisms, electromagnetic induction, plant transport — then get targeted blocks rather than a permanent weekly slot. Escalate to a second specialist when the evidence says so, not when a report card says so.

sections.heading: Where science tutoring money is wasted in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: The commonest waste is paying for explanation that the school already delivered well. In a large Al Warqa cohort the lesson content is usually covered properly and on time; what is missing is individual correction. A tutor who spends the hour re-teaching diffusion to a student who can already define it has produced a pleasant session and no change in marks. You can detect this quickly: ask what was marked, not what was covered.

The second waste is buying hours instead of buying a decision. A family spending AED 1,200 a month on physics while their child remains entered for Core tier is paying for a ceiling of grade C. The entry decision is worth more than any number of hours, it is made by the school months in advance, and it is reversible only before the exams officer submits. One properly evidenced conversation with the head of science in the autumn term is worth more than a term of lessons.

The third is late buying. Science tutoring purchased six weeks before the June series across three subjects cannot do more than triage, and triage priced at specialist rates is the most expensive hour on this page. The fourth is group classes bought on price: a tuition centre class of twelve at AED 80 a head is good value for content revision and poor value for the thing most Al Warqa students actually need, which is somebody reading their own handwriting against a mark scheme.

None of this argues for spending more. It argues for spending the same amount differently: fewer tutors, more marking, one decision made early, and a fortnightly block on the practical paper that currently gets nothing at all.

sections.heading: The papers you are paying to fix, component by component
paragraphs: Cambridge splits each separate science into three components, and the weightings are public. The multiple-choice paper carries 30% of the grade, the structured theory paper 50%, and the practical component 20%. A parent who knows those three numbers can audit a tutoring plan in about a minute. If every session is spent on theory recall, half the grade is receiving all of the attention and the other half none.

The theory paper is where the most marks sit and where Dubai scripts lose them most predictably. Command verbs are the mechanism. Describe asks what happens; explain asks why; suggest invites a reasoned answer to an unfamiliar context; compare requires both sides in the same sentence. A candidate who answers every six-mark question with a description scores consistently around half. Fixing that is a technique job of a few weeks, not a content job of a year.

The practical component is the quiet one. Paper 5 is a hands-on test; Paper 6 is the alternative to practical, answered on paper. Both examine the same reasoning: variable control, measurement precision, table construction, graph plotting, anomaly identification, and improvements to a method. A student can score strongly on it with no laboratory access at all, because what is being tested is written reasoning about experiments rather than manual dexterity. This is why online delivery is not a handicap on this component, and why we treat it as a separate purchasable block. A student who has drawn thirty marked graphs will outscore one who has watched thirty demonstrations, and the difference costs a handful of sessions rather than a term.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets both price and ceiling
paragraphs: Core tier caps at grade C. That sentence should govern every spending decision a family makes on this route, and in large Dubai cohorts it is frequently discovered late. A student placed on Core in Year 10 on the strength of one weak term, who then recovers, may still be entered for Core because nobody revisited the decision. Tutoring cannot lift a Core candidate above the ceiling of the paper they are sitting.

The decision is made by the school, not the family, and it is submitted to Cambridge by the exams officer. What a family can do is supply evidence: marked Extended-standard questions, a run of past-paper scores on supplement content, a tutor's written view on whether the mathematical demand of 0625 Extended is manageable. Schools respond to evidence far better than to requests. Producing that evidence is a legitimate and cheap use of four or five tutoring sessions in the autumn term of Year 11.

The honest version of this also runs the other way. Extended is not automatically the right answer. A student whose 0580 algebra is insecure will find Extended Physics punishing, and a candidate who scrapes an E on Extended has not done better than a confident C on Core for most progression purposes. We say so when we see it, and we have talked families out of a term of tutoring on that basis. A tier recommendation should come with the marked scripts that justify it.

sections.heading: The practical component when lessons are online
paragraphs: Parents in Al Warqa reasonably ask how practical science can be taught over video. The answer depends on which component your child sits. If the school enters candidates for Paper 6, the alternative to practical, then nothing is lost: that paper is answered in writing, and preparing for it means working through experimental descriptions, drawing results tables, plotting graphs and explaining anomalies. A shared screen and a document camera are perfectly adequate, and in some respects better than a lab bench, because every graph the student draws can be marked immediately.

If the school enters candidates for Paper 5, the hands-on practical test, the laboratory work itself happens at school and cannot be replaced by any tutor, in person or otherwise. What a tutor contributes is the written layer around it: how to record readings to a consistent precision, how to construct a table before taking any measurement, how to decide which variable goes on which axis, and how to phrase an improvement so it earns the mark. That layer is where most of the marks in Paper 5 are actually lost.

For Pearson candidates on 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 or 4SD0 the practical reasoning is distributed through the written papers rather than isolated, so the preparation is the same work done in smaller pieces. In all three cases the honest summary is that online delivery costs nothing on this component, which is precisely the component Al Warqa families are least likely to be paying for.

sections.heading: In-home science tutoring in Al Warqa, priced honestly
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is what most parents searching this phrase have in mind, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. The Dubai market prices an in-home one-to-one visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for an equivalent qualified tutor online, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions have been advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. The premium is real and it is paid for driving, not for teaching.

From Al Warqa that premium buys a particular kind of inconvenience. A tutor willing to drive to Al Warqa 2 on a weekday evening is, by definition, a tutor who lives within a reasonable radius of Al Warqa 2. For a Core-tier biology top-up that radius contains plenty of competent people. For Extended Physics 0625 with a shaky algebra base and a tier decision pending, it may contain nobody at all, and the family ends up choosing on geography rather than on subject expertise.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Al Warqa families are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, which is how a student in the eastern suburbs gets a tutor chosen for knowing 0625 rather than for living nearby. The comparison below is the argument, stated in the terms a parent can check, and it is the same argument whether your address is in Al Warqa 1 or Al Khawaneej.

sections.heading: A spending plan for the June series, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the Cambridge June and November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, which matters because a family reading an India-facing tutoring site may plan to the wrong calendar entirely. Pearson runs May/June and November for its International GCSEs. Both boards publish live timetables, and both revise them, so the only safe practice is to work from the official page rather than from a date restated anywhere else, including here.

Counting backwards from a June sitting, the useful sequence for an Al Warqa science family looks like this. In the autumn term of Year 11, settle the tier and spend money on evidence rather than hours. Through the winter, buy marking: one science at a time, long answers corrected against the scheme, with the weakest discipline rotating into the slot. In the new year, add the practical block, because Paper 5 and Paper 6 preparation is short, cheap and almost universally neglected.

From the mock results onwards the plan should narrow rather than broaden. Three sciences cannot all be rebuilt at once in the final weeks, so pick the paper where the gap between current and achievable marks is widest and concentrate there. Keep one eye on the November series as a genuine option rather than a failure: a resit in a single science, prepared properly over the summer, is often cheaper and more effective than three panicked subjects in spring.

Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after consulting the wrong version. Your child's school knows its zone. Ask for it in writing, and plan the final fortnight from that document.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: Send the syllabus code from your child's exam entry statement — 0610, 0620, 0625, 0654, 0653, 4SD0 — along with the current tier and the most recent marked assessment. Those three pieces of information let us match a tutor who has taught that exact specification rather than a general science teacher.

process.title: A trial session that diagnoses rather than sells
process.description: The first session is at no cost and is spent on your child's own marked work. The tutor identifies whether the gap is content, written technique or the practical component, and says which. If the honest answer is that tutoring is not the right purchase, you will be told that in writing.

process.title: Agree the spend before the schedule
process.description: We set out how many hours the diagnosis actually justifies and where they should go, using the market bands on this page as the reference. One science weekly, a fortnightly practical block, or a short evidence-gathering series for a tier decision are different purchases with different prices.

process.title: Marking between sessions, visible to you
process.description: Written answers are corrected against the published scheme and returned with the mark breakdown, so you can see which marks were missed and why. This is the part that distinguishes the middle of the Dubai rate card from the bottom of it, and it is what you are paying the difference for.

process.title: Review on evidence, every few weeks
process.description: Every four to six weeks we look at the marked work and decide whether to keep the slot, move it to a different science, or stop. Sessions that have stopped producing movement should end rather than continue, and a tutor who never recommends reducing hours is not giving you advice.

whyPoints.title: The rates on this page are sourced, not implied
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. Three of the most visible competitor pages in this market publish no figure at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not what an Al Warqa family pays in.

whyPoints.title: A tutor chosen for the syllabus, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the pool for Extended Physics 0625 is every tutor who teaches it, not the subset who will drive to the eastern suburbs on a Tuesday. For a niche need — 0606 Additional Mathematics alongside triple science — that difference decides whether a suitable tutor exists at all.

whyPoints.title: The practical component is treated as a real component
whyPoints.description: Paper 5 and Paper 6 carry a fifth of a Cambridge science grade and are the least-tutored part of the course in Dubai. We sell preparation for them as a defined short block, because that is the shape of the work and because it is the cheapest grade movement available.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on coursework and assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on your child's own work. We do not write, complete or edit to completion anything that is submitted for assessment, and we do not supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads. Those are published by Cambridge and Pearson and should be obtained from them.

whyPoints.title: Permit position stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Ask any tutor, including ours, to show theirs. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK or Ministry of Education approval and does not claim any.

whyPoints.title: Advice that sometimes costs us the sale
whyPoints.description: If the diagnosis is that the tier decision matters more than the hours, or that the school is already doing what a tutor would do, we say so. On a 4,500-word page about cost it would be inconsistent to pretend every problem is solved by buying more of what we sell.

faqs.question: How much should an Al Warqa family budget for one IGCSE science subject?
faqs.answer: At the rates Dubai providers published in October 2026, a qualified online science tutor costs AED 150 to 300 an hour, so one weekly session is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month. Budget tutors start around AED 45 to 65 on EdFlik's own rate card, and specialist IGCSE support runs from AED 200 to 450 and above. For a single science with a clear, named weakness, the middle band is usually the right purchase. The figure that matters more than the hourly rate is how many sciences you are supporting at once, because that is what multiplies the bill.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to support Co-ordinated Sciences than three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and the transcript barely suffers. Cambridge 0654 reports a double grade and counts as two subjects, but it is one syllabus with one tutor and one revision calendar. Three separate sciences on 0610, 0620 and 0625 typically attract three weekly tutors, three diagnoses of the same graph-drawing weakness and three invoices. At market mid-rates that is roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600 a month against AED 600 to 1,400 for the double award. The route is chosen by the school in Year 9 or 10, so the saving is only available if the conversation happens then.

faqs.question: Which of the three sciences is most expensive to leave until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Physics 0625 at Extended tier. Its difficulty is mathematical as much as conceptual: rearranging equations, handling prefixes, and working with standard form under time pressure. A student who reaches Year 11 with insecure 0580 algebra needs the algebra fixed before the physics will move, which means paying for two problems in sequence rather than one. Biology 0610 is the opposite case — accessible content where marks are lost to imprecise writing, which a few properly marked long answers will shift quickly. Chemistry sits between them, with mole calculations behaving like physics and organic naming behaving like biology.

faqs.question: Does a tutor at AED 60 an hour work for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: For some purposes, yes. If your child has missed three weeks of lessons and needs the content delivered again, a careful undergraduate at the bottom of the Dubai market will do it and the saving is real. What that band generally does not include is marking: reading your child's six-mark answer against the published scheme and explaining which two marks were not awarded. Since that is the gap in most large Al Warqa cohorts, the cheaper hour often changes nothing measurable. Judge the purchase by what gets corrected, not by what gets covered.

faqs.question: What does the in-home travel premium actually buy a science family here?
faqs.answer: Driving. The Dubai market quotes in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for an equivalent qualified tutor online, and that gap is travel time priced into the hour. From the eastern suburbs it also narrows your choice to tutors living within reach of Al Warqa on a weekday evening, which is a geographic filter rather than an academic one. For Core-tier biology that pool is adequate. For Extended Physics 0625 with a pending tier decision, it may not contain the right person at all.

faqs.question: Should we hire a separate tutor for each science?
faqs.answer: Not at first. Graph construction, units, significant figures and command-verb discipline are shared across all three syllabuses and should be taught once by one person. Our recommendation for triple-science students is a single lead science tutor who moves the hour to whichever discipline the marked work says is weakest, reviewed every few weeks. Add a second specialist when the evidence names a specific content gap that the lead tutor cannot cover — organic mechanisms, or electromagnetic induction, for instance — rather than because a report card showed three middling grades.

faqs.question: How much of our spend should go on marking rather than teaching?
faqs.answer: More than most families allocate. In a cohort where a science teacher sees well over a hundred students a week, content delivery is usually sound and individual correction is the scarce commodity. A useful test is to ask, after each session, what was marked rather than what was covered. If the answer is consistently that work was reviewed verbally, you are paying a marking rate for a teaching service. Expect written answers to come back with the mark breakdown shown, because that is the specific thing distinguishing the middle of the Dubai rate card from the bottom.

faqs.question: Is a group science class at a Dubai tuition centre good value?
faqs.answer: It is good value for one job and poor value for another. A class of ten or twelve at AED 80 a head is an efficient way to revise content, work through a topic sequence and keep a student engaged through the winter term. It cannot give individual correction on your child's handwriting, and it cannot make a tier judgement. If the diagnosis is missing content, the group class is a sensible purchase. If the diagnosis is that answers are too short and graphs are unlabelled, it will not touch the problem however many weeks you buy.

faqs.question: What does practical-paper preparation cost compared with content teaching?
faqs.answer: Much less, because it is finite. Paper 5 and Paper 6 test a defined set of skills: variable control, table construction before measuring, axis choice, scale selection, anomaly identification and method improvement. Six to eight fortnightly sessions covers it, which at market mid-rates is roughly AED 900 to 2,400 once. Against a component carrying a fifth of the final grade that is the highest-yield money on this page. Almost no Al Warqa family buys it, which is why it stays the cheapest improvement available in the subject.

faqs.question: Does our school's exam board change what tutoring should cost?
faqs.answer: It changes what the tutoring has to do. Cambridge isolates practical reasoning in Paper 5 or Paper 6, worth 20% of the grade, so it can be bought as a separate short block. Pearson distributes practical questions through the written papers on 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4SD0, so the same preparation happens in smaller pieces inside the main sessions. The hourly rate does not differ. What differs is the plan, which is why a tutor needs the syllabus code from the entry statement rather than just the subject name.

faqs.question: Is paying for a November science resit worth it after a disappointing June?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and it is usually cheaper than the alternative. One science prepared properly over the summer and resat in November concentrates spending on a single known gap, with a diagnosis already in hand from the June script. Compare that with spreading the same money across three subjects in a panic the previous spring. Check two things first: whether your child's school will enter them for the November series, and what the centre charges a private candidate if it will not. Both answers come from the school's exams officer.

faqs.question: How many weeks before we should expect to see something change?
faqs.answer: For written technique, four to six weeks of marked long answers is usually enough to see movement on school assessments, because the fault is a habit rather than a knowledge gap. For missing content — a whole unit of organic chemistry, say — expect a term. For practical-paper skills, improvement shows within two or three sessions, since the marks being recovered require no new science. If nothing has shifted on marked work after six weeks on a technique brief, the problem has been diagnosed wrongly and the plan should change rather than continue.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education reduce the science time available?
faqs.answer: They occupy timetable space, yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students. In practice that means a Year 11 week in Al Warqa holds fewer discretionary science periods than a parent assumes from the subject list. It is an argument for planning the revision calendar early rather than for buying more hours, and it is published on the KHDA website if you want to read the requirement yourself.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both our children and reduce the bill?
faqs.answer: If they are on compatible routes, often yes, though not in the same session. A tutor covering 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences for a Year 10 and 0620 Chemistry for a Year 11 holds one body of knowledge and can run consecutive slots from the same household with less switching cost than two separate arrangements. What does not work is teaching two children of different ability in one hour and calling it one-to-one. Tell us both syllabus codes and both school timetables, and we will say honestly whether one tutor is the sensible answer.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for triple science at the level we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with whoever is available. The honest sequence is this: if no UAE-based tutor covers the exact specification and tier, we look across our wider pool, which includes tutors based in India teaching the same Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses to Gulf Standard Time. If that still does not produce the right match, we say the need is unmet and suggest what else to try, including your school's own intervention programme. A tutor who does not know 0625 Extended will cost you a term before you find out.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-warqa.closingHeading: Start with the diagnosis, then decide what to spend
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-warqa.closingBody: If you are weighing science tutoring for a child in Al Warqa, the useful first step is not choosing a price band. It is finding out whether the lost marks are content, written technique or the practical component, because the three cost very different amounts to fix. Send the syllabus code, the current tier and one recent marked assessment, and the trial session will give you that answer at no cost. You may be told that a conversation with the head of science matters more than a term of lessons. On a page about where the money goes, that is the only consistent position to take.

Pick the one whose subject and series match your child's entry, and use the free trial to check the fit before committing to a block.

intro.heading: Start with the date, then work out how many lessons fit before it
paragraphs: There are two useful questions a parent in Al Wasl can ask about IGCSE science, and only one of them is the one usually asked first. The common question is "is my child behind?" The better question is "how many teaching hours remain before the papers are sat, and what must be finished in each of them?" The second question has an arithmetic answer. Count the weeks to the first science paper, subtract the half-term break and the days the school loses to mocks, multiply by the number of sessions a week a household can realistically protect, and you have the size of the container. Everything else is deciding what goes in it.

That arithmetic is why this page reads like a calendar rather than a brochure. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the November timetable is the resit and second-chance route for UAE candidates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and November, and its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Those two sentences fix the whole plan. A student who is weak on electricity in Physics 0625 in September has a very different amount of runway than the same student in March, and the sensible tutoring response is different in kind, not just in intensity.

Al Wasl families have a specific advantage and a specific problem. The advantage is proximity: the villa streets off Al Wasl Road sit inside a tight ring of British-curriculum secondaries, so school-day finish times are early enough that a 4.30pm session is workable on most weekdays without a two-hour commute eating the afternoon. The problem is that the same proximity produces complacency about timing. Parents assume there is more runway than there is, because the school is ten minutes away and the term feels long. Entry deadlines, tier decisions and coursework cut-offs all sit months before the paper, and they are the dates that actually constrain the plan.

The second thing that matters here is the structure of IGCSE science itself. It is not one subject. A child may be entered for three separate sciences, or for Coordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award, or for Combined Science 0653 as a single award, and each of those routes has a different paper count, a different weighting pattern and a different set of places where marks go missing. A tutor who does not know which of those three a student is on cannot plan a term. The first thing we ask for is the syllabus code on the entry, not the year group.

What we do not do is send anybody to a villa in Al Wasl. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Science tuition for Al Wasl is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video, with a shared whiteboard for working, the paper on screen for both people to annotate, and a recording of the session the student can return to the night before a test. On a subject where the hard part is often reading the question properly, having the question visible to both parties for the whole hour is not a compromise.

The pages this one sits beside take other angles. The Al Wasl physics page works through syllabus content in detail; the Al Wasl home-tutor pages compare this neighbourhood with its neighbours. This one answers the calendar question, because for a science entry the calendar is usually what is actually biting.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-wasl.programmesIntro: An Al Wasl household usually meets IGCSE science as the middle of three stages: a lower-secondary run-up, the two IGCSE years themselves, and then a post-16 fork between A Level and the IB Diploma. The tutoring question is different at each stage, so it is worth naming which one your child is actually in before booking anything.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary science (Years 7 to 9)
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE syllabus formally begins. Science is usually taught as one subject with separate biology, chemistry and physics strands, and Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October. The content matters less than the habits: drawing a results table before an experiment, writing a conclusion that refers to the data, converting units without being reminded. A student who leaves Year 9 without those habits spends Year 10 paying for it.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Wasl most children on this track are inside a British-curriculum school within a short run of Al Wasl Road, and the year is light enough that a weekly session can be genuinely preventative rather than remedial. This is the cheapest point on the whole curve to fix a science problem, and the point at which almost nobody books.

programmes.name: IGCSE science, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, one terminal set of papers, and an entry decision made by the school partway through. Cambridge options include Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, Combined Science 0653 and Coordinated Sciences 0654; Pearson Edexcel runs 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Each is examined by two or three papers plus an alternative-to-practical or practical component, and the weightings differ enough that a revision plan built for one is wrong for another.
programmes.countryNote: This is the bulk of our Al Wasl science work. The pattern is predictable: a strong Year 10 report, a shaky set of Year 11 mocks in January, and a parent with four months to work out whether the problem is content, technique or exam nerves. Separating those three is the first job, and it is usually possible inside two sessions.

programmes.name: The post-IGCSE fork: A Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: Several schools in the Al Wasl and Al Safa cluster run A Level after IGCSE while others run the IB Diploma, and a few run both. For science the choice changes the next two years sharply: A Level narrows to three or four subjects with linear papers, while the Diploma keeps six subjects plus an Internal Assessment in each science and the Extended Essay. IGCSE grades in the sciences are the main evidence a school uses when advising on Higher Level entry.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Wasl family sometimes has to move a child at sixteen to get the route they want, because the school that suits a British primary does not always run the post-16 programme the family wants. Knowing that in Year 10 rather than Year 11 is worth more than any amount of last-minute tutoring.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects running alongside
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in Dubai private schools
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These sit on top of the IGCSE timetable rather than replacing anything.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Wasl parents the practical consequence is that the school week is fuller than the IGCSE syllabus alone suggests, so the number of free evening hours is smaller than it looks. That is a scheduling fact rather than an academic one, and it is the main reason weekday sessions here cluster after 4.30pm.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-wasl.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE science entries we are asked for most often by Al Wasl families, named by syllabus code because the code is what determines the papers. If your child's entry code is not here, say so when you enquire and we will tell you honestly whether we cover it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-dense rather than conceptually hard, which misleads students into thinking reading is revision. Marks go missing on the required practical skills, on genetics problems set out as crosses, and on extended-response questions where a command term asks for an explanation and gets a description instead.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: The syllabus splits into principles, inorganic and organic chemistry, and students who can balance an equation still lose marks on mole calculations under time pressure. Qualitative analysis tests and the chemistry of a named reaction are both high-yield revision targets because they are predictable in form.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are where Extended candidates most reliably lose ground, usually because circuit reasoning was never secured in Year 10. Graph work, unit conversion and the difference between a definition and a derivation account for a large share of avoidable marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Three sciences in two GCSE-equivalent awards, which means breadth without the depth of the separate codes. The planning difficulty is that revision has to cover all three strands against a single paper set, so topic prioritisation matters more here than in any separate science.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: One award covering all three sciences, common for students who need a science qualification without three separate entries. Students often arrive assuming it is easier; it is narrower, which is not the same thing, and the mark scheme is as exacting on command terms as any other code.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Untiered, with two papers and no separate practical examination, so practical understanding is tested inside the written papers. The style of question differs from Cambridge enough that past-paper practice has to come from the right board, which is the single most common mistake we correct.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Two papers, with calculation-heavy questions spread across both rather than concentrated. Students moving from Cambridge resources often under-practise the longer multi-step calculations, which carry a disproportionate share of the higher-grade marks.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two papers with a formula sheet position that differs from Cambridge, so recall expectations differ too. The practical skills questions reward students who have actually handled apparatus and can describe a method in the right order, which is coachable without a laboratory.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Not a science, but the reason a science grade stalls more often than any single science topic. Rearranging formulae, standard form, ratio and graph gradients appear across all three sciences, and a student weak on those loses marks in Physics that look like physics errors and are not.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Environmental Management 0680
subjects.description: A half-credit option some schools in the cluster run alongside the sciences, assessed by two papers with heavy data interpretation. Useful for students who read well but calculate slowly, and it rewards the same source-handling skills as geography.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE science tutor in Al Wasl actually has to deliver this term
paragraphs: An IGCSE science tutor in Al Wasl has one job that nobody else in the student's week is doing: holding the whole calendar in view while working on one topic at a time. The school teaches a scheme of work. The student revises what feels urgent. Neither of those is the same as asking what has to be true by the end of February for the June papers to go well, and then working out which fortnight does which piece of it.

Concretely, the term in front of you has to achieve three things. The syllabus content that was never secured has to be taught properly rather than reviewed, because reviewing something a student never understood produces a feeling of familiarity and no marks. The examinable technique has to be built: command terms, working shown, units carried, graphs drawn to the mark scheme's expectations rather than to the student's taste. And timed practice has to happen often enough that the first full paper under exam conditions is not the real one.

The order of those three matters, and it is where most self-directed revision goes wrong. Students start with past papers because past papers feel like exam preparation, discover they cannot do the questions, and conclude they are bad at science. The honest sequence is content first on the specific gaps, technique on top, timing last. A tutor earns the hour by knowing which of the three a given student is actually short of, and by refusing to do the other two until that one is fixed.

For an Al Wasl household the operational constraint is the afternoon. School finishes early enough here that a weekday session is viable, but the window between arriving home and losing the student to fatigue is roughly ninety minutes. One focused hour inside that window, every week, without a commute at either end, is worth more than a two-hour block on a Saturday that the student resents.
bullets: Teach the real gaps, do not review content that was never understood in the first place
Build examinable technique separately: command terms, working, units, graph conventions
Timed practice last and often, so the first full paper is never the real one
Protect one weekday hour rather than chasing a longer weekend block

sections.heading: The exam series counted backwards, milestone by milestone
paragraphs: Nobody ranking for these searches publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is the thing a parent is actually trying to solve. The table below is the shape of a series counted backwards from the papers. Dates that belong to the board are given where they are published and sourced; dates that belong to your child's school are marked as such, because they vary by school and the school is the only authority on them.

Two board facts anchor everything. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series exists but is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate should ignore it entirely. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The one administrative detail that catches families out is Cambridge zoning. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the school sits in, and check the paper times against that version rather than against a generic timetable found online.

Treat every date below as something to verify on the board's own live timetable before acting on it. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the International GCSE November window up to a year before it opens, which means a date can be revised after publication. The useful habit is to link the official timetable once and check it each half term, rather than to copy a date into a family calendar in September and trust it in May.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE science marks are actually lost, paper by paper
paragraphs: Ask a student where they lose marks and you get a topic name. Ask a mark scheme and you get something more useful: a pattern of behaviour. The same errors recur across Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, and almost all of them are correctable inside a handful of sessions because they are habits rather than knowledge gaps.

The largest single category is command-term failure. A question asks a student to explain and receives a description. It asks for a comparison and receives two separate statements with no comparative word between them. It asks to suggest, which invites reasoning from unfamiliar data, and receives a recalled fact. None of this is ignorance of biology; it is ignorance of what the verb is asking for, and it is examined in every paper of every science.

The second category is working. A multi-step calculation in Chemistry attracts method marks that survive an arithmetic slip, but only if the method is on the page. Students who do mole calculations in their heads and write one number collect nothing when the number is wrong. The habit of writing the relationship, substituting, then evaluating is worth more marks across a series than any additional topic knowledge.

The third is the practical component. In most UAE centres practical skills are examined through a written alternative-to-practical paper, which rewards students who can describe a method in the right order, identify a control variable, read a scale to the correct precision and spot why a result is anomalous. That is all teachable over video with a paper on screen, and it is the component students neglect most because it does not look like revision.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: a decision with a grade ceiling attached
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE sciences are tiered. Core and Extended are not two difficulty settings on the same paper set; they are different entries with different papers and different grade ranges, and the Extended route is the one that keeps the higher grades available. A student entered on Core cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, which is why this is an entry decision rather than a classroom preference.

The decision usually gets made somewhere in Year 11, on evidence from mocks and classwork, and the school owns it. Where tutoring helps is in making sure the evidence is real. A student who has never sat an Extended paper under timed conditions is being assessed on an impression. One timed Extended past paper, marked honestly against the official mark scheme, converts the conversation from opinion to data, and it is a single session's work.

The reverse case matters too. A student pushed onto Extended who is losing marks across the board may do better on Core, where the grade available is still enough for the route they want. That is an uncomfortable conversation and worth having early, because the entry deadline closes it. Checking what the receiving post-16 route actually requires is part of the same conversation: a sixth form running A Level sciences has a minimum IGCSE grade in mind, and that number is the real constraint.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, which removes this decision entirely and replaces it with a different one: whether the student's past-paper diet matches the board they are sitting. A household that has spent a year on Cambridge resources for a Pearson entry has a problem that looks like weak science and is actually wrong practice material.

sections.heading: The eight-week block: what each fortnight has to achieve
paragraphs: Most Al Wasl science enquiries arrive with about eight weeks of usable time. That is enough to move a grade if the eight weeks are planned and almost useless if they are spent on general revision. Here is the shape we use, which is simply the term's work divided by the number of fortnights available and allocated to named outcomes.

The first fortnight is diagnosis and the worst topic. Session one is a full past paper, timed, marked against the official mark scheme with the student present for the marking. That single exercise produces a list of lost marks sorted by cause rather than by topic, and the list usually surprises the parent more than the student. The rest of the fortnight goes to the single largest cause on the list, taught properly from the beginning rather than skimmed.

The second and third fortnights are content repair on the remaining gaps, in order of how many marks they cost rather than in syllabus order. The fourth fortnight stops teaching altogether. From there it is timed papers, mark-scheme reading and the alternative-to-practical component, with the student marking their own work against the scheme so they learn what the examiner rewards. The last week has no new content in it at all, by design.

Two things make or break this. The household has to protect the slots, including through mock week, because a block with three cancelled sessions is a six-week block pretending to be eight. And the student has to do the timed papers between sessions, not during them: an hour of tutor time spent watching a student sit a paper is an hour not spent explaining why the marks went.

sections.heading: How practical science works when the lessons are online
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online science tuition is practical work, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. A tutor over video cannot run a titration with your child. What a tutor can do is prepare the component that is actually examined, which in most UAE centres is a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory assessment.

That paper tests a specific and narrow set of skills: identifying independent, dependent and control variables; describing a method in a sequence another person could follow; reading an instrument to the right precision; plotting and interpreting a graph; spotting an anomalous result and saying why it is anomalous; suggesting an improvement that addresses the actual source of error rather than repeating a generic line about doing it three times. Every one of those is a writing and reasoning skill, and every one is coachable with the question on a shared screen.

The school handles the hands-on work, and it should. Where tutoring adds value is in the translation: a student who has done the experiment in a laboratory and still cannot describe it in the examiner's language is losing marks on something they already know how to do. Sitting with the mark scheme and rewriting their own method until it earns the marks is the highest-yield hour available in the last month before a series.

Screen sharing also solves a problem the laboratory does not. Both people are looking at the same question, the same graph, the same working, at the same time, and the tutor can see the student's handwriting as it happens. On a subject where most lost marks come from how something was written rather than whether it was known, that visibility is the point rather than a substitute for something better.

sections.heading: What IGCSE science tutoring costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure, because that is the number a household budget actually works in. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those monthly numbers decompose into hourly bands that are worth knowing before any quote arrives. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit between AED 150 and 300: Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, run AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching AED 500. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650.

Every figure in the preceding paragraph belongs to the provider named beside it, published on that provider's own page or in Bestimate's 2026 table. None of them is an IB Gram price, and we do not publish a rate card on a landing page because the honest answer depends on subject, level and how many weeks remain. The free trial lesson and the consultation exist so that a quote is given against a real plan rather than a guess.

What a parent can verify independently is the context. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. So the school fee line is flat this year while tutoring is not, which makes the tutoring decision more visible in the household budget than it was.

sections.heading: Online versus in-home science tuition from an Al Wasl address
paragraphs: This page targets a search that parents type, and it would be dishonest to dodge the comparison. In-home one-to-one tuition is a real market in Dubai and it is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and science tuition for Al Wasl is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video.

The argument for that is not cost, though cost is part of it. The argument is the size of the pool. A household that requires a tutor to be physically present is choosing from the people willing to drive to Al Wasl at 4.30pm on a Tuesday. A household that accepts live video is choosing from everyone who teaches Cambridge 0620 to the mark scheme, including the person who happens to be the right fit for a student struggling specifically with mole calculations. On a narrow requirement, the second pool is the one that contains the right answer.

The travel premium is worth naming precisely. Between the in-home band and the qualified-online band there is a gap of roughly AED 100 to 200 an hour in the published market figures, and that gap buys a journey rather than teaching. For a family on two sessions a week across an eight-week block, that is a meaningful sum spent on a car being in traffic on Al Wasl Road.

There are genuine trade-offs and it is better to state them. A younger child who needs physical supervision to stay on task benefits from someone in the room. A student who cannot be trusted with a laptop unsupervised needs a parent nearby for the first few sessions. And a household with an unreliable connection should test it on the free trial rather than discover the problem in week three. None of those is solved by pretending online works identically for everyone.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and what they do to the week
paragraphs: KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. It inspects private schools annually and publishes a band for each, and that published band on KHDA's own listing is the figure worth checking before a school decision. Abu Dhabi is regulated by ADEK, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The regulatory fact with the biggest practical effect on an Al Wasl science timetable is the mandatory subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited.

Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can ask about directly. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

Read together, these rules explain something Al Wasl parents notice without being able to name: the school week is fuller than the IGCSE syllabus alone implies. Science revision therefore competes for a smaller pool of evening hours than a UK timetable would leave, which is the real reason a single protected weekday hour outperforms an ambitious plan nobody can keep. Dubai's private sector is also still growing: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a science tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: This matters even at IGCSE, where there is less assessed coursework than in the Diploma, because the habits formed now are the ones a student carries into an Internal Assessment. A tutor teaches, explains, questions, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not produce the work. The distinction is not a technicality; at IB level it is a malpractice trigger with consequences for the student rather than the tutor.

In practice the line is easy to hold once it is stated. A tutor may work through a past-paper method question and explain why the mark scheme rewards one sequence over another. A tutor may read a student's written method and say which step is out of order and why the examiner would not award the mark. A tutor may not write the method, dictate sentences for the student to copy, or hand over an answer the student then submits as their own.

There are sellers in this market who cross that line openly, including one offering completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach and the risk sits entirely with the student. If any provider offers to produce assessed work, that is sufficient reason to stop the conversation, whatever the price or the promised grade.

The related honesty point is about materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. We reference them and link to the official source; we do not reproduce or redistribute them. A parent should be able to find the same document themselves on the board's own site, and that is the right way for it to work.

sections.heading: Permits, and how an Al Wasl parent can check one
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a parent is entitled to ask about it. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. It lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure circulating online should be treated as unverified.

Two further points apply to an Al Wasl household considering a teacher at their own child's school. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy document, but the direction is clear enough that "your child's own teacher, privately" is not an arrangement to pursue.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps. IB Gram does not operate premises in the UAE and does not hold that permit, and no page of ours should ever suggest otherwise. What we are is a matching platform delivering online lessons, which is a different thing and worth stating plainly.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency, and why IGCSE science grades feed into it
paragraphs: Families in Al Wasl planning a UAE university route eventually meet equivalency, and it is better met in Year 10 than in Year 13. For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. That detail is worth holding onto, because one ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject requirement for UAE candidates, which is not what the sourced rule says. If a provider's page contradicts the published rule on something this checkable, treat the rest of their factual claims with the same caution.

For the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics at at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so we publish none; anyone quoting an IB equivalency figure should be able to show it on moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority page.

Two caveats. Equivalency is a process the Ministry and the attestation authorities run, not something a tutoring platform performs or can speed up, and we do not present it as such. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, university admission or school progression; anybody implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. What IGCSE science tutoring does is affect the grades that feed the subject count, which is a narrower and more honest claim.
