process.title: Tell us the date and the code
process.description: The two pieces of information that make a plan possible are the exam series your child is entered for and the syllabus code on the entry. Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are both IGCSE Physics and they need different past papers. Year group alone is not enough to plan from.

process.title: A free trial lesson, on a real question
process.description: The trial runs on an actual past-paper question rather than an introductory chat, so you can see how the tutor explains and how your child responds. There is no payment before it and no card required to book it. If the fit is wrong, say so and we will try a different tutor.

process.title: A diagnostic paper, marked with the student present
process.description: The first paid session is usually a full past paper, timed, marked against the official mark scheme with the student watching the marking. This produces a list of lost marks sorted by cause rather than by topic, and it is the document the rest of the block is planned from.

process.title: A written fortnight-by-fortnight plan
process.description: You get the block mapped out: which topics in which fortnight, when teaching stops and timed practice starts, and which papers the student sits between sessions. A plan you can see is a plan you can hold us to, and it makes a cancelled session's cost visible.

process.title: Fixed slots on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are booked on GST around the Al Wasl school run, typically 4.30pm or later on weekdays with weekend mornings available. During Ramadan slots shift later, including post-Iftar timings, and the schedule is agreed in advance rather than improvised week by week.

process.title: Review at the halfway point
process.description: Halfway through a block we look at the same diagnostic question types again and compare. If the marks have not moved on the targeted cause, the plan changes or the tutor does. Carrying on unchanged because the sessions are booked is how families end up paying for eight weeks of comfort.

whyPoints.title: The series is the planning unit, not the term
whyPoints.description: Plans are built backwards from the first science paper, with named outcomes per fortnight. That is the difference between tutoring that moves a grade and tutoring that fills a weekly slot pleasantly for four months without changing anything measurable.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: We match on 0610, 0620, 0625, 0653, 0654, 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 rather than on the word science. The board determines question style, paper count and whether tiering applies, and getting it wrong wastes a term of past-paper practice.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published and attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page carries the provider or source that published it, so you can check it. Three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote USD, a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for a narrow entry in your window, we say so rather than putting a generalist in the slot. Where the right specialist for an IGCSE science code is based outside the UAE, the lesson is still online and we tell you that upfront.

whyPoints.title: The academic honesty line is explicit
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work. Nobody writes an assessment, and we say so on the page rather than leaving it ambiguous, because there are sellers in this market who do the opposite.

whyPoints.title: Sources you can check yourself
whyPoints.description: Regulatory and board facts here come from u.ae, web.khda.gov.ae, mohre.gov.ae, cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com. Where a date can be revised, we say to check the live timetable instead of trusting a figure copied onto a page.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE science exams actually held for a student in Al Wasl?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February/March series exists but is offered to India only, so it does not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The dates that matter to your household are on your child's school's zone timetable, because every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones. Ask the exams officer which zone the school sits in, then read the paper times off that version of the timetable.

faqs.question: There are eight weeks left before the science papers - what can that realistically achieve?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to move a grade if the eight weeks are planned, and close to useless if they are spent on general revision. The structure that works is diagnosis first: one full past paper, timed, marked against the official mark scheme with your child present, which produces a list of lost marks sorted by cause. Two fortnights then go to content repair ranked by marks lost, and the final fortnight stops teaching entirely in favour of timed papers and mark-scheme reading. The two things that break it are cancelled sessions during mock week and papers not sat between sessions.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for Core or Extended in Cambridge science?
faqs.answer: The school owns that decision, but you can make sure it rests on evidence. Core and Extended are separate entries with different papers, and Core carries a grade ceiling that cannot be exceeded however well your child performs. The cheapest way to settle it honestly is one timed Extended past paper marked strictly against the official mark scheme, which converts an impression into a script. Check what the receiving post-16 route requires as well: a sixth form running A Level sciences has a minimum IGCSE grade in mind, and that number is the real constraint on the choice.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE science tutor in Al Wasl cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai, each attributed to its publisher, run roughly as follows. Budget online and student tutors advertise AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits including travel run AED 180 to 500 per Bestimate and home-tutor listings. IGCSE and IB specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. None of these is an IB Gram price; ask for a quote against a plan after the free trial.

faqs.question: Does my child need a practical exam for IGCSE science in Dubai?
faqs.answer: In most UAE centres practical skills are assessed through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory examination, though the component depends on the syllabus code and the centre, so confirm it with the exams officer. That paper tests variables, method sequencing, instrument precision, graph interpretation and identifying anomalies. All of those are writing and reasoning skills, which is why they can be prepared properly over live video with the question on a shared screen. It is also the component students neglect most, because revising it does not feel like revising science.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child's school use, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: The school's exams officer can tell you in a sentence, and it is worth asking before buying any revision material. Cambridge IGCSE sciences use codes such as 0610, 0620 and 0625 and are tiered into Core and Extended. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences use 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 and are untiered. Question style, paper count and the position of formula information all differ. A household that has spent a year on Cambridge resources for a Pearson entry has a problem that looks like weak science and is really wrong practice material.

faqs.question: What does the eight-week block look like week by week?
faqs.answer: Fortnight one is diagnosis plus the single largest cause of lost marks, taught from the beginning rather than skimmed. Fortnights two and three are content repair on the remaining gaps, ordered by how many marks each costs rather than by syllabus order. Fortnight four introduces nothing new: it is timed papers, mark-scheme reading and the alternative-to-practical component, with your child marking their own work against the scheme. The final week carries no new content by design, because new content in the last week costs confidence and gains almost nothing.

faqs.question: What time can a science session realistically start for an Al Wasl household?
faqs.answer: Al Wasl sits close to its main British-curriculum secondaries, so arrival home is earlier than in most Dubai communities and a 4.30pm start is workable on most weekdays. Families at the Safa Park end sometimes manage 4pm. From Jumeirah 3 and Umm Suqeim the realistic first slot drifts to 5pm or later because the run is longer at pick-up. Saturday mornings are widely used where weekday evenings are full of activities. Slots are booked on Gulf Standard Time and shift later during Ramadan, including post-Iftar timings.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all three IGCSE sciences for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the stage. For Years 7 to 9 and for Combined Science 0653, a single well-qualified science tutor covering all three strands is usually the right arrangement and simplifies scheduling. For separate Extended entries in Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 in Year 11, depth matters more than convenience, and the better outcome normally comes from a specialist in whichever science is actually costing marks. Start from the diagnostic: if one science is the problem, buy one specialist rather than three generalists.

faqs.question: Is the person tutoring my child in Al Wasl legally permitted to do it?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you see online as unverified.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the practical method questions if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: That is one of the things live video does best. The method question is a writing task: describe a procedure another person could follow, name the control variables, state the precision of each measurement, identify the anomaly and suggest an improvement that addresses the real source of error. With the question on a shared screen the tutor watches your child write and marks it against the official scheme in real time. The laboratory work belongs to the school; the translation into the examiner's language is what the tutored hour is for.

faqs.question: Why would an Al Wasl family choose online over an in-home science tutor?
faqs.answer: The decisive reason is the size of the pool. Requiring physical attendance limits you to tutors willing to drive to Al Wasl at 4.30pm on a weekday. Accepting live video opens the choice to everyone who teaches your child's specific syllabus code to the mark scheme. On a narrow requirement, such as mole calculations in Chemistry 0620, that is the difference between a near-fit and the right person. Cost supports it too: the published gap between in-home and qualified-online bands is roughly AED 100 to 200 an hour, and that gap pays for a journey rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Al Wasl?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, the past paper visible to both people, and a recording your child can return to. We target the home-tutor search because it is the phrase parents type, and we answer it honestly rather than implying a service we do not sell. The in-home market exists and is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour if you prefer it.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory UAE subjects affect science revision time?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates their instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit while requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. The practical consequence is that the school week is fuller than the IGCSE syllabus alone suggests, so fewer evening hours are genuinely free. That is the real reason one protected weekday hour beats an ambitious four-session plan that collapses by week three.

faqs.question: What happens if my child sat the June papers and needs the November series?
faqs.answer: Start with the component breakdown rather than with content. Which paper carried the loss, whether the tier entered was the right one, and how many weeks sit between results arriving and the next entry deadline all shape the plan before any teaching begins. June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so the turnaround is tight in both directions. Check the live official timetable for the series rather than relying on a date copied onto a third-party page, including ours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write up my child's science coursework or method for them?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider offering that should end your consideration of them. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on work your child has produced. A tutor does not write, dictate or complete anything that will be submitted for assessment. At IB level this is a malpractice trigger and the consequences fall on the student, not the tutor. One seller in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price; that is an academic-integrity breach, and the fact that it is openly sold does not make it survivable.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-wasl.closingHeading: Count the weeks, then book the trial
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-al-wasl.closingBody: The useful next step is arithmetic. Find the first science paper on your school's zone timetable, count the usable weeks between now and then, subtract the half-term and the mock window, and you have the size of the plan. Then book a free trial lesson on a real past-paper question and see whether the tutor can explain the thing your child has been stuck on. Tell us the syllabus code and the series at the same time, so the first paid session can be a diagnostic rather than an introduction. Lessons run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, around the Al Wasl school run.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-arabian-ran.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE biology, chemistry and physics on both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel syllabuses. Each works to the paper structure of the specific code a student is entered for, marks past-paper answers against the published scheme, and drills the practical paper conventions that lose the most marks.

intro.heading: The syllabus code decides everything, and almost nobody checks it
paragraphs: A parent in Arabian Ranches who asks for an IGCSE science tutor usually describes the problem as science. The school describes it as biology, chemistry and physics. The examination board describes it as 0610, 0620 and 0625, or as 0654, or as 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, or as 4SD0. Those are not labels for the same thing. They differ in how many papers are sat, how many grades are awarded, whether a tier caps the grade, and whether there is a practical examination at all. A tutor who does not know the code is guessing at half the work.

The difference is large enough to change a revision plan completely. A Cambridge candidate on the separate sciences sits a multiple-choice paper worth 30 per cent of the subject, a theory paper worth 50 per cent, and either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper worth the remaining 20 per cent, and does that three times for three grades. A Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences candidate covers all three sciences at reduced depth for a double award. A Pearson Edexcel candidate sits two untiered written papers per science with experimental skills examined inside them and no separate practical paper.

Tiering adds a second layer. Cambridge splits most science syllabuses into Core and Extended. Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4. The content overlaps substantially but not entirely, and the grade available to a Core candidate is capped. A student working through Extended past papers while entered for Core is wasting time on material that will not appear, and a student entered for Core who could manage Extended is capped for no good reason. Both happen, and both are visible in a single conversation with the school examinations officer.

Arabian Ranches sits inside a dense cluster of British-curriculum schools. JESS Arabian Ranches runs the English National Curriculum through IGCSE inside the community, with Ranches Primary School covering the early years in Arabian Ranches 2. Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, GEMS Metropole School in Motor City, GEMS FirstPoint School in The Villa, South View School towards Remraam and The Aquila School in Dubailand all run science to 16. KHDA inspects every one of them annually and publishes the report. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, with the British curriculum the largest by enrolment at around 37 per cent.

IB Gram teaches IGCSE science live over video, one-to-one, with the session timed to Gulf Standard Time and the paper on screen. We do not send a tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and that is stated on every country page on this site. For science the online format carries a specific advantage: the past paper, the mark scheme and the student's own script can all be on the same screen while the marks are counted out loud.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-arabian-ran.programmesIntro: IGCSE science sits in the middle of a British-curriculum school career, with something before it and a choice after it. The four stages below describe what each one actually demands, because the stage a student is at changes what a tutor should be doing.

programmes.name: International GCSE sciences, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years of teaching leading to terminal written examinations in the May/June or the November series. Cambridge separate sciences award one grade each from three papers; Co-ordinated Sciences awards a double award; Pearson Edexcel awards one grade per science from two untiered papers, or two grades from the Double Award route. Entries are made by the school months before the first paper.
programmes.countryNote: Every British-curriculum school around Arabian Ranches runs this stage, and they do not all use the same board. JESS Arabian Ranches, Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills and GEMS Metropole School in Motor City each make their own syllabus choices, which is why a Ranches parent should ask for the code rather than assume it from the subject name.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, where science is taught as a single subject before it splits. Cambridge runs Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which give a school an external reference point before the IGCSE course begins. The content gap that causes trouble later is usually mathematical rather than scientific.
programmes.countryNote: Ranches families who act at this stage spend far less overall. A Year 9 student who can rearrange a formula, plot a graph with a sensible scale and handle units confidently will find IGCSE science a matter of content rather than of technique. Two or three sessions in Year 9 are worth more than ten in the spring of Year 11.

programmes.name: IB Diploma after IGCSE
programmes.description: The Diploma route taken by JESS Arabian Ranches students and by those moving to Fairgreen International School, GEMS International School Al Khail or Emirates International School Meadows. Diploma sciences assess Paper 1 at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44 per cent and an individual scientific investigation at 20 per cent, with no option topics on the 2023 guides.
programmes.countryNote: The step from IGCSE Extended into a Diploma science is manageable; the step from a double award is wider. A Ranches student on Cambridge 0654 or Edexcel 4SD0 who intends to take a science at Higher Level should plan a catch-up block during Year 11 rather than discovering the gap in DP1.

programmes.name: A Level after IGCSE
programmes.description: The linear two-year route run by most British-curriculum schools in the Ranches belt, with practical endorsement rather than an assessed investigation. Content depth in the first year assumes Extended-tier IGCSE knowledge, particularly in quantitative chemistry and in mechanics.
programmes.countryNote: Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills and GEMS Metropole School in Motor City take this route, so for many Ranches-belt families the A Level question arrives before the IB question does. A Core-tier IGCSE candidate who wants A Level science usually needs the Extended content taught in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-arabian-ran.subjectsIntro: Below are the actual science syllabuses a Ranches-belt student might be entered for, with the paper structure and the thing each one is most often misunderstood about. Ask the school examinations officer which of these codes appears on your child's entry.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Multiple choice at 30 per cent, theory at 50 per cent, and practical or alternative-to-practical at 20 per cent. Extended-only material concentrates in transport in plants, homeostasis, genetics and inheritance. Biology marks are lost to vocabulary precision more than to reasoning: diffusion, osmosis and active transport must be distinguished in the exact terms the scheme uses.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: The same 30, 50 and 20 split. Extended adds quantitative work including mole calculations, electrolysis products at each electrode, and rates in more depth. The characteristic Core-to-Extended jump is arithmetic: a student comfortable with qualitative chemistry can still be defeated by a two-step mole calculation under time pressure.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Same structure again. Extended-only content sits in moments, momentum, electromagnetic induction and parts of thermal physics. Physics is the science where graph interpretation costs the most: students read the area when the question wants the gradient, and lose the mark without ever doubting the answer.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics taught together and reported as a double award rather than three grades. The content per science is thinner than the separate syllabuses, which matters for anyone intending a science at A Level or Higher Level. Papers follow the same multiple-choice, theory and practical pattern.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: A single science grade covering all three disciplines at the lightest content load of the Cambridge routes. Appropriate where science is not going further, and a real obstacle where it is. A student on 0653 who later wants A Level chemistry is starting from considerably further back than a 0620 candidate.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Two written papers, untiered, with no separate practical examination. Experimental skills are assessed inside the written questions, which means practical method and variable control still have to be taught properly even though there is no Paper 6 to point at. Grades 9 to 1 are available to every candidate.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Two untiered written papers. The content map overlaps heavily with Cambridge 0620 but the question style differs: Edexcel leans towards longer structured calculation chains and Cambridge towards shorter discrete items. Past papers from the other board are useful for content and misleading for timing.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two untiered written papers, with the first carrying the larger share of the marks. No practical paper. The formula handling expectation is higher than it looks: students are asked to rearrange and substitute in the same question, and arithmetic slips cost more here than on a multiple-choice paper.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Double Award Science 4SD0
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics papers at reduced content load, awarding two grades. Common in Dubai schools that want every student to carry science to 16 without filling the timetable with three separate subjects. The gap into a post-16 science is wider from here than from the separate syllabuses.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Not a science, and the most common hidden cause of science underperformance. Rearranging formulae, handling standard form, reading scales and plotting graphs are mathematics skills examined inside science papers. A science tutor who identifies a mathematics problem and says so is more useful than one who re-teaches the biology.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by a minority of Year 11 students and the best possible preparation for a post-16 physics or chemistry course. It introduces calculus early, which removes most of the difficulty from A Level mechanics and from Diploma kinematics before either course begins.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. These sit outside the IGCSE science question but they occupy timetable hours and homework time, and families planning a tuition schedule should count them. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies.

sections.heading: Which science route is your child actually on?
paragraphs: Before any teaching happens, establish three facts: the board, the syllabus code, and the tier. Those three facts determine which papers are sat, how many grades are awarded, what the maximum grade is, and which past papers are worth the time. They are all written on the school's examination entry, and the examinations officer will confirm them in a two-minute conversation. Guessing them from the subject name on a report card is the most common avoidable error in IGCSE tutoring.

The routes differ more than parents expect. Separate sciences give three grades and three times the content. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences gives a double award from a thinner syllabus. Cambridge Combined Science gives a single grade from the lightest load of all. Pearson Edexcel runs untiered single sciences with no practical paper, and a Double Award route that awards two grades. A student who moves between schools mid-course can end up on a different route from the one they started, which happens regularly in the Ranches belt.

The consequence sits further down the line. Post-16 science courses assume the content of the separate syllabuses. A student arriving at A Level chemistry from Cambridge 0653 Combined Science, or at Diploma biology from Edexcel 4SD0, has a real gap to close and usually does not know it until the first assessment comes back. That is a planning problem rather than an ability problem, and Year 11 is the cheap time to solve it.

The table lays out each route with the papers, the grades awarded and what it leads into. Find your child's row first; everything else on this page reads differently depending on which one it is. If the row cannot be identified with confidence, that itself is the first action: ask the school for the code before buying a single hour of tuition.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and what the grade ceiling really means
paragraphs: Cambridge science syllabuses are tiered. Core candidates sit the Core multiple-choice paper and the Core theory paper; Extended candidates sit the Extended versions of both. Both tiers then sit the same practical or alternative-to-practical paper. The content is not simply harder on Extended; there is Extended-only material that a Core candidate will never be asked about, and there is a cap on the grade a Core candidate can be awarded.

That cap is the decision that matters, and it is made by the school, usually in Year 10, sometimes provisionally and sometimes not. A student placed on Core who could have managed Extended carries a ceiling into the examination for no reason. A student placed on Extended who is not ready can score less than they would have on Core, because the Extended papers leave less room for partially correct work. Both outcomes are reversible if the conversation happens early enough, and both become fixed once entries close.

For a Ranches family the practical steps are small. Ask which tier your child is provisionally entered for in each science, ask when that decision becomes final, and ask what the school would want to see in order to change it. Then work on exactly that. A tutor can be genuinely useful here, because the question is not whether the child is clever but whether the specific Extended-only topics are within reach in the time available.

Pearson Edexcel removes this problem by running untiered papers, with grades 9 to 1 available to every candidate. That is a real advantage for a student whose ability is uncertain in Year 10, and it is one reason some Dubai schools prefer the Edexcel route. It also means an Edexcel candidate has no Extended-only list to work through, so the revision question becomes depth across the whole specification rather than coverage of a tier.

sections.heading: Paper by paper: where the mark split sends your revision
paragraphs: Cambridge science splits the marks three ways: the multiple-choice paper carries 30 per cent of the subject, the theory paper carries 50 per cent, and the practical or alternative-to-practical paper carries the remaining 20 per cent. That distribution should shape revision and usually does not. Students spend most of their time on content, which serves the theory paper, and almost none on the practical paper, which is a fifth of every science grade and is the most pattern-driven component of the three.

The multiple-choice paper rewards elimination rather than recall. A student who reads all four options, discards two on a definite reason, and chooses between the remaining two, scores better than one who recognises the right answer and moves on without checking. That is a technique, not knowledge, and it transfers across all three sciences in a single session.

The theory paper is where command words decide the marks. State wants a short fact. Describe wants observable detail without cause. Explain wants cause. Suggest wants a reasoned answer to an unfamiliar situation. Compare wants both sides in the same sentence. Calculate wants working. Determine wants the method chosen as well as executed. A student who answers an explain question with a description loses every available mark while writing something entirely true.

The practical paper is the cheapest 20 per cent available. Its questions recur in recognisable shapes: identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables; state how to improve reliability; identify an anomalous result and say what to do about it; plot a graph with sensible axes and a best-fit line; describe a safety precaution relevant to this experiment rather than in general. These are learnable in a handful of sessions, which makes them the first place a short tutoring block should go.

sections.heading: The practical paper when the tutoring happens online
paragraphs: This is the question Ranches parents ask most often and the one with the clearest answer. The laboratory belongs to the school. Your child's practical lessons, the equipment, the supervision and, where the school enters it, the Paper 5 practical test all happen at JESS Arabian Ranches, Jebel Ali School, GEMS Metropole or wherever they are enrolled. Nothing about online tutoring changes that, and no tutoring provider should be offering to replace it.

Most schools in the UAE enter candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper rather than the practical test, because it is written rather than supervised in a laboratory. That paper is assessed on experimental reasoning expressed in writing, which is exactly the kind of work a video lesson handles well. The student reads a method, identifies the variables, spots the flaw, plots the results and writes the improvement, and the tutor marks each of those against the scheme while both are looking at the same page.

Where there is a practical test, the online session still helps with everything except the physical handling. Measurement technique, recording to the correct precision, tabulating before plotting, drawing a best-fit line rather than joining the dots, and identifying which result to discard are all discussed and practised on paper first. Students who do that arrive at the laboratory knowing what the examiner is looking for rather than discovering it while holding a burette.

Pearson Edexcel candidates have no separate practical paper at all, which sometimes leads a family to assume practical skills do not matter. They matter more, not less: the experimental questions are distributed through both written papers, where they arrive without warning in the middle of a content question. An Edexcel candidate who has never been drilled on variable control will meet it anyway, with fewer marks of warning.

sections.heading: The mark-scheme traps in IGCSE science
paragraphs: Five errors account for most preventable loss across all three sciences, and none of them is about not knowing the science. The first is answering the wrong command word, which was covered above and is worth repeating because it is the largest single cause. The second is units. An answer without a unit, or with the wrong unit after a correct calculation, loses the mark that the calculation earned. Standard form and prefix conversion between milli, centi, kilo and mega account for a surprising share of lost physics and chemistry marks.

The third is significant figures and rounding, where the expectation is an answer to the precision the data supports rather than the full calculator display. The fourth is graph marks, which are awarded mechanically: labelled axes with units, a scale that uses most of the grid, accurately plotted points, and a best-fit line that does not simply join the dots. Students lose two or three marks per graph for reasons that have nothing to do with the biology, chemistry or physics involved.

The fifth is extended writing. A six-mark question needs six distinct creditable points, written in a structure the examiner can follow, and most students write three good points at length instead. The fix is to plan in the margin: list the points first, then write. That single habit moves extended-writing marks more reliably than any amount of content revision, and it works identically in biology, chemistry and physics.

All five are diagnosed from a student's own marked script rather than from a conversation. That is why the most productive first session is usually a marking clinic: the student brings two papers with the marks on them, and the tutor classifies every loss as content, technique or presentation. Ranches families are frequently surprised by the result, because a report card that says science is a problem often turns out to mean mathematics and command words are the problem.

sections.heading: Past-paper method when there are three sciences to cover
paragraphs: A Year 11 student with three sciences, mathematics, English and two more subjects cannot do everything, so the order matters. The method that works is narrow and repeatable. Sit one paper, timed and closed-book. Mark it against the published scheme without generosity. Classify each loss as content, technique or presentation. Then spend the next block on the largest category rather than on the most recent topic. Most students invert this, revising whatever the school taught last week.

Classification is the step that needs another pair of eyes. A loss that feels like not knowing the content is often a command-word error, and a loss that feels careless is often a genuine gap. Getting this wrong wastes weeks. A tutor who reads two marked scripts and names the pattern has already earned more than one who spends the same hour re-teaching photosynthesis to a student whose problem is graph plotting.

Match the papers to the tier and the board. Extended papers are not useful practice for a Core candidate, and Cambridge papers are not useful timing practice for an Edexcel candidate even where the content overlaps. Where a school has changed board mid-course, as happens in the Ranches belt when families move campus, the useful set is the board the entry is actually made under, not the one the student started with.

On the papers themselves, the boundary is worth stating. IB Gram does not host, copy or distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables. Those belong to Cambridge Assessment International Education and to Pearson, and the legitimate routes are the school, the official store and each board's own website. A tutoring provider offering a downloadable archive is giving away something it does not own, and the material in such archives is frequently from the wrong syllabus version.

sections.heading: Five subjects, grade E, and UAE Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: For families who intend their child to apply to a UAE university, or to need an attested secondary certificate in the Emirates, the equivalency rule is worth knowing before Year 11 subject decisions are finalised. On the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

The detail that catches people out is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. A student carrying five subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has not met the requirement, however good the grades. One ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. The correct number is five, excluding those two.

Science counts towards the five, and this is where the route decision reappears. Three separate sciences contribute three of the five subjects. A double award contributes two. A single combined science grade contributes one. For a student taking a thin subject load, the science route can be the difference between meeting the requirement comfortably and meeting it with nothing to spare. That is a conversation for Year 10, not for the spring of Year 11.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and nothing on this page should be read as advice about a specific application. The process belongs to the Ministry of Education and to the emirate's attestation authority, and the requirement should be verified on moe.gov.ae before anything is relied upon. No IB Diploma points threshold is published here, because the figure has not been read on the Ministry's own pages and an unsourced number would be worse than none.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson session dates, counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November each year. Both publish official timetables, and both revise them, which is why a plan should be built from the school's own entry confirmation rather than from a figure on a tutoring page.

The Pearson Edexcel November 2026 International GCSE series makes the structural point better than any general statement. Written papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from the November 2025 sitting reached students on 22 January 2026, roughly nine weeks after the last paper. Entries for a November sitting close in the preceding summer and entries for the Cambridge June series close in the spring, in both cases several months before the first paper rather than weeks. The exact day sits on the statement of entry the school issues. A family deciding in September to change tier or add a subject for a November sitting has already missed the window.

Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong one. For a Ranches family that is one question to the school examinations officer, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The backwards plan below is the one a Year 11 student should be working to. It counts from the mock rather than from the series, because the mock is the deadline that changes behaviour, and because every school in the Ranches belt sets its own mock dates. Confirm every date with the school, and treat any date published on a tutoring site, including a provisional one, as a prompt to check rather than as a fact.

sections.heading: What IGCSE science tuition costs in the Ranches belt
paragraphs: Start at the cheapest end, because that is where most families start and where the most money is wasted. EdFlik advertises online sessions from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. At that price the tutor is usually a university student, and for checking homework or keeping a Year 9 student company through revision that can be perfectly adequate. For Extended-tier Year 11 work against a specific syllabus code it generally is not, and three months of it is more expensive than one month of something that works.

The next band up is where most IGCSE work sensibly sits. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 research puts qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour, and Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. In monthly terms the same research estimates AED 600 to 1,200 for a weekly one-hour session at the mid-market level, against AED 240 to 600 at the budget end. An advertised online package of AED 799 a month for eight sessions sits inside that band.

Above it sit the specialist and premium tiers, which matter less for IGCSE than for the Diploma. Bestimate puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and BartyED's examiner-led tier reaches AED 650. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with monthly in-home packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Every one of those figures was published by the company or research service that charges it.

The useful conclusion for a Ranches family is that the decision is about fit rather than tier. A Year 11 Extended chemistry candidate needs someone who knows 0620 Paper 4 and can mark against its scheme; that person exists in the middle band. A Year 9 student needs mathematics-for-science discipline, which is cheaper. Buying the premium tier for a Core-tier candidate is an expensive way to solve a problem that is not there. For context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27, so tuition is the part of the budget still changing.

faqs.question: Does my child sit separate sciences or Co-ordinated Sciences at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Only the school can tell you, and the answer is on the examination entry rather than the report card. Separate sciences produce three grades from three sets of papers. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 produces a double award from a thinner syllabus. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 produces a single grade. Pearson Edexcel runs separate sciences as 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 or a Double Award as 4SD0. Ask the examinations officer for the code; it decides the papers, the grades, the past papers worth using and the post-16 options.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0654 and three separate science syllabuses?
faqs.answer: Content depth and grades awarded. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 covers biology, chemistry and physics together at reduced depth and reports a double award. The separate syllabuses, 0610, 0620 and 0625, each cover one science in full and each award their own grade. For a student going on to A Level or Diploma science the separate route is the stronger preparation; the double award leaves a real gap, particularly in quantitative chemistry and in the physics topics that post-16 courses assume as known.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science papers does a Core candidate sit instead of Extended?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge science syllabuses a Core candidate sits the Core multiple-choice paper and the Core theory paper, while an Extended candidate sits the Extended versions of both. Both tiers sit the same practical or alternative-to-practical paper. The important consequence is the grade ceiling: the top grades are not available on Core. The second consequence is practice material, because Extended past papers contain questions a Core candidate will never be asked and are therefore a poor use of revision time.

faqs.question: How is IGCSE science practical work assessed if lessons happen online?
faqs.answer: The practical work itself stays at school, where the laboratory, the equipment and the supervision are. Most UAE schools enter candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper, which assesses experimental reasoning in writing, and that is well suited to a video lesson: the student reads a method, identifies the variables, spots the weakness, plots the results and writes the improvement while the tutor marks each step against the scheme. Where a school enters the practical test instead, everything except the physical handling can still be rehearsed on paper first.

faqs.question: What are the hardest Extended-only topics across the three IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: In biology, transport in plants, homeostasis and the genetics and inheritance material cause the most difficulty. In chemistry it is the quantitative work: mole calculations, electrolysis products at each electrode, and rates in greater depth. In physics it is moments, momentum and electromagnetic induction. The useful point for a family is that these form a finite, listable set rather than a general increase in difficulty, so a student moving from Core to Extended has a specific body of work to do rather than an open-ended one.

faqs.question: Should my child take Edexcel 4SD0 Double Award or Cambridge separate sciences?
faqs.answer: In practice the school decides, and the real question is what the choice costs later. Separate sciences give three grades and the strongest preparation for post-16 science. The Double Award gives two grades from a lighter load, which helps a crowded timetable and leaves a gap into A Level or Diploma science. For Ministry of Education equivalency the arithmetic matters too, since separate sciences contribute three of the five required subjects and a double award contributes two. Raise it in Year 10 while the timetable is still movable.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE science tuition cost per hour around Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Published market figures, cheapest first: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai research puts qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150; specialists reach AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 because the drive is inside the price. Those are other companies' rates, named and dated. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE science subjects count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Each separate science grade counts as one of the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects required on the British track, which must be achieved at no less than grade E or grade 3. A double award contributes two subjects and a single combined science grade contributes one. Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the count of five. A competitor page in this market states that six subjects are required; the published rule says five. Verify it on moe.gov.ae before relying on it for an application.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge IGCSE science entries have to be submitted?
faqs.answer: Months before the examination, and the school makes the entry rather than the family. A UAE candidate sits the Cambridge June series or the November series, and for both the final entry deadline falls several months ahead of the first paper: entries for June close in the spring, entries for November in the preceding summer. Cambridge publishes the exact dates for each series and does revise them, so the figure that governs a family plan is the one printed on the school statement of entry rather than any date quoted on a tutoring page. If a tier change or an added subject is under discussion it has to happen before that deadline, so ask the school examinations officer for the internal cut-off date, which usually sits a week or two earlier again.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover biology, chemistry and physics for the same IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: For technique work, yes, and it is often the most efficient arrangement. Command words, units, significant figures, graph conventions and extended-writing structure are identical across the three sciences, so one block of that work moves all three grades. For content, a specialist in the weakest subject is usually better value than a generalist across all three, particularly at Extended tier where the examiner expects depth. Many Ranches families run a technique block first and then a subject specialist for whichever science is still lagging.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well in class tests but badly on past papers?
faqs.answer: Class tests usually cover the topic just taught, in the style the teacher used, with generous marking. A past paper mixes topics, uses the board's own command words and is marked against the published scheme. Students who rely on recent recall rather than retained understanding are exposed by the first format change. The other common cause is timing: a paper that is comfortable untimed becomes a different task under the clock. Both are fixable, and both are diagnosed from the marked script rather than from the score.

faqs.question: What is the alternative to practical paper and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: It is the written alternative to the laboratory practical test, carrying 20 per cent of a Cambridge science grade, and it assesses experimental skill through questions about method rather than through handling apparatus. The marks follow recurring shapes: identify independent, dependent and controlled variables; explain how to improve reliability; identify an anomalous result and say what to do with it; plot a graph with labelled axes, a sensible scale and a best-fit line; state a safety precaution specific to this experiment. All of it is learnable in a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: How early in Year 10 should IGCSE science support begin?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families start, and the reason is the tier decision rather than the content. Cambridge tier placements are usually discussed in Year 10, and a student who wants Extended needs to demonstrate it before entries close. The second reason is mathematics: rearranging formulae, standard form, scale reading and graph plotting are examined inside science papers, and making them automatic in Year 10 is far cheaper than repairing them in the spring of Year 11, when there is no spare time left.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE science grades matter for IB Diploma subject choices at Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. Schools commonly set an entry expectation for a science at Higher Level, often expressed as a minimum IGCSE grade, and that expectation is the school's rather than the IB's, so it varies between JESS Arabian Ranches, Fairgreen International School and GEMS International School Al Khail. The second way is readiness: a student entering Diploma chemistry from the Extended separate syllabus starts in a different place from one arriving from a double award. Ask each school for its own published requirement.

faqs.question: Is a Ranches student at a disadvantage sitting IGCSE science in the November series?
faqs.answer: Not academically. Cambridge runs June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November, so a November entry is a normal route rather than a resit badge. What changes is the calendar: the teaching year is shorter before a November sitting, results arrive at a different point relative to post-16 applications, and the mock timetable has to be rebuilt. Confirm the series on the school entry, then plan backwards from it. Cambridge also allocates centres to administrative zones, so check the school is using the correct zone timetable.

A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0625 Physics to exam plans a very different session from one whose experience is Pearson 4PH1, because only one of those boards sets a separate practical paper.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one free evening, and the sum nobody does
paragraphs: Start with the week rather than the subject. A Year 11 in Arabian Ranches 2 taking three separate sciences is carrying three schemes of work, three sets of homework, three practical programmes and three teachers with independent deadlines. On top of that sit the mandatory UAE subjects, which Dubai private schools must teach regardless of their licensed curriculum, plus English, maths, a language and whatever else the option blocks produced. The number of genuinely free evenings in that week is usually one, occasionally two.

Now add the geography. There is no secondary school inside Arabian Ranches 2. Students from Casa, Rosa, Palma, Lila, Camelia, Azalea, Reem, Yasmin and Rasha travel out to Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Nad Al Sheba, Al Barsha South, DAMAC Hills or the Sustainable City. Those schools finish between roughly 15:00 and 15:30, and a bus that loops through Dubailand communities puts a child back inside the gates between 15:45 and 16:30. For a family on a long route, the usable evening starts at 17:30 and ends when homework does.

What follows is an allocation problem, and most families solve it badly by refusing to solve it. They buy a science tutor, give them the one free slot, and then discover that one hour a week cannot service three subjects. The tutor rotates - biology this week, chemistry next - and nothing gets fixed properly, because rotating attention across three syllabuses at one hour a week is slower than the rate at which new content arrives.

The alternative is triage, and it is uncomfortable rather than complicated. Identify which of the three sciences is genuinely behind rather than merely hard. Fix that one properly over eight to twelve weeks. Accept that the other two are being held rather than improved during that period. Families who do this get one science repaired and two held; families who rotate get three sciences mildly annoyed with them. The first outcome is better for a sixth-form application and considerably cheaper. The evidence for which subject to pick is already in the house: three marked papers, read side by side for the pattern behind the marks rather than for the marks themselves. Sometimes the pattern shows two weak sciences caused by one quantitative weakness, which is the cheapest diagnosis in this whole subject group and the one most often missed.

IB Gram supports Arabian Ranches 2 families with one-to-one IGCSE science teaching over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For a timetable this tight that is the practical point: the forty minutes a visiting tutor would spend driving into Dubailand stays inside your evening, and a session can start the moment your child is fed rather than when a car arrives.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-arabian-ran.programmesIntro: Four science routes account for nearly all entries in this catchment, and they differ by how much timetable they consume rather than only by difficulty. That matters more than anything else when one evening is all there is.

programmes.name: Three separate sciences
programmes.description: Cambridge 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Three qualifications, three grades, three practical programmes. The heaviest option on a timetable and the standard route for students aiming at science or medicine after school.
programmes.countryNote: The usual reason a triple-science student needs help is not ability but arrival rate: new content lands in three subjects simultaneously and one weak link in any of them compounds across two years. Families in Arabian Ranches 2 who recognise this in Year 10 spend far less than those who recognise it after the Year 11 mocks.

programmes.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences, double award
programmes.description: One entry producing two grades, covering biology, chemistry and physics at reduced depth. Theory sits in a two-hour paper of 120 marks, with multiple choice and a practical component alongside it. Substantially lighter on the timetable than three separate sciences, and widely misunderstood as a lesser choice.
programmes.countryNote: The commonest expensive error in this community is hiring three single-subject tutors for a child entered for 0654. One tutor who has taught the double award knows which sub-topics are excluded and prepares the correct papers, at a third of the cost. Check the entry code before buying anything.

programmes.name: Combined or single-award science
programmes.description: One entry, one grade, the lightest science load available. Chosen by students whose strengths and intended next steps sit elsewhere, and a sensible choice when it frees timetable space for subjects that matter more to the application.
programmes.countryNote: Worth checking against sixth-form entry requirements before it is settled. Some A Level and Diploma science courses in Dubai publish a requirement that a single-award route does not satisfy, and discovering that after results is a harder conversation than having it in Year 10.

programmes.name: Year 9, and the entry that gets decided there
programmes.description: Where the science route and the tier are effectively chosen. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October, and a Year 9 who is shaky in quantitative work is a Year 10 who gets placed on a lighter route or a capped tier.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest point to intervene in the whole sequence and the one families in this catchment skip most often. Ten hours in Year 9 costs a fraction of thirty in Year 11, and it is the difference between choosing a science route and being allocated one.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-arabian-ran.subjectsIntro: A science tutoring plan is built from specific components and specific topics. The entries below are what sessions actually contain, and the practical papers are where the recoverable marks hide.

subjects.name: Cambridge Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-heavy, so students mistake reading for revision. Marks move on command-term discipline and on the extended responses, where describe and explain are confused. Transport in plants, enzymes and inheritance are the recurring losses in this catchment, and the diagrams are worth practising rather than looking at.

subjects.name: Cambridge Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and rates of reaction absorb the hours. Extended candidates sit Paper 2 for multiple choice, Paper 4 for theory and either Paper 5 or Paper 6 for the practical component. Quantitative work is the barrier for most students, which is why a shared maths weakness often shows up first here.

subjects.name: Cambridge Physics 0625
subjects.description: The most drillable of the three and therefore good value per paid hour. Losses concentrate in electricity, where circuit reasoning fails, and in equation recall under time pressure. A physics session that consists of timed questions rather than explanation produces more marks than one that feels more comfortable.

subjects.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Three sciences at reduced depth, one entry, two grades. Theory sits in a two-hour 120-mark paper alongside multiple choice and the practical component. A tutor who has taught it knows the exclusions; a tutor who has not will teach content the student is never examined on, using hours that are already scarce.

subjects.name: Pearson Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Paper 1 runs two hours for 110 marks and Paper 2 one hour fifteen for 70 marks. No separate practical examination: practical skills are assessed inside the written papers, so method and variable questions appear without warning in a theory context. Revision plans built for Cambridge miss this entirely.

subjects.name: Pearson Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Same two-paper architecture as the Pearson sciences generally, with practical understanding examined in writing rather than in a laboratory sitting. The quantitative load is comparable to Cambridge; the assessment style is not, and past-paper sets from the two boards are not interchangeable.

subjects.name: Pearson Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two written papers, practical skills assessed within them, and a heavier emphasis on applying a small number of relationships across unfamiliar contexts. Students who have drilled Cambridge past papers often find the question style unfamiliar, which is a board problem rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: Cambridge Paper 5, practical test
subjects.description: A real practical sitting worth 20% of the grade, where marks go on following a method precisely, recording readings properly and handling a result that does not look right. Rehearsable, rarely rehearsed, and the component most often left until the fortnight before the series.

subjects.name: Cambridge Paper 6, alternative to practical
subjects.description: A written paper on practical work, also 20% of the grade. It asks about apparatus choice, control of variables, sources of error and reading scales. Entirely learnable without a laboratory, which makes it the highest-value component for a student taking this option.

subjects.name: Shared quantitative skills
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, units, significant figures and reading graphs. When two sciences are weak at once, this is usually the single cause. Fixing it once improves physics and chemistry together, which is the only genuine shortcut available to a family with one free evening.

sections.heading: What this search is actually trying to solve
paragraphs: A parent looking for an IGCSE science tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 has usually been told by a school report that one or more sciences are below target, and has one evening in which to do something about it. The literal search is for proximity. The real problem is capacity. Those are different problems and only one of them has a useful solution.

Proximity, on its own terms, is answerable: agencies serve the whole of Dubai and will send someone into Dubailand for a travel-loaded rate, and a few independent tutors live locally. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table putting ordinary in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. The drive from the city into Arabian Ranches 2 in evening traffic is long, so the premium here sits at the upper end of that band while the teaching is the same as the online version at AED 150 to 300.

Capacity is the harder question, and it is where an honest answer differs from a sales one. One hour a week cannot service three sciences. New content arrives in all three faster than a single rotating hour can consolidate it, so a tutor who agrees to cover biology, chemistry and physics in alternate weeks is agreeing to something that does not work. Saying so costs us a larger booking and saves you a term.

What the hour can do is repair one subject properly, or fix a shared skill that improves two at once. Those are the two productive uses of a single slot, and choosing between them needs one marked paper from each science. IB Gram delivers this support one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE at all. For a week this tight, the forty minutes that a visiting tutor spends in traffic is not a small consideration.

sections.heading: A triple-science Year 11 week, hour by hour
paragraphs: The table below is the version of the week that families in this community recognise, and it is worth looking at before deciding how many sciences to buy help for. School finishes between 15:00 and 15:30. Bus arrival in Arabian Ranches 2 lands between 15:45 and 16:30 depending on the cluster. Between arrival and bedtime there is homework from three sciences plus everything else, and in a Dubai school there is also the mandatory subject load, which occupies real timetable space during the day and real revision space outside it.

Two observations fall out of it. First, the apparent gap straight off the bus is not usable. A child who has sat two double periods and travelled forty minutes is capable of low-demand work and nothing more, which is precisely the wrong moment for chemistry calculations or a timed physics paper. Second, the weekend is not spare capacity to be left empty; it is the only part of the week in which anything resembling exam conditions is possible.

The third observation is the one that changes spending. Looking at the week honestly, most families discover they have one reliable weekday slot and one weekend morning. That is two sessions of capacity, which is enough to repair one science and practise the practical component, and not enough to support three subjects. The decision then becomes which science, rather than how many, and that is a decision a marked paper can make.

A note on practical catch-up, which is specific to science and often missed in planning. Students who miss a practical through absence or a timetable clash are frequently asked to make it up after school, which removes an afternoon without notice. Families planning a fixed weekly slot in science should expect this to happen two or three times a term and build in the flexibility rather than treating each occurrence as a crisis.

sections.heading: Which science to fix first, and how to tell
paragraphs: Triage needs evidence rather than impressions, and the evidence is three marked papers - one from each science. What you are looking for is not the lowest mark but the pattern behind it, because two of the three common patterns are fixable in a term and the third is not a science problem at all.

The first pattern is a quantitative one: marks lost on calculation, units, rearrangement and graph work, appearing in both physics and chemistry and absent from biology. That is one problem presenting as two weak subjects, and fixing it with a short shared-skills block improves both at once. It is the cheapest and most satisfying diagnosis available in this subject group, and it is missed constantly because the two subjects are taught by different teachers who each see only their half of it.

The second pattern is content arrears in one subject only: a gap that opened in Year 10, was never closed, and now sits under everything newer. Electricity in physics and moles in chemistry are the usual culprits in this catchment. That is a genuine eight to twelve week job for the single subject, and it is what the weekday slot should be spent on. Attempting it while also rotating through two other sciences is how a term disappears.

The third pattern is answered-well-then-abandoned: the first two thirds of each paper correct, the last third blank, across all three sciences. That is pacing, and more content teaching will not move it. It is trained in short timed blocks, ideally on the weekend morning when the student is rested, and it is the one pattern where the fix is cheaper than the diagnosis implied.

sections.heading: Why the slot you choose changes which science works
paragraphs: Different sciences survive different hours, and this is not a theory about learning styles. It is about what each subject demands at the moment of study. Chemistry calculations, physics problem-solving and anything timed need working memory and sustained attention. Biology recall, diagram labelling and vocabulary consolidation need much less. Putting the wrong subject in the wrong slot wastes a paid hour and teaches a child they are worse at something than they are.

The practical consequence for a family in Camelia or Azalea, where the bus arrives nearest 16:30, is that the weekday slot should carry the subject that most needs a tutor driving the session. That is usually chemistry or physics: a tutor working through a calculation on a shared screen carries the cognitive load while the student follows and questions. Biology is the better subject to handle independently or in the lower-energy part of the evening, because recall work survives tiredness in a way that multi-step calculation does not.

The weekend morning, by contrast, is the only part of the week when a student is close to the state they will be in during an examination. That makes it the right place for two things: timed papers of any kind, and the practical component. A Paper 6 alternative-to-practical question set, worked under time and then marked together, is a better use of a rested Saturday hour than any amount of content teaching.

None of this requires more paid hours, which is the point. Moving the subjects around inside the same two slots typically produces better marks than adding a third session, because each hour is now being spent on work the student can actually do at that moment. Families who rearrange before they expand usually find they do not need to expand.

sections.heading: Triple, double and single award: what each one costs in timetable
paragraphs: Science routes differ by timetable consumption as much as by difficulty, and for a family whose problem is capacity, that is the more useful comparison. Three separate sciences means three qualifications, three practical programmes and three independent sets of deadlines. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is one entry producing two grades across all three disciplines at reduced depth. A single or combined award is one entry and one grade.

The error that costs most money in this community is buying three single-subject tutors for a child entered for the double award. It is a straightforward misunderstanding - the child studies biology, chemistry and physics, so three tutors looks logical - and it triples a bill to cover content the student is not examined on. One tutor who has taught 0654 knows what is excluded and prepares the correct papers, including the two-hour 120-mark theory paper that has no equivalent in the separate sciences.

Tiering is the other thing to check, and it differs by board. Cambridge tiers its sciences into Core and Extended: a Core entry cannot be awarded above a grade C, while Extended spans A* to E. Pearson's International GCSE sciences are untiered and report 9 to 1. So a Cambridge Core candidate working comfortably above a C has a ceiling problem that no amount of teaching can solve, and the fix is an entry change through the school's exams officer.

For a family weighing routes in Year 9 or Year 10, the honest advice is to check sixth-form entry requirements before the timetable argument is settled. Some A Level and Diploma science courses in Dubai publish requirements that a single-award route does not satisfy. That is a ten-minute conversation with the school in Year 10 and a much harder one after results, and it costs nothing at the point where it is still useful.

sections.heading: The practical component, and what it means for a family without a laboratory
paragraphs: Cambridge candidates sit either Paper 5, a real practical test, or Paper 6, a written alternative to practical. Either way the component carries twenty per cent of the grade in each science. Pearson works differently: its International GCSE sciences have no separate practical paper, and practical understanding is examined inside the written papers instead, where a method or variable question can appear in the middle of a theory section.

For a student entered for Paper 6, this is genuinely good news and almost nobody exploits it. The paper asks about apparatus choice, controlling variables, sources of error, reading scales and interpreting results tables. All of that can be taught and practised without any apparatus at all, which makes it the single most learnable twenty per cent in the qualification. A tutor working on a shared screen with a results table is doing exactly the right thing for this component.

For a Paper 5 candidate the laboratory work itself belongs to the school, and no tutoring arrangement should pretend otherwise. What a tutor can do is everything surrounding it: make sure the student knows what the method is asking before they walk in, understand how to record readings to a sensible precision, and know what to do when a reading looks wrong. Debriefing a practical afterwards from the student's own recorded results is productive work and entirely suited to a screen.

Pearson candidates need a specific warning. Because the practical content is embedded in the written papers rather than isolated, students who have drilled Cambridge past papers for practice encounter an unfamiliar question style in the real thing. Past-paper sets are not interchangeable between boards, and a tutor should be setting work from the board your child is actually entered for. Ask which board's papers will be used in the first session; the answer is a reasonable test of whether the match is right.

sections.heading: Term by term: when each science tends to go wrong here
paragraphs: Science problems in this catchment appear on a fairly predictable schedule, and knowing it lets a family act before the report rather than after it. Year 10 term one is the quiet period: content is introductory, marks look fine, and the quantitative gap from Year 9 is forming invisibly. Year 10 term two is where chemistry first separates students, usually at moles and reacting masses, because it is the first point at which the subject requires sustained calculation.

Physics follows in Year 10 term three or Year 11 term one, almost always at electricity. Circuit reasoning requires holding several relationships in mind simultaneously, and a student who is slow at rearranging formulae cannot do it however well they understand the physics. This is the single clearest example of a maths weakness presenting as a science weakness, and treating it as physics teaching wastes the term.

Biology arrives last, in Year 11, and the trigger is volume rather than difficulty. The content accumulates until recall alone stops being enough and the extended-response questions start demanding selection and structure. Students who have coped by reading suddenly cannot, and the mark drop looks sharper than the underlying change because it is really a change in what the questions ask for.

The practical component is the exception: it does not go wrong at a particular time, it simply never gets addressed until the fortnight before the series. That is why a weekend slot allocated to Paper 5 or Paper 6 work from Year 11 term one is one of the better decisions available, and why it so rarely gets made. Twenty per cent of three grades is a large amount of marks to leave to a fortnight.
