sections.heading: The subjects that are not sciences, and the hours they take
paragraphs: Any realistic plan for a Dubai Year 11 has to account for the mandatory subject load, because it occupies timetable space that families moving from a UK school do not expect. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The structure is specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

For a science family the practical consequence is arithmetic. Those lessons are in the school day, which compresses science teaching time, and for students who find Arabic difficult they also consume evening hours. A tutoring plan that assumes a Dubai Year 11 has the same free evenings as a UK Year 11 will over-commit. Plan from the actual school timetable, and if Arabic is itself the pressure point, that is a separate conversation about a separate kind of tutor.

sections.heading: Rates, permits and what happens when the slot cannot be filled
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures, with each source named: budget online and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150; in-home visits run AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500; IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

On availability, the honest position is that the 17:30 to 19:00 Gulf Standard Time window is the busiest hour in this market, and three sciences each want it. If no specialist is free for your subject and slot, we will say so and set out the alternatives with rates attached: a different weekday evening, a weekend morning, or a tutor whose hours sit outside the Gulf peak. What we will not do is put a biology tutor in front of a physics problem because the hour was available.

Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work and the permit is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no official fine schedule is published.

Two limits worth stating before anybody books. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, so your child's own science teacher privately is not an arrangement we will make. And IB Gram holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the licence a tutoring operation with premises in Dubai requires, because we run no premises in the UAE.

We plan the slot from when your child is home and fed, because a session that starts while they are still in the car is a session nobody gets value from.

process.title: Send one marked paper from each science
process.description: Three scripts let us read the pattern rather than the marks: shared quantitative errors across physics and chemistry, content arrears in one subject, blanks in the last third of every paper, or practical questions wrong while theory is right. Those four findings lead to four completely different plans.

process.title: Agree the triage before the timetable
process.description: If one hour a week is what the week allows, we will tell you which single science to spend it on and what happens to the other two. That is a less comfortable conversation than agreeing to cover all three, and it is the one that produces a repaired subject rather than three partly-served ones.

process.title: Take the free trial and fix the two slots
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, before any payment and with no card details taken. Afterwards we settle which subject sits in the weekday slot, what the weekend morning is for, and what the first four sessions will cover, in writing.

process.title: Expect practical catch-ups to disrupt it
process.description: Science students get called back for missed practicals two or three times a term, usually at short notice. We build that into the arrangement rather than treating each one as a cancellation, and we use the displaced session for the practical-paper work that would otherwise never get scheduled.

whyPoints.title: Planned from the bus, not the bell
whyPoints.description: Schools in this catchment finish between 15:00 and 15:30, and Dubailand bus loops add forty to seventy minutes. We start from arrival time, which is why most Arabian Ranches 2 families end up with a 17:30 or 18:00 weekday slot and a weekend morning rather than the 16:15 session that looked obvious.

whyPoints.title: Triage instead of rotation
whyPoints.description: One hour a week cannot service three sciences, because new content arrives faster than a rotating hour consolidates it. We identify which science is genuinely behind, fix that one, and say plainly that the other two are being held. That is the arrangement that produces a grade change.

whyPoints.title: The shared-skills shortcut
whyPoints.description: Physics and chemistry weak at the same time is usually one quantitative problem wearing two subject names. Four to six hours on rearranging formulae, units, standard form and graph reading improves both at once, and it is the only real shortcut available to a family with one free evening.

whyPoints.title: The practical 20% taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Paper 6 is a written paper about practical work, worth a fifth of each Cambridge science grade and entirely learnable without a laboratory. We schedule it into the rested weekend hour from Year 11 term one, rather than leaving a fifth of three grades to the fortnight before the series.

whyPoints.title: Board-correct practice papers
whyPoints.description: Cambridge sets a separate practical paper; Pearson examines practical understanding inside its written papers. Past-paper sets are not interchangeable, and a tutor drilling the wrong board's questions is using scarce hours to build the wrong familiarity. We match on the code your child is entered for.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the hour
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 because somebody is driving into Dubailand in evening traffic, and from the back clusters of this community the drive is longest. Online delivery at AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor keeps that time inside your evening instead.

faqs.question: What time can a science session start for a Year 11 bussed back to Arabian Ranches 2?
faqs.answer: Plan from arrival, not from the school bell. Schools this community feeds finish between roughly 15:00 and 15:30, and Dubailand bus loops put students back inside the gates between 15:45 and 16:30 depending on the cluster. Casa, Rosa and Palma can sometimes manage a 17:00 start; Camelia, Azalea and Reem are realistically 18:00. The 16:15 slot that looks like the obvious gap is the least productive hour of the week, particularly for chemistry calculations or anything timed.

faqs.question: My child takes three sciences and we have one free evening. Which one do we tutor?
faqs.answer: Send one marked paper from each and read the pattern rather than the marks. Calculation and unit errors in physics and chemistry while biology is fine means one shared quantitative problem, fixable in four to six hours and improving both subjects at once. One subject clearly behind means eight to twelve weeks on that subject alone, with the other two held rather than improved. Blanks in the last third of all three papers means pacing, which is trained in short timed blocks instead.

faqs.question: Can one tutor rotate between biology, chemistry and physics week by week?
faqs.answer: They can, and it does not work. New content arrives in three subjects faster than a single rotating hour consolidates it, so each science gets touched roughly once a fortnight while its scheme of work moves on weekly. The result is three subjects mildly supported and none repaired. A tutor who agrees to this arrangement is agreeing to a larger booking rather than a better outcome. One science fixed properly beats three sciences visited occasionally.

faqs.question: Does biology revision work in the late part of the evening?
faqs.answer: Better than chemistry or physics does. Recall work, diagram labelling and vocabulary consolidation survive tiredness reasonably well, while multi-step calculation and timed problem-solving do not. That is a scheduling point rather than a claim about ability: the tutor-led weekday slot should carry whichever subject most needs someone driving the session, usually chemistry or physics, and biology recall can sit in the lower-energy part of the evening or be done independently.

faqs.question: Why did physics slip in Year 11 while biology stayed fine?
faqs.answer: Almost always electricity, and almost always a maths problem rather than a physics one. Circuit reasoning requires holding several relationships in mind at once, and a student who rearranges formulae slowly cannot do it however well they grasp the concept. Biology is unaffected because it makes different demands. Treating this as physics teaching wastes a term; four to six hours on rearrangement, units and standard form usually moves physics and chemistry together.

faqs.question: Our school entered our daughter for Core science. What does that mean for her grades?
faqs.answer: In the Cambridge sciences, a Core entry cannot be awarded above a grade C, while an Extended entry spans A* to E. Pearson's International GCSE sciences are untiered and report 9 to 1, so this question only arises for Cambridge candidates. If she is working comfortably above a C, the problem is the entry rather than her preparation, and the fix is an entry change through the school's exams officer. That conversation has to happen before the entry deadline, which sits months ahead of the papers.

faqs.question: How does Pearson assess practical science if there is no practical exam?
faqs.answer: Practical understanding is examined inside the written papers rather than in a separate sitting, so a method, apparatus or variable-control question can appear in the middle of a theory section without warning. Cambridge instead sets Paper 5, a real practical test, or Paper 6, a written alternative, each worth 20% of the grade. The practical consequence is that past-paper sets are not interchangeable between the two boards, and a student drilling the wrong board's questions is building the wrong familiarity.

faqs.question: Is Paper 6 worth scheduling if we have no laboratory at home?
faqs.answer: It is the highest-value component available to a family without one. Paper 6, the alternative to practical, is a written paper about practical work carrying 20% of each Cambridge science grade, and it asks about apparatus choice, controlling variables, sources of error, reading scales and interpreting results tables. All of that is teachable and practisable on a shared screen with no equipment at all. Most students leave it until the fortnight before the series, which is why it is reliably recoverable marks.

faqs.question: We were told to hire three tutors because our son studies all three sciences. Is that right?
faqs.answer: Check the entry code first. If he is entered for Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, that is one entry producing two grades across all three disciplines at reduced depth, with its own two-hour 120-mark theory paper. Three single-subject tutors will teach content he is never examined on and triple the bill. One tutor who has taught the double award knows the exclusions and prepares the right papers. This is the most expensive misunderstanding in science tutoring in this community.

faqs.question: How much of a Dubai Year 11 timetable goes to subjects outside the sciences?
faqs.answer: More than families arriving from a UK school expect. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA calculates the instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs under twenty-five minutes. Separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies.

faqs.question: What happens to the weekly slot when the school day shortens during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: The slot usually moves rather than disappears, often to after Iftar, and the sensible change is to the type of work rather than the amount. Content teaching and tutor-led worked examples run perfectly well in a later slot. Timed papers do not, particularly for a student who is fasting, because the resulting script measures fatigue rather than science. Shift timed work to the weeks either side and use the shortened weeks for content and practical-paper preparation instead.

faqs.question: Our son keeps getting called back for missed practicals. How do we plan around that?
faqs.answer: Expect it two or three times a term and build it in rather than treating each one as a cancellation. Science students miss practicals through absence and timetable clashes, and the catch-up is often arranged at short notice after school. The useful response is to have a default alternative use for the displaced session: practical-paper questions, a timed theory section, or the shared quantitative work that always needs more time. That turns a disruption into the work nobody otherwise schedules.

faqs.question: Should the weekend be kept free or used for science?
faqs.answer: Used, but briefly and deliberately. A weekend morning is the only part of the week when a student in this community is close to the state they will be in during an examination, which makes it the right place for timed papers and for the practical component. Forty-five to sixty minutes is enough, and keeping it short is what lets it survive family weekends and sport fixtures. Using the whole weekend is how a plan collapses by half-term.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE science tutor cost per month for a family in this community?
faqs.answer: Published monthly estimates for a single weekly hour in Dubai are AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Hourly, qualified online subject tutors are listed at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150, against AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits where the rate includes a drive into Dubailand. Each figure belongs to the publisher named, not to IB Gram.

faqs.question: Both physics and chemistry are weak. Is that two problems or one?
faqs.answer: Usually one. Check whether the lost marks in both subjects are on calculation, units, rearrangement and graph reading, and whether biology is unaffected. If so, it is a single quantitative weakness presenting as two weak sciences, and four to six hours on those skills improves both at once. It gets missed constantly because the two subjects are taught by different teachers who each see only their half of the pattern, and because the school report lists two problems rather than one.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-arabian-ran.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics to Year 10 and Year 11 students across the Dubailand communities. Each one works to a named syllabus code rather than a general science brief, and each one marks written answers against the published assessment objectives before a session ends.

intro.heading: Why the community on the map matters less than the syllabus code on the exam entry
paragraphs: Arabian Ranches 3 is a young community. The villas filled quickly, the school-age population arrived in a rush, and the result is a lot of families asking the same question in the same autumn: who can help with Year 10 science. The search almost always has a postcode in it. Parents type the community name because that is how you find a plumber, a swimming coach or a piano teacher, and there is no obvious reason science should work differently.

It does work differently, and the reason is boring. A plumber has to be in the room. A science tutor has to know which of five possible IGCSE science routes your child's school entered them for, which papers that route sits, and which of the twenty-odd topics on it are the ones that quietly lose marks in May. A tutor who lives two roundabouts away but teaches to the wrong specification is worse than useless; a tutor who has marked four hundred Paper 6 scripts and happens to be elsewhere is the one who moves the grade.

This page is written as a comparison on purpose. Arabian Ranches 3 sits inside a ring of communities that share almost everything: Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2 to the north, Mudon and Remraam to the south, Town Square to the east, Motor City and Dubai Sports City to the west, DAMAC Hills either side. The schools overlap. The school-run timings overlap. The tutoring question overlaps so completely that the sensible answer is identical in all of them, and saying so is more useful than pretending each community needs its own bespoke advice.

What is genuinely local is the timetable. Families here drive, not walk. The afternoon run out of the Ranches school cluster and back into the newer phases of Arabian Ranches 3 eats the hour between three and four, and an online lesson that starts at 4.30pm with a child who has eaten something works far better than one squeezed into a car at 3.15pm. That scheduling detail is worth more to a Year 11 science grade than any claim about proximity.

One more piece of local arithmetic is worth stating before the detail. Arabian Ranches 3 filled while the school pipeline was still catching up, so a larger share of children here travel further to school than in the older phases, and a larger share changed schools at least once. Both facts show up in science: a child who moved mid-key-stage has usually met two different schemes of work and skipped the overlap between them. That is a diagnosable gap rather than a vague weakness, and it is the first thing worth checking.

The rest of the page does four things. It sorts out which science route your child is actually on, with syllabus codes. It shows where marks go missing in each paper. It publishes what the Dubai market charges in AED, with attribution, because almost nobody in this search result publishes a number at all. And it says plainly how lessons are delivered: one-to-one, live, over video, with a shared whiteboard and a recording your child can rewatch the night before a test.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-arabian-ran.programmesIntro: Four programmes matter to a family in Arabian Ranches 3 thinking about science at 14 to 16. Two are the IGCSE boards themselves, one is the middle-school programme that feeds into them, and one is the sixth-form route that will judge whatever grade your child comes out with.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Sciences
programmes.description: Cambridge runs Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 as separate qualifications, plus Combined Science 0653 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 for students who want breadth without three full timetable blocks. Each separate science is tiered: Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 with a grade ceiling of C, Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach A*. Every route also carries a practical component, either Paper 5 under laboratory conditions or Paper 6, the written alternative.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after using the wrong zone timetable. Dubai schools sit the June series and the November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not a window an Arabian Ranches 3 family can plan around. A Year 11 student here should know their school's zone letter before anyone builds a revision plan around published dates, because two zones can sit the same Chemistry paper on different days.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Sciences
programmes.description: Pearson's separate sciences are 4BI1 Biology, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4PH1 Physics, each assessed by two written papers with no separate practical paper. Practical skills are examined inside the written papers instead, which changes revision completely: a student cannot bank marks by rehearsing apparatus drawings, and must instead handle experimental method questions cold. Double Award Science 4SD0 compresses all three subjects into two grades.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson offers International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026. Several schools near Arabian Ranches 3 moved to Edexcel for the shorter paper count, so check the entry form rather than assuming Cambridge.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The IB schools in this part of Dubai run MYP sciences with criterion-based assessment: Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science. Students are marked 1-8 against each criterion rather than against a percentage. Families often arrive at an IGCSE science tutor because a child has moved from an MYP school into a British-curriculum one and the written-paper conventions are unfamiliar.
programmes.countryNote: That MYP-to-IGCSE move is common in the Dubailand belt because community growth outpaced school places, so children change schools mid-key-stage more often than they would in a settled market. The gap is almost never content. It is exam grammar: command terms, mark allocation, and the habit of writing to the number of marks on the line rather than to the length of the thought.

programmes.name: IB Diploma and A Level Sciences
programmes.description: Whatever your child does at 16 is the thing that reads their IGCSE science grade. DP Chemistry HL and A Level Chemistry both assume fluency with moles, bonding and organic mechanisms that IGCSE only introduces. Physics at HL assumes algebraic rearrangement that Core-tier candidates have never been asked to do. A good Year 11 science year is partly about the grade and partly about not arriving in Year 12 with gaps that take a term to repair.
programmes.countryNote: Schools around Arabian Ranches 3 split both ways at 16: some run A Levels, some run the IB Diploma, a few run both and ask families to choose in Year 11. The practical consequence is that the Year 11 science conversation in this part of Dubai is a sixth-form conversation as well, and it happens in January while mocks are still being marked.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-arabian-ran.subjectsIntro: Science is not one subject. A tutor who treats Biology, Chemistry and Physics as interchangeable will teach the recall and skip the mathematics, or teach the mathematics and skip the terminology. These are the components families around Arabian Ranches 3 ask for most, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis, rates of reaction, organic chemistry and the qualitative analysis tables. Extended candidates meet reacting-mass problems that need two conversion steps, and the marks lost are almost always unit errors or a failure to state the limiting reactant. The qualitative analysis section rewards rote accuracy and punishes approximation.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Forces and motion, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, and atomic physics. Electricity is where this syllabus separates grades: series and parallel reasoning, potential dividers, and the difference between what an ammeter reads and what a student assumes it reads. Graph-gradient questions carry easy marks that go missing for want of units on the axes.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Characteristics of living organisms, transport in plants and humans, respiration, coordination and response, inheritance and ecology. Biology looks like a memory subject and is assessed as a precision subject. Marks go on specified terminology, on naming the correct structure rather than its region, and on explaining a mechanism in the order the mark scheme lists it.

subjects.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: All three sciences assessed across Papers 1 to 4 plus a practical component, awarded as two IGCSE grades. Content depth is close to the separate sciences, which surprises families who chose it expecting a lighter load. The real saving is timetable blocks, not revision hours, and any tutor should say so before the first session.

subjects.name: Cambridge Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: One grade covering Biology, Chemistry and Physics at reduced depth. It suits a student carrying nine or ten subjects who will not continue science past 16. It does not satisfy entry to DP HL science or A Level science at most schools, so the choice needs making with the sixth-form plan in view, not after it.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Two written papers, no practical paper, and experimental method examined inside the written questions. Untiered entry means every candidate meets the hardest material, which helps a strong student and exposes a weak one. Organic chemistry and the mole appear in both papers, so a gap cannot be parked for the second sitting.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers forces, electricity, waves, energy and magnetism; Paper 2 adds astrophysics and particle content. The formula sheet is sparser than students expect and several relationships must be recalled. Candidates lose marks by quoting a formula correctly and then substituting in the wrong units, particularly with prefixes.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Two papers across the five topic areas, with a noticeably heavier weighting on data handling than the Cambridge equivalent. Students who have been drilled on recall arrive unprepared for questions that hand them an unfamiliar graph and ask for an inference. That skill transfers from practice papers and almost nowhere else.

subjects.name: Paper 6 technique, alternative to practical
subjects.description: A written paper about experiments the candidate has not performed. It tests reading a measuring instrument, identifying a variable, spotting an anomalous result, suggesting an improvement and drawing a table with correct headings and units. Every one of those is a teachable habit, and most schools run out of time to teach them.

subjects.name: Mathematics for science
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, significant figures, percentage change, gradients and ratio. A Year 11 student failing Physics questions is often failing the algebra inside them. Half an hour a week on this strand usually shows up in Chemistry and Biology marks as well, because the data questions are the same skill wearing different clothes.

subjects.name: Required practical knowledge
subjects.description: Titration, rates of reaction by gas collection, food tests, osmosis in potato strips, resistance of a wire, specific heat capacity. Online lessons work through real data sets from these experiments rather than simulating apparatus, which is what the written papers actually ask about.

schoolClusters.note: These are the schools students in Arabian Ranches 3 and the neighbouring phases most commonly attend. sections.heading: What an IGCSE science tutor in Arabian Ranches 3 actually needs to know
paragraphs: The useful answer to this search is a question back: which syllabus, which tier, and which papers. There are at least five IGCSE science routes running in schools used by families in Arabian Ranches 3, and they are assessed differently enough that a tutor who gets it wrong will spend three weeks teaching content your child will never be examined on. A parent who can say "Cambridge 0620, Extended, Paper 6 route" has already made the match twice as likely to work.

Proximity, the thing the search phrase is actually about, has a smaller effect than almost anyone expects. A tutor who lives in Arabian Ranches 2 is fifteen minutes away on a good afternoon and forty on a bad one, and either way the hour they spend driving is an hour they are not teaching, paid for by somebody. Market in-home rates in Dubai sit higher than online rates for exactly this reason, and the gap is travel, not teaching quality.

What proximity does buy is cultural fluency: a tutor in the same belt knows which school sets which textbook, which head of science marks hard, and what the mock timetable looks like. That knowledge is real and worth having. It is also knowledge a tutor can hold without living nearby, because it comes from teaching students at those schools, and teaching them online does not reduce it.

So the recommendation for Arabian Ranches 3 is the same recommendation as for Mudon, Town Square, Motor City or Remraam: pick for the syllabus code and the paper experience, and take the delivery format that leaves the most teaching minutes in the hour. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. There are no home visits in Dubai on our side; that is an India-only service, and the next section's table is the argument for why that is not a concession.

sections.heading: The five science routes, with their syllabus codes
paragraphs: This is the single most useful table a Dubai science page can carry, and it is the one almost no competing page has. Before anything else happens, establish which row your child is on. The school's exam-entry confirmation names it; a report card usually does not, and a child in Year 10 very often does not know.

The tiering question matters as much as the board. Cambridge separate sciences are tiered: a Core entry caps the grade at C, and a student entered for Core in October who is working at B standard by February is in trouble that only the school can fix, because entries can usually be amended but not indefinitely. Any tutor who spots a mismatch between tier and working standard should say so early enough for the school to act.

Pearson's separate sciences take the opposite approach with a single untiered entry, so every candidate sees the full difficulty range. That is better for an ambitious student and harder on a struggling one, and it changes how a tutor sequences topics: there is no safe material to retreat to, so the work has to be on technique for the hardest question types from the start.

The practical component is the other real fork. Cambridge candidates sit either Paper 5, under laboratory conditions at the school, or Paper 6, a written alternative about experiments they have not run. Pearson examines experimental method inside the written papers. A tutor needs to know which of those three situations applies, because the preparation for each is genuinely different work.

sections.heading: Paper 5, Paper 6 and what happens to practical work when lessons are online
paragraphs: This is the objection every Dubai science parent raises, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. A tutor cannot run a titration with your child over video, and nobody should pretend otherwise. What a tutor can do is prepare your child for the thing that is actually examined, which in every case is a written response about practical work rather than the practical work itself.

Cambridge Paper 5 is sat at the school, in the school laboratory, supervised by school staff. No private tutor has ever sat in that room. Preparation for it is reading apparatus accurately, recording to consistent decimal places, drawing a results table with units in the headings, plotting with a sensible scale and writing a conclusion that refers to the data. Every one of those is better taught on a screen with a real past-paper data set than at a bench, because the bench time gets used up on the procedure.

Paper 6, the alternative to practical, is a written paper from end to end. It asks a candidate to describe how they would test a variable, identify what is wrong with a described method, read a thermometer or burette from a diagram, and spot the anomalous point in somebody else's table. Students lose marks here for vagueness rather than ignorance: "measure the temperature" where the mark scheme wants "measure the temperature every 30 seconds for five minutes".

Pearson candidates have no practical paper, which does not mean no practical content. Experimental method appears inside 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 as data-handling and method-evaluation questions, often worth four or five marks in a single block. A student who has only ever revised content walks into those blind. Working through them cold, with the mark scheme covered and then revealed, is the fastest fix available and needs nothing but a screen and a pen.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE science marks actually go missing
paragraphs: A mock result of 58% tells you nothing about what to do next. The same 58% can mean a student who understands everything and writes badly, or one who writes well and has three topic gaps, and the remedies are opposite. The first thing a competent tutor does with a Year 11 is take the mock paper apart question by question and sort the lost marks into categories, because the category decides the plan.

Across the three sciences the categories repeat with depressing consistency. Unit and prefix errors. Formula quoted correctly and then misapplied. A mechanism explained in the wrong order. Terminology that is nearly right, which in Biology scores zero. Graph work without units on the axes. Answers that are two sentences long for a one-mark question and one sentence long for a four-mark question. None of these is a knowledge problem and all of them are fixable inside a half-term.

The table below is the version of this a parent can use. It is deliberately specific about what a fortnight of focused work actually achieves, because the honest answer to "can tutoring fix this" varies enormously by category. Terminology and technique move fast. A missing term's worth of electricity does not, and anyone who says otherwise is selling.

One caution on past papers. Reference them, work from them, and get them from the school or the board's own site. No tutor should be supplying syllabus documents, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, and no page should be reproducing them. Cambridge and Pearson publish what they intend parents to have, and the rest is somebody else's copyright.

sections.heading: What IGCSE science tuition costs around Arabian Ranches 3, in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for this kind of search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai family transacts in. So here are the figures, with attribution, and with a clear statement of what they are: market rates for Dubai as a whole, not an IB Gram price list.

Budget online tuition, typically delivered by a university student or a non-specialist, advertises from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour; EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, runs AED 180 to 500; Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts the band at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors go to 500. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270.

Read the in-home row next to the online row and the price gap is the story. The difference is not teaching; it is a car, a driver's hour, and the fact that a tutor who travels can teach perhaps four students a day where one who does not can teach seven. In the outer Dubailand communities that gap widens, because the drive from a central Dubai neighbourhood out to Arabian Ranches 3 at five in the afternoon is not a short one.

The context figure worth knowing is that KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are flat; tutoring is the variable. For our own pricing, the route is the introductory lesson and a conversation, because quoting a number before anyone has established whether your child needs 0620 Extended support or Paper 6 technique would be guesswork dressed as a quote.

sections.heading: Arabian Ranches 3 against the community next door: does the answer change?
paragraphs: This page was written from a comparison, so here is the comparison done properly. Take the nine communities that share this school cluster and road network, and ask what is genuinely different about arranging science tuition in each. The differences turn out to be about timing, not about availability or price, and timing is solvable.

The pattern that repeats is the afternoon. Every one of these communities empties towards the same handful of schools between seven and eight in the morning and refills between two and four. A child who gets home at 3.10pm is not ready to think about electrolysis at 3.30pm, and a child who gets home at 4.15pm has lost the early slot entirely. The communities differ in which of those two situations they are usually in, and that single fact decides what a workable weekly slot looks like.

The second pattern is the sports calendar. Dubai Sports City and the academies around it pull students from the whole belt on weekday evenings, and Motor City and Arabian Ranches 2 both have well-used club schedules. Families consistently underestimate this when booking: a Tuesday 6pm slot that collides with football is a slot that gets cancelled twice a month, which does more damage to a Year 11 than a less convenient time that actually happens.

What does not differ is the thing families expect to differ: who is available to teach. Online delivery means the pool for Cambridge 0620 Extended is the same pool whether you are in Remraam or in Arabian Ranches. That is the whole point of the comparison, and it is why this page gives the same recommendation in every row of the table below.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and the Year 11 timetable squeeze
paragraphs: KHDA is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, and it is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. It inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the published report for your child's school is the single most useful free document available to a parent in this emirate. It will often name science specifically as a strength or a weakness at secondary level.

KHDA also sets something that directly affects a Year 11 science plan: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools, whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and the requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; combined classes for both groups are not permitted because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

Instructional time for those mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary the lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. That arithmetic is why a British-curriculum Year 11 in Dubai has less discretionary time than the same year group in the UK, and why a science catch-up plan that assumes free periods usually collides with reality.

One more point for completeness, because it is the thing nobody in this search result explains. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, past papers and what a science tutor may not do
paragraphs: IGCSE sciences carry no coursework component on the routes described above, which removes the most common academic-honesty problem before it starts. There is still a line, and it is worth stating because this search result contains providers who cross it. A tutor explains, demonstrates, questions and gives feedback. The answers that go on an exam script are the student's own, produced under exam conditions, and no amount of preparation changes that.

The grey area in science is homework and internal assessment. A Year 10 required to submit a practical write-up for school assessment must produce that write-up themselves. A tutor may teach how a results table should be headed, why a conclusion must cite the data, and what an evaluation paragraph is for. A tutor may not dictate sentences into a document that will be submitted with a student's name on it. If a child asks for that, the correct answer is no, and the reason is that the student is the one who carries the consequence.

The same principle applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and the right thing to do is link to the boards' own pages and work from what the school has issued. Any tutor or site offering a downloadable library of mark schemes is distributing someone else's property, and in the case of unreleased material is creating a malpractice exposure for your child.

This matters more in the UAE than it might elsewhere, because ADEK's professional-ethics rules in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's school. The point for a Dubai family is simply this: a tutor who offers something that sounds too convenient is usually offering something that is against a rule somebody enforces.

sections.heading: What happens when no UAE-based specialist is free for your slot
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider in this market has availability limits and almost none of them say so. Here is ours, stated plainly, because a family in Arabian Ranches 3 planning a Year 11 science year deserves to know the failure mode before they commit rather than after.

For mainstream requests, Cambridge or Pearson Biology, Chemistry and Physics at either tier, UAE-based availability is good and a match for a standard weekday evening slot is usually quick. The pressure points are predictable: the 4pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window in the eight weeks before a June series, when every family in Dubai wants the same hour, and narrow combinations such as a student who needs Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 taught as a single coherent course rather than three fragments.

When no UAE-based specialist covers a slot, the options are a different time with the right specialist, the same time with a strong generalist who hands back to the specialist later, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed before anything is booked rather than concealed behind a local number. An IB and IGCSE specialist teaching from India into a Dubai evening is a real and often excellent option; a provider pretending the tutor is around the corner is not.

The last honest caveat is about timing. Starting science support in March for a June series is not pointless, but it changes what can be achieved: technique, paper discipline and triage of the two or three topics carrying the most marks. Starting in September buys the thing families actually want, which is the chance to repair a foundation rather than manage a deficit. Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus code
process.description: The first message should name the board, the subject, the tier and the papers: Cambridge 0620 Extended, Paper 6 route, Year 11. If you do not have it, the school's exam-entry confirmation does. This one detail decides which tutors are even candidates, and it saves a wasted first session more often than anything else.

process.title: Send the mock paper, not the report card
process.description: A report grade says where a student is. A marked mock paper says why. Photographs of the script, including the pages that went badly, let a tutor sort the lost marks into categories before meeting your child, so the introductory lesson starts with a plan rather than a diagnosis.

process.title: Pick the slot that survives the week
process.description: Choose the time that works on a bad Tuesday in Arabian Ranches 3, not the time that works on a good one. A 5pm slot that happens every week beats a 4pm slot cancelled twice a month for football, and consistency is the single largest controllable factor in a Year 11 science year.

process.title: Use the introductory lesson properly
process.description: One lesson with the matched tutor, before any commitment. Ask your child two questions afterwards: did the tutor explain something the school had not, and did they mark anything. A session that only built rapport has told you nothing about whether the match works.

process.title: Review at the half-term
process.description: Six to eight weeks in, compare the error categories from the first mock against the current ones. Terminology and technique errors should be falling. If the only thing that has changed is confidence, the plan needs adjusting, and changing tutor is a normal outcome rather than a failure.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: A tutor is selected for knowing 0620 Extended or 4PH1 specifically, including which topics the mark schemes treat harshly. Geography is irrelevant to that and we do not pretend otherwise, which is why the comparison tables on this page exist rather than a claim about local coverage.

whyPoints.title: The whole hour is teaching
whyPoints.description: No part of the fee pays for a car on Al Qudra Road at five in the afternoon. In the outer Dubailand communities that difference is substantial, and it is the main reason in-home market rates in Dubai sit AED 30 to 200 above online rates for comparable experience.

whyPoints.title: Prices stated as the market, with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the date. We do not publish an invented price list, and we do not quote in dollars at a family that pays in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: Paper technique taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Command terms, mark allocation, Paper 6 conventions and data-table headings are taught as content in their own right, because that is where most of the recoverable marks are. Students who have never been shown how a four-mark question is marked usually gain the fastest.

whyPoints.title: Recordings and written feedback
whyPoints.description: Each session is recorded and followed by a short written note listing what was covered, what was set and which errors recurred. It means the night before a paper has something to work from, and it means a parent can see progress without sitting in the lesson.

whyPoints.title: Limits disclosed before you book
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based specialist covers your slot, you are told, and told what the alternatives are, including a tutor teaching into Gulf Standard Time from elsewhere. A provider that never mentions a coverage limit has one anyway.

faqs.question: Does my child need a laboratory if IGCSE science lessons in Arabian Ranches 3 are online?
faqs.answer: No, because the laboratory part of the qualification happens at school. Cambridge Paper 5 is sat in the school laboratory under school supervision, and Paper 6 is a written paper about experiments the candidate has not performed. Pearson's separate sciences have no practical paper at all and examine method inside the written papers. What a tutor prepares is the written response: reading an instrument from a diagram, heading a results table with units, identifying an anomalous result and writing a conclusion that refers to the data. All of that works better on a shared screen with a real past-paper data set than at a bench.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 easier than three separate IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: It is lighter on timetable blocks rather than lighter on content. Co-ordinated Sciences covers all three sciences across Papers 1 to 4 plus a practical component and awards two IGCSE grades, with depth close to the separate subjects. Families who choose it expecting a reduced workload are often surprised in Year 11. Combined Science 0653 is the genuinely reduced route, awarding a single grade at lower depth, but it does not satisfy entry to DP Higher Level science or A Level science at most schools. Choose with the sixth-form plan in view rather than after it.

faqs.question: My son sits Edexcel 4CH1 rather than Cambridge 0620 — does that change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Pearson's 4CH1 has two written papers, no practical paper and a single untiered entry, so every candidate meets the hardest material and there is no safer tier to retreat to. Experimental method is examined inside the written papers as data-handling and evaluation blocks worth four or five marks at a time. Cambridge 0620 is tiered, with Core capped at grade C, and carries a separate practical component. A tutor who teaches one as though it were the other will drill apparatus technique your child will never be asked about, or skip data questions that carry real marks.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE science tuition cost around Arabian Ranches 3 and Mudon?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market figures, as of October 2026, put budget online tuition at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180 to 500 including travel, and an IGCSE or A Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those are market bands from providers including EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate's Dubai rate table, not an IB Gram price list. The in-home premium is almost entirely travel, which in the outer Dubailand communities is a long drive at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: Would a tutor living in Arabian Ranches 2 be better than one three communities away?
faqs.answer: Not for a reason that shows up in a grade. What a nearby tutor genuinely offers is familiarity with the local school cluster: which textbook is set, which head of science marks hard, when the mocks fall. That knowledge comes from teaching students at those schools, and it survives being delivered over video. What proximity costs is teaching minutes and money, because a travelling tutor's drive is paid for by somebody. Match on the syllabus code and the paper experience first; the community the tutor sleeps in is the least predictive detail available.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the June series should IGCSE science revision properly start?
faqs.answer: Treat the mock results in January as the starting gun and plan backwards from the published timetable rather than from the exam month. A realistic shape is six to eight weeks per genuine topic gap, four to five sessions to fix graph and data technique, and two weeks to make answer-length discipline automatic. That means a student with two topic gaps and weak paper technique needs most of the spring term, not April. Starting in March is not pointless, but it changes the goal from repair to triage of whichever two topics carry the most marks.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Biology, Chemistry and Physics for the same Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being careful about. A science teacher can usually teach all three competently to Core or Combined level. At Extended or Double Award, the depth in each subject is enough that most strong tutors are genuinely specialist in one and solid in the others. If one subject is the problem, use a specialist in that subject. If a student needs general science support across the board, a single tutor is better for continuity. What does not work is one hour a week split three ways.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge Paper 5 and Paper 6 in IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Paper 5 is a practical examination sat in the school laboratory, under supervision, with apparatus in front of the candidate. Paper 6 is the alternative to practical: a written paper about experiments the candidate has not carried out, asking them to describe a method, read an instrument from a diagram, identify a flaw in a described procedure or spot an anomalous result in somebody else's table. The school decides which route a candidate takes and it appears on the exam entry. Preparation for the two is different work, so establish which applies before any revision plan is built.

faqs.question: Are there enough IGCSE science tutors available for a community as new as Arabian Ranches 3?
faqs.answer: Local headcount is not the constraint, because delivery is online and the pool for Cambridge 0620 Extended is the same pool in Remraam as in Arabian Ranches. The real constraint is the hour. Between four and six in the afternoon, Gulf Standard Time, in the eight weeks before a June series, every family in Dubai wants the same slot. Booking a time that is slightly less convenient but reliably free is the practical answer, and it is better advice than any claim about how many tutors live nearby.

faqs.question: My daughter was entered for Core science and is now working above it — can that be changed?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it is a school question rather than a tutor question. Cambridge separate sciences are tiered, with a Core entry capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*, and schools can usually amend an entry up to the board's deadline. Those deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, not weeks: for a June series the entry window closes in the spring, roughly four months before the first script, and the exact day is printed on your school's statement of entry rather than anywhere we could publish it. Work backwards from that and the useful conversation happens in the autumn term, while there is still time to gather evidence. Raise it with the head of science early and ask what they need to see. A tutor's useful contribution is producing an Extended past-paper script that shows she can work at that level.

faqs.question: How does the Dubailand school run affect when a science session can realistically start?
faqs.answer: More than most families allow for. The communities around Arabian Ranches 3 empty towards the same few schools between seven and eight in the morning and refill between two and four. A child home at 3.10pm is not ready to think about electrolysis at 3.30pm, and one home at 4.15pm has lost the early slot. Pick the time that works on a bad Tuesday rather than a good one. A 5pm slot that happens every week is worth considerably more to a Year 11 than a 4pm slot cancelled twice a month.

faqs.question: Will the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons clash with a Year 11 science catch-up plan?
faqs.answer: They occupy real timetable space, which is the point worth understanding. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises no mandatory-subject lesson runs under 25 minutes. The practical effect is that a Dubai Year 11 has less discretionary time than the same year group in the UK, so a catch-up plan built around free periods usually needs rebuilding around evenings.

faqs.question: Do we need KHDA permission to hire a private science tutor in Arabian Ranches 3?
faqs.answer: The permit sits with the tutor, not the family, and it is issued by MoHRE rather than KHDA. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. KHDA's separate Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises, which is a different thing entirely.

faqs.question: How can I check that a science tutor is legally permitted to teach privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and ask which eligibility category they applied under, because the categories are published and a genuine permit holder knows theirs. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion. Be wary of anyone describing themselves as approved by a regulator; the permit is a permit, not an endorsement.

faqs.question: What happens if no UAE-based IGCSE Physics specialist is free in our evening slot?
faqs.answer: You are told before anything is booked, and given three options. Take a different time with the right specialist. Take your preferred time with a strong generalist who hands back to a specialist once a slot opens. Or take a tutor based outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time, which for IB and IGCSE sciences is often an excellent option and is disclosed rather than hidden behind a local phone number. What we will not do is fill the slot with whoever is available and let you discover the mismatch in week three.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches 3?
faqs.answer: No. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing and a session recording. There are no home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates; that service exists only in India. The reason is not logistics but selection: an online slot can be filled by the right Cambridge 0620 Extended specialist, where a visit can only be filled by whoever is willing to drive out to the Dubailand belt at five in the afternoon. The rate comparison table on this page shows what that difference costs.

intro.heading: Three subjects, one bill, and nobody doing the arithmetic
paragraphs: Science is the only part of the IGCSE curriculum where a family can accidentally triple their tutoring spend. A student sitting biology, chemistry and physics as separate awards has three syllabuses, three sets of papers and three teachers at school, so when a report card disappoints, the natural response is to arrange support in each. Three weekly sessions at the Dubai market band for a qualified subject tutor, roughly AED 150-300 an hour, is AED 5,400 to AED 10,800 across a twelve-week term.

Sometimes that is the correct purchase. Usually it is not, and the way to tell is cheap: ask the school for component marks across all three subjects rather than the overall grades. If the losses look similar in all three, the problem is command terms, graph skills and time allocation, which is one intervention of four to six hours that pays in three sets of papers. If one subject is clearly worse, a single six to eight week block there and a reassessment costs a third as much and usually achieves more.

The award route changes the arithmetic before any of that. Cambridge Combined Science is a single award at reduced depth. Coordinated Sciences, syllabus 0654, is a double award covering all three at intermediate depth. The separate sciences, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, are three full awards. Pearson has its own equivalents, including Science Double Award alongside separate 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Most families do not know which they have, and it determines whether one tutor can plausibly cover the ground or three are genuinely needed.

Then there is the practical route, which is a cost question too. Cambridge syllabuses offer a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and the school chooses. The paper version is among the most learnable components in the whole qualification, with question types that repeat, which makes a short targeted block unusually good value. The practical test needs lab rehearsal the school has to provide and a tutor cannot sell you.

Every AED figure here was read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 Dubai rate table, and each is attributed. They describe the market, not our price list. We publish no price list on these pages, because the honest number depends on the diagnosis and on which award route is in play.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run in India only, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. On a cost page the relevant detail is that Bluewaters is reached by one road bridge: the gap between the published in-home band of AED 180-350 and the online band of AED 150-300 is the evening journey, and with three subjects to cover it is a gap that compounds.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-bluewaters-.programmesIntro: Three award structures appear in Bluewaters households, and each carries a different tutoring cost profile. Establish which one applies before anybody quotes for anything.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences
programmes.description: A double award covering biology, chemistry and physics in one integrated syllabus, producing two grades. Content depth sits between Combined Science and the separate sciences, and each paper spans all three disciplines rather than examining them separately.
programmes.countryNote: The cost implication here is specific and favourable. Because every paper spans all three sciences, a single weak discipline drags every paper, which means one targeted block with a specialist in that discipline lifts the whole award. A Coordinated candidate almost never needs three tutors, and being told they do is a sign the diagnosis was never done.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE separate sciences
programmes.description: Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 taken as three full awards, each tiered Core and Extended with Core capped at grade C. Content depth is greatest here, each subject has its own papers plus a practical component, and three awards means three grades and substantially more revision.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the three-tutor default takes hold, and where sequential blocks save the most. Three subjects also means a timetabling problem in the same study leave, which is planning work rather than teaching work and should not be sold as three separate weekly commitments without a component-mark diagnosis first.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences
programmes.description: Pearson offers Science Double Award alongside separate Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1, graded 9-1 and untiered in the International GCSE sciences. Practical skills are assessed within the written papers rather than through a separate practical component.
programmes.countryNote: Because practical skills sit inside the written papers, there is no discrete practical block to buy or skip, and the skills appear wherever they appear. That changes the cost profile: a short block on graph work, variable control and evaluation phrasing pays across every paper rather than being confined to one component.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-bluewaters-.subjectsIntro: Science work with the band each piece needs and whether it pays in one subject or three. The last column is what decides a fixed budget, and no provider in this market publishes it.

subjects.name: Command terms across the sciences
subjects.description: State wants a fact, describe wants an account, explain wants a named reason, compare needs both items in the same statement. Pays in all three subjects and every paper, which makes it the cheapest intervention available at four to six hours in the qualified band.

subjects.name: Graph and table skills
subjects.description: Axes labelled with quantity and unit, scales using most of the grid, a best-fit line drawn as a line, a gradient named as a physical quantity. Sits between topics, badly taught nearly everywhere, and pays in all three subjects at once.

subjects.name: Variable control and evaluation phrasing
subjects.description: Independent, dependent and controlled variables with the control explained rather than listed, plus limitations named instead of human error apologised for. Mark-scheme phrasing that transfers across every practical-skill question on any route.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1. Parallel resistance using reciprocals, and explaining a brightness change by naming the quantity that changed. Single-subject work, but high yield within it and cheap to fix.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, moments and motion
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, moments and pressure. Moments questions are lost on an omitted distance from the pivot or mixed units. Mechanical and suited to short sessions at the lower bands.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Relative formula mass, moles, concentration and reacting masses. The gate in chemistry, because a slow student loses marks across the whole paper. Pure drill, so the budget band is adequate and the yield is high.

subjects.name: Chemistry: electrolysis and organic
subjects.description: Products at each electrode, half equations with balanced charges, homologous series and addition. Half equations are lost on unbalanced charges, which is notation rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and homeostasis
subjects.description: Xylem and phloem, transpiration, the circulatory system, temperature and glucose control. Negative feedback needs receptor, coordinator, effector and correction named in order, and most students supply two of four.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Monohybrid crosses, genetic diagrams, variation and selection. Crosses are lost on undefined allele symbols, which the mark scheme requires, and on omitting the phenotype ratio when it is asked for.

subjects.name: Broad three-subject revision, final weeks
subjects.description: The lowest-yield and most expensive purchase in the subject. By that stage the recoverable marks are in command terms, graph skills and two or three named topics taken from a mock script, not in covering three syllabuses again.

sections.heading: The three-subject arithmetic, done properly
paragraphs: Start with the number nobody puts on a page. A Dubai term is roughly twelve weeks. Three weekly one-hour sessions is thirty-six hours. At the market band for a qualified IGCSE subject tutor online, roughly AED 150-300 an hour with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, that is AED 5,400 to AED 10,800 for one term. Across Year 10 and Year 11 at that rate it becomes the largest discretionary education cost most families carry.

Now the alternatives. A shared-skills block of four to six hours on command terms, graph work and evaluation phrasing is AED 600 to AED 1,800 and pays in all three subjects, because the same mark-scheme habits are being tested in every paper. A single six to eight week subject block is twelve to sixteen hours, or AED 1,800 to AED 4,800. Both of those are available before anybody commits to the thirty-six-hour version.

The diagnosis that chooses between them costs nothing. Ask the school for component marks across all three sciences rather than the overall grades. Losses that look similar in all three mean shared skills. One subject clearly worse means a single block. Genuine weakness in all three, which does occur, means the larger commitment is justified, and in that case it should be staggered across the week rather than stacked on two evenings.

On Bluewaters the arithmetic gets sharper, because an in-home arrangement multiplies the travel premium by three. The published gap between in-home at AED 180-350 and online at AED 150-300 is the journey, and three tutors crossing one bridge in evening traffic is three premiums on a week that, on this island, has room for perhaps one weekday session anyway.

sections.heading: What the award route does to the bill
paragraphs: The award route is the first thing to establish and it changes the cost logic substantially. Email the exams officer and ask for the board, the syllabus code per science, the tier where one applies and the series, in writing. Most Bluewaters families cannot answer this from memory, and the answer determines whether one tutor can cover the ground or three are genuinely needed.

Coordinated Sciences 0654 is the cheapest route to support well, which is counterintuitive. Because every paper spans biology, chemistry and physics, a single weak discipline drags every paper, so one targeted block with a specialist in that discipline lifts the entire double award. A Coordinated candidate who is told they need three tutors is being quoted without a diagnosis.

Combined Science is cheaper still in principle, since content depth is reduced across all three, though it carries a different cost later: many Dubai sixth forms prefer separate sciences for A Level science routes, and a student intending A Level chemistry from Combined Science may find they have not covered material the course assumes. That is a curriculum decision with a financial tail, and it belongs in Year 10 rather than Year 12.

The separate sciences are the most expensive to support, and legitimately so: three full syllabuses, three sets of papers and three times the revision. But the shared-skills argument applies with more force here, not less, because command-term and graph work bought once pays in three separate awards rather than two. The expensive mistake is buying three content tutors before buying the one shared-skills block.

sections.heading: Shared skills: buy once, pay in three papers
paragraphs: This is the single best-value purchase in IGCSE science and it is almost never offered, because it does not look like a subject. Command terms, graph and table skills, variable control and evaluation phrasing are tested in biology, chemistry and physics alike, by the same mark schemes using the same language, and a student who is weak in them is losing marks in all three papers simultaneously.

Command terms first. State wants a fact and no reasoning. Describe wants an account of features or a sequence. Explain wants a reason or mechanism named. Suggest wants a plausible answer where more than one is defensible. Calculate wants working shown. Compare needs both items addressed in the same statement, which is where students most often score zero on a question they understood completely, by writing two separate paragraphs.

Graph skills next, and they are badly taught almost everywhere because they sit between topics rather than inside one. Axes labelled with quantity and unit. Scales chosen so the points occupy most of the grid, since a cramped plot loses accuracy marks on reading values. A line of best fit drawn as a line rather than joined dot to dot, which is a different claim about the data. A gradient calculated and then named as a physical quantity, so the interpretation mark can be awarded.

Then variable control and evaluation phrasing. Independent, dependent and controlled variables, with the control explained rather than listed, and limitations named rather than human error apologised for. Four to six hours covers all of this at the qualified band, which is AED 600 to AED 1,800, and the return appears across every science paper the student sits.
bullets: Compare questions need both items in one statement, not two separate accounts
Axes carry quantity and unit; scales should use most of the grid
Best fit is a line, never joined dot to dot
A gradient must be named as a physical quantity to earn the interpretation mark
Evaluation names a limitation; it does not apologise for human error

sections.heading: The practical route, and whether it needs paid help
paragraphs: Cambridge science syllabuses offer two practical assessment routes and the school chooses which candidates sit. One is a practical test performed under exam conditions. The other is an alternative-to-practical paper assessing the same skills on paper: recognising apparatus from a diagram, identifying variables, completing a results table, plotting, drawing a line of best fit, calculating a gradient and evaluating a method.

The cost implications differ sharply. The alternative-to-practical paper is among the most learnable components in the whole qualification, because the question types repeat across series and the mark scheme rewards specific phrasing. A short targeted block of four to six hours on past papers of that component is genuinely good value, and it overlaps almost entirely with the shared-skills work above, which means one purchase often covers both.

The practical test is different. It needs rehearsal with apparatus, which the school must provide and which no tutor can sell you. What a tutor can do is drill the recording and processing that happens alongside the practical work, and make sure the student is not meeting the results table format for the first time under exam conditions. Beyond that, lab time is the school's responsibility and a family should be asking the department for it rather than buying a substitute.

Pearson International GCSE sciences take a third approach, assessing practical skills within the written papers. There is no discrete component to prepare for, which means the skills appear wherever they appear and the shared-skills block is the only sensible preparation. Ask the exams officer which route applies before buying anything described as practical preparation.

sections.heading: Spending a fixed budget well
paragraphs: Suppose a family decides on a number, say AED 3,000 for the term, and wants it spent as well as possible across three sciences. That is a real constraint rather than a hypothetical, and the allocation below is what we would actually recommend.

First AED 600 to AED 1,800: the shared-skills block, four to six hours at the qualified band. Command terms, graph and table work, variable control and evaluation phrasing. This is bought regardless of the diagnosis, because almost no student in this market is strong in all four and the return appears in three papers.

Remaining AED 1,200 to AED 2,400: a single subject block of six to twelve hours in whichever science the component marks identify, with a specialist in that discipline rather than a general science tutor. For chemistry that usually starts with mole drill, which could be bought even cheaper at the budget band from AED 45 an hour if the budget is tight. For physics it starts with explanation structure. For biology it starts with command-term precision and the negative feedback sequence.

What that allocation deliberately excludes is broad revision across three syllabuses, which is what the same money buys if spread across three weekly sessions for a month. It also excludes the premium band entirely, because at IGCSE level there is very little in the sciences that a qualified subject teacher cannot teach as well as an examiner. Spending at AED 500-650 an hour here is the clearest overspend available in this part of the market.
