sections.heading: Group science classes and what they actually save
paragraphs: Tuition centres across the Marina, JBR and JLT run group science classes, and for a family facing three subjects the saving is the most attractive in this market. A group of four or six working through a topic with a teacher at the board costs a fraction of one-to-one per student, and for content delivery it is a reasonable use of everybody's time.

The honest limits are three. Group teaching moves at the average pace, so the students who need the most help get the least, which is particularly damaging for drill-type work like mole calculations where the slowest student is precisely the one who needed the repetition. It cannot do individual diagnosis, so a student losing marks to command-term misreads will not have that identified in a group. And a mixed-route group, with Coordinated and separate-science candidates together, teaches to neither depth properly.

Where it does work well is as a replacement for broad content revision, which is the thing this page recommends against buying one-to-one anyway. If a family wants the syllabus covered again before mocks, a well-run group class is the sensible way to buy that, at a fraction of the individual cost.

Add travel honestly when comparing. A group class in Al Barsha from Bluewaters is the fee plus two bridge crossings in evening traffic, which for a Year 11 student is most of an evening. Two such commitments a week, for two subjects, and the week has no capacity left for anything else, which is a cost that does not appear on the invoice.

sections.heading: The tier question, which can cap the return on any spend
paragraphs: Before committing money to Cambridge separate sciences, establish the tier, because it may already have decided what grade is reachable. The separate sciences are tiered Core and Extended, and Core is capped at grade C. A student performing at the very top of Core cannot be awarded a B, and if a sixth-form science entry requirement is a B or a grade 6, no amount of tutoring changes the outcome.

That makes the tier the first thing to check on a cost page, because it determines whether the spend has a ceiling. A family paying for twelve hours of Extended-level chemistry support for a student entered for Core is paying for material that will not appear on their papers, which happens more often than it should because nobody checks.

The decision is genuinely open in the first term of Year 10 and close to closed by the second term of Year 11, since Extended content never taught would have to be learned alongside revising everything else. If a move is being considered, the cheapest useful step is asking the school for a timed Extended paper and having it marked properly, then deciding from the script rather than from classwork, which flatters a student working at a comfortable level.

Pearson International GCSE sciences are untiered and graded 9-1, which removes this complication entirely. That is worth knowing if a family is choosing between schools, though it is rarely the deciding factor and should not be presented as one.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and getting a written quote
paragraphs: Start with the check that costs nothing, and bear in mind that three sciences often means more than one tutor, so it may be a check you run three times. The instrument is Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit; it runs two years and is granted free of charge, so it adds nothing to a Bluewaters Island quote and skipping it saves a tutor nothing either. MoHRE's service page states a two-working-day completion time, with the application going through its app, website or e-services. The eligibility list is deliberately wide - teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18 - which covers essentially every person likely to be teaching your child chemistry on a Tuesday evening. u.ae states that tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere, so treat any specific figure quoted to you as invention.

Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which inspects annually and publishes ratings from Outstanding to Very Weak. IB Gram is not KHDA approved, Cambridge accredited or Pearson approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and has no UAE office. We publish no aggregate rating because we have none we could evidence, while competitors in our research publish conflicting review counts on a single page.

On academic honesty, the boundary applies to any school-set investigation or project. A tutor teaches the skills, explains what the criteria reward, questions the approach, and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor never writes, rewrites or completes assessed work or generates data. We also do not reproduce or distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material.

What to ask for before paying is a written answer naming which intervention each of the three sciences needs, which band it requires, and roughly how many hours in total. That is comparable between providers, and it is the document to hold us to as well. An hourly rate multiplied by three subjects is not a quote; it is an assumption dressed as one.

faqs.question: Are group science classes in the Marina a sensible saving?
faqs.answer: For broad content revision, genuinely yes, and a well-run group class is the sensible way to buy that at a fraction of one-to-one cost. The limits are three: group teaching moves at the average pace, so drill-type work such as mole calculations fails the students who most need the repetition; individual diagnosis of command-term losses does not happen; and a mixed group of Coordinated and separate-science candidates teaches to neither depth. Add two bridge crossings in evening traffic per class when comparing the true cost.

faqs.question: Could the Core tier cap what our spending can achieve?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the first thing to check. Cambridge separate sciences are tiered Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C, so a student at the very top of Core cannot be awarded a B. If a sixth-form science requirement is a B or a grade 6, no amount of tutoring changes the outcome. Worse, families sometimes pay for Extended-level content a Core candidate will never sit. Ask for the tier in writing, and if a move is being weighed, ask for a timed Extended paper and decide from the script.

faqs.question: Which science usually gives the quickest return on a short block?
faqs.answer: Physics, on explanation structure, and chemistry, on mole work. Physics explain questions award marks for naming the quantity that changed, the relationship, the direction and the consequence, and students who describe outcomes instead score little however correct they are. Chemistry mole reasoning underpins stoichiometry, electrolysis calculations and most quantitative questions, so a slow student loses marks across the whole paper. Biology is slower because the difficulty is content volume, and it is better served by steady work than by a short block.

faqs.question: Should we ever pay AED 500 or more an hour for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: We would not propose it. At this level there is very little in biology, chemistry or physics that a qualified subject teacher at AED 150-300 an hour cannot teach as well as an examiner, because the mark schemes are less specialised than at Diploma or A Level. The premium band of AED 500-650, with BartyED publishing AED 650, is the clearest overspend available in this part of the market. If a provider proposes it for IGCSE science, ask specifically what the premium is buying.

faqs.question: Why is it more expensive to have three in-home tutors on Bluewaters?
faqs.answer: Because the travel premium applies three times. Dubai in-home one-to-one runs roughly AED 180-350 an hour against AED 150-300 online for the same tier, and that gap is the journey the tutor cannot teach in. From the Al Barsha campus ring it means Sheikh Zayed Road, the Marina approach, one bridge and visitor parking, in the two hours a Year 11 student is free. Three tutors making that journey weekly is three premiums on a week that has room for perhaps one weekday session anyway.

faqs.question: What should a written science quote actually contain?
faqs.answer: Three things per subject: which intervention it needs, which band that requires, and roughly how many hours, plus a total. That is comparable between providers. An hourly rate multiplied by three subjects is not a quote, because it assumes the diagnosis rather than stating it, and the difference between a four-hour shared-skills block and thirty-six hours of weekly sessions is the entire value of the decision. Ask also whether the provider would ever recommend fewer subjects, and treat the answer as informative.

faqs.question: Do you send science tutors to our apartment on Bluewaters?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. Across three subjects the online format also means graph and table work happens on a shared whiteboard that is saved, so revision later starts from the student's own corrected plots. Independent home tutors do work across the Marina and JBR at roughly AED 180-350 an hour, and for a younger child who needs physical presence they can genuinely be the better choice.

faqs.question: Which exam sittings will a Dubai science candidate have?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise, so ask which zone applies.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with school-set science investigations?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches the skills the task assesses, explains what the criteria reward, questions the approach before weeks go into something unworkable, and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor never writes, rewrites or completes any part of it, and never generates data, because the line is authorship and the consequence of crossing it falls on the student. We also do not reproduce or distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material held by the boards.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-bluewaters-.closingHeading: Diagnose across three subjects, then buy once
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-bluewaters-.closingBody: The science bill triples by default rather than by decision. Ask the school for component marks in all three subjects, get the award route and syllabus codes from the exams officer, and check the tier before committing anything. Then buy the shared-skills block first, because command terms, graph work and evaluation phrasing pay in every paper your child sits. Add one subject block where the marks point, review it in writing, and only then consider whether a second is needed. Most families find it is not.

intro.heading: Three different qualifications, one word on the report
paragraphs: Ask five families in Bur Dubai what IGCSE science their child is taking and you will get five answers that all sound the same and are not. One child is sitting three separate sciences and will leave with three IGCSE grades. One is sitting a double award and will leave with two grades covering all three disciplines. One is sitting a single combined award and will leave with one. The content, the number of papers, the depth and - most importantly - which sixth-form and university routes remain available afterwards differ sharply between them. The word science on a school report does not distinguish any of this.

That matters for tutoring in the most practical way. A tutor asked to help with IGCSE physics who assumes separate Cambridge physics while the student is sitting coordinated sciences will set the wrong past papers, teach content that is not on the student's syllabus, and skip content that is. In a twelve-week run-in that is not a minor inefficiency; it is most of the programme. The first question in any useful first session is the syllabus code, and it is printed on the exam entry slip or available from the science department in one email.

The decision itself usually happened in Year 9, when option choices were made, and it is often made on timetable logistics rather than on where the child is heading. A student intending medicine or engineering generally wants the separate sciences, because the double and single awards cover all three disciplines in less depth and some A Level and Diploma Higher Level courses assume the separate route. A student heading for humanities or business may be better served by a double award and an extra subject elsewhere. Neither is wrong; what is wrong is not knowing which one is in play.

Bur Dubai parents also compare schools constantly - against Al Mankhool, against Karama, against Oud Metha, against the Deira side of the creek - and the comparison almost never includes the science award structure. Two schools five minutes apart can offer different routes, and that difference affects a child's options at sixteen far more than a difference of one inspection band. The comparison table later on this page is the one we would want a Year 9 parent in this district to read.

On delivery: IB Gram is an online platform and for every family in the UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India. For science this works, including for the practical component, because the practical papers test experimental reasoning on paper rather than manual skill in a room. And it means a Pearson double award specialist is available to a Karama family whether or not one happens to live nearby, which in this district is the argument that actually matters.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-bur-dubai.programmesIntro: The four routes a Bur Dubai student might actually be on. Find the syllabus code before buying any tutoring, because these need different papers and different preparation.

programmes.name: Separate sciences - triple award
programmes.description: Three distinct qualifications: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, or Pearson International GCSE Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1. Each has its own papers and its own grade, and each goes deeper than any coordinated route. This is the standard expectation for a student heading towards Higher Level sciences in the Diploma or towards medicine and engineering at A Level.
programmes.countryNote: Separate sciences occupy three option blocks in a Dubai timetable that also has to carry mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies. That pressure is the usual reason a school steers a student towards a coordinated route, and it is worth understanding the trade before accepting it.

programmes.name: Coordinated or double award science
programmes.description: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0. All three disciplines are covered and two IGCSE grades are awarded, in less depth than the separate route and in fewer option blocks. Perfectly respectable and widely accepted, but it is not identical to the separate sciences and some sixth-form courses treat it differently. Ask the school what it opens and closes before Year 10 starts.
programmes.countryNote: Double award is common in the Bur Dubai and Al Mankhool school cluster precisely because it frees a timetable block. Students who later decide on a Higher Level science in the Diploma can usually still take it, but they arrive with less depth and the first DP1 term is harder. Plan for that rather than discover it.

programmes.name: Combined or single award science
programmes.description: Cambridge Combined Science 0653 or Pearson Science Single Award 4SS0. All three disciplines in one qualification and one grade, in the least depth. A sensible choice where science is not the direction of travel and the timetable is needed elsewhere, and a restrictive one if a science Higher Level or an A Level science is later wanted. The restriction is the thing to be explicit about.
programmes.countryNote: Where a single award has been taken and a science Diploma subject is now wanted, the honest answer is that there is a real gap to close and it is measured in months rather than weeks. We will say that rather than sell a short block that cannot do it.

programmes.name: What comes next: the Diploma or A Level
programmes.description: Diploma sciences at Standard or Higher Level, or A Level sciences, both of which assume a quantitative foundation. The transition is smoothest from separate sciences, manageable from a double award, and demanding from a single award. In all three cases the gap that bites is mathematical - rearranging equations, handling units, reading gradients - rather than content recall.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students moving from IGCSE into Diploma sciences frequently report the new subject as hard when the actual difficulty is the mathematics inside it. Two or three sessions on algebraic technique at the start of DP1 is the cheapest intervention available and it serves all three sciences at once.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-bur-dubai.subjectsIntro: What a science tutor should be working on, split by discipline and by the skills that cut across all three. The failure modes differ by subject more than families expect.

subjects.name: Biology - recall and precision
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The content volume is the largest of the three and the marks go to precision of language rather than to understanding. Describing osmosis without naming a partially permeable membrane, or enzyme action without naming the active site, scores nothing. Biology rewards learning the exact wording the mark scheme expects, which is a different study habit from the one physics needs.

subjects.name: Biology - the long explain questions
subjects.description: Six-mark questions on topics such as transport in plants, the nervous system or inheritance want a sequence of distinct creditable points, not a flowing paragraph. Students who write beautifully and score three marks are usually making four points where six were available. Explicit practice on point-per-mark structure moves this quickly.

subjects.name: Chemistry - the mole and the equation
subjects.description: Relative formula mass, moles, concentration and reacting-mass calculations, plus balancing equations and writing ionic ones. This is the quantitative spine of IGCSE chemistry and it carries marks across many topics. A student shaky here looks broken in several places at once, which is why it should be diagnosed before any topic is re-taught.

subjects.name: Chemistry - qualitative analysis and tests
subjects.description: Ion tests, gas tests, flame colours and precipitate colours, which are pure memorisation and therefore pure available marks. Students lose them by half-learning: knowing a precipitate is white without knowing which three cations give one. A single session with a well-organised table fixes this and it recurs in every series.

subjects.name: Physics - formula rearrangement
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The single most common source of lost physics marks at IGCSE is algebra, not physics. Rearranging a formula with the unknown in the denominator, converting units before substituting, and keeping track of prefixes such as kilo, milli and micro. This is mathematics teaching inside a physics lesson and it is where a short block should start.

subjects.name: Physics - electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Series and parallel behaviour, potential dividers, and the discipline of drawing a circuit before reasoning about it. Students who try to reason about a parallel branch without redrawing it get it wrong consistently. Electricity is the topic Bur Dubai families name most often and it responds well to a mechanical procedure.

subjects.name: Experimental and practical reasoning
subjects.description: Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, suggesting improvements, judging reliability, reading a measuring instrument correctly and spotting anomalous results. Examined in Cambridge's practical or alternative-to-practical paper and inside Pearson's written papers. It is reasoning on paper, which is why it can be taught entirely online.

subjects.name: Graphs, tables and calculations
subjects.description: Choosing axes, plotting accurately, drawing a line of best fit, calculating a gradient and stating what it physically represents, and processing a results table. Shared across all three sciences and routinely taught in none of them properly. A fortnight of deliberate work here pays in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously.

subjects.name: Command words
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, calculate, suggest, compare, evaluate - each with a defined expected response. Describe asks what happens; explain asks why; suggest expects application to an unfamiliar context. Students who answer every question with everything they know lose marks for the wrong kind of answer rather than for a wrong answer.

subjects.name: Significant figures and units
subjects.description: Giving an answer to a justified number of figures and with the correct unit. Marks are lost here on nearly every paper and they are the cheapest marks in science to recover. Ten minutes of attention per session, consistently, removes the problem inside a month.

subjects.name: Required practicals and apparatus
subjects.description: The standard experiments a syllabus expects familiarity with, described and reasoned about rather than performed. Questions ask what apparatus would be used, how a variable would be controlled, and what would be improved. Reading a method critically is the skill, and it transfers between the three disciplines.

subjects.name: Mathematical skills inside science
subjects.description: Standard form, percentages, ratio, proportionality, rearranging and substituting. Science papers assume these and do not teach them. A student who is behind in mathematics will appear to be behind in science, and the cheapest fix is to treat it as a mathematics problem rather than a science one.

sections.heading: Triple, double or single: what the award actually decides
paragraphs: The award structure is the most consequential decision in IGCSE science and it is routinely made on timetable grounds. Three separate sciences occupy three option blocks and yield three grades. A coordinated or double award covers all three disciplines in two blocks and yields two grades. A combined or single award does it in one block and yields one. Nobody announces this as a decision about a child's options at sixteen, but that is what it is.

The practical consequence sits downstream. A student heading for Diploma Higher Level biology, chemistry or physics, or for A Level sciences, is on the smoothest path from the separate sciences, because the depth is already there. From a double award the path is manageable and the first DP1 term is harder, because the same content was covered in less depth and the quantitative work is lighter. From a single award the gap is real and measured in months. None of these routes is a wall, and we will not pretend a short tutoring block closes the single-award gap when it cannot.

There is a second consequence that families in Bur Dubai raise more than any other: how many science grades appear on the certificate. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A student with three separate sciences has three of the five from science alone; a single-award student has one. That is not a reason to choose by itself, but it is arithmetic worth seeing before Year 10.

The question to ask the school is narrow and answerable: which award is my child entered for, how many IGCSE grades will it produce, and does this school's sixth form - or the schools we might apply to - accept it for the science courses we have in mind? Any science department can answer all three in a short meeting. Almost no family asks.

sections.heading: Bur Dubai against the districts next door, school by school
paragraphs: Families in this part of Dubai compare neighbourhoods seriously, and the comparison usually runs on fees, inspection band and commute. For IGCSE science specifically, the variable that matters most is which award structure a school offers and by which board, because that is what changes a child's position at sixteen. Two schools a five-minute drive apart can differ on it.

The Bur Dubai, Al Mankhool and Oud Metha cluster is heavily British and Indian curriculum, and it contains the widest mix of award structures in Old Dubai. Across the creek in Al Garhoud and Al Mamzar the IB presence is denser, and students there more often take a coordinated route feeding into the Diploma. Out towards Al Qusais and Al Nahda, the Indian-curriculum schools lean towards separate sciences. The commute, not the teaching, is what differs most between a Karama address and a Bur Dubai one.

Here is the conclusion that surprises people, and it is the honest one: once you have established the award and the board, the tutoring shortlist is identical from any of these addresses. A Pearson double award specialist is the same specialist whether the student lives in Karama, Bur Dubai, Oud Metha or Al Nahda, because the examination is identical and the teaching is delivered over video. The neighbourhood changes the school and the journey. It does not change which syllabus codes need teaching or who can teach them.

What the neighbourhood does change is the hour. Oud Metha and Al Mankhool households can realistically hold a 4pm or 4.30pm start. Karama is usually workable by five. Deira-side and Al Nahda families are better served after six, and during Ramadan all of these shift. Choosing the session time against the worst realistic commute rather than the best one is the single most useful local decision a family makes, and it has nothing to do with who is nearby.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same science
paragraphs: Two boards dominate IGCSE science in Dubai and they examine the same disciplines differently. A tutor who does not know which board is in play will set the wrong past papers, and in science that is more damaging than in most subjects because the paper structures differ substantially rather than cosmetically.

Cambridge separate sciences - Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 - run a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper, and then a practical component which the school chooses: either a laboratory practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Which of those two your child's school enters matters, because they are prepared for differently: the alternative-to-practical paper tests experimental reasoning entirely on paper, while the practical test requires performance in a laboratory. A parent can and should ask which one is entered.

Pearson International GCSE sciences - Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1, Physics 4PH1 - take a different approach. There is no separate practical examination; practical and investigative skills are assessed inside the written papers. Pearson physics runs a longer first paper and a shorter second, with the first carrying the larger share of the marks. For a student, the implication is that experimental reasoning questions arrive mixed into theory papers rather than isolated in one, and revision has to treat them as part of normal preparation.

Grade scales add a final layer of confusion in Dubai households. Pearson International GCSE reports on the 9 to 1 scale. Cambridge reports A* to G on some syllabuses and 9 to 1 on others depending on the school's choice. A parent comparing one child's 7 with another's B is not comparing like with like, and a tutor should establish both the scale and the tier before making any claim about where a student stands.

sections.heading: The practical component, and how it is examined without a laboratory
paragraphs: This is the question parents ask most when they hear that lessons are online, and it deserves a direct answer. The practical skills examined at IGCSE are, in the main, reasoning skills assessed on paper. Identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables. Reading a measuring instrument to the right precision. Spotting an anomalous result and saying what should be done about it. Judging whether a method would give reliable data and proposing a specific improvement. Drawing and interpreting a graph. None of those require a student to be standing in a laboratory while they are being taught.

Where a school enters the Cambridge practical test rather than the alternative-to-practical paper, there is a genuine manual element, and that is school work: the apparatus, the technique and the rehearsal happen in the school laboratory with the school's teacher. We do not pretend otherwise and we do not offer to replace it. What a tutor can add even for a practical-test candidate is the reasoning around the technique - why a step is taken, what would go wrong if it were skipped, what the result should look like - which is exactly what the written parts of the assessment reward.

For Pearson candidates the issue mostly dissolves, because practical and investigative skills are examined within the written papers. Experimental questions appear alongside theory, and students who have treated them as a separate category to revise later tend to meet them unprepared. The right approach is to work experimental questions continuously as part of ordinary past-paper practice rather than saving them for a block at the end.

A note on what we will not supply. We do not publish, reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or syllabus documents. We reference them, cite the official source and link out, because reproducing them is someone else's copyright. Your child's science department can usually provide past papers directly, and that is the correct route.

sections.heading: Three disciplines, three different places the marks go
paragraphs: Treating science as one subject is the commonest tutoring mistake at this level. The three disciplines fail differently, and a student can be losing marks in biology for reasons that have nothing in common with why they are losing them in physics. A tutor who applies the same approach to all three will fix one and leave two.

Biology is a precision-of-language subject with a large content volume. Marks go on naming the right structure, using the right term, and making one creditable point per mark in extended answers. A student who understands osmosis perfectly and does not say partially permeable membrane scores nothing. The study habit biology needs is learning exact wording, which is quite different from problem-solving.

Chemistry splits in two. The descriptive half - reactivity, tests, bonding, the periodic table - behaves like biology and rewards precise recall, with ion and gas tests being pure available marks that students half-learn. The quantitative half - formula mass, moles, concentration, reacting masses - behaves like mathematics, and weakness there surfaces in several topics at once. Diagnose which half is the problem before teaching either.

Physics is the one most often misdiagnosed. The overwhelming majority of IGCSE physics marks lost in this district are lost to algebra and units, not to physics: a formula rearranged wrongly when the unknown sits in the denominator, a prefix such as milli or kilo not converted before substituting, an answer given without a unit. Families report that their child cannot do physics when their child cannot yet rearrange an equation under time pressure. It is cheaper and faster to fix as mathematics, and the improvement shows across every topic at once.

What varies is the travel premium attached to an in-home arrangement, and in Old Dubai that premium buys a drive across the creek rather than better science.

Market figures, each attributed and read in October 2026. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which buys homework supervision rather than examination coaching. A qualified subject tutor online is published by Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places IGCSE, IB and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. Monthly packages run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 monthly at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

Three sciences multiply this, which is the budgeting trap specific to IGCSE science. A family taking separate sciences and buying tutoring in all three at a mid-market rate is committing to three times the monthly figure, and that is rarely necessary. In our experience one discipline is usually doing the damage and a second is fine, and a diagnostic paper in each identifies which within two sessions. Buying three standing hours before diagnosing is the most common way money is wasted on this subject in this district.

We hold no office or centre in the UAE, and we are not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, Cambridge International, Pearson or anyone else. sections.heading: The in-home question, and why the answer is the same in Karama as in Bur Dubai
paragraphs: Parents here ask for a home tutor for sensible reasons: visibility, no journey, and a younger sibling who cannot be left. Those arguments are real, and they are the same arguments on both sides of the creek.

Our position, stated before payment rather than after: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a family in Bur Dubai, Karama, Al Mankhool or Oud Metha is one-to-one over live video. We state it because two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas numbers without disclosing where the tutor actually sits, and that is something a family should know before paying.

The reason the answer comes out the same from every address in Old Dubai is that the thing you are buying does not vary by postcode. A Cambridge 0654 coordinated sciences specialist, or a teacher who can read a Pearson 4PH1 script and rank where marks are leaking, is defined by the syllabus rather than by geography. Insisting on physical proximity narrows the pool to whoever is nearby and free, and for a specific code and tier that often means accepting a generalist. From Karama or from Bur Dubai, the specialist pool online is the same pool and it is much larger.

What the online format adds for science specifically is the shared surface. A results table, a graph being plotted, a circuit being redrawn, a mark scheme and the student's own attempt can all be on screen together, annotated and saved for the next session. Three sheets of paper across a table cannot do that and they leave with the tutor. And the hour holds: in a twelve-week run-in across three disciplines, a session lost to a blocked creek crossing is a real cost, and it is a cost that only exists in the travel-based model.

sections.heading: Equivalency, the regulator and the permit a parent can check
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. The sector was 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of pupils and Indian at 26 per cent. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no private school fee increase for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places.

On equivalency, which is what makes the number of science grades matter: for the Ministry of Education's British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five. Verify your own case through the Ministry's own channel - we describe the process and neither perform nor guarantee it, and tutoring is not required for it.

Alongside the international curriculum, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Those hours are part of why three separate sciences is a heavy timetable in a Dubai school and why coordinated routes are common here.

On permits, the position is checkable by any parent. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and states a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no official fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: What is the difference between triple, double and single award IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: They are three different qualifications. Separate or triple award means three distinct syllabuses and three IGCSE grades - Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 - with the most depth. Coordinated or double award, such as Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SD0, covers all three disciplines across two grades in less depth and fewer timetable blocks. Combined or single award, Cambridge 0653 or Pearson 4SS0, gives one grade. The number of grades and the depth both affect which sixth-form science routes stay open.

faqs.question: Does a double award IGCSE science close off Higher Level sciences in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Generally no, but it makes the first DP1 term harder. A double award covers all three disciplines in less depth than the separate route and with lighter quantitative work, so a student arriving at Higher Level biology, chemistry or physics has ground to make up rather than a wall to climb. Ask the receiving school directly what it accepts rather than assuming. From a single combined award the gap is larger and measured in months, and we will tell you that rather than sell a short block that cannot close it.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE science syllabus my child is actually taking?
faqs.answer: It is on the exam entry slip, or the science department will tell you in one email. Ask for five things: the award structure, the board, the syllabus codes, the tier, and - if it is Cambridge - whether the school enters the practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper. Those five answers determine which past papers a tutor should use and how the practical component needs preparing. A tutor working from the wrong code teaches content that is not on your child's syllabus and skips content that is.

faqs.question: How is the IGCSE science practical examined if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Most of what is examined is experimental reasoning on paper: identifying variables, reading instruments to the right precision, spotting anomalous results, judging reliability and proposing specific improvements, and interpreting graphs. None of that requires standing in a laboratory. Where a school enters the Cambridge practical test there is a genuine manual element, and that belongs to the school's laboratory and the school's teacher - we do not offer to replace it. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers, so experimental questions arrive mixed with theory.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science does my child in Bur Dubai most likely need help with?
faqs.answer: Statistically, physics - and within physics, the algebra rather than the physics. The most common losses on a script in this district are a formula rearranged wrongly when the unknown sits in the denominator, a prefix such as milli or kilo not converted before substituting, and an answer without a unit. Families report that their child cannot do physics when their child cannot yet rearrange an equation under time pressure. It is faster and cheaper to treat as a mathematics problem, and the gain shows across every topic at once.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose biology marks when the answers look right?
faqs.answer: Because biology is marked on precision of language. A student who understands osmosis and does not write partially permeable membrane scores nothing for the idea. The same applies to active site in enzyme questions and to dozens of other required terms. The second recurring loss is in extended answers: a six-mark question wants six distinct creditable points, and a fluent paragraph making four of them earns four. Mark-scheme wording drills and point-per-mark structure practice usually move both within two to four sessions.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel better for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Neither is better; they examine differently and the school has already chosen. Cambridge separate sciences run a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component the school selects between a laboratory test and an alternative-to-practical written paper. Pearson has no separate practical examination and assesses those skills inside the written papers, with a longer first paper carrying more of the marks. The practical consequence is simply that past papers from one board are of limited use to a candidate on the other.

faqs.question: Do we need to pay for tutoring in all three sciences?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and buying three standing hours before diagnosing is the commonest way money is wasted on this subject here. Run a diagnostic paper in each discipline first; in most cases one is doing the damage and the others are adequate. Three disciplines at a mid-market rate triples a monthly commitment that Bestimate's Dubai estimates already put at AED 600 to 1,200 for a single weekly hour. Two sessions of diagnosis tends to save considerably more than it costs.

faqs.question: Does living in Karama rather than Bur Dubai change the tutoring we should buy?
faqs.answer: No, once the syllabus code is known. A Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SD0 specialist is defined by the examination rather than by geography, and the examination is identical from every Old Dubai address. What the neighbourhood genuinely changes is the earliest realistic session time and the travel risk attached to any in-home arrangement. Al Mankhool and Oud Metha households can often hold 4pm, Karama around five, and Deira-side or Al Nahda families usually do better after six.

faqs.question: Do you send a science tutor to our home in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Bur Dubai or Karama family is one-to-one over live video, stated before payment. For science the shared screen is genuinely useful: a results table, a graph being plotted, a circuit being redrawn and the mark scheme can all sit together, annotated and saved for next time. The stronger argument is supply, since a specialist in a particular code and tier need not live nearby.

faqs.question: What does Core and Extended mean for IGCSE science grades?
faqs.answer: They are tiers, and the lower tier carries a hard grade ceiling that no amount of tutoring lifts. Cambridge splits into Core and Extended; Pearson splits into Foundation and Higher. The school decides, usually for sound reasons - a student placed on a tier they cannot cope with risks coming away with nothing. The problem is that families often do not know the decision has been made. Ask in writing which tier is entered and what the ceiling is, and ask when the decision could be reviewed.

faqs.question: How many science IGCSEs count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. Sciences count as subjects like any others, which is why a triple-award student has three of the five from science alone and a single-award student has one. Verify your own case through the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: When should we make the IGCSE science award decision?
faqs.answer: In Year 9, when option choices are made, and with the destination in mind rather than the timetable. A student aiming at Diploma Higher Level sciences or A Level sciences is best served by the separate route. A student heading for humanities or business is often better off with a double award and a stronger subject elsewhere. Ask the science department which award is offered, how many grades it produces, and whether the sixth forms you might apply to accept it for the courses you have in mind.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science series do students in Dubai sit?
faqs.answer: The June and November series. Cambridge runs June as the main series with November as the resit route for UAE centres, and Pearson International GCSE is available in May/June and November. The February and March series that appears in online searches is offered to India only and does not apply here. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, so take the timetable from your school rather than from a search result.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supply official science past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: We do not host or redistribute them. Cambridge and Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and syllabus documents are copyright material belonging to the boards, and reproducing them is not ours to do. We reference them, cite the official source and link out. In practice your child's science department can usually supply past papers directly, and that is the right route. Any tutoring site offering a download library of official papers is taking a risk a family has no need to share in.

faqs.question: What should we ask for after the science mocks?
faqs.answer: The scripts for all three disciplines, not just the grades. Mocks usually use real past papers, so the losses on those scripts are the losses likely to recur in the series. With three scripts in hand, a first tutoring session can establish which discipline is actually costing the most and whether the losses are content, terminology, algebra or command words. Without them, the first hour goes on establishing what the department already knew in December, which is an expensive way to start.

Once you have them, run a diagnostic paper in each discipline before committing to anything, because usually one science is doing the damage. The free trial lesson is a good place to do that: one hour, no cost, with the tutor you would continue with, worked on a real question from the correct code and marked against the official scheme. All lessons for Bur Dubai and Karama families are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-business-ba.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics, and the double-award science courses, to students across Dubai's central corridor. Each works from the syllabus code and the school's own topic order rather than a generic science scheme.

intro.heading: Three sciences, several codes, and one entry slip that settles it
paragraphs: IGCSE science is not one subject. A Business Bay student in Year 10 may be sitting three separate qualifications, or a double award counted as two, or a single award counted as one, and the paper structure differs in every case. Before anything useful can be planned, somebody has to look at the entry slip or the school's option sheet and read the code. Cambridge Biology, Chemistry and Physics carry the codes 0610, 0620 and 0625; the Cambridge double award is 0654 and the combined single award 0653. Pearson Edexcel runs 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with 4SD0 as the double award.

That is not pedantry. The two boards build their papers differently. Cambridge tiers the written papers into Core and Extended, so a student entered at Core cannot access the top grades no matter how well they perform, and it assesses practical work through a separate paper — either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper. Pearson Edexcel does not tier the International GCSE sciences and assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead. A tutor who does not know which of those two worlds your child is in will teach the wrong exam technique for a term.

This page is written from the subject outward rather than from the neighbourhood inward, because the syllabus is what decides the grade. Below you will find the component structure for each board, the places Extended-tier marks genuinely disappear, what the practical component asks of a student who is taught online, how the two examination series a UAE candidate sits are actually spaced, and the past-paper sequence that moves a science grade in the final two terms. Business Bay comes into it only where it affects the clock.

On that point: Business Bay has towers and a canal and no secondary school campus. Every pupil here commutes out, usually towards Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf, Al Quoz, Al Barsha or Jumeirah, and returns in the late afternoon. Lessons are delivered live online, one-to-one, over video, which means the school run sets the start time and nothing else has to be negotiated. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The phrase parents search is often a home tutor, and the honest answer is the comparison rather than a promise nobody intends to keep.

A word on what this page will not do. It will not tell you your child needs tutoring, because plenty of Year 10 students do not. It will not quote an IB Gram price list, because the honest starting point is a free trial lesson and a conversation about what a marked paper shows. And it will not hand you an examination date, because dates are revised and the board publishes the live timetable. What it will do is give you the structure of your child's actual qualification, the places marks are lost in it, the market rates with the source that published each one, and the questions worth asking before any money changes hands.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-business-ba.programmesIntro: Three stages matter to a Business Bay science family: the lower secondary years that build the arithmetic, the two IGCSE years themselves, and the post-16 route the science grades lead into.

programmes.name: Lower secondary science, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Science is usually taught as one subject with topics rotating between biology, chemistry and physics. The content is not the problem; the arithmetic is. Students who reach Year 10 unable to rearrange a formula, convert units or read a scale confidently lose marks in every science paper afterwards, and the loss is misdiagnosed as a science weakness for the next two years.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools on the UK curriculum often run Cambridge Lower Secondary and its Checkpoint tests, which are available in March, May and October. Those results are the earliest honest signal a Business Bay parent gets about whether triple science in Year 10 is realistic, and they arrive while there is still time to act on them.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years ending in externally marked papers. A student takes either three separate sciences, a double award counted as two subjects, or a single combined award. Cambridge entries are tiered between Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel entries are not. Grades are reported 9 to 1 or A* to G depending on the board and syllabus, and the school chooses the tier, usually in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: For the UAE Ministry of Education's British equivalency route, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. Science subjects are therefore doing heavy lifting in that count, which is one reason a dropped science matters more here than families expect.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma routes
programmes.description: Most Dubai schools split after Year 11 into International A Levels or the IB Diploma. Science grades at IGCSE are what gate entry to a science at the next level, and schools typically want a strong Extended-tier grade before admitting a student to A Level Chemistry or Higher Level sciences in the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Business Bay families often attend schools that offer one route and not the other, so the IGCSE science grade can decide which school a child continues at as well as which subjects they take. That makes Year 11 science a decision about the next two years rather than a single certificate, and it changes how much support is worth buying in the spring term.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-business-ba.subjectsIntro: These are the science and adjacent courses a Business Bay student most often needs help with, and what each one actually assesses rather than what it is called.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to revise badly. Marks concentrate in the explain and describe distinction, in transport and exchange topics where diagrams carry the answer, and in genetics questions requiring a worked cross rather than a remembered rule.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The most procedural of the three. Moles, concentration and reacting-mass calculations account for a large share of Extended-tier loss, and the organic section rewards students who can write a general formula rather than recall one example.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Algebra in disguise. Electricity circuits and the kinematics graphs are where Extended students most often stall, and almost all of the loss traces back to rearranging and substituting rather than to the physics itself.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: The double and single award routes. Content is reduced rather than easier, and the papers still demand the same command-term discipline. A student moved onto a double award in Year 11 needs the overlap mapped carefully or revises content that is no longer examined.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The quiet cause of most science mark loss. Rearrangement, standard form, ratio and graph reading appear in every science paper, and repairing them once improves three subjects at the same time rather than one.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Year 11 students, often alongside triple science, as a bridge to A Level Maths. Useful context for a tutor to know about, because it competes for the same evening hours as science revision in the spring term.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Relevant to science because six-mark questions are marked on written communication as well as content. Students with strong recall and weak written structure lose marks that look like science gaps and are not.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A common fourth option alongside the sciences. Shares the habit of precise, stepwise explanation that science extended-response questions reward, which is why students who do well in one often improve in the other.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, and taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. It occupies timetable hours that a science-heavy option block would otherwise use, which is worth knowing when planning revision weeks.

subjects.name: Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Also mandatory under the emirate's requirements, with the language of instruction set by whether the student is Arab or non-Arab. Business Bay parents planning a triple-science revision schedule should count these hours in before assuming the week has room.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-business-ba.regionsIntro: Business Bay students travel for school, and the direction they travel shapes which board they are sitting. These are the districts and clusters the entry slips come from.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Towers either side of the canal, no secondary campus. Pupils commute in every direction, so a single street here can hold Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel candidates in the same science subject.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Also campus-free and reaching the same schools. Families here face the same late-afternoon return and the same split between boards, which is why a tutor must ask for the code rather than assume it.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf and Culture Village
regions.note: Creek-side pockets with one IB continuum school and otherwise an outward commute. Students from here often sit the double award rather than triple science because of option-block timing.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Two established schools inside the community, both running a British curriculum through Year 11. The commonest source of Extended-tier Cambridge science entries in this corridor.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Quoz 4
regions.note: Mixed residential and industrial with several schools nearby, including Indian-curriculum options. Families switching a child into IGCSE from CBSE often come from here, and the science content map differs sharply.

regions.name: Meydan and Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Villa communities with longer runs in both directions. Science sessions here usually settle at a weekend morning plus one weeknight rather than two weeknights.

regions.name: Al Barsha and the Al Khail corridor
regions.note: The second direction a Business Bay bus turns, with several large British-curriculum schools. A high proportion of Pearson Edexcel International GCSE science entries come from this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf and the creek side
schoolClusters.note: The nearest cluster to Business Bay and the most common destination. Between them these schools run British curricula through Year 11 and IB continuum programmes, so a parent cannot infer the science board from the postcode.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Quoz and Al Khail
schoolClusters.note: Large British-curriculum schools drawing from the central corridor, several with sixth forms. This is where a Business Bay family most often finds a Pearson Edexcel science entry rather than a Cambridge one.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Reached along Al Wasl Road, mostly British-curriculum schools with established Year 11 cohorts. The slowest afternoon return of the three directions, which pushes science sessions towards 18:30 on weeknights.

modes.title: Single-science weekly support
modes.description: One subject, one fixed weekly session, running a week ahead of the school's topic order so the lesson pre-teaches rather than repairs. The most common arrangement for a Year 10 student whose other two sciences are secure, and the cheapest way to stop one subject dragging a triple-science profile down.
bullets: Taught against the exact syllabus code
A timed past-paper question every session from month two
Written note after each lesson naming one target

modes.title: Triple-science review block
modes.description: A shorter arrangement covering all three sciences across a term, usually one subject a week in rotation. Suited to a student whose problem is examination technique rather than content, because the command terms and six-mark structure transfer directly between the three papers.
bullets: Rotates Biology, Chemistry and Physics weekly
Shared work on command terms and extended response
Arithmetic repair done once rather than three times

modes.title: Final-series past-paper sprint
modes.description: Eight to twelve weeks of timed paper work before the series, sequenced from a marked mock rather than from a syllabus checklist. Multiple choice, theory and the practical component are rehearsed separately because they reward different habits and mixing them wastes the sprint.

sections.heading: Find the syllabus code before you buy a single lesson
paragraphs: The first useful act is administrative. Ask the school's examinations officer, or look at the statement of entry, for the exact syllabus codes your child is entered for and the tier against each. A Business Bay parent who does this before booking anything has already made the single most valuable decision available, because every later choice follows from it: which papers, which tier, whether a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, how many subjects the science block counts as.

Cambridge separates its sciences into Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, with Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award and Combined Science 0653 as a single. Pearson Edexcel runs Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1, with Science Double Award 4SD0. These are not interchangeable. The command-term conventions differ, the paper durations differ, the way practical skills are examined differs, and the published past papers a student should be working through are entirely different documents.

The commonest avoidable error in this market is a tutor who teaches generic science and hands a student past papers from the wrong board. It costs nothing to prevent and cannot be undone in the final term. Insist on the code in the first conversation, and watch whether the person you are speaking to recognises it immediately. A specialist will tell you what Paper 6 is before you have finished the sentence; a generalist will ask you to send more details.

One more reason to start here: the code tells you how many subjects the science block is worth. Triple science counts as three, the double award as two, the single combined award as one. That arithmetic feeds straight into the five-subject count the UAE Ministry of Education's British equivalency route requires, and families who discover the difference in Year 11 have very little room left to change it.
bullets: Get the statement of entry from the school, not a verbal answer
Pearson Edexcel: 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4SD0
Confirm the tier as well as the code; Cambridge Core caps the grade
Past papers must come from the examined board and nowhere else

sections.heading: The two boards build the same subject differently
paragraphs: The table below compares the structures a Business Bay student will meet. The important differences are tiering and practical assessment. Cambridge single sciences are tiered: a Core entry sits a different multiple-choice paper and a different theory paper from an Extended entry, and the grade accessible at Core is capped. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are not tiered, so every candidate sits the same papers and the full grade range is open to all of them.

Practical work is the second fork. In the Cambridge single sciences the practical component is a separate paper, and most schools in this corridor enter candidates for the alternative-to-practical written paper rather than the laboratory practical test. That paper asks a student to read an unfamiliar method, criticise apparatus choices, record results into a prepared table and identify sources of error. It is a learnable paper and it is routinely under-prepared because it does not look like the rest of the course.

Pearson Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead, which spreads the same demand across the whole examination rather than concentrating it. Neither approach is easier. What matters is that a student knows which one they are facing by the autumn of Year 11, and that the past papers in front of them match. Confirm the current component structure, durations and weightings for your child's code with the school, because specifications are revised and the school holds the authoritative version.

A practical consequence for Business Bay families specifically: a single apartment block here can contain candidates from both boards, because children commute in several directions to different schools. Comparing notes with a neighbour is therefore unreliable advice. The only authority on your child's papers is your child's own school.

sections.heading: Component by component: where the marks sit in a Cambridge science
paragraphs: For a Cambridge single science the grade is built from three unequal pieces, and most students revise as though it were one. The multiple-choice paper carries roughly thirty per cent, the theory paper roughly half, and the practical component the remaining fifth. Those proportions change what good revision looks like. A student who has spent four months making content notes has prepared for one of the three.

The multiple-choice paper rewards speed and precision in equal measure. Its distractors are built from the specific misconceptions examiners know students hold, so a student who is almost right picks the wrong option confidently. Drilling it is not glamorous and it is the highest-yield hour available in the final month. The theory paper rewards command-term discipline: state, describe, explain and suggest want different things, and the mark scheme awards nothing for a correct answer to a different question.

The practical component is the one most Business Bay families ignore until February of Year 11. It carries the same weight as a fifth of the grade and it is the most learnable of the three, because the question types repeat: identify the dependent variable, explain why a particular apparatus was chosen, state a source of error that is not human error, suggest an improvement that is actually measurable. Six timed attempts under feedback usually moves this paper more than six weeks of content revision moves the other two.

A short note on mocks. School mocks carry no weight with the board, but they are the only evidence a tier decision gets made on, and they are often written to test recall rather than to mirror the real paper. Read the mock paper itself, not just the mark, and ask whether it included a practical-paper section at all.

sections.heading: Where Extended-tier science marks actually disappear
paragraphs: The losses are specific and they repeat across cohorts. In Chemistry the mole is the gate: students who can recite the relationship between mass, moles and molar mass still lose marks on reacting-mass and concentration questions because they do not write a balanced equation first. In Physics it is rearrangement under pressure, and the circuit questions where a student must decide what is constant before anything else. In Biology it is the describe-versus-explain distinction, and genetics questions answered from a remembered ratio rather than a drawn cross.

Across all three, the single largest avoidable loss is the extended-response question. A student who knows the content writes four true sentences and earns two marks, because the mark scheme wanted a sequence: cause, mechanism, consequence, in that order, with the technical term named. This is a writing problem living inside a science paper, and it is fixed by marking the student's own answers against the published scheme until they can predict the mark before they are told it.

The second largest is unit and significant-figure discipline. It is trivially fixable and it is routinely ignored because it feels like carelessness rather than a skill. In a timed paper it is a skill. A student who converts centimetres to metres automatically, writes the unit on every line and rounds only at the end stops donating the two or three marks a grade boundary usually turns on.

A final, unglamorous category: questions left blank. In a timed paper students skip a question intending to return, and then do not. Teaching a student to write the first line of every question before returning to any of them recovers marks that no amount of content revision would have found.
bullets: Chemistry: balanced equation before any mass or concentration calculation
Physics: decide what is constant before touching a circuit question
Biology: draw the genetic cross rather than recall the ratio
All three: extended response as a sequence, not a list of true facts
All three: units on every line, rounding only at the end

sections.heading: The two series a UAE science candidate sits, counted backwards
paragraphs: A Business Bay candidate sits the June series or the November series. The February/March series exists but is offered to India only, and a tutor or page that hands a UAE family spring dates is giving them a timetable for another country. That matters because entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and a family acting on the wrong calendar misses a deadline it cannot recover.

Pearson Edexcel publishes its International GCSE timetables in advance: the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January — the November 2025 results landed with students on 22 January 2026. For the summer, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series, which is precisely why any date should be read from the live official timetable rather than from a tutoring page.

Cambridge adds a complication worth knowing about. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in, then read that zone's timetable. The table below counts a series backwards so the work lands before the deadline rather than after it.

sections.heading: How a science is taught online when the laboratory is at school
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how a practical subject works over video. The answer is that the laboratory work is the school's job and the examined practical skills are not laboratory skills. What the practical paper actually tests is reading a method, choosing apparatus with a reason, recording results into a sensible table, identifying a genuine source of error and proposing an improvement that could be measured. Every one of those is a paper skill and all of them are better taught on a screen where the method and the mark scheme can sit side by side.

In a session that means the tutor shares the question, the student fills the results table themselves, and then the published mark scheme is opened and compared line by line. The student sees why their source of error earned nothing — human error, read the scale wrongly, not enough time — and what phrasing the examiner accepts instead. That loop is impossible to run from the back of a classroom with thirty students and it is routine one-to-one.

The same logic applies to the content papers. Screen sharing puts a past-paper question, the student's working and the mark scheme in one view, which is how a student learns to predict their own mark. Business Bay families get a second practical benefit: no travel at either end of a weeknight, which in this district means a session can start at 17:30 after a late bus and still finish before homework. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and the comparison below is why that is not a compromise.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs in this corridor, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because that is where most families start and it is where the money is most often wasted. Tutopiya advertises online tuition from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. At that level you are usually buying homework supervision from a university student. For a Year 10 student who simply is not doing the work, that can be exactly right. For an Extended-tier candidate losing marks on the mole concept, it is money spent on company rather than teaching.

The next band up is a qualified subject tutor working online: Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. Above that sit named IB and IGCSE specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's rate table giving 200 to 450 or more. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and as high as AED 500 by independent home tutors, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits circulate in this market. At the top end BartyED publishes AED 650.

All of those are market figures attributed to the providers who published them; none of them is an IB Gram price. Read the spread as a question about what each extra hundred dirhams buys. From AED 50 to AED 150 it buys subject knowledge. From AED 150 to AED 270 it buys diagnosis — someone who can look at a marked paper and name the specific failure. From AED 270 to AED 500 for an in-home visit it buys travel, which changes nothing a student writes in an examination. Begin with the free trial lesson and judge the first marked piece of work rather than the rate card.

sections.heading: Equivalency, the permit, and the honest limits
paragraphs: Science grades carry weight beyond the next school. For the UAE Ministry of Education's British equivalency route a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. One page currently ranking in this market tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five. For the post-16 stage the same route requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

No IB points threshold for equivalency is published in the sources available here, so any figure a tutoring page gives you for the Diploma route should be checked against the Ministry's own pages before you act on it. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees; it is a process you complete with the authority, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

On the permit: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Ask to see it. IB Gram holds no accreditation or partnership with KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, operates no office in the UAE, and does not write any part of a student's coursework or assessed work.
