process.title: Send the statement of entry and a marked paper
process.description: The syllabus codes, the tier and one marked science paper are enough to plan from. That combination tells a tutor which board's past papers to use, whether a practical or alternative-to-practical paper is coming, and which of the classic loss points this particular student has.

process.title: Free trial lesson against the real paper
process.description: A full session with the specialist you would keep, worked on a past-paper question from your child's own board. The tutor marks it against the published scheme in front of you and names the specific failure, so you can judge the diagnosis rather than the sales pitch.

process.title: Decide subjects and components
process.description: Triple science rarely needs three tutors. The plan states which sciences get sessions, which components get priority, and where shared work on command terms and arithmetic will cover all three at once, so the hours go where the marks are.

process.title: Weekly sessions with timed paper work
process.description: From the second month, every session includes at least one question done to time and marked against the scheme. The written note afterwards records the mark, the error and the one target for next week, which is what makes progress visible between reports.

process.title: Rebuild the plan after the mock
process.description: A marked mock in January is the honest checkpoint for a June series. The plan is reset around it, usually by adding timed practical-paper work and dropping content that is now secure, and sometimes by advising that paid support is no longer needed.

whyPoints.title: The code comes first
whyPoints.description: No lesson is planned before the syllabus code and tier are confirmed from the school's own entry information. It is the cheapest safeguard in this market and the error it prevents — past papers from the wrong board — cannot be undone in the final term.

whyPoints.title: Components taught as separate skills
whyPoints.description: Multiple choice, theory and the practical paper reward different habits and are rehearsed separately. A student who has only made content notes has prepared for one of the three, which is why mock results so often surprise families in January.

whyPoints.title: Marked against the published scheme, in view
whyPoints.description: The student's own answer and the mark scheme sit side by side on screen until the student can predict their own mark. That loop is what turns four true sentences into a four-mark answer, and it is difficult to run any other way.

whyPoints.title: The right series, never the wrong one
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November. The February/March series is offered to India only, and we do not put spring dates in front of a Dubai family. Exact dates are read from the board's live timetable, by Cambridge zone where that applies.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, a currency Dubai families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: If no specialist for a particular code and tier is free at your hour, you are told the wait rather than handed a generalist. Lessons are online only in the UAE, no grade is promised, and no part of a student's assessed work is written for them.

faqs.question: Do Business Bay families usually choose triple science or the double award?
faqs.answer: Both are common and the choice is made by the school's option blocks as much as by the student. Triple science counts as three subjects and is the usual route for anyone considering a science at A Level or Higher Level later. The double award counts as two and reduces content without reducing the command-term demand, which suits a student carrying a heavy option block or a language. The decision matters for the equivalency count as well, since five subjects at grade 3 or above are required for the British route. Ask the school which blocks allow which combination before assuming a preference is available.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and how should we prepare for it?
faqs.answer: It is the written paper Cambridge candidates sit in place of a laboratory practical test, and it carries roughly a fifth of a single-science grade. It asks a student to read an unfamiliar method, justify apparatus choices, record results into a prepared table, identify a real source of error and suggest a measurable improvement. The question types repeat year on year, which makes it the most learnable component in the subject and the most under-prepared. Six timed attempts marked against the published scheme generally moves this paper further than six weeks of content revision moves the theory paper.

faqs.question: Where do Business Bay parents find the science syllabus code their child sits?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer for the statement of entry, or check the option sheet issued at the start of Year 10. It lists the board, the syllabus code and the tier for each subject. Cambridge sciences are 0610, 0620 and 0625, with 0654 and 0653 for the double and single awards; Pearson Edexcel uses 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4SD0. Get this in writing rather than verbally, because the tier in particular is sometimes still under discussion, and a Core entry caps the grade a student can reach however well they perform.

faqs.question: How do Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel science papers differ in structure?
faqs.answer: Cambridge tiers its single sciences into Core and Extended, sets a dedicated multiple-choice paper and examines practical skills in a separate paper, usually the alternative-to-practical. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, have no separate multiple-choice paper, and assess practical skills inside the written papers. Neither is easier. The practical consequence is that the examination technique, the timing drills and the past papers are different documents, so a tutor must know the board before the first lesson. Confirm the current structure with your school, which holds the authoritative version of the specification.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better point to start science tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if the aim is a grade rather than a rescue. Year 10 is where the arithmetic habits that determine science marks are either built or missed: rearrangement, units, balanced equations, reading a scale. Repairing those early improves all three sciences at once and costs far fewer hours than fixing them in the spring of Year 11 while also revising content. Starting in Year 11 is still worth doing, but the work becomes triage, focused on the components with the fastest return — the multiple-choice drilling and the practical paper rather than broad content coverage.

faqs.question: My child understands the content but loses marks on six-mark questions. Why?
faqs.answer: Because an extended-response question is marked as a sequence, not as a collection of true statements. The scheme typically wants cause, then mechanism, then consequence, with the technical term named at the right point. A student who writes four accurate sentences in the wrong order earns two marks and leaves the examination believing they answered it. The repair is mechanical: the student answers, then marks their own work against the published scheme, then rewrites. After eight or ten of those they start predicting the mark before being told it, which is the point at which the problem is solved.

faqs.question: What does the Extended tier add that the Core tier leaves out?
faqs.answer: Extended covers additional content and, more importantly, asks questions that combine two ideas rather than testing one. It also opens the full grade range: a Core entry is capped, so a student who outperforms the tier cannot be rewarded for it. Schools usually decide the tier in Year 11 on the evidence of mock results. If you believe your child has been entered too cautiously, ask for the tier decision in writing with the evidence behind it, and ask when the final entry deadline falls, because after it the decision cannot be changed.

faqs.question: When do science candidates in Dubai actually sit their written papers?
faqs.answer: In the June series or the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a UAE candidate. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results reach students in January — the November 2025 results arrived with students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Read the exact dates from the board's live official timetable, because provisional timetables are published early and can be revised.

faqs.question: How do we check the correct Cambridge exam timetable for our school?
faqs.answer: Ask the school which administrative zone it is allocated to. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The zone affects the dates and times papers are sat. Once you have the zone, read the timetable from Cambridge's own exam administration pages rather than from a tutoring site, and check it again closer to the series in case of revisions.

faqs.question: Should we book one tutor for all three sciences or a specialist for each?
faqs.answer: Often yes at IGCSE level, and it can be the better arrangement. A single tutor sees the shared failures — unit discipline, extended-response structure, rearrangement — and fixes them once rather than three times, and keeps one view of where the student's revision time is going. Where a student is close to a grade boundary in one subject with specific content gaps, a subject specialist for that one science alongside a generalist for the other two is usually more efficient. The honest answer depends on whether the problem is technique, which transfers, or content, which does not.

faqs.question: How many weekly sessions does triple science realistically need?
faqs.answer: Through Year 10, one session a week rotating between the three sciences is enough for most students, because the work at that stage is habit-building rather than content coverage. Through the spring of Year 11, families carrying real content gaps commonly move to two sessions a week, with one reserved for timed paper work across all three subjects. More than two a week rarely helps, because the limiting factor becomes the student's own practice time rather than teaching hours, and a tutor who recommends four should explain what the student will stop doing to make room.

faqs.question: Does online science tutoring work when the laboratory is at school?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the examined practical skills are paper skills. The practical component tests whether a student can read a method, justify an apparatus choice, record results properly, identify a genuine source of error and propose a measurable improvement. Those are taught best with the question, the student's own answer and the mark scheme visible together, which is exactly what screen sharing provides. The actual laboratory work remains the school's responsibility. Business Bay families get a second benefit: no travel at either end of a weeknight, so a session can start soon after the bus arrives.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor for a Business Bay student need to be in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, and insisting on it narrows the field for no gain. The syllabus is set by Cambridge or Pearson and is identical wherever it is taught, so what matters is whether the tutor has taught that specific code and tier repeatedly. Timing matters more than location: a tutor must be able to teach at a Gulf Standard Time hour that fits after the Business Bay school run. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai in any case — home visits are an India-only service — so every UAE lesson is live online and the tutor's own address is irrelevant to it.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: The sourced British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. At the post-16 stage the same route asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. A page currently ranking in this market states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. Verify on the Ministry's own pages before acting, and note that equivalency is a process you complete with the authority.

faqs.question: Does a private science tutor in Dubai need a permit from MoHRE?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation free of charge for two years, applied for through its app, website and e-services. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-business-ba.closingBody: Everything useful about IGCSE science support begins with the syllabus code and the tier. Get those from the school in writing, send one marked paper alongside them, and book a free trial lesson with a tutor who recognises the code before you finish the sentence. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around when the Business Bay bus actually arrives. Market rates on this page are attributed to whoever published them. No grade is promised, no board accreditation is claimed, and no part of a student's assessed work is written for them.
